title: Real-world underwater fish recognition and identification, using sparse representation
reason: Primary study proposing a sparse-representation classification method and a detection preprocess for free-living coral reef fish in real-world underwater video from a field observation system in southern Taiwan.

title: Multi-well imaging of development and behavior in Caenorhabditis elegans
reason: Laboratory imaging of C. elegans model organisms in agar-filled glass wells; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Using virtual reality to investigate comparative spatial cognitive abilities in chimpanzees and humans
reason: Behavioural study presenting virtual-reality environments to captive chimpanzees and humans; navigation trajectories from joystick are analysed, no computer vision analysis of animal images or video.

title: Center of mass mechanics of chimpanzee bipedal walking
reason: Biomechanics study of three trained subadult chimpanzees walking on a laboratory runway with force plates. Video was used only to digitize markers by hand; there is no computer vision method and no wild animals.

title: The Catlin Seaview Survey - kilometre-scale seascape assessment, and monitoring of coral reef ecosystems
venue: Aquatic Conservation Marine and Freshwater Ecosystems
reason: Applies computer vision (image clustering, automated benthic annotation, stereo 3D reconstruction) to underwater imagery of wild coral reefs; corals are wild, free-living animals and the paper reports its own case studies.

title: Genetic fingerprinting proves cross‐correlated automatic photo‐identification of individuals as highly efficient in large capture–mark–recapture studies
reason: Primary study evaluating automatic photo-identification software (AMPHIDENT) on ventral pattern photographs of wild-caught great crested newts in a capture-mark-recapture study, validated against genetic fingerprinting.

title: Sex determination of Amur tigers ( Panthera tigris altaica ) from footprints in snow
reason: Develops a footprint-image-based sex classification technique for Amur tigers; trained on captive tiger footprints and applied to snow footprints (direct signs) of free-ranging tigers.

title: The effects of auditory enrichment on gorillas
reason: Behavioural study of zoo gorillas using direct human observation (instantaneous and all-occurrence sampling). No image or video analysis, no computer vision; subjects are captive.

title: Relevance Feedback in Biometric Retrieval of Animal Photographs
reason: Individual identification (re-ID) of wild animals (whale sharks, salamanders, geckos, skinks) from photographs using image retrieval with relevance feedback.

title: Ground-Nesting Insects Could Use Visual Tracking for Monitoring Nest Position during Learning Flights
reason: Applies template-based visual tracking of the nest entrance (a direct animal sign) to views reconstructed from field-recorded learning flights of wild ground-nesting wasps and bees.

title: Fast Automatic Detection of Wildlife in Images from Trap Cameras
reason: Proposes an image-differencing method to detect/segment wild ocelots in camera-trap photographs taken in a forest.

title: A rule-based event detection system for real-life underwater domain
reason: Proposes a computer vision system (detection, tracking, species recognition, trajectory-based behaviour event detection) on underwater videos of free-living coral reef fish in Taiwan.

title: Hierarchical classification with reject option for live fish recognition
reason: Proposes a hierarchical classifier with reject option for recognising free-swimming fish species in underwater videos recorded in the open sea.

title: Inter- and intra-specific diurnal habitat selection of zooplankton during the spring bloom observed by Video Plankton Recorder
reason: Applies Video Plankton Recorder imaging with automated ROI extraction (segmentation threshold, focus) to wild zooplankton in Disko Bay to study diel vertical migration; identification and counting were manual, so this is a borderline include.

title: Defeated chameleons darken dynamically during dyadic disputes to decrease danger from dominants
reason: Behavioural study of captive male veiled chameleons in staged trials in a university vivarium arena; brightness measured manually from photographs. No wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: A method for estimating colony sizes of Adélie penguins using remote sensing imagery
reason: Primary study applying supervised maximum likelihood pixel classification to VHR satellite imagery to map current-year guano (a direct sign of wild Adélie penguin colonies) and estimate breeding pair abundance.

title: Assessing penguin colony size and distribution using digital mapping and satellite remote sensing
reason: Applies supervised maximum likelihood classification to QuickBird2 satellite imagery. The aim is to map the area of wild penguin colonies from guano staining, which is a direct sign of the animals.

title: Heat loss in air of an Antarctic marine mammal, the Weddell seal
reason: Physiology study of wild Weddell seals using infrared thermography. Surface temperatures were read manually from thermograms in the camera maker's software and fed into heat-transfer and statistical models. No computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Evaluating cluster detection algorithms and feature extraction techniques in automatic classification of fish species
reason: Fish species classification on images of formaldehyde-preserved specimens and of four live fish (one individual each) photographed at a prototype fish ladder; no wild, free-ranging animals are shown in the analysed data.

title: Automatic fish taxonomy using evolution-constructed features for invasive species removal
reason: Computer vision classification of wild fish species from field study images (fish captured, photographed, released) for invasive species management.

title: Use of photogrammetry as a means to assess hybrids of rhesus (Macaca mulatta) and long-tailed (M. fascicularis) macaques
reason: Photogrammetric analysis of photographs of free-ranging macaques (open zoo, temples, parks) to measure tail length and pelage colour and identify species and hybrids; some captive monkeys were also photographed.

title: Giving the Forest Eyes: The Benefits of Using Camera Traps to Study Unhabituated Chimpanzees (Pan troglodytes verus) in Southeastern Senegal
reason: Camera-trap study of wild chimpanzees in which all images were sorted and individuals identified manually by the researchers; no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: A Novel Use of Camera Traps to Study Demography and Life History in Wild Animals: A Case Study of Spider Monkeys (Ateles belzebuth)
reason: Camera trap photographs of wild spider monkeys were reviewed and individuals identified manually by researchers; no computer vision or automated image analysis is applied.

title: Marine artificial structures as amplifiers of Aurelia aurita s.l. blooms: a case study of a newly installed floating pier
reason: Ecological field study that applies image-analysis software (ImageJ) to underwater photographs to count wild Aurelia aurita polyps on a floating pier. Borderline: computer vision is only a measurement tool and the paper does not say how automated the counting was.

title: Continuous monitoring of near-bottom mesoplankton communities in the East China Sea during a series of typhoons
reason: In situ underwater plankton camera images of wild mesoplankton and fish at a coral reef observatory; objects are automatically bounded as regions of interest by software and then manually sorted into taxonomic categories.

title: Flying Insect Classification with Inexpensive Sensors
reason: Flying insects from laboratory colonies are classified from pseudo-acoustic signals of a laser/phototransistor sensor recorded as audio; no image or video analysis is performed.

title: The Ignorant Led by the Blind: A Hybrid Human–Machine Vision System for Fine-Grained Categorization
reason: Primary study that develops a computer vision and human-in-the-loop system for bird species identification, evaluated on bird images (CUB-200-2011). Bird identification is the stated application. The paper does not state how the images were obtained; wild status is inferred from the wild bird species named.

title: Local Alignments for Fine-Grained Categorization
reason: General fine-grained categorization method; birds (CUB-2011) and dog breeds (Stanford Dogs) serve only as benchmark classes, and wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Biodiversity conservation: an example of a multidisciplinary approach to marine dispersal

title: Symmetry Evaluation by Comparing Acquisition of Conditional Relations in Successive (Go/No-Go) Matching-to-Sample Training
reason: Behavioural psychology experiment on symmetry in conditional discrimination with two laboratory capuchin monkeys using a touchscreen; no computer vision or image analysis of animals.

title: Classification of Wild Animals based on SVM and Local Descriptors

reason: Stereoscopic video of wild Anopheles gambiae swarms in the field in Mali; computer vision used to localize and track individual mosquitoes in 3D and to analyse male movement.

title: Behaviour of hibernating little brown bats experimentally inoculated with the pathogen that causes white-nose syndrome
reason: Wild-caught bats held in laboratory environmental chambers; infrared video was scored manually by a human observer, with no computer vision or automated image analysis.

title: Cross-species variation in gaze following and conspecific preference among great apes, human infants and adults
reason: Eye-tracking study of gaze following in great apes housed at a primate research centre, compared with human infants and adults. All the animals are captive. No computer vision method is developed or applied to images of wild animals; the study measures gaze with a commercial eye-tracker.

title: Influence of enclosure size on the distances covered and paced by captive tigers (Panthera tigris)
reason: Behavioural study of captive zoo tigers using manual real-time observation and route mapping on paper; no image or video analysis or computer vision. The animals are also captive only.

title: GPS technology as a proxy tool for determining relationships in social animals: An example with African elephants
reason: The study uses GPS collar location data and behavioural observations of zoo elephants. No images or video are analysed, so there is no computer vision; the animals are also captive.

title: Automatic identification of butterfly species based on local binary patterns and artificial neural network
reason: Butterflies were caught, killed, pinned and dried as museum materials; the images analysed show these prepared specimens, not live free-ranging animals.

title: Identification of butterfly based on their shapes when viewed from different angles using an artificial neural network
reason: Butterfly species identification from images of specimens (wing shapes), not wild free-ranging animals; museum/collection specimens are excluded.

title: Tachykinin-Expressing Neurons Control Male-Specific Aggressive Arousal in Drosophila
reason: Neurogenetics study of aggression in laboratory Drosophila; automated behaviour detection is used only as a measurement tool on lab flies in an arena, with no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Assessment of benthic disturbance associated with stingray foraging for ghost shrimp by aerial survey over an intertidal sandflat
reason: Aerial imagery of an intertidal sandflat analysed (tracing, binarization, watershed segmentation, area measurement) to map and quantify feeding pits of wild stingrays, which are direct animal signs.

title: Marine mammals trace anthropogenic structures at sea
reason: Study analyses animal-borne GPS tracking data of wild seals with state-space models; no image or video analysis.

reason: Proposes a texton-based KDE background modeling method and evaluates it on real-life underwater videos of wild fish on a Taiwanese coral reef (Fish4Knowledge), alongside people and vehicle benchmarks.

title: Hierarchical Bayesian models for unsupervised scene understanding
reason: Generic unsupervised scene understanding method tested on standard benchmarks (MSRC, LabelMe, UIUC sports) and an AUV dataset of seafloor habitat classes (sand, reef, rubble, kelp). No animals are the subject of the analysis, only habitat types.

title: Nonparametric label propagation using mutual local similarity in nearest neighbors
reason: Proposes a nearest-neighbour label propagation method and applies it to underwater video images of fish in their natural environment (Fish4Knowledge), including fish species labelling and classification.

title: High resolution vertical distribution of the copepod Calanus chilensis in relation to the shallow oxygen minimum zone off northern Peru using LOKI, a new plankton imaging system

reason: Ecological study of wild copepod vertical distribution using an optical plankton recorder. The images were annotated and measured manually, so no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

reason: Evaluates stereo photogrammetry and laser-scaled video measurement of wild deep-sea benthic megafauna imaged in situ by an ROV at Station M.

reason: Classifies Euglossa bee species from images of the forewings of male specimens, taken with a digital camera on a magnifying glass. These are specimen images, not images of free-ranging animals.

title: Evaluating the performance of artificial neural networks for the classification of freshwater benthic macroinvertebrates

venue: Journal of Experimental Marine Biology and Ecology

reason: Physiology/behaviour study of captive, experimentally inoculated bats in environment chambers; video was viewed manually and no computer vision method was applied.

reason: Applies satellite image classification (Spectral Angle Mapper) to detect guano, a direct sign of wild seabird colonies, in Antarctica.

title: Measurements of behavioral quiescence in Caenorhabditis elegans
reason: Laboratory strains of C. elegans imaged in microfluidic chambers to measure quiescence; no wild or free-ranging animals.

reason: Primary study that uses a three-camera stereo video system with segmentation, tracking and 3D reconstruction on wild starling flocks filmed in the field in Rome.

title: Counting whales in a challenging, changing environment

title: Male motion coordination in anopheline mating swarms
reason: Primary study that applies a stereo-video multi-target tracking algorithm to field footage of wild mosquito mating swarms in a Malian village, then analyses the resulting 3D trajectories.

title: Characterizations of kinetic power and propulsion of the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans based on a micro-particle image velocimetry system
reason: Laboratory study of cultured C. elegans worms confined in a droplet under a microscope; motility derived by micro-particle image velocimetry. No wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Support system for surveying moving wild animals in the snow using aerial remote-sensing images

reason: The images show collected butterfly specimens kept as museum material, not live free-ranging animals. Museum specimens fall under E-CAPTIVE.

reason: Butterflies were caught, killed, pinned and prepared as museum specimens before being photographed; images show specimens only, not living free-ranging animals.

title: Space Use as an Indicator of Enclosure Appropriateness in African Wild Dogs (Lycaon pictus)

title: Automated identification of social interaction criteria in Drosophila melanogaster
reason: Laboratory strains and mutants of Drosophila melanogaster recorded in an arena; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Wing tucks are a response to atmospheric turbulence in the soaring flight of the steppe eagle Aquila nipalensis

title: Mapping the stereotyped behaviour of freely moving fruit flies
venue: Journal of The Royal Society Interface
reason: Laboratory study of Drosophila melanogaster (Oregon-R strain) filmed individually in a custom-made arena; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Finite-Size Scaling as a Way to Probe Near-Criticality in Natural Swarms
reason: Primary study that reconstructs 3D trajectories of individual insects from multi-camera video of wild midge swarms in the field; the vision-based tracking is a tool for a statistical-physics analysis rather than the paper's contribution.

title: A novel approach for species detection from oceanographic video

reason: Computer vision method for detecting wild deep-sea crabs in seafloor observatory video imagery.

reason: Generic human-in-the-loop fine-grained categorization method evaluated on the CUB-200-2011 bird benchmark; it is presented as applicable to any basic-level category, and wildlife conservation is never the stated application.

title: Birdsnap: Large-Scale Fine-Grained Visual Categorization of Birds

title: Nonparametric Part Transfer for Fine-Grained Recognition

title: Tracking Indistinguishable Translucent Objects over Time Using Weakly Supervised Structured Learning

reason: Tracking of Drosophila larvae (laboratory model organism) on a well plate under controlled experimental conditions; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: A thermal infrared video benchmark for visual analysis

title: A Convolutional Neural Network for Automatic Analysis of Aerial Imagery

reason: Primary study proposing a CNN-based detector for dugongs (wild marine mammals) in aerial survey images.

venue: International Conference on Digital Image Computing: Techniques and Applications (DICTA)
reason: Computer vision system for detecting, tracking, counting and measuring free-swimming fish in stereo baited remote underwater video (BRUVS) footage of a natural underwater environment.

title: Clustering based image segmentation for elephant detection

reason: Proposes k-means segmentation plus a K-NN classifier to recognise elephants in infrared images, meant to reduce human-elephant conflict. The dataset mixes wild-type animals (elephant, deer, lion, tiger, bear) with domestic ones (pig, cow, horse, dog).

title: A novel system for automatic detection and classification of animal
reason: Primary study applying image-based classification (BOW + SVM) to images of wild animals (fox, deer, wolf, brown bear, wild boar) for monitoring wildlife migration corridors.

title: Recognition of elephants in infrared images using mean-shift segmentation

title: Deep convolutional neural network based species recognition for wild animal monitoring

title: Foreground object detection in highly dynamic scenes using saliency

title: Recognizing live fish species by hierarchical partial classification based on the exponential benefit

reason: Proposes a hierarchical partial classification method to recognise species of live, freely-swimming fish in underwater images captured by a trawl-mounted camera system in open aquatic habitat.

title: Learning Features and Parts for Fine-Grained Recognition

reason: Generic fine-grained recognition method evaluated only on the Cars benchmark; no animal images are analysed.

title: Automated Social Behaviour Recognition at Low Resolution
venue: Proceedings - International Conference on Pattern Recognition/Proceedings/International Conference on Pattern Recognition
reason: Tracking and behaviour classification of laboratory fruit flies recorded in a dedicated imaging chamber (FlyWorld); no wild or free-ranging animals.

reason: Activity recognition from cameras mounted on four pet dogs; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

reason: Vision-based obstacle avoidance for an underwater robot; segments water vs. obstacles (divers, artificial objects). Animals are not the subject of the image analysis.

reason: The only animals analysed are dogs, a domestic species, filmed in road videos. No wild or non-domestic animals are in the analysed data.

reason: Primary study proposing a computer vision pipeline (preprocessing, background subtraction, blob tracking) to count wild fish in deep-sea observatory video recorded in their natural habitat.

reason: Computer vision method detecting and recognising wild kichiji rockfish in seafloor photographs taken by an AUV during a field survey.

reason: Barcode-tag identification of three-spined sticklebacks kept in a laboratory tank; the paper analyses no wild or free-ranging animals.

reason: 3D digitization (CT, laser triangulation, photogrammetry) of coral skeletons from a university zoology collection, i.e. museum specimens, not wild free-ranging animals.

reason: Zoo giraffes recorded by camera traps in indoor enclosures; the videos were watched and coded by a human observer, so there is no computer vision method either.

reason: Motion estimation of bears in a zoo enclosure and den (Lycksele Zoo); no wild free-ranging animals analysed.

reason: Primary study proposing a SLIC + deep CNN pipeline to detect dugongs in aerial wildlife survey images.

title: Effect of density on traffic and velocity on trunk trails of Formica pratensis
reason: Field study of wild ants on trunk trails. The video was analysed by hand (frame counting and path-length measurement in ImageJ), and no computer vision method was developed or applied.

reason: UAV aerial photographs of wild Antarctic penguins and seals were counted and measured manually in Adobe Photoshop; no computer vision method was developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Uncertainty-aware estimation of population abundance using machine learning
reason: Proposes a logistic-regression count-correction method on classifier scores, developed for ecologists monitoring fish population abundance from video and evaluated on a 12-species fish image collection (alongside cell and traffic-sign data). The paper does not explicitly say the fish are wild; this is inferred from the population-monitoring application.

title: A high-accuracy, time-saving method for extracting nest watch data from video recordings
reason: Applies video tracking software (EthoVision XT) to nest-box videos of free-living Mountain Bluebirds to extract provisioning events.

title: Genetic evidence of female specific eggshell colouration in the Common Crane (Grus grus)
reason: Image analysis of field photographs of wild Common Crane eggs (direct signs at nests) used to identify individual females.

title: Methods and measurement variance for field estimations of coral colony planar area using underwater photographs and semi-automated image segmentation
reason: Semi-automated image segmentation of in situ underwater photographs of wild coral colonies on reefs to measure planar area.

title: Fine-grained object recognition in underwater visual data
reason: Primary study presenting a fish image/video dataset recorded underwater in real-life settings for biodiversity monitoring, plus two computer vision methods for fish species classification.

title: Multisensor and multitemporal data from Landsat images to detect damage to coral reefs, small islands in the Spermonde archipelago, Indonesia
reason: Satellite (Landsat) mapping of shallow-water bottom habitat types (live coral, rubble, sand, dead coral with algae) and their change over time. This is habitat / land-cover mapping, not analysis of individual animals.

title: VAT: A System for Visualizing, Analyzing and Transforming Spatial Data in Science
reason: The paper describes a geo-spatial workflow and processing system. Its use case models wildcat habitat from land-cover and climate rasters plus GBIF occurrence points. No images or video of animals are analysed with computer vision.

title: Developing an automated risk management tool to minimize bird and bat mortality at wind facilities
reason: Thermal video of free-flying wild birds and bats at an onshore wind turbine and an offshore platform is analysed with an automated target detection and tracking program; primary research.

title: Proximity as a proxy for interactions: issues of scale in social network analysis
reason: Forum article on social network analysis using field observations of colour-marked birds; no image or video analysis.

title: Social context modulates idiosyncrasy of behaviour in the gregarious cockroach Blaberus discoidalis
reason: Laboratory behavioural study of purchased, tagged cockroaches tracked in an indoor arena; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Factors influencing stereotypic behaviours of animals rescued from Asian animal markets: A slow loris case study
reason: Behavioural study of rescued slow lorises in a rescue centre based on direct human observation and statistical analysis; no image or video analysis. Animals are captive.

title: Defining pacing quantitatively: A comparison of gait characteristics between pacing and non-repetitive locomotion in zoo-housed polar bears
reason: Gait analysis from video of zoo-housed polar bears only; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Prevalence of stereotypies and its possible causes among captive Asian elephants (Elephas maximus) in Tamil Nadu, India
reason: Behavioural study of captive Asian elephants that used direct focal observation and statistical analysis. It analyses no images or video and uses no computer vision.

title: Behavioural analysis of captive tigers (Panthera tigris): A water pool makes the difference
reason: Behavioural welfare study of captive zoo tigers using manual instantaneous focal sampling by human observers and statistical models; no computer vision or image analysis (animals are also zoo-only).

title: Two novel local binary pattern descriptors for texture analysis
reason: Generic texture descriptor paper (LBP variants) evaluated on texture benchmarks; the butterfly dataset is only one test set and wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Pose estimation-dependent identification method for field moth images using deep learning architecture
reason: Identification of orchard moth pests captured on sticky pest traps for integrated pest management (crop pests in production); training uses lab colonies.

title: GroupTracker: Video tracking system for multiple animals under severe occlusion
reason: Tracking method demonstrated only on laboratory-bred medaka fish filmed in an indoor plastic water tank; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Regional- and local-scale variations in benthic megafaunal composition at the Arctic deep-sea observatory HAUSGARTEN
venue: Deep Sea Research Part I Oceanographic Research Papers
reason: Ecological study of deep-sea benthic megafauna in which seafloor images were annotated manually by a taxonomic expert. The only automated image analysis is detecting laser points to measure image area, which is not analysis of animals.

title: Long-term maintenance and public exhibition of deep-sea hydrothermal fauna: The AbyssBox project
venue: Deep Sea Research Part II Topical Studies in Oceanography
reason: Describes a pressurized aquarium for long-term captive maintenance and exhibition of deep-sea vent crustaceans; no image or video analysis.

title: Two “pillars” of cold-water coral reefs along Atlantic European margins: Prevalent association of Madrepora oculata with Lophelia pertusa, from reef to colony scale
venue: Deep Sea Research Part II Topical Studies in Oceanography
reason: Cold-water coral density and coverage come from manual counting and hand-drawn contours in ImageJ on ROV frame-grabs. No computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: APHIS: A new software for photo-matching in ecological studies
reason: Presents photo-matching software for individual identification, evaluated on images of wild-caught and released lizards and salamanders from capture-photo-recapture field studies.

title: Classification of birds and bats using flight tracks
reason: Thermal video of free-flying wild birds and bats; flight tracks extracted from video and used to classify taxa and flight path types.

title: Two-dimensional thermal video analysis of offshore bird and bat flight
reason: Develops automated image processing to detect and track free-flying wild birds and bats in thermal video recorded in the field.

title: Supporting the annual international black-faced spoonbill census with a low-cost unmanned aerial vehicle
reason: Uses UAV aerial photographs and image processing (k-means classification, hit-or-miss transform, blob analysis) to identify and count wild black-faced spoonbills in Taijiang National Park.

title: Low-cost small action cameras in stereo generates accurate underwater measurements of fish
venue: Journal of Experimental Marine Biology and Ecology
reason: Compares stereo-camera hardware (GoPro vs Sony) for fish length measurement; measurements are made manually by video analysts in EventMeasure software, with no automated image analysis method developed or evaluated.

title: Applying a fast, effective and reliable photographic identification system for green turtles in the waters near Luichiu Island, Taiwan
venue: Journal of Experimental Marine Biology and Ecology
reason: Wild green turtles photographed underwater, but individuals were matched by eye from facial scales. No computer vision or automated image analysis was used.

title: Three-dimensional kinematics of the pelvis and hind limbs in chimpanzee (Pan troglodytes) and human bipedal walking
reason: Marker-based 3-D motion capture of trained chimpanzees walking on a laboratory runway, compared with humans. The animals are laboratory or captive subjects, and no wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Zooplankton abundance, biovolume and size spectra at western boundary currents in the subtropical North Pacific during winter 2012
reason: Applies ZooScan image digitisation and automatic classification (ZooProcess) to net-sampled wild marine zooplankton from field stations to estimate abundance, biovolume and size spectra.

title: Long-term imaging of circadian locomotor rhythms of a freely crawling C. elegans population
reason: Laboratory imaging and tracking of C. elegans strains on agar plates inside incubators; no wild or free-ranging animals in the analysed data.

title: ZOOPS- O2: A broadband echosounder with coordinated stereo optical imaging for observing plankton in situ
reason: Instrument/method paper using calibrated stereo optical imaging (stereo triangulation) to localize and measure size and orientation of free-living pelagic copepods in situ, coupled with sonar.

title: DeepFish: Accurate underwater live fish recognition with a deep architecture
reason: Proposes a deep architecture to classify wild live fish species in underwater videos from the open sea.

title: Mapping Sub-Second Structure in Mouse Behavior
reason: Depth imaging and unsupervised behavioural modelling of laboratory mice in open-field arenas; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Interactive tracking of insect posture
reason: Tracks body parts of harnessed insects (honey bees, ant) in laboratory behavioural experiments; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: A software system for automated identification and retrieval of moth images based on wing attributes
reason: Computer vision system for moth species identification and retrieval using images of curated museum-style specimens photographed against uniform backgrounds, not free-ranging animals.

title: Automatic 3D tracking system for large swarm of moving objects
reason: 3D multi-camera tracking of fruit flies kept in a transparent acrylic box in the laboratory, plus simulated targets; no wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Automatic classification of flying bird species using computer vision techniques
reason: Computer vision classification of flying bird species from video; the seven species include wild birds (House Martin, Wood Pigeon, Black Bird) alongside pet/aviary species (Budgie, Cockatiel, Nanday Parakeet, Superb Starling), so the data appear mixed, although the paper does not state the captive status explicitly.

title: Nasal temperature drop in response to a playback of conspecific fights in chimpanzees: A thermo-imaging study
reason: Thermal imaging of nasal temperature in chimpanzees kept in research facilities (WKPRC Germany, Kumamoto Sanctuary Japan); no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Animal Classification System: A Block Based Approach
reason: Primary study proposing a computer vision method for classifying animal images; images come from the web and the authors' own photographs of animals found around their place, but the paper does not state whether the animals are wild, captive or domestic, and does not name the classes.

title: Object-based Image Analysis for Coral Reef Benthic Habitat Mapping with Several Classification Algorithms
reason: Landsat 8 satellite benthic habitat mapping (sand, rubble, rock, seaweed classes); habitat/land cover classification, not animals as subject.

title: Sponge diversity gradients in marine caves of the eastern Mediterranean
venue: Journal of the Marine Biological Association of the United Kingdom
reason: Ecological survey of wild sponges in marine caves using photoquadrats; sponge outlines were drawn by hand and coverage calculated in software. There is no automated computer vision method.

title: Long-distance dispersal of an Amur tiger indicates potential to restore the North-east China/Russian Tiger Landscape
reason: Conservation news items (tortoise hunting, Amur tiger dispersal, tea plantations, media workshops). Camera-trap photos were used only to document a tiger's dispersal, and no computer vision or image analysis method is applied.

title: Snapshot Serengeti, high-frequency annotated camera trap images of 40 mammalian species in an African savanna
reason: Data descriptor of a camera-trap image dataset of wild Serengeti animals labelled by citizen-science volunteers and aggregated with a plurality vote; no computer vision or image analysis method is developed, applied or evaluated on the images.

title: Australian sea-floor survey data, with images and expert annotations
reason: Data descriptor of an expert-annotated AUV benthic image dataset (BENTHOZ-2015) of wild sea-floor biota including corals, sponges and other invertebrates, released to enable automated labeling by computer vision; no algorithm is applied in the paper itself.

title: Wide Field-of-View Fluorescence Imaging of Coral Reefs
reason: Primary study presenting an in situ fluorescence imaging system for wild reef corals (animals) and testing semi-automated image segmentation of live coral on the field images.

title: How deeply does your mutant sleep? Probing arousal to better understand sleep defects in Drosophila
reason: Video tracking of laboratory Drosophila melanogaster strains housed in glass tubes in an incubator for sleep/arousal research; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: A microfluidic device to study neuronal and motor responses to acute chemical stimuli in zebrafish
reason: Laboratory neuroscience study on agarose-restrained transgenic zebrafish larvae in a microfluidic device with two-photon calcium imaging; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: A tool for developing an automatic insect identification system based on wing outlines
reason: Wing-outline identification tool tested only on pinned owlfly specimens from a university insect collection, photographed on a copy stand; no images of wild, free-ranging animals.

title: Analyzing animal behavior via classifying each video frame using convolutional neural networks
reason: Laboratory Drosophila recorded in egg-laying chambers for neuroscience behaviour analysis; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Automated measurement of mouse social behaviors using depth sensing, video tracking, and machine learning
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
reason: Automated behaviour classification of laboratory mouse strains recorded in a customized behavioural chamber; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: A Universal Animal Welfare Framework for Zoos
venue: Journal of Applied Animal Welfare Science
reason: Policy/framework paper on zoo animal welfare assessment using questionnaire tools; no image or video data and no computer vision method.

title: A Multi-Institutional Assessment of Factors Influencing Locomotion and Pacing in Captive Okapis (Okapia johnstoni)
venue: Journal of Applied Animal Welfare Science
reason: Behavioural study of captive okapis in North American zoos based on direct human observation with a handheld computer and on surveys. No image or video analysis or computer vision is performed. The animals are also zoo-only.

title: Effects of water flow and drilling waste exposure on polyp behaviour inLophelia pertusa
reason: In situ time-lapse and ROV images of wild cold-water coral were analysed, but polyp expansion states were identified and classified manually by the authors; no computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Automatic analysis and characterization of the hummingbird wings motion using dense optical flow features
reason: Optical-flow analysis of wing motion of hummingbirds trained in a laboratory flight chamber; no wild free-ranging animals in the data.

title: Dominance network structure across reproductive contexts in the cooperatively breeding cichlid fish Neolamprologus pulcher
reason: Behavioural study of laboratory-reared cichlids in aquaria. A human observer recorded the dominance interactions directly and the data were analysed with network statistics (ERGMs). No image or video analysis was done.

title: When Optimal Strategy Matters to Prey Fish

title: Discarding of cod in the Danish Fully Documented Fisheries trials
reason: Fisheries electronic monitoring study: CCTV footage of cod discards is reviewed manually by human viewers who count baskets; no computer vision or automated image analysis is developed or applied.

title: Video capture of crustacean fisheries data as an alternative to on-board observers
reason: Primary study measuring size and sex of wild-caught crabs and lobsters from on-board video stills on fishing vessels; image analysis is manual measurement in ImageJ with a regression calibration, not automated.

title: Measuring in situ krill tilt orientation by stereo photogrammetry: examples for Euphausia superba and Meganyctiphanes norvegica
reason: Stereo photogrammetric image analysis of free-swimming wild krill in situ (South Atlantic, Norwegian fjords), plus one ex situ mesocosm dataset, to measure body tilt, length and school density.

title: Activity profiles and hook-tool use of New Caledonian crows recorded by bird-borne video cameras
reason: Bird-borne video of wild New Caledonian crows was scored manually with a media player and a macro script; no computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Emergence of collective changes in travel direction of starling flocks from individual birds' fluctuations
venue: Journal of The Royal Society Interface
reason: Primary study applying a 3D stereo-video tracking algorithm to video of natural, free-flying starling flocks in order to analyse collective turns.

title: Appearance-based multiple fish tracking for collective motion analysis
venue: IAPR Asian Conference on Pattern Recognition (ACPR)
reason: The method tracks a school of sardines filmed in an aquarium tank. All the data shows captive animals; none shows wild ones.

title: Real-time 3D fish tracking and behaviour analysis
venue: IEEE Jordan Conference on Applied Electrical Engineering and Computing Technologies
reason: Laboratory zebrafish tracked in a fish tank during invasive scientific procedures; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Fish detection and movement tracking
venue: International Conference on Advanced Technologies for Communications
reason: Detection and tracking of zebrafish in a laboratory tank with mirrors and controlled pollutant concentrations; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: A thermal Object Tracking benchmark
venue: IEEE International Conference on Advanced Video and Signal Based Surveillance (AVSS)

title: Automatic Fish Recognition and Counting in Video Footage of Fishery Operations

reason: Primary study proposing a computer vision method (ANN pixel classifier, statistical shape model, rule-based counting) to recognise and count wild-caught fish (tuna, swordfish, mahi-mahi) on the deck in video of capture-fishery operations. title: Drifter Sensor Network for Environmental Monitoring
venue: Conference on Computer and Robot Vision (CRV)
reason: Sensor-network/drifter design paper whose vision part stitches seafloor images into mosaics for coral reef/ocean floor mapping; habitat mapping, no analysis of animals as individual subjects.

title: Building a bird recognition app and large scale dataset with citizen scientists: The fine print in fine-grained dataset collection

title: The application of two-level attention models in deep convolutional neural network for fine-grained image classification
venue: IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings - IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings
reason: Generic fine-grained image classification method evaluated on ILSVRC2012 dog/bird subsets and CUB200-2011; wildlife conservation is not the stated subject or application.

title: Deep LAC: Deep localization, alignment and classification for fine-grained recognition
venue: IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings - IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings
reason: Generic fine-grained recognition method (localization, alignment, classification network) evaluated on CUB bird benchmarks; wildlife monitoring or conservation is not the stated application.

title: Articulated motion discovery using pairs of trajectories
venue: Proceedings of the IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition
reason: Unsupervised motion-pattern (behaviour) discovery on video of tigers from nature documentaries, described as tigers in the wild, together with YouTube videos of domestic dogs.

title: Becoming the expert - interactive multi-class machine teaching
venue: IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings - IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings
reason: General machine-teaching method for teaching humans visual categories. It is tested on four mixed datasets (Chinese characters, leaves, museum butterflies, seabed fauna); wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Small instance detection by integer programming on object density maps
venue: Proceedings of the IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition
reason: Proposes a small-instance detection and counting method evaluated on image/video data that includes fish, seagulls, honeybees and flies collected from the Internet, alongside pedestrians and cell images. title: Subset feature learning for fine-grained category classification
venue: IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)
reason: Generic fine-grained categorisation method evaluated on bird benchmarks (Caltech-UCSD, Birdsnap); wildlife/conservation is not the stated application.

title: RS-CPS: A distributed architecture of robotic surveillance cyber-physical system in the nature environment
venue: IEEE International Conference on Cyber Technology in Automation, Control, and Intelligent Systems
reason: System architecture paper with a deployed robotic camera and camera-trap system that does video-based detection of wild animals in a Chinese nature reserve. The computer vision part is thin, but the paper is primary research on wild animals.

title: Research on the Architecture of Wildlife Observation and Communication System
venue: International Conference on Cyber-Enabled Distributed Computing and Knowledge Discovery (CyberC)
reason: System architecture paper on GPS/GSM bird tracking devices with accelerometer-based behaviour recognition; no image or video analysis.

title: Multifactorial uncertainty assessment for monitoring population abundance using computer vision
venue: IEEE International Conference on Data Science and Advanced Analytics (DSAA)
reason: A conceptual framework for assessing uncertainty in fish counts from computer vision systems. It analyses no images: the bias-correction method is shown only with made-up numbers in tables, and empirical evaluation is left to future work.

title: A comparison of background subtraction algorithms for detecting avian nesting events in uncontrolled outdoor video
venue: Proceedings 11th IEEE International Conference on Escience Escience 2015
reason: Primary study comparing background subtraction algorithms on outdoor nest-camera video of wild birds (grouse, tern, plover) to detect nesting events.

title: Face recognition for great apes: Identification of primates in videos
venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics Speech and Signal Processing
reason: Computer vision face detection, tracking and identification of chimpanzees in videos; data include free-living chimpanzees in Taï National Park as well as zoo animals.

title: Detecting kangaroos in the wild: The first step towards automated animal surveillance
venue: ICASSP IEEE International Conference on Acoustics Speech and Signal Processing Proceedings
reason: Primary study proposing a DPM-based detector for wild kangaroos in camera images collected in Queensland national parks.

title: Visual and acoustic identification of bird species
venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics Speech and Signal Processing
reason: Proposes a bird species identification method that classifies bird images with SIFT features and an SVM, with acoustic verification. Wild bird species identification is the stated subject.

title: Use of convolutional neural networks to automate the detection of wildlife from remote cameras
venue: IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (CIS-RAM)
reason: Applies MSER and a pre-trained CNN to detect wild grizzly bears in remote camera time-lapse images from Banff National Park.

title: A simple approach to count and track underwater fishes from videos
venue: International Conference on Computer and Information Technology (ICCIT)
reason: Computer vision method for counting and tracking fish in stock videos from the web (koi carp, goldfish, tilapia, tuna). title: Deep sea high-definition camera system based on marine creature classification technology
venue: IEEE International Conference on Communication Technology (ICCT)
reason: Deep-sea camera system whose video frames of wild marine creatures are segmented by shape and classified with BP neural network and SVM.

title: Bilinear CNN Models for Fine-Grained Visual Recognition
venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)
reason: Generic fine-grained recognition architecture (bilinear CNN) tested on bird, aircraft and car benchmarks; birds appear only as classes of a fine-grained benchmark and wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Component-Wise Modeling of Articulated Objects
venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)
reason: Generic 3D modelling method for articulated objects. Animals (mostly domestic, plus giraffe, hippo, kangaroo from web photos and rendered 3D models) serve only as example object classes; wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Robust Statistical Face Frontalization
venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)
reason: Face frontalization and landmark localization method for human faces and face sketches; cat faces (a pet, from the CAT database) appear only as a secondary demonstration. No wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Intelligent tuna recognition for fisheries monitoring
venue: International Computer Conference on Wavelet Active Media Technology and Information Processing (ICCWAMTIP)
reason: Computer vision method recognising wild-caught tuna in video footage from a commercial fishing boat deck, for fisheries monitoring. This is wild-capture fishing, not aquaculture.

title: A vision based human - elepahant collision detection system
venue: International Conference on Image Information Processing (ICIIP)
reason: Applies computer vision (PHOG+SVM, frame differencing, particle filtering) to detect and track elephants moving near roads and railway tracks in video.

title: Fine-grained bird species recognition via hierarchical subset learning
venue: Proceedings - International Conference on Image Processing
reason: Generic fine-grained classification method evaluated only on the CUB200-2011 benchmark. Birds are benchmark classes and the paper states no wildlife or conservation application.

title: Coupled ensemble graph cuts and object verification for animal segmentation from highly cluttered videos
venue: Proceedings - International Conference on Image Processing
reason: Proposes an animal segmentation method for wildlife camera-trap videos showing wild animals.

title: Mine the fine: Fine-grained fragment discovery
venue: Proceedings - International Conference on Image Processing
reason: A generic fine-grained classification method tested only on the CUB-200-2011 benchmark. The paper does not state wildlife or conservation as its subject.

title: Modelling local deep convolutional neural network features to improve fine-grained image classification
venue: Proceedings - International Conference on Image Processing
reason: Proposes a CNN-based local feature method for fine-grained classification, evaluated on a fish species dataset. Part of the dataset is in-situ underwater images of wild fish, and the rest is fish specimens. A food dataset is also used.

title: Construction of a bird image dataset for ecological investigations
venue: Proceedings - International Conference on Image Processing
reason: Constructs and evaluates an image dataset of wild flying birds recorded near a wind turbine, with bird vs non-bird recognition experiments.

title: Simulation based algorithm for tracking fish population in unconstrained underwater
venue: International Conference on Microwave, Optical and Communication Engineering
reason: Proposes a classical tracking algorithm for multiple moving fish in unconstrained underwater videos; fish are the subject, and the unconstrained underwater setting suggests free-ranging fish, though the paper does not say so explicitly.

title: Vision-based 3D motion reconstruction of octopus arm swimming and comparison with an 8-arm underwater robot
venue: Proceedings IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation
reason: The octopuses were filmed in a water tank in a university neurobiology laboratory. No wild or free-ranging animals appear in the analysed data.

title: Imaged based species recognition system
reason: Eigenface-based image recognition of feral pest species (possums, cats, weasels) for wildlife pest traps. The source of the images is not described.

title: Detection of seals in remote sensing images using features extracted from deep convolutional neural networks
venue: IEEE International Geoscience and Remote Sensing Symposium (IGARSS)
reason: Proposes a CNN-feature plus SVM method to detect wild harp seals and pups on sea ice in aerial survey images.

title: Robotic detection and tracking of Crown-of-Thorns starfish
venue: IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
reason: Primary study developing a vision-based detector and tracker for Crown-of-Thorns starfish; training images come from underwater footage of wild starfish in their natural reef habitat, although evaluation is done in a laboratory by scanning printed posters with a robot arm camera.

title: A model for honey bee tracking on 2D video
venue: International Conference on Image and Vision Computing New Zealand (IVCNZ)
reason: Tracks managed honey bees at a beehive entrance (beekeeping), which falls under the agricultural exclusion.

title: Effective Parameterization of Laser Radar Observations of Atmospheric Fauna
venue: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Quantum Electronics
reason: Method for detecting and parameterizing free-flying wild insects in kHz lidar time-range images (line-scan camera TIFF images) using thresholding and morphological image processing over farmland in Sweden.

title: $K$-Means Clustering-Based Data Compression Scheme for Wireless Imaging Sensor Networks
reason: Proposes a K-means clustering image compression scheme and evaluates it on about 100,000 images of wild bird nests from a field deployment of wireless imaging sensor nodes at the James Reserve. It is image processing applied to wildlife monitoring imagery.

title: Underwater image segmentation via dark channel prior and multiscale hierarchical decomposition
reason: Generic underwater image segmentation method tested only on images of a scale board in an experimental pool; no animals are analysed.

title: Marine life observation using classification algorithms on ocean surface photographs
reason: Proposes detection and classification approaches for wild marine animals and seabirds in airborne sea-surface photographs. It is a methodological proposal; no experiments are reported yet.

title: Underwater hyperspectral imaging for environmental mapping and monitoring of seabed habitats
reason: Underwater hyperspectral imaging from ROVs used to automatically classify wild benthic fauna on the seabed in Norwegian waters.

title: GUARD1: An autonomous system for gelatinous zooplankton image-based recognition
reason: Presents an autonomous underwater imaging system with recognition algorithms for wild gelatinous zooplankton (Mnemiopsis leidyi), validated on images acquired in the field.

title: Recognition of fish based on generalized color Fourier descriptor
reason: Recognition of individual ornamental koi fish recorded in a cultured fish tank; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Automated beehive surveillance using computer vision
reason: Video surveillance of managed honeybee hives in an apiary for beekeepers (beekeeping); no wild, free-ranging non-domestic animals are analysed.

title: Image Segmentation Assessment from the Perspective of a Higher Level Task
venue: SIBGRAPI Conference on Graphics, Patterns and Images (SIBGRAPI)
reason: The paper evaluates image segmentation methods by how well plankton images, including copepods and nauplii, are classified afterwards. Plankton are free-living aquatic organisms, so the study counts as computer vision on wild animals.

title: Classification of fish species with two dorsal fins using centroid-contour distance

reason: The fish were collected through the university's fisheries department and photographed under controlled conditions as specimens on a plain background. No free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Marine Object Detection Using Background Modelling and Blob Analysis
venue: Conference proceedings/Conference proceedings - IEEE International Conference on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics
reason: Proposes a computer vision detection method for wild box jellyfish and sea snakes in images from a surveillance camera near a reef in Queensland.

title: Detecting Densely Distributed Graph Patterns for Fine-Grained Image Categorization
reason: General fine-grained image categorization method (graphlet kernel) evaluated on standard fine-grained and generic benchmarks (birds, butterflies, dogs, flowers, insects, VOC, CIFAR); wildlife is not the stated subject.

title: Fused One-vs-All Features With Semantic Alignments for Fine-Grained Visual Categorization
reason: Generic fine-grained visual categorization method evaluated on standard fine-grained benchmarks (CUB birds, dog and pet breeds); wildlife conservation is not the stated application.

title: GReTA-A Novel Global and Recursive Tracking Algorithm in Three Dimensions
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
reason: Proposes a 3D multi-target tracking algorithm and tests it on multi-camera field video of free-ranging starling flocks, midge swarms and bats, alongside synthetic data.

title: Development of a UAV-type jellyfish monitoring system using deep learning
venue: International Conference on Ubiquitous Robots and Ambient Intelligence
reason: UAV-based computer vision system (superpixels + CNN) to recognise wild Aurelia aurita jellyfish on the sea surface; training/test images obtained in Masan Bay; a pond feasibility test used replicas.

title: A vision-based detection algorithm for moving jellyfish in underwater environment
venue: International Conference on Ubiquitous Robots and Ambient Intelligence
reason: Primary study proposing a vision-based algorithm to detect moving jellyfish in underwater video; the paper does not state whether the video was recorded in the sea or in a tank, so the wild status of the animals is not reported.

title: Segmentation of underwater video objects using Extended Markov Random Field Model
reason: Generic underwater video object segmentation with camera parameter estimation; the paper never states that the segmented objects are animals or that wildlife is the subject.

title: Multiple Insect Tracking with Occlusion Sub-tunnels
venue: IEEE Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision
reason: Tracking of ant colonies and termites confined in a dish in laboratory set-ups; no free-ranging animals.

title: Dolphin Detection and Tracking
reason: Detection and tracking of captive bottlenose dolphins in zoo pools; no wild or free-ranging animals in the analysed data.

title: Automated Detection of Rockfish in Unconstrained Underwater Videos Using Haar Cascades and a New Image Dataset: Labeled Fishes in the Wild
