title: Monitoring Giraffe Behavior in Thermal Video
reason: Thermal video of four giraffes kept in an enclosed savanna at Disney's Animal Kingdom Lodge; animals are captive only.

title: Bottom-type classification in coral reef area using hyperspectral bottom index imagery
venue: Workshop on Hyperspectral Image and Signal Processing: Evolution in Remote Sensing
reason: Benthic bottom-type (habitat) mapping of a coral reef from airborne hyperspectral imagery. Coral is only one of the habitat/substrate classes (sand, rubble, algae, seagrass, ...), and no individual animals are analysed.

title: MotionMeerkat: Integrating motion video detection and ecological monitoring
reason: Presents a motion-detection (background subtraction) tool and tests it on field videos of wild hummingbirds at flowers, plus terrestrial and underwater wildlife videos.

title: A high‐resolution panorama camera system for monitoring colony‐wide seabird nesting behaviour
reason: The paper describes a robotic panorama camera system for a wild shy albatross colony. Nests and marked birds were scored manually by zooming into the panoramas; the only automated image processing is proprietary panorama stitching, so no computer vision method is applied to the animals.

title: Image calibration and analysis toolbox – a free software suite for objectively measuring reflectance, colour and pattern
reason: Software toolbox for camera calibration and colour measurement; validation uses grey reflectance standards and colour pastels photographed in a dark room. No wild animal images are analysed.

title: Crowdsourced geometric morphometrics enable rapid large‐scale collection and analysis of phenotypic data
reason: Fish images from the Encyclopedia of Life are landmarked by hand by crowdsourced workers and experts. No automated computer vision is applied to the images; the analyses are statistical (Procrustes, PCA, BAMM) on manually placed landmarks.

title: Smart nest box: a tool and methodology for monitoring of cavity‐dwelling animals
reason: Presents a smart nest box camera system for wild Tengmalm's owls, but the video was analysed manually by a person; the event detector is an IR light barrier. No automated image analysis or computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Using morphometrics to quantitatively differentiate African wild dog footprints from domestic dog footprints – a pilot study
reason: Footprint images come only from African wild dogs held in a rehabilitation facility enclosure and from domestic dogs at a dog club in Sweden. None of the analysed data shows free-ranging animals.

title: Insights into long‐distance dispersal by African wild dogs in East Africa
reason: Study analyses GPS collar movement data of dispersing African wild dogs; no image or video analysis.

title: Evidence for Partial Migration in the Southern Monarch Butterfly, Danaus erippus, in Bolivia and Argentina
reason: Ecological life-history study of butterfly migration. Images of field-collected specimens are used only for manual wing measurements in ImageJ; no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Quantifying the response of structural complexity and community composition to environmental change in marine communities
reason: Uses AUV stereo imagery and photogrammetric 3D reconstruction of wild coral reef communities (corals are animals) to quantify structural complexity and community change.

title: Low‐budget ready‐to‐fly unmanned aerial vehicles: an effective tool for evaluating the nesting status of canopy‐breeding bird species
reason: UAV photographs of wild hooded crow nests were inspected manually by the researchers (zooming in on photographs); no computer vision or automated image analysis method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Risks and advantages of using surface laser photogrammetry on free‐ranging marine organisms: a case study on white sharks Carcharodon carcharias
reason: Free-ranging white sharks are photographed, but their size is measured by hand, by placing laser-marked photographs into a measurement template in Photoshop. Individuals are recognised by manual dorsal-fin photo-ID. No computational image analysis or computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Photo‐identification as a simple tool for studying invasive lionfish Pterois volitans populations
reason: Primary study testing software-based pattern matching (I3S Pattern) on underwater photographs of wild invasive lionfish for individual identification.

title: Estimating flight height and flight speed of breeding Piping Plovers
reason: Wild Piping Plovers were filmed, but flight height and speed were worked out by hand: an observer read the bird's size against a rifle-scope reticle and counted video frames. No computer vision or automated image analysis method is developed or applied.

title: Quantifying the reefscape transformation of a coastal Caribbean coral reef during a phase shift and the associated coastal landscape change
reason: The computer vision step is a supervised classification of IKONOS satellite images into reef habitat and land-cover classes (seagrass-, algae- and algae-coral-dominated habitats; vegetation, bare ground, urban). This maps habitat, not individual animals. The underwater video transects were scored by hand with points on an acetate sheet, not by image analysis.

title: Estimating A lpine ibex C apra ibex abundance from photographic sampling
reason: Wild Alpine ibex photographed by camera trap and digiscoping, but individuals were identified manually from horn patterns and abundance estimated with capture-recapture models; no computer vision or automated image analysis.

title: Two separated populations of the Indo‐Pacific humpback dolphin (Sousa chinensis) on opposite sides of the Taiwan Strait: Evidence from a larger‐scale photo‐identification comparison
reason: Wild dolphins were identified from photographs, but two human experts did the matching by hand. Software was used only to manage the catalogs. No automated image analysis or computer vision method is used.

title: Automated Fish Detection in Underwater Images Using Shape‐Based Level Sets
reason: Fish outline detection for southern bluefin tuna filmed during transfers into aquaculture grow-out cages; the paper states the approach is developed for a farming aquaculture environment, not wild habitats.

title: Machine vision automated species identification scaled towards production levels
reason: All analysed images are wing photographs of pinned museum specimens of fruit flies and mosquitoes taken under a stereoscope; no images of wild, free-ranging animals.

title: THE EFFECTIVENESS OF FISH LENGTH MEASUREMENT SYSTEM USING NON-CONTACT MEASURING APPROACH
reason: Image-based fish length measurement device developed for the aquaculture industry, tested on a prototype fish and one real fish in water; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Locomotor play drives motor skill acquisition at the expense of growth: A life history trade-off
reason: Behavioural ecology study of wild Assamese macaques. Photos are used only for manual photogrammetric measurement (pixel counts in ImageJ) of forearm length; no computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Shared decision-making drives collective movement in wild baboons
reason: Study of collective movement in wild olive baboons based on GPS collar tracking data; no image or video analysis and no computer vision method is used.

title: Tara Oceans studies plankton at planetary scale
reason: Editorial introduction to a special issue summarizing Tara Oceans research articles (genomics, metagenomics); not primary computer vision research on wild animals.

title: A protocol for the aerial survey of penguin colonies using UAVs
reason: UAV survey protocol for a wild gentoo penguin colony; penguins were counted manually by placing dots in iTag. The only automated image processing is mosaic stitching, so no computer vision analysis of the animals is performed.

title: Assessing use of and reaction to unmanned aerial systems in gray and harbor seals during breeding and molt in the UK
reason: Primary study using UAS imagery of wild gray and harbor seals at haulouts and breeding colonies; individual photo-ID with semi-automated pattern extraction and matching software (ExtractCompare) and image-based body measurement.

title: Evaluation of an unmanned aircraft system for detecting surrogate caribou targets in Labrador
reason: UAS aerial images of plywood surrogate caribou targets were reviewed manually by human photo analysts and analysed with logistic regression; no computer vision method is applied and no real animals were imaged.

title: Evaluation of an unmanned rotorcraft to monitor wintering waterbirds and coastal habitats in British Columbia, Canada
reason: UAV photos of wild wintering waterbirds were identified and counted manually by human observers; no computer vision method was applied to the animal images. The only automated image processing was photogrammetric orthomosaic generation for habitat mapping.

title: Photogrammetry of killer whales using a small hexacopter launched at sea
reason: Field note on using a hexacopter to collect aerial photographs of free-ranging killer whales. Measurement and individual identification are done manually from the images; no automated computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Error control in the set-up of stereo camera systems for 3d animal tracking
venue: The European Physical Journal Special Topics
reason: Stereo-camera 3D reconstruction/tracking set-up and error analysis applied to field recordings of wild starling flocks and midge swarms.

title: A transfer entropy analysis of leader-follower interactions in flying bats
venue: The European Physical Journal Special Topics
reason: Wild bats filmed in a cave with a multi-camera near-infrared system; 3D trajectories reconstructed from video by triangulation and analysed for leader-follower behaviour.

title: Dynamics of animal systems
venue: The European Physical Journal Special Topics
reason: Editorial introducing a topical issue on dynamics of animal systems; summarises contributed papers and open questions, no primary computer vision research.

title: Automated Analysis of Wild Fish Behavior in a Natural Habitat
reason: Computer vision analysis of underwater video of wild Plainfin midshipman fish in their natural nests.

title: Naturalism and ACI
venue: International Conference on Advances in Computer Entertainment Technology (ACE)
reason: Discussion/literature and staff-interview study on naturalism and animal-computer interaction in zoo enclosures; no image or video analysis, and the animals are captive zoo animals.

title: The Killer Fly Hunger Games: Target Size and Speed Predict Decision to Pursuit
reason: Behavioural study of predatory attack decisions in killer flies. High-speed video is only digitized with custom scripts to obtain positions; no computer vision method is developed, applied as the subject, or evaluated.

title: Visual pop-out in barn owls: Human-like behavior in the avian brain
reason: Behavioural visual-search experiment with two hand-raised barn owls from a breeding colony, run in a laboratory experimental chamber. Computer vision is applied to the owls' head-camera videos of stimulus arrays, not to wild animals.

title: Marine Biota and Psychological Well-Being
reason: Environmental psychology study of human physiological and mood responses to stocking levels of an aquarium exhibit. No images or video are analysed with computer vision, and the animals are captive aquarium fish and crustaceans.

title: Automated identification of copepods using digital image processing and artificial neural network
reason: Field-collected copepods were preserved and imaged under a compound microscope in the laboratory. This is microscopy of preserved specimens, not imagery of free-ranging animals.

title: Establishing the fundamentals for an elephant early warning and monitoring system
reason: Project note presenting acoustic and visual (colour-model plus tracking) detection of elephants; the visual method is evaluated on video of free-ranging elephants in Addo Elephant National Park.

title: Thermal reference points as an index for monitoring body temperature in marine mammals
reason: Infrared thermography of marine mammals housed only at the Oceanografic Aquarium of Valencia; no wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Application of a computer vision technique to animal-borne video data: Extraction of head movement to understand sea turtles' visual assessment of surroundings
reason: Primary study applying template matching (computer vision) to animal-borne video of free-ranging green turtles in the wild to track head movements.

title: When hawks attack: animal-borne video studies of goshawk pursuit and prey-evasion strategies
reason: Behavioural study of goshawk pursuit using headcam and ground video; target tracking and optical flow were measured manually in ImageJ, with no automated computer vision method. A falconry goshawk appears together with wild prey.

title: The roles of visual parallax and edge attraction in the foraging behaviour of the butterfly Papilio xuthus
reason: Behavioural experiment on laboratory-reared butterflies flying in an indoor cage arena; video tracking is used only as a tool in a lab set-up, with no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Capuchin Monkeys Alternate Play and Reward in a Dual Computerized Task
reason: Behavioural cognition study of captive capuchin monkeys doing a joystick computer task; no image or video analysis of animals is performed.

title: Where to look when identifying roadkilled amphibians?
reason: Online questionnaire in which human herpetologists identified roadkilled amphibians in photographs. No computer vision method was developed or run; the results are only meant to guide future algorithms.

title: A Generative Statistical Algorithm for Automatic Detection of Complex Postures
reason: Posture detection method for laboratory-reared C. elegans strains (wild-type N2 and coiler mutants) imaged in sealed chambers under magnification; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Model-Independent Phenotyping of C. elegans Locomotion Using Scale-Invariant Feature Transform
reason: Computer vision phenotyping of locomotion in laboratory C. elegans mutant strains recorded on agar plates under a microscope, plus simulated worms; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Population Census of a Large Common Tern Colony with a Small Unmanned Aircraft
reason: Terns in the UAS imagery were counted manually by an observer with the Photoshop count tool; the only automated image analysis is a supervised classification of ground cover, not of animals.

title: The First Description of Dominance Hierarchy in Captive Giraffe: Not Loose and Egalitarian, but Clear and Linear
reason: Behavioural study of dominance hierarchy in zoo giraffes based on direct observation; no image or video analysis or computer vision, and animals are captive only.

title: Field Flight Dynamics of Hummingbirds during Territory Encroachment and Defense
reason: Primary study using multi-camera high-speed video with an automated tracker (background subtraction + Haar cascade) to reconstruct 3D flight trajectories of free, wild hummingbirds at an outdoor feeder.

title: An Assessment of the Effectiveness of High Definition Cameras as Remote Monitoring Tools for Dolphin Ecology Studies
reason: Wild dolphins filmed by fixed cameras, but trained human observers found the dolphins by watching the footage. The only software is a photogrammetric position calculator and a statistical GEE model. There is no automated computer vision analysis.

title: A Semi-Automated Image Analysis Procedure for In Situ Plankton Imaging Systems
reason: Primary study developing a segmentation and SVM classification procedure for in situ images of free-living zooplankton collected by a towed imaging system in Chesapeake Bay.

title: How Lovebirds Maneuver Rapidly Using Super-Fast Head Saccades and Image Feature Stabilization
reason: Video tracking of trained captive lovebirds flying in a custom-built laboratory flight arena; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Towards Automated Annotation of Benthic Survey Images: Variability of Human Experts and Operational Modes of Automation
reason: Primary study evaluating automated point annotation (computer vision) of in-situ coral reef survey photoquadrats; corals and other benthic invertebrates on wild reefs are the subject.

title: Estimating Orientation of Flying Fruit Flies
reason: Orientation estimation of fruit flies flying in a laboratory flight arena with a back-lit multi-camera set-up; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Towards Quantitative Optical Cross Sections in Entomological Laser Radar – Potential of Temporal and Spherical Parameterizations for Identifying Atmospheric Fauna
reason: The only camera image analysis is of a fruit fly released in a laboratory chamber, used to get its flight heading. The field data on wild insects are lidar backscatter time series, not images.

title: A New Dimension in Documenting New Species: High-Detail Imaging for Myriapod Taxonomy and First 3D Cybertype of a New Millipede Species (Diplopoda, Julida, Julidae)
reason: Taxonomic description of a new millipede species using microCT imaging of preserved museum type specimens; no free-ranging animals imaged.

title: BEEtag: A Low-Cost, Image-Based Tracking System for the Study of Animal Behavior and Locomotion
reason: Fiducial-tag tracking software validated on a commercial bumblebee colony kept indoors in a nest box and on printed tags; no images of wild, free-ranging animals are analysed in the experiments.

title: Asian Elephant (Elephas maximus), Pig-Tailed Macaque (Macaca nemestrina) and Tiger (Panthera tigris) Populations at Tourism Venues in Thailand and Aspects of Their Welfare
reason: Welfare survey of captive elephants, macaques and tigers at tourism venues using score sheets, interviews and direct observation; no computer vision or image analysis is performed, and the animals are captive.

title: Assessment of Flooring Renovations on African Elephant (Loxodonta africana) Behavior and Glucocorticoid Response
reason: Behavioural and cortisol study of three captive zoo African elephants; video footage was scored manually by observers using scan sampling, so no computer vision method is used. The subjects are also captive only.

title: Inselect: Automating the Digitization of Natural History Collections
reason: Software for segmenting scanned images of museum specimens (pinned insects, microscope slides); no free-ranging animals.

title: With a Little Help from My Friends: Group Orientation by Larvae of a Coral Reef Fish
reason: Behavioural ecology study of wild-caught reef fish larvae observed in situ. Larval positions in the DISC camera images were recorded by a person clicking in a GUI, and bearings were then analysed with circular statistics. There is no automated computer vision analysis of the images.

title: Computational Methods for Tracking, Quantitative Assessment, and Visualization of C. elegans Locomotory Behavior
reason: Single-worm tracker and analysis software for laboratory C. elegans (wild-type strain N2 and tph-1 mutants) crawling on agar plates; no wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Single-camera Three-dimensional Tracking of Underwater Objects
venue: International Journal of Signal Processing Image Processing and Pattern Recognition
reason: Proposes a computer vision method for 3D tracking of underwater animals (sea turtles, fish, shark) in real underwater videos of marine scenes.

title: STUDY ON SPATIAL DISTRIBUTION OF CORAL REEFS IN LY SON ISLAND USING GIS AND REMOTE SENSING TECHNIQUE
venue: Vietnam Journal of Marine Science and Technology
reason: Benthic habitat mapping (live coral, dead coral, seagrass, sand, deep water) from 30 m Landsat 8 imagery; this maps habitat/cover classes, not images of individual animals.

title: Learning Predictable and Discriminative Attributes for Visual Recognition
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
reason: Generic attribute-learning method for visual recognition, evaluated on the AwA and Caltech256 benchmarks. Animals only appear as benchmark classes; wildlife is not the stated subject.

title: A Geometric Morphometric Study of the Wing Shapes ofPieris rapae(Lepidoptera: Pieridae) from the Qinling Mountains and Adjacent Regions: An Environmental and Distance-Based Consideration
reason: Landmarks were placed by hand on photos of collected butterfly specimens, followed by statistical shape analysis. No automated computer vision or image analysis method is developed or applied.

title: Barriers to adding UAVs to the ecologist's toolbox
venue: Frontiers in Ecology and the Environment
reason: Peer-reviewed letter (perspective) on regulatory barriers to UAV use in ecological research in the US; no image data or computer vision analysis is presented.

title: Terrestrial mammal three‐dimensional photogrammetry: multispecies mass estimation
reason: Builds 3D photogrammetric models from photographs to estimate body mass of 16 mammal species, both captive (zoo) and wild (Kruger National Park). Image-based reconstruction with wild animals in part of the data.

title: Multi-Purpose Exploration of Uncertain Data for the Video Monitoring of Ecosystems
venue: Envirvis 2015 Workshop on Visualisation in Environmental Sciences
reason: The paper proposes an interactive visualization system for exploring the outputs and uncertainty of an existing fish video monitoring pipeline; it performs no image analysis itself.

title: Rapid image processing and classification in underwater exploration using advanced high performance computing
reason: The paper segments poly-metallic nodules on the seafloor for resource exploration and speeds up image enhancement. Megafauna appears in the images but is not analysed, so the study covers habitat and seafloor only.

title: Marine animal classification using combined CNN and hand-designed image features
reason: Develops a CNN plus hand-designed feature classification method on underwater imagery of marine animals (sea fish and benthic animals) from real-world datasets.

title: When underwater imagery analysis meets deep learning: A solution at the age of big visual data
reason: Deep CNN classification and fast-RCNN detection of live fish in open-sea underwater video (Fish4Knowledge).

title: Fast accurate fish detection and recognition of underwater images with Fast R-CNN
reason: Applies Fast R-CNN to detect and recognise wild fish species in underwater videos from Taiwan coral reefs.

title: Real-time fish localization with binarized normed gradients
reason: Proposes a binarized normed gradients method to localize fish in underwater video frames from Fish4Knowledge and ImageCLEF; free-swimming fish are the subject.

title: Quantifying California current plankton samples with efficient machine learning techniques
reason: Machine learning classification of ZooScan images of zooplankton from field-collected (wild) CalCOFI net samples, preserved before scanning; primary research.

title: A computer-aided framework for subsurface identification of white shark pigment patterns
reason: Applies computer-aided contour-recognition software to underwater video images of free-ranging white sharks for individual identification.

title: Remote Sensing of Epibenthic Shellfish Using Synthetic Aperture Radar Satellite Imagery
reason: Analyses SAR satellite imagery and field photographs (structure-from-motion) to map wild intertidal oyster and mussel beds in the Wadden Sea and Oosterschelde.

title: Ground-Level Classification of a Coral Reef Using a Hyperspectral Camera
reason: Pixel-wise classification of in situ hyperspectral images of a natural coral reef, with classes for hard corals, soft coral, fire coral and bleached coral (wild animals).

title: Semi-Automated Object-Based Classification of Coral Reef Habitat using Discrete Choice Models
reason: Maps coral reef habitat and land cover classes from satellite imagery. Animals are not the subject; this is habitat mapping only.

title: Accuracy and precision of habitat structural complexity metrics derived from underwater photogrammetry
reason: Photogrammetric 3D reconstruction of museum coral skeleton specimens imaged in a pool, plus a rocky reef habitat patch; no wild, free-ranging animals are the analysed subject.

title: Mapping Submerged Habitats and Mangroves of Lampi Island Marine National Park (Myanmar) from in Situ and Satellite Observations
reason: Satellite-based benthic and coastal habitat mapping (coral, seagrass, mangrove cover); it maps habitat cover classes, not animals.

title: Automated Tracking of Drosophila Specimens
reason: Tracking of laboratory Drosophila melanogaster (model organism) in a Petri plate under controlled lighting in a laboratory; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Towards an autonomous vision-based unmanned aerial system againstwildlife poachers
reason: Develops and evaluates a visual tracking algorithm on UAV aerial video of wild rhinos and elephants in Africa; the paper also covers human face detection and UAV control, but the animal tracking part meets all inclusion conditions.

title: Evaluating the Potential of Aerial Infrared as a Lek Count Method for Prairie Grouse
venue: Journal of Fish and Wildlife Management
reason: Wild sharp-tailed grouse are filmed with aerial thermal video, but a human observer counts the birds by reviewing the footage after the flight. The paper uses no computer vision or automated image-analysis method; it compares a manual survey method with ground counts.

title: A key to larvae of Diamesa Meigen, 1835 (Diptera, Chironomidae), well known as adult males and pupae from Alps (Europe)
venue: Journal of Entomological and Acarological Research
reason: Taxonomic identification key for Diamesa larvae based on cleared, slide-mounted specimens under an optical microscope; the only image analysis is an RGB colour profile of head-capsule micrographs. No images of wild, free-ranging animals.

title: Fine-grained Recognition Datasets for Biodiversity Analysis
reason: Images show prepared museum/collection specimens of moths and butterflies with artificially spread wings, photographed in a controlled environment; no images of living free-ranging animals.

title: WHOI-Plankton- A Large Scale Fine Grained Visual Recognition Benchmark Dataset for Plankton Classification
reason: Introduces an expert-labelled image dataset of plankton imaged in situ from natural seawater and evaluates classifiers (random forest, CNNs) on it; primary research on wild organisms.

title: Quantification in-the-wild: data-sets and baselines
reason: Introduces and benchmarks image datasets of in-situ plankton and Caribbean coral reef surveys for CNN-based quantification of class distributions; wild marine organisms.

title: Sparse Coral Classification Using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
reason: MSc thesis proposing a CNN-based point classification of coral genera in underwater images of wild shallow and deep-sea coral reefs.

title: WILDLIFE MULTISPECIES REMOTE SENSING USING VISIBLE AND THERMAL INFRARED IMAGERY ACQUIRED FROM AN UNMANNED AERIAL VEHICLE (UAV)
venue: The international archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences/International archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences
reason: UAV visible/thermal imagery of animals kept in separate enclosures at a wildlife observation centre; no wild or free-ranging animals in the analysed data.

title: HOW MANY HIPPOS (HOMHIP): ALGORITHM FOR AUTOMATIC COUNTS OF ANIMALS WITH INFRA-RED THERMAL IMAGERY FROM UAV
venue: The international archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences/International archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences
reason: Primary study developing an image-processing algorithm to automatically detect and count wild hippos in UAV thermal infrared imagery from Garamba National Park.

title: WIMUAS: DEVELOPING A TOOL TO REVIEW WILDLIFE DATA FROM VARIOUS UAS FLIGHT PLANS
venue: The international archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences/International archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences
reason: UAV images of wild savannah mammals are counted manually by human observers with a point-and-click QGIS plugin. The only image processing is projecting image footprints; no computer vision analysis is applied to the animals.

title: Part Localization using Multi-Proposal Consensus for Fine-Grained Categorization
reason: General fine-grained keypoint localization and categorization method evaluated on the CUB-200-2011 benchmark; wildlife or conservation is not the stated application.

title: Optimizing Partition Trees for Multi-Object Segmentation with Shape Prior
reason: Generic segmentation method (partition tree optimization) evaluated on microscopy cell nuclei and urban satellite images; no animals analysed.

title: Automated Identification of Individual Great White Sharks from Unrestricted Fin Imagery
reason: The paper applies computer vision to fin images to identify individual great white sharks, a wild marine species. Only the coversheet and dataset note are available, so the methods cannot be coded in detail.

title: Invariant Image-Based Species Classification of Butterflies and Reef Fish
reason: Proposes an image representation for species classification of butterflies and reef fish from internet images, which the paper describes as taken in the wild.

title: Convolutional Neural Networks for Counting Fish in Fisheries Surveillance Video
reason: Primary study that segments and counts wild-caught fish in CCTV video from operational fishing trawlers. The fish are landed catch on a conveyor belt, not free-swimming, but they are wild, non-farmed animals, so the paper is included.

title: Design of a Video Summarization Scheme in the Wavelet Domain Using Statistical Feature Extraction
venue: International Journal of Image Graphics and Signal Processing
reason: Proposes a classical video summarization method that detects events of interest (animal movement) in underwater videos of fish, crabs and frogs, aimed at marine research. The paper does not say whether the animals are wild.

title: Burst muscle performance predicts the speed, acceleration, and turning performance of Anna’s hummingbirds
reason: Wild-caught Anna's hummingbirds were housed in cages and filmed in an indoor flight chamber with a multi-camera tracking system; no images of free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Photos provide information on age, but not kinship, of Andean bear
reason: Ages and kinship are estimated from photos by human observers (manual measurements, visual estimates of nose colour, an online survey) and then analysed with statistical regression. The paper does not develop or apply any computer vision method.

title: Can we measure beauty? Computational evaluation of coral reef aesthetics
reason: The images are reef scenes of wild coral reef communities, but the analysis scores the aesthetics and status of the whole ecosystem or habitat. Animals are not the analysed subject: the study does not detect, classify or identify them.

title: Captive chimpanzee foraging in a social setting: a test of problem solving, flexibility, and spatial discounting
reason: Behavioural foraging experiment with six zoo-housed chimpanzees; the video footage was coded by hand by researchers and no computer vision was applied. The animals are also captive only.

title: Growth trajectories in wild geladas (Theropithecus gelada)
reason: Applies digital photogrammetry (parallel lasers) to photographs of wild geladas to measure body length and growth; image-based measurement of wild animals. Domestic dogs were photographed only to check accuracy.

title: Gait characteristics and spatio‐temporal variables of climbing in bonobos (Pan paniscus)
reason: Gait study of zoo bonobos only (Planckendael Zoo); video was digitized manually frame by frame, with no automated computer vision.

title: Effect of body mass distribution on the ontogeny of positional behaviors in non‐human primates: Longitudinal follow‐up of infant captive olive baboons (Papio anubis)
reason: Behaviour of captive infant baboons was filmed and coded manually from video in annotation software; no computer vision method is applied, and the animals are captive only.

title: Population structure, residency patterns and movements of whale sharks in Southern Leyte, Philippines: results from dedicated photo‐ID and citizen science
venue: Aquatic Conservation Marine and Freshwater Ecosystems
reason: Primary photo-ID study of wild whale sharks. Computer vision use is limited to computer-assisted spot-pattern matching (I3S, Wildbook for Whale Sharks) alongside manual matching, so inclusion is borderline against E-NOCV.

title: Photographic identification of individuals of a free‐ranging, small terrestrial vertebrate
reason: Primary study evaluating computer-assisted pattern matching (I3S Pattern) against human observers for individual identification of free-ranging Slater's skinks from photographs.

title: Noninvasive unmanned aerial vehicle provides estimates of the energetic cost of reproduction in humpback whales
reason: UAV aerial photographs of free-ranging humpback whales are measured manually by researchers (photogrammetry via an R script, manual photo-identification); no automated computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Ontogeny of head and caudal fin shape of an apex marine predator: The tiger shark ( G aleocerdo cuvier)
reason: Primary study that quantifies head and caudal fin shape of live, wild-caught tiger sharks from digital photographs, using image-based outline extraction and elliptical Fourier analysis.

title: Stereo‐imaging AUV detects trends in sea urchin abundance on deep overgrazed reefs
reason: Stereo-imaging AUV imagery of wild sea urchins and sea cucumbers on reefs, processed with stereo SLAM and 3D meshing, then used to estimate abundance and compared with diver surveys.

title: 3D scanning as a highly precise, reproducible, and minimally invasive method for surface area and volume measurements of scleractinian corals
reason: 3D scanning reconstruction of coral fragments kept in an aquarium tank; no wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Fish species classification in unconstrained underwater environments based on deep learning
reason: Proposes a CNN-based method for species classification of free-swimming fish in underwater video from Taiwan coral reefs (LifeCLEF 2014/2015).

title: StingerCam: A tool for ecologists and stakeholders to detect the presence of venomous tropical jellyfish
reason: Fixed jetty camera images of wild box jellyfish in coastal waters, analysed with an image-analysis pipeline to identify and count jellyfish.

title: Validation methods for plankton image classification systems
reason: Plankton water samples imaged with a FlowCAM flow-imaging microscope at 100X; microscopy of collected samples (mostly phytoplankton and protists), not images of free-ranging animals in situ.

title: Construction, implementation and testing of an image identification system using computer vision methods for fruit flies with economic importance (Diptera: Tephritidae)
reason: Image identification system for tephritid fruit fly pests built on microscope photographs of pinned or alcohol-preserved museum and quarantine specimens; only a few test images from the Internet show living insects.

title: Robotic Coral Reef Health Assessment Using Automated Image Analysis
reason: Primary study applying texture-based computer vision to underwater images of live coral (animals) on wild reefs, collected by an AUV in Barbados and from a public reef data set.

title: An invasive‐native mammalian species replacement process captured by camera trap survey random encounter models
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Camera-trap video of wild hares is identified and measured manually by human observers (Photoshop grid overlay) and fed into random encounter models; no computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Wildlife speed cameras: measuring animal travel speed and day range using camera traps
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Camera-trap study of wild mammals, but movement paths are reconstructed manually in the field with a measuring tape and analysed statistically; no computer vision or image analysis method is applied.

title: A simple method for estimating the effective detection distance of camera traps
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Camera-trap field method for estimating effective detection distance; photographs are annotated manually by an analyst and analysed with distance-sampling statistics. No computer vision or automated image analysis is applied.

title: WiSE - a satellite-based system for remote monitoring
venue: International Journal of Satellite Communications and Networking
reason: System paper on a satellite-backhauled camera-trap platform deployed for wildlife monitoring. Image analysis (image-based motion detection to discard frames without a target) is a small but real part of the system, and the imagery shows wild animals. Borderline with E-NOCV, because no vision method is evaluated quantitatively.

title: Visible and thermal infrared remote sensing for the detection of white‐tailed deer using an unmanned aerial system
reason: UAV visible and thermal imagery of nine white-tailed deer kept in a closed zoo enclosure; no wild or free-ranging animals in the analysed data.

title: Circadian rhythm of salivary cortisol secretion in female zoo-kept African elephants (Loxodonta africana)
reason: Endocrinological study measuring salivary cortisol in zoo elephants by enzyme immunoassay; no image or video analysis.

title: Effects of guest feeding programs on captive giraffe behavior
reason: Live behavioural observation study of zoo giraffes using scan and continuous sampling with statistical analysis; no image or video analysis, and animals are captive only.

title: Feature Extraction as Ellipse of Wild-Life Images
reason: Proposes an image feature extraction method (spots as ellipses) for individual identification of wild ocelots photographed by camera traps in a forest in Michoacan, Mexico.

title: Counting in the Wild
reason: CNN-based counting of wild penguins in images from fixed cameras in Antarctica; also introduces the dataset.

title: A Fully-Automated Zebra Animal Identification Approach Based on SIFT Features
venue: Advances in intelligent systems and computing
reason: Proposes a SIFT-based computer vision method for identifying individual zebras from images collected at a Kenyan conservancy.

title: Coral Reef Fish Detection and Recognition in Underwater Videos by Supervised Machine Learning: Comparison Between Deep Learning and HOG+SVM Methods
reason: Primary study comparing HOG+SVM and a CNN for detecting and recognising free-ranging coral reef fishes in diver-recorded underwater videos.

title: A lure at both ends: aggressive visual mimicry signals and prey-specific luring behaviour in an ambush-foraging snake
reason: Behavioural ecology study of free-ranging puff adders using field video; recordings were reviewed manually by the authors and no computer vision or automated image analysis was applied.

title: Morphological and ecological evidence for two sympatric forms of Type B killer whale around the Antarctic Peninsula
reason: Applies image-based laser photogrammetry (pixel measurements scaled by laser dots) to photographs of wild killer whales to measure body dimensions; primary research.

title: The piggybacking stingray
reason: Short natural-history note reporting photographs of piggybacking stingrays; no computer vision or image analysis is performed.

title: In situ growth rates of deep-water octocorals determined from 3D photogrammetric reconstructions
reason: Primary study applying structure-from-motion photogrammetry to ROV video of wild deep-water octocoral colonies in situ to measure growth rates.

title: Mapping coral reefs using consumer-grade drones and structure from motion photogrammetry techniques
reason: Drone structure-from-motion photogrammetry is used to map the bathymetry and habitat structure of a shallow coral reef lagoon; the output is an orthomosaic and DEM of reef habitat, and no animals are detected, classified or otherwise analysed as subjects.

title: Carnivores’ diversity and conflicts with humans in Musk Deer National Park, Azad Jammu and Kashmir, Pakistan
reason: Camera-trap and questionnaire survey of carnivore diversity and human-carnivore conflict; photos were reviewed without any computer vision or automated image analysis, and statistics are GLMs on questionnaire data.

title: Evaluating camera traps as an alternative to live trapping for estimating the density of snowshoe hares (Lepus americanus) and red squirrels (Tamiasciurus hudsonicus)
reason: Camera-trap videos of wild snowshoe hares and red squirrels were viewed and scored manually; hit rates were related to live-trapping densities by linear regression. No computer vision or automated image analysis is applied.

title: Morphological variations of wild populations of Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) living in extreme environmental conditions in the Kenyan Rift-Valley
reason: Geometric morphometric study of preserved fish specimens; landmarks were digitised by hand in tpsDig and then analysed statistically (PCA, LDA, MANCOVA). No computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Remotely sensing the German Wadden Sea—a new approach to address national and international environmental legislation
reason: Satellite optical and SAR image classification to map wild blue mussel and Pacific oyster beds in the Wadden Sea. Seagrass is also mapped, but part of the analysed data shows wild animals.

title: Baited remote underwater video as a promising nondestructive tool to assess fish assemblages in clearwater Amazonian rivers: testing the effect of bait and habitat type
reason: Baited remote underwater video of wild river fish, but the footage was reviewed manually by one person in VLC; no computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: AntCounter Software: Counting Leaf-Cutting Ants Was never so Precise, fast and Easy
reason: Software using computer vision (frame differencing, tracking) to count free-ranging leaf-cutting ants on a foraging trail of a wild nest recorded in the field.

title: Robust tracking of fish schools using CNN for head identification
reason: Tracking of zebrafish schools filmed in a laboratory acrylic water tank; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Automatic identification of cattle using muzzle point pattern: a hybrid feature extraction and classification paradigm
reason: Individual identification of domestic cattle from muzzle images taken at a university dairy/animal husbandry department; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Robust Statistical Frontalization of Human and Animal Faces
reason: Generic face frontalization and landmark localization method evaluated mainly on human face databases; the only animal data are pet cat photographs from Flickr, with no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Behavior Discovery and Alignment of Articulated Object Classes from Unstructured Video
reason: Computer vision method (behavior discovery and spatial alignment) on animal video: tigers from documentaries plus domestic horses and dogs from YouTube. Borderline: the paper is framed around generic articulated object classes and never states whether the tigers are wild or captive.

title: Automated Visual Fin Identification of Individual Great White Sharks
reason: Proposes a computer vision photo-ID system that detects dorsal fins and identifies individual great white sharks in unconstrained natural imagery used by white shark researchers.

title: A newt does not change its spots: using pattern mapping for the identification of individuals in large populations of newt species
reason: Primary study applying computer-assisted pattern recognition software (Wild-ID) to photographs of wild-caught newts from a natural breeding pond for individual identification.

title: Random bounce algorithm: real-time image processing for the detection of bats and birds
reason: Proposes a real-time image processing algorithm for detecting bats and birds; evaluated on captive bats in a laboratory flight tunnel and on free-flying wild birds at an onshore wind energy plant.

title: Development and experimental testing of an autonomous jellyfish detection and removal robot system
venue: International Journal of Control Automation and Systems
reason: Primary study that develops and tests a vision-based detection algorithm on video of free-floating wild jellyfish (Aurelia aurita) at the sea surface, as part of a jellyfish removal robot.

title: Vertical distribution of giant jellyfish, Nemopilema nomurai using acoustics and optics
reason: Wild giant jellyfish are surveyed with visual counting, trawls, acoustics and a towed underwater camera. Jellyfish in the video are counted, but the paper describes no computer vision or automated image analysis method.

title: Toward an Automated Identification of Anastrepha Fruit Flies in the fraterculus group (Diptera, Tephritidae)
reason: Images are microscope photographs of dissected wings and aculei of preserved fruit fly specimens mounted on slides; no images of live free-ranging animals.

title: Does enrichment improve reptile welfare? Leopard geckos (Eublepharis macularius) respond to five types of environmental enrichment
reason: Behavioural welfare study of captive laboratory leopard geckos. The videos were coded manually by human observers in Observer XT and analysed with statistics only, so no computer vision method is used. The animals are also housed in a vivarium, not wild.

title: Associations and the role of affiliative, agonistic, and socio-sexual behaviors among common bottlenose dolphins (Tursiops truncatus)
reason: Behavioural study of dolphins kept in a sea pen. Researchers watched and coded the underwater video by hand, and the analysis is statistical (ANOVA/MANOVA). No computer vision is used, and the animals are captive.

title: Tarangire revisited: Consequences of declining connectivity in a tropical ungulate population
reason: Applies computer-assisted photographic identification (SIFT-based pattern matching) to field photos of wild wildebeest to identify individuals for capture-mark-recapture abundance estimation.

title: How Wasps Acquire and Use Views for Homing
reason: Primary study filming free-ranging ground-nesting wasps at field colonies with synchronized high-speed cameras and extracting 3D head position and gaze from the video via stereo triangulation.

title: Mechanical Constraints on Flight at High Elevation Decrease Maneuvering Performance of Hummingbirds
reason: Wild-caught Anna's hummingbirds were filmed only inside flight chambers under experimental conditions (translocation and gas substitution); no images of free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Biometric assessment of deep-sea vent megabenthic communities using multi-resolution 3D image reconstructions
venue: Deep Sea Research Part I Oceanographic Research Papers
reason: Stereo imagery of wild deep-sea vent megabenthos is processed with a visual SLAM stereo pipeline into 3D colour reconstructions used to map animal distribution and biomass. Animal labels were made manually by an expert, so the computer vision component is the 3D reconstruction only.

title: Seabird image identification in natural scenes using Grabcut and combined features
reason: Proposes a segmentation and classification method for images of wild seabirds taken in natural scenes.

title: AnimalFinder: A semi-automated system for animal detection in time-lapse camera trap images
reason: Develops an image-processing system to detect wild deer, wild pigs and raccoons in time-lapse camera trap images from a field survey.

title: Semi-automated classification method addressing marine strategy framework directive (MSFD) zooplankton indicators
reason: Wild Baltic zooplankton were caught with nets, preserved in formaldehyde, stained and scanned in the laboratory. The images show preserved specimens in a lab set-up, not free-ranging animals in situ.

title: MapReduce-based fast fuzzy c-means algorithm for large-scale underwater image segmentation
reason: Proposes a parallel fuzzy c-means segmentation method and applies it to underwater images of fish in seawater (fish4knowledge), with the goal of segmenting fish from the background.

title: The use of underwater hyperspectral imaging deployed on remotely operated vehicles - methods and applications
reason: Underwater hyperspectral imaging from ROV used to classify and map seafloor objects of interest, including wild benthic animals such as corals, sponges, sea stars, anemones and sea urchins, in field surveys.

title: Interactive technology and human–animal encounters at the zoo
reason: HCI case study of interactive systems (iPads, signs) at Melbourne Zoo using interviews, observations and documents; no computer vision or image analysis, and animals are captive zoo animals.

title: Benchmarking of data fusion algorithms in support of earth observation based Antarctic wildlife monitoring
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
reason: The paper benchmarks image fusion (pansharpening) algorithms on very-high-resolution satellite images of wild Antarctic penguin colonies (guano) and seals, to support wildlife monitoring.

title: Photographic identification method (PIM) using natural body marks: A simple tool to make a long story short
reason: Photo-identification of individual wild salamanders and stag beetles captured in the field; includes evaluation of an automated image-matching tool (Wild-ID, SIFT) on salamander photos.

title: Evaluating the effect of soak time on bottomfish abundance and length data from stereo-video surveys
venue: Journal of Experimental Marine Biology and Ecology
reason: Baited stereo-video of wild bottomfish in Hawaii, but human analysts annotated the video by hand (MaxN counts, fork lengths with stereo-photogrammetric software). No computer vision method is developed or evaluated; the study tests how camera soak time affects survey statistics.

title: Quantifying the degree of coral bleaching using digital photographic technique
venue: Journal of Experimental Marine Biology and Ecology
reason: Develops an image analysis method (grey-scale intensity calibration) to quantify bleaching in wild coral colonies photographed in situ in Hong Kong.

title: Using minimally invasive techniques to determine green sea turtle Chelonia mydas life-history parameters
venue: Journal of Experimental Marine Biology and Ecology
reason: Photo-ID of free-ranging green turtles from underwater photographs, using I3S Pattern matching software, plus laser photogrammetry measurement from images.

title: Image processing based method to assess fish quality and freshness
reason: Assesses post-harvest freshness of pond-raised Rohu fish for food quality; aquaculture/food production, not wild animals.

title: Investigating the spatial distribution of growth anomalies affecting Montipora capitata corals in a 3-dimensional framework
reason: Applies structure-from-motion 3D reconstruction to underwater photographs of wild Montipora capitata coral colonies on a reef to map where disease lesions are.

title: Development and validation of a video analysis software for marine benthic applications
reason: Video analysis software validated on in situ ROV video of wild deep-water corals plus laboratory videos of a mud shrimp and polychaete worms; image analysis of animals.

title: High frequency mesozooplankton monitoring: Can imaging systems and automated sample analysis help us describe and interpret changes in zooplankton community composition and size structure — An example from a coastal site
reason: Applies image analysis (Zooscan imaging, segmentation, Random Forest classification) to net-collected wild marine zooplankton from a coastal time series.

title: Effects of environmental variables on surface temperature of breeding adult female northern elephant seals, Mirounga angustirostris, and pups
reason: Infrared thermograms of wild breeding northern elephant seals are analysed pixel-wise to measure surface temperature. Thermal windows are segmented with a threshold, which counts as image analysis of free-ranging animals.

title: Underwater image processing method for fish localization and detection in submarine environment
venue: Journal of Visual Communication and Image Representation
reason: Proposes an image processing method (denoising, segmentation, likelihood ratio test) to detect fish in underwater AUV video recorded in the Baltic Sea.

title: Responses of ghost crabs to habitat modification of urban sandy beaches
reason: Ecological field study of ghost crab burrow densities on urban beaches. Burrows were counted and measured manually in quadrats; the only image analysis is ImageJ thresholding of photographs to estimate percent cover of wrack (washed-up organic material), so no animals or animal signs are analysed in images.

title: A computer vision approach for monitoring the spatial and temporal shrimp distribution at the LoVe observatory
reason: Computer vision detection of wild shrimp in their natural cold-water coral reef habitat, using images from a fixed underwater observatory.

title: The LOKI underwater imaging system and an automatic identification model for the detection of zooplankton taxa in the Arctic Ocean
reason: Develops an automatic classification model for in-situ images of wild zooplankton taken by the LOKI underwater imaging system in the Canadian Arctic.

title: Imperfect automatic image classification successfully describes plankton distribution patterns
reason: Primary study applying automatic image classification (ZooProcess/PkID Random Forest with probability filtering) to in situ towed-camera images of free-living marine plankton, including zooplankton and fish larvae.

title: Combining imperfect automated annotations of underwater images with human annotations to obtain precise and unbiased population estimates
reason: Develops statistical estimators combining automated computer-vision detections of wild sea scallops in underwater HabCam survey images with manual annotations to estimate population size.

title: Automated measurements of fish within a trawl using stereo images from a Camera-Trawl device (CamTrawl)
reason: Automated image-based measurement of wild walleye pollock captured passing through a midwater trawl during a fisheries survey using stereo cameras.

title: Sensorimotor Transformations Underlying Variability in Song Intensity during Drosophila Courtship
reason: Neuroscience study of courtship song in laboratory Drosophila strains (genetically manipulated, tethered or in a behavioural chamber); video fly tracking is only a supporting measurement and no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Wildlife recognition in nature documentaries with weak supervision from subtitles and external data
reason: Primary study proposing a weakly supervised multi-label classification method to recognise animals in key frames of a BBC wildlife documentary showing animals in their natural habitat.

title: Diversity, distribution and population size structure of deep Mediterranean gorgonian assemblages (Menorca Channel, Western Mediterranean Sea)
reason: Ecological study of wild deep-sea gorgonians using manual annotation of ROV/submersible video; no computer vision or automated image analysis method is developed or applied.

title: The Effect of Sunglint on Benthic Habitats Mapping in Pari Island Using Worldview-2 Imagery
reason: Satellite-based benthic habitat (substrate/land cover) mapping with sunglint correction; classes are habitat types (live coral, seagrass, sand, rubble), not animals as subjects.

title: On the (virtual) getting of wisdom: Immersive 3D interfaces for eliciting spatial information from experts
reason: Pilot study of immersive 3D virtual-reality interfaces for eliciting expert knowledge on rock wallaby habitat suitability; expert responses are analysed with a linear mixed effects model. No computer vision method is applied to images or video of animals.

title: Population size, distribution and status of the remote and Critically Endangered Bawean deer Axis kuhlii
reason: Camera-trap and faecal pellet survey estimating density of wild Bawean deer with a random encounter model; photographs and videos are reviewed manually and no computer vision or image analysis method is used.

title: Computers on the reef
reason: Journalistic news feature (Nature Toolbox) describing other groups' tools for analysing coral-reef images; it is not primary research and analyses no data itself.

title: In situ imaging reveals the biomass of giant protists in the global ocean
reason: In situ underwater images of free-living plankton are extracted, measured and classified with computer-assisted image analysis (ZooProcess) to estimate abundance and biomass. The focal taxa are Rhizaria, which are protists rather than animals, but wild zooplankton animals (copepods, jellyfish, fish larvae and others) are also imaged, classified and counted, so inclusion is a borderline call.

title: Camouflage predicts survival in ground-nesting birds
reason: Calibrated digital image analysis (luminance, Fourier pattern and colour metrics) of in situ photographs of wild ground-nesting birds and their eggs in Zambia, used to quantify camouflage and relate it to clutch survival.

title: Precision wildlife monitoring using unmanned aerial vehicles
reason: UAV images of wild seabird colonies were counted manually by human counters in Photoshop; no computer vision or automated image analysis method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Improving Automated Annotation of Benthic Survey Images Using Wide-band Fluorescence
reason: CNN-based automated classification of in situ reef survey images of wild corals and hydrozoans (animals) captured during a field deployment; primary research.

title: Perceptual Modalities Guiding Bat Flight in a Native Habitat
reason: Primary field study that applies multi-camera thermal video detection, 3D reconstruction and tracking to free-flying wild bats emerging from a roost.

title: Observations of movement dynamics of flying insects using high resolution lidar
reason: Field study of wild flying insects with a Scheimpflug lidar; the data are one-dimensional backscatter time series analysed by signal processing (wing-beat frequency, optical cross section), not image or video analysis.

title: MATSAP: An automated analysis of stretch-attend posture in rodent behavioral experiments
reason: Software for automated scoring of stretch-attend posture in laboratory mice filmed in open field and elevated plus maze tests; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Social context affects tail displays by Phrynocephalus vlangalii lizards from China
reason: Behavioural ecology study of wild lizards filmed in the field; tail points were located frame by frame in Matlab and reconstructed in 3D with direct linear transformation, with no automated computer vision method described.

title: Accurate Segmentation for Infrared Flying Bird Tracking
reason: Proposes a segmentation-based tracking method for free-flying birds in infrared video collected by an airport-oriented bird surveillance system in real-world situations.

title: Daily Evolution of the Insect Biomass Spectrum in an Agricultural Landscape Accessed with Lidar
reason: Entomological lidar study: insect events are found by signal thresholding on range-time lidar returns from a linear detector array and converted to optical cross sections; no image or video analysis of animals is performed.

title: Exploitation of Multi-Band Lidar for the Classification of Free-Flying Migratory Birds: A Pilot Study Over Athens, Greece
reason: Multi-band lidar remote sensing of free-flying wild migratory birds; detection of bird events in lidar time-range data and spectral analysis toward species classification.

title: How chimpanzees cooperate in a competitive world
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
reason: Behavioural study of captive chimpanzees at a primate research centre. Human raters coded the videos by hand and no computer vision or automated image analysis was used. The animals are also captive.

title: Photogrammetry using in‐field calibration: a non‐invasive tool for predicting sex and life stages tested on Hector's dolphins in the wild
venue: New Zealand Journal of Marine and Freshwater Research
reason: Develops and validates a stereophotogrammetry method (image-based measurement) applied to photographs of wild Hector's dolphins in Akaroa Harbour.

title: Hybrid deep learning for automated lepidopteran insect image classification
reason: Classification of lepidopteran species from photographs of pinned museum/collection specimens, not live wild animals.

title: Observational Learning in Capuchin Monkeys: A Video Deficit Effect
reason: Behavioural psychology experiment showing video demonstrations to captive capuchin monkeys; no computer vision or automated image analysis is performed.

title: Corals & benthic habitat mapping using DubaiSat-2: a spectral-spatial approach applied to Dalma Island, UAE (Arabian Gulf)
reason: Satellite-based benthic habitat mapping where coral reef is one habitat/land-cover class (fringing reef, seabed, macroalgae, deep sea). The subject is habitat mapping, not animals as individuals or their signs.

title: Brood Parasitism Is Linked to Egg Pattern Diversity within and among Species of Australian Passerines
reason: Image pattern analysis is applied to photographs of museum egg specimens from the Australian National Wildlife Collection, not to images of free-ranging animals; museum specimens fall under E-CAPTIVE.

title: Combining Human Computing and Machine Learning to Make Sense of Big (Aerial) Data for Disaster Response
reason: Although labelled a perspective, the paper reports its own pilot experiments: crowdsourced annotation plus machine-learning classifiers to detect wild animals in aerial images of a Namibian wildlife reserve.

title: zWEDGI: Wounding and Entrapment Device for Imaging Live Zebrafish Larvae
reason: Laboratory microscopy study of zebrafish larvae in an immobilisation device for wound-healing imaging; no wild animals and no computer vision method beyond manual measurement and image registration in FIJI.

title: Temperature modifies activity, inter-individual relationships and group structure in fish
reason: Hatchery-reared brown trout fry filmed in a laboratory arena; behaviour was scored manually with ImageJ and The Observer software, with no wild animals and essentially no automated computer vision.

title: Application of a predator–prey overlap metric to determine the impact of sub-grid scale feeding dynamics on ecosystem productivity
reason: Ecological modelling study computing a predator-prey overlap metric. The image analysis is done on figures taken from published papers. ISIIS plankton images give abundances, but the paper describes no computer vision method for analysing them.

title: Fish identification from videos captured in uncontrolled underwater environments
reason: Image set classification method for identifying species of free-swimming fish in underwater videos from unconstrained natural environments.

title: The combined effects of reduced pH and elevated temperature on the shell density of two gastropod species measured using micro-CT imaging
reason: Laboratory ocean-acidification experiment on gastropods kept in controlled tanks; shells of frozen specimens were scanned by micro-CT and analysed by grey-value thresholding. No images of wild, free-ranging animals.

title: Debunking the viper's strike: harmless snakes kill a common assumption
reason: Biomechanics study of snake strike performance in a laboratory arena; high-speed videos were digitized with Tracker software to obtain kinematics, with no computer vision method developed, applied or evaluated, and no wild free-ranging animals in the data.

title: Rules to fly by: pigeons navigating horizontal obstacles limit steering by selecting gaps most aligned to their flight direction
reason: Wild-caught pigeons were housed and filmed in an indoor laboratory flight corridor. Their 3D flight kinematics were reconstructed from LED markers tracked in high-speed cameras, so this is a laboratory set-up, not free-ranging animals.

title: A novel video-tracking system to quantify the behaviour of nocturnal mosquitoes attacking human hosts in the field
venue: Journal of The Royal Society Interface
reason: Computer vision video-tracking of mosquitoes, including wild-collected Culex populations tracked in a field hut in Tanzania, alongside laboratory colony mosquitoes.

title: Hummingbirds control turning velocity using body orientation and turning radius using asymmetrical wingbeat kinematics
venue: Journal of The Royal Society Interface
reason: Biomechanics study of wild-caught hummingbirds housed in a vivarium and filmed in an acrylic flight chamber; kinematics come from digitized marker points in a laboratory set-up, not from wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Using collision cones to assess biological deconfliction methods
venue: Journal of The Royal Society Interface
reason: Multi-camera video of wild emerging bats and free-flying cliff swallows (plus fish in a laboratory tank) was tracked and reconstructed into 3D trajectories, which are then compared with a collision avoidance algorithm.

title: Error and bias in size estimates of whale sharks: implications for understanding demography
reason: Applies stereo-video photogrammetry, plus photo-identification matching with I3S, to measure free-swimming wild whale sharks at Ningaloo Reef.

title: Atypical residency of short-beaked common dolphins (Delphinus delphis) to a shallow, urbanized embayment in south-eastern Australia
reason: Ecological residency study of wild common dolphins using manual photo-identification of dorsal fins by human observers; no computer vision or automated image analysis is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Zebrafish response to a robotic replica in three dimensions
reason: Laboratory behavioural experiment on purchased zebrafish in an experimental tank with a robotic replica; video tracking is used, but no wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Fine-scale flight strategies of gulls in urban airflows indicate risk and reward in city living
venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences
reason: Wild gull flight tracks were recorded with a laser-rangefinder Ornithodolite and by observer counts, then analysed with CFD and statistical models. The paper does no image or video analysis.

title: I 3 S Classic and Insect Species Identification of Diptera and Hymenoptera (Mosquitoes and Bees)
reason: Species identification from landmark points marked on photographs of dissected wings of dead mosquito and bee specimens under a microscope; no images of live free-ranging animals (specimens only, some laboratory reared or from maintained colonies).

title: Autonomous UAVs wildlife detection using thermal imaging, predictive navigation and computer vision
reason: UAV thermal detection system intended for wildlife, but the only animal data analysed is a single domestic dog used as a test target; no images of wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Machine vision algorithms for robust animal species identification
venue: 2015 IEEE Applied Imagery Pattern Recognition Workshop Aipr 2015
reason: Primary study developing cascade classifiers and a neural network to detect free-ranging squirrels in outdoor video for endangered-species census on military bases.

title: Multi-vehicle autonomous tracking and filming of white sharks Carcharodon carcharias
reason: AUVs track tagged wild white sharks with acoustic USBL tracking and film them. People watched the video by eye. No computer vision or automated image analysis is developed or applied.

title: 3D tracking swimming fish school using a master view tracking first strategy
venue: IEEE International Conference on Bioinformatics and Biomedicine (BIBM)
reason: 3D tracking of zebrafish schools filmed in a container with a calibrated three-camera laboratory set-up; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Recognition and classification of animals based on texture features through parallel computing
venue: International Conference on Cognitive Computing and Information Processing
reason: Image-based classification of 30 animal classes, including wild species such as zebra, using texture features. Primary method paper; the image source is not stated.

title: Multi-target tracking of Zebrafish based on particle filter
reason: Multi-target tracking of zebrafish, a laboratory model organism, filmed in a water tank; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: A Proposed Multithreading Fuzzy C-Mean Algorithm for Detecting Underwater Fishes
venue: International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Networks (CINE)
reason: Proposes a computer vision method (fuzzy c-means with optical flow) to detect and track fish in underwater video. The fish are not stated to be captive, and the paper presents the setting as unconstrained underwater.

title: Fish recognition from low-resolution underwater images
venue: International Congress on Image and Signal Processing, BioMedical Engineering and Informatics (CISP-BMEI)
reason: Proposes a super-resolution plus deep-feature framework for classifying fish species in underwater videos of fish in their natural environment (FishCLEF 2015).

title: Subsea fauna enumeration using vision-based marine robots
venue: Proceedings 2016 13th Conference on Computer and Robot Vision Crv 2016
reason: Applies computer vision (Gabor/colour features + SVM) to AUV seafloor imagery to detect and count wild benthic crustaceans.

title: KinectScenes: Robust real-time RGB-D fusion for animal behavioural monitoring
venue: Proceedings 2016 13th Conference on Computer and Robot Vision Crv 2016
reason: The paper presents a method for RGB-D 3D scene reconstruction (fusing Kinect point clouds). The only animal data is a horse RGB-D dataset, and horses are domestic animals. No wild animals are analysed.

title: Polyp Activity Estimation and Monitoring for Cold Water Corals with a Deep Learning Approach
reason: CNN-based classification of polyp activity in in-situ photos of a wild cold-water coral reef (Lophelia pertusa) recorded by a fixed underwater observatory; primary research.

title: Closed-Loop Tracking-by-Detection for ROV-Based Multiple Fish Tracking
reason: Primary method paper that detects, tracks and counts live fish in real-world underwater ROV videos for fish abundance estimation.

title: Data-Driven Long Term Change Analysis in Marine Observatory Image Streams
reason: Proposes an unsupervised computer vision method to detect long-term changes in image streams from a fixed underwater observatory on a wild cold-water coral reef. The changes are linked to corals (Lophelia pertusa) and sponges.

title: Adaptive Foreground Extraction for Deep Fish Classification
reason: Primary method paper performing background estimation and CNN-based fish classification on streaming underwater video from an unconstrained real-world marine environment.

title: Live Tracking of Rail-Based Fish Catching on Wild Sea Surface
reason: Computer vision method (background subtraction, trajectory tracking, CRF segmentation) to track wild fish caught on a fishing rail at sea for fishery monitoring.

title: Shrinking Encoding with Two-Level Codebook Learning for Fine-Grained Fish Recognition
reason: Proposes a bag-of-features codebook learning method for fine-grained species recognition of fish imaged in a mid-water trawl camera system (Cam-trawl) and a chute multi-spectral dataset; the Cam-trawl data shows wild fish passing through the trawl.

title: Data Enrichment in Fine-Grained Classification of Aquatic Macroinvertebrates
reason: Collected, preserved macroinvertebrate specimens are imaged in a laboratory test-tube set-up; no images show wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Plankton Image Classification Based on Multiple Segmentations
reason: Classical computer vision pipeline (segmentation, feature extraction, SVM) classifying plankton targets cropped from videos collected in situ at coastal locations in Brazil and Uruguay.

title: Detecting Migrating Birds at Night
venue: IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings - IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings
reason: Primary study proposing a stereo-vision method to detect wild migrating birds in flight in night-sky videos.

title: Learning Deep Features for Discriminative Localization
venue: IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings - IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings
reason: Generic vision paper proposing class activation mapping for weakly supervised localization on general benchmarks (ILSVRC, scene and object datasets). Animals appear only as benchmark classes (e.g. CUB-200-2011 birds); wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Distinguishing Weather Phenomena from Bird Migration Patterns in Radar Imagery
venue: IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops
reason: CNN and Fisher Vector image classification applied to rendered weather radar scans to screen out precipitation so that migrating wild birds can be studied; the images show free-ranging migrating birds, although the classified label is rain versus no rain.

title: ReSeg: A Recurrent Neural Network-Based Model for Semantic Segmentation
venue: IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)
reason: Generic semantic segmentation architecture (ReSeg) evaluated on general benchmarks (Weizmann Horse, Oxford Flowers, CamVid); horses appear only as a benchmark foreground class and wildlife is not the subject or application.

title: Exploiting Temporal Information for DCNN-Based Fine-Grained Object Classification
venue: International Conference on Digital Image Computing: Techniques and Applications (DICTA)
reason: Proposes video-based fine-grained classification of 100 bird species, using a new video dataset of birds recorded by expert bird watchers, and evaluates DCNN methods on it.

title: Kangaroo Vehicle Collision Detection Using Deep Semantic Segmentation Convolutional Neural Network
venue: International Conference on Digital Image Computing: Techniques and Applications (DICTA)
reason: Computer vision method (semantic segmentation CNN) for detecting kangaroos, a wild species, to prevent vehicle collisions. Training and test data are synthetic depth images of animated kangaroo models in road scenes.

title: Accurate wild animal recognition using PCA, LDA and LBPH
