title: Segmentasi Citra Ikan Tuna dengan Mahalanobis Histogram Thresholding dan Mahalanobis Fuzzy C-Means
reason: Segments images of harvested tuna for classification in the fish processing/production industry; the animals are not free-ranging wild animals in their habitat.

title: Automatic optical tracking of a flying bird
venue: Kashika Jouhou Gakkai rombunshuu gappon/Kashika Jouhou Gakkai rombun gapponshuu/Kashika Jouhou Gakkai rombunshuu
reason: Develops a real-time image-processing optical tracking system and applies it to video of wild birds flying near Haneda Airport.

title: Photo-ID as a tool for studying and monitoring the endangered Saimaa ringed seal
reason: Camera-trap and DSLR photo-ID study of wild Saimaa ringed seals in which individuals were matched entirely by hand; no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Enhanced pelagic biomass around coral atolls
reason: The study analyses 38 kHz echosounder acoustic backscatter of mid-water fauna with regression models; no image or video computer vision is used.

title: Use of mangroves by fish: new insights from in‑forest videos
reason: Ecological study of fish use of mangroves from underwater video; fish were identified manually by two researchers viewing the videos, with no computer vision or automated image analysis.

title: Improving the estimation of deep-sea megabenthos biomass: dimension to wet weight conversions for abyssal invertebrates
reason: The paper builds conversions from body size to wet weight using trawl-caught museum specimens. People identified and measured the animals in the seabed photographs by hand (methods in Morris et al. 2014), and no computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Comparison of image annotation data generated by multiple investigators for benthic ecology
reason: The study compares manual annotations of seabed photographs made by three human investigators; no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to investigate shark and ray densities in a shallow coral lagoon
reason: UAV video of wild sharks and rays was counted manually by two human observers; no computer vision or automated image analysis was applied.

title: Hydrodynamic Performance of Aquatic Flapping: Efficiency of Underwater Flight in the Manta
reason: Biomechanics/CFD study of manta swimming. Videos of aquarium mantas were digitized by hand, frame by frame, to get kinematics, so no automated computer vision method is developed or evaluated. A wild manta video appears only as an illustration.

title: Sensor Fusion and Autonomy as a Powerful Combination for Biological Assessment in the Marine Environment
reason: The study uses only acoustic data from dual-frequency echosounders on an AUV to detect squid. No optical image or video data is analysed.

title: Development of a Regional Coral Observation Method by a Fluorescence Imaging LIDAR Installed in a Towable Buoy
reason: The paper develops a fluorescence imaging LIDAR in a towed buoy to observe wild reef corals. A data analyst classified the images by eye, so no computer vision or automated image analysis is applied.

title: Spectral Reflectance of Polar Bear and Other Large Arctic Mammal Pelts; Potential Applications to Remote Sensing Surveys
reason: Point spectroradiometer reflectance measurements of museum pelts; no image or video analysis and no computer vision method is applied. Satellite band responses are simulated from spectra, not from imagery.

title: An Object-Based Image Analysis Approach for Detecting Penguin Guano in very High Spatial Resolution Satellite Images
reason: Primary study applying object-based image analysis to satellite imagery to detect guano stains, a direct sign of wild Adélie and chinstrap penguin breeding colonies in Antarctica.

title: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) and Artificial Intelligence Revolutionizing Wildlife Monitoring and Conservation
reason: UAV thermal detection, tracking and counting pipeline validated only on koalas held in a rehabilitation enclosure with a known number of animals; no wild free-ranging animals in the analysed validation data.

title: High Resolution Trichromatic Road Surface Scanning with a Line Scan Camera and Light Emitting Diode Lighting for Road-Kill Detection
reason: Develops a trailer-mounted road-scanning imaging system and early computer vision detectors (Haar classifier, SIFT) for wild amphibian road-kills, which are direct signs of free-ranging animals. Testing used 3D-printed models and pictures of amphibian casualties.

title: Looking inside the Ocean: Toward an Autonomous Imaging System for Monitoring Gelatinous Zooplankton
reason: Primary study presenting an underwater imaging system and image recognition methods for wild gelatinous zooplankton, recorded in situ in the Ligurian Sea.

title: A note on captive breeding and reproductive parameters of the Chinese pangolin, Manis pentadactyla Linnaeus, 1758
reason: A captive-breeding observation report on Chinese pangolins (gestation, morphology, weight records). It uses no image analysis or computer vision, and the animals were housed in a captive facility.

title: Animal Classification System Based on Image Processing & Support Vector Machine
reason: Primary study that classifies tiger, dog and cat images with MPEG-7 descriptors and an SVM, for a stated wildlife photography and research application. The paper does not say where the images come from or whether the animals are wild, so inclusion rests on the stated wildlife purpose and the non-domestic tiger class.

title: Comparison of Three Techniques to Identify and Count Individual Animals in Aerial Imagery
venue: Journal of Signal and Information Processing
reason: The analysed aerial imagery shows only domestic cattle and horses in fenced pastures, used as a proof of concept; no wild or free-ranging animals are in the data.

title: Towards Automatic Wild Animal Monitoring: Identification of Animal Species in Camera-trap Images using Very Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
reason: Primary study applying very deep CNNs to classify wild animal species in camera-trap images from Serengeti National Park and a second camera-trap dataset.

title: Right whale recognition using convolutional neural networks
reason: Primary study applying CNNs and kNN to images of free-ranging North Atlantic right whales to recognise individuals.

title: 3D Menagerie: Modeling the 3D shape and pose of animals
reason: Proposes a 3D articulated shape model of quadrupeds (learned from toy scans) and fits it to real images of animals, including wild species such as tigers, lions, cheetahs, zebras and hippos, alongside domestic ones.

title: Rapid Population Estimate of a Surface-nesting Seabird on a Remote Island Using a Low-cost Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
reason: UAV photographs of wild albatrosses were examined and counted manually by a person; no computer vision or automated image analysis method is developed or applied.

title: The burying and grazing effects of plateau pika on alpine grassland are small: a pilot study in a semiarid basin on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau
reason: The automated image analysis segments vegetation and bald patches with an excess green threshold. The pika piles were marked by hand on the aerial photos, so no computer vision was applied to the animals or their signs.

title: POLLEN BEARING HONEY BEE DETECTION IN HIVE ENTRANCE VIDEO RECORDED BY REMOTE EMBEDDED SYSTEM FOR POLLINATION MONITORING
venue: ISPRS annals of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences
reason: Computer vision on managed honey bees at a hive entrance in an apiary (beekeeping); no wild, free-ranging non-domestic animals.

title: AUTOMATIC SEA BIRD DETECTION FROM HIGH RESOLUTION AERIAL IMAGERY
venue: The international archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences/International archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences
reason: Image processing method (MSER + graph cuts + feature thresholding) for detecting wild sea birds in aerial survey imagery of the Baltic Sea.

title: MONITORING SEABIRDS AND MARINE MAMMALS BY GEOREFERENCED AERIAL PHOTOGRAPHY
venue: The international archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences/International archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences
reason: Aerial digital imagery of wild seabirds and marine mammals, but people find and identify the animals by eye with software support. No computer vision method is developed or applied; automated recognition is only named as future work.

title: Towards a Tracking Algorithm based on the Clustering of Spatio-temporal Clouds of Points
reason: Proposes a 3D multi-camera tracking algorithm for collective animal behaviour. It is tested on semi-natural images made from real field trajectories of midge swarms.

title: Fine-grained Recognition in the Noisy Wild: Sensitivity Analysis of Convolutional Neural Networks Approaches
reason: Generic sensitivity analysis of CNN architectures under simulated noise and transformations, using fine-grained benchmarks (CUB-200-2011, Oxford Flowers, Oxford Pets) only to test a general method; wildlife is not the stated subject.

title: Improving the accuracy of Multispectral-based benthic habitats mapping using image rotations: the application of Principle Component Analysis and Independent Component Analysis
reason: Satellite multispectral per-pixel mapping of benthic habitat cover classes (coral reefs, seagrass, macro algae, bare substratum); habitat/land-cover mapping rather than analysis of animals.

title: Using ORB, BoW and SVM to identify and track tagged Norway lobster Nephrops norvegicus (L.)
reason: Norway lobsters were recorded in a laboratory fiberglass tank experiment. No free-ranging animals were imaged.

title: Chimp&See: an online citizen science platform for large-scale, remote video camera trap annotation of chimpanzee behaviour, demography and individual identification
reason: Poster abstract on camera trap videos of wild chimpanzees annotated by citizen scientists, with a comparison against automated facial detection software and expert annotators.

title: Automated annotation of corals in natural scene images using multiple texture representations
reason: Automated classification of corals and benthic organisms in natural underwater images from the Great Barrier Reef using texture features and SVM fusion.

title: Automated annotation of corals in natural scene images using multiple texture representations
reason: Primary study proposing a computer vision method (multi-feature SVM fusion) to classify corals and other benthic organisms in underwater photographs taken on the Great Barrier Reef; corals and sponges are wild animals in situ.

title: Sebastes stereo image analysis software.
reason: Software report describing stereo-image triangulation tools for measuring, ranging and counting wild fish in underwater camera surveys; computer vision (stereo calibration and 3D triangulation) is applied to images of free-ranging fish.

title: Postprandial sleep mechanics in Drosophila
reason: Laboratory study of sleep and feeding in Drosophila strains housed in a custom behavioural chamber; machine vision tracking is used only as a measurement tool on laboratory animals, with no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Fully-automated identification of fish species based on otolith contour: using short-time Fourier transform and discriminant analysis (STFT-DA)
reason: Images are stereomicroscope photographs of otoliths extracted from dead fish bought at landing sites or wet markets. This is laboratory microscopy of specimens, not imagery of free-ranging animals.

title: Characterizing abnormal behavior in a large population of zoo-housed chimpanzees: prevalence and potential influencing factors
reason: Staff questionnaire survey on abnormal behaviour of zoo-housed chimpanzees, analysed with logistic regression; there is no image or video analysis, and all animals are captive.

title: Assessing the use of a camera system within an autonomous underwater vehicle for monitoring the distribution and density of sea scallops (Placopecten magellanicus) in the Mid-Atlantic Bight
reason: AUV seafloor photographs of wild sea scallops were counted and sized manually by trained annotators with a pixel-measuring tool; no automated computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Zooplankton community response to the winter 2013 deep convection process in the NW M editerranean S ea
reason: Applies image-based automatic classification and counting (ZooScan/ZooProcess/Plankton Identifier, UVP/EcoTaxa) to wild marine zooplankton sampled in the NW Mediterranean.

title: Automated face detection for occurrence and occupancy estimation in chimpanzees
reason: Evaluates automated chimpanzee face detection software on camera trap videos of unhabituated wild chimpanzees in Uganda and Liberia for occurrence and occupancy estimation.

title: Body growth and life history in wild mountain gorillas (Gorilla beringei beringei) from Volcanoes National Park, Rwanda
reason: Applies image-based parallel laser photogrammetry to photographs of wild, habituated mountain gorillas to measure body dimensions and model growth.

title: Comparative Three‐Dimensional Morphology of Baleen: Cross‐Sectional Profiles and Volume Measurements Using CT Images
reason: CT image analysis of baleen from museum specimens and dead stranded whales; no free-ranging animals are imaged, and museum specimens fall under E-CAPTIVE.

title: Unmanned aerial vehicles for surveying marine fauna: assessing detection probability
reason: UAV images and video of wild humpback whales were reviewed manually by a human observer; no computer vision method is applied to animal imagery (the only automated image analysis measures sun glitter), and the analysis is statistical estimation of detection probability and availability.

title: Flight performance in the altricial zebra finch: Developmental effects and reproductive consequences
reason: Captive zebra finches from pet stores housed in a lab colony. Their flight was filmed with a high-speed camera in laboratory trials, and the video was digitised with DLTdv5. No wild or free-ranging animals appear.

title: Comparison of photo‐matching algorithms commonly used for photographic capture–recapture studies
reason: Primary study comparing four photo-matching (individual identification) algorithms on image databases of wild amphibians captured in capture-recapture field studies.

title: Time‐lapse camera trapping as an alternative to pitfall trapping for estimating activity of leaf litter arthropods
reason: Time-lapse camera-trap photographs of wild leaf litter arthropods were identified and counted manually by the authors; no computer vision or automated image analysis method is used.

title: Field swimming performance of bluegill sunfish, Lepomis macrochirus: implications for field activity cost estimates and laboratory measures of swimming performance
reason: Biomechanics study of wild bluegill filmed in a lake. Fish positions were digitised by hand (landmark estimated visually) and behaviour was categorised manually; the only computational image steps are stereo camera calibration and DLT triangulation, so no automated computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: The little things that run: a general scaling of invertebrate exploratory speed with body mass
reason: Wild-collected forest-litter invertebrates were filmed individually in glass arenas inside a laboratory environmental chamber; no images of free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Strike kinematics and performance in juvenile ball pythons (Python regius)
venue: Journal of Experimental Zoology Part A Ecological and Integrative Physiology
reason: Laboratory kinematics study of captive-bred juvenile ball pythons filmed in an experimental arena; landmarks were dotted on high-speed video in Tracker software. No wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Coregistered Hyperspectral and Stereo Image Seafloor Mapping from an Autonomous Underwater Vehicle
reason: AUV stereo colour imagery co-registered with hyperspectral spectrometer readings is used to classify seafloor biota, including wild coral genera, on the Great Barrier Reef. Image texture features (LBP) are part of the classifier.

title: Swimming behaviour and ascent paths of brook trout in a corrugated culvert
reason: Video recordings of wild brook trout in a field culvert analysed with a semiautomated digitizing program and image spatial calibration to extract ascent paths (video-based tracking).

title: Semi‐automated detection of eagle nests: an application of very high‐resolution image data and advanced image analyses to wildlife surveys
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Primary study developing semi-automated object-based image analysis to detect nests (direct signs) of wild white-bellied sea eagles in aerial photography.

title: Coral reef atoll assessment in the South China Sea using Planet Dove satellites
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Satellite mapping of geomorphic benthic bottom types (deep reef, shallow reef, sand) on atolls; habitat/cover mapping rather than analysis of animals themselves.

title: Pictures or pellets? Comparing camera trapping and dung counts as methods for estimating population densities of ungulates
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Camera-trap photos of wild ungulates are analysed manually (visual estimation of distances, angles and species) and fed into a statistical random encounter model; no computer vision method is applied to the images.

title: Bird detection and species classification with time‐lapse images around a wind farm: Dataset construction and evaluation
reason: Primary study that builds a dataset of wild birds photographed around a wind farm and evaluates detection and species classification methods on it.

title: Applying behavior‐analytic methodology to the science and practice of environmental enrichment in zoos and aquariums
reason: Commentary/perspective on single-subject behavior-analytic designs for evaluating enrichment in zoos and aquariums; it uses only hypothetical data, analyses no images or video and applies no computer vision.

title: Variables affecting the manifestation of and intensity of pacing behavior: A preliminary case study in zoo‐housed polar bears
reason: Video-based gait analysis of zoo-housed polar bears only; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: LifeCLEF 2017 Lab Overview: Multimedia Species Identification Challenges
reason: Evaluation campaign overview; SeaCLEF task evaluates computer vision on underwater videos of reef fish and salmon, web images of marine animals, and whale fluke photo-identification. Plant and bird-audio tasks are not animal vision tasks.

title: A New Approach of 2D Measurement of Injury Rate on Fish by a Modified K-means Clustering Algorithm Based on L*A*B* Color Space
reason: Image segmentation of injuries on fish for industrial food quality / fish pump unloading automation; not wild free-ranging animals in their environment.

title: Automatic Detection and Recognition of Individuals in Patterned Species
reason: Develops a CNN-based framework for detecting and individually recognising wild patterned animals (tigers, zebras, jaguars) in camera trap images.

title: A More Efficient CNN Architecture for Plankton Classification
venue: Communications in computer and information science
reason: Proposes an efficient CNN for classifying plankton images captured by underwater cameras of seafloor observation networks (Plankton Dataset).

title: Using stereoscopic video cameras to evaluate seagrass meadows nursery function in the Mediterranean
reason: Stereo baited underwater video with stereo calibration used to measure size and abundance of wild juvenile fish in seagrass meadows.

title: Determination of size, sex and maturity stage of free swimming catsharks using laser photogrammetry
reason: Laser photogrammetry measurements were made manually in ImageJ on wild-caught catsharks filmed in an indoor observation tank and on dead bycatch specimens; no images of free-ranging animals in the wild were analysed.

title: Are some sharks more social than others? Short- and long-term consistencies in the social behavior of juvenile lemon sharks
reason: Behavioural ecology study of wild-caught juvenile lemon sharks filmed in a semi-captive sea pen; positions were tracked manually in MtrackJ and a rule-based algorithm scored social behaviour from the coordinates, so no automated image analysis is performed.

title: Automatic identification of butterfly species based on HoMSC and GLCMoIB
reason: All analysed images are photographs of butterfly museum specimens on white background downloaded from a specimen website; no free-ranging animals.

title: Camera-trap images segmentation using multi-layer robust principal component analysis
reason: Proposes a multi-layer RPCA background subtraction method to segment wild animals in camera-trap images from the Colombian forest.

title: Enhancement of deep-sea floor images obtained by an underwater vehicle and its evaluation by crab recognition
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Technology
reason: Proposes an image enhancement method for deep-sea floor images taken by an AUV and evaluates it by recognising wild crabs on the seafloor.

title: Redescription of the bump-head sunfish Mola alexandrini (Ranzani 1839), senior synonym of Mola ramsayi (Giglioli 1883), with designation of a neotype for Mola mola (Linnaeus 1758) (Tetraodontiformes: Molidae)
reason: Taxonomic redescription based on manual morphological measurements and counts of museum and fresh specimens; no computer vision or image analysis method.

title: Semi-automated camera trap image processing for the detection of ungulate fence crossing events
reason: Develops an image-processing program (background subtraction, histogram rules) for camera trap images of wild ungulates crossing fences in an ecological reserve; free-roaming cattle also appear in the images.

title: Mapping the change of coral reefs using remote sensing and in situ measurements: a case study in Pangkajene and Kepulauan Regency, Spermonde Archipelago, Indonesia
reason: Benthic habitat / land-cover mapping of coral reef cover classes (live coral, dead coral, seagrass, sand) from 30 m Landsat pixels; habitat mapping rather than imaging of animals as subjects.

title: FDCNet: filtering deep convolutional network for marine organism classification
reason: Proposes a CNN classification method (FDCNet) and a dataset of deep-sea marine organism images drawn from the JAMSTEC deep-sea image library, i.e. wild marine animals.

title: Marine animal classification using UMSLI in HBOI optical test facility
reason: LiDAR imagery was captured only of taxidermy replicas of marine animals mounted in a laboratory test tank. No images show wild, free-ranging animals.

title: Classification of Coral Reef Submarine Images and Videos Using a Novel Z with Tilted Z Local Binary Pattern (Z⊕TZLBP)
reason: Proposes a texture descriptor (ZTZLBP) with KNN to classify submarine images and videos of wild coral reefs, i.e. corals and other reef animals, in their natural setting.

title: A cetacean monitoring system that integrates citizen science and satellite imagery
reason: Conceptual framework proposal for cetacean monitoring combining citizen science and satellite imagery; no data analysed, no experiments or evaluation reported, so not primary empirical research.

title: Semi-automated software for dorsal fin photographic identification of marine species: application to Carcharodon carcharias
reason: Develops and tests semi-automated image-matching software for photo-identification of individual wild white sharks from dorsal fin photographs taken at sea.

title: Cognitive Modeling of the Natural Behavior of the Varroa destructor Mite on Video
reason: Video analysis of Varroa destructor mites confined with honeybee pupae in artificial transparent cells in a controlled laboratory environment; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Habitat-dependent variation in motion signal structure between allopatric populations of lizards
reason: Stereo video of free-living lizards is used to reconstruct their territorial display motion in 3D. A gradient detector algorithm quantifies plant motion noise in video. This is primary field research.

title: Stereotypy of group flight in Brazilian free-tailed bats
reason: Video analysis (custom tracking/counting program) of wild Brazilian free-tailed bats emerging from a cave colony to measure flight parameters.

title: The association between infrared thermal imagery of core eye temperature, personality, age and housing in cats
reason: Study of domestic (pet) cats in rehoming centres using manual thermal-image temperature readings; no wild animals and no computer vision algorithm.

title: Why pace? The influence of social, housing, management, life history, and demographic characteristics on locomotor stereotypy in zoo elephants
reason: Zoo elephants were video-recorded and stereotypic behaviour was scored manually by human observers, then analysed with epidemiological regression models. No computer vision method was used, and all animals were captive.

title: The 24/7 approach to promoting optimal welfare for captive wild animals
reason: Conceptual/perspective paper proposing a welfare framework and assessment tool for zoo animals; no image or video analysis and no primary computer vision research.

title: Optimal marine mammal welfare under human care: Current efforts and future directions
reason: Literature review of welfare of captive marine mammals in zoos and aquaria; it does no computer vision or image analysis and concerns captive animals only.

title: Assessing the effectiveness of a large marine protected area for reef shark conservation
reason: Study of grey reef shark movements using conventional tags, satellite telemetry and AIS vessel tracking; no image or video data are analysed and no computer vision method is used.

title: Do opposites attract? Effects of personality matching in breeding pairs of captive giant pandas on reproductive success
reason: Behavioural study of personality and reproduction in captive giant pandas using caretaker surveys and observer point sampling; there is no image or video analysis and the animals are captive.

title: Classification of radiolarian images with hand-crafted and deep features
reason: Classifies Scanning Electron Microscope images of fossilized radiolarian specimens (microscopy of specimens); not wild free-ranging animals.

title: An automatic active contour method for sea cucumber segmentation in natural underwater environments
reason: Segmentation of cultured sea cucumbers in an aquaculture fishery pool; aquaculture is excluded.

title: Distasteful Nectar Deters Floral Robbery
reason: Ecological study that applies an automated computer-vision monitoring system (motion and blob detection) to video of wild bumblebees visiting flowers in a botanic garden; a laboratory bioassay with commercial colonies is filmed but scored manually.

title: Consistent Individual Differences Drive Collective Behavior and Group Functioning of Schooling Fish
reason: Behavioural experiments on wild-caught sticklebacks housed and tracked in laboratory tanks; video tracking is used only as a measurement tool in a controlled lab set-up, no images of free-ranging animals.

title: Dynamic benthic megafaunal communities: Assessing temporal variations in structure, composition and diversity at the Arctic deep-sea observatory HAUSGARTEN between 2004 and 2015
venue: Deep Sea Research Part I Oceanographic Research Papers
reason: Wild deep-sea megafauna were annotated and counted manually by a taxonomic expert in BIIGLE. The only automated algorithm detects laser points to measure image area, not animals, so no computer vision method is applied to the animals.

title: A simple and efficient method for making a high-resolution seagrass map and quantification of dugong feeding trail distribution: A field test at Mayo Bay, Philippines
reason: Applies image processing (photogrammetric orthomosaic, thresholding, colour segmentation) to underwater field photos to quantify feeding trails of wild dugongs, a direct sign of the animals, alongside seagrass mapping.

title: Modeling polyp activity of Paragorgia arborea using supervised learning
reason: Photographs of wild cold-water corals were labelled manually (extended/retracted); the supervised learning (logistic regression) uses only oceanographic time-series features, not image content, so no computer vision is applied to the images.

title: Towards automatic wild animal monitoring: Identification of animal species in camera-trap images using very deep convolutional neural networks
reason: Primary study applying deep CNNs to classify wild animal species in camera-trap images (Snapshot Serengeti and a second camera-trap dataset).

title: Visual versus video methods for estimating reef fish biomass
reason: Compares diver visual census with stereo diver-operated video for reef fish biomass; the video is annotated and measured manually by an operator in EventMeasure software, with no automated computer vision method developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Assessing machine learning classifiers for the detection of animals’ behavior using depth-based tracking
reason: Depth-based posture and body-part recognition of pet (domestic) cats recorded indoors; no wild animals.

title: Spatio-contextual Gaussian mixture model for local change detection in underwater video
reason: Proposes a background subtraction method for detecting moving fish in underwater video benchmark sequences. The paper does not state whether the fish are wild.

title: Development of stereo camera methodologies to improve pelagic fish biomass estimates and inform ecosystem management in marine waters
reason: Primary study that builds and field-tests an underwater stereo camera and uses stereo-triangulation on still images to measure length, range, tilt and yaw of wild pelagic fish. Species identification and point marking are manual, so the computer vision component is limited to stereo photogrammetry; inclusion is a borderline judgement.

title: Wireless Integrated Sensor Network: Boundary Intellect system for elephant detection via cognitive theory and Fuzzy Cognitive Maps
reason: The paper is a sensor-fusion decision system based on Fuzzy Cognitive Maps and fuzzy if-then rules. Camera images are only sorted into distance categories (S/M/L) by unspecified rules, and no image analysis method is described or evaluated. The focal elephants were handled by keepers and caretakers.

title: Benchmarking sensor fusion capabilities of an integrated instrumentation package
reason: Wild seals, diving birds and fish are detected, tracked and classified, but all the automatic image analysis runs on multibeam sonar and acoustic camera data. The optical camera images were only reviewed by hand, so the computer vision is on sonar only.

title: DSP: Discriminative Spatial Part modeling for Fine-Grained Visual Categorization
reason: Generic fine-grained visual categorization method evaluated on CUB-200-2011 birds and FGVC-Aircraft benchmarks; wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Implications of sensor design for coral reef detection: Upscaling ground hyperspectral imagery in spatial and spectral scales
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
reason: Pixel-level classification of hyperspectral imagery of a natural coral reef that separates Scleractinian corals, soft corals and other benthic classes. Corals are wild animals, so this is primary computer vision research on images of wild organisms.

title: Detecting plague-host abundance from space: Using a spectral vegetation index to identify occupancy of great gerbil burrows
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
reason: Satellite image analysis (object-based segmentation, Random Forest classification of NDVI) to detect wild great gerbil burrows and classify their occupancy; burrows are direct animal signs.

title: The use of Micro-Photogrammetry and Geometric Morphometrics for identifying carnivore agency in bone assemblages
reason: Image-based 3D reconstruction (photogrammetry) of carnivore tooth marks (direct animal signs) to identify the carnivore. Part of the sample comes from wild wolves and foxes; the rest comes from captive lions, hyenas and jaguars.

title: Does fish behaviour bias abundance and length information collected by baited underwater video?
venue: Journal of Experimental Marine Biology and Ecology
reason: Baited stereo-video of wild reef fish is annotated manually by human analysts in EventMeasure (species ID, MaxN, lengths); no computer vision or automated image analysis method is developed or applied.

title: The origin of bipedality as the result of a developmental by-product: The case study of the olive baboon (Papio anubis)
reason: Gait timing of captive infant baboons was annotated by hand, frame by frame, in Elan video software. No computer vision method is used, and the animals live in an enclosure.

title: Learning to recognize rat social behavior: Novel dataset and cross-dataset application
reason: Laboratory rats recorded in a controlled open-field cage for behavioural neuroscience; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Automated face recognition of rhesus macaques
reason: Face detection and individual recognition of group-housed rhesus macaques kept in indoor enclosures at a breeding facility; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: High tech cognitive and acoustic enrichment for captive elephants
reason: Research-through-design study of interactive acoustic enrichment devices for captive elephants; behaviour was assessed by human observation and keeper opinion, with no computer vision or automated image analysis. All animals are captive.

title: Coral reef image classification employing Improved LDP for feature extraction
venue: Journal of Visual Communication and Image Representation
reason: Proposes a texture feature extraction method (ILDP) for classifying corals (wild marine animals) in submarine coral reef images.

title: High-resolution facies zonation within a cold-water coral mound: The case of the Piddington Mound, Porcupine Seabight, NE Atlantic
reason: Applies video mosaicking (SIFT-based image matching) to ROV video of a wild cold-water coral mound to map live/dead coral framework and other facies.

title: Seabed image acquisition and survey design for cold water coral mound characterisation
reason: The study maps seabed habitat facies (live and dead coral framework, rubble, sediment) on a coral mound from a mosaic made with SIFT. Facies classes are assigned by hand, and the focus is survey design for habitat and facies mapping rather than computer vision on animals.

title: Change detection of Bunaken Island coral reefs using 15 years of very high resolution satellite images: A kaleidoscope of habitat trajectories
reason: Satellite-based change detection of reef-flat benthic habitat polygons (coral, seagrass, sand, rubble) via image differencing and photo-interpretation; the subject is habitat cover change, not animals as individual image subjects.

title: A swarm behaviour for jellyfish bloom detection
reason: The paper proposes a UAV swarm behaviour and tests it only in simulation. It explicitly does not describe or apply a vision algorithm; aerial images are used only to build simulator maps.

title: On applications of micro-photogrammetry and geometric morphometrics to studies of tooth mark morphology: The modern Olduvai Carnivore Site (Tanzania)
reason: Images are of bone specimens bearing carnivore tooth marks, photographed on a photographic table for micro-photogrammetric 3D reconstruction; the reference samples come from carnivores in a reserve and the study is taphonomic morphometrics. No living wild animals or field signs are imaged, so the specimen case under E-CAPTIVE applies.

title: Mask-CNN: Localizing parts and selecting descriptors for fine-grained bird species categorization
reason: Generic fine-grained image recognition method evaluated on standard fine-grained bird benchmarks (CUB200-2011, Birdsnap); the paper does not state wildlife or conservation as its subject or application.

title: Convolutional low-resolution fine-grained classification
reason: Generic low-resolution fine-grained classification method evaluated on cars, birds and flowers benchmarks; wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Comparison of Background Subtraction Methods on Near Infra-Red Spectrum Video Sequences

reason: Applies a CNN to UAV video of wild jellyfish (Aurelia aurita) on the sea surface to recognise them and map their distribution.

title: An Open-Source Platform for Underwater Image and Video Analytics
venue: IEEE Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision
reason: Open-source computer vision platform with detectors and classifiers applied to underwater imagery of free-ranging fish, scallops and benthic organisms collected by towed vehicles and camera arrays.

title: Who Moved My Cheese? Automatic Annotation of Rodent Behaviors with Convolutional Neural Networks
venue: IEEE Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision
reason: Laboratory rodents recorded in neuroscience memory experiments (OLM/NOR) inside test chambers; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Reef accessibility impairs the protection of sharks
reason: Ecological study of reef shark richness and abundance; BRUVS videos were annotated manually with EventMeasure software and visual censuses by divers; no computer vision method is developed or applied (analysis is boosted regression trees on count data).

title: Estimating animal density without individual recognition using information derivable exclusively from camera traps
reason: Statistical density-estimation model (REST) using camera-trap videos of wild duikers; staying time and detections are measured manually from the videos, with no computer vision or automated image analysis.

title: Phylogenomics using formalin‐fixed and 100+ year‐old intractable natural history specimens
reason: Phylogenomic DNA sequencing study of formalin-fixed museum snake specimens; no image or video analysis.

title: Expert, Crowd, Students or Algorithm: who holds the key to deep‐sea imagery ‘big data’ processing?
reason: Primary study evaluating a computer vision algorithm (against expert, students and crowd) for counting wild sablefish in deep-sea observatory video.

title: Radar wind profilers and avian migration: a qualitative and quantitative assessment verified by thermal imaging and moon watching
reason: Study analyses radar wind profiler time series manually to quantify wild bird migration; thermal imaging only provides comparison counts from earlier work, with no computer vision analysis of image/video data.

title: Distance sampling with camera traps
reason: Statistical distance-sampling method for camera-trap data; animal distances were estimated manually by comparing videos with reference videos, with no computer vision or automated image analysis.

title: Estimating occupancy and abundance using aerial images with imperfect detection
reason: Statistical N-mixture / point process model for abundance and detection probability from aerial images; sea otters were counted manually by an observer, no computer vision or automated image analysis is applied.

title: Long‐term video surveillance and automated analyses reveal arousal patterns in groups of hibernating bats
reason: Automated image analysis (saturated-pixel and blob measurement) of thermal-infrared video of wild bats hibernating in natural caves; primary research.

title: patternize: An R package for quantifying colour pattern variation
reason: Presents an image alignment and colour-segmentation package. It is applied to images of naturally occurring wild Heliconius hybrids, Galápagos wolf spiders and fire salamanders, along with laboratory guppy crosses.

title: ToxTrac: A fast and robust software for tracking organisms
reason: Tracking software evaluated only on videos of organisms held in closed laboratory arenas for behavioural assays; no wild or free-ranging animals in the analysed data.

title: In situ measurements of animal morphological features: A non‐invasive method
reason: Image-based size estimation tested only on cardboard models, museum bird specimens and free-ranging domestic chickens; there are no images of live wild animals. The field test used livestock (domestic chickens).

title: AcuityView : An r package for portraying the effects of visual acuity on scenes observed by an animal
reason: Software for Fourier-based filtering of images to show what an animal with given acuity could resolve. The only analysed image shows a milkweed plant. Animals are hypothetical viewers, not the subject of the images, and there is no wildlife image analysis.

title: Integrating evolutionary biology with digital arts to quantify ecological constraints on vision‐based behaviour
reason: Borderline include. Motion and saliency analysis is applied to rendered 3D animation video of a lizard display; the display itself was filmed from a free-ranging Jacky dragon in the field and reconstructed in 3D from two camera views. The analysed video is synthetic, but it derives from field footage of a wild animal and no exclusion criterion fits.

title: AutoMorph: Accelerating morphometrics with automated 2D and 3D image processing and shape extraction
reason: Software for imaging museum/fossil specimens (microfossils, shells, fish teeth) under light microscopy; no live wild free-ranging animals.

title: Laser photogrammetry reveals variation in growth and early survival in free‐ranging bottlenose dolphins
reason: Laser photogrammetry, a photograph-based measurement method, is used to estimate the body length of free-ranging wild bottlenose dolphins photographed during boat-based photo-identification surveys.

title: Camera trap data on mammal presence, behaviour and poaching: A case study from Mainaro, Kibale National Park, Uganda
reason: Camera trap survey of wild mammals in Kibale NP where images were reviewed and counted manually; no computer vision or automated image analysis method is developed or applied.

title: Ontogenetic changes in spot configuration (numbers, circularity, size and asymmetry) and lateral line in Neurergus microspilotus (Caudata: Salamandridae)
reason: Newts were hatched and reared in a captive breeding facility and photographed in a Petri dish. Spot traits were measured by hand in AutoCAD, so there is no wild-animal image data and essentially no automated computer vision.

title: Habitat structural complexity metrics improve predictions of fish abundance and distribution
reason: Computer vision (stereo 3D terrain reconstruction from AUV imagery) is applied only to reef habitat structure. Fish were counted manually from BRUV video by observers, so no CV is applied to the animals.

title: A ‘dynamic’ landscape of fear: prey responses to spatiotemporal variations in predation risk across the lunar cycle
reason: Ecological study of prey anti-predator behaviour using camera-trap images that were classified by citizen-science volunteers; no computer vision or automated image analysis is applied, only statistical modelling (GLMMs).

title: Using super‐high resolution satellite imagery to census threatened albatrosses
reason: Albatrosses in satellite images and photographs were counted manually by human observers; no automated image analysis or computer vision method is applied.

title: Unmanned aircraft systems to unravel spatial and temporal factors affecting dynamics of colony formation and nesting success in birds
reason: UAS aerial photographs of a wild black-headed gull colony were analysed by manual photointerpretation in GIS; no computer vision method was applied to the images.

title: Site affinity of whitespotted eagle rays Aetobatus narinari assessed using photographic identification
reason: Applies computer-assisted photo-identification (I3S Spot pattern matching) to in-water photographs of free-swimming wild whitespotted eagle rays to identify individuals and study site affinity.

title: Comparative analysis of vestibular ecomorphology in birds
reason: Micro-CT scans of museum bird crania (specimens) analysed by segmentation and geometric morphometrics; no images of live wild animals.

title: Plant and habitat use by Black-breasted Pufflegs (Eriocnemis nigrivestis), a critically endangered hummingbird
reason: Applies motion-detection software (Motion Meerkat) to time-lapse camera video of wild Black-breasted Puffleg hummingbirds visiting flowers in Ecuador.

title: Detectability and categorization of California sea lions using an unmanned aerial vehicle
reason: Wild California sea lions were photographed from a UAV, but animals were counted and categorized manually by an observer with the Photoshop Count Tool; no computer vision method was developed, applied or evaluated.

title: A day in the life of a dolphin: Using bio‐logging tags for improved animal health and well‐being
reason: The study analyses accelerometer, magnetometer and pressure data from bio-logging tags on dolphins in human care; no image or video analysis is performed (video only served as a reference for building the fluking template).

title: Evidence for a widely expanded humpback whale calving range along the Western Australian coast
reason: Wild humpback whales were photographed from aircraft, but the photographs were examined by people to count and classify calves. No computer vision or automated image analysis was applied.

title: Fear of feces? Tradeoffs between disease risk and foraging drive animal activity around raccoon latrines
reason: Ecological camera-trap study of wild animal behaviour at raccoon latrines; photos were identified and scored manually, with no computer vision or automated image analysis.

title: New technology reveals the role of giant larvaceans in oceanic carbon cycling
reason: In situ ROV video of wild giant larvaceans is analysed by measuring particle streak lengths and by manual annotation counts; the paper describes no automated computer vision method (PIV analysis was explicitly not used).

title: The effects of external cues on individual and collective behavior of shoaling fish
reason: Captive-bred x-ray tetras filmed and tracked in a laboratory annular arena; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Seasonal patterns in acoustic detections of marine mammals near Sachs Harbour, Northwest Territories
reason: Passive acoustic monitoring study of marine mammal vocalizations from hydrophone recordings; automated detectors work on sound, and no image or video data of animals are analysed.

title: Comparing occupied and unoccupied aircraft surveys of wildlife populations: Assessing the gray seal (Halichoerus grypus) breeding colony on Muskeget Island, USA
reason: Analyses aerial imagery (occupied aircraft and UAS, RGB and thermal) of wild gray seals at a breeding colony. The images are stitched into orthomosaics, seals are counted and pup molt stages are assessed. This is image-based analysis of wild animals, although the counting itself is done by hand.

title: Kinecting with Orangutans
venue: CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
reason: HCI study of zoo visitors' empathy for captive orangutans at Melbourne Zoo using a Kinect-based interactive installation; animals are captive only and the study is about the visitors rather than image analysis of wild animals.

title: Where's The Bear?
venue: ACM/IEEE International Conference on Internet of Things Design and Implementation (IoTDI)
reason: End-to-end IoT/edge system that applies CNN image classification to camera-trap images of wild bears, deer and coyotes at a research reserve.

title: Learning to Count Mosquitoes for the Sterile Insect Technique
venue: ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (KDD)
reason: Computer vision is applied to factory-reared, immobilized mosquitoes imaged in petri dishes for quality assurance of the Sterile Insect Technique; no images of wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Fine-grained Discriminative Localization via Saliency-guided Faster R-CNN
venue: ACM International Conference on Multimedia (ACM MM)
reason: Generic fine-grained image classification method evaluated only on the CUB-200-2011 bird benchmark; wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Placement Strategy of Multi-Camera Volumetric Surveillance System for Activities Monitoring
venue: International Conference on Distributed Smart Cameras
reason: Camera placement strategy for monitoring golden eagles near wind turbines; only a laboratory calibration with a chessboard pattern is carried out, and no images of animals are analysed.

title: Fish Tracking Using Acoustical and Optical Data Fusion in Underwater Environment
reason: Primary study that fuses underwater camera video and sonar to localize and track wild fish in the open sea.

title: Supporting animal welfare with automatic tracking of giraffes with thermal cameras
reason: Thermal-camera tracking of giraffes (and zebras) in a zoo enclosure at Melbourne Zoo; only captive animals are analysed.

title: Faster R-CNN for Marine Organism Detection and Recognition Using Data Augmentation
venue: International Conference on Video and Image Processing (ICVIP)
reason: Applies Faster R-CNN with underwater-specific data augmentation to detect and recognise sea cucumbers, sea urchins and scallops on the sea floor in underwater images. The paper does not say the animals are farmed.

title: Geometric morphometrics, scute patterns and biometrics of loggerhead turtles (Caretta caretta) in the central Mediterranean
reason: Photographs of wild loggerhead turtles (bycatch, strandings) are used only for manual landmark digitisation and geometric morphometric statistics. No computer vision method is developed or applied; the scute and biometric data are manual measurements.

title: An unsupervised learning approach for tracking mice in an enclosed area
reason: Tracking and behaviour classification of laboratory C57BL/6 mice in an open field arena and a standard cage; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Photo-id of blue whale by means of the dorsal fin using clustering algorithms and color local complexity estimation for mobile devices
venue: EURASIP Journal on Image and Video Processing
reason: Primary study proposing clustering-based segmentation of dorsal fins in photographs of free-ranging blue whales taken in their natural habitat for photo-identification.

title: Methods for quantitative studies of seafloor hydrothermal systems using 3D visual reconstructions
reason: Develops and applies a 3D visual reconstruction system on ROV imagery of the deep seafloor, used to map and quantify wild Shinkaia crosnieri squat lobster populations.

title: LemurFaceID: a face recognition system to facilitate individual identification of lemurs
reason: Develops a face recognition system for individual identification of lemurs using photographs mostly of wild red-bellied lemurs, plus a few captive individuals and web images.

title: Monitoring butterflies with an unmanned aerial vehicle: current possibilities and future potentials
reason: UAV videos of wild butterflies were reviewed and counted by hand in VLC player. The paper applies no computer vision or automated image analysis method.

title: Possibility of applying unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) and mapping software for the monitoring of waterbirds and their habitats
reason: Drone video of wild waterbirds was identified manually by a bird expert; no computer vision method is applied to the animal images. Software is used only for photogrammetric orthomosaics of the habitat.

title: Treefrog lateral line as a mean of individual identification through visual and software assisted methodologies
reason: Evaluates software-assisted (Wild-ID, SIFT) photographic individual identification of treefrogs from both lab-housed and wild field-caught populations.

title: Flowtrace: simple visualization of coherent structures in biological fluid flows
reason: Image-processing method (sliding maximum intensity projection) applied to videos of animals; includes a crawling army ant swarm filmed in the field (free-ranging), alongside laboratory organisms.

title: Monitoring the behavioral and adrenal activity of giraffe (Giraffa camelopardalis) to assess welfare during seasonal housing changes.
reason: Zoo welfare study of four giraffe that uses direct behavioural observation, accelerometer data loggers and fecal hormone assays. No image or video analysis is done, and the animals are captive.

title: A pattern-based tool for long-term, large-sample capture-mark-recapture studies of fire salamanders Salamandra species (Amphibia: Urodela: Salamandridae)
reason: Individual fire salamanders are identified from 44 spot-pattern characteristics that a person codes by hand and enters into a database. Matching runs on these numeric codes, and the images themselves are never analysed computationally.

title: Ultra-Fine Scale Spatially-Integrated Mapping of Habitat and Occupancy Using Structure-From-Motion
reason: Primary study applying Structure-from-Motion photogrammetry to ground-based images of a wild gentoo penguin colony to reconstruct 3D terrain and map nest locations.

title: WiseEye: Next Generation Expandable and Programmable Camera Trap Platform for Wildlife Research
reason: Develops a camera trap platform with on-board background subtraction to flag false-positive images, tested on free-ranging gulls and pigeons visiting a rooftop.

title: Collective behavior quantification on human odor effects against female Aedes aegypti mosquitoes-Open source development
reason: Machine-vision blob detection of insectary-reared Aedes aegypti mosquitoes released into an indoor laboratory observation chamber; no wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: The challenge of monitoring elusive large carnivores: An accurate and cost-effective tool to identify and sex pumas (Puma concolor) from footprints
reason: Analyses footprint images (direct signs) of pumas to identify individuals and sex; training data from captive pumas, validated with footprints from free-ranging pumas in Texas and California.

title: GnRH-mediated olfactory and visual inputs promote mating-like behaviors in male zebrafish
reason: Laboratory neurobiology study of zebrafish mating-like behaviour. Videos were scored manually with a hand-defined scoring scheme; no computer vision or automated image analysis is applied.

title: Prevalence and determinants of stereotypic behaviours and physiological stress among tigers and leopards in Indian zoos
reason: Behavioural focal observations and faecal hormone assays of zoo tigers and leopards; no image or video analysis or computer vision. The animals are also captive only.

title: Modified FlowCAM procedure for quantifying size distribution of zooplankton with sample recycling capacity
reason: Wild-caught copepods are preserved in formalin and imaged in a laboratory FlowCAM microscope imaging-in-flow set-up. The paper is about a lab sample-processing procedure and size estimation, not about imaging free-ranging animals.

title: Drivers of abundance and spatial distribution of reef-associated sharks in an isolated atoll reef system
reason: Ecological study of wild reef sharks from stereo-BRUVS video. Identification and counting were done manually by trained analysts in EventMeasure; no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Long term monitoring of jaguars in the Cockscomb Basin Wildlife Sanctuary, Belize; Implications for camera trap studies of carnivores
reason: Ecological capture-recapture study of wild jaguars from camera-trap photographs. Individuals were identified manually from spot patterns and analysed with statistical population models; no computer vision or automated image analysis is applied.

title: Feature point based 3D tracking of multiple fish from multi-view images
reason: 3D multi-view tracking of zebrafish swimming in a small laboratory container; no wild or free-ranging animals in the analysed data.

title: An improved camera trap for amphibians, reptiles, small mammals, and large invertebrates
reason: The paper presents and tests a camera-trap hardware trigger (HALT) and compares detection probabilities with PIR triggers; images are reviewed manually and no computer vision or image analysis method is applied.

title: An accurate and adaptable photogrammetric approach for estimating the mass and body condition of pinnipeds using an unmanned aerial system
reason: Primary study measuring body size and estimating mass of free-ranging leopard seals from UAS aerial photographs. Borderline: the image analysis is semi-automated photogrammetry in ImageJ with observer-placed landmarks, not an automated computer vision model.

title: Fish Image Segmentation Algorithm (FISA) for Improving the Performance of Image Retrieval System
venue: International Journal of Advanced Computer Science and Applications
reason: Proposes an image segmentation algorithm for fish images (body parts) evaluated on QUT_fish_data, which includes fish photographed in natural situations as well as controlled and out-of-water images.

title: Pixying Behavior: A Versatile Real-Time andPost HocAutomated Optical Tracking Method for Freely Moving and Head Fixed Animals
reason: Colour-based optical tracking of whiskers, limbs and head of laboratory mice in head-fixed and enclosure set-ups; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Biology goes in the air
reason: This is a journalistic Science & Society feature on how biologists use UAVs. It reports no primary computer vision research or image analysis of its own.

title: Animal Recognition System Based on Convolutional Neural Network
venue: Advances in Electrical and Electronic Engineering
reason: Proposes a CNN to classify images of five wild animal classes (fox, wolf, bear, hog, deer) from an author-created database described as wild animals; how and where the images were taken is not stated.

title: Weakly Supervised Learning of Part Selection Model with Spatial Constraints for Fine-Grained Image Classification
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
reason: Generic fine-grained image classification method evaluated only on the CUB-200-2011 benchmark; wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Scute Patterns as an Individual Identification Tool in an American Crocodile (Crocodylus acutus) Population on Coiba Island, Panama
reason: Dorsal scute patterns of wild-caught American Crocodiles are coded and compared manually from photographs with statistical tests; no computer vision or automated image analysis is applied.

title: Fish Recognition based on HOG Feature Extraction using SVM Prediction
reason: Applies HOG+SVM image classification to recognise wild-caught fish species on fishing boats from boat camera images, aimed at preventing fishing of endangered fish.

title: Learning to Recognize Animals by Watching Documentaries: Using Subtitles as Weak Supervision
reason: Primary study developing weakly supervised animal recognition models from wildlife documentary key frames and evaluating transfer to Snapshot Serengeti camera-trap images of wild animals.

title: Presentation Investigation of SVM Classifier for the Recognition of Shark Fish
reason: Primary study applying image processing and an SVM classifier to UAV aerial images of coastal areas to recognise sharks versus non-sharks.

title: Automatic bird identification for offshore wind farms: A case study for deep learning
reason: Applies a CNN+SVM image classifier to photographs of wild birds in flight at an offshore wind farm test location for species identification.

title: Specimen identification technique of melanophiniscus species through digital image processing
reason: Digital image processing method for photo-identification of individual wild Melanophryniscus toads from ventral spot patterns, using photographs taken on field trips.

title: Characterization of skin patterns in Pseudoplatystoma Magdaleniatum
reason: Classical image-processing segmentation of skin patterns in photographs of wild catfish caught by artisanal fisheries in Colombian rivers.

title: PATTERN RECOGNITION APPROACH FOR FISH MASK SEGMENTATION AND DETECTION FROM VIDEO
venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Computer Science
reason: Classical image processing method for segmenting, detecting and counting fish in video frames, framed as monitoring fish in the ocean. The data comes from online videos, and the paper does not say whether the fish are wild or captive.

title: DENSITY BASED FISH COUNTING WITH COMPUTER VISION FOR AQUARIUM AND BOX STORAGE IN NOISY ENVIRONMENTS
reason: Counts fish held in aquariums and storage boxes for fish inventory; no wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Classification of Serranidae Species Using Color Based Statistical Features
reason: Fish specimens photographed lying on a white background floor in a fixed position; no free-ranging animals imaged, so equivalent to specimen imagery.

title: Estimates of Sea Scallop (Placopecten magellanicus) Incidental Mortality from Photographic Multiple Before—After-Control—Impact Surveys
reason: AUV seafloor photographs of wild sea scallops were annotated manually by trained human annotators; images were only contrast-enhanced and no automated computer vision analysis was performed.

title: Affordable and accurate stereo-video system for measuring dimensions underwater: a case study using oceanic whitetip sharks Carcharhinus longimanus
reason: Stereo-video (image-based 3D reconstruction) used to measure the length of wild oceanic whitetip sharks in situ in The Bahamas.

title: Using unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) to measure jellyfish aggregations
reason: Primary study applying image analysis (texture analysis and k-means pixel clustering) to UAV imagery of wild jellyfish aggregations to estimate areal extent and percent cover.

title: A Tale of Two Crowds: Public Engagement in Plankton Classification
reason: Published as a Perspective article: it recounts and compares two crowd-sourcing approaches (citizen science and a data-science competition) for classifying in situ plankton imagery, rather than reporting a primary computer vision study.

title: In situ Analysis of Coral Recruits Using Fluorescence Imaging
reason: Develops a fluorescence imaging and image-processing method (automatic SURF/RANSAC registration, ambient-light subtraction, annotation software) to survey wild coral recruits in situ on reefs in the Gulf of Aqaba. A preliminary aquarium experiment with captive-reared recruits was also run.

title: Inexpensive Aerial Photogrammetry for Studies of Whales and Large Marine Animals
reason: UAV photogrammetry hardware/calibration system for measuring wild southern right whales; image measurement is done manually by user mouse clicks in a MATLAB GUI, with no automated image analysis.

title: Thermal Imaging and Biometrical Thermography of Humpback Whales
reason: Thermal infrared images and video of wild humpback whales are analysed quantitatively. The authors extract brightness temperature anomalies and estimate blow heights and velocities from pixel measurements, to support automated whale detection.

title: An Economical Custom-Built Drone for Assessing Whale Health
reason: The paper describes a custom drone that physically samples humpback whale blow for microbiota sequencing. The on-board video is only reviewed manually to confirm samples and identify individuals; no computer vision method is applied.

title: Head Stabilization in the Pigeon: Role of Vision to Correct for Translational and Rotational Disturbances
reason: Laboratory neuroscience experiment on breeder-obtained pigeons housed in an aviary, recorded with a marker-based optical motion capture system on a motion platform in a windowless room; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Pigeons (C. livia) Follow Their Head during Turning Flight: Head Stabilization Underlies the Visual Control of Flight
reason: Housed, trained pigeons filmed in an indoor netted flight corridor with marker-based 3D kinematics; a laboratory set-up, not wild free-ranging animals.

title: Size Matters: Observed and Modeled Camouflage Response of European Cuttlefish (Sepia officinalis) to Different Substrate Patch Sizes during Movement
reason: Behavioural experiment on wild-caught cuttlefish held and filmed in an indoor laboratory tank with artificial backgrounds; image analysis is a simple reflectance measurement with manual tracking, not on free-ranging animals.

title: Quantifying the Availability of Vertebrate Hosts to Ticks: A Camera-Trapping Approach
reason: Ecological camera-trapping study of host passage rates for ticks; species and passage distances were recorded by people from the images, and no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Vision-Based Perception and Classification of Mosquitoes Using Support Vector Machine
reason: Image-based classification of mosquitoes versus bees and flies, using images from field collection and the web. The animals are free-ranging insects, not livestock or lab colonies.

title: Automatic Counting of Large Mammals from Very High Resolution Panchromatic Satellite Imagery
reason: Develops an image-analysis method (wavelet + ANFIS) to detect and count wild large mammals in satellite imagery of the Maasai Mara National Reserve.

title: Multiple Drosophila Tracking System with Heading Direction
reason: Tracking system for laboratory fruit flies (Drosophila melanogaster, a model organism) walking in a closed circular arena; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Visual Detection and Tracking System for a Spherical Amphibious Robot
reason: Proposes a vision-based detection and tracking system for an amphibious robot aimed at ecological observation. It is evaluated on underwater observatory videos of free-swimming fish from Fish4Knowledge, alongside sequences of a toy fish in a tank and a small robot in a lab.

title: Monocular Vision-Based Underwater Object Detection
reason: Generic underwater salient object detection method for man-made and natural objects; animals are only one type of target and wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Towards the Automatic Detection of Pre-Existing Termite Mounds through UAS and Hyperspectral Imagery
reason: Develops an image-analysis pipeline (SVM on UAV hyperspectral imagery plus shape analysis) to detect termite mounds, a direct sign of wild termites, in a national park.

title: The Modular Optical Underwater Survey System
reason: Describes a stereo-video camera hardware system for fish surveys. Fish are counted and measured by human analysts in EventMeasure software; no automated computer vision method is developed or evaluated, and automated analysis is named only as future work.

title: SwarmSight: Measuring the temporal progression of animal group activity levels from natural-scene and laboratory videos
reason: Presents a background-subtraction video tool for group activity levels and applies it to free-ranging wild birds and stingless bees at hives, alongside laboratory cockroaches.

title: Wild-Animal Recognition in Agriculture Farms Using W-COHOG for Agro-Security
venue: International Journal of Computational Intelligence Research
reason: Proposes a W-CoHOG feature and linear classifier to recognise wild animals in images, evaluated on a camera-trap dataset and a wild-animal image dataset.

title: A suitable ichthyometer for systemic application
venue: Latin American Journal of Aquatic Research
reason: Image-based length measurement device tested on farmed tilapia from intensive aquaculture cultures in a lab; no wild animals.

title: Identification of the Anteroposterior and Mediolateral Position of Lion Paws and Tracks Using 3D Geometric Morphometrics
reason: Photogrammetric 3D models built from photographs of wild African lion paws and tracks, analysed with geometric morphometrics and LDA to identify foot position; wild animals and their direct signs (tracks).

title: Seasonal, Diel, and Age Differences in Activity Budgets of a Group of Bottlenose Dolphins (Tursiops truncatus) Under Professional Care
reason: Behavioural study of captive bottlenose dolphins in an oceanarium. A human observer collected the data by scan sampling, and no images or video were analysed with computer vision.

title: Automatic Recognition of Mammal Genera on Camera-Trap Images using Multi-Layer Robust Principal Component Analysis and Mixture Neural Networks
reason: Primary study proposing a segmentation and genus classification method on camera-trap images of wild mammals in the Colombian forest.

title: The iNaturalist Species Classification and Detection Dataset
reason: Presents a citizen-science image dataset of wild species (animals and plants) for species classification and detection, with baseline CV experiments; framed as useful for biodiversity monitoring and conservation.

title: The Devil is in the Tails: Fine-grained Classification in the Wild
reason: Evaluates CNN fine-grained species classification on citizen-science photographs of wild birds from eBird, studying long-tailed class distributions; bird species recognition is the stated application.

title: Differentiating Objects by Motion: Joint Detection and Tracking of Small Flying Objects
reason: Proposes a deep joint detection and tracking network evaluated on video of free-flying birds around a wind farm (plus a UAV dataset).

title: Wildbook: Crowdsourcing, computer vision, and data science for conservation
reason: System overview of Wildbook reporting two photographic censuses in which computer vision detects and individually identifies wild zebras and giraffes in citizen-scientist photographs from Kenya.

title: Harnessing the Power of Deep Learning to Save Animals
reason: Perspective/overview paper describing deep learning concepts and summarising existing use cases (Snapshot Serengeti, sea cow detector, snow leopard classifier, BeeScanning); no own data, experiments or model development.

title: Biological and environmental rhythms in (dark) deep-sea hydrothermal ecosystems
reason: Deep-sea vent fauna were counted manually on video stills in Photoshop. Only microbial cover was quantified with the ImageJ magic wand. No computer vision method was developed or applied to the animals; the analysis is ecological time-series statistics.

title: Seabed images from Southern Ocean shelf regions off the northern Antarctic Peninsula and in the southeastern Weddell Sea
reason: Data paper describing collection and publication of seabed images of wild benthic fauna; no computer vision or image analysis method is developed or applied.

title: COMPARISON OF COMMERCIAL STRUCTURE-FROM-MOTION PHOTOGRAMMETY SOFTWARE USED FOR UNDERWATER THREE-DIMENSIONAL MODELING OF CORAL REEF ENVIRONMENTS
venue: The international archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences/International archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences
reason: Applies Structure-from-Motion photogrammetry (computer vision 3D reconstruction) to underwater images of wild coral colonies and reef plots, comparing two software packages.

title: UNDERWATER PHOTOGRAMMETRY, CODED TARGET AND PLENOPTIC TECHNOLOGY: A SET OF TOOLS FOR MONITORING RED CORAL IN MEDITERRANEAN SEA IN THE FRAMEWORK OF THE ”PERFECT” PROJECT
venue: The international archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences/International archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences
reason: Develops photogrammetric and plenoptic 3D reconstruction and measurement tools applied to underwater images of wild red coral colonies (Corallium rubrum) in the Mediterranean.

title: Advances in Ecosystem Research: Saildrone Surveys of Oceanography, Fish, and Marine Mammals in the Bering Sea
reason: Saildrone surveys use passive acoustics and active echosounder (sonar) data only; no image or video analysis.

title: Insights into the Biodiversity, Behavior, and Bioluminescence of Deep-Sea Organisms Using Molecular and Maritime Technology
reason: Retrospective overview of 30 years of MBARI deep-sea research (ROV video, manual annotation in VARS, molecular methods). It is not primary research and no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated; video is annotated by people.

title: Automatic Assessing Body Condition Score from Digital Images by Active Shape Model and Multiple Regression Technique
venue: Proceedings of International Conference on Artificial Life and Robotics
reason: Estimates body condition score of dairy cattle (livestock) from rear-view images.

title: Behaviour and welfare: the visitor effect in captive felids
reason: Zoo welfare study of captive felids; video recordings were scan-sampled manually for behaviour and space use and analysed with statistics only. No computer vision method is used, and all animals are captive.

title: Snake classification from images
reason: Snake images were photographed at a serpentarium, so the animals were held in captivity. The paper also says images were taken 'under wild conditions', but it describes no free-ranging field data.

title: Phenotypic variation in dorsal fin morphology of coastal bottlenose dolphins ( Tursiops truncatus ) off Mexico
reason: Wild dolphin photo-ID images are used, but fin landmarks are placed by hand by an operator and then analysed statistically (PCA/DFA). No computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Skin temperature and reproductive condition in wild female chimpanzees
reason: Wild chimpanzees were imaged with a thermal camera, but temperatures were read manually by drawing polygon regions of interest in the vendor's software and then analysed statistically. No computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Quantifying the behavior of fish in response to a moving camera vehicle by using benthic stereo cameras and target tracking
reason: Stereo image analysis and target tracking of wild vermilion snapper on a reef to quantify avoidance behavior toward a camera vehicle.

title: Comparison of Different Deep Structures for Fish Classification
venue: International Journal of Computer Theory and Engineering
reason: CNN-based fish species classification on QUT fish images, part of which show fish in their natural environment.

title: A user's guide for the quantitative analysis of substrate characteristics and locomotor kinematics in free‐ranging primates
reason: Wild primates are filmed in the field, but gait events and spatial points are digitised by hand in a GUI (GaitKeeper), and substrate photogrammetry measures branches in ImageJ. No computer vision is applied to the animal images.

title: Research of animals image semantic segmentation based on deep learning
venue: Concurrency and Computation Practice and Experience
reason: Semantic segmentation (FCN + CRF-RNN) trained and tested only on the generic PASCAL VOC 2012 benchmark. Animals appear only as benchmark classes (mostly domestic: cat, cow, dog, horse, sheep), and no wildlife data is analysed.

title: Can drones count gulls? Minimal disturbance and semiautomated image processing with an unmanned aerial vehicle for colony‐nesting seabirds
reason: UAV imagery of a wild breeding gull colony is analysed with a semiautomated supervised image classification to count birds and differentiate species.

title: Monitoring marine mammals using unmanned aerial vehicles: quantifying detection certainty
reason: UAV images of wild cetaceans were inspected manually by analysts; no computer vision method is applied to the animals. The only image computation is mean RGB luminance used as a covariate in a logistic model of analyst detection certainty.

title: A morphometric dive into fish diversity
reason: Outline morphometrics (elliptical Fourier transform) on photographs and drawings of fish taken from online image databases; the images are specimen-style lateral views and illustrations, not images of wild free-ranging animals in situ.

title: Three novel methods to estimate abundance of unmarked animals using remote cameras
reason: Statistical abundance estimators (time to event, space to event, instantaneous sampling) applied to camera-trap photographs that were viewed and counted manually; no computer vision or automated image analysis is used.

title: Perspectives on the Application of Unmanned Aircraft for Freshwater Fisheries Census
reason: Perspective with a field feasibility study: drone video of wild Taimen in Mongolian rivers. Fish were found and sized only by people reviewing the video and measuring by hand. No computer vision method was developed or applied; automated detection is named only as future work.

title: Does repeated human handling of study animals during the mating season affect their offspring?
venue: Journal of Experimental Zoology Part A Ecological and Integrative Physiology
reason: Experimental ecology study of handling effects on wood frog reproduction. Photographs of laboratory-reared froglets were only measured manually in ImageJ; no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: A suspensory way of life: Integrating locomotion, postures, limb movements, and forces in two‐toed sloths Choloepus didactylus (Megalonychidae, Folivora, Pilosa)
venue: Journal of Experimental Zoology Part A Ecological and Integrative Physiology
reason: Behavioural and kinematic video analysis of captive two-toed sloths in two zoos only (Nowe Zoo Poznań, Central Florida Zoo); no wild animals, and video analysis was manual frame-by-frame scoring and digitising.

title: Multicomponent structures in camouflage and mimicry in butterfly wing patterns
reason: Comparative morphological study: researchers visually identify wing pattern components on butterfly specimens and photographs and then run Fisher's exact tests. No computer vision or automated image analysis is used.

title: Krill motion in the Southern Ocean: quantifying in situ krill movement behaviors and distributions during the late austral autumn and spring
reason: In situ stereo-camera imaging of wild Antarctic krill in the Southern Ocean, with semi-automated detection, counting and tracking of individuals.

title: Measuring the in situ tilt orientation of fish and zooplankton using stereo photogrammetric methods
reason: The authors used stereo photogrammetry on in situ underwater images to measure the 3D tilt and length of wild krill in the Gulf of Alaska.

title: Automated plankton image analysis using convolutional neural networks
reason: Primary study that develops and evaluates a CNN classification pipeline on in situ shadowgraph images of free-living marine plankton (zooplankton, larval fish, gelatinous organisms) collected in the northern Gulf of Mexico.

title: Zooglider: An autonomous vehicle for optical and acoustic sensing of zooplankton
reason: Presents an autonomous glider with an in situ shadowgraph camera imaging free-living marine zooplankton; images are segmented with Canny edge detection and classified with CNNs.

title: Automated Detection of Bird Roosts using NEXRAD Radar Data and Convolutional Neural Networks
