venue: SHAREOK (University of Oklahoma; Oklahoma State University; Central Oklahoma University)
reason: Applies CNNs to radar images (rendered as 2D images) to detect roosts of wild Purple Martins and Tree Swallows.

title: Assessing agricultural damage by wild boar using drones
reason: Image analysis (GEOBIA + Random Forest) of UAV photographs to map rooting and crop damage, a direct sign of free-ranging wild boar. No animals are imaged directly, so inclusion rests on treating damage as a direct sign; otherwise E-PLANT would apply.

title: Successful care and propagation of the endangered amargosa vole (Microtus californicus scirpensis) in captivity
reason: Husbandry report on a captive vole colony; camera trap images were only reviewed manually, with no computer vision analysis. The animals are also captive only.

title: Cognitive judgement bias is associated with frequency of anticipatory behavior in bottlenose dolphins
reason: Behavioural/welfare study of captive bottlenose dolphins; return latencies were measured manually from video footage and behaviour was scored by a human observer. No computer vision method is used, and all animals are captive.

title: Relative response to digital tablet devices and painting as sensory enrichment in captive chimpanzees
reason: A behavioural enrichment study of zoo chimpanzees. A human observer recorded behaviour by instantaneous sampling, and no image or video analysis was done. The animals are also captive only.

title: Patterns of nocturnal activity in captive greater flamingos
reason: Study of a captive greater flamingo flock in a zoo/wetland-centre enclosure. Camera-trap photos were scored by hand, with no computer vision method.

title: Using Convolutional Neural Networks to Recognition of Dolphin Images
venue: Advances in intelligent systems and computing
reason: CNN classification of aerial video images of free-ranging dolphins and seabirds in the open sea.

title: Recognition in Terra Incognita
venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science Including Subseries Lecture Notes in Artificial Intelligence and Lecture Notes in Bioinformatics
reason: Introduces a camera-trap dataset (CCT-20) and benchmarks detection and classification of animals at new locations. The camera-trap images show mostly wild animals, together with some domestic cats and dogs.

title: Fish Image Segmentation Using Salp Swarm Algorithm
venue: Advances in intelligent systems and computing
reason: Proposes an image segmentation method for fish images. The dataset includes natural underwater images of fish alongside controlled and out-of-the-water specimen images.

title: Individual egg camouflage is influenced by microhabitat selection and use of nest materials in ground-nesting birds
reason: Digital image analysis (calibrated multispectral photos, thresholding, difference-of-Gaussians, pattern energy analysis) of nests and eggs of wild ground-nesting birds in the field, used to quantify egg camouflage.

title: A pilot(less) study on the use of an unmanned aircraft system for studying polar bears (Ursus maritimus)
reason: UAS imagery and spotting-scope video of wild polar bears were reviewed manually by human observers; no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Study of fauna population changes on Penguin Island and Turret Point Oasis (King George Island, Antarctica) using an unmanned aerial vehicle
reason: UAV aerial images of wild Antarctic seabirds and pinnipeds were counted and identified manually by a human photo interpreter in ArcGIS; no computer vision method was applied (automatic estimation is only mentioned as planned future work).

title: Estimating the abundance of polar bears on Wrangel Island during late summer using high-resolution satellite imagery: a pilot study
reason: Polar bears are counted on satellite imagery by manual visual search in GIS, with a second image used for visual comparison; no automated image analysis or computer vision method is applied.

title: AUV-based classification of benthic communities of the Ningaloo shelf and mesophotic areas
reason: AUV seabed images of wild benthic biota (corals, sponges, other filter feeders) were scored manually by a human with a point-grid overlay; k-means clustering was applied to the resulting per cent cover data, not to the images. No computer vision method is used.

title: Heat flux in manatees: an individual matter and a novel approach to assess and monitor the thermal state of Florida manatees (Trichechus manatus latirostris)
reason: Physiological heat-flux study of two captive manatees in a seawater tank. The only image use is measuring appendage surface area from photographs in ImageJ, and no wild animals are imaged.

title: Hot-spring bathing of wild monkeys in Shiga-Heights: origin and propagation of a cultural behavior
reason: Historical editorial about the origin of hot-spring bathing in wild Japanese macaques. It contains no image analysis or computer vision; the photos are illustrations only.

title: A road mobile mapping device for supervised classification of amphibians on roads
reason: Primary study applying a Haar cascade computer vision algorithm to road-surface images to detect alive and road-killed amphibians, including real surveys on national roads alongside control tests with plastic models and collection specimens.

title: Assessing the ecological relevance of swimming performance traits: a case study of bluegill sunfish (Lepomis macrochirus)
reason: Field 3D stereo videography of wild bluegill sunfish in a lake, with calibrated camera pairs and video-based center-of-mass tracking used to quantify swimming behaviour.

title: Nutrient Balancing by Captive Golden Snub-Nosed Monkeys (Rhinopithecus roxellana)
reason: Nutritional study of captive monkeys based on direct or video-assisted manual feeding observations and lab nutrient analysis; no computer vision or image analysis method is used.

title: Deep-Sea Organisms Tracking Using Dehazing and Deep Learning
reason: Develops a dehazing plus YOLO pipeline to detect and track deep-sea organisms (shrimp, squid, crab, shark) in deep-sea videos from the JAMSTEC archive; primary research on free-ranging marine animals.

title: Coral reef image/video classification employing novel octa-angled pattern for triangular sub region and pulse coupled convolutional neural network (PCCNN)
reason: Proposes a texture descriptor and classifier for classifying coral reef images/videos from reef surveys (wild marine invertebrates).

title: A novel framework for real-time diseased coral reef image classification
reason: Proposes texture feature descriptors and classifiers for classifying diseases in images of wild corals photographed on a reef off Shingle Island, India.

title: Enhanced Bird Detection from Low-Resolution Aerial Image Using Deep Neural Networks
reason: Proposes a super-resolution plus deep-learning detection framework for birds in low-resolution images captured under wild conditions (BIRD-50, CUB-200).

title: Image dataset of ophiuroid and other deep sea benthic organisms in 2015 extracted from the survey off Sanriku, Japan, by the research following the Great East Japan Earthquake 2011
reason: Data paper that compiles cropped ROV images of deep-sea benthic organisms and occurrence records; it proposes the images as training data but applies no computer vision method itself.

title: An automated behavior analysis system for freely moving rodents using depth image
reason: Behaviour analysis of laboratory Sprague-Dawley rats in a homecage with implanted electrodes; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Performance optimization of rotation-tolerant Viola–Jones-based blackbird detection
reason: All analysed images show red-winged blackbirds photographed in an outdoor aviary (captive setting); no free-ranging animals in the data.

title: Informative and misinformative interactions in a school of fish
reason: Fish bought from a shop were filmed in a laboratory ring-shaped tank and tracked with idTracker. No wild or free-ranging animals appear in the data.

title: Automatic benthic imagery recognition using a hierarchical two-stage approach
reason: The paper classifies seabed cover (benthic habitat) into red algae, sand, lithothamnium, kelp and sponge. It is about mapping habitat and substrate cover. Sponge is the only animal class, and animals are not the stated subject.

title: Underwater Object Recognition Based on Deep Encoding-Decoding Network
venue: Journal of Ocean University of China
reason: Proposes a CNN encoding-decoding network to classify fish species in underwater images from the Fish4Knowledge dataset.

title: Automatic Identification of Butterfly Species Based on Gray-Level Co-occurrence Matrix Features of Image Block
reason: Images are of butterfly specimens downloaded from a specimen website, photographed on white background; no free-ranging animals.

title: 3D Local Spatio-temporal Ternary Patterns for Moving Object Detection in Complex Scenes
reason: Proposes a background-subtraction descriptor for moving object detection, motivated by underwater scenes and evaluated on the Fish4Knowledge underwater dataset. The other two benchmarks (I2R, Change Detection) show people and general scenes. This is a borderline call: the paper never writes 'fish' outside the dataset name, but it names underwater object detection as its stated application.

title: FPGA implementation of elephant recognition in infrared images to reduce the computational time
venue: Journal of Ambient Intelligence and Humanized Computing
reason: Applies image segmentation and k-NN classification to infrared images to recognise elephants, motivated by human-elephant conflict. The data mixes wild species (elephant, tiger, lion, deer, bear) with domestic ones (pig, cow, horse, dog). The image source is not stated.

title: Spatial positioning of individuals in a group of feral horses: a case study using drone technology
reason: Drone photographs of feral horses are analysed by manually derived pixel coordinates and body-length measurements, followed by spatial statistics and social network analysis; no computer vision or automated image analysis method is developed, applied or evaluated (only lens-distortion correction in Photoshop).

title: Volume-concentrated searching by an aerial insectivore, the common swift, Apus apus
reason: Applies stereo-video optical 3D tracking (automated silhouette centroid and cross-correlation matching) to wild common swifts foraging near their breeding colony.

title: Measuring welfare in captive flamingos: Activity patterns and exhibit usage in zoo-housed birds
reason: Behaviour and enclosure-use study of zoo-housed flamingos at WWT Slimbridge. Behaviour was scored manually from photographs, with no computer vision method. Only captive animals are studied.

title: Hormonal correlates of behavioural profiles and coping strategies in captive capuchin monkeys (Sapajus libidinosus)
reason: Behavioural observation and faecal hormone study of captive capuchin monkeys; no image or video analysis.

title: Dopamine D1 and D2 receptor antagonism during development alters later behavior in zebrafish
reason: Laboratory pharmacology study of colony-bred zebrafish; behaviour is tracked with commercial video-tracking software in laboratory assays. No wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Remote electronic monitoring as a potential alternative to on-board observers in small-scale fisheries
reason: Vessel-mounted camera photos of wild-caught target catch and bycatch were reviewed manually by a human photo analyst and compared with on-board observer reports; no computer vision or automated image analysis was applied.

title: Use of an unmanned aerial vehicle (drone) to survey Nile crocodile populations: A case study at Lake Nyamithi, Ndumo game reserve, South Africa
reason: Drone survey of wild Nile crocodiles, but crocodiles were identified and measured manually in ArcMap on an orthomosaic. The only automated processing is photogrammetric stitching, and no computer vision method is applied to the animals.

title: Automated monitoring for birds in flight: Proof of concept with eagles at a wind power facility
reason: Evaluates a camera-based automated system that detects, tracks and classifies wild eagles and other birds in flight at a wind power facility.

title: Automatic in-trap pest detection using deep learning for pheromone-based Dendroctonus valens monitoring
reason: Images show dead bark beetle specimens (collected from field pheromone traps) thrown into a trap collection cup in the laboratory to simulate field traps; no images of wild, free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: A new skeleton based flying bird detection method for low-altitude air traffic management
reason: Proposes a computer vision method to detect flying birds in images and video, using images of wild birds.

title: Peak in biomass driven by larger-bodied meso-predators in demersal fish communities between shelf and slope habitats at the head of a submarine canyon in the south-eastern Indian Ocean
reason: Wild demersal fish recorded with stereo-BRUVs, but species identification, MaxN counts and lengths come from manual video annotation in EventMeasure software. No automated computer vision method is developed or applied; the analysis is ecological statistics.

title: Biological Motion as an Innate Perceptual Mechanism Driving Social Affiliation
reason: Laboratory behavioural neuroscience study of juvenile zebrafish in glass dishes with a virtual-reality projection set-up; video tracking is used only to measure positions of laboratory-reared animals, no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Classification of bird species from video using appearance and motion features
reason: Computer vision classification of flying birds from video collected by the authors; includes free-ranging species (gull, house martin, sparrow, starling, wood pigeon) together with parrots filmed with the help of a parrot sanctuary.

title: A Deep learning method for accurate and fast identification of coral reef fishes in underwater images
reason: Primary study training a CNN to identify coral reef fish species in underwater videos recorded on wild reefs around Mayotte.

title: Detection of changes in shallow coral reefs status: Towards a spatial approach using hyperspectral and multispectral data
reason: Airborne hyperspectral and satellite image analysis to estimate and map living coral cover (wild benthic animals) and its change on a natural reef in Reunion Island.

title: An evaluation of the efficiency of passive acoustic monitoring in detecting deer and primates in comparison with camera traps
reason: Compares passive acoustic monitoring (HMM sound recognizers) with camera traps for sika deer and Japanese macaques; camera-trap photographs are reviewed manually to compute relative abundance, with no computer vision method applied to images.

title: Like night and day: Reversals of thermal gradients across ghost crab burrows and their implications for thermal ecology
reason: Thermal ecology study of ghost crab burrows. Thermal images are read for temperature with vendor software; no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: What's a picture really worth? On the use of drone aerial imagery to estimate intertidal rocky shore mussel demographic parameters
reason: Primary study applying supervised pixel classification to drone aerial imagery to map wild intertidal mussel beds (Mytilus galloprovincialis) on rocky shores and estimate coverage and density.

title: Towards highly accurate coral texture images classification using deep convolutional neural networks and data augmentation
reason: Primary study evaluating CNNs for classifying underwater texture image patches of corals (animals) photographed on natural reefs.

title: A biometric-based model for fish species classification
reason: Fish species classification on images of individual landed fish photographed in a controlled imaging set-up (rotating object, fixed light and camera); no images of wild, free-ranging animals.

title: Rapid biomass and size-frequency estimates of edible jellyfish populations using drones
reason: Drone imagery with automated image processing (thresholding, particle analysis) to count and size wild jellyfish in a coastal lake.

title: Evaluation of passage and sorting of adult Pacific salmonids through a novel fish passage technology
reason: Evaluates a fish passage system that uses machine vision cameras and an image-based decision algorithm to measure and sort migrating adult salmonids returning from the Columbia River by size. Borderline: the image analysis is a built-in component of the system and the fish are hatchery-origin returning adults.

title: Sea Cucumber Image Dehazing Method by Fusion of Retinex and Dark Channel
reason: Image dehazing/enhancement of underwater sea cucumber images from aquaculture (sea cucumber breeding), i.e. farmed animals.

title: Benchmark database for fine-grained image classification of benthic macroinvertebrates
reason: Wild-collected benthic macroinvertebrates are preserved and imaged as specimens in a laboratory imaging set-up (cuvette filled with alcohol). The animals are not imaged in the wild.

title: A novel method for photo-identification of sea turtles using scale patterns on the front flippers
venue: Journal of Experimental Marine Biology and Ecology
reason: Photo-identification of wild nesting adult and hatchling sea turtles from flipper scale pattern images using APHIS matching software.

title: Color changes of fiddler crab between seasons and under stressful conditions: Patterns of changes in lightness differ between carapace and claw
venue: Journal of Experimental Marine Biology and Ecology
reason: Colour of wild fiddler crabs was measured with a handheld colorimeter (CIE L*a*b*), not from images or video, so no computer vision is used.

title: Benthic video image analysis facilitates monitoring of Dreissena populations across spatial scales
reason: Underwater video images of wild quagga mussels in the Great Lakes are processed with image software (colour-range thresholding) to estimate coverage, druse counts and density.

title: Step width and frontal plane trunk motion in bipedal chimpanzee and human walking
reason: Biomechanics study of trained research chimpanzees and humans walking on a laboratory runway, recorded with marker-based motion capture and force plates. No wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Massively parallel C. elegans tracking provides multi-dimensional fingerprints for phenotypic discovery
reason: Machine vision tracking platform for laboratory-cultured C. elegans model organisms on agar and multi-well plates for drug screening; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Object detection from dynamic scene using joint background modeling and fast deep learning classification
venue: Journal of Visual Communication and Image Representation
reason: Primary method paper on detecting humans and wild animals in camera-trap image sequences using background modelling and a CNN classifier.

title: Automated estimate of fish abundance through the autonomous imaging device GUARD1
reason: Primary study that develops an image segmentation and classification method to recognise and count free-ranging fishes in underwater images taken by an autonomous imaging device deployed at sea.

title: fvUnderwater sea cucumber identification based on Principal Component Analysis and Support Vector Machine
reason: Identification of farmed sea cucumbers in an aquaculture farm to support aquaculture automation; the animals are farmed, not wild.

title: Transferring deep knowledge for object recognition in Low-quality underwater videos
reason: CNN transfer-learning framework for recognising fish species in live underwater videos (Fish4Knowledge) of freely swimming fish; primary research.

title: A Brain Module for Scalable Control of Complex, Multi-motor Threat Displays
reason: Neuroscience study of laboratory-reared Drosophila melanogaster filmed in behaviour chambers; automated tracking and behaviour classification are used as tools, with no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Spatial and temporal effects of management on the reef seascape of a marine protected area in the Mexican Caribbean
reason: Benthic habitat mapping from multispectral satellite imagery (land/seascape cover classes); no individual animals are analysed as subjects.

title: Environmental and physiological determinants of huddling behavior of molting female southern elephant seals (Mirounga leonina)
reason: Physiological/behavioural field study of wild elephant seals; thermal images are only measured manually (polygons/spot temperatures in FLIR software) with no computer vision method developed or applied.

title: High-frequency observations from a deep-sea cabled observatory reveal seasonal overwintering of Neocalanus spp. in Barkley Canyon, NE Pacific: Insights into particulate organic carbon flux
reason: Automated image analysis of seafloor observatory video to count wild overwintering Neocalanus copepods in Barkley Canyon.

title: Autonomous Underwater Vehicle for Vision Based Tracking
reason: The vision-based tracking was tested only on a live goldfish in an aquarium tank and on a printed fish image. No wild or free-ranging animals were imaged.

title: A Support Vector Machine with Gabor Features for Animal Intrusion Detection in Agriculture Fields
reason: Computer vision pipeline (watershed segmentation, Gabor features, SVM) classifying images of nilgai (a wild animal intruding in crop fields) versus dog for animal intrusion detection.

title: Geometric-morphometric analysis of tooth pits and the identification of felid and hyenid agency in bone modification
reason: 3D structured-light digitisation and geometric morphometric classification of tooth pits (direct signs) left by free-ranging lions and hyenas at the modern Olduvai Carnivore Site, compared against pits made by animals in a nature park

title: Coral reef habitat mapping: A combination of object-based image analysis and ecological modelling
reason: The paper maps coral reef habitat: geomorphic zones and benthic cover from Landsat imagery, plus coral morphology predicted by a wave model. It is habitat mapping rather than computer vision on images of animals.

title: A continent-wide search for Antarctic petrel breeding sites with satellite remote sensing
reason: Satellite (Landsat-8) image analysis detecting guano stains of wild Antarctic petrel breeding colonies (direct signs) across Antarctica.

title: Using satellite imagery to assess the distribution and abundance of southern hairy-nosed wombats (Lasiorhinus latifrons)
reason: Wombat warrens were identified, counted and measured by manual visual interpretation of satellite imagery in Google Earth and SAS·Planet. The paper applies no computer vision or automated image analysis method.

title: Detecting mammals in UAV images: Best practices to address a substantially imbalanced dataset with deep learning
reason: Develops and evaluates a CNN-based detector for large mammals in UAV images of a Namibian wildlife reserve; primary research on free-ranging wildlife.

title: Coral reef applications of Sentinel-2: Coverage, characteristics, bathymetry and benthic mapping with comparison to Landsat 8
reason: Satellite (Sentinel-2/Landsat 8) remote sensing of coral reef habitat: bathymetry, geomorphic zones and benthic cover mapping. It maps habitat and land cover, not individual animals.

title: Application of UAV BVLOS remote sensing data for multi-faceted analysis of Antarctic ecosystem
reason: Wild penguins and seals were imaged from a UAV, but they were identified and counted by a person interpreting the orthophoto. No computer vision method was applied to the animals; SfM was used only to build the orthophoto.

title: Towards automated scyphistoma census in underwater imagery: A useful research and monitoring tool
reason: Develops a CNN-based detection and counting method for wild moon jellyfish polyps in underwater photographs taken in situ.

title: Estimating the population size of migrating Tibetan antelopesPantholops hodgsoniiwith unmanned aerial vehicles
reason: UAV aerial photographs of wild Tibetan antelopes were mosaicked into orthoimages, but animals were identified and counted manually by eye in ArcGIS; no computer vision method is applied to the animals.

title: A global effort to improve species monitoring for conservation
reason: The text is a set of Oryx conservation news items (ibis sightings by human observers, the IUCN Species Monitoring Specialist Group, a restoration evidence website). No image or video data are analysed and no computer vision method is used.

title: Spatial fidelity of workers predicts collective response to disturbance in a social insect
reason: Image-based automated tag tracking (BEEtag) of commercially obtained bumble bee colonies housed in indoor nest chambers but foraging freely in a natural outdoor environment; computer vision on video of partly free-ranging non-domestic insects, primary research.

title: Synchronization of speed, sound and iridescent color in a hummingbird aerial courtship dive
reason: Behavioural ecology study of wild hummingbird courtship dives; birds were tracked manually in video with a digitizing tool and gorget regions were manually selected in specimen photographs, so no automated computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Differential vulnerability to climate change yields novel deep-reef communities
reason: AUV seafloor images of wild sessile invertebrates were scored manually with the CATAMI scheme; the random forests model presence/absence against environmental covariates, not image content. No computer vision method is applied to the images.

title: An open-source platform for analyzing and sharing worm-behavior data
reason: Open database, file format and tracking software for laboratory C. elegans behaviour videos (strains, genotypes, ageing experiments); no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Fast animal pose estimation using deep neural networks
reason: Pose estimation method developed and evaluated only on laboratory fruit flies and laboratory mice filmed in indoor arenas; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Multi-modal survey of Adélie penguin mega-colonies reveals the Danger Islands as a seabird hotspot
reason: Primary study applying a deep neural network detector to UAV imagery to count nesting wild Adélie penguins in the Danger Islands, Antarctica.

title: Utilizing individual fish biomass and relative abundance models to map environmental niche associations of adult and juvenile targeted fishes
reason: Stereo-BRUV video of wild fish was annotated and measured manually with EventMeasure software; the analysis is statistical species distribution modelling (GAMs), with no computer vision method applied to the images.

title: Automated detection and manipulation of sleep in C. elegans reveals depolarization of a sleep-active neuron during mechanical stimulation-induced sleep deprivation
reason: Laboratory study of the model organism C. elegans cultured in microfluidic chambers and imaged by microscopy; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Detecting intermittent switching leadership in coupled dynamical systems
reason: The paper applies information-theoretic causality measures to trajectory time series: simulated particles, a fish model, and 3D bird trajectories taken from a previously published dataset. The paper itself does no image or video analysis.

title: Automatic multiple zebrafish tracking based on improved HOG features
reason: Multi-individual tracking of laboratory zebrafish (plus drosophila and mouse models) filmed in tanks in a laboratory observation system; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Examining the viability of dorsal fin pigmentation for individual identification of poorly-marked delphinids
reason: Primary study extracting computer vision features from field photographs of free-ranging common dolphin dorsal fins to identify individuals.

title: Underwater hyperspectral imaging as an in situ taxonomic tool for deep-sea megafauna
reason: Applies hyperspectral image analysis (spectral contrast angle and SVM classification) to detect and classify wild deep-sea benthic megafauna imaged in situ from an ROV.

title: Tracking Fish Abundance by Underwater Image Recognition
reason: Primary study developing a genetic-programming-based image recognition method to detect and count free-ranging fish in images from a cabled underwater observatory in a marine reserve.

title: Coordinated Turning Behaviour of Loitering Honeybees
reason: Behavioural kinematics study of honeybees from a managed, freely foraging hive. Bee positions were digitised manually in stereo video and triangulated; no automated computer vision method is developed or evaluated.

title: DolFin: an innovative digital platform for studying Risso’s dolphins in the Northern Ionian Sea (North-eastern Central Mediterranean)
reason: Primary study presenting an automated photo-identification algorithm (SPIR, SURF-based) applied to dorsal fin photos of free-ranging Risso's dolphins photographed during vessel surveys in the Gulf of Taranto.

title: Data Descriptor: Time-lapse imagery and volunteer classifications from the Zooniverse Penguin Watch project
reason: Data descriptor presenting time-lapse images of wild penguin colonies with citizen-science click annotations; annotations are aggregated by clustering volunteer clicks and validated against expert counts. No computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated on the images; computer vision is only named as a future use of the data.

title: Training CNNs with image patches for object localisation
reason: Generic object-localisation method; animals are a case study using ImageNet classes, wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Automatic underwater moving object detection using multi‐feature integration framework in complex backgrounds
reason: Proposes a background-modelling method for moving object detection and evaluates it on Fish4Knowledge underwater videos recorded by static underwater cameras; the moving objects are free-ranging fish, although the paper does not name them as such.

title: Animal classification using facial images with score‐level fusion
reason: Generic image-classification method (score-level fusion of CNN and KFA features) tested only on the LHI-Animal-Faces benchmark of animal head images, which includes a human class and domestic animals; the paper does not state that the images show wild or free-ranging animals and wildlife is not the stated application.

title: Automated monitoring of behavior reveals bursty interaction patterns and rapid spreading dynamics in honeybee social networks
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
reason: Barcoded honeybees from experimentally established colonies are imaged in a glass-walled observation hive kept in a dark, temperature-controlled room; this is a laboratory set-up with managed (domestic) bees, not wild free-ranging animals.

title: Automatically identifying, counting, and describing wild animals in camera-trap images with deep learning
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
reason: Trains deep CNNs to identify, count and describe wild animals in camera-trap images from Serengeti National Park.

title: Distance-dependent defensive coloration in the poison frog Dendrobates tinctorius , Dendrobatidae
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
reason: Analyses in situ photographs of wild Dendrobates tinctorius with log-Gabor filter features and SVM classification to separate frog from background; additional ex situ UV photos of captive frogs.

title: Conserved behavioral circuits govern high-speed decision-making in wild fish shoals
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
reason: Wild reef fish filmed in situ by GoPro cameras on a coral reef; computer vision software tracks the fish's positions and headings to study how they escape threats.

title: Using an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) to study wild yak in the highest desert in the world
reason: UAV survey of wild yak in which animals are counted, outlined and sized manually and movement paths are vectorized in GIS; images are only mosaicked with stitching software and no automated computer vision analysis of animals is performed.

title: Very high-resolution mapping of emerging biogenic reefs using airborne optical imagery and neural network: the honeycomb worm (Sabellaria alveolata) case study
reason: Applies a neural network to airborne multispectral imagery to map the relative abundance of wild honeycomb worm (Sabellaria alveolata) reefs, using field photoquadrats as ground truth.

title: Very high resolution mapping of coral reef state using airborne bathymetric LiDAR surface-intensity and drone imagery
reason: Borderline include: a neural network classifies airborne LiDAR rasters, trained on drone imagery, into reef states defined by wild reef-building coral genera (animals) in a natural lagoon. It could alternatively be read as benthic habitat mapping (E-PLANT).

title: Fine resolution remote sensing of species in terrestrial and coastal ecosystems
reason: Editorial preface summarising a special issue on remote sensing species mapping (mainly vegetation and coral reef habitats); not primary research and no analysis of wild animal images.

title: Hot monkey, cold reality: surveying rainforest canopy mammals using drone-mounted thermal infrared sensors
reason: Drone thermal and RGB survey of wild canopy mammals, but animals were detected and identified manually by operators; no computer vision method was developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Ensemble of deep learning, visual and acoustic features for music genre classification
reason: Music genre classification from audio; the animal data are sound recordings (bird vocalisations, whale calls) converted to spectrogram-type images. No images or video of animals are analysed.

title: Elephant detection using boundary sense deep learning (BSDL) architecture
venue: Journal of Experimental & Theoretical Artificial Intelligence
reason: Elephant images E1-E4 were taken in elephant camps with keepers placing the animals inside the sensor unit; the only other data are 604 images from unspecified net sources. No wild or free-ranging animals are stated in the analysed data, although the intended application is human-elephant conflict.

title: Can ensemble techniques improve coral reef habitat classification accuracy using multispectral data?
reason: Satellite-based benthic habitat / bottom-cover mapping (dense coral, sparse coral, coral rubble, sand). The subject is habitat cover classes rather than animals as such, so it is coded as habitat/land-cover only, although corals are wild animals.

title: Use of a semi-automated object based analysis to map benthic composition, Heron Reef, Southern Great Barrier Reef
reason: The study maps benthic habitat cover (coral, algae, sand, rubble, rock) from satellite imagery with OBIA. This is habitat or land-cover mapping, not computer vision on images of animals.

title: Autonomous monitoring framework for resource-constrained environments
reason: Primary study deploying a camera-based wildlife monitoring system in a national park, using image differencing to confirm animal presence in motion-triggered images; a second case study on road temperature monitoring is not vision-based.

title: An analysis of rotation matrix and colour constancy data augmentation in classifying images of animals
reason: Data augmentation method for CNN classification of animal images. One dataset is UAV imagery of cows (livestock); the other two are bird and fish species datasets of non-domestic animals, so wild taxa appear alongside domestic ones. The paper does not state how the bird and fish images were taken.

title: Body-terrain interaction affects large bump traversal of insects and legged robots
reason: Laboratory biomechanics study of purchased discoid cockroaches and a legged robot running over a bump on an obstacle track; video is used only for fiducial-tag (BEEtag) motion tracking, no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Crowdsourcing annotation system of object counting dataset for deep learning algorithm
venue: IOP Conference Series Earth and Environmental Science
reason: The paper describes a crowdsourcing annotation and validation system for object-counting datasets. Its sample images show coins, so no animals and no wildlife application are involved.

title: Honey Bees Species Differentiation using Geometric Morphometric on Wing Venations
venue: IOP Conference Series Earth and Environmental Science
reason: Landmarks on microscope photos of cut wings from collected bee specimens were placed by hand in tpsDig2, then analysed with geometric morphometrics and statistics. No automated computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Bears habituate to the repeated exposure of a novel stimulus, unmanned aircraft systems
reason: The study flies a drone over captive bears and measures their heart rate with implanted cardiac biologgers. No images or video are analysed, and the animals are captive.

title: Diel, seasonal, and interannual patterns in mesozooplankton abundance in the Sargasso Sea
reason: Applies ZooScan imaging with machine-learning identification software (Zooprocess/PkID) to classify and count wild marine mesozooplankton collected by net tows in the Sargasso Sea; the animals are field-collected, preserved samples imaged in the lab.

title: Monitoring the mammalian fauna of urban areas using remote cameras and citizen science
reason: The study evaluates human (citizen scientist) classification of urban camera-trap images against experts. No automated image analysis produces any result; the only image processing is frame differencing to highlight movement as a visual aid for the human classifiers.

title: Interception by two predatory fly species is explained by a proportional navigation feedback controller
venue: Journal of The Royal Society Interface
reason: Behavioural study that applies stereo high-speed video tracking and 3D trajectory reconstruction to predatory flights of wild, in situ robber flies (Holcocephala fusca) and lab-reared or greenhouse killer flies (Coenosia attenuata). Borderline: image analysis is a measurement step, the main contribution is guidance-law modelling, and the paper does not say whether tracking was automatic.

title: The bat–bird–bug battle: daily flight activity of insects and their predators over a rice field revealed by high-resolution Scheimpflug Lidar
reason: Scheimpflug Lidar imaging (time-range maps from a CMOS line detector) is used to detect free-flying wild insects, bats and birds over a rice field and sort them into size classes. The animals are wild, not livestock, and the paper studies their ecology. Lidar time-range data are treated here as image data.

title: Repeatable group differences in the collective behaviour of stickleback shoals across ecological contexts
venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences
reason: Wild-caught sticklebacks were kept in lab housing and filmed in experimental laboratory tanks. All analysed video shows a laboratory set-up, not free-ranging animals.

title: Inconspicuous echolocation in hoary bats ( Lasiurus cinereus )
venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences
reason: Wild hoary bats were recorded in the field with calibrated infrared video camera arrays, and their 3D flight trajectories were reconstructed from the video to analyse echolocation behaviour.

title: Experimental disturbances reveal group-level costs of social instability
venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences
reason: Behavioural experiment on captive zebra finch colonies housed in indoor aviaries; automated tag-based video tracking is used, but no wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Inferring the rules of social interaction in migrating caribou
venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences
reason: Primary study that uses UAV video and computer vision tracking (OpenCV) to obtain trajectories of wild, free-ranging migrating caribou, then infers social interaction rules from them.

title: Using imaging photoplethysmography for heart rate estimation in non-human primates
reason: Pulse rate is estimated from facial videos of head-stabilized laboratory rhesus monkeys seated in a primate chair in an experimental room; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Implementing new portable touchscreen-setups to enhance cognitive research and enrich zoo-housed animals
reason: The paper describes touchscreen hardware for cognitive testing of zoo-housed great apes. It analyses touch responses, not images, and the animals are captive only.

title: Machine learning to classify animal species in camera trap images: applications in ecology
reason: Trains and evaluates a CNN to classify wildlife species in camera trap images from field sites in the United States, Canada and Tanzania; some classes are domestic (cattle, horses).

title: Measuring Orangutan nest structure using Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) and ImageJ
reason: The UAV images of orangutan nests (direct signs of rehabilitant orangutans in a forest reserve) were measured by hand in ImageJ against a leaf-length scale. No automated or computer vision analysis was developed or applied.

title: Monkey Features Location Identification Using Convolutional Neural Networks
reason: Proposes a CNN for keypoint (nose, shoulders) localisation on monkey images, which the paper describes as showing monkeys in their natural environment.

title: An open source platform for analyzing and sharing worm behavior data
reason: Open database, file format and tracking software for laboratory C. elegans behaviour videos (model organism tracking experiments); no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Taxonomic Classification of Ants (Formicidae) from Images using Deep Learning
reason: Classifies ant species from images of mounted museum specimens (AntWeb and Naturalis collection), not living free-ranging animals.

title: Image analysis for taxonomic identification of Javanese butterflies
reason: Images are of pinned/stored museum butterfly specimens from the Naturalis collection (plus orchid plant photos); no live wild animals analysed.

title: A comparison of visual features used by humans and machines to classify wildlife
reason: Trains a CNN to classify wild African mammal species in camera-trap images from Gorongosa National Park and interprets the learned features.

title: Underwater-Drone With Panoramic Camera for Automatic Fish Recognition Based on Deep Learning
reason: The fish recognition experiments use only web images of popular aquarium fish; no images of wild, free-ranging fish are analysed (drone field images are left to future work).

title: Autoencoder-Combined Generative Adversarial Networks for Synthetic Image Data Generation and Detection of Jellyfish Swarm
reason: Proposes an autoencoder-combined GAN to synthesise jellyfish image patches and trains an FCN plus regression network to estimate jellyfish swarm density on UAV video of a wild jellyfish bloom in the sea.

title: A Biological Sensor System Using Computer Vision for Water Quality Monitoring
reason: Computer vision analysis of zebra fish behaviour in a glass tank during a laboratory toxicity experiment for water quality monitoring; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Improving Transfer Learning and Squeeze- and-Excitation Networks for Small-Scale Fine-Grained Fish Image Classification
reason: Proposes a CNN method for fine-grained fish species image classification, evaluated on fish image datasets (Croatian, QUT, Fish4Knowledge); fish are the stated subject. The paper does not itself state whether the fish in the datasets are wild or captive.

title: BioSense: Real-Time Object Tracking for Animal Movement and Behavior Research
venue: IEEE Applied Imagery Pattern Recognition Workshop
reason: General-purpose tracking software for animal behavior experiments, evaluated on six experiment-style videos (bee, shiner, spider, termite, treehopper, tadpole); the paper does not state that any footage shows wild, free-ranging animals and frames the data as behavior research experiments.

title: Dolphin Recognition with Adaptive Hybrid Saliency Detection for Deep Learning Based on DenseNet Recognition
venue: 2018 IEEE Asia Pacific Conference on Circuits and Systems Apccas 2018
reason: Primary study proposing a saliency-masking plus DenseNet121 method for individual identification of dolphins photographed at sea, for wildlife conservation.

title: Detection, Localization and Classification of Fish and Fish Species in Poor Conditions using Convolutional Neural Networks
reason: CNN object detector for fish detection and species classification; trained on aquarium footage and evaluated on images of free-ranging fish in the Baltic Sea and the Weser river.

title: Mesobot: An Autonomous Underwater Vehicle for Tracking and Sampling Midwater Targets
reason: Design and concept paper for a planned autonomous underwater vehicle. It describes hardware, mission profile and mission-executive software in the future tense; no images of animals are analysed and no computer vision experiment or evaluation is reported.

title: Multi-Class Object Detection from Aerial Images Using Mask R-CNN
venue: IEEE International Conference on Big Data (BigData)
reason: The paper detects military and civilian vehicles and road obstacles in synthetic aerial images. No animals are analysed.

title: Face Recognition: Primates in the Wild
venue: IEEE International Conference on Biometrics: Theory, Applications and Systems (BTAS)
reason: Proposes a CNN for individual face recognition of primates; data include wild golden monkeys in Volcanoes National Park and wild chimpanzees (C-Tai) together with captive lemurs and zoo chimpanzees.

title: Active Learning to Assist Annotation of Aerial Images in Environmental Surveys
venue: International Conference on Content-Based Multimedia Indexing (CBMI)
reason: The objects detected in aerial images are humans gathering shellfish, not wild animals.

title: Deep Learning for Marine Resources Classification in Non-Structured Scenarios: Training vs. Transfer Learning
reason: Applies CNN classification to images of wild-caught marine fish species captured by onboard fishing-boat cameras for fisheries monitoring and conservation.

title: Deep learning object detection methods for ecological camera trap data
venue: Proceedings 2018 15th Conference on Computer and Robot Vision Crv 2018
reason: Primary study training and comparing deep learning object detectors (Faster R-CNN, YOLO v2.0) on camera trap images of wild animals.

title: Underwater Fish Detection Using Deep Learning for Water Power Applications
venue: International Conference on Computational Science and Computational Intelligence (CSCI)
reason: YOLOv3 is trained and evaluated to detect free-ranging fish in underwater video recorded at real-world tidal, river and dam water power sites.

title: Lean Multiclass Crowdsourcing
venue: IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings - IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings
reason: Proposes a method combining crowdsourced worker-skill models with computer vision (Inception-v3 features + SVM) to label species in images of wild birds from NABirds and iNaturalist.

title: Lions and Tigers and Bears: Capturing Non-rigid, 3D, Articulated Shape from Images
venue: IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings - IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings
reason: Method paper reconstructing 3D articulated animal shape and texture from images/video of quadrupeds. Data mix green-screen (captive) footage, YouTube videos of wild species such as bear, wolf and rhino, domestic animals (dog, pig, horse, cow) and a zoo-filmed Tasmanian tiger. The paper does not explicitly state that the analysed YouTube frames show free-ranging animals, so inclusion rests on a lenient reading.

title: Large Scale Fine-Grained Categorization and Domain-Specific Transfer Learning
venue: IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings - IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings
reason: Generic fine-grained visual categorization and transfer learning paper; animals (birds, dogs, iNaturalist species) appear only as classes of benchmarks alongside cars, aircraft, food and flowers. Wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: People, Penguins and Petri Dishes: Adapting Object Counting Models to New Visual Domains and Object Types Without Forgetting
venue: IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings - IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings
reason: Multi-domain CNN object counting method; wildlife counting (penguin colonies, Penguins dataset) is one of the four stated application domains and is evaluated explicitly, alongside crowds, vehicles and cells.

title: The iNaturalist Species Classification and Detection Dataset
venue: IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings - IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings
reason: Primary dataset paper presenting citizen-science photographs of plant and animal species taken in the wild, with baseline CNN classification and detection experiments; conservation and field biology are stated applications.

title: Automated Analysis of Marine Video with Limited Data

reason: CNN detection, classification and tracking applied to UAV footage of wild sharks and rays and underwater images of wild fish.

title: A Comparison of Deep Learning Methods for Semantic Segmentation of Coral Reef Survey Images
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)
reason: Primary study comparing CNN and FCNN methods for classifying and segmenting in situ underwater images of wild coral reef organisms (corals, sea fans, other octocorals).

title: Stingray Detection of Aerial Images Using Augmented Training Images Generated by a Conditional Generative Model
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)
reason: Deep-learning detection of wild stingrays in UAV aerial sea-surface images, with GAN-like augmentation.

title: Camera calibration for underwater 3D reconstruction based on ray tracing using snell's law
venue: IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops
reason: Camera calibration method for 3D reconstruction in a laboratory aquarium, evaluated only on a calibration rod with coloured balls; no animals and no wild animals are imaged.

title: Large-Scale Ecological Analyses of Animals in the Wild Using Computer Vision
venue: IEEE/CVF Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition Workshops (CVPRW)
reason: Applies CNN species classification to camera trap images of wild animals in Costa Rica and SIFT-based individual jaguar identification on wild and zoo images.

title: Smart Surveillance: A Nature Ecological Intelligent Surveillance System with Robotic Observation Cameras and Environment Factors Sensors
venue: IEEE International Conference on Cyber Technology in Automation, Control, and Intelligent Systems
reason: Presents a surveillance system with PTZ cameras that detects, classifies and tracks wild animals (panda, snow leopard, etc.) in video.

title: CNN Based Wildlife Recognition with Super-Pixel Segmentation for Ecological Surveillance
venue: IEEE International Conference on Cyber Technology in Automation, Control, and Intelligent Systems
reason: Proposes SLIC super-pixel preprocessing plus a CNN for species classification of wild animals in camera-trap images from Chinese nature reserves.

title: Performance Comparison of Deep Learning Techniques for Recognizing Birds in Aerial Images
venue: IEEE International Conference on Data Science in Cyberspace
reason: Evaluates deep learning detection and segmentation methods on aerial images of wild waterfowl and water birds in Illinois wetlands.

title: Determination of the big mammals migration corridors in the particular areas using remotely-operating intelligent camera system
venue: 12th International Conference Elektro 2018 2018 Elektro Conference Proceedings
reason: Computer vision system detecting, tracking and classifying large mammals in video; the data include animals filmed in natural conditions and in a zoo.

title: Research on Fish Image Classification Based on Transfer Learning and Convolutional Neural Network Model
venue: International Conference on Natural Computation, Fuzzy Systems and Knowledge Discovery (ICNC-FSKD)
reason: Fish images come from the internet and from cameras in an aquarium. The paper never says that any image shows wild or free-ranging fish, and the classes are mostly ornamental fish (goldfish, arowana).

title: Environmental Monitoring Using Low-Cost Hardware and Infrastructureless Wireless Communication
reason: Hardware/communication platform paper for environmental monitoring; the only vision component is generic on-device concept detection (InceptionNet v3) on an undescribed image set, with no stated wildlife subject in the analysed images.

title: Coarse-To-Fine Segmentation Refinement and Missing Shape Recovery for Halibut Fish
venue: IEEE Global Conference on Signal and Information Processing
reason: Proposes a contour-based segmentation refinement method for images of wild-caught halibut in a chute-based electronic monitoring system for fisheries surveys (not aquaculture).

title: Fish Tracking and Counting using Image Processing
venue: IEEE International Conference on Humanoid, Nanotechnology, Information Technology, Communication and Control, Environment, and Management (HNICEM)
reason: Fish are placed on a purpose-built plywood fish pass prototype and photographed from above in a controlled experimental set-up; no wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: A self induced warning system for wild animal trespassing using machine vision system
venue: Proceedings of IEEE International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Communication for Smart World I2c2sw 2018
reason: Applies image-based pattern matching to camera images to detect wild elephants approaching villages at the forest-village border.

title: Detection of Birds in the Wild using Deep Learning Methods
venue: International Conference for Convergence in Technology (I2CT)
reason: Comparative evaluation of deep learning object detectors (YOLOv2, YOLOv3, Mask R-CNN) on images of birds in the wild; primary research.

title: Vision Based Technique for Animal Detection
venue: 2018 International Conference On Advances in Communication and Computing Technology (ICACCT)
reason: Vision-based detection of animals on roads for collision avoidance; the only animals the paper states it tested on are domestic ones (dog, cow, goat, buffalo) on Indian roads. Wild animals are named only as motivation in the introduction.

title: Low Resolution Image Fish Classification Using Convolutional Neural Network
reason: Proposes a CNN to classify fish species in low-resolution images from the FishCLEF 2015 dataset of reef fish; primary computer vision research on wild animals.

title: Underwater Fish Species Classification using Convolutional Neural Network and Deep Learning
venue: 2017 9th International Conference on Advances in Pattern Recognition Icapr 2017
reason: Proposes a CNN with image-processing preprocessing to classify fish species in underwater images from the Fish4Knowledge dataset.

title: Development of Application for Forest Insect Classification using CNN
venue: International Conference on Control, Automation, Robotics and Vision (ICARCV)
reason: CNN classification of 30 forest insect taxa from web photographs (insects on petals/leaves) and specimen images, for a mobile identification app; part of the data plausibly shows free-ranging insects.

title: Multi-Object Tracking of Swarms with Active Target Avoidance
venue: 2018 15th International Conference on Control Automation Robotics and Vision Icarcv 2018
reason: Generic 3D multi-object tracking method evaluated only on synthetic Reynolds-flocking simulation data; no images of real wild animals are analysed.

title: Real-World Field Snail Detection and Tracking
venue: International Conference on Control, Automation, Robotics and Vision (ICARCV)
reason: Detection and tracking of pest snails on farmland for smart farming and pest control; crop pests in production fall under E-AGRI.

title: Multi-Scale Object Detection with Feature Fusion and Region Objectness Network
venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics Speech and Signal Processing
reason: Proposes a multi-scale detection CNN that is evaluated on a self-built dataset of wild birds photographed in the Shenzhen Bay coastal wetland, alongside a car dataset.

title: Classification of Corals in Reflectance and Fluorescence Images Using Convolutional Neural Network Representations
venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics Speech and Signal Processing
reason: Applies CNN-feature-based classification to point-annotated images of corals photographed in a nighttime reef survey in the Red Sea.

title: The Monkeys are Coming ─ Design of Agricultural Damage Warning System by IoT-Based Objects Detection and Tracking
venue: IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics - Taiwan (ICCE-Taiwan)
reason: Detects wild Taiwan macaques entering farm fields from IP camera images to warn farmers; the animals are wild crop raiders, not livestock.

title: The Design of Automatic Bird Data Capture Systems
venue: IEEE International Conference on Consumer Electronics - Taiwan (ICCE-Taiwan)
reason: Describes a web crawler system that collects bird posts and pictures from Facebook fan pages. Filtering is done by matching text to a bird database and by manual human review. No image analysis is performed; image recognition is only mentioned as future work.

title: Active Learning for the Classification of Species in Underwater Images from a Fixed Observatory
venue: Proceedings 2017 IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision Workshops Iccvw 2017
reason: Proposes an active learning method to classify image patches of wild marine species (starfish, crab, sea urchin) from a fixed underwater observatory at a coral reef.

title: Pareto Optimization of Parameter Selection Speeds Up and Improves Quality of Motion Computation: Applying Evolutionary Multi-objective Optimization to Randomized-Subspace Robust PCA
venue: IEEE ... International Conference on Data Mining workshops
reason: Primary study that optimises a motion-template (foreground extraction) method on camera-trap images of wild snow leopards.

title: Identification and mapping of coral reefs using Landsat 8 OLI in Astola Island, Pakistan coastal ocean
reason: Benthic habitat mapping (coral reef and seagrass classes) from Landsat 8 satellite imagery; it is habitat/land-cover style mapping, not image analysis of individual animals.

title: High-speed CAMShift Tracking of Insect on GPU
venue: IEEE International Conference on Information and Automation (ICIA)
reason: GPU CAMShift tracking algorithm tested on high-speed video of a bee and a fly recorded on a laboratory high-speed vision platform, plus a rotating fan target and a generic VOT2014 sequence; no wild or free-ranging animals are stated.

title: Flying Bird Detection under Shaking Background
venue: IEEE International Conference on Information and Automation (ICIA)
reason: Proposes a motion-detection algorithm for detecting free-flying wild birds in video with a shaking background.

title: Counting Fish in Sonar Images
venue: Proceedings - International Conference on Image Processing
reason: Deep CNN counting of fish in imaging sonar video frames recorded in river/sea environments; imaging sonar is image data, so it is not audio-only.

title: Real-Time Underwater Fish Tracking Based on Adaptive Multi-Appearance Model
venue: Proceedings - International Conference on Image Processing
reason: Proposes a correlation-filter tracking method for fish in underwater videos recorded in natural environments.

title: Changing Background to Foreground: An Augmentation Method Based on Conditional Generative Network for Stingray Detection
venue: Proceedings - International Conference on Image Processing
reason: Proposes a generative data augmentation method to improve CNN detection of wild stingrays in UAV aerial sea-surface videos.

title: IoT-Enabled Smart Elephant Detection System for Combating Human Elephant Conflict
venue: International Conference on Information Technology Research (ICITR)
reason: The system detects elephants with a geophone (seismic sensor) and does no image or video analysis. In testing, elephant footsteps were simulated by hitting the ground with a wooden mallet, so no real animals were recorded.

title: Fine-Grained Bird Classification Based on Low-Dimensional Bilinear Model
venue: IEEE International Conference on Image, Vision and Computing (ICIVC)
reason: Proposes a CNN-based fine-grained bird species classification model, evaluated on CUB-200-2011 and a new web-collected dataset of birds in China.

title: Automatic Detection of Moving Baw Baw Frogs in Camera Trap Videos
venue: IEEE International Conference on Mechatronics and Automation (ICMA)
reason: Motion detection in camera-trap videos of Baw Baw Frogs, but all recordings come from a captive population at the Melbourne Zoo; no wild or free-ranging animals in the analysed data.

title: Evaluation of Different Features and Classifiers for Classification of Rays from Underwater Digital Images
reason: Compares image features and classifiers for classifying wild rays (blue-spotted and manta) in underwater images.

title: Towards Automatic Detection of Monkey Faces
venue: Proceedings - International Conference on Pattern Recognition/Proceedings/International Conference on Pattern Recognition
reason: Applies and evaluates face detection (Viola-Jones, Faster R-CNN) on images/video of wild macaques.

title: Single Shot Feature Aggregation Network for Underwater Object Detection
venue: Proceedings - International Conference on Pattern Recognition/Proceedings/International Conference on Pattern Recognition
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for marine organisms (sea cucumber, sea urchin, scallop) in real coastal underwater images; the paper does not describe the animals as farmed or captive.

title: Fish Detection from Low Visibility Underwater Videos
venue: Proceedings - International Conference on Pattern Recognition/Proceedings/International Conference on Pattern Recognition
reason: Primary study proposing a background-subtraction-based computer vision framework to detect fish in underwater videos recorded in a natural environment (fish passing a camera in a real underwater setting).

title: CNN for Butterfly Classification
venue: International Conference on Recent Innovations in Electrical, Electronics & Communication Engineering (ICRIEECE)
reason: Applies a CNN to classify butterfly species from images for electronic field guides; butterflies are wild non-domestic animals, images web-scraped.

title: Species recognition technology based on migration learning and data augmentation
venue: International Conference on Systems and Informatics (ICSAI)
reason: Primary study applying CNN transfer learning to classify images of rare, non-domestic animal species for conservation. The paper does not state where or how the images were taken, so whether the animals are wild or captive is not reported; included because the stated subject is rare wildlife.

title: Enhanced Image Edge Detection Methods for Crab Species Identification
reason: Edge detection on crab images aimed at automating the commercial marine food industry (seafood packaging/sorting). The paper does not say whether the crabs are wild or where they came from. The application is food production, not wildlife.

title: JellyMonitor: automated detection of jellyfish in sonar images using neural networks
reason: Develops a blob detection, tracking and CNN classification pipeline on imaging-sonar frames of moon jellyfish; data include captive tank jellyfish, released jellyfish in a harbour and wild jellyfish off Oban.

title: Recognition of Endangered Pantanal Animal Species using Deep Learning Methods
reason: Primary study proposing a thermal+RGB region-proposal CNN method to detect and classify eight Pantanal wildlife species; the paper states the test images were taken under real conditions in a wild forest. The acknowledgements thank a wildlife rehabilitation centre for assistance, but the paper does not state that the animals were captive.

title: Assessing fish abundance from underwater video using deep neural networks
reason: Faster R-CNN detection and species recognition of wild fish and crustaceans in underwater video from beaches and estuaries in southeast Queensland.

title: Transfer Learning with deep Convolutional Neural Network for Underwater Live Fish Recognition
venue: IEEE International Conference on Image Processing, Applications and Systems (IPAS)
reason: Transfer-learning CNN for species classification of live fish in underwater images from the open sea.

title: Vision-Based Autonomous Underwater Swimming in Dense Coral for Combined Collision Avoidance and Target Selection
venue: IEEE/RSJ International Conference on Intelligent Robots and Systems (IROS)
reason: A CNN-based vision controller is trained and evaluated on underwater images of wild coral reef in the open ocean, with close-range coral monitoring as the stated application. Coral (a sessile wild animal) is the visual target and an automated coral classifier measures coral coverage. Borderline case: the paper's main focus is robot navigation rather than the coral itself.

title: PCA-Based Animal Classification System
venue: International Symposium on Multidisciplinary Studies and Innovative Technologies (ISMSIT)
reason: PCA-based classification of images of domestic animals (cow, cat, dog, goat, rabbit); motivated by pet identification; no wild or free-ranging animals in the analysed data.

title: Real-Time Drone Surveillance and Population Estimation of Marine Animals from Aerial Imagery
venue: International Conference on Image and Vision Computing New Zealand (IVCNZ)
reason: Deep learning detection and counting of wild dolphins and stingrays in drone video from Queensland beaches.

title: Individual Common Dolphin Identification Via Metric Embedding Learning
venue: International Conference on Image and Vision Computing New Zealand (IVCNZ)
reason: Primary study applying a triplet-loss CNN to field photographs of dorsal fins of wild New Zealand common dolphins for individual identification.

title: Hidden Features: Experiments with Feature Transfer for Fine-Grained Multi-Class and One-Class Image Categorization
venue: International Conference on Image and Vision Computing New Zealand (IVCNZ)
reason: Animal images are of museum moth specimens photographed in dorsal view (plus plant branches). No live or free-ranging animals are imaged, so the paper falls under museum specimens.

title: Fine-grained Collaborative K-Means Clustering
venue: International Conference on Image and Vision Computing New Zealand (IVCNZ)
reason: Proposes a clustering method for fine-grained species recognition and tests it on bird and butterfly species image datasets. It also introduces a new dataset of Indian butterflies, and the paper's motivation is recognising endangered species. Wildlife species recognition is the stated application.

title: Deep Image Representations for Coral Image Classification
reason: Deep learning classification of wild corals in AUV seafloor imagery from Western Australian reefs, with coral cover analysis.

title: A Low-Complexity Mosaicing Algorithm for Stock Assessment of Seabed-Burrowing Species
reason: Primary study proposing a video mosaicing (image registration and blending) algorithm for underwater TV survey footage of the seabed, used to count burrows (direct signs) of wild Nephrops for stock assessment.

title: Marine Animal Classification With Correntropy-Loss-Based Multiview Learning
reason: Proposes correntropy-loss multi-view learning for classifying marine animals. It is evaluated on the Taiwan sea fish (Fish4Knowledge) colour images and on Lidar images of animal replicas in a test tank. The sea fish data are taken to show free-ranging fish, although the paper does not say this outright.

title: An Optical Image Transmission System for Deep Sea Creature Sampling Missions Using Autonomous Underwater Vehicle
reason: Image processing system (enhancement, saliency-based selection of images containing marine life, compression) applied to AUV seafloor images of wild deep-sea creatures in the Sea of Okhotsk.

title: Time Series based Gastropod Classification
venue: International Conference on Knowledge and Smart Technology
reason: The paper classifies gastropod (mollusk) shells from images in a conchology database. These are shell specimen images, not images of free-ranging animals in the field. Most of the text is garbled, so this is the best reading available.

title: LOOP Descriptor: Local Optimal-Oriented Pattern
reason: Proposes a hand-crafted image descriptor for fine-grained species recognition of lepidoptera (moths/butterflies), a wild, non-domestic insect group, and introduces a new NZ Lepidoptera dataset aimed at native species recognition. The images' capture conditions are not described.

title: Landmarks Detection by Applying Deep Networks
venue: International Conference on Multimedia Analysis and Pattern Recognition (MAPR)
reason: Landmark prediction on images of beetle body parts (pronotum) from a specimen collection, all photographed with the same camera under the same controlled conditions. These are not images of free-ranging animals in the field.

title: Dynamic Behavior of Running Insect Activated by High-Speed Microdroplets Manipulation
venue: International Conference on Manipulation, Automation and Robotics at Small Scales (MARSS)
reason: A laboratory robotic set-up that visually tracks a single ant placed in a wall-less container under a high-speed camera and stimulates it with microdroplets; no wild or free-ranging animals in the field.

title: The promise of machine learning in the Risso’s dolphin Grampus griseus photo-identification
venue: IEEE International Workshop on Metrology for the Sea; Learning to Measure Sea Health Parameters (MetroSea)
reason: Develops an automated photo-identification method (SIFT + PCA + RUSBoost) on photographs of wild Risso's dolphins taken during vessel-based surveys in the Gulf of Taranto.

title: Site fidelity, residency and habitat use of the Risso’s dolphin Grampus griseus in the Gulf of Taranto (Northern Ionian Sea, Central-eastern Mediterranean Sea) by photo-identification
venue: IEEE International Workshop on Metrology for the Sea; Learning to Measure Sea Health Parameters (MetroSea)
reason: Photo-identification of wild Risso's dolphins is done manually: a MATLAB routine only displays reference images for the user to click on. No automated image analysis is applied.

title: Exploiting species-distinctive visual cues towards the automated photo-identification of the Risso’s dolphin Grampus griseus
venue: IEEE International Workshop on Metrology for the Sea; Learning to Measure Sea Health Parameters (MetroSea)

title: MDNet: Multi-Patch Dense Network for Coral Classification
reason: Proposes a CNN to classify coral taxa from underwater reef survey images of wild coral reefs (MLC dataset).

title: GPU-Assisted Learning on an Autonomous Marine Robot for Vision-Based Navigation and Image Understanding
reason: Autonomous underwater robot applies a DCNN to classify live coral (wild animals) in reef imagery, alongside vision-based navigation.

title: Embedded Online Fish Detection and Tracking System via YOLOv3 and Parallel Correlation Filter
reason: Develops YOLOv3 + parallel correlation filter fish detection and tracking on underwater video of fish recorded in the sea (Orchid Island, Shandong sea areas).

title: Sea urchin survey by small ROV : – Study of the Urchin barren –
reason: Applies a machine learning image classifier to ROV video to detect and count wild sea urchins in Shizugawa bay, Japan.

title: Transferred Parallel Convolutional Neural Network for Large Imbalanced Plankton Database Classification
reason: CNN classification of in situ plankton images (WHOI-Plankton from the Imaging FlowCytobot) showing the natural distribution of plankton in the ocean; the paper proposes a method for class imbalance.

title: Development of a Towed Optical Camera Array System (SSS: Speedy Sea Scanner) for Sea Environmental Monitoring
reason: Develops a towed camera array for seabed habitat mapping (orthophotos, 3D models of coral and seagrass areas). It does not analyse animals as subjects, so it is habitat-only monitoring.

title: Towards Automated Fish Detection Using Convolutional Neural Networks
reason: Applies a CNN object detector (SSD Inception v2) to AUV seafloor imagery of wild fish, sea stars and sponges in their natural habitat for fisheries stock assessment.

title: Deep Pyramidal Residual Networks for Plankton Image Classification
reason: Applies CNN (PyramidNet) to classify images of marine plankton collected in situ by the Imaging FlowCytobot; plankton are free-living, non-domestic organisms.

title: Underwater LiDAR Signal Processing for Enhanced Detection and Localization of Marine Life
reason: LiDAR processing pipeline tested only on artificial fish models in a controlled test tank; no wild or live animals in the analysed data.

title: Fast Classification and Detection of Fish Images with YOLOv2
reason: Applies a customized YOLOv2 detector to images of wild-caught fish (tuna, sharks, etc.) on fishing boats for fisheries monitoring; primary research using computer vision on wild animals.

title: Texture and Shape Information Fusion of Convolutional Neural Network for Plankton Image Classification
reason: Classification of microscopic plankton images (in situ imaging of microscopic organisms, mostly phytoplankton); falls under microscopy rather than wildlife imagery of free-ranging animals.

title: Development of Coral-Coverage Estimation Method Using Deep Learning and Sea Trial: at Kujuku-Shima Islands
reason: CNN-based pixel-wise segmentation of wild corals in underwater ortho photos from a sea trial in Japan.

title: Automated Interpretation of Seafloor Visual Maps Obtained Using Underwater Robots
reason: A CNN classifies wild deep-sea megabenthic taxa (galatheid crabs and mussels) in seafloor image mosaics collected by an underwater robot at a hydrothermal vent.

title: Flounders Measurement System Using Obtained Optical Images by AUV
reason: Proposes a CV system to recognise and measure wild flounders in seafloor images taken by an AUV.

title: Fish Recognition from a Vessel Camera Using Deep Convolutional Neural Network and Data Augmentation
reason: CNN classification of wild-caught fish species in images from fishing vessel cameras for fisheries monitoring.

title: Transfer Learning for Small-Scale Fish Image Classification
reason: Primary study proposing an improved transfer-learning fine-tuning strategy with B-CNNs for fine-grained classification of fish species images (Croatian Fish Dataset, F4K fish dataset); animals are the subject and data show free-ranging fish.

title: Coral Identification and Counting with an Autonomous Underwater Vehicle
venue: IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Biomimetics (ROBIO)
reason: The authors detect, track and count wild corals and sponges in video from coral reefs in Barbados, recorded with an AUV and a hand-held camera.

title: Analysis of Image Clusterization Methods for Oceanographical Equipment
reason: Classical image processing method for detecting, segmenting and counting zooplankton and other marine invertebrates in video from a plankton video analyzer, using a sample taken from the Black Sea coastal zone.

title: Development of a Prevention System for Beast Damage of Agricultural Products Using Deep Learning
venue: Joint International Conference on Soft Computing and Intelligent Systems and International Symposium on Advanced Intelligent Systems (SCIS&ISIS)
reason: Primary study training a CNN to classify monkey versus human images for a trap system aimed at wild monkeys that damage crops. The paper does not state where the 7344 images came from, so whether they show wild animals is not reported; inclusion rests on the stated wild-monkey application.

title: Bandwidth-efficient live video analytics for drones via edge computing
venue: Proceedings 2018 3rd ACM IEEE Symposium on Edge Computing Sec 2018
reason: Proposes a drone/edge video analytics pipeline for search tasks, including wildlife conservation. It is evaluated on aerial videos that include a task of detecting elephants in their natural habitat.

title: Image classification using manifold learning based non-linear dimensionality reduction
venue: Signal Processing and Communications Applications Conference (SIU)
reason: The paper compares manifold-learning dimensionality reduction methods for general image classification, tested on the KTH-animal dataset. Wildlife conservation or ecology is never given as the subject or application, and the classes mix wild and domestic animals.

title: Classification of radiolarian fossil images with deep learning methods
venue: Signal Processing and Communications Applications Conference (SIU)

title: Human-animal recognition in camera trap images
venue: Signal Processing and Communications Applications Conference (SIU)
reason: Applies feature-based computer vision classification to camera trap images of wild animals and humans captured in natural environments (human vs. animal recognition).

title: Automatic Key Frame Extraction From Videos For Efficient Mouse Pain Scoring
venue: International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)
reason: Computer vision pipeline for key frame extraction from videos of laboratory mice (C56BL6) in acrylic boxes for grimace scale pain scoring; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: A Vector Mosquitoes Classification System Based on Edge Computing and Deep Learning
venue: Conference on Technologies and Applications of Artificial Intelligence (TAAI)
reason: Computer vision (CNN on trap video frames) classifying wild mosquitoes captured in the field in Taiwan, combined with laboratory mosquitoes.

title: Fish Tracking and Segmentation From Stereo Videos on the Wild Sea Surface for Electronic Monitoring of Rail Fishing
venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology
reason: Primary study proposing a computer vision tracking and segmentation method on stereo video of wild-caught fish being pulled from the sea on commercial fishing vessels (fishery electronic monitoring).

title: Classification of Coral Reefs in the South China Sea by Combining Airborne LiDAR Bathymetry Bottom Waveforms and Bathymetric Features
