reason: Benthic habitat mapping: seafloor points from airborne LiDAR bathymetry are classified as 'coral reefs' vs 'others'. The output is habitat or land-cover mapping, not analysis of animals.

title: IPST: Incremental Pictorial Structures for Model-Free Tracking of Deformable Objects
reason: Generic model-free part-based tracking method evaluated mainly on human face and body benchmarks; the only animal data are cat face videos used as an ad hoc test case, and wildlife is not the subject.

title: The Whole Is More Than Its Parts? From Explicit to Implicit Pose Normalization
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
reason: Generic fine-grained classification method (alpha-pooling, neural activation constellations) evaluated on standard benchmarks (CUB birds, Oxford flowers, Oxford-IIIT pets, Stanford 40 actions); wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: FFDet: a Fully Convolutional Network for Coral Reef Fish Detection by Layer Fusion
venue: IEEE Visual Communications and Image Processing (VCIP)
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for wild coral reef fish in underwater monitoring videos (SeaCLEF).

reason: Classifies hematophagous diptera from Wing Interference Pattern images of insect wings. These are specimen images taken in a laboratory-style set-up, not images of free-ranging animals.

title: An Animal Detection Pipeline for Identification
venue: Proceedings 2018 IEEE Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision Wacv 2018
reason: Proposes a five-component DCNN detection pipeline and a new dataset (WILD) of in-situ photographs of wild animals (giraffes, zebras, sea turtles, whale flukes) for downstream individual identification.

title: Experimental brood enlargement differentially influences the magnitude of the corticosterone stress response in closely related, co‐occurring songbirds
reason: Ecophysiology field study of free-living nestbox-breeding swallows; a computer vision motion-detection tool (MotionMeerkat) was applied to nest videos to count adult feeding visits. CV is a minor supporting component but is applied to video of wild birds.

title: GRAPHITE: A graphical environment for scalable in situ video tracking of moving insects
reason: Video tracking software demonstrated only on tagged honey bees from managed colonies at apiaries (beekeeping); no wild, non-domestic animals in the analysed data.

title: A remote‐controlled observatory for behavioural and ecological research: A case study on emperor penguins
reason: Image/video-based observatory for monitoring a wild emperor penguin colony; images analysed for counting, colony segmentation and individual tracking.

title: Drones count wildlife more accurately and precisely than humans
reason: The analysed drone images show only plastic duck decoys in replica seabird colonies, an experimental set-up; no wild or free-ranging animals appear in the data. No criterion fits exactly; E-LAB (experimental set-up) is the closest.

title: trackdem : Automated particle tracking to obtain population counts and size distributions from videos in r

title: An automated barcode tracking system for behavioural studies in birds
reason: Barcode-based visual tracking of domesticated zebra finches kept only in indoor aviaries; no wild or free-ranging animals in the data.

title: Scene-specific convolutional neural networks for video-based biodiversity detection
reason: Develops a motion-detection plus CNN pipeline to find wild hummingbirds visiting flowers in field time-lapse videos from the Ecuadorian Andes.

title: Quantifying camouflage and conspicuousness using visual salience
reason: Proposes a species-relevant visual saliency model (computer vision) applied to images to quantify camouflage of prey, validated with lab quail and wild birds in the field and illustrated on a peacock image.

title: Boundary strength analysis: Combining colour pattern geometry and coloured patch visual properties for use in predicting behaviour and fitness

title: Identifying animal species in camera trap images using deep learning and citizen science

title: Machine learning to classify animal species in camera trap images: Applications in ecology

title: pat‐geom : A software package for the analysis of animal patterns

reason: Primary study that trains a CNN to detect and count wild olive ridley sea turtles in drone imagery collected at sea during a mass-nesting event.

title: Developmental stability of foraging behavior: evaluating suitability of captive giant pandas for translocation
reason: Behavioural study of captive giant pandas where videos were decoded manually by human observers; no computer vision method is applied, and all animals are in captive enclosures.

title: Giraffe bed and breakfast: Camera traps reveal Tanzanian yellow‐billed oxpeckers roosting on their large mammalian hosts
reason: Ecological camera-trap study of oxpecker roosting behaviour; images were identified by citizen science volunteers and inspected visually by an author, with no computer vision method applied.

title: The spotted ghost: Density and distribution of serval Leptailurus serval in Namibia
reason: Camera trap survey of wild serval where individuals were identified manually from pelage patterns and density estimated with spatial capture-recapture; no computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: A framework for investigating illegal wildlife trade on social media with machine learning
reason: Short perspective/essay proposing a conceptual framework for using machine learning on social media content about illegal wildlife trade; it reports no experiments or image analysis of its own and only summarises earlier work.

title: Applying deep learning to right whale photo identification
reason: Primary study presenting a CNN pipeline for individual photo identification of wild North Atlantic right whales from aerial survey photographs.

title: Integrating multiple data sources for assessing blue whale abundance and distribution in Chilean Northern Patagonia
reason: Species distribution modelling of blue whale abundance from visual line-transect sightings and presence-only records with satellite-derived oceanographic covariates; no computer vision is applied to images or video of animals.

title: It's not just what you have, but how you use it: solar‐positional and behavioural effects on hummingbird colour appearance during courtship
reason: The authors video-recorded courtship displays of free-ranging wild Costa's hummingbirds and analysed the footage with frame-by-frame video tracking. title: Colour pattern divergence in reef fish species is rapid and driven by both range overlap and symmetry

title: Ongoing changes in migration phenology and winter residency at Bracken Bat Cave
reason: Press release summarising a study that used historical weather radar data to monitor a wild bat colony; no computer vision analysis of images or video is described.

title: Heat waves and their significance for a temperate benthic community: A near‐natural experimental approach
reason: Marine ecology mesocosm experiment on heat-wave effects on benthic macrofauna. title: Tundra be dammed: Beaver colonization of the Arctic
reason: Applies satellite image analysis (Landsat trend analysis with Random Forest classification, then visual checking on high-resolution imagery) to detect beaver ponds and dams, which are direct signs of wild beavers.

title: Photo‐identification as a tool to study small‐spotted catshark Scyliorhinus canicula
reason: Primary study testing semi-automated spot-pattern photo-identification (APHIS/I3S algorithm) on photographs of wild-caught small-spotted catsharks taken from commercial trawlers.

title: Using unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) surveys and image analysis in the study of large surface‐associated marine species: a case study on reef sharks Carcharhinus melanopterus shoaling behaviour
reason: Image analysis of UAV video frames to locate free-ranging blacktip reef sharks and quantify their shoaling behaviour in a lagoon.

title: Bone cortical compactness in ‘tree sloths’ reflects convergent evolution
reason: The images are CT scans and thin-section images of humeri from museum specimens (extant and fossil xenarthrans), not images of living free-ranging animals. Museum specimens fall under E-CAPTIVE.

title: Detectability and visibility biases associated with using a consumer-grade unmanned aircraft to survey nesting colonial waterbirds
reason: Human observers manually counted waterbird decoys in UAS image mosaics; no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated, and live birds in the imagery were excluded from analysis.

title: Monitoring tropical forest ungulates using camera‐trap data
reason: Camera-trap images of wild chevrotain were identified manually by the author and density was estimated with a statistical random encounter model; no computer vision or automated image analysis is used.

title: Effect of drone‐based blow sampling on blue whale (Balaenoptera musculus) behavior
reason: Study of whether drone-based blow sampling changes blue whale behaviour. Observers recorded the behaviour directly and analysed it with ANOVA and t-tests. The drone camera was used for piloting, not for computer vision analysis of images.

title: Quantifying variation in killer whale ( Orcinus orca) morphology using elliptical Fourier analysis
reason: Image analysis (outline extraction, elliptical Fourier analysis, LDA classification) of photo-identification images of wild killer whales to discriminate ecotypes.

title: The prevalence of ectoparasitic barnacles discriminates stocks of Atlantic common bottlenose dolphins (Tursiops truncatus) at risk of entanglement in coastal gill net fisheries
reason: Photographs of wild dolphins are analysed only by manual measurement of barnacle cover in image software and by manual photo-identification matching. No computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Estimating morphometric attributes of baleen whales with photogrammetry from small UASs: A case study with blue and gray whales
reason: Primary study developing an image-based photogrammetric measurement method (lens distortion correction, scaling, analyst-guided digitization) on UAS video frames of free-swimming wild gray and blue whales.

title: Whales from space: Four mysticete species described using new VHR satellite imagery
reason: Whales are detected, described and counted manually by human observers on VHR satellite imagery, with descriptive spectral radiance analysis; no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Detecting Animals in Infrared Images from Camera-Traps
reason: Applies CNN classification and deep learning object detection to camera-trap images of wild game animals crossing a highway green bridge.

title: In Defense of Active Part Selection for Fine-Grained Classification
reason: Generic fine-grained classification method (SVM ensemble with part selection) evaluated only on the CUB-200-2011 benchmark. Wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Aerial photographic identification of narwhal (Monodon monoceros) newborns and their spatial proximity to the nearest adult female
reason: Narwhal newborns are identified in aerial photographs manually by human observers using a dichotomous key; no computer vision or automated image analysis is applied.

title: Interannual repeatability of eggshell phenotype in individual female Common Murres (Uria aalge)
reason: The main analysis uses photos of eggs laid by captive murres at the Oregon Coast Aquarium. Eggshells collected in Iceland were used only to validate the colour measurement, not to study wild animals.

title: An assessment of thermal-image acquisition with an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) for direct counts of coastal marine mammals ashore
reason: Thermal and photographic imagery of wild New Zealand fur seals was acquired by UAV and tripod camera, but seals were counted manually by viewing imagery on a monitor; no computer vision method is applied.

title: Counting crocodiles from the sky: monitoring the critically endangered gharial (Gavialis gangeticus) population with an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)
reason: UAV images of wild gharials and muggers in a Nepalese river. Borderline: counts are mainly manual by three analysts, but positive images were additionally screened with object-counting software and images were stitched by software, so image analysis is present.

title: Performance of manned and unmanned aerial surveys to collect visual data and imagery for estimating arctic cetacean density and associated uncertainty
reason: Aerial imagery of wild arctic cetaceans was reviewed manually by human photo analysts; no computer vision or automated image analysis method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Snow Leopard Recognition Using Deep Convolution Neural Network
venue: International Conference on Information System and Data Mining (ICISDM)
reason: Primary study applying a deep CNN to camera-trap images of wild snow leopards and other animals in the Himalayas.

title: AirSim-W

reason: Develops a simulation environment generating synthetic thermal infrared UAV imagery and evaluates Faster RCNN detection of animals and poachers on real thermal UAV videos collected over African conservation areas.

reason: The UAV detection system is trained and tested only on cattle and people. Cattle are livestock, and no wild animals appear in the analysed data.

title: Deep Learning for Practical Image Recognition
venue: ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery & Data Mining (KDD)

title: WildFish

reason: Introduces a web-collected image dataset of 1,000 fish categories for fish recognition in the wild and evaluates deep learning classifiers on it.

title: Towards calibration of outdoor multi-camera visual monitoring system
venue: International Conference on Distributed Smart Cameras
reason: The paper proposes a multi-camera calibration method evaluated only on images of an artificial LED/GNSS reference marker around a wind turbine. Bird monitoring is the motivating application, but no animal images are analysed.

title: Dog activity classification with movement sensor placed on the collar
reason: Behaviour of pet dogs is classified from collar accelerometer time series; video is used only for manual behaviour annotation, so there is no computer vision analysis of images.

title: Gorilla game lab

title: Computer tasks for great apes promote functional naturalism in a zoo setting
reason: Describes touch-panel computer tasks and feeders for zoo-housed orangutans as enrichment; no image or video analysis or computer vision method. Animals are captive only.

title: A Novel Saliency Detection Method for Wild Animal Monitoring Images with WMSN
reason: Proposes a saliency detection method evaluated on field-captured images of wild animals from a wireless camera sensor network in a nature reserve.

title: Design and Implementation of an Assistive Real‐Time Red Lionfish Detection System for AUV/ROVs
reason: CNN-based real-time detection of invasive red lionfish in ROV video recorded at artificial reefs in the Gulf of Mexico; wild free-ranging fish, primary research.

title: Taxonomic and nomenclatural status of Iberian Algyroides (Lacertidae)
reason: Morphological taxonomic study of preserved museum lizard specimens using microscope, calipers and photographs; no computer vision or image analysis method.

title: A Simple and Effective Method for Separating Meteorological from Nonmeteorological Targets Using Dual-Polarization Data
venue: Journal of Atmospheric and Oceanic Technology
reason: Weather radar polarimetric echo classification (meteorological vs biological); not computer vision on camera images or video of animals.

title: A deep neural network to assess spontaneous pain from mouse facial expressions
reason: CNN classification of pain facial expressions in laboratory CD-1 mice filmed in lab cubicles; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Using UAV remote sensing to analyze the population and distribution of large wild herbivores
reason: UAV images of wild herbivores and livestock were counted by manual visual interpretation (human-computer interaction) using an interpretation key. No computer vision method was developed or applied; automatic recognition is named only as future work.

title: Joining the dots: Reconstructing 3D environments and movement paths using animal-borne devices
reason: Trial of an animal-borne depth-sensing and visual-inertial odometry device on a single domestic dog on a lead; the analysed data are 3D point clouds of the forest environment (tree trunks, ground), with no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: A tale of two tails: asymmetry in Great Grey Shrike (Lanius excubitor)

title: Effect of initial body orientation on escape probability in prey fish escaping from predators
reason: Laboratory predator-prey experiment in a glass aquarium with hatchery-reared prey and aquarium-kept predators; video digitized manually for kinematics. No free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Foot-propelled swimming kinematics and turning strategies in common loons
reason: Wild-origin common loons were filmed only in an indoor pool at a wildlife rehabilitation clinic, which makes them enclosure animals. The analysis is manual 3D digitisation for biomechanics rather than computer vision on free-ranging animals.

title: Hand pressures during arboreal locomotion in captive bonobos ( Pan paniscus )
reason: Biomechanics study measuring hand pressure with a pressure mat in captive zoo bonobos. Video was only inspected by eye, with no computer vision analysis. The animals are also captive only, so E-CAPTIVE would apply as well.

title: Automated measurement of upper thermal limits in small aquatic animals
reason: Laboratory-reared clonal Daphnia magna filmed in a thermostatic well plate to measure upper thermal limits; no wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: UMATracker: An intuitive image-based tracking platform
reason: Tracking software for videos of animals in laboratory arenas (mice in a cage, insects on plates, zebrafish); no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Ascending flight and decelerating vertical glides in Anna's hummingbirds
reason: Biomechanics study of wild-caught hummingbirds filmed in an indoor flight chamber; landmarks were digitized from high-speed video and no automated computer vision method is described.

title: Evaluation of somatotype in the reticulated giraffe (Giraffa camelopardalis reticulata) using three-dimensional laser measurement
reason: 3D laser point-cloud measurement of three zoo-housed giraffes only; no wild animals in the analysed data.

title: Butterfly Image Classification Using Color Quantization Method on HSV Color Space and Local Binary Pattern
reason: Applies colour (HSV quantization) and texture (LBP) features with SVM to classify butterfly species in photographs that show them perched on twigs, leaves and flowers.

title: TuLUMIS - a tunable LED-based underwater multispectral imaging system
reason: The paper describes an underwater multispectral imaging system. Its quantitative analysis is done on a colour checkerboard in a water tank. title: A simple computer vision pipeline reveals the effects of isolation on social interaction dynamics in Drosophila
reason: Laboratory-reared Drosophila melanogaster tracked in a closed indoor walking arena; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: An evaluation of three-dimensional photogrammetric and morphometric techniques for estimating volume and mass in Weddell seals Leptonychotes weddellii
reason: 3D photogrammetric reconstruction from photographs of free-ranging (temporarily sedated) Weddell seals in Antarctica to estimate volume and mass.

title: Ant genera identification using an ensemble of convolutional neural networks
reason: CNN ensemble classifies ant genera from AntWeb photographs of pinned, mounted specimens (collection specimens), not images of wild free-ranging animals.

title: Impacts of human recreation on carnivores in protected areas
reason: Ecological occupancy study of wild carnivores using camera traps, track plates and sign surveys. Species were identified manually and analysed with occupancy models; no computer vision or automated image analysis is applied.

title: D-Track—A semi-automatic 3D video-tracking technique to analyse movements and routines of aquatic animals with application to captive dolphins
reason: Video tracking method developed and tested only on two captive bottlenose dolphins in a marine theme park pool; no wild or free-ranging animals in the data.

title: A new use of technology to solve an old problem: Estimating the population size of a burrow nesting seabird
reason: UAV aerial photographs of a wild seabird colony were stitched into orthomosaics, but burrows were counted and marked manually by two people in QGIS; no automated image analysis or computer vision method was applied.

title: An evaluation of the error and uncertainty in epibenthos cover estimates from AUV images collected with an efficient, spatially-balanced design
reason: AUV images of wild epibenthos were scored manually with random points; cover was then modelled with GAMs on bathymetric covariates. The paper applies no computer vision or automated image analysis.

title: Body condition and adrenal glucocorticoid activity affects metabolic marker and lipid profiles in captive female elephants in Thailand
reason: Physiological study of captive tourist-camp elephants; photographs are scored visually by veterinarians for body condition, no computer vision method is applied. Animals are also captive only.

title: Passive acoustics and sound recognition provide new insights on status and resilience of an iconic endangered marsupial (koala Phascolarctos cinereus) to timber harvesting
reason: Passive acoustic survey of wild koalas; male bellows are detected with sound-recognition software and used for occupancy modelling. No image or video data are analysed.

title: The development of honey bee colonies assessed using a new semi-automated brood counting method: CombCount
reason: Semi-automated image analysis of hive frame photographs from managed commercial honey bee colonies (beekeeping); no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: MAIA—A machine learning assisted image annotation method for environmental monitoring and exploration
reason: Primary study proposing a machine-learning assisted detection/annotation method (autoencoder novelty detection + Mask R-CNN) applied to seabed images of wild benthic megafauna captured in the field.

title: The influence of depth and a subsea pipeline on fish assemblages and commercially fished species
reason: Ecological survey using stereo-BRUV video of wild fish; species identification, MaxN counts and length measurements were done manually in EventMeasure software. No automated computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Analysis and tracking of animal movements through granulation of temporal domain (GTD)
reason: Proposes a background-subtraction and granular-computing method to detect and track animals in video, aimed at wildlife protection. The paper does not say which animals were filmed or whether they were wild.

title: Underwater Optical Fish Classification System by Means of Robust Feature Decomposition and Analysis using Multiple Neural Networks
venue: International Journal of Advanced Computer Science and Applications
reason: Proposes a computer vision classification system for live fish species in underwater optical images and video recorded by an underwater platform. The paper does not clearly say whether the fish were wild or captive.

title: Using laser photogrammetry to measure long-finned pilot whales (Globicephala melas)
venue: Proceedings of the Nova Scotian Institute of Science
reason: Wild free-ranging pilot whales are photographed, but body measurements and photo-identification are done by hand in ImageJ/GIMP. No computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Incremental Environmental Monitoring for Revealing the Ecology of Endangered Fish
reason: Computer vision (SSD detection, background subtraction trajectories) is applied to underwater video of endangered Japanese rosy bitterling, but the analysed video comes from a small artificial university fish-farm pond described as a controlled habitat where the fish's movement is restricted; no free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: SPOT Poachers in Action: Augmenting Conservation Drones With Automatic Detection in Near Real Time
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
reason: Faster RCNN-based detection of poachers and wild animals in thermal infrared UAV videos from African national parks; primary research with animal-specific model and evaluation.

title: Audio Visual Attribute Discovery for Fine-Grained Object Recognition
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
reason: Generic fine-grained object recognition method evaluated on the CUB-200-2011 benchmark, extended with web videos. Wildlife or conservation is not the stated application.

title: Automatic analysis of deep-water remotely operated vehicle footage for estimation of Norway lobster abundance
venue: Frontiers of Information Technology & Electronic Engineering
reason: Primary study proposing a computer vision framework to detect, track and count wild Norway lobsters and their burrows in deep-water ROV video.

title: Marine information technology: the best is yet to come
venue: Frontiers of Information Technology & Electronic Engineering
reason: Editorial overview of a special issue on marine information technology; no primary computer vision research on animal images.

title: Pholidosis Abnormalities and Injuries in the European Pond Turtle (Emys orbicularis) in the Conditions of the Khopersky Nature Reserve
reason: Field morphological study of scute abnormalities and injuries in wild turtles examined by hand; there is no image or video analysis or computer vision method.

title: Underwater Platform for Intelligent Robotics and its Application in Two Visual Tracking Systems
reason: An AUV's sampling system uses a visual attention model on seabed images to find living sea-creatures in the open sea and tracks them visually for sampling.

title: Vision System for an Autonomous Underwater Vehicle with a Benthos Sampling Function
reason: AUV vision system evaluated only in an experimental tank with a crab model and a metal piece; no field images of wild animals were analysed.

title: Using a benthic lander to explore and monitor vulnerable ecosystems in the Mediterranean Sea
reason: Baited benthic lander videos of wild deep-sea fauna were analysed manually with Adobe Premiere Pro and ImageJ to identify species, count them and describe behaviour. No computer vision method was developed or applied.

title: LOCAL BINARY PATTERN METHOD AND FEATURE SHAPE EXTRACTION FOR DETECTING BUTTERFLY IMAGE
reason: Computer vision classification of butterfly species images using texture and shape features; images show butterflies on twigs, leaves and flowers, so they are natural rather than lab or captive scenes.

title: Towards automatic identification of elephants in the wild
reason: Computer vision system for identifying individual wild elephants from field photographs taken at a forest clearing in the Dzanga-Sangha reserve.

title: Research on Real - time Processing System of Deep Sea Biological Image for Manned Submersible Vehicle
reason: Applies classical image processing (filtering, edge detection, segmentation) to images of wild deep-sea creatures taken by a manned submersible.

title: Image Analysis Based Fish Tail Beat Frequency Estimation for Fishway Efficiency
reason: Image analysis (background subtraction and periodicity detection) estimates tail beat frequency from video of fish in a river fishway. Laboratory research videos from Lauder Lab are also used, so the data is mixed.

title: Towards Automatic Detection of Animals in Camera-Trap Images
reason: Re-trains and combines deep-learning object detectors (YOLOv2, SSD) to detect, classify and count wild Serengeti animals in camera-trap images.

title: Near Real-Time Detection of Poachers from Drones in AirSim
venue: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
reason: Faster RCNN detection of poachers and wild animals in thermal infrared UAV video for conservation; animals are detected and evaluated alongside poachers.

title: Crop Protection by an alert Based System using Deep Learning Concept
venue: International Journal of Scientific Research in Computer Sciences and Engineering
reason: Proposes an alert system that classifies images of wild animals entering farmland with deep learning to trigger a deterrent buzzer. It is a human-wildlife conflict application on wild animals, although the image analysis is described only minimally.

title: DoggyVision: Examining how dogs (Canis familiaris) interact with media using a dog-driven proximity tracker device.
reason: Study of two pet Labrador dogs in their owners' homes. An IR proximity sensor triggers the media, and the webcam video was coded by hand, not analysed automatically. No wild animals are involved.

title: An Intelligent Software for Measurements of Biological Materials: BioMorph
reason: This is a technical note describing general morphometric software for any 'bio-object' (leaves, fish, skulls, medical uses). It reports no animal dataset and no evaluation, and it never states that wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Bird Identification by Image Recognition
reason: Applies CNN feature extraction with an SVM to classify the species of wild birds in images downloaded from Google Images.

title: Population estimation, distribution, and habitat preference of Irrawaddy dolphins Orcaella brevirostris (Owen in Gray, 1866) in the Brunei Bay, Malaysian waters
reason: The authors photographed the dorsal fins of free-ranging Irrawaddy dolphins in Brunei Bay. They identified individuals with DARWIN, software that matches fin outlines, and used the identities for mark-recapture estimation. This counts as applying image-based identification to wild animals.

title: Fish species classification in underwater video monitoring using Convolutional Neural Networks
reason: CNN-based species classification of free-ranging river fish recorded by underwater video monitoring in fish passes of Austrian rivers; primary research.

title: Convolutional Neural Networks Predict Fish Abundance from Underlying Coral Reef Texture
reason: The images analysed are depth images made from 3D models of coral reef structure. Fish never appear in them: divers counted the fish by eye, and those counts serve only as labels. The vision method looks at habitat only.

title: Background extraction method for analysis of natural images captured by camera traps
reason: Proposes a modified Gaussian mixture model background extraction method to localize wild animals and birds in camera trap images from a wildlife sanctuary.

title: Using aerial photogrammetry to detect changes in body condition of endangered southern resident killer whales
reason: Primary study analysing aerial images of wild killer whales to measure body condition via photogrammetry (image-based measurement) and photo-identification.

title: Allometry and morphometry of blue whales photographed in the Gulf of California: insights into subspecies taxonomy in the Eastern North Pacific
reason: Wild blue whales photographed from an aircraft, but body proportions were measured by hand in pixels using Sigma Scan Pro software. No computer vision method is developed or applied; the analysis is manual photogrammetry followed by allometric statistics.

title: Individual identification of flapper skate Dipturus intermedius using a baited camera lander
reason: Wild flapper skates were filmed with baited underwater cameras, but videos were analysed manually and individuals were matched by eye. No computer vision method was used.

title: Loggerhead turtle Caretta caretta density and abundance in Chesapeake Bay and the temperate ocean waters of the southern portion of the Mid-Atlantic Bight
reason: Sea turtle abundance is estimated from human observer aerial line-transect surveys and satellite telemetry; no image or video analysis is performed.

title: I3S Pattern as a mark-recapture tool to identify captured and free-swimming sea turtles: an assessment
reason: Evaluates I3S Pattern software for photo-identification of individual wild green and hawksbill sea turtles from captured and free-swimming photos.

title: Maternal body size and condition determine calf growth rates in southern right whales
reason: Applies UAV aerial photogrammetry (image-based morphometric measurement) to free-ranging southern right whales to estimate body volume and growth.

title: Composition and functional diversity of macrofaunal assemblages on vertical walls of a deep northeast Pacific fjord
reason: Ecological survey of wild deep-fjord macrofauna from ROV video; the images were annotated by hand in VideoMiner and PhotoQuad, and no computer vision method was developed or applied.

title: Comparison of a Cost-Effective Integrated Plankton Sampling and Imaging Instrument with Traditional Systems for Mesozooplankton Sampling in the Celtic Sea
reason: Imaging and image analysis (PIA line-scan imaging, Zooscan with machine-learning categorisation) of wild mesozooplankton sampled at sea in the Celtic Sea, to estimate taxon abundances.

title: Cephalopod Experimental Projected Habitat (CEPH): Virtual Reality for Underwater Organisms
reason: Laboratory behavioural apparatus: wild-caught octopuses are held and tracked in an indoor experimental tank; no images of free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Looking Without Landing—Using Remote Piloted Aircraft to Monitor Fur Seal Populations Without Disturbance
reason: Drone survey protocol for a wild fur seal colony; images are stitched with photogrammetry software and animals are counted manually by an observer in a web portal. No automated computer vision analysis of the animals is developed or evaluated.

title: Linking Ross Sea Coastal Benthic Communities to Environmental Conditions: Documenting Baselines in a Spatially Variable and Changing World
reason: Ecological survey of Antarctic benthic communities; diver video transects were analysed manually and linked to environmental variables with multivariate statistics (MDS, CCA). No computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Long-Term Photo-Identification Reveals the Population Dynamics and Strong Site Fidelity of Adult Whale Sharks to the Coastal Waters of Donsol, Philippines
reason: Primary study applying pattern-recognition photo-ID software (I3S, Wildbook) to in-water photographs of free-ranging whale sharks to identify individuals for population analysis.

title: Swimming Energy Economy in Bottlenose Dolphins Under Variable Drag Loading
reason: Captive trained dolphins in a man-made lagoon at a dolphin facility; the study is about biomechanics and energetics, and positions in the aerial video were digitised manually.

title: The Dominant Role of Visual Motion Cues in Bumblebee Flight Control Revealed Through Virtual Reality
reason: Behavioural experiment on commercially reared bumblebees flying in an indoor laboratory flight arena; video tracking is only a tool for a virtual-reality set-up, and no wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Tracking All Members of a Honey Bee Colony Over Their Lifetime Using Learned Models of Correspondence
reason: Tracking of individually tagged honey bees of a managed colony inside an instrumented one-frame observation hive (research set-up with a model organism); no wild, free-ranging non-domestic animals are imaged.

title: RenderGAN: Generating Realistic Labeled Data
reason: The paper generates and decodes images of barcode-like markers attached to managed honeybees in a hive (BeesBook project); no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Assessment of Welfare in Zoo Animals: Towards Optimum Quality of Life
reason: Narrative review of zoo animal welfare assessment approaches; no computer vision analysis of image data and no primary study of wild animals.

title: Large-Scale Fine-Grained Bird Recognition Based on a Triplet Network and Bilinear Model
reason: Proposes a CNN model (triplet network plus bilinear model) for fine-grained classification of bird species, motivated by bird protection, tested on a custom bird dataset and on CUB200-2011.

title: Deep Learning Case Study for Automatic Bird Identification
reason: CNN-based image classification of wild birds in flight photographed at an offshore wind farm test site in Finland; primary research.

title: Assessment of Chimpanzee Nest Detectability in Drone-Acquired Images
reason: Drone images of wild chimpanzee nests were inspected visually by one human observer; no computer vision method was applied. Analysis is statistical (GLMs) on manual detections.

title: Drone-Based High-Resolution Tracking of Aquatic Vertebrates
reason: Wild sharks are tracked by flying a drone manually above them and using the drone's GPS flight log as the animal's position. No image analysis is done; the video was only used to see behaviours and mark when tracks started.

title: Drone Monitoring of Breeding Waterbird Populations: The Case of the Glossy Ibis
reason: Primary study applying supervised pixel classification and particle analysis to UAV imagery of a wild Glossy ibis breeding colony to count nests.

title: Change Detection in Coral Reef Environment Using High-Resolution Images: Comparison of Object-Based and Pixel-Based Paradigms
reason: Object-based change detection of reef island land cover and benthic coral reef habitat classes from satellite imagery; no individual animals are the subject, only habitat/land cover change.

title: A Simple Setup to Perform 3D Locomotion Tracking in Zebrafish by Using a Single Camera
reason: Laboratory zebrafish tracked in an acrylic tank for biomedical/behavioural research; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Automated Image Analysis of Offshore Infrastructure Marine Biofouling
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Applies automated image annotation software (CoralNet) to ROV images of wild marine biofouling invertebrates (anemones, corals, mussels, hydroids) on North Sea offshore platforms; primary research.

title: Photogrammetric Surveys and Geometric Processes to Analyse and Monitor Red Coral Colonies
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Photogrammetric 3D reconstruction and measurement of wild red coral colonies photographed in situ by divers; some dead colonies from collections also modelled.

title: Improving Animal-Human Cohabitation with Machine Learning in Fiber-Wireless Networks
venue: Journal of Sensor and Actuator Networks
reason: Early warning system that detects wild animals near roads/rails, using a PIR-triggered camera on a Raspberry Pi and a MobileNet CNN that classifies animal presence/absence. The data source of the classified images is not described.

title: Hyperspectral Shallow-Water Remote Sensing with an Enhanced Benthic Classifier
reason: Benthic habitat mapping of a coral reef from airborne hyperspectral imagery into substrate classes (sand, algae, seagrass, coral). It is habitat and land-cover classification, not a study of animals as individuals or populations.

title: Assessment of Machine Learning Algorithms for Automatic Benthic Cover Monitoring and Mapping Using Towed Underwater Video Camera and High-Resolution Satellite Images
reason: Primary study classifying towed underwater camera images and a satellite image into benthic cover classes. One class is corals, which are wild sessile animals on a natural reef. Borderline with E-PLANT, since the stated aim is benthic habitat mapping and the other classes are algae, seagrass and sediments.

title: Application of UAV Remote Sensing for a Population Census of Large Wild Herbivores—Taking the Headwater Region of the Yellow River as an Example
reason: UAV census of wild herbivores and livestock in which animals were identified and counted by manual visual interpretation of the images in ArcGIS; no computer vision method is applied to the animal images.

title: Animal Detection Using Thermal Images and Its Required Observation Conditions
reason: Primary study applying a moving-object detection algorithm to thermal images of free-ranging sika deer (airborne) and wild ducks; a UAV test also includes a human and a domestic dog.

title: SfM-Based Method to Assess Gorgonian Forests (Paramuricea clavata (Cnidaria, Octocorallia))
reason: Primary study applying SfM photogrammetry and point-cloud classification to in-situ underwater imagery of wild red gorgonian (Paramuricea clavata) colonies to estimate density, morphometry and biomass.

title: Evaluation of Spatial Generalization Characteristics of a Robust Classifier as Applied to Coral Reef Habitats in Remote Islands of the Pacific Ocean
reason: Satellite (Landsat 8) pixel classification of coral vs non-coral bottom type for benthic habitat mapping; habitat/cover mapping rather than imaging of individual animals.

title: Underwater Object Segmentation Based on Optical Features
reason: Generic underwater object segmentation method; the paper never states that animals or wildlife are the subject, only unspecified 'underwater objects' and 'participants' in YouTube images.

title: Effective Vehicle-Based Kangaroo Detection for Collision Warning Systems Using Region-Based Convolutional Networks
reason: Develops a Faster R-CNN kangaroo detector for vehicle collision warning, trained on synthetic depth images and tested on real depth images of live kangaroos in an urban traffic environment. The paper does not say the real kangaroos were captive.

title: UAVs, Hyperspectral Remote Sensing, and Machine Learning Revolutionizing Reef Monitoring
reason: UAV hyperspectral and RGB imagery of wild reef corals (animals) at Pandora Reef is classified by genus and bleaching level with an SVM; primary research.

title: Underwater Target Detection and 3D Reconstruction System Based on Binocular Vision
reason: Underwater stereo vision system tested on man-made objects (barrier, warning notice, flowerpot) in a water pool; no animals are analysed and wildlife is not the stated subject.

title: IMAGE THRESHOLDING BASED ON HIERARCHICAL CLUSTERING ANALYSIS AND PERCENTILE METHOD FOR TUNA IMAGE SEGMENTATION
venue: NJCA (Nusantara Journal of Computers and Its Applications)
reason: The paper segments images of caught tuna supplied by a tuna processing company so that sorting in fish production can be automated. These are fisheries and food-production specimens, not wild free-ranging animals imaged in the wild.

title: Mymou: A low-cost, wireless touchscreen system for automated training of nonhuman primates
reason: Automated touchscreen training system with facial recognition for laboratory-housed rhesus monkeys in their home cage; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Supporting citizen scientists with automatic species identification using deep learning image recognition models
reason: Conference abstract that applies deep learning image recognition to identify species in citizen-science field observation photos from Observation.org, including insects.

title: Jellyfish Identification Software for Underwater Laser Cameras (JTRACK)
reason: This is a grant proposal that describes planned work. It analyses no image data and reports no results, so it is not primary research.

title: Individual Minke Whale Recognition Using Deep Learning Convolutional Neural Networks
venue: Journal of Geoscience and Environment Protection
reason: Primary study training a segmentation CNN to recognise individual wild dwarf minke whales from underwater photographs taken in the Great Barrier Reef.

title: EFFECTS OF ENVIRONMENTAL ENRICHMENTS ON THE BEHAVIORS OF FOUR CAPTIVE JAGUARS: INDIVIDUALITY MATTERS
reason: Behavioral study of four captive zoo jaguars using direct human observation (focal scan sampling with binoculars) and proportion tests; no image or video analysis, and animals are captive only.

title: Tracking all members of a honey bee colony over their lifetime
reason: Tracks marked honey bees of a managed colony in an observation hive (beekeeping), not wild free-ranging animals.

title: SpaRTA - Tracking across occlusions via global partitioning of 3D clouds of points
reason: Proposes a 3D multi-target tracking method and evaluates it on multicamera video of wild bat colonies emerging from a natural cave.

title: The Automatic Identification of Butterfly Species
reason: Faster R-CNN detection and species identification of butterflies in field photographs of wild butterflies in their natural environment; training also uses specimen pattern images.

title: BioTracker: An Open-Source Computer Vision Framework for Visual Animal Tracking
reason: Software framework paper for animal tracking; the only analysed footage shown is fish in an experimental tank (laboratory set-up). No wild free-ranging animal data is analysed.

title: Flexible and Scalable Deep Learning with MMLSpark
reason: Distributed deep learning library applied to classify wild snow leopards in camera trap images from the Snow Leopard Trust.

title: Recognition in Terra Incognita
reason: Presents a camera trap dataset (CCT-20) of free-ranging animals in the American Southwest and benchmarks detection and classification generalization to new locations. Classes also include domestic cats and dogs.

title: Fine-grained visual recognition with salient feature detection
reason: Generic fine-grained recognition method evaluated only on the CUB200-2011 benchmark. Wildlife monitoring or conservation is not the stated subject.

title: Maximum-Entropy Fine-Grained Classification
reason: Generic fine-grained classification regularisation method evaluated on standard benchmarks (CUB, NABirds, Stanford Dogs, Cars, Aircraft, CIFAR); wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Optimizing the Human-Machine Partnership with Zooniverse
reason: Short perspective paper summarising Zooniverse infrastructure and prior human-machine citizen science work; no new primary computer vision experiments on wildlife images are reported.

title: Bird Species Classification using Transfer Learning with Multistage Training
reason: Deep learning classification of bird species from photographs of birds in natural settings (occlusion by leaves/branches); the paper does not say whether the birds are wild or captive.

title: Unique Identification of Macaques for Population Monitoring and Control
reason: Proposes a face detection and individual identification method for free-ranging urban rhesus macaques photographed in India; also uses lab macaque images and zoo and national-park chimpanzee images.

title: Cross-domain Deep Feature Combination for Bird Species Classification with Audio-visual Data
reason: Proposes CNN-based multimodal (image + audio spectrogram) fusion for bird species classification, evaluated on CUB-200-2011 bird images; wild bird species are the stated subject.

title: Towards Automatic Identification of Elephants in the Wild
reason: Primary study proposing a computer vision pipeline (YOLO head detection, ResNet50 features, SVM) to identify individual wild elephants photographed in the field at a forest clearing.

title: A Survey on Snake Species Identification using Image Processing Technique
reason: The paper calls itself a survey and only describes a proposed snake identification system (YOLO + CNN). It reports no experiments, data analysis or results, so it is not primary research.

title: Texture Classification of Sea Turtle Shell Based on Color Features: Color Histograms and Chromaticity Moments
venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence & Applications
reason: Primary study applying colour-feature extraction with KNN/SVM to classify sea turtle species from shell patches cropped from online photos of turtles shown in their natural environment.

title: MONITORING CORAL GROWTH – THE DICHOTOMY BETWEEN UNDERWATER PHOTOGRAMMETRY AND GEODETIC CONTROL NETWORK
venue: The international archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences/International archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences
reason: Underwater photogrammetric 3D reconstruction and multi-temporal change detection of a wild coral reef (corals are animals) in Moorea from diver-acquired images.

title: QUASI-ORTHORECTIFIED PROJECTION FOR THE MEASUREMENT OF RED GORGONIAN COLONIES
venue: The international archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences/International archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences
reason: Photogrammetric multi-view stereo and image projection to measure wild red gorgonian colonies in situ underwater.

title: COASTAL MAPPING AND KITESURFING
venue: The international archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences/International archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences
reason: Citizen-science kite/SUP-mounted action cameras collect underwater and aerial images of coral reefs in Mauritius. Image analysis is preliminary: a generic AWS recognition test that identifies a ray and a 3D photogrammetric reconstruction of a coral reef. Both use images of wild marine animals.

title: Automatic Acquisition and Sustainable Use of Political-Ecological Data
reason: The paper's only image analysis counts captive elephants in a zoo safari park exhibit using satellite images. The other components are text mining and website or security protocols.

title: Towards Automated Biometric Identification of Sea Turtles (Chelonia mydas)
venue: Journal of ICT Research and Applications
reason: All analysed images show juvenile green sea turtles kept in captivity at a private breeding farm, photographed inside an artificial perimeter; no wild or free-ranging animals are in the data.

title: An approach for using off-the-shelf object-based image analysis software to detect and count birds in large volumes of aerial imagery
reason: Primary study developing an object-based image analysis routine to detect and count wild Lesser Snow Geese in aerial imagery of Arctic breeding colonies.

title: Deep sea spy: a collaborative annotation tool
reason: Describes an online citizen-science manual annotation tool for deep-sea observatory images; no computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: A Deep Learning algorithm for accurate and fast identification of coral reef fishes in underwater videos
reason: Primary study that trains a convolutional neural network to identify coral reef fish species in underwater images and video for marine biodiversity monitoring. Only the abstract page was available; the fish are coded as wild because the images show reef environment, though the text does not state this explicitly.

title: The Automatic Identification of Butterfly Species
reason: Primary study developing a Faster R-CNN based automatic butterfly identification system (detection + species recognition) on images, part of which are photographs of butterflies in their living (wild) environment, combined with standard specimen pattern images.

title: A kinematic synergy for terrestrial locomotion shared by mammals and birds
reason: Comparative locomotion study in which anatomical landmarks were tracked by hand, frame by frame, in videos, followed by PCA of the joint angles. There is no automated computer vision method. The animals are mostly in zoos, on a farm or in labs, plus free-walking sika deer in Nara city.

title: Assessing the disturbance potential of small unoccupied aircraft systems (UAS) on gray seals (Halichoerus grypus) at breeding colonies in Nova Scotia, Canada
reason: Disturbance study of wild gray seals using UAS imagery; seals were counted and assessed manually (iTag, Photoshop) with no computer vision method applied.

title: High definition video loggers provide new insights into behaviour, physiology, and the oceanic habitat of a marine predator, the yellow-eyed penguin
reason: Animal-borne video of a free-ranging yellow-eyed penguin was analysed manually, frame by frame, in video editing software. No computer vision method was applied; automated analysis is only named as future work.

title: Seeing spots: quantifying mother-offspring similarity and assessing fitness consequences of coat pattern traits in a wild population of giraffes ( Giraffa camelopardalis )
reason: Applies image analysis (ImageJ thresholding and particle analysis) to photographs of wild, free-ranging Masai giraffes to quantify coat pattern traits.

title: A gradient of pollination specialization in three species of Bolivian Centropogon
reason: Field pollination study that films wild hummingbirds and bats visiting flowers and uses the computer vision program MotionMeerkat to find motion events in the videos; the vision component is minor but applied to wild animals.

title: Prehensile kinematics of the marmoset monkey: Implications for the evolution of visually‐guided behaviors
reason: Laboratory study of reach-to-grasp kinematics in captive, trained and partly lesioned marmosets; video is analysed with 2D tracking software, no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Benthic responses to an Antarctic regime shift: food particle size and recruitment biology
reason: Ecological long-term comparison of Antarctic benthic invertebrates; photographs were analysed manually (planimeter, ImageJ counts) without any computer vision method.

title: Making inference with messy (citizen science) data: when are data accurate enough and how can they be improved?
reason: Trail camera images of wild animals are classified by crowdsourced volunteers and experts; the paper evaluates misclassification with regression screening models and occupancy simulations on metadata, with no computer vision analysis of image content.

title: Animal Scanner: Software for classifying humans, animals, and empty frames in camera trap images
reason: Develops computer vision software (background subtraction plus DCNN) to detect and classify humans, animals and empty frames in camera trap images of wild animals.

title: Wildlife surveillance using deep learning methods
reason: Develops CNN classifiers for still images and video of wild animals (badger, fox, rat, rabbit, birds) together with domestic animals (cats) visiting UK farm buildings.

title: Automatic counting of birds in a bird deterrence field trial
reason: Primary study applying a cascade object detector to video stills of free-ranging wild birds visiting baited food tables in an open-field deterrence trial.

title: Design patterns for wildlife‐related camera trap image analysis
reason: Primary paper on design patterns for camera trap image analysis software (Timelapse); applies image differencing, dark-image classification and imports MegaDetector detections on camera trap images of wild mountain goats.

title: Species‐level image classification with convolutional neural network enables insect identification from habitus images
reason: The analysed images are scans of pinned or card-mounted museum specimens of ground beetles; no images of wild, free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Citizen science reveals female sand tiger sharks (Carcharias taurus) exhibit signs of site fidelity on shipwrecks
reason: Applies Wildbook spot-pattern matching software to citizen-science photographs of wild sand tiger sharks to re-identify individuals and infer site fidelity.

title: Bright lights in the big cities: migratory birds’ exposure to artificial light
venue: Frontiers in Ecology and the Environment
reason: Ecological analysis of weather surveillance radar reflectivity and satellite night-light radiance to quantify migratory bird exposure to artificial light; no computer vision image analysis of animals (random forest on derived radar profile variables, GAM interpolation).

title: Identification of gravid mosquitoes from changes in spectral and polarimetric backscatter cross sections
reason: Optical sensor study using photodetector backscatter time-series (no images or video) of laboratory-reared mosquitoes flying in an enclosure; not image analysis.

title: Benthic communities and their drivers: A spatial analysis off the Antarctic Peninsula
reason: Ecological study of Antarctic seabed fauna. Seabed photos were scored visually by experts (percentage cover classes) and analysed with community statistics; no computer vision or automated image analysis is applied.

title: Improving plankton image classification using context metadata
reason: CNN and feature-based classification of in situ images of free-living marine zooplankton acquired by an autonomous underwater glider; primary research.

title: CoralSeg: Learning coral segmentation from sparse annotations
reason: Develops and evaluates semantic segmentation on underwater images of wild coral reefs (corals are animals), with coral monitoring as the stated application.

title: Engaging ‘the crowd’ in remote sensing to learn about habitat affinity of the Weddell seal in Antarctica
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Wild Weddell seals in satellite imagery, but the images were searched by citizen-science volunteers. The only algorithm (CrowdRank) aggregates volunteer votes and does no automated image analysis, so there is no computer vision method.

title: Using by‐catch data from wildlife surveys to quantify climatic parameters and timing of phenology for plants and animals using camera traps
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Camera-trap images of wild animals were classified manually by human observers; no computer vision or automated image analysis method was developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Marmots from space: assessing population size and habitat use of a burrowing mammal using publicly available satellite images
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Burrows of wild Bobak marmots were digitized manually by human observers on satellite images; no computer vision or automated image analysis method was applied.

title: Efficacy of automated detection of motion in wildlife monitoring videos
reason: Evaluates an automated motion-detection program (background subtraction) on continuous videos of wild woodpecker nest cavities and their potential nest predators in a national forest.

title: Testing unmanned aerial systems for monitoring wildlife at night
reason: Wild deer were recorded by thermal UAS and camera traps, but animals were found and counted by people looking at the images. The only processing was photogrammetric mapping and GIS interpolation, so no computer vision analysis of animals was done.

title: Comparing infrared imagery to traditional methods for estimating ringed seal density
reason: Wild ringed seals on sea ice were surveyed from the air with infrared and DSLR imagery. However, seals were found by a human analyst looking at the video in FLIR software. No computer vision or automated image analysis method was developed or applied; the study compares survey and density-estimation methods.

title: Estimating density and detection of bobcats in fragmented midwestern landscapes using spatial capture–recapture data from camera traps
reason: Camera-trap photographs of wild bobcats were identified to individual manually by human observers and analysed with spatial capture-recapture statistics; no computer vision method is applied to the images.

title: Sleep‐related behaviors in zoo‐housed giraffes (Giraffa camelopardalis reticulata): Basic characteristics and effects of season and parturition
reason: Behavioural study of two zoo-housed giraffes. Human observers coded the infrared video by hand; no computer vision or automated image analysis was used. The animals are also captive only.

title: The Andean bear alopecia syndrome may be caused by social housing
reason: Epidemiological study of alopecia in zoo-housed Andean bears based on questionnaires, husbandry and veterinary records analysed with GLMs; no image or video analysis, and the animals are captive.

title: Assessment of contrafreeloading preferences in giraffe (Giraffa camelopardalis)
reason: Behavioural study of zoo giraffes in an indoor enclosure; videos were coded manually and no computer vision method is used.

title: DeepEye: A Dedicated Camera for Deep-Sea Tripod Observation Systems
reason: The paper is about restoring deep-sea seafloor images (descattering, denoising, colour correction). Deep-sea biology is mentioned as a motivation, but no animals are identified or analysed. The image processing is generic scene enhancement.

title: Creatures Great and SMAL: Recovering the Shape and Motion of Animals from Video
reason: Computer vision method for 3D shape and pose recovery of quadrupeds from video; evaluated on real video of animals including wild species (tiger, bear, impala, rhino) alongside domestic ones (dog, cat, cows, horse) and synthetic data.

title: Biometric Fish Classification of Temperate Species Using Convolutional Neural Network with Squeeze-and-Excitation
reason: CNN classification of fish species from underwater video frames recorded in natural coastal environments (Taiwan and Norway).

title: Primate Face Identification in the Wild
reason: Proposes a deep-learning face identification method for individual primates; data include free-ranging rhesus macaques in an urban area and chimpanzees from a national park, together with zoo chimpanzees.

title: Distinguishing individual red pandas from their faces
venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science Including Subseries Lecture Notes in Artificial Intelligence and Lecture Notes in Bioinformatics
reason: All images of red pandas were collected at a captive breeding base; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: SSD-Mobilenet Implementation for Classifying Fish Species
venue: Advances in intelligent systems and computing
reason: Applies a CNN detector to images of wild-caught fish species (fishing/sports images from ImageNet) for species detection and classification aimed at fisheries management.

title: Proposal-Refined Weakly Supervised Object Detection in Underwater Images
reason: Detection of sea cucumbers, sea urchins and scallops is framed as support for aquaculture harvesting robots (marine products in production). The paper does not describe where the images come from or whether the animals are wild.

title: Bird Species Classification Using Transfer Learning with Multistage Training
venue: Communications in computer and information science
reason: Deep learning classification of bird species from photographs of birds in natural settings (occlusion by leaves/branches, varied lighting); primary method study.

title: Effects of the Neonicotinoid Insecticide Clothianidin on Southern Leopard Frog (Rana sphenocephala) Tadpole Behavior
venue: Bulletin of Environmental Contamination and Toxicology
reason: Ecotoxicology laboratory experiment: wild-collected tadpoles were exposed to an insecticide in aquaria and video-tracked in indoor observational arenas; no images of free-ranging animals.

title: Deep learning analysis of nest camera video recordings reveals temperature-sensitive incubation behavior in the purple martin (Progne subis)
reason: Applies a deep learning frame classifier to nest camera video of wild purple martins breeding in nest boxes at a wildlife refuge to quantify incubation behaviour.

title: Underwater photogrammetry in Antarctica: long-term observations in benthic ecosystems and legacy data rescue
reason: Primary study applying photogrammetry (structure from motion, multi-view stereo) to diver-recorded video of wild Antarctic benthic animals in situ to produce 3D models and orthophotos used for abundance and volume estimates.

title: Using 3D photogrammetry from ROV video to quantify cold-water coral reef structural complexity and investigate its influence on biodiversity and community assemblage
reason: Primary study applying structure-from-motion photogrammetry to ROV video of a wild cold-water coral reef and its associated fauna to derive 3D rugosity and coral cover.

title: Automatic identification and behavioral analysis of phlebotomine sand flies using trajectory features
reason: Sand flies were trapped in the field, but all the analysed videos were recorded in a wooden box under laboratory conditions. No images show free-ranging animals.

title: The Role of Forest Elephants in Shaping Tropical Forest–Savanna Coexistence
reason: Ecological study of wild forest elephants using camera traps; the images were classified and counted manually by citizen-science volunteers and aggregated with a plurality vote. No computer vision method is applied to the images.

title: Herding mechanisms to maintain the cohesion of a harem group: two interaction phases during herding
reason: Drone video of free-ranging feral horses in Portugal, analysed with video tracking software to get individual trajectories during herding.

title: Photography as a tool for avian morphometric measurements
reason: Wild migrating birds caught in mist nets were photographed, and a person measured them by hand with the ImageJ measure tool. No automated computer vision or algorithmic image analysis is developed or applied.

title: EventFinder: a program for screening remotely captured images
reason: Develops and evaluates a background-subtraction program to screen camera trap images of free-ranging animals collected in a provincial recreation area.

title: PelagiCam: a novel underwater imaging system with computer vision for semi-automated monitoring of mobile marine fauna at offshore structures
reason: Primary study applying motion-detection computer vision software to underwater video of wild pelagic fish and jellyfish around an offshore mussel farm and open-water control sites.

title: Analysis of Anemotactic Flight Tendencies of the Spotted Lanternfly (Lycorma delicatula) during the 2017 Mass Dispersal Flights in Pennsylvania
reason: Smartphone video of free-flying wild (invasive) spotted lanternflies, processed with background subtraction, detection, trajectory tracking and template matching to analyse flight behaviour.

title: Context is more important than habitat type in determining use by juvenile fish
reason: Ecological study of juvenile fish habitat use from remote underwater video. Fish were identified and counted manually by experts; the only machine learning is classification and regression trees on tabular habitat and assemblage data, not image analysis.

title: Ocelot identification through spots
reason: Proposes a computer vision method to identify individual wild ocelots from camera-trap images using spot patterns.

title: A structural based feature extraction for detecting the relation of hidden substructures in coral reef images
reason: Proposes colour texture descriptors for classifying underwater coral reef images (corals are animals, imaged in situ), evaluated on four coral reef datasets plus generic texture benchmarks.

title: Interactive rodent behavior annotation in video using active learning
reason: Behaviour annotation of laboratory rats and mice recorded in confined arenas (neuroscience experiments); no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: An efficient interactive segmentation algorithm using color correction for underwater images
reason: Generic underwater image segmentation (colour correction + DCP + GrabCut); no animals are named as subjects and wildlife is not the stated application.

title: Automatic Fish Species Classification Using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
reason: CNN classification of fish species using images including in situ underwater images of fish in their natural environment (QUT fish, LifeCLEF 2015).

title: Saliency Subtraction Inspired Automated Event Detection in Underwater Environments
reason: Proposes a saliency-based computer vision method for event detection in unconstrained underwater videos showing free-ranging fish and other marine life.

title: Machine vision based local fish recognition
reason: Images are of dead fish photographed at local fish markets on a white background, not free-ranging animals in the wild; treated as specimens.

title: Camera traps provide a robust alternative to direct observations for constructing social networks of wild chimpanzees
reason: Camera-trap videos of wild chimpanzees were coded manually by human observers to identify individuals for social network analysis; no computer vision or automated image analysis is applied.

title: Common bottlenose dolphin (Tursiops truncatus) problem solving strategies in response to a novel interactive apparatus
reason: Behavioural cognition study of zoo-housed dolphins; videos were coded manually by a human coder, with no computer vision analysis (animals are also captive only).

title: Real-time thermal imagery from an unmanned aerial vehicle can locate ground nests of a grassland songbird at rates similar to traditional methods
reason: Field comparison of UAV thermal nest searches with traditional searches; a human pilot inspects the live thermal feed by eye and no computer vision or automated image analysis is applied.

title: Measuring the spectral signature of polar bears from a drone to improve their detection from space
reason: Drone multispectral imagery of live wild polar bears analysed with supervised pixel classification to separate bears from background.

title: Comparing an automated high-definition oblique camera system to rear-seat-observers in a wildlife survey in Tsavo, Kenya: Taking multi-species aerial counts to the next level
reason: Aerial oblique images of wild animals (with some livestock) were interpreted visually by human interpreters; no computer vision or automated image analysis method is developed or applied.

title: The Making of a Flight Feather: Bio-architectural Principles and Adaptation
reason: Developmental and biophysical study of feather architecture. Image analysis is applied to microscopy of histological feather-rachis sections and micro-CT of feathers from farm, laboratory, pet-store, taxidermy and carcass sources; no images of wild, free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: An assessment of fish and marine growth associated with an oil and gas platform jacket using an augmented remotely operated vehicle
reason: Stereo-video imagery from an ROV of wild fish at an offshore platform; fish were counted and measured from stereo video, and individual whale sharks were re-identified with the I3S spot-matching software.

title: Probabilistic Models of Larval Zebrafish Behavior Reveal Structure on Many Scales
reason: Laboratory study of larval zebrafish filmed in an indoor arena with a moving camera; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Anabranch network for camouflaged object segmentation
reason: Proposes a segmentation network and a web-collected dataset of camouflaged objects, most of which are naturally camouflaged animals (mammals, insects, birds, reptiles, amphibians, underwater animals) in natural environments; wildlife preservation is a stated application. The dataset also contains camouflaged humans.

title: Fish-Pak: Fish species dataset from Pakistan for visual features based classification
reason: Data article on six carp species popular for fish farming, taken from farms, pools and head works and photographed out of water against a uniform background in a controlled set-up. Some fish were captured at the Chenab River, so a wild origin for part of the data cannot be ruled out, but no free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Analysis of the population structure of a gorgonian forest (Placogorgia sp.) using a photogrammetric 3D modeling approach at Le Danois Bank, Cantabrian Sea
venue: Deep Sea Research Part I Oceanographic Research Papers
reason: Primary study applying Structure-from-Motion photogrammetric 3D reconstruction to underwater video of a wild deep-sea gorgonian coral (animal) population in a marine protected area.

title: Spatial patterns of arctic sponge ground fauna and demersal fish are detectable in autonomous underwater vehicle (AUV) imagery
venue: Deep Sea Research Part I Oceanographic Research Papers
reason: AUV imagery of wild deep-sea megafauna and demersal fish was annotated manually by experts; no automated computer vision analysis of animals is developed or applied (only automatic photomosaic stitching for visualisation).

title: A SIFT-based software system for the photo-identification of the Risso's dolphin
reason: Computer vision photo-identification of wild Risso's dolphins photographed from a boat in the Gulf of Taranto.

title: An automated program to find animals and crop photographs for individual recognition
reason: Develops and tests a HOG+SVM object detector to automatically find and crop giraffe torsos in photographs of wild, free-ranging Masai giraffes for individual recognition.

title: Real-time fish detection in complex backgrounds using probabilistic background modelling
reason: Proposes a background-modelling method to detect free-swimming fish in underwater videos of coral reefs (Fish4Knowledge).

title: Cascaded deep network systems with linked ensemble components for underwater fish detection in the wild
reason: Proposes a deep detection network for fish in underwater videos taken in the wild; primary research with computer vision on free-ranging animals.

title: Semantic region of interest and species classification in the deep neural network feature domain
reason: Proposes a DNN-feature-domain semantic region detection and species classification method for camera-trap images of wild animals (Snapshot Serengeti).

title: Image-based species identification of wild bees using convolutional neural networks
reason: A CNN identifies wild bee species from wing images. The bee images come from wild species collected by entomologists. A second dataset uses pinned museum butterfly specimens.

title: Zilong: A tool to identify empty images in camera-trap data
reason: Proposes a non-machine-learning image-processing algorithm and software to identify empty images in camera-trap data of wild animals from Snapshot Serengeti and Mt. Gongga.

title: Detection and identification of European woodpeckers with deep convolutional neural networks
reason: The study analyses only acoustic recordings of woodpecker drums and calls; image CNNs are applied to spectrograms of sound, not to images or video of animals.

title: RoI detection and segmentation algorithms for marine mammals photo-identification
reason: Develops and compares RoI detection and segmentation methods on photos of wild Commerson's dolphins taken in the open from boats.

title: Animals exhibit consistent individual differences in their movement: A case study on location trajectories of Japanese macaques
reason: Individual identification from 3D location trajectories recorded by Bluetooth Low Energy beacons; no image or video data are analysed. The animals are also captive, housed in a cage at a research institute.

title: Spatial pattern of pika holes and their effects on vegetation coverage on the Tibetan Plateau: An analysis using unmanned aerial vehicle imagery
reason: Applies image classification to UAV imagery to map pika holes (burrows, direct signs of wild plateau pikas) in Tibetan grasslands.

title: Comparing random forests and convoluted neural networks for mapping ghost crab burrows using imagery from an unmanned aerial vehicle
reason: Applies RF and CNN within OBIA to UAV imagery to map burrows (direct signs) of wild ghost crabs on a sandy beach.

title: A segmentation-based approach for polyp counting in the wild
reason: Proposes a CNN segmentation-based method to detect and count jellyfish polyps in underwater images captured in the wild.

title: Underwater video mosaicing using topology and superpixel-based pairwise stitching
reason: Proposes a computer vision mosaicing method for underwater videos of wild coral reefs (corals are animals) for benthic surveys.

title: Fish movements and schooling behavior across the tidal channel in a Mediterranean coastal lagoon: An automated approach using acoustic imaging
reason: Applies automated image analysis (background subtraction and blob counting) to multibeam imaging-sonar video to count wild fish migrating through a tidal channel of a coastal lagoon.

title: A powerful method for measuring fish size of small-scale fishery catches using ImageJ
reason: Develops an automatic image-analysis (ImageJ grey-level segmentation) procedure to measure length of wild reef fishes from small-scale fishery catches in Madagascar.

title: Digital image analysis of flatfish bleeding injury
reason: Dead, trawl-caught flatfish (fresh or defrosted) were photographed on a lighting table in a laboratory set-up to quantify bleeding injury; no images show wild, free-ranging animals.

title: Improving Pest Bird Detection in a Vineyard Environment using Super-Resolution and Deep Learning
reason: Computer vision (motion detection, super-resolution, CNN classification) on video of free-flying wild pest birds in a vineyard and a blueberry field; primary research.

title: ResFeats: Residual network based features for underwater image classification
reason: Proposes deep ResNet features for classifying benthic marine species (corals, urchins, sponges, tunicates) in underwater reef survey images; wild animals in situ are the stated application.

title: Comparison of diver operated stereo-video and visual census to assess targeted fish species in Mediterranean marine protected areas
venue: Journal of Experimental Marine Biology and Ecology
reason: Wild fish were filmed with diver-operated stereo-video, but the footage was annotated manually in EventMeasure software. The study compares survey methods (stereo-video vs. visual census). It does not develop, apply or evaluate an automated image-analysis method.

title: A comparison of stereo-BRUV, diver operated and remote stereo-video transects for assessing reef fish assemblages
venue: Journal of Experimental Marine Biology and Ecology
reason: Compares stereo-video sampling techniques for wild reef fish; videos were analysed manually by observers in EventMeasure software. The paper uses no automated computer vision method.

title: MarmoDetector: A novel 3D automated system for the quantitative assessment of marmoset behavior
reason: Kinect depth-based tracking of purchased laboratory marmosets housed in experimental cages for neuroscience research; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Towards image-based animal tracking in natural environments using a freely moving camera
reason: Primary study that develops a visual detection and tracking method for animals filmed in their natural environment with a hand-held or drone camera, evaluated on field videos of ants, a dung beetle, a woodlouse and wild dogs.

title: An analysis of altitude, citizen science and a convolutional neural network feedback loop on object detection in Unmanned Aerial Systems
reason: CNN with feedback loop to detect and count wild lesser snow geese in UAS imagery from Wapusk National Park.

title: Coral species identification with texture or structure images using a two-level classifier based on Convolutional Neural Networks
reason: CNN-based species classification of underwater images of wild corals and other reef invertebrates, with a new dataset of coral structure images.

title: Automated species-level identification of planktic foraminifera using convolutional neural networks, with comparison to human performance
