reason: CNN classification of planktic foraminifera tests picked from sediment cores and imaged under a reflected-light microscope in the lab; these are microscopy specimens, not wild free-ranging animals in images.

title: Changes in logbook reporting by commercial fishers following the implementation of electronic monitoring in Australian Commonwealth fisheries
reason: The study statistically compares fisher-reported logbook catch, discard and protected-species interaction rates before and after electronic monitoring was introduced. It applies no computer vision or image analysis; camera footage is only reviewed by human analysts outside the study.

title: Use of computer vision onboard fishing vessels to quantify catches: The iObserver
reason: Primary study developing a computer vision device that identifies species and estimates length of wild-caught fish on a vessel conveyor belt for fisheries monitoring. The fish are wild-caught, non-domestic animals, but they are dead catch rather than free-ranging animals, so inclusion is a borderline call.

title: A test of camera surveys to study fungus-animal interactions
reason: Primary study applying motion-detection software to time-lapse camera images of wild animals (mainly insects) visiting mushrooms in a forest.

title: Faster R-CNN for marine organisms detection and recognition using data augmentation
reason: Proposes underwater-specific data augmentation for Faster R-CNN detection and recognition of marine organisms (sea urchin, sea cucumber, scallop) in real underwater seafloor images. The paper does not say whether the animals are wild or ranched, so 'wild_free_ranging' is an assumption.

title: Fine-grained visual categorization of butterfly specimens at sub-species level via a convolutional neural network with skip-connections
reason: CNN classification of lab-photographed butterfly specimens; no images of wild, free-ranging animals.

title: Reliability of marine faunal detections in drone-based monitoring
reason: Drone video of wild marine fauna is analysed only by human observers (live pilot sightings versus manual post-analysis in a media player); no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated. Neural networks are only discussed as a future option.

title: Novel event analysis for human-machine collaborative underwater exploration
reason: Proposes CV methods for detecting, tracking and summarizing novel events (e.g., deep sea fish, lobster) in video from a deep sea submersible.

title: Drivers of stereotypic behaviour and physiological stress among captive jungle cat (Felis chaus Schreber, 1777) in India
reason: The study measures behaviour of captive jungle cats in Indian zoos through direct focal observation and faecal glucocorticoid assays. It analyses no images or video and uses no computer vision.

title: Evaluating the ecological status of cold-water coral habitats using non-invasive methods: An example from Cassidaigne canyon, northwestern Mediterranean Sea
reason: Applies photogrammetry (structure-from-motion 3D reconstruction) to ROV images and video of wild cold-water coral colonies in a submarine canyon to measure distribution, density and size.

title: A generalised volumetric method to estimate the biomass of photographically surveyed benthic megafauna
reason: Proposes and tests an image-based measurement method (GVM) to estimate the biomass of wild benthic megafauna from AUV seafloor photographs and from photos of trawl-caught specimens. The image analysis is manual measurement in Image-Pro Plus, so inclusion is borderline.

title: Design of an Animal Detection System for Motor Vehicle Drivers
reason: Engineering design of a vehicle-mounted infrared animal warning system. The only image analysis is colour-histogram matching against a database, tested on a bench photograph of a dairy cow. No images of wild, free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Salient Spin Images: An application to archaeozoology for bones recognition
reason: 3D recognition of archaeological horse bone specimens from excavation pits; no wild free-ranging animals imaged.

title: Animal species recognition in the wildlife based on muzzle and shape features using joint CNN
reason: Proposes a joint CNN for species recognition on camera-trap images of wild animals from Ergaki national park; the classes include a domestic dog alongside wild species.

title: First assessments of the taphonomic behaviour of jaguar (Panthera onca)
reason: Taphonomic study of tooth marks left by captive jaguars on horse bones; marks are examined with hand lenses and compared statistically, and no computer vision or image analysis is applied. The animals are also captive only.

title: Who ate OH80 (Olduvai Gorge, Tanzania)? A geometric-morphometric analysis of surface bone modifications of a Paranthropus boisei skeleton
reason: Analyses 3D scans of bone surface marks on a fossil hominin femur compared with tooth pits made by carnivores in a nature park enclosure; no images of wild free-ranging animals, only specimens and captive-produced marks.

title: Fluid lensing and machine learning for centimeter-resolution airborne assessment of coral reefs in American Samoa
reason: Develops a supervised machine learning segmentation of drone fluid-lensing imagery of a wild coral reef, separating living coral (branching, mounding) from non-living structure; corals are wild animals.

title: SealNet: A fully-automated pack-ice seal detection pipeline for sub-meter satellite imagery
reason: Proposes a CNN pipeline (SealNet) to detect and count wild Antarctic pack-ice seals in WorldView-3 satellite imagery.

title: Wildlife Insights: A Platform to Maximize the Potential of Camera Trap and Other Passive Sensor Wildlife Data for the Planet
reason: Platform description paper that develops a CNN species-identification service for camera trap images of wildlife. Borderline: no experiments or evaluation are reported, so it could also be read as a perspective (E-REVIEW).

title: Emperors on thin ice: three years of breeding failure at Halley Bay
reason: Applies supervised image classification to very high resolution satellite imagery to estimate the size of wild emperor penguin colonies.

title: Hawks steer attacks using a guidance system tuned for close pursuit of erratically manoeuvring targets
reason: The analysed video shows only captive-bred, falconer-handled Harris' Hawks chasing an artificial lure in a staged experiment; no wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Artificial intelligence reveals environmental constraints on colour diversity in insects
reason: Deep learning is applied to photographs of dead, spread moth specimens kept in an institute collection. The moths were caught in the wild, but the images show museum-type specimens, not free-ranging animals.

title: Real-time analysis of the behaviour of groups of mice via a depth-sensing camera and machine learning
reason: Real-time depth/infrared tracking and behaviour analysis of laboratory mutant mice housed in test cages; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: idtracker.ai: tracking all individuals in small or large collectives of unmarked animals
reason: Tracking and identification method tested only on laboratory-reared animals (zebrafish, fruit flies, mice, medaka, ants) filmed in laboratory arenas; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Unsupervised identification of the internal states that shape natural behavior
reason: Laboratory study of Drosophila melanogaster courtship in behavioural chambers; computer vision (DeepFlyTrack) is used only to track lab-reared flies, with no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Using DeepLabCut for 3D markerless pose estimation across species and behaviors
reason: Toolbox/protocol paper for markerless pose estimation. The new use case analyses cheetahs kept at a cheetah centre (captive, pursuit task), plus laboratory mice, flies and horses; no wild free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Isolation and no-entry marine reserves mitigate anthropogenic impacts on grey reef shark behavior
reason: Ecological study of grey reef shark occurrence and behaviour from baited underwater videos. Videos were coded manually by observers and analysed with statistical models (GLM, multinomial); no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: High resolution mapping of a cold water coral mound
reason: Object-based image analysis and machine learning classification of an ROV video mosaic to map live cold-water corals and individual sponges (wild benthic animals) on a deep-sea mound.

title: Automated detection of koalas using low-level aerial surveillance and machine learning
reason: Primary study applying deep-learning object detection to drone thermal imagery of free-ranging koalas in natural eucalypt forest.

title: Computer vision enables short- and long-term analysis of Lophelia pertusa polyp behaviour and colour from an underwater observatory
reason: Computer vision (segmentation and CNN patch classification) applied to in-situ images of a wild cold-water coral reef (Lophelia pertusa) from a fixed underwater observatory.

title: Background matching and disruptive coloration as habitat-specific strategies for camouflage
reason: Image analysis of camouflage in wild-caught shore crabs, but the crabs were photographed only in a laboratory photography room; the field images show habitat backgrounds without animals, so no image shows wild free-ranging animals.

title: Biological effects 26 years after simulated deep-sea mining
reason: Ecological study of deep-sea megafauna from AUV photo-mosaics; animals were identified and measured manually by a human annotator in BIIGLE, with no automated image analysis of animals.

title: Insights and approaches using deep learning to classify wildlife
reason: Trains and interprets CNNs for species classification on camera-trap images of wild African mammals from Gorongosa National Park.

title: Using weather radar to monitor the number, timing and directions of flying-foxes emerging from their roosts
reason: The study estimates flying-fox numbers, emergence timing and direction from weather radar reflectivity and radial velocity using threshold-based signal processing; no computer vision method is applied to image or video data.

title: Measuring vision using innate behaviours in mice with intact and impaired retina function
reason: Laboratory mice (visually intact and retinal degeneration strains) tracked in an open field arena to assay vision; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Morphological differences between coastal bottlenose dolphin (Tursiops aduncus) populations identified using non-invasive stereo-laser photogrammetry
reason: Applies image-based stereo-laser photogrammetry to photographs of free-ranging bottlenose dolphins to measure body length; image measurement of wild animals (borderline, as measurement is manual in ImageJ).

title: Migrating eastern North Pacific gray whale call and blow rates estimated from acoustic recordings, infrared camera video, and visual sightings
reason: Infrared video of wild gray whales was processed manually: an analyst clicked on each blow. No computer vision method detects or analyses the animals. The only image processing is a greyscale variance measure used as a visibility check. The study is about acoustic and blow cue rates.

title: Emergence of consistent intra-individual locomotor patterns during zebrafish development
reason: Laboratory study of zebrafish larvae locomotor behaviour in well plates, tracked with commercial video-tracking software; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Automated tracking and analysis of ant trajectories shows variation in forager exploration
reason: Deep learning detection and tracking of wild carpenter ants filmed on undisturbed foraging trails in a tropical forest.

title: Whale counting in satellite and aerial images with deep learning
reason: Primary study proposing a two-step CNN system to detect and count free-ranging whales in satellite and aerial images.

title: Divergent evolution of terrestrial locomotor abilities in extant Crocodylia
reason: Gait analysis by video of captive crocodylians at a zoo (St. Augustine Alligator Farm Zoological Park), with footfalls coded by hand and markers digitized. All animals were captive.

title: Robust mouse tracking in complex environments using neural networks
reason: Tracking of single laboratory mice in open field arenas for behavioural experiments; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Snail shell colour evolution in urban heat islands detected via citizen science
reason: Citizen-science smartphone photos of wild Cepaea nemoralis were classified for shell colour and banding by human validators and then analysed statistically; no computer vision or automated image analysis is applied.

title: Varied channels region proposal and classification network for wildlife image classification under complex environment
reason: Proposes a CNN-based region proposal and classification network for camera-trap images of wild mammals in a wetland preserve.

title: Image recognition in UAV videos using convolutional neural networks
reason: CNN classification of UAV video images of wild dolphins and seabirds in the open sea.

title: Extracting animal migration pattern from weather radar observation based on deep convolutional neural networks
reason: Applies a fully convolutional network to segment biological echoes (wild migrating birds and insects) from weather echoes in weather radar images. This counts as image-based computer vision on free-ranging animals.

title: Animal species classification using machine learning techniques
reason: Primary study classifying images of animal faces as predator or pet using hand-crafted features with SVM and MLP. The data combine non-domestic predator animals with pets; the paper does not state whether the predator images show free-ranging animals.

title: Beach safety: can drones provide a platform for sighting sharks?
reason: Drone video of plywood shark analogues was reviewed by a human pilot and a human observer; no computer vision method is applied to the imagery.

title: Precision mapping of snail habitat provides a powerful indicator of human schistosomiasis transmission
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
reason: Epidemiological/ecological field study relating snail counts (physical quadrat sampling) and habitat area to human schistosomiasis. Drone and Google Earth imagery was hand-scored for vegetation/habitat area only; no computer vision method is applied, and the imagery shows habitat, not animals.

title: Optimizing observing strategies for monitoring animals using drone-mounted thermal infrared cameras
reason: The paper gives physics-based guidance for planning drone thermal-infrared surveys (flying height, atmosphere, ground temperature, vegetation). Riverine rabbits were found by visual inspection of footage and confirmed by observers on foot; no computer vision method is developed or evaluated on the animal images.

title: A Proposal of an Animal Detection System Using Machine Learning
reason: Primary study that applies block-based feature extraction and ML classifiers to detect animals in images, aimed at wildlife-vehicle collisions on roads. The analysed data are synthetic images that mix wild animals (capybara, snake) with domestic ones (horse, bull, dog).

title: Coral habitat mapping: a comparison between maximum likelihood, Bayesian and Dempster–Shafer classifiers
reason: Satellite-based benthic habitat / substrate cover mapping (live coral, dead coral with algae, rubble, sand); the subject is habitat cover classes, not animals as such.

title: Using radio frequency identification for behavioral monitoring in little blue penguins
venue: Journal of Applied Animal Welfare Science
reason: Behavioural monitoring of captive zoo penguins uses RFID tags and antennae, not image analysis. Video was only compared by hand to validate the RFID system.

title: Etho-morphology using smartphone apps to identify aves
reason: Education study in which students identify zoo birds by hand from smartphone photos in an app; there is no computer vision analysis of images. The animals are also captive (Bandung Zoo).

title: Butterfly Recognition Based on Faster R-CNN
reason: Applies Faster R-CNN to detect and classify butterflies in photos; data combine specimen pattern photos with ecological photos of butterflies taken in the wild.

title: Comparative Study of Tiger Identification Using Template Matching Approach based on Edge Patterns
reason: Primary study applying edge detection and template matching to internet images of a wild Sumatran tiger ('Bonita') on oil palm plantations.

title: Fish Species Classification Using Probabilistic Neural Network
reason: Computer vision classification of landed, dead fish photographed out of water at a fishing port and a market; the images show specimens, not wild free-ranging animals. Borderline: the fish are wild-caught, non-domestic species.

title: Turtle species identification design based on CNN
reason: Applies a CNN to classify turtle species in images crawled from the internet. The paper does not say whether the turtles are wild or captive, and turtles are non-domestic taxa, so the paper is included.

title: Automatic detection of flying bird species using computer vision techniques
reason: Proposes a CNN-based camera system to detect, count and classify free-flying bird species in an outdoor area; the image data used are not described, so the subject type of analysed data is not reported.

title: Competition and cooperation among chimney swifts at roost entry
reason: Primary study applying automatic multi-camera video tracking and 3D reconstruction to free-flying wild chimney swifts entering a roost chimney.

title: Intelligent audio bird repeller for transmission line tower based on bird species variation
venue: IOP Conference Series Materials Science and Engineering
reason: Proposes a bird repeller system that identifies wild bird species approaching transmission towers from camera images (YOLO-LITE) as well as from vocalizations; primary system design paper.

title: Using web-sourced photography to explore the diet of a declining African raptor, the Martial Eagle (Polemaetus bellicosus)
reason: Researchers looked through web-sourced photographs of wild Martial Eagles by eye to identify their prey. No computer vision method is used to analyse the animals; the only automated step is MORPHIC's duplicate-image removal.

title: Building a Body Shape Morphospace of Teleostean Fishes
reason: Body shape traits of museum fish specimens were measured by hand with calipers and analysed with phylogenetic comparative methods. Photographs were used only to manually re-measure some erroneous values in ImageJ, so there is no computer vision analysis.

title: Scaling of size, shape and surface roughness in Antarctic krill swarms
reason: Wild Antarctic krill swarms are analysed, but only from acoustic echosounder (sonar) echograms. No camera images or video are used.

title: Automatic fish detection in underwater videos by a deep neural network-based hybrid motion learning system
reason: Proposes a hybrid GMM + optical flow + R-CNN method to detect freely swimming fish in unconstrained underwater videos of coral reefs.

title: Identifying the species of harvested tuna and billfish using deep convolutional neural networks
reason: Primary study applying CNN image classification to photographs of wild-caught tuna, billfish, shark and other fish taken on the decks of longline fishing vessels (fishery catch monitoring, not aquaculture). The fish are harvested wild animals, so wild_free_ranging is the closest subject type.

title: Deep neural networks for analysis of fisheries surveillance video and automated monitoring of fish discards
reason: Primary study applying instance segmentation and species classification to CCTV video of wild-caught fish (discards) on conveyor belts of commercial and research fishing trawlers; wild capture fisheries, not aquaculture. title: Automatic segmentation of fish using deep learning with application to fish size measurement
reason: Instance segmentation (Mask R-CNN) of wild marine fish imaged by an in-trawl stereo camera during survey cruises; primary research.

title: Image-based, unsupervised estimation of fish size from commercial landings using deep learning
reason: Computer vision is applied, but only to dead, landed commercial fish in boxes at an auction centre; no images of wild, free-ranging animals are analysed. No exclusion code fits exactly; E-NOCV is the forced single choice and is not literally accurate (the paper does use image analysis).

title: Automatic detection of Western rock lobster using synthetic data
reason: Deep-learning object detection of wild Western rock lobsters in AUV-collected underwater images, trained with synthetic parts data.

title: Optimizing image-based protocol to monitor macroepibenthic communities colonizing artificial structures
reason: The paper optimises a manual point-count annotation protocol (point density, projection method, sampling area, taxonomic resolution) for diver photographs of benthic communities. All labelling is done visually by humans; no automated image analysis is applied.

title: Automatic plankton quantification using deep features
reason: The paper quantifies class prevalence of marine phytoplankton and other microscopic plankton (diatoms, ciliates, flagellates) imaged by an in situ imaging flow cytometer; the imaged particles are chlorophyll-containing microorganisms, not animals.

title: Automated Taxonomic Identification of Insects with Expert-Level Accuracy Using Effective Feature Transfer from Convolutional Networks
reason: CNN feature transfer for taxonomic identification of insects from images of preserved (museum/collection) specimens photographed in lab settings; no images of wild, free-ranging animals.

title: Eyes on the size: accuracy of visual length estimates of white sharks, Carcharodon carcharias
reason: The study tests how accurate human visual length estimates of wild white sharks are. Stereo-video is used only as a reference: lengths are measured by hand, point to point, in EventMeasure software. No computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Early-life lessons of the courtship dance in a dance-duetting songbird, the Java sparrow
reason: Behavioural study of laboratory-bred captive Java sparrows. The videos were scored manually and analysed with statistical models (GLMM/LME). There is no computer vision or automated image analysis.

title: The pursuit strategy of predatory bluefish (Pomatomus saltatrix)
venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences
reason: Biomechanics study of pursuit kinematics of bluefish held in an outdoor tank; fish positions were tracked manually in video, with no computer vision method developed or applied.

title: Müllerian mimicry in bumble bees is a transient continuum
reason: Applies a pretrained CNN (VGG-16) to standardised colour-pattern images of wild bumble bee species to measure how similar the patterns look, in order to study mimicry. Borderline: the images are drawn templates, not photographs.

title: Satiety, Thermosensation and Mechanosensation Regulate a Spontaneous C. elegans Sleep State
reason: Laboratory neuroscience study of C. elegans sleep behaviour in microfluidic chambers imaged under microscopes; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Modelling the Perception of Colour Patterns in Vertebrates with HMAX
reason: Method paper presenting HMAX/sparse-HMAX and applying it to images of a wild, non-domestic primate species (mandrill faces) for individual similarity; capture conditions (wild vs captive) are not stated.

title: A low-cost, open-source framework for tracking and behavioural analysis of animals in aquatic ecosystems
reason: Develops a deep-learning and structure-from-motion framework to detect, track and analyse behaviour of free-ranging fish filmed underwater in their natural environment.

title: ezTrack: An open-source video analysis pipeline for the investigation of animal behavior
reason: Open-source video tracking and freezing analysis tool validated only on laboratory mice in behavioural assays (place preference, light-dark box, elevated plus maze, water maze, linear track, fear conditioning); no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: MARGO (Massively Automated Real-time GUI for Object-tracking), a platform for high-throughput ethology
reason: Real-time tracking software developed and tested on laboratory fruit flies and other laboratory organisms in behavioural arenas and multiwell plates; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: DeepPoseKit, a software toolkit for fast and robust animal pose estimation using deep learning
reason: Deep-learning pose estimation toolkit evaluated on laboratory fly and locust datasets and on drone video of wild Grévy's zebras, so part of the data shows wild free-ranging animals.

title: FoxMask: a new automated tool for animal detection in camera trap images
reason: Primary study presenting a background-subtraction tool to detect animal presence in camera trap images of wild arctic foxes at dens.

title: The conspicuousness of the toxic Heliconius butterflies across time and habitat
reason: Calibrated photography and colour analysis of the fresh wings of collected butterfly specimens, photographed in the field. The analysed images show dead specimens, not free-ranging animals.

title: Measuring Perceptual Distance of Organismal Color Pattern using the Features of Deep Neural Networks
reason: The method measures colour-pattern similarity, but none of the analysed images show free-ranging animals. The images are published colour templates and plates, pinned museum specimens (velvet ants), laboratory-crossed guppies and synthetic cartoon images.

title: An Open Source Unsupervised Algorithm for Identification and Fast Prediction of Behaviors
reason: Unsupervised behaviour segmentation method developed and evaluated on video of laboratory mice in an open-field arena (plus lab rat, fruit fly and human demonstration data); no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Looking for mimicry in a snake assemblage using deep learning
reason: Primary study that fine-tunes CNNs on Internet and field photographs of Western Palearctic snakes to quantify visual resemblance and detect candidate Batesian mimics.

title: Automated analysis of sleep in adult C. elegans with closed-loop assessment of state-dependent neural activity
reason: Laboratory study of sleep behaviour and neural activity in cultured C. elegans strains inside microfluidic devices under a microscope; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Automating the analysis of fish abundance using object detection: optimising animal ecology with deep learning
reason: Primary study applying Mask R-CNN object detection to underwater video of wild luderick in seagrass meadows of Australian estuaries to estimate abundance.

title: finFindR : Computer-assisted Recognition and Identification of Bottlenose Dolphin Photos in R
reason: Develops neural-network software for detecting dorsal fins and re-identifying individual free-ranging bottlenose dolphins from field survey photographs.

title: Deep learning-based methods for individual recognition in small birds
reason: CNN-based individual re-identification from images of two wild bird populations (sociable weavers, great tits) plus a captive zebra finch population; primary research.

title: Concept for and Implementation of Wildlife Monitoring to Contribute Sustainable Development Goals

title: An Algorithm for Tracking Multiple Fish Based on Biological Water Quality Monitoring
reason: Multi-fish tracking of indicator fish in an indoor experimental tank under controlled laboratory conditions for water quality monitoring; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Multi-Scale Fish Segmentation Refinement and Missing Shape Recovery
reason: Segmentation method for images of wild-caught fish bycatch photographed in an onboard chute before release from trawlers; the animals are wild but captured at imaging time, so inclusion is a borderline call.

title: Video-Based Real Time Analysis of Plankton Particle Size Spectrum
reason: Plankton in collected water samples are imaged through a 10x microscope objective with a bench camera set-up; this is microscopy of samples, not in-situ imaging of free-ranging animals.

title: Deer Crossing Road Detection With Roadside LiDAR Sensor
reason: Detection and classification of wild deer crossing a wildlife overpass using roadside 3D LiDAR point clouds, a primary field study.

title: Bird Image Retrieval and Recognition Using a Deep Learning Platform
reason: Primary study that trains a CNN to recognise 27 bird species endemic to Taiwan from crowdsourced and Internet bird photographs, deployed as a birdwatching mobile app. The paper does not explicitly state that the photographed birds are wild; this is inferred from the birdwatching context.

title: Underwater Object Segmentation Integrating Transmission and Saliency Features

title: Semi-Supervised Fine-Grained Image Categorization Using Transfer Learning With Hierarchical Multi-Scale Adversarial Networks

title: Increasingly Specialized Perception Network for Fine-Grained Visual Categorization of Butterfly Specimens
reason: Fine-grained classification of photographed dead butterfly specimens under lab lighting; no free-ranging animals imaged. Other datasets are generic benchmarks.

title: 3-D Video Tracking of Multiple Fish in a Water Tank

reason: Primary study proposing saliency-based progressive image compression/restoration and an improved Faster RCNN for recognising six wild species in infrared-triggered monitoring-node images collected in the field in northern China.

title: Detection and Analysis of Behavior Trajectory for Sea Cucumbers Based on Deep Learning
reason: A single sea cucumber was filmed in an indoor glass aquarium as a laboratory set-up, and the stated goal is aquaculture. No wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Pose-Informed Face Alignment for Extreme Head Pose Variations in Animals

reason: Facial landmark localisation and head pose estimation for sheep (livestock) aimed at animal welfare and pain detection; no wild, free-ranging non-domestic animals.

title: Estimating the Population of Large Animals in the Wild Using Satellite Imagery: A Case Study of Hippos in Zambia’s Luangwa River

reason: Proposes a CNN-based object detection method for underwater images of marine animals (sea urchin, sea cucumber, scallop, starfish). The paper never says whether the animals are wild or farmed. They are marine life in underwater scenes, so the paper is included.

title: Incorporating Stereo with Convolutional Neural Networks for Real-Time Fish Detection and Classification
venue: IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Intelligent Systems and IEEE Conference on Robotics, Automation and Mechatronics (CIS-RAM)

reason: Trains a CNN for species recognition on camera-trap images of wild animals from nature reserves, with distributed multi-GPU training to speed it up.

reason: Proposes automatic image-based individual recognition of brown trout from uncontrolled photographs taken in the wild.

title: Underwater Object Tracking Benchmark and Dataset
venue: IEEE International Symposium on Technologies for Homeland Security (HST)

reason: Classification of smartphone photos of captured indigenous food fish (Bangladesh), framed around food production and nutrition; the fish were photographed out of their habitat and the paper does not say they are wild or free-ranging.

reason: Behaviour recognition of singly housed laboratory mice in home cages; no wild or free-ranging animals.

reason: Fish classification/localization framed for fisheries; classes are mostly ornamental/pet aquarium fish (goldfish, guppy, fighter, angel fish) and the image source is never stated, so there is no evidence of wild free-ranging animals.

title: Region Based Convolutional Neural Network for Human-Elephant Conflict Management System
venue: International Conference on Computational Intelligence in Data Science (ICCIDS)
reason: Applies CNN object detectors to images of elephants, lions and wolves collected from websites for a human-elephant conflict system intended for elephant corridors; whether the web images show wild or captive animals is not stated.

title: Fish Detection And Tracking For Turbid Underwater Video
venue: International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Control Systems (ICICCS)
reason: Fish detection and tracking is tested only on videos of a fish model in a laboratory water tank with milk-induced turbidity; no wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Three-D safari: Learning to estimate zebra pose, shape, and texture from images 'in the wild'

reason: Proposes a neural network method for 3D pose, shape and texture estimation of Grevy's zebras, evaluated on real images of zebras captured in Kenya.

title: Selective Sparse Sampling for Fine-Grained Image Recognition
venue: IEEE/CVF International Conference on Computer Vision (ICCV)
reason: Generic fine-grained recognition method evaluated on CUB birds, FGVC-Aircraft and Stanford Cars; wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Presence-Only Geographical Priors for Fine-Grained Image Classification

title: Pose-guided complementary features learning for amur tiger re-identification

title: A strong baseline for tiger Re-ID and its bag of tricks
venue: Proceedings 2019 International Conference on Computer Vision Workshop Iccvw 2019
reason: Primary study proposing a CNN-based re-identification method for tigers on the ATRW dataset, framed for wildlife monitoring; the paper does not state whether the tigers are wild or captive.

reason: Tiger detection method trained and evaluated only on the ATRW dataset, whose images the paper says were taken in wild zoos rather than of free-roaming tigers.

title: Part-Pose Guided Amur Tiger Re-Identification

title: Primate Markerless Pose Estimation and Movement Analysis Using DeepLabCut

title: A Deep Learning based CNN framework approach for Plankton Classification
venue: International Conference on Image Information Processing (ICIIP)
reason: Applies CNN-based image classification to web images of plankton groups, including free-living marine animals (crustaceans, cnidarians, molluscs). This is primary research.

title: Motion Saliency Based Generative Adversarial Network for Underwater Moving Object Segmentation

reason: Proposes a GAN-based moving object segmentation method evaluated on Fish4Knowledge underwater videos recorded by static underwater cameras (fish as moving foreground objects), alongside a generic change detection benchmark.

title: Giant Panda Face Recognition Using Small Dataset

reason: Individual face recognition of giant pandas on 163 images collected by a panda breeding base; no images of wild, free-ranging pandas are stated to be analysed.

title: Triplet Transform Learning for Automated Primate Face Recognition
venue: Proceedings - International Conference on Image Processing
reason: Proposes a computer vision method (Triplet Transform Learning) for individual face recognition of non-domestic primates (macaques, chimpanzees, gorillas), motivated by conservation. The paper does not say whether the images show wild or captive animals.

title: Recognizing Fish Species Captured Live on Wild Sea Surface in Videos by Deep Metric Learning with a Temporal Constraint
venue: Proceedings - International Conference on Image Processing
reason: Proposes a CNN-based fine-grained species classification method for wild-caught fish filmed by electronic monitoring cameras as they are pulled from the sea onto fishing vessels.

title: Cross-Connected Networks for Multi-Task Learning of Detection and Segmentation
venue: Proceedings - International Conference on Image Processing
reason: Proposes a multi-task CNN for detection and segmentation and tests it on wild-bird surveillance landscape images from wind turbine sites in Japan, as well as on pedestrians.

title: Transfer Learning Based Wildlife Recognition for Tele-Observation in Field Occlusion Environment

reason: Proposes an anti-occlusion loss for CNN species classification of camera-trap images of wild animals from nature reserves in China.

reason: CNN-based species-level insect image classification on indoor and outdoor photos collected from the Atlas of Living Australia, a biodiversity database that includes citizen science records.

title: Object Detection with Deep Learning for Underwater Environment

title: Compare More Nuanced: Pairwise Alignment Bilinear Network for Few-Shot Fine-Grained Learning
venue: IEEE International Conference on Multimedia and Expo (ICME)
reason: Generic few-shot fine-grained recognition method evaluated on standard benchmarks (birds, dogs, cars, MiniImageNet); wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Classification of Breeding Fish using Deep Learning from the Captured Video

title: Improving Underwater Obstacle Detection using Semantic Image Segmentation

reason: Tracking of tagged bottlenose dolphins housed in a zoo dolphinarium using ceiling-mounted cameras and on-body sensors; no wild or free-ranging animals in the data.

title: The Importance of Metric Learning for Robotic Vision: Open Set Recognition and Active Learning
venue: Proceedings - IEEE International Conference on Robotics and Automation/Proceedings
reason: Generic open set recognition and active learning method for robotic vision; birds appear only as classes of a fine-grained benchmark (CUB Birds200) alongside cars and flowers, and wildlife is not the stated subject.

title: Classification of Fish Species with Augmented Data using Deep Convolutional Neural Network
venue: IEEE International Conference on System Engineering and Technology (ICSET)

reason: Deep learning multilevel taxonomic classification of citizen-science photographs of Diptera (wild insects) photographed by nature enthusiasts.

title: Coral Classification Using DenseNet and Cross-modality Transfer Learning
reason: CNN- and GAN-based classification of corals in underwater reef survey images (EFC and MLC datasets), so the subjects are wild marine animals.

title: Underwater sea cucumbers detection based on pruned SSD
venue: IEEE Advanced Information Management, Communicates, Electronic and Automation Control Conference (IMCEC)
reason: Detection of farmed sea cucumbers at a sea cucumber breeding base, aimed at automated harvesting for the aquaculture industry.

title: A Novel Hierarchical Edge Computing Solution Based on Deep Learning for Distributed Image Recognition in IoT Systems
reason: Edge-computing CNN system that classifies images of wild animals (monkeys, birds, bears, wild boars) intruding into agricultural fields; this is a human-wildlife conflict application using camera images.

title: Proposal and Evaluation of A Method for Automatically Classifying Images of Agricultural Work and Animals Acquired with Motion Sensor Cameras

title: MFCC-based Houston Toad Call Detection using LSTM

title: Low Cost Autonomous Amphibious Bird Chasing Robot
reason: A robot uses a CNN detector on camera images to detect Canada geese on golf courses. The training data and demonstration include real, wild geese alongside decoys.

title: Image-Based Classification of Snake Species Using Convolutional Neural Network
venue: International Seminar on Research of Information Technology and Intelligent Systems (ISRITI)
reason: Applies CNNs to classify images of five wild, non-domestic venomous snake species. The paper does not say whether the snakes were photographed in the wild or in captivity.

title: Are These Birds Similar: Learning Branched Networks for Fine-grained Representations
venue: International Conference on Image and Vision Computing New Zealand (IVCNZ)
reason: Generic multimodal fine-grained image classification method evaluated on the CUB-200-2011 benchmark. Birds are only benchmark classes, and the paper does not state a wildlife or conservation application.

title: Vision-Based In Situ Monitoring of Plankton Size Spectra Via a Convolutional Neural Network
reason: Primary study that builds an in situ underwater imaging system and a CNN to segment and count free-living plankton in a pool and a river. title: Development of an Efficient Coral-Coverage Estimation Method Using a Towed Optical Camera Array System [Speedy Sea Scanner (SSS)] and Deep-Learning-Based Segmentation: A Sea Trial at the Kujuku-Shima Islands
reason: Applies deep-learning segmentation and SfM reconstruction to underwater imagery of wild corals (animals) in a natural reef area offshore Kujuku-Shima, Japan.

title: Three-Dimensional Localization of Bats: Visual and Acoustical

title: Dynamic Behavioral Analysis of Stimulus Response of Running Ants by High-Speed Robotic Platform
venue: International Symposium on Micro-NanoMechatronics and Human Science
reason: Single ants are tracked and stimulated on a laboratory robotic platform (XY stage, inkjet, water-trench enclosure); no images of wild, free-ranging animals in their habitat.

venue: IEEE International Workshop on Multimedia Signal Processing (MMSP)

reason: Hardware and system design paper for a mangrove forest robot. title: Marine Bird Detection Based on Deep Learning using High-Resolution Aerial Images
reason: Proposes a CNN-based sliding-window method to detect wild marine birds in aerial images of the sea.

title: Towards Developing Visual Statistical Cues for Biodiversity, Abundance, Biomass around Mariana Trench in an Embeddable Smart Module
reason: Applies a deep-learning detector and segmentation to ROV images of wild deep-sea animals around hydrothermal vents in the Mariana Trench, to estimate biodiversity, abundance and biomass.

title: BIIGLE2Go—A scalable image annotation system for easy deployment on cruises
reason: Software architecture paper for a manual image annotation tool (BIIGLE2Go on Raspberry Pi); evaluation is server response time, no computer vision analysis of animal images.

title: Design Structure of SYMBIOSIS: An Opto-Acoustic System for Monitoring Pelagic Fish
reason: The paper describes the mechanical and hardware design of a planned opto-acoustic monitoring system for pelagic fish. No images are analysed and no computer vision experiments are reported.

title: Research on marine creature recognition from seafloor videos

title: In situ real-time Zooplankton Detection and Classification

title: Quantification of Aggregation and Associated Brain Areas in Drosophila Melanogaster

reason: Laboratory study of Drosophila melanogaster tracked in an experimental arena to quantify aggregation and relate it to brain areas; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Coral Reef Management in Persian Gulf Using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
reason: Primary study applying a CNN to images of wild corals (animals) from Persian Gulf reefs to classify healthy versus diseased corals.

title: Dynamic Bird Detection Using Image Processing and Neural Network
reason: Proposes a CNN-based method with background subtraction to detect free-flying birds in video, aimed at preventing bird strikes.

title: Underwater Fish Classification of Trout and Grayling

reason: Applies CNN transfer learning to classify wild brown trout and grayling in underwater videos recorded by a sensor-triggered camera.

title: Underwater Fish Species Recognition Using Deep Learning Techniques
venue: International Conference on Signal Processing and Integrated Networks (SPIN)

title: On Confidences and Their Use in (Semi-)Automatic Multi-Image Taxa Identification

reason: Images show preserved benthic macroinvertebrate specimens photographed in an alcohol-filled cuvette with a laboratory imaging device; no images of wild, free-ranging animals.

reason: Generic underwater image/object classification with classes aquatic fern, background, diver, diver with rock, rock, rope and tyre; no animals appear in the data and wildlife is not the stated subject.

title: Half a Percent of Labels is Enough: Efficient Animal Detection in UAV Imagery Using Deep CNNs and Active Learning

reason: Proposes an active learning strategy for CNN-based detection of large mammals in UAV images of a wildlife reserve in Namibia.

title: Walsh–Hadamard-Kernel-Based Features in Particle Filter Framework for Underwater Object Tracking
reason: Proposes a classical computer vision tracking method evaluated on underwater videos of free-swimming fish and a turtle from public underwater datasets.

title: SpaRTA Tracking Across Occlusions via Partitioning of 3D Clouds of Points
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
reason: Proposes a 3D multi-object tracking method and evaluates it on multicamera video of wild bat colonies emerging from a natural cave.

title: Deep Learning for Inexpensive Image Classification of Wildlife on the Raspberry Pi
venue: IEEE Annual Ubiquitous Computing, Electronics & Mobile Communication Conference (UEMCON)
reason: Snow leopard classifier trained and tested on ImageNet pictures that the paper says are mostly from zoos or enclosures; no field data of wild animals was analysed (live test used print-outs of the same images).

title: Benthos Sampling by Autonomous Underwater Vehicle Equipped a Manipulator with Suction Device
reason: An AUV uses image processing (saliency-map detection and template matching) on seafloor images to find and sample benthos (shells) in Sagami Bay. This is applied computer vision on wild marine animals.

title: The Effect of Physics-Based Corrections and Data Augmentation on Transfer Learning for Segmentation of Benthic Imagery
reason: Applies DeepLabV3 semantic segmentation to AUV seafloor survey images containing wild benthic animals (crabs, whelks, shrimp, sponges, fish).

title: Low-Shot Learning From Imaginary 3D Model
venue: IEEE Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision
reason: General low-shot learning method (3D-model-based image hallucination with self-paced selection); birds appear only as classes of the fine-grained CUB-200-2011 benchmark and wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Measuring phenotypes in fluctuating environments
reason: Laboratory experiment on a clonal Daphnia magna culture; video tracking in a thermostatic well-plate is used only to measure time to immobilization. No images of wild, free-ranging animals.

title: Using unmanned aerial vehicles with thermal‐image acquisition cameras for animal surveys: a case study on the Sichuan snub‐nosed monkey in the Qinling Mountains
reason: UAV thermal video survey of wild Sichuan snub-nosed monkeys; animals appear as bright dots that are counted by the researchers. No computer vision or automated image analysis method is described.

title: A comparison of deep learning and citizen science techniques for counting wildlife in aerial survey images
reason: Primary study applying a YOLOv3 detector (compared with citizen-science counts) to aerial survey photographs of free-ranging wildebeest in the Serengeti.

title: Tracktor: Image‐based automated tracking of animal movement and behaviour
reason: Tracking software tested on videos of animals (fish, spiders, termites, tadpoles, mice) in experimental laboratory arenas; no wild, free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: pavo 2: New tools for the spectral and spatial analysis of colour in r
reason: Software paper (R package pavo 2) whose worked example analyses images of a 1916 colour plate of Heliconius butterfly specimens rather than images of wild, free-ranging animals; the image data are specimen-based only.

title: A field and video analysis guide for diver operated stereo‐video
reason: Practical field guide for diver-operated stereo-video fish surveys; videos are annotated manually (identification, counting, measurement in EventMeasure) and no data or automated image analysis is presented.

title: Monitoring large and complex wildlife aggregations with drones
reason: Primary study developing a semi-automated machine learning approach to map and count nests of wild breeding waterbird colonies in drone imagery.

title: pathtrackr : An r package for video tracking and analysing animal movement

title: Drones and convolutional neural networks facilitate automated and accurate cetacean species identification and photogrammetry
reason: Primary study applying a CNN (Mask R-CNN) to drone imagery of free-ranging whales for species identification and length measurement.

title: Improving the precision and accuracy of animal population estimates with aerial image object detection
reason: Evaluates a CNN object detector (RetinaNet) on aerial survey images of free-ranging elephants, giraffes and zebras in Kenyan savanna reserves; cattle also appear in the images but are treated as background.

title: M ist N et : Measuring historical bird migration in the US using archived weather radar data and convolutional neural networks
reason: Develops a CNN (MistNet) that segments weather radar images to separate biology (migrating wild birds) from precipitation; radar imagery is image data and wild birds are the subject.

title: CORIGAN: Assessing multiple species and interactions within images
reason: Object detection pipeline (YOLOv3-based) applied to field images of free-ranging invertebrate communities (ants, cockroaches, spiders, slugs) visiting sentinel prey in a tropical agrosystem; the focus is the predator community and its interactions, not pest control in production.

title: Using machine vision to estimate fish length from images using regional convolutional neural networks
reason: Develops an R-CNN based method to detect and estimate total length of wild-caught European sea bass from images taken by fishers on shore and afloat; animals are wild fish captured in recreational and commercial fishing.

title: Estimating body mass of free‐living whales using aerial photogrammetry and 3D volumetrics
reason: Primary study using UAV aerial photogrammetry (image-based measurement) of free-living southern right whales to estimate body volume and mass.

title: Quantitative Colour Pattern Analysis (QCPA): A comprehensive framework for the analysis of colour patterns in nature
reason: Methods framework for colour pattern analysis. The only images actually analysed are flowers (a daisy, a flower meadow). Animals appear only as modelled viewers (bee, blue tit), not as the subjects of the images.

title: Thinking like a naturalist: Enhancing computer vision of citizen science images by harnessing contextual data
reason: Primary study building CNN and multi-input neural network models to classify citizen-science images of wild ladybirds to species level using images plus contextual metadata.

title: Using digitized museum collections to understand the effects of habitat on wing coloration in the Puerto Rican monarch
reason: Image analysis (ImageJ thresholding) of wing melanization on digitized pinned museum specimens of the Puerto Rican monarch; no images of live free-ranging animals.

title: Cold‐water coral assemblages on vertical walls from the Northeast Atlantic

reason: Proposes a CNN plus particle filter method to detect and track free-ranging (provisioned) Japanese macaques in outdoor video recordings.

title: Lateral position preference in grazing feral horses

title: Manual fish length measurement accuracy for adult river fish using an acoustic camera (DIDSON)
reason: Fish lengths were measured manually by human operators on DIDSON acoustic-camera (imaging sonar) frames of fish in an experimental tank; no computer vision method is developed or evaluated, and the animals are not free-ranging.

title: Recognition software successfully aids the identification of individual small‐spotted catsharks Scyliorhinus canicula during their first year of life
reason: Photo-identification with I3S software applied only to 18 captive-bred catsharks held in laboratory tanks; no wild or free-ranging animals in the analysed data.

title: Computer‐aided photo‐identification of a rare stingray, Megatrygon microps
reason: Primary study applying I3S computer-aided photo-matching software to underwater photographs of wild, free-ranging smalleye stingrays to identify individuals.

title: Risk balancing through selective use of social and physical information: a case study in the humbug damselfish
reason: Wild damselfish behaviour was scored by eye from video. The only computer vision is photogrammetric 3D reconstruction of coral habitat, so the image analysis targets habitat, not animals.

title: Estimating day range from camera‐trap data: the animals’ behaviour as a key parameter
reason: Camera-trap photos and videos of wild boar are used to estimate day range from speed and activity, but animal positions and behaviours are derived manually with reference markers and statistical models; no computer vision or automated image analysis is applied.

title: “Nose-metrics” of wild southern elephant seal (Mirounga leonina) males using image analysis and geometric morphometrics
venue: Journal of Zoological Systematics & Evolutionary Research
reason: Applies image-based 2D photogrammetry and geometric morphometrics to field photographs of wild, non-sedated southern elephant seal males to measure proboscis size and shape.

title: Temporal variations in terrestrial counts of Pacific harbor seals in the southern California Current System
reason: Wild harbor seals were counted directly by human observers with binoculars and spotting scopes, and the counts were modelled with GAMs. No images or video were analysed.

title: Unoccupied aerial system assessment of entanglement in Northwest Atlantic gray seals ( Halichoerus grypus )
reason: UAS images of wild gray seals were analysed only by manual stitching, manual counting (ImageJ cell counter) and visual inspection; no computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Occurrence of Bryde's whales, Balaenoptera edeni , in the northern Beibu Gulf, China
reason: Occurrence study based on fishermen records, questionnaires and field sightings; drone photographs were only inspected visually to confirm species. No computer vision method was applied.

title: Feeding of humpback whales ( Megaptera novaeangliae ) on the Pacific coast of Nicaragua
reason: Short field note on humpback whale feeding behaviour from boat-based observations. Photos were taken for standard manual photo-identification, but no computer vision or automated image analysis is developed or applied.

title: Evaluating the power of photogrammetry for monitoring killer whale body condition
reason: Measures body condition of free-ranging Southern Resident killer whales from UAV images using photogrammetry.

title: Underwater 3D Recording and Modelling
reason: This is a page of conference announcements from The Photogrammetric Record. It has no primary research, no image analysis and no animal subjects.

title: A Robust Visual Tracking Method for Unmanned Mobile Systems
venue: Journal of Dynamic Systems Measurement and Control
reason: Visual tracking method for unmanned mobile systems, tested on a remote-control submarine and a robotic fish in a laboratory water tank; no live or wild animals are analysed.

title: Underwater and airborne monitoring of marine ecosystems and debris
reason: Primary study applying YOLO v3 object detection to underwater images of sea life (fish, sea turtles, jellyfish), including video taken by scuba diving of free-ranging fish, alongside marine debris detection.

title: Establishing the baseline for using plankton as biosensor
reason: Analyses microscopic plankton images from submersible imaging-in-flow cytometry (microscopy of microorganisms, mostly protists/phytoplankton), not images of wild animals in the usual sense; falls under microscopy exclusion.

title: Intra- versus intergroup variance in collective behavior
reason: Laboratory study of colony-reared desert locust nymphs tracked with barcode tags in an indoor arena; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Chimpanzee face recognition from videos in the wild using deep learning
reason: Deep CNN pipeline for face detection, tracking and individual recognition of wild chimpanzees in field video from Bossou, Guinea.

title: Deep learning on butterfly phenotypes tests evolution’s oldest mathematical model
reason: Deep learning applied to photographs of museum butterfly specimens from the NHM London collection; no images of live free-ranging animals.

title: Range of motion in the avian wing is strongly associated with flight behavior and body mass
reason: Comparative morphology study; video digitization of wings from bird cadavers (museum/rehabilitation specimens) plus in vivo flight of captive pigeon and zebra finches in a lab arena; no wild free-ranging animals imaged.

title: Taxonomic Revisions and Specimen Databases in the Internet Age: Dealing with a Species Rich Insect Taxon
reason: The paper describes a relational specimen database (Arthropod Easy Capture) of museum plant bug specimens and analyses their distribution and host-plant records. It does no image analysis or computer vision.

title: Comparison of sampling precision for nearshore marine wildlife using unmanned and manned aerial surveys
reason: Compares human observer counts from a helicopter, a drone pilot in real time, and manual post-hoc review of drone video; no computer vision or automated image analysis is applied.

title: Successful observation of orangutans in the wild with thermal-equipped drones

title: Evaluating UAV-based techniques to census an urban-nesting gull population on Canada’s Pacific coast
reason: Wild rooftop-nesting gulls were surveyed with UAV imagery, but the nests were counted manually by human observers on orthomosaics. No automated computer vision analysis of the animals was done.

title: Designing a Raspberry Pi sensor network for remote observation of wildlife

reason: Compares CNNs and capsule networks for species classification on Serengeti camera-trap images of wild animals.

title: An Application of Image Classification to Saltwater Fish Identification in Louisiana Fisheries
venue: International Conference on Information System and Data Mining (ICISDM)
reason: Applies CNN image classification to web images of wild saltwater fish species (mostly angler catches) for fisheries management.

title: Identification of Various Osteichthyes Class of Fishes Through Gaussian Mixture Model, Kalman Filter, Pyramid Histogram of Visual Words and Support Vector Machine
venue: International Conference on Biomedical Engineering and Technology (ICBET)
reason: Computer vision pipeline (GMM, Kalman filter, PHOW, SVM) for detecting, tracking and identifying freshwater fish in underwater video; data come from an aquarium with purchased fish (controlled testing) and from a deployment in a natural creek (uncontrolled testing).

reason: Generic fine-grained classification method evaluated on CUB-200-2011 birds and Stanford Cars benchmarks; wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Automated Deep Learning Analysis of Purple Martin Videos Depicting Incubation and Provisioning

reason: CNN classification of nest-box video frames of free-ranging purple martins breeding at a wildlife refuge; primary research.

title: Eyes in the Sky: Assessing the Feasibility of Low-Cost, Ready-to-Use Unmanned Aerial Vehicles to Monitor Primate Populations Directly
reason: This is a feasibility study of using low-cost UAVs to photograph and observe wild sifakas. In the pages provided, the imagery is collected and looked at by people. No computer vision or automated image analysis method is described.

title: Robust features extraction for general fish classification
venue: International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering (IJECE)
reason: Computer vision classification of fish images (specimens, out-of-water and in-situ images of wild fish taxa) from FishBase into dangerous/non-dangerous families.

title: Comparison among three body parts and three software packages to optimise photographic identification of a reptile (tuatara, Sphenodon punctatus)
reason: Primary study evaluating photo-identification software (computer vision pattern matching) on photographs of tuatara, including both captive and free-roaming individuals.

title: Mapping out bare-nosed wombat (Vombatus ursinus) burrows with the use of a drone
reason: Drone images of wild wombat burrows were turned into orthomosaics, but an analyst found the burrows by eye in ArcMap. No computer vision method was applied to detect or analyse the animals or their signs.

title: Where to spot: individual identification of leopard cats (Prionailurus bengalensis euptilurus) in South Korea
reason: Applies the HotSpotter image-matching algorithm to identify individual leopard cats from camera-trap images of wild individuals and DSLR images of captive individuals in rescue centers.

title: Magnetic body alignment in migratory songbirds: A computer vision approach
reason: Wild-caught songbirds were filmed only inside indoor experimental houses in a controlled laboratory set-up. No free-ranging animals were imaged.

title: Scaling of swimming performance in baleen whales
reason: Biomechanics study of wild baleen whales based on inertial tag data and hydrodynamic modelling. Drone images were only measured by hand in ImageJ (manual photogrammetry); no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Research of Improved Fine-Grained Image Classification Based on Saliency
reason: Generic fine-grained image classification method evaluated on benchmark datasets CUB-200-2011 (birds), Stanford Dogs and Cars; wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Ecosystem Controlling Using Identification of Animal Based on Deep Learning and GLCM (Gray Level Co-occurrence Matrix) Method
venue: Universal Journal of Electrical and Electronic Engineering
reason: Primary study applying GLCM texture features and a neural network to camera images to identify animals (wildlife entering plantations). The paper does not describe where the analysed animal images come from, so wild status of the data is not stated.

title: Enhancing underwater optical imaging by using a low-pass polarization filter
reason: Underwater image dehazing method tested on letter targets and markers in water tanks and at sea; no animals are analysed.

title: Field demonstration of a wing-beat modulation lidar for the 3D mapping of flying insects
reason: Lidar instrument paper; insect wing-beat signals in single-beam time-range lidar returns, identified manually by a human user through DFT inspection. No computer vision analysis of image/video data.

title: Remote reefs and seamounts are the last refuges for marine predators across the Indo-Pacific
reason: Ecological survey of wild marine predators with baited underwater video; the footage was analysed by human technicians and the modelling (boosted regression trees) uses environmental and human-pressure variables, not images. No computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Development of a behavioural welfare assessment tool for routine use with captive elephants
reason: Develops a behavioural welfare assessment tool for zoo elephants; video footage is scored manually by humans with an ethogram, with no computer vision analysis. Animals are also captive only.

title: Benefits of zebra stripes: Behaviour of tabanid flies around zebras and horses
reason: Behavioural study of wild tabanid flies around captive zebras and domestic horses; fly trajectories were digitized manually from video and behaviours scored by human observers. No automated computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Measurement of time-varying kinematics of a dolphin in burst accelerating swimming
reason: The analysed video shows one captive dolphin in an aquarium tank, plus a 3-D scan of a museum specimen. No wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

reason: Animal-borne video loggers on wild humpback whales; video frames analysed with image processing (filtering, Find maxima, particle analysis) to count krill and estimate relative prey density, and footage inspected for other whales.

title: Aerial-trained deep learning networks for surveying cetaceans from satellite imagery
reason: Primary study training CNNs on aerial survey imagery of wild minke whales and testing on WorldView-3 satellite imagery of wild southern right and humpback whales.

title: A mark–recapture approach for estimating population size of the endangered ringed seal (Phoca hispida saimensis)
reason: Photo-identification of wild Saimaa ringed seals was done manually by human observers and followed by statistical mark-recapture modelling; no computer vision method is applied to the images.

title: Quantifying the effect of Jacobiasca lybica pest on vineyards with UAVs by combining geometric and computer vision techniques
reason: UAV RGB imagery of a commercial vineyard is used to segment vegetation damaged by a crop pest (the leafhopper Jacobiasca lybica) in production; the images show vegetation and soil only, no animals.

title: Characterizing the benthic community in Maryland’s offshore wind energy areas using a towed camera sled: Developing a method to reduce the effort of image analysis and community description
reason: Wild benthic organisms imaged with a towed camera sled, but all images were annotated manually; the method is a frame-subsampling strategy for manual annotation with no automated image analysis.

title: The challenges of recognising individuals with few distinguishing features: Identifying red foxes Vulpes vulpes from camera-trap photos
reason: Camera-trap photos of wild urban red foxes were identified to individual entirely manually by one human observer; no computer vision or automated image analysis method was developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Using virtual reality and thermal imagery to improve statistical modelling of vulnerable and protected species
