title: On the impact of Citizen Science-derived data quality on deep learning based classification in marine images
reason: Primary study that trains a deep learning classifier on AUV seabed images of wild deep-sea megafauna and tests how simulated citizen-science annotation errors affect classification accuracy.

title: A framework for the development of a global standardised marine taxon reference image database (SMarTaR-ID) to support image-based analyses
reason: The paper proposes a database structure and a management framework for morphospecies reference image catalogues of deep-sea fauna. It develops, applies and evaluates no computer vision or image analysis method.

title: Enhanced convolutional neural network for plankton identification and enumeration
reason: CNN+SVM classification of in situ zooplankton images taken by an underwater imaging system deployed in the Bering Sea; wild free-ranging animals, primary research.

title: Drone-based effective counting and ageing of hippopotamus (Hippopotamus amphibius) in the Okavango Delta in Botswana
reason: Wild hippos are filmed by drone, but the videos are counted by eye and the hippos are measured by hand in ImageJ. The paper uses no computer vision method.

title: Low-cost solution for rodent home-cage behaviour monitoring
reason: Video monitoring of laboratory C57BL/6 mice in home-cages for sleep/wake scoring; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Detection of two Arctic birds in Greenland and an endangered bird in Korea using RGB and thermal cameras with an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)
reason: UAV RGB and thermal images of free-living wild birds are analysed with temperature-contour thresholding to delineate, detect and count birds. Borderline: much of the identification is visual interpretation by researchers, and the paper itself says it lacks automated image processing.

title: Using remote sensing to detect whale strandings in remote areas: The case of sei whales mass mortality in Chilean Patagonia
reason: Primary study testing manual and automated (Spectral Angle Mapper) detection and counting of stranded wild sei whale carcasses in very high resolution satellite imagery.

title: Identifying genetic lineages through shape: An example in a cosmopolitan marine turtle species using geometric morphometrics
reason: Wild green turtles were photographed, but landmarks were digitized by hand in TPS Dig and only statistical shape analysis (Procrustes, PCA, CVA) followed. There is no automated computer vision analysis of the images.

title: Establishing an infrastructure for collaboration in primate cognition research
reason: Behavioural cognition study (delayed-response task) on captive primates at zoos, sanctuaries and research centres. The sessions were videotaped only so that humans could score them by hand. No computer vision or automated image analysis was done.

title: MARGO (Massively Automated Real-time GUI for Object-tracking), a platform for high-throughput ethology
reason: Real-time tracking software developed and tested on laboratory model organisms (fruit flies, C. elegans, larval zebrafish, bumblebees in an artificial nestbox) in laboratory behavioural arenas; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Using Video to Evaluate Depth and Velocity Selection by Arctic Grayling (Thymallus arcticus) in Pools of an Engineered Tundra Stream
reason: Wild-caught adult Arctic grayling released into a field tundra stream; their positions were taken from overhead GoPro video using OpenCV lens calibration and a re-projected sampling grid, with fish marked by hand in the frames.

title: The Effect of Background on A Deep Learning Model in Identifying Images of Butterfly Species
venue: Electrical and Electronics Engineering An International Journal
reason: Classification of butterfly family from scanned images of specimens in a monograph; the test photos from a Taiwanese website are not described as showing wild animals.

title: In situ growth of deep-sea octocorals after the Deepwater Horizon oil spill
reason: Supplementary material with statistical tables on coral growth (Paramuricea biscaya); no computer vision method on image data is described, only statistical models of growth measurements.

title: The intriguing co-distribution of the copepods Calanus hyperboreus and Calanus glacialis in the subsurface chlorophyll maximum of Arctic seas
reason: Applies an in situ underwater imaging profiler and a machine-learning image classifier to wild Arctic copepods to study their fine-scale vertical distribution.

title: Interneurons Regulate Locomotion Quiescence via Cyclic Adenosine Monophosphate Signaling During Stress-Induced Sleep in Caenorhabditis elegans
reason: Laboratory genetics study of sleep in C. elegans strains kept on agar plates; imaging is automated quiescence quantification in microchips and fluorescence microscopy, with no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Study on spatial distribution of coral reefs in Nam Yet island by using GIS and remote sensing techniques
venue: Vietnam Journal of Marine Science and Technology
reason: Satellite-based benthic habitat mapping of coral reef zones (live, poorly developed, dead coral, sand) around Nam Yet island; the output is a habitat distribution map, not analysis of individual animals.

title: Invasive wild boars and native mammals in agroecosystems in the Atlantic Forest of Western Brazil
reason: Camera-trap ecology study (relative biomass index, occupancy modelling, activity overlap). Species in the photos were identified without any computer vision or automated image analysis.

title: Application of camera trapping to species inventory and assessment of wild animals across China’s protected areas
reason: Editor's note introducing a special issue on camera-trap data analysis in Chinese protected areas; it reports no primary research and no computer vision analysis of images.

title: Fotokapan Görüntülerinde Yerel Öznitelikler ile Nesne Tespiti
venue: Gümüşhane Üniversitesi Fen Bilimleri Enstitüsü Dergisi
reason: Primary study applying local-feature matching (SIFT, SURF, BRIEF, ORB) for object detection on camera-trap images of wild animals from the Kays et al. dataset.

title: Foto-kapan Görüntülerinde Hareketli Nesne Tespiti ve Konumunun Belirlenmesi
venue: Erzincan Üniversitesi Fen Bilimleri Enstitüsü Dergisi
reason: Classical image-processing method for detecting and localising moving objects (animals, humans) in camera-trap image sequences recorded in the natural environment.

title: Neural Naturalist: Generating Fine-Grained Image Comparisons
reason: Introduces a dataset and model for generating natural-language comparisons of iNaturalist photographs of wild birds; computer vision on images of wild animals.

title: Implementing portable touchscreen-setups to enhance cognitive research and enrich zoo-housed animals
reason: Describes a portable touchscreen system for cognitive testing of zoo-housed great apes. The webcam only films the animals and no image analysis is done; the data are touch records. The animals are also captive only.

title: Appearance pattern of sika deer (Cervus nippon) in Japanese cedar (Cryptomeria japonica) plantations using time-lapse camera
reason: Time-lapse camera trap survey of wild sika deer in which photos were inspected and recorded by hand; no computer vision or automated image analysis is applied. Deep learning is only mentioned as a future possibility.

title: Zooglider-Based Measurements of Planktonic Foraminifera in the California Current System
reason: In situ underwater shadowgraph images of free-living planktonic foraminifera, taken by an autonomous glider, with automated ROI detection and CNN classification before morphometric analysis.

title: Usability and Feasibility of a Smartphone App to Assess Human Behavioral Factors Associated with Tick Exposure (The Tick App): Quantitative and Qualitative Study
reason: Supplementary appendix describing the design and focus-group testing of a mobile survey app on tick exposure; users can submit tick pictures, but no computer vision or image analysis is performed.

title: Otomasi Kamera Perangkap Menggunakan Deteksi Gerak dan Komputer Papan Tunggal
venue: IJEIS (Indonesian Journal of Electronics and Instrumentation Systems)
reason: Self-built camera trap with MOG motion detection, framed as wildlife monitoring, but the only animal the paper identifies in its test videos is a domestic cat; no wild or free-ranging animals are stated in the analysed data.

title: Automatically Counting and Identifying Breeds of Different Animals using Neural Networks
venue: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
reason: Proposed CNN system identifies breeds of animals (breeds imply domestic animals) and counts them; no wild or free-ranging animals stated in the analysed data, and the dataset is described only as a publicly available animals' dataset.

title: A Robust Image Enhancement Techniques for Underwater Fish Classification in Marine Environment
venue: International journal of intelligent engineering and systems
reason: Primary study proposing an image-enhancement plus texture-feature and neural-network workflow to classify fish species in underwater images from the marine environment (Fish4Knowledge / LifeCLEF 2014).

title: Bird species identification using neural networks: Empowering bird watching with technological precision
reason: Primary study applying CNN transfer learning (VGG16, VGG19) to classify bird species from images, with stated conservation and birdwatching application; the paper does not say whether the birds pictured are wild or captive.

title: A Validation Tool For Improving Semantic Segmentation of Complex Natural Structures
reason: Semantic segmentation of wild soft corals in an orthomosaic of a Mozambique coral reef, with an interactive tool for validating the CNN's output.

title: Laser quadrat and photogrammetry based autonomous coral reef mapping ocean robot
venue: Is and T International Symposium on Electronic Imaging Science and Technology
reason: Primary study that builds a surface robot and applies image stitching, colour thresholding and 3D reconstruction to images of wild coral reefs to estimate live coral cover and bleaching; corals are animals in their natural marine habitat.

title: Fishery monitoring system with AUV based on YOLO and SGBM
reason: The paper presents a fishery (fish-farming) monitoring system that estimates fish growth by size from stereo images; the application is fishery/aquaculture growth monitoring, not wild free-ranging animals, and the paper does not describe the fish as wild.

title: An Image-based Sea Turtle Identification using Postorbital Facial Feature Points Matching Technique
venue: International Conference on Control, Automation and Systems (ICCAS)
reason: Proposes an image-based photo-identification method that recognises individual sea turtles from their postorbital facial scale patterns, framed as wildlife identification. The paper does not say where the images came from or how they were taken; treating the turtles as wild is an assumption based on that framing.

title: Data Augmentation Method for Object Detection in Underwater Environments
venue: International Conference on Control, Automation and Systems (ICCAS)
reason: Underwater object detection of tools (pipe, hammer, wrench) for robot manipulation; no animals are analysed.

title: Structuring the information resources for intelligent ecosystem monitoring system based on camera traps
venue: International Convention on Information and Communication Technology, Electronics and Microelectronics
reason: Primary study that applies image-processing and neural-network methods to camera-trap images of wild animals from protected natural territories in the Krasnoyarsk region and stores the results in a data warehouse.

title: GAN-based Color Correction for Underwater Object Detection
reason: Underwater object detection of sea cucumber, sea urchin and scallop is presented as part of a smart aquaculture support system using an ROV. The paper never says the animals are wild or free-ranging.

title: Weakly supervised learning of point-level annotation for coral image segmentation
reason: Proposes a weakly supervised CNN+LDA segmentation method for images of wild corals (animals) taken at Pulley Ridge in the Gulf of Mexico.

title: Action Learning for Coral Detection and Species Classification
reason: Proposes a CV (YOLOv3 coral detection and species classification) plus RL framework for AUV monitoring of coral reef habitats; evaluated on simulated ocean-floor coral scenes, no real-image data.

title: Algorithmic Design and Implementation of Unobtrusive Multistatic Serial LiDAR Image
reason: Develops LiDAR image detection and classification algorithms for monitoring marine animals near MHK turbines; field data include natural harbor seals and fishes.

title: Automated Analysis of Underwater Imagery: Accomplishments, Products, and Vision
reason: Technical report on the NOAA Automated Image Analysis initiative. It reports original CV results on wild marine animals: CamTrawl fish classification and length estimation, HabCam skate detection and coral cover estimation with CoralNet.

title: Processing Photomosaic Imagery of Coral Reefs Using Structure-from-Motion Standard Operating Procedures
reason: Describes and tests a Structure-from-Motion photogrammetry pipeline (3-D point clouds and orthophotos) built from diver-collected underwater imagery of wild coral reefs, used to extract coral colony demographic data.

title: Monitoring the Behavior and Habitat Use of Animals to Enhance Welfare using the ZooMonitor App
reason: Presents a manual behavioural-recording app (ZooMonitor) used by human observers at a zoo; no computer vision or image analysis is done. The animals are zoo pygmy hippos and domestic chickens.

title: A biometric for shark dorsal fins based on boundary descriptor matching
reason: Primary study proposing a contour-based computer vision metric to identify individual sharks from dorsal fin images, framed as wildlife research. The paper does not state where the two shark images come from, so wild origin is assumed from the framing rather than stated; no exclusion criterion applies.

title: Harmonization of the use of hunting statistics for wild boar density estimation in different study areas
reason: Camera-trap images of wild boar are reviewed and measured manually to feed a random encounter model; no computer vision or automated image analysis method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Transfer learning using VGG-16 with Deep Convolutional Neural Network for Classifying Images
venue: International Journal of Scientific and Research Publications
reason: The paper classifies images of domestic dogs and cats (pets) with transfer learning. No wild animals are analysed.

title: Estimating sightability of greater sage-grouse at leks using an aerial infrared system and N-mixture models
reason: Aerial infrared imagery is used, but birds are counted by human observers and analysed with Bayesian/N-mixture sightability models. The paper describes no computer vision or automated image analysis method.

title: A protocol for using drones to assist monitoring of large breeding bird colonies
reason: Protocol paper on drone surveys of wild waterbird colonies; imagery is only mosaicked with photogrammetry software and nests are counted manually, with no automated computer vision analysis.

title: Photo-identification of horseshoe whip snakes (Hemorrhois hippocrepis, Linnaeus, 1758) by a semi-automatic procedure applied to wildlife management
reason: Semi-automatic photo-matching software (APHIS, I3S procedure) is applied to head photographs of wild, trapped-and-released invasive snakes for individual identification in a capture-mark-recapture study.

title: Monitoring amphibian species with complex chromatophore patterns: a non-invasive approach with an evaluation of software effectiveness and reliability
reason: Evaluates photo-identification software (computer vision pattern matching) on field photographs of wild cave salamanders captured in a natural population.

title: In-water methods reveal population dynamics of a green turtle Chelonia mydas foraging aggregation in the Philippines
reason: Applies image-based photo-identification (I3S pattern-recognition software) and photogrammetric measurement to underwater images of wild green turtles.

title: Decadal changes in adult size of salmon-eating killer whales in the eastern North Pacific
reason: Applies aerial (drone) image photogrammetry to measure body length of free-ranging northern resident killer whales; individuals identified from images.

title: Using small drones to photo-identify Antillean manatees: a novel method for monitoring an endangered marine mammal in the Caribbean Sea
reason: Wild Antillean manatees were filmed by drone, but observers reviewed the videos and identified individuals by hand. No computer vision or automated image analysis method is developed or applied.

title: Physical and ecological factors explain the distribution of Ross Sea Weddell seals during the breeding season
reason: Wild Weddell seals were identified by eye: citizen volunteers and an expert tagged them on satellite images. No automated image analysis is used; the analysis is a logistic regression habitat model.

title: Automated identification of benthic epifauna with computer vision
reason: Primary study training a CNN classifier (Inception V3, transfer learning) to identify wild deep-sea benthic epifauna in seafloor images collected by an AUV.

title: Validation of the photogrammetric method to assess body condition of an odontocete, the shortfinned pilot whale Globicephala macrorhynchus
reason: Photogrammetric body-condition validation study on short-finned pilot whales held in aquaria (SeaWorld); no free-ranging animals imaged.

title: Behavioural development in southern right whale calves
reason: UAV video of wild southern right whales was coded by hand for behaviour in Solomon Coder, and body length came from manual photogrammetric pixel measurements. No computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Detailed Mapping of Hydrothermal Vent Fauna: A 3D Reconstruction Approach Based on Video Imagery
reason: Applies Structure from Motion 3D reconstruction to ROV video of wild deep-sea hydrothermal vent fauna to quantify abundances and map faunal assemblages.

title: Distribution of Deep-Sea Sponge Aggregations in an Area of Multisectoral Activities and Changing Oceanic Conditions
reason: Ecological study of deep-sea sponges based on manual annotation and counting of morphotypes in towed-camera frames. No computer vision method is applied to the animals; image processing is used only for a seabed-visibility correction factor.

title: Contrasting Habitat Use and Population Dynamics of Reef Manta Rays Within the Nusa Penida Marine Protected Area, Indonesia
reason: Population ecology study of wild reef manta rays based on photo-identification. Photographs were matched manually by trained observers, with software only assisting. The paper neither develops nor evaluates a computer vision method; its analyses are statistical residency and movement models.

title: Leveraging Automated Image Analysis Tools to Transform Our Capacity to Assess Status and Trends of Coral Reefs
reason: Primary study evaluating an automated machine-learning image classifier (CoralNet) on in-situ benthic photographs of wild coral reefs (corals are animals) in Hawaii and American Samoa.

title: Using 3D Models to Improve Estimates of Marine Mammal Size and External Morphology
reason: A 3D mesh was built by hand in Blender over a few reference photographs and then scaled using tape-measure morphometrics from stranded whales. The paper applies no automated image analysis or computer vision method.

title: Doctor Drone: Non-invasive Measurement of Humpback Whale Vital Signs Using Unoccupied Aerial System Infrared Thermography
reason: Drone infrared thermography of free-ranging humpback whales, but the image analysis is manual measurement with FLIR Tools+ line tools and pixel-intensity extraction followed by spectral/wavelet time-series analysis; no computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Next-Generation Optical Sensing Technologies for Exploring Ocean Worlds—NASA FluidCam, MiDAR, and NeMO-Net
reason: Develops and applies optical imaging (fluid lensing, MiDAR) and a CNN (NeMO-Net) to map wild coral reefs, classifying mounding vs branching coral from UAV imagery in American Samoa; corals are wild animals.

title: The Effect of Melatonin on Locomotor Behavior and Muscle Physiology in the Sea Cucumber Apostichopus japonicus
reason: Laboratory physiology experiment: sea cucumbers obtained from a marine ranch were kept in aquariums, injected with melatonin, and their locomotion was video-tracked with commercial software. No wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Developing a Metric of Usable Space for Zoo Exhibits
reason: The paper develops a usable-space metric for zoo exhibits using tape-measure measurements and a hand-built 3D model. It does no image analysis or computer vision, and the only animals involved are captive zoo pygmy marmosets.

title: High-Tech and Tactile: Cognitive Enrichment for Zoo-Housed Gorillas
reason: Evaluation of a cognitive enrichment device for zoo-housed gorillas; video footage was coded manually by a human observer, no computer vision method is applied, and all animals are captive.

title: Selecting and Testing Environmental Enrichment in Lemurs
reason: Behavioural study of captive zoo lemurs using paired-choice food preference tests and manual scan sampling on handheld devices; no image or video analysis is done.

title: ClassifyMe: A Field-Scouting Software for the Identification of Wildlife in Camera Trap Images
reason: Software tool applying a YOLOv2 deep learning model to identify animal species in field camera trap images; the analysed classes include wild animals (fox, macropod, dingo) alongside domestic sheep.

title: The Visitor Effect on Zoo Animals: Implications and Opportunities for Zoo Animal Welfare
reason: Literature review of visitor effects on zoo animal behaviour and welfare; no computer vision or image analysis, and animals are captive zoo animals.

title: Exploratory Investigation of Infrared Thermography for Measuring Gorilla Emotional Responses to Interactions with Familiar Humans
reason: Infrared thermography of three captive-born zoo gorillas at the Detroit Zoo; no wild animals in the data. Analysis is manual ROI temperature measurement.

title: Using Thermal Imaging to Monitor Body Temperature of Koalas (Phascolarctos cinereus) in A Zoo Setting
reason: Thermal imaging of three captive-born koalas held only in Wildlife Sydney Zoo enclosures; no wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: A Novel Extraction Method for Wildlife Monitoring Images with Wireless Multimedia Sensor Networks (WMSNs)
reason: Proposes a foreground extraction (segmentation) method for images of wild animals captured by a field-deployed wireless sensor camera network in a nature reserve.

title: An Integrated Wildlife Recognition Model Based on Multi-Branch Aggregation and Squeeze-And-Excitation Network
reason: Proposes an SE-ResNeXt CNN for species recognition in camera-trap images of wild animals from a Chinese nature reserve and from Snapshot Serengeti.

title: Vision-Based Classification of Mosquito Species: Comparison of Conventional and Deep Learning Methods
reason: Mosquito specimens were photographed on a white background under controlled illuminance with an SLR camera and a smartphone; no images of wild, free-ranging animals in their habitat are analysed.

title: Recognize the Little Ones: UAS-Based In-Situ Fluorescent Tracer Detection
reason: Proof-of-principle experiment detecting fluorescent dye traces printed on paper sheets with a UAS; no animals or animal-produced signs appear in the analysed images.

title: A Rapid UAV Method for Assessing Body Condition in Fur Seals
reason: UAV orthomosaics of wild Australian fur seals are measured manually by two observers with a GIS ruler tool; structure-from-motion is used only to build the orthomosaic, and no automated image analysis of the animals is performed.

title: Applications of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles to Survey Mesocarnivores
reason: UAV thermal survey of wild mesocarnivores in which animals were found and identified by the pilot and by manual review of videos and photos; no computer vision method is applied.

title: Thermal Infrared Imaging from Drones Offers a Major Advance for Spider Monkey Surveys
reason: Thermal drone footage of wild spider monkeys was reviewed and counted manually by human observers; no computer vision or automated image analysis was applied.

title: Using Fixed-Wing UAV for Detecting and Mapping the Distribution and Abundance of Penguins on the South Shetlands Islands, Antarctica
reason: UAV survey of wild chinstrap penguin colonies, but the orthomosaics were screened and the penguins counted manually in QGIS; no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated on the animal images.

title: Extracting Interactions between Flying Bat Pairs Using Model-Free Methods
reason: Wild bats leaving a cave were filmed with infrared and thermal multi-camera setups. 3D trajectories were extracted from the video and then analysed for pairwise interactions.

title: A Population Census of Large Herbivores Based on UAV and Its Effects on Grazing Pressure in the Yellow-River-Source National Park, China
venue: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
reason: UAV images of wild kiangs and Tibetan gazelles plus livestock were counted by manual human-computer interaction interpretation in GIS software. No computer vision method was applied, and the authors list automatic recognition only as future work.

title: An improved mobile mapping system to detect road-killed amphibians and small birds
venue: ISPRS International Journal of Geo Information
reason: Primary study that develops a vehicle-mounted camera system with a CNN to detect road-killed wild amphibians and small birds on roads; real surveys on national roads plus controlled trials with dead specimens.

title: Comparative Quantification of Trail-Following Behavior in Pest Ants
reason: Laboratory behavioural study of pest ants; videos were inspected manually and paths were traced by hand onto graph paper. No computer vision method is used. The set-up is also a laboratory one (E-LAB).

title: A Contrast-Guided Approach for the Enhancement of Low-Lighting Underwater Images
reason: Generic low-light underwater image enhancement (dehazing) method. Marine animals appear in some seafloor images alongside artificial objects, but wildlife is not the stated subject and no animal-specific analysis is done.

title: Towards Image Classification with Machine Learning Methodologies for Smartphones
reason: Applies image classification (ML/DL) to butterfly species from web images, with app testing on smartphone photos of butterflies in a conservatory; non-domestic animals are the subject.

title: Shallow-Water Habitat Mapping using Underwater Hyperspectral Imaging from an Unmanned Surface Vehicle: A Pilot Study
reason: Benthic habitat mapping study: pixel classes are mostly algae, seafloor and reference plates. Invertebrates (mostly Metridium senile) are only one coarse class, so the subject is habitat or land cover, not animals.

title: DisCountNet: Discriminating and Counting Network for Real-Time Counting and Localization of Sparse Objects in High-Resolution UAV Imagery
reason: The method counts and localizes cattle (livestock) in UAV images of a grazing paddock. No wild animals are in the analysed data.

title: Coral Reef Change Detection in Remote Pacific Islands Using Support Vector Machine Classifiers
reason: Pixel-based benthic cover-type (habitat) mapping and change detection of coral reefs from 30-m Landsat imagery. Although corals are animals, the paper classifies a coral-dominated benthic cover class per pixel, i.e. habitat / cover mapping rather than analysis of individual animals. Borderline judgement call.

title: Thermal Airborne Optical Sectioning
reason: Thermal synthetic-aperture drone imaging to remove vegetation occlusion; the only target imaged is a person hiding behind a bush. Animal inspection is named only as a potential application.

title: Coral Reef Mapping of UAV: A Comparison of Sun Glint Correction Methods
reason: Primary study that compares sun glint correction methods and applies SVM pixel-based classification to UAV multispectral imagery to map wild live coral classes (corals are animals) on a reef in Malaysia. Borderline with habitat mapping, but live coral taxa are the mapped subject.

title: Real-Time Underwater Image Recognition with FPGA Embedded System for Convolutional Neural Network
reason: Classifies underwater lake scene images into water, algae, bubbles and rocks for AUV navigation. No animals are analysed; the lake was chosen because it has no fish.

title: Multi-Pig Part Detection and Association with a Fully-Convolutional Network
reason: The study detects group-housed pigs in commercial swine facility pens (precision livestock farming); no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: A Novel Hierarchical Coding Progressive Transmission Method for WMSN Wildlife Images
reason: Proposes a CNN-based saliency segmentation plus progressive coding method for wildlife images captured by field WMSN camera nodes in a nature reserve.

title: Application of Deep-Learning Methods to Bird Detection Using Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Imagery
reason: Deep-learning object detectors are trained and evaluated on UAV aerial photographs of wild birds (plus bird decoys) taken at wild bird habitats in South Korea.

title: A pilot study for estimating the cardiopulmonary signals of diverse exotic animals using a digital camera
reason: All animals filmed were zoo animals in enclosures at Adelaide Zoo; no wild or free-ranging animals are in the analysed data.

title: Abnormal Water Quality Monitoring Based on Visual Sensing of Three-Dimensional Motion Behavior of Fish
reason: Fish are kept in an experimental tank with added pollutants and filmed to judge water quality; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Automated photogrammetric method to identify individual painted dogs (Lycaon pictus)
reason: Individual identification of painted dogs using Hotspotter, but all images come from zoo animals in an enclosure at Yokohama Zoo; no wild data analysed.

title: Scene Illustration of Terrestrial Animals with Its Monitoring, Tracking and Recognizing Through Deep Learning in Relation with Granular Computing
venue: International Journal of Engineering and Advanced Technology
reason: Applies Mask R-CNN combined with granular computing to video of deer for detection, segmentation and tracking. The paper does not say where the video came from, but it is framed as monitoring terrestrial animals in natural ecosystems, and nothing indicates captivity.

title: CBNWI-50: A Deep Learning Bird Dataset for Image Translation and Resolution Improvement using Generative Adversarial Network
venue: International Journal of Innovative Technology and Exploring Engineering
reason: Proposes a dataset of photographs of wild birds in North-Western India and applies GAN-based image translation and super resolution to the bird images.

title: Coral Reef Image Classifications with Hybrid Methods
venue: International Journal of Innovative Technology and Exploring Engineering
reason: Primary study applying handcrafted texture descriptors and CNN features to classify underwater image patches of corals (marine invertebrate animals) and urchins taken on a natural reef near Eilat.

title: Animal detection in highly cluttered natural scenes by using faster R-CNN
venue: International Journal of Recent Technology and Engineering
reason: Applies Faster R-CNN to detect wild animals in camera-trap images of natural scenes; primary research.

title: Butterfly Family Detection and Identification using Convolutional Neural Network for Lepidopterology
venue: International Journal of Recent Technology and Engineering (IJRTE)
reason: Primary study applying a CNN to classify butterfly images collected on a field trip and by web scraping; butterflies are wild, non-domestic animals and the subject of the work.

title: Modelling wildlife species abundance using automated detections from drone surveillance
reason: Applies an automated image detection algorithm to drone thermal imagery of a free-ranging, radio-collared koala population and models abundance from the detections.

title: A Novel Automated Mass Digitisation Workflow for Natural History Microscope Slides
reason: Digitisation workflow for museum microscope slides of parasitic lice (natural history specimens); no wild free-ranging animals, and the image processing is only barcode reading and cropping.

title: Embedding Computer Vision in Citizen Science
reason: Two-page conference abstract announcing a presentation. It reports no data, experiments or results, and does not identify the animal taxa analysed; one strand concerns flowers. It is not primary research with analysable computer vision results.

title: Efficient Pipeline for Automating Species ID in new Camera Trap Projects
reason: Conference abstract presenting a pipeline (generic animal detector plus project-specific species classifiers) for camera trap images of wild animals.

title: Artificial Intelligence's Role in Global Camera Trap Data Management and Analytics via Wildlife Insights
reason: Conference abstract describing the Wildlife Insights platform, which uses AI to classify camera trap images of wild animals (blank, human or animal, then species).

title: Machine Learning Model for Identifying Dutch/Belgian Biodiversity
reason: Conference abstract describing a deep learning image-based species identification model trained on citizen-science photographs of wild organisms (including birds, mammals, insects) from the Netherlands and Belgium.

title: Smart Insect Cameras
reason: Conference abstract describing field-deployed smart cameras that detect, identify, track and count free-ranging insects landing on screens using deep learning.

title: Agouti: A platform for processing and archiving of camera trap images
reason: Conference abstract describing a data management platform for camera-trap images; only a passing mention of basic image recognition, no computer vision method developed or evaluated.

title: Research and Teaching Applications of Remote Sensing Integrated with GIS: Examples from the Field
reason: UAS thermal and RGB survey of free-ranging bison and mule deer, but animals were found by manual inspection of the imagery in a GIS; automated detection is only proposed as future work. The deep-learning part (3D U-Net) concerns terrain point clouds, not animals.

title: Identification and limitation of Aquatic Organisms Using Extended Kalman Filter
reason: Wild-caught zooplankton are imaged in a laboratory transparent cell with a microscope high-speed camera to check whether ballast water treatment worked. This is a lab/microscopy set-up, not imaging of free-ranging animals.

title: CoCoNet: A Collaborative Convolutional Network
reason: Proposes a fine-grained classification network with bird species recognition as the stated application, evaluated on bird image datasets including a new dataset of Indian endemic birds collected from birder and citizen-scientist web repositories. Whether the photographed birds are wild is not stated.

title: See Better Before Looking Closer: Weakly Supervised Data Augmentation Network for Fine-Grained Visual Classification
reason: Generic fine-grained visual classification method evaluated on standard benchmarks (birds, dogs, cars, aircraft); wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: The iWildCam 2018 Challenge Dataset
reason: Presents a camera-trap challenge dataset of wild animals with a CNN baseline for animal vs. empty classification across locations.

title: Weakly Labeling the Antarctic: The Penguin Colony Case
reason: Primary study proposing a weakly-supervised deep learning method to segment guano stains (direct signs) of wild Adélie penguin colonies in satellite imagery.

title: Efficient Pipeline for Camera Trap Image Review
reason: Proposes a detection-plus-classification pipeline for camera trap images of wild animals and applies it to images from the Idaho Department of Fish and Game.

title: The iWildCam 2019 Challenge Dataset
reason: Dataset and challenge paper on species classification in camera trap images of wild animals, with a trained CNN baseline.

title: Efficient Method for Categorize Animals in the Wild
reason: Primary study that detects and classifies wild animal species in camera-trap images from the iWildCam 2019 competition.

title: Animal Wildlife Population Estimation Using Social Media Images Collections
reason: Estimates wild Grevy's zebra population from citizen-science and social media images, using Wildbook individual identification and image features.

title: The Northumberland Dolphin Dataset: A Multimedia Individual Cetacean Dataset for Fine-Grained Categorisation
reason: Dataset paper presenting above- and below-water photo-id images of wild white-beaked dolphins off the Northumberland coast, intended for individual identification.

title: Cross-Domain Adaptation for Animal Pose Estimation
reason: Pose estimation method evaluated quantitatively only on domestic animals (dog, cat, horse, sheep, cow) from VOC/COCO images; wild taxa appear only as extra bounding-box data or in qualitative failure examples, not as the analysed subject.

title: Neural Naturalist: Generating Fine-Grained Image Comparisons
reason: Introduces a dataset and a neural model generating comparative descriptions of iNaturalist photographs of wild birds; primary research with computer vision on images of free-ranging animals.

title: Beyond image classification: zooplankton identification with deep vector space embeddings
reason: Deep metric embedding (siamese CNN) for classifying images of zooplankton, which are wild aquatic organisms, from the public ZooScan dataset.

title: Conservation AI: Live Stream Analysis for the Detection of Endangered Species Using Convolutional Neural Networks and Drone Technology
reason: Rhino detection from drone video; the authors' own images and the field trial come from the rhino enclosure at a safari park, supplemented by Google Images of unstated provenance. No data is stated to show wild, free-ranging animals.

title: RoIMix: Proposal-Fusion among Multiple Images for Underwater Object Detection
reason: Proposes a data augmentation method (RoIMix) for detecting underwater marine creatures (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish) in the URPC dataset; also evaluated on Pascal VOC.

title: Algorithmic Design and Implementation of Unobtrusive Multistatic Serial LiDAR Image
reason: Develops underwater LiDAR image detection and classification algorithms. They are evaluated on field data from a test site that includes natural harbor seals and fishes, alongside artificial targets.

title: Evaluation of small unmanned aerial systems as a census tool for Aleutian Tern Onychoprion aleuticus colonies
reason: UAS images of a wild tern colony were searched for nests and identified to species manually by observers; the only computational image processing is Structure-from-Motion orthomosaic generation, with no automated analysis of the animals.

title: Effectiveness, efficiency, and safety of censusing Eurasian Oystercatchers Haematopus ostralegus by unmanned aircraft
reason: Wild oystercatchers were counted from drone video, but human observers did the counting by watching the videos. The paper applies no computer vision or automated image analysis.

title: Analysis of Learning Techniques: Bird Species Classification
reason: Applies CNN features and classical classifiers to classify bird species in CUB-200-2011 images, which are Flickr photographs of birds; wildlife bird identification is the stated subject.

title: Auto-filtering validation in citizen science biodiversity monitoring: a case study
reason: Citizen science biodiversity platform that applies image recognition (Clarifai API) to verify species type of submitted observation photos, including butterflies and birds observed in the wild. Plants are also covered, but wild animals are part of the subject.

title: INTRASEASONAL VARIABILITY OF GUANO STAINS IN A REMOTELY SENSED PENGUIN COLONY USING UAV AND SATELLITE
venue: ISPRS annals of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences
reason: Applies GEOBIA image classification to UAV and satellite images to map guano stains (direct signs) of a wild penguin colony on Ardley Island.

title: DETECTING ANTARCTIC SEALS AND FLYING SEABIRDS BY UAV
venue: ISPRS annals of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences
reason: UAV images of wild Antarctic seals and seabirds are analysed only by human observers in a manual detection trial; no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: SEMANTIC SEGMENTATION OF BENTHIC COMMUNITIES FROM ORTHO-MOSAIC MAPS
venue: The international archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences/International archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences
reason: CNN semantic segmentation of wild soft corals on a reef ortho-mosaic from Mozambique; primary method research.

title: SEMI-AUTOMATIC METHOD OF FAN SURFACE ASSESSMENT TO ACHIEVE GORGONIAN POPULATION STRUCTURE IN LE DANOIS BANK, CANTABRIAN SEA
venue: The international archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences/International archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences
reason: The paper uses Structure-from-Motion photogrammetry on underwater video to build 3D models of a wild deep-sea gorgonian coral population, then measures colony fan surfaces from those models.

title: 3D HABITAT COMPLEXITY OF CORAL REEFS IN THE NORTHWESTERN HAWAIIAN ISLANDS IS DRIVEN BY CORAL ASSEMBLAGE STRUCTURE
venue: The international archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences/International archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences
reason: Applies Structure-from-Motion photogrammetry (computer vision 3D reconstruction) to underwater images of wild coral reefs to relate coral assemblages to 3D habitat complexity.

title: ANIMAL DETECTION USING A SERIES OF IMAGES UNDER COMPLEX SHOOTING CONDITIONS
venue: The international archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences/International archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences
reason: Primary study proposing a background-modelling computer vision method to detect wild animals in camera-trap images from a natural park.

title: Geographic variation in Prionotus punctatus (Bloch) (Teleostei, Scorpaeniformes, Triglidae): a geometric morphometric analysis
reason: Geometric morphometric study based on caliper measurements of preserved museum fish specimens; no image or video analysis.

title: Using iNaturalist in a Coverboard Protocol to Measure Data Quality: Suggestions for Project Design
reason: Citizen-science data quality study: volunteers photograph wild herpetofauna under coverboards with smartphones, and identification is done by human iNaturalist identifiers and herpetologists. No computer vision or automated image analysis is applied; the analysis is statistical (mixed models, contingency tables).

title: Detection and counting of wild animals as source value by image processing technique
venue: Pamukkale University Journal of Engineering Sciences
reason: Primary study developing an image-processing pipeline (GMM background subtraction, shape and colour features, ANN classifier) to detect, classify and count wild animals in camera-trap videos.

title: Detection and counting of wild animals as source value by image processing technique
venue: Pamukkale University Journal of Engineering Sciences
reason: Image processing system for detecting, classifying and counting wild animals (deer, fox, wolf, wild horse) in camera trap videos from protected areas.

title: Spatio-temporal population change of Arctic-breeding waterbirds on the Arctic Coastal Plain of Alaska
reason: Population trends are estimated from counts made by human observers in aircraft during aerial surveys, analysed with statistical models. The paper does not analyse any animal images or video.

title: Application of CNN for Fish Species Classification
venue: The Journal of the Korean Institute of Information and Communication Engineering
reason: All fish images were filmed by the authors in a laboratory tank. Dataset 2 only blends these images with underwater backgrounds, so no wild free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: DeepPoseKit, a software toolkit for fast and robust animal pose estimation using deep learning
reason: Deep-learning pose estimation toolkit evaluated on laboratory fly, locust and mouse images and on drone video of wild Grévy's zebras, so part of the data shows wild free-ranging animals.

title: DeepFly3D, a deep learning-based approach for 3D limb and appendage tracking in tethered, adult Drosophila
reason: 3D pose estimation of tethered laboratory Drosophila on a spherical treadmill in an imaging chamber; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Elements of a stochastic 3D prediction engine in larval zebrafish prey capture
reason: Laboratory study of larval zebrafish (WIK strain) hunting paramecia in a small acrylic tank; custom computer vision is used for tracking, but no wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: QUANTIFYING THE SEVERITY OF GIRAFFE SKIN DISEASE VIA PHOTOGRAMMETRY ANALYSIS OF CAMERA TRAP DATA
reason: Primary study analysing camera-trap and vehicle-survey photographs of wild giraffes to measure skin-disease lesions. Borderline: the lesion measurement is manual photogrammetry in Photoshop; the only automated vision tool is Wild-ID for individual identification.

title: The running kinematics of free-roaming giraffes, measured using a low cost unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)
reason: Biomechanics study of free-roaming giraffes filmed by UAV. Kinematic points were digitised manually and strides segmented manually; no automated computer vision is applied to the animal images. Photogrammetry is used only to build a terrain mesh for calibration. Borderline case, since images are analysed, but by hand.

title: Quantitative color profiling of digital images with earth mover’s distance using the R package colordistance
reason: Method paper presenting an image-processing R package (colour histograms, k-means, earth mover's distance) applied to images of non-domestic animals (Heliconius butterflies, winter flounder, parrotfishes). Whether the animals were wild, captive or specimens is not stated.

title: Management factors affecting physical health and welfare of tourist camp elephants in Thailand
reason: Veterinary welfare study of captive tourist camp elephants using physical examination scores and GEE statistical models; no image or video analysis is performed. The animals are also captive only.

title: Use of aerial thermography to reduce mortality of roe deer fawns before harvest
reason: Wild roe deer fawns in alfalfa fields were found with a UAV-mounted thermal camera, but a human operator watched the live display to spot them. No computational image analysis or computer vision method is used.

title: Impact of digital video analytics on accuracy of chemobehavioural phenotyping in aquatic toxicology
reason: Laboratory ecotoxicology study benchmarking animal-tracking software on video of hatched brine shrimp larvae in fabricated test chambers; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Image based quantitative comparisons indicate heightened megabenthos diversity and abundance at a site of weak hydrocarbon seepage in the southwestern Barents Sea
reason: ROV images were stitched into photomosaics, but every animal was marked and counted by hand in ArcMap. No computer vision method was developed or applied to the animals.

title: Measuring body dimensions of leopards (Panthera pardus) from camera trap photographs
reason: Primary study measuring body dimensions of free-ranging leopards from scaled camera trap photographs with ImageJ. The measurement is manual, software-assisted image analysis rather than an automated vision algorithm, so inclusion is borderline; E-NOCV was not applied because image analysis is performed.

title: Infrared thermography cannot be used to approximate core body temperature in wild primates
reason: Physiology study of wild vervet monkeys: surface temperatures were read manually from thermal images with vendor software and analysed with linear models; no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: A chomped chimp: New evidence of tooth marks on an adult chimpanzee ( Pan troglodytes verus )
reason: Taphonomic description of tooth marks on one museum chimpanzee cranium. The authors examine it by eye, photograph it, micro-CT and laser-scan it, and measure it with calipers. No computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Underwater image enhancement using improved generative adversarial network
venue: Concurrency and Computation Practice and Experience
reason: Generic underwater image enhancement (color restoration) with a GAN; animals are not the stated subject and no wildlife application is analysed.

title: Wild boar recognition using convolutional neural networks
venue: Concurrency and Computation Practice and Experience
reason: Primary study retraining four CNNs to classify images of wild boar and two native peccary species collected from the Internet, for wildlife monitoring. The paper does not state whether the animals shown are free-ranging or captive; images are described as real-world footage taken with camera traps and smartphones.

title: Spatial and temporal variation in prey color patterns for background matching across a continuous heterogeneous environment
reason: Photographs of a wild shore skink population and their backgrounds are analysed computationally: RGB values are extracted and calibrated to measure colour and background matching. This counts as image analysis of wild animals.

title: Three critical factors affecting automated image species recognition performance for camera traps
reason: Primary study training and evaluating six CNN classifiers on camera trap images of free-ranging wildlife from Alberta parks; the classes also include a few domestic animals (dog, horse, cattle) and human activity.

title: A study on giant panda recognition based on images of a large proportion of captive pandas
reason: Individual identification of giant pandas from face images; all analysed images show captive pandas (breeding base), no wild or free-ranging animals in the data.

title: An “orientation sphere” visualization for examining animal head movements
reason: The paper proposes a visualization of head-mounted accelerometer and magnetometer tag data; no image or video data are analysed with computer vision.

title: Variation in brown rat cranial shape shows directional selection over 120 years in New York City
reason: Geometric morphometric study of museum rat skulls using a 3D contact digitizer for landmarks; no image or video analysis or computer vision.

title: A regionally scalable habitat typology for assessing benthic habitats and fish communities: Application to New Caledonia reefs and lagoons
reason: Human annotators scored fish counts and habitat attributes from the underwater videos by hand. The analysis then runs clustering, random forest and rule mining on those tabular attributes. No computer vision method is applied to the images.

title: New technologies in the mix: Assessing N‐mixture models for abundance estimation using automated detection data from drone surveys
reason: Primary study that applies an automated image detection algorithm to drone thermal imagery of free-ranging, radio-collared koalas and evaluates abundance estimates derived from those detections against ground counts.

title: Applications of deep convolutional neural networks to predict length, circumference, and weight from mostly dewatered images of fish
reason: CNN regressors predict length, girth and weight from images of wild-caught fish from Great Lakes and Mississippi River tributaries, imaged in a portable scanning device during routine field assessments and then released.

title: Improving the accessibility and transferability of machine learning algorithms for identification of animals in camera trap images: MLWIC2
reason: Trains and evaluates deep CNNs to classify species and empty images in camera trap images of wild animals (with some domestic species) and releases an R package.

title: Camera settings and biome influence the accuracy of citizen science approaches to camera trap image classification
reason: The paper compares the accuracy of crowdsourced human (citizen scientist) classifications of camera trap images against expert review. No computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated; volunteer answers are only aggregated by a plurality vote.

title: Automated facial recognition for wildlife that lack unique markings: A deep learning approach for brown bears
reason: Primary study developing a deep learning facial recognition pipeline (BearID) for individual identification of wild brown bears from photographs taken in British Columbia and Alaska.

title: Robust and simplified machine learning identification of pitfall trap‐collected ground beetles at the continental scale
reason: Classifies dead, ethanol-stored ground beetle specimens (pitfall-trap collected, vouchered) photographed on a tile in a laboratory imaging set-up; no images of live free-ranging animals.

title: Genotyping validates the efficacy of photographic identification in a capture‐mark‐recapture study based on the head scale patterns of the prairie lizard (Sceloporus consobrinus)
reason: Primary study evaluating semi-automated photographic identification software (I3S) on photographs of wild-caught prairie lizards in a capture-mark-recapture study, cross-validated with genotyping.

title: Chimpanzee identification and social network construction through an online citizen science platform
reason: Camera trap videos of wild chimpanzees are detected, counted and individually identified manually by citizen scientists and experts; no computer vision or automated image analysis method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Intra‐ and inter‐annual variation in gray whale body condition on a foraging ground
reason: Applies drone-image photogrammetry (image-based morphometric measurement) to wild free-ranging gray whales to assess body condition.

title: Calibrating and adjusting counts of harbor seals in a tidewater glacier fjord to estimate abundance and trends 1992 to 2017
reason: Aerial photographs of wild harbor seals were counted manually by a trained observer; the analysis is Bayesian statistical calibration and trend modelling, with no computer vision method applied to the images.

title: Octopuses punch fishes during collaborative interspecific hunting events
reason: Natural history report of wild octopus–fish hunting behaviour recorded in the field. The behaviour is described from observation, with no computer vision or automated image analysis.

title: Recent Advances in Visual Sensing and Machine Learning Techniques for in-situ Plankton-taxa Classification
reason: Proposes and evaluates a deep learning architecture (COAPNet) for classifying plankton taxa in images captured in-situ in the marine environment, embedded in an autonomous underwater vehicle.

title: How many sea scallops are there and why does it matter?
venue: Frontiers in Ecology and the Environment
reason: Wild sea scallops are surveyed with drop-camera quadrat images, but they are counted and measured by hand from the images. No computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Egg patterns as identity signals in colonial seabirds: a comparison of four alcid species
venue: Journal of Experimental Zoology Part B Molecular and Developmental Evolution
reason: Image analysis of egg patterns from museum egg specimens only; no free-ranging animals imaged.

title: The skin of birds' feet: Morphological adaptations of the plantar surface
reason: Morphological study of museum spirit-collection bird specimens using micro-CT and SEM; no wild free-ranging animals imaged and no computer vision method developed.

title: Fast cropping method for proper input size of convolutional neural networks in underwater photography
venue: Journal of the Society for Information Display
reason: CNN-based fish species classification with a fast cropping method; training images come from an experimental environment, test images from an underwater camera system installed in ponds / a fish passage, in the context of invasive species management.

title: Estimating Abundance of an Unmarked, Low‐Density Species using Cameras
reason: Camera-trap photos of wild cougars were reviewed manually by people; density is estimated with statistical encounter-rate models (time-to-event, space-to-event, REM, genetic SCR). No computer vision or image analysis method is applied.

title: Paired high‐throughput, in situ imaging and high‐throughput sequencing illuminate acantharian abundance and vertical distribution
reason: In situ plankton images of acantharians (unicellular protists, not animals) were viewed, cropped and counted manually by a researcher; no computer vision method is applied, and automatic classification is only mentioned as future work.

title: Investigating uncertainties created by camera improvement in an optical survey
reason: Wild Atlantic sea scallops are photographed with an underwater drop camera, but people count and measure them by eye. The paper only analyses camera detection differences statistically (SELECT model); no computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: The Scripps Plankton Camera system: A framework and platform for in situ microscopy
reason: Describes an in situ underwater imaging microscope and applies CNN classification to images of free-living zooplankton (the copepod Oithona sp.) recorded in the ocean; a second study covers phytoplankton. Borderline case because it is microscopy, but the imaging is in situ on wild organisms, not a laboratory set-up.

title: Learning features from georeferenced seafloor imagery with location guided autoencoders
reason: Unsupervised feature learning for seafloor habitat/substrate mapping (rock, sand, carbonate, shell fragment, bacterial mat, cable, artificial object). Animals are not the subject; crabs appear only as one qualitative image-search query.

title: Assessing the potential for spectrally based remote sensing of salmon spawning locations
reason: Applies machine learning and object-based image analysis to UAS imagery to detect nests (redds) of wild Chinook salmon in a river; redds are direct animal signs.

title: Cameras replace human observers in multi‐species aerial counts in Murchison Falls, Uganda
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Aerial survey images of wild African mammals were counted and identified visually by human airphoto interpreters; no computer vision or automated image analysis method was developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Influence of altitude on tropical marine habitat classification using imagery from fixed‐wing, water‐landing UAV s
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: UAV orthomosaics are classified into habitat cover classes (coral, mangrove, sea, sand, seagrass) for marine habitat mapping. Coral is treated only as a habitat cover class; no animals are the subject of the analysis.

title: Discovery of new colonies by Sentinel2 reveals good and bad news for emperor penguins
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Emperor penguin colonies are found by manual visual inspection of Sentinel2 satellite imagery for guano stains; no computer vision or automated image analysis method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Dual visible‐thermal camera approach facilitates drone surveys of colonial marshbirds
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Drone visible and thermal imagery of wild marshbird colonies was interpreted and counted manually by a human observer in QGIS; no computer vision method was developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Wildlife trail or systematic? Camera trap placement has little effect on estimates of mammal diversity in a tropical forest in Gabon
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Camera-trap survey of wild mammals in Gabon comparing placement strategies; videos were identified manually and entered into a database, analysis is statistical (occupancy, RAI, ordination). No computer vision method is applied to the images.

title: Using very‐high‐resolution satellite imagery and deep learning to detect and count African elephants in heterogeneous landscapes
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Primary study applying a CNN object detector to very-high-resolution satellite images of free-ranging African elephants in a national park in South Africa and in the Maasai Mara, Kenya.

title: Edge‐adaptable serverless acceleration for machine learning Internet of Things applications
reason: Systems paper on edge/cloud serverless scheduling whose stated application is CNN classification of camera-trap images of wild animals at a natural reserve. Evaluation focuses on latency rather than vision accuracy, but computer vision is applied to wild animal images.

title: Comparison of Underwater Video with Electrofishing and Dive Counts for Stream Fish Abundance Estimation
venue: Transactions of the American Fisheries Society
reason: Underwater video of wild Brook Trout was reviewed and counted manually by one human observer; no computer vision or automated image analysis was applied.

title: Deep learning–based automatic bird identification system for offshore wind farms
reason: Primary study that builds a CNN image classifier for free-flying wild seabirds and raptors photographed at an offshore wind farm.

title: Identifying Individual Jaguars and Ocelots via Pattern‐Recognition Software: Comparing HotSpotter and Wild‐ID
reason: Primary study evaluating two pattern-recognition programs (HotSpotter, Wild-ID) for individual identification of wild jaguars and ocelots in camera-trap images from Belize.

title: Evaluating the Use of Drones Equipped with Thermal Sensors as an Effective Method for Estimating Wildlife
reason: Thermal drone video of an enclosed (captive) white-tailed deer population was analysed manually by two human observers; no computer vision method was developed, applied or evaluated.

title: A Comparison of Two Methods to Monitor Translocated Prairie Dogs
reason: Compares PIT-tag readers with trail-camera photographs for monitoring captive, translocated prairie dogs in a fenced enclosure; all photographs were viewed manually and no computer vision method was used.

title: Using Natural Pelt Patterns to Estimate Population Abundance with Mark–Resight Models
reason: Camera-trap images of free-ranging wild pigs are identified to individual entirely by human observers using a manual photo-ID catalogue; no computer vision or automated image analysis is applied. Abundance is estimated with statistical mark-resight models.

title: Natural environmental conditions and collaborative efforts provide the secret to success for sand tiger shark Carcharias taurus reproduction in aquaria
reason: Husbandry report on sand tiger shark reproduction in an aquarium. Underwater video is used only to watch fetal movement by eye; no computer vision or image analysis. The animals are also captive.

title: Analyzing Underwater Videos for Fish Detection, Counting and Classification
venue: Advances in intelligent systems and computing
reason: Computer vision pipeline for detecting, counting, tracking and classifying fish species in FishCLEF underwater videos of free-swimming fish.

title: Animal Species Recognition Using Deep Learning
venue: Advances in intelligent systems and computing
reason: Applies CNN classification to camera-trap images of wild North American mammals (BCMOTI and Snapshot Wisconsin) to reduce wildlife-vehicle collisions.

title: 3D Bird Reconstruction: A Dataset, Model, and Shape Recovery from a Single View
venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science Including Subseries Lecture Notes in Artificial Intelligence and Lecture Notes in Bioinformatics
reason: The main analysed data are 15 cowbirds housed in an outdoor aviary. CUB-200 appears only as a supplementary qualitative generalisation demo.

title: System of Ornithological Protection of Airfields
venue: Lecture notes in networks and systems
reason: Describes a bioacoustic bird-repelling hardware system for airfields; no image or video analysis is performed.

title: Reasoning About Neural Network Activations: An Application in Spatial Animal Behaviour from Camera Trap Classifications
venue: Communications in computer and information science
reason: The paper uses a CNN to classify camera-trap images of wild mammals in northern Borneo, then feeds the classifier outputs into Bayesian networks to study spatial behaviour.

title: Butterfly Detection and Classification Based on Integrated YOLO Algorithm
venue: Advances in intelligent systems and computing
reason: Proposes an integrated YOLO v3 ensemble to detect and classify butterflies in photographs taken in the natural ecological environment; specimen photographs were excluded from the data used.

title: Analysis of Pruned Neural Networks (MobileNetV2-YOLO v2) for Underwater Object Detection
reason: The images are lab video of domestic ornamental goldfish breeds swimming in an aquarium. No wild or free-ranging animals are analysed, and pets fall under E-AGRI.

title: Investigating the age composition of Indo-Pacific humpback dolphins in the Pearl River Estuary based on their pigmentation pattern
reason: Image analysis (non-white ratio quantification of dorsal-region photos) applied to photo-identification images of free-ranging Indo-Pacific humpback dolphins to estimate age composition.

title: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) survey of the Antarctic shag (Leucocarbo bransfieldensis) breeding colony at Harmony Point, Nelson Island, South Shetland Islands
reason: UAV survey of a wild seabird colony in which nests were marked and counted manually on an orthomosaic. The only computational image processing is structure-from-motion photogrammetry of the terrain; no computer vision method is applied to the animals.

title: Quantifying life history demographics of the scleractinian coral genus Pocillopora at Palmyra Atoll
reason: Applies Structure-from-Motion photogrammetry to diver-collected field images of wild Pocillopora coral colonies; area is then measured from the image pixels to quantify demographics.

title: l2,p-norm sequential bilateral 2DPCA: a novel robust technology for underwater image classification and representation
reason: Generic robust 2DPCA dimensionality-reduction method evaluated on underwater image datasets (fish, underwater creatures, pool objects) and a face dataset. Wildlife is not the stated subject, and the paper does not say whether the animals are wild.

title: Scale-aware feature pyramid architecture for marine object detection
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for marine animals (sea cucumber, sea urchin, scallop). The underwater images were captured by the authors' robot in a natural ocean environment.

title: Research on underwater object recognition based on YOLOv3
reason: Detection of sea cucumber, scallop and sea urchin on the URPC dataset. The stated goal is the detection part of an underwater catching robot for marine pasture, which is harvesting in aquaculture or sea ranching. The paper never says whether the animals are wild.

title: Visualization of dynamic structure in flocking behavior
reason: The paper proposes a sequential GTM clustering method applied to simulated Boids agents' positions and velocities; no images or video are analysed and no real animals appear in the data.

title: Social spatial cognition: social distance dynamics as an identifier of social interactions
reason: Laboratory open-field study of rat, gerbil and fat sand rat dyads (laboratory rats and captive-colony rodents) tracked with EthoVision; no wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: WISH cages: constructing multiple habitats for captive chimpanzees
reason: Historical editorial/perspective on environmental enrichment for captive chimpanzees in Japan. It reports no primary computer vision research; a chimpanzee face recognition system is only mentioned in passing.

title: Sharing waters: the impact of recreational kayaking on moulting mute swans Cygnus olor
reason: Behavioural disturbance study of wild moulting mute swans; drone photos were only used manually to extract coordinates and time stamps in QGIS, and behaviour was scored by human observers. No computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Automated detection of European wild mammal species in camera trap images with an existing and pre-trained computer vision model
reason: Applies a pre-trained object detection model to camera trap images of wild European mammals from a national park and evaluates detection and classification accuracy.

title: Discolouring the Amazon Rainforest: how deforestation is affecting butterfly coloration
reason: Wild-caught butterflies were killed, deposited in an entomological collection and photographed as specimens for colour measurement. No images of live free-ranging animals are analysed, so this counts as specimen imaging.

title: Deep learning for automated analysis of fish abundance: the benefits of training across multiple habitats
reason: Primary study training Mask R-CNN object detection models on underwater video of wild luderick in seagrass and reef habitats to detect fish and estimate abundance (MaxN).

title: Towards a robust baseline for long-term monitoring of Antarctic coastal benthos
reason: Applies SfM photogrammetry to underwater video to reconstruct the seafloor and produce orthophotos. Wild Antarctic megabenthic animals are then counted and mapped from these orthophotos for monitoring.

title: Using a Touchscreen Paradigm to Evaluate Food Preferences and Response to Novel Photographic Stimuli of Food in Three Primate Species (Gorilla gorilla gorilla, Pan troglodytes, and Macaca fuscata)
reason: Behavioural study of food preferences of zoo-housed primates using a touchscreen. Photographs of food are only used as stimuli, and no computer vision or image analysis is done on animal images. The animals are also captive only.

title: Crosspooled FishNet: transfer learning based fish species classification model
reason: Proposes a CNN-based fish species classification model evaluated on underwater video images of free-ranging fish from the Fish4Knowledge dataset.

title: Deep interactive encoding with capsule networks for image classification
reason: Generic image-classification paper proposing capsule network variants, tested on four general benchmarks (CIFAR10, MARVEL, ANIMALS, PETS). Animals appear only as benchmark classes; wildlife is not the stated subject or application, and the paper does not say whether the animal images show wild animals.

title: Dolphin movement direction recognition using contour-skeleton information
reason: Computer vision method (Mask R-CNN + OpenPose + classifier) to recognise movement direction of dolphins in underwater video from a documentary; non-domestic animals, captivity status not stated.

title: A pattern analysis based underwater video segmentation system for target object detection
reason: Proposes a classical image-processing pipeline for detecting and segmenting target objects in underwater videos from a public underwater benchmark. The paper never names the animals in its own data; its stated application is underwater and sea-life monitoring.

title: A New Supervised Clustering Framework Using Multi Discriminative Parts and Expectation–Maximization Approach for a Fine-Grained Animal Breed Classification (SC-MPEM)
reason: Proposes a fine-grained animal classification method (SC-MPEM) and evaluates it on Snapshot Serengeti camera-trap images of wild mammals alongside three domestic dog/cat breed datasets.

title: Gradient Based Aura Feature Extraction for Coral Reef Classification
reason: Primary study proposing a texture feature descriptor with a CNN classifier to classify coral types in underwater coral reef images and videos; corals are wild animals imaged on reefs.

title: Intelligent animal detection system using sparse multi discriminative-neural network (SMD-NN) to mitigate animal-vehicle collision
reason: Proposes an animal detection method to mitigate animal-vehicle collisions, evaluated on animal image datasets that contain wild animals (e.g. giraffe, alligator, penguin, zebra) together with domestic ones (cat, dog, horse, sheep).

title: Measuring Complex Morphological Traits with 3D Photogrammetry: A Case Study with Deer Antlers
reason: Photogrammetric 3D reconstruction of deer antlers on museum skull specimens; no live free-ranging animals imaged.

title: Intelligent object recognition in underwater images using evolutionary-based Gaussian mixture model and shape matching
reason: Proposes an image segmentation and shape-matching method for recognising fish species in underwater images of reef fish taken from fish databases.

title: Multi-scale ResNet for real-time underwater object detection
reason: Proposes a CNN detector (M-ResNet) for detecting fish in underwater video, using the public Fish4Knowledge dataset and the authors' own underwater-drone footage.

title: Challenges in the deep learning-based semantic segmentation of benthic communities from Ortho-images
reason: Applies CNN semantic segmentation to ortho-projections of wild coral reef plots, segmenting the coral genera Porites, Montipora and Pocillopora.

title: Object Detection and Tracking with UAV Data Using Deep Learning
venue: Journal of the Indian Society of Remote Sensing
reason: Generic UAV object detection and tracking on the UAV123 benchmark. The objects shown are cars and boats; wildlife monitoring comes up only as an example UAV application.

title: Active and Incremental Learning with Weak Supervision
reason: Active and incremental learning for object detection, validated on camera trap images of wild and free-ranging mammals (alongside domestic livestock) in a Portuguese national park; also uses generic benchmarks.

title: Component processes of detection probability in camera-trap studies: understanding the occurrence of false-negatives
reason: Camera-trap detection-probability study (trigger, registration, capture quality) using CCTV as a control; footage was reviewed manually and analysed with statistical GLMMs, with no computer vision method applied to images. Animals are wild fox and badger plus captive otters.

title: Invariant Features-Based Fuzzy Inference System for Animal Detection and Recognition Using Thermal Images
reason: Fuzzy-logic detection and recognition of animals in thermal images, aimed at wild animal monitoring. The data mix domestic animals photographed in Vellore, zoo animals, and web images of wild species (lion, tiger, cheetah, elephant). The paper does not say whether the web images show free-ranging animals, so inclusion rests on the wild-species classes and the stated wildlife application.

title: Deep learning for plankton and coral classification
venue: Archivio istituzionale della ricerca (Alma Mater Studiorum Università di Bologna)
reason: CNN ensembles for classifying images of plankton sampled from the sea and coral reef image patches; computer vision on images of wild marine organisms, primary research.

title: Reproductive performance of captive Asian elephants (Elephas maximus) in large tourist camps in Thailand
reason: Statistical analysis of written breeding records of captive tourist-camp elephants; no image or video analysis.

title: Shedding light into the dark: Age and light shape nocturnal activity and sleep behaviour of giraffe
reason: Behaviour of zoo-housed giraffes was annotated manually from infrared video in BORIS and analysed with statistical models. No computer vision method was used, and all animals were captive (E-CAPTIVE would also apply).

title: Identification of Indian butterflies using Deep Convolutional Neural Network

title: Optimization of convolutional neural network hyperparameters for automatic classification of adult mosquitoes

reason: Primary study using drone images of wild waterbirds in Poland and evaluating automatic counting tools (ImageJ/Fiji particle analysis, DenoiSeg neural network) for bird censusing.

title: Critical summer foraging tradeoffs in a subarctic ungulate

title: Estimating animal abundance and effort–precision relationship with camera trap distance sampling
reason: Camera trap distance sampling study of wild forest mammals; videos were processed and distances measured manually by people, and the analysis is statistical abundance estimation. No computer vision method is applied to the images.

title: Frame‐by‐frame annotation of video recordings using deep neural networks

title: Survival of the fattest: linking body condition to prey availability and survivorship of killer whales
reason: Wild Southern Resident killer whales were imaged from a helicopter and drones, but the images were only measured by hand (eye patch ratio).
