title: Narwhal (Monodon monoceros) detection by infrared flukeprints from aerial survey imagery
reason: Infrared aerial video of wild narwhals was reviewed manually in vendor software; no computer vision or automated image analysis method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Eastern Canada Flocks: images and manually annotated bird positions
reason: Data paper releasing aerial survey images of wild bird flocks with manually annotated bird positions, intended for testing image-analysis methods that detect, identify and count animals.

title: A real‐world dataset and data simulation algorithm for automated fish species identification
reason: Data paper providing an annotated image dataset and synthetic image generator for automated species identification of wild pelagic fish imaged by an in-trawl camera during research surveys.

title: Trait‐based approach using in situ copepod images reveals contrasting ecological patterns across an Arctic ice melt zone
reason: Automated image analysis (segmentation, morphological descriptors, random forest classification) of in situ underwater images of wild copepods in Baffin Bay.

title: Zooglider‐measured association of zooplankton with the fine‐scale vertical prey field
reason: Applies image segmentation and CNN classification to in situ images of wild marine zooplankton taken by an autonomous glider, to study their vertical distribution relative to prey.

title: Automatic plankton image classification—Can capsules and filters help cope with data set shift?
reason: Deep learning classification (CNN and CapsNet) of in situ Video Plankton Recorder images of free-living marine zooplankton from the North Sea; primary research.

title: In situ three‐dimensional video tracking of tagged individuals within site‐attached social groups of coral‐reef fish
reason: Primary study developing a semi-automated CNN-based video detection and 3D tracking system for tagged wild damselfish in their natural coral-reef environment.

title: Low‐Cost Paper‐Based Conducting Polymer‐Hydrogel Flexible Bio‐Radar Sensor for Detecting Biological Objects
reason: Materials-science paper on a paper-based proximity (impedance) sensor tested on human fingers and laboratory mice in an open field arena; video tracking with commercial software serves only as validation. No wild or free-ranging animals.

title: 21 000 birds in 4.5 h: efficient large‐scale seabird detection with machine learning
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Primary study developing a CNN to detect and classify wild breeding seabirds (terns, gulls) in UAV imagery of colonies on the West African coast.

title: Drone‐based thermal remote sensing provides an effective new tool for monitoring the abundance of roosting fruit bats
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Primary study that develops and evaluates semi-automated image analysis (computer vision thresholding and OBIA machine learning) to count wild roosting grey-headed flying-foxes in drone-acquired thermal orthomosaics.

title: Machine learning to detect marine animals in UAV imagery: effect of morphology, spacing, behaviour and habitat
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Primary study training a CNN to detect wild seals, sea turtles and gannets in UAV imagery and to reconstruct turtle trajectories.

title: Underwater robots provide similar fish biodiversity assessments as divers on coral reefs
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Wild coral reef fish were filmed with stereo video from an underwater robot and by a diver. Humans then identified, counted and measured the fish by hand in VidSync. No automated image analysis was done, and the paper says video analysis 'is now done by humans'.

title: Multispecies detection and identification of African mammals in aerial imagery using convolutional neural networks
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Primary study comparing CNN object detectors to detect and identify wild African mammal species in UAV and light-aircraft imagery from national parks and reserves.

title: Trialling camera traps to determine occupancy and breeding in burrowing seabirds
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Camera-trap images of wild burrowing petrels were tagged manually; the only analysis is statistical (PCA, LDA, PERMANOVA) on activity metrics derived from those tags, with no computer vision method applied to the images.

title: A convolutional neural network architecture designed for the automated survey of seabird colonies
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Primary study proposing a CNN segmentation model for guano stains (a direct sign) of wild Adelie penguin colonies in high-resolution satellite imagery of Antarctica.

title: Real‐time insect tracking and monitoring with computer vision and deep learning
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Primary study presenting a camera system with YOLOv3 detection/classification and tracking of free-ranging flower-visiting insects recorded in situ on a green roof.

title: Enumerating White‐Tailed Deer Using Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
reason: UAV thermal images of wild white-tailed deer were counted manually by four human observers; no computer vision or automated image analysis method was developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Michigan ZoomIN: Validating Crowd‐Sourcing to Identify Mammals from Camera Surveys
reason: Camera-trap images are classified by human volunteers on a crowd-sourcing platform; the 'consensus algorithms' aggregate human votes and no computer vision / automated image analysis is applied.

title: An Adaptive Automatic Approach to Filtering Empty Images from Camera Traps Using a Deep Learning Model
reason: Primary study training a deep CNN to filter empty images from camera traps deployed for wildlife monitoring in the Baimaxueshan Mountains, China.

title: Drone Nest Searching Applications Using a Thermal Camera
reason: Drone thermal imagery of wild bird nests was interpreted manually by the operator in the field; no computer vision or automated image analysis was applied.

title: Allometric Regression of Snake Body Length from Head Image Measurements
reason: Allometric regression of snake body length from caliper head measurements. Image measurements are taken by hand with a measurement tool in image-editing software; no automated computer vision method is developed or applied, and no image-based size estimates are reported.

title: Use of Drones With Thermal Infrared to Locate White‐tailed Deer Neonates for Capture
reason: Drone thermal and RGB imagery of wild white-tailed deer fawns was interpreted visually by human observers in real time; no computer vision or automated image analysis method was developed or applied.

title: An evaluation of interactive projections as digital enrichment for orangutans
reason: Captive orangutans at Melbourne Zoo interact with a projection enrichment system. A Kinect depth sensor detects their touches. No wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Biological and environmental factors as sources of variation in nocturnal behavior of giraffe
reason: Behavioural study of giraffe kept only in zoos. The night-time videos were scored by hand in BORIS, and no automated computer vision is used.

title: Documenting nocturnal activity of dragon‐headed katydids (Lesina blanchardi) under artificial light
reason: Zoo-housed katydids filmed in an enclosure; video scored manually by a human observer, so no computer vision method is applied either.

title: Sentinel behavior in captive meerkats ( Suricata suricatta )
reason: Behavioural study of captive zoo meerkats; videos were coded manually with Solomon Coder and analysed statistically, with no computer vision method. Animals are captive only.

title: Mosquito Classification Using Convolutional Neural Network with Data Augmentation
venue: Advances in intelligent systems and computing
reason: Applies a CNN to classify images of non-domestic mosquitoes (Aedes, Anopheles, Culex) taken from web stock photo sites. The paper does not say whether the mosquitoes were wild or kept in a lab.

title: Video-Based Hierarchical Species Classification for Longline Fishing Monitoring
reason: Proposes a hierarchical CNN that classifies wild-caught fish species in electronic monitoring video from longline fishing vessels. This is capture fisheries, not aquaculture.

title: Betrayed by Motion: Camouflaged Object Discovery via Motion Segmentation
reason: Proposes a motion-based segmentation method to discover camouflaged animals in videos of natural scenes and introduces the MoCA dataset of camouflaged animals.

title: Biodiversity Image Quality Metadata Augments Convolutional Neural Network Classification of Fish Species
venue: Communications in computer and information science
reason: Images are of preserved museum fish specimens from the Illinois Natural History Survey Fish Collection, not live wild animals; museum specimens are excluded under E-CAPTIVE.

title: Life-Saving APP: Snake Classification ‘Venomous and Non-venomous’ Using fast.ai Based on Indian Species
venue: Lecture notes in networks and systems
reason: Applies CNN transfer learning to classify images of wild Indian snake species (venomous vs non-venomous) collected from Google Images.

title: A First Step Towards Automated Species Recognition from Camera Trap Images of Mammals Using AI in a European Temperate Forest
venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science Including Subseries Lecture Notes in Artificial Intelligence and Lecture Notes in Bioinformatics
reason: Applies YOLOv5 to camera trap images of wild mammals in the Białowieża Forest for detection and species classification.

title: End-to-End Learning of Fisher Vector Encodings for Part Features in Fine-Grained Recognition
reason: Generic fine-grained recognition method (Fisher vector encoding of part features) evaluated on standard fine-grained benchmarks (birds, dogs, moths); wildlife conservation is not the stated application.

title: A Machine Learning Enabled IoT Device to Combat Elephant Mortality on Railway Tracks
venue: Lecture notes on data engineering and communications technologies
reason: The paper reviews elephant-train collision statistics and proposes an IoT/ML concept. It only describes a planned ResNet experiment and analyses no images.

title: Computer Vision based Animal Collision Avoidance Framework for Autonomous Vehicles
venue: Communications in Computer and Information Science
reason: Animal-vehicle collision avoidance from dashcam video; the animals actually evaluated are stray cows and dogs (domestic), with no wild, non-domestic animals in the analysed results.

title: Using complementary visual approaches to investigate residency, site fidelity and movement patterns of the dusky grouper (Epinephelus marginatus) in a Mediterranean marine protected area
reason: Primary field study applying semi-automated photo-identification software (I3S Pattern) to underwater photographs of wild dusky grouper in a marine protected area.

title: Water clarity affects collective behavior in two cyprinid fishes
reason: Wild-caught shiners were housed in a laboratory and filmed in an indoor observation tank under controlled turbidity treatments; no images show free-ranging animals.

title: Putting sea cucumbers on the map: projected holothurian bioturbation rates on a coral reef scale
reason: Wild holothurians are counted in drone imagery, but only by manual digitizing in ArcGIS. No computer vision method is developed or applied to the animals. Automated counting is only suggested as future work.

title: Development of a multi-excitation fluorescence (MEF) imaging method to improve the information content of benthic coral reef surveys
reason: Laboratory proof-of-concept of a fluorescence imaging method on aquarium-cultured corals and algae, imaged through a microscope and bench cameras; no wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Microhabitats of sharknose goby (Elacatinus evelynae) cleaning stations and their links with cleaning behaviour
reason: Computer vision (structure-from-motion 3D reconstruction) is used only to measure coral-head habitat structure. The cleaner fish themselves were observed directly by snorkelers, not analysed in images.

title: High spatial resolution photo mosaicking for the monitoring of coralligenous reefs
reason: Proposes and evaluates a photomosaicking method (SIFT-based image stitching) on underwater images of wild coralligenous reef assemblages that include sessile invertebrates (bryozoans, gorgonians, ascidians, serpulids).

title: Kernel density estimation and correntropy based background modeling and camera model parameter estimation for underwater video object detection
reason: Proposes a background-modelling method for moving object detection in underwater videos, tested on videos of wild marine animals (beaked whale, whale shark, sea turtle, chimaera).

title: Deep vision-based surveillance system to prevent train–elephant collisions
reason: Primary study training CNN classifiers to recognise elephants on or near rail tracks to prevent train-elephant collisions; data include an elephant image dataset and internet images of elephants on tracks.

title: SHetConv: target keypoint detection based on heterogeneous convolution neural networks
reason: The paper proposes a keypoint detection network and evaluates it on Amur tiger images from the Tiger Pose Keypoint dataset, but it does not state whether the tigers are wild or captive, so the wild/free-ranging condition is not established. The contribution is a general efficient-convolution method also tested on CIFAR-10 and MPII.

title: DeepRecog: Threefold underwater image deblurring and object recognition framework for AUV vision systems
reason: Proposes a deblurring and object detection framework for underwater images of marine life (fishes, jellyfish, starfish, sharks, tortoises, corals) compiled from open image datasets. title: Estimating Pelagic Fish Biomass in a Tropical Seascape Using Echosounding and Baited Stereo-Videography
reason: Stereo-BRUVS video of wild pelagic fish is analysed manually with EventMeasure software (species ID, MaxN, lengths) and combined with echosounder data and GAMs; no automated computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Sex differences in habitat use, positional behavior, and gaits of Golden Snub-Nosed Monkeys (Rhinopithecus roxellana) in the Qinling Mountains, Shaanxi, China
reason: Field behavioural study of wild golden snub-nosed monkeys. Behaviour was recorded by focal observation, and gait parameters were measured manually from videos. No computer vision or automated image analysis method is developed or applied.

title: An evaluation of thermal imaging as a welfare monitoring tool for captive chimpanzees
reason: Thermal imaging study of sanctuary-housed captive chimpanzees in enclosures only; no wild or free-ranging animals analysed.

title: Assessing the activity of deer and their influence on vegetation in a wetland using automatic cameras and low altitude remote sensing (LARS)

title: Random encounter model to estimate density of mountain-dwelling ungulate
reason: Camera-trap density estimation with the random encounter model; photographs are processed manually and statistically, no computer vision or image analysis method is applied.

title: Learn class hierarchy using convolutional neural networks

title: Temperate fish detection and classification: a deep learning based approach
reason: Deep learning detection and classification of wild temperate fish in underwater video recorded in natural coastal environments.

title: Multi-stream fish detection in unconstrained underwater videos by the fusion of two convolutional neural network detectors

title: Using convolutional neural networks for tick image recognition – a preliminary exploration
reason: CNN classification of images of free-living questing ticks collected in the field from residential yards; the ticks are wild, non-domestic animals, though they were imaged as collected specimens under a stereomicroscope in the laboratory.

title: Detection of Anolis carolinensis using drone images and a deep neural network: an effective tool for controlling invasive species
reason: Primary study applying a CNN object detector (SSD) to drone imagery of free-ranging invasive Anolis carolinensis lizards on Ani-jima, Ogasawara Islands.

title: RETRACTED ARTICLE: A distributed submerged object detection and classification enhancement with deep learning
reason: The text is only a retraction notice. It contains no methods, data or image analysis, and it does not say whether animals were studied.

title: Use of unique brook trout spot patterns over a short duration for a mark-recapture study
reason: Primary study applying computer-assisted photo identification (I3S spot pattern matching) to photographs of wild stream brook trout captured and released for a mark-recapture estimate.

title: Automated virtual elephant fence based on detection, alarming, and coordinated redirection of wild elephants
reason: Detection and deterrence system tested only on elephants at the Pinnawala Elephant Orphanage, which the paper calls captive elephants; it does not test wild free-ranging animals.

title: Statistical Modeling based Directional Pattern Design (SMDPD) feature extraction for coral reef classification

title: Rapid assessment of Dreissena population in Lake Erie using underwater videography

title: Flow, force, behaviour: assessment of a prototype hydraulic barrier for invasive fish

title: Comparison of neuronal responses in primate inferior-temporal cortex and feed-forward deep neural network model with regard to information processing of faces
reason: Computational neuroscience study comparing AlexNet layer representations with neuronal recordings from laboratory macaques; the images are face stimuli of monkey and human models shown in a laboratory set-up, not wild or free-ranging animals.

title: A hybridized modified densenet deep architecture with CLAHE algorithm for humpback whale identification and recognition
reason: Primary study proposing a modified DenseNet deep model to identify individual humpback whales from fluke photographs of a Kaggle challenge dataset; the paper describes photo identification of whales in the ocean.

title: Underwater target detection with an attention mechanism and improved scale

title: Animal detection based on deep convolutional neural networks with genetic segmentation
reason: Animal vs non-animal classification evaluated only on a generic salient-object benchmark (ECSSD); no data shown to depict wild, free-ranging animals and no wildlife species or field setting is described.

title: Research on multiple jellyfish classification and detection based on deep learning
reason: Primary study applying CNN classification and Faster R-CNN detection to underwater images of jellyfish and fish, with jellyfish monitoring as the stated application. Images come from ImageNet and a web gallery; the paper does not state whether the animals are wild or captive.

title: An ultra-specific image dataset for automated insect identification
reason: Introduces an image dataset of tiger beetles photographed mostly in their natural habitat and benchmarks image classification algorithms on it.

title: Deep learning algorithm as a strategy for detection an invasive species in uncontrolled environment
venue: Reviews in Fish Biology and Fisheries
reason: Trains and compares CNN object detectors (YOLOv4 tiny, SSD-MobileNet-v2) to detect invasive lionfish in underwater images and videos taken in their natural reef environment.

title: Enhancing the identification accuracy of deep learning object detection using natural language processing
reason: Deep learning object detection combined with NLP to identify wild bird species of Taiwan from social media and mobile app photos.

title: An Infrared Touch System for Automatic Behavior Monitoring
reason: Laboratory behaviour-monitoring system for C57BL6/J mice in a behaviour box (infrared touch frame compared with video tracking); no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Density Estimation of Nemopilema nomurai (Scyphozoa, Rhizostomeae) Using a Drone

reason: Drone images of wild jellyfish swarms at sea are analysed with ImageJ colour thresholding and particle counting to estimate density.

title: Investigations of butterfly species identification from images in natural environments

title: Assessing the detectability of the Irish stoat Mustela erminea hibernica using two camera trap-based survey methods

title: Classification of Marine Plankton Based on Few-shot Learning

reason: Proposes a few-shot CNN method to classify images of marine plankton, including zooplankton sampled from the sea and imaged in situ (ISIIS) or with ZooScan.

title: A fully automatic classification of bee species from wing images
reason: Computer vision classification of bee and wasp species from images of detached forewings mounted between microscope slides; the data show preserved specimen parts in a laboratory set-up, not wild free-ranging animals.

title: Elephant–railway conflict minimisation using real-time video data and machine learning
reason: Computer vision (Haar cascade/AdaBoost) detection of wild elephants in video, crossing railway tracks and entering villages, to reduce elephant-train collisions.

title: Distribution and Abundance of Coastal Elasmobranchs in Tenerife (Canary Islands, NE Atlantic Ocean) with Emphasis on the Bull Ray, Aetomylaeus bovinus

title: catRlog: a photo-identification project management system based in R

title: Assessing the performance of open-source, semi-automated pattern recognition software for harbour seal (P. v. vitulina) photo ID
reason: Primary study evaluating three semi-automated pattern recognition software programmes for individual photo ID of wild harbour seals photographed at haulout sites in Scotland.

title: Advanced image recognition: a fully automated, high-accuracy photo-identification matching system for humpback whales
reason: Primary study developing and evaluating a CNN-based photo-identification algorithm on fluke photographs of free-ranging humpback whales from research catalogs and citizen science.

title: A simple tool for linking photo-identification with multimedia data to track mammal behaviour

title: Female behaviour is differentially associated with specific components of multimodal courtship in ring doves
reason: Domesticated ring doves recorded in a laboratory recording apparatus; no wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Social network stability is impacted by removing a dominant male in replicate dominance hierarchies of a cichlid fish

title: Automating the analysis of fish grazing behaviour from videos using image classification and optical flow
reason: Deep learning and optical flow used to classify grazing behaviour of free-swimming wild luderick in in-situ underwater field videos.

title: Measuring mimicry: methods for quantifying visual similarity

title: Social connectedness and movements among communities of giraffes vary by sex and age class
reason: Field photographs of wild Masai giraffes are individually identified using the pattern-matching program Wild-ID (computer-vision re-identification). The resulting identities feed a social network analysis.

title: Relationship quality underpins pair bond formation and subsequent reproductive performance
reason: Behavioural study of captive-bred zebra finches housed in aviaries; birds are tracked via 2D barcode tags in images. No wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Female–female conflict is higher during periods of parental care in a group-living cichlid fish
reason: Applies Mask R-CNN detection/segmentation and tracking to field underwater video of wild cichlid fish groups in Lake Tanganyika.

title: Toward in situ zooplankton detection with a densely connected YOLOV3 model
reason: Proposes a YOLOv3-based detector for marine zooplankton imaged by in situ/ocean imaging instruments (public EcoTaxa and WHOI-Plankton datasets); wild marine organisms.

title: Does the provision of environmental enrichment affect the behaviour and welfare of captive snakes?
reason: Animal welfare study of captive corn snakes housed at a university; video recordings were coded manually with BORIS and analysed statistically, with no computer vision method. The animals are also captive only.

title: Naturalising diet to reduce stereotypic behaviours in slow lorises rescued from wildlife trade
reason: Behavioural study of captive slow lorises in a rescue centre. Behaviour was recorded by a human observer using continuous sampling, and no image or video analysis was done. The animals are also captive only.

title: The behavioral response of the crab-eating fox to olfactory enrichment
reason: Behavioural study of captive zoo crab-eating foxes; videos were scored manually by an observer, with no computer vision method. The animals are also captive only (E-CAPTIVE).

title: A survey of stereotypic behaviors in tourist camp elephants in Chiang Mai, Thailand
reason: Behavioural survey of captive tourist-camp elephants based on direct observation and mahout questionnaires; no computer vision or image analysis is performed (and animals are captive).

title: Monitoring of free-range rabbits using aerial thermal imaging
reason: Applies a deep learning detector to UAV thermal images to detect and count wild rabbits in fields on Lemnos.

title: Effects of human-altered landscapes on a reintroduced ungulate: Patterns of habitat selection at the rangeland-wildland interface
reason: Elk and cattle in satellite images were located and classified manually by a trained observer. The study has no automated computer vision method; the analysis is ecological habitat-selection modelling.

title: Identifying optimal wavelengths to maximise the detection rates of marine fauna from aerial surveys

title: Involving fishers in scaling up the restoration of cold-water coral gardens on the Mediterranean continental shelf
reason: An AUV took video and geo-referenced photo-mosaics of wild cold-water gorgonians, both restored transplants and a natural control population. title: Micro-scale fragmentation of the alpine meadow landscape on the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau under external disturbances
reason: Image analysis classifies UAV images into bare and healthy meadow patches (land cover) for landscape fragmentation metrics; pika burrows were mapped by manual visual interpretation, so animals are not the subject of the computer vision.

title: Relationships between dietary breadth and flexibility in jaw movement: A case study of two recently diverged insular populations of Podarcis lizards
venue: Comparative Biochemistry and Physiology Part A Molecular & Integrative Physiology
reason: The lizards were caught in the wild but kept in captivity. Their feeding was filmed in a laboratory set-up with high-speed cameras, and the jaw points were digitised by hand for a study of feeding kinematics. No images of free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Anipose: A toolkit for robust markerless 3D pose estimation
reason: 3D pose estimation toolkit evaluated on laboratory mice, tethered laboratory fruit flies, a calibration board and a human dataset; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Small-sample learning with salient-region detection and center neighbor loss for insect recognition in real-world complex scenarios
reason: Proposes a small-sample, fine-grained CNN classification method for 220 insect species from real-world images taken in natural scenes (crawled from iNaturalist).

title: Aquatic organism recognition using residual network with inner feature and kernel calibration module
reason: CNN classification of aquatic organism images; some images come from an underwater vehicle in the sea off Qingdao (wild animals), others from aquariums and the internet.

title: Forest pest identification based on a new dataset and convolutional neural network model with enhancement strategy
reason: CNN classification of images of 67 forest insect pests. These are non-domestic insects in forests, not crop pests in production or lab animals. The paper does not say where the images came from.

title: Deep learning-based framework for cardiac function assessment in embryonic zebrafish from heart beating videos
reason: Deep learning segmentation of the heart ventricle in bright-field microscopy videos of laboratory zebrafish embryos (biomedical model organism); no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Fine-grained classification of fly species in the natural environment based on deep convolutional neural network
reason: Proposes a CNN fine-grained classification method for fly species photographed in the natural environment (web and IP102 images), relevant to invasive species monitoring.

title: Decreasing body lengths in North Atlantic right whales
reason: Aerial photogrammetry (image-based length measurement) and photo-identification of free-ranging North Atlantic right whales from crewed aircraft and drone images.

title: Robust optical flow estimation to enhance behavioral research on ants
reason: Proposes an optical flow (computer vision) method to estimate the motion of ants filmed outdoors. Ants are non-domestic and were recorded outdoors, not in a lab or enclosure.

title: Megabenthic assemblages on bathyal escarpments off the west Corsican margin (Western Mediterranean)
venue: Deep Sea Research Part I Oceanographic Research Papers
reason: The authors took ROV still images of wild deep-sea megabenthos and built 3D photogrammetric reconstructions from them, then used the models to locate and count organisms. title: Identification of animals and recognition of their actions in wildlife videos using deep learning techniques
reason: Primary study applying deep-learning detection, instance segmentation and action recognition to camera-trap videos of free-ranging wild mammals at a wildlife crossing in Germany.

title: Learning niche features to improve image-based species identification
reason: Proposes a joint image deep learning and niche model (NicheNet) to classify images of wild Chinese Galliformes taken by researchers and citizen scientists.

title: Large-scale zero-shot learning in the wild: Classifying zoological illustrations
reason: The images are digitised 19th-century zoological illustrations held in museum and library archives. They are not images or video of free-ranging animals; E-CAPTIVE is the closest criterion because it covers museum specimens.

title: Animal reidentification using restricted set classification
reason: The only data is a stock video of ornamental koi carp in a fish pond. Koi are domestic decorative fish, not wild or free-ranging animals.

title: A quantitative detection algorithm based on improved faster R-CNN for marine benthos
reason: Proposes an improved Faster R-CNN to detect and count wild marine benthos (scallops, starfish) in seafloor images from HabCam towed underwater vehicles.

title: Exploring the potential to use low cost imaging and an open source convolutional neural network detector to support stock assessment of the king scallop (Pecten maximus)
reason: Applies CNN detectors to underwater seabed images of live king scallops placed on natural seabed in Scottish bays; primary research on marine wildlife.

title: Applying object detection to marine data and exploring explainability of a fully convolutional neural network using principal component analysis
reason: Applies YOLOv3 to detect wild fish in underwater images from a seafloor station in a Norwegian fjord, and examines the network's feature maps with PCA.

title: Deep learning approach to classify Tiger beetles of Sri Lanka
reason: CNN classification of tiger beetle genera from images that include live beetles photographed in their natural habitats, along with curated specimens photographed in laboratories.

title: Online computational ethology based on modern IT infrastructure
reason: The only image data shows captive banded mongooses in a zoo enclosure. The wild bat case uses ultrasonic audio recordings only, so no wild animals appear in image or video data.

title: Automatic underwater fish species classification with limited data using few-shot learning

title: Automatic interpretation of salmon scales using deep learning
reason: The CNN analyses images of scale samples taken from salmon (wild and farmed escapees). These are images of tissue samples, not of free-ranging animals or their direct field signs, so the paper is closer to lab-based specimen analysis.

title: Desert bighorn sheep (Ovis canadensis) recognition from camera traps based on learned features
reason: Primary study applying CNN-feature-based image classification to camera-trap images of wild desert bighorn sheep and co-occurring wild species in a protected area in Mexico.

title: A systematic study of the class imbalance problem: Automatically identifying empty camera trap images using convolutional neural networks
reason: Applies a CNN to classify camera trap images of wild animals in Serengeti National Park as empty or animal, studying class imbalance.

title: Image Filtering and Labelling Assistant (IFLA): Expediting the analysis of data obtained from camera traps
reason: Develops and evaluates an image-differencing software tool to find animals in camera-trap images of wild animals from a field monitoring project.

title: Saving costs for video data annotation in wildlife monitoring
reason: Proposes an automatic annotation strategy (Mask R-CNN + Tracktor) for camera trap videos of wild mammals at a wildlife crossing in Germany.

title: Dynamic β-VAEs for quantifying biodiversity by clustering optically recorded insect signals

title: Using a two-stage convolutional neural network to rapidly identify tiny herbivorous beetles in the field
reason: Two-stage CNN detection and species identification of free-living Phyllotreta flea beetles in field photographs and video from an outdoor field garden; primary research.

title: Underwater object detection based on bi-dimensional empirical mode decomposition and Gaussian Mixture Model approach
reason: Proposes a BEMD-GMM computer vision method for detecting fish in underwater video sequences from benchmark datasets of natural underwater scenes.

title: Automatic animal identification from drone camera based on point pattern analysis of herd behaviour
reason: Drone video of wild herbivores in two protected areas in Botswana, analysed with object detection models and point pattern classification for species identification.

title: Camera traps and artificial intelligence for monitoring invasive species and emerging diseases
reason: Short perspective letter that sets out a conceptual framework combining camera traps, citizen science, AI and wireless technology. It contains no primary image analysis or experiments.

title: Identification and measurement of tropical tuna species in purse seiner catches using computer vision and deep learning
reason: Primary study applying deep-learning segmentation, species classification and size estimation to images of wild-caught tropical tuna on the conveyor belt of commercial purse seiners (electronic monitoring of a wild-capture fishery, not aquaculture).

title: Performance of iSharkFin in the identification of wet dorsal fins from priority shark species
reason: Image-based machine learning identification of species from photographs of wet dorsal fins of wild-caught sharks in fisheries landings; primary evaluation study.

title: InsectCV: A system for insect detection in the lab from trap images
reason: Crop pest monitoring: dead trapped aphids and parasitoids from wheat-field traps are scanned in the lab to support integrated pest management; no images of live free-ranging animals.

title: Automated classification of bat echolocation call recordings with artificial intelligence
reason: The data are acoustic zero-cross recordings of bat echolocation calls; the images classified are frequency-over-time plots generated from sound, not images or video of animals.

title: A novel feature descriptor based coral image classification using extreme learning machine with ameliorated chimp optimization algorithm
reason: Proposes a texture feature descriptor with an optimized ELM classifier for classifying underwater coral reef images (wild marine invertebrates) from public coral datasets.

title: Improving wildlife tracking using 3D information

title: Overcoming the distance estimation bottleneck in estimating animal abundance with camera traps
reason: Proposes an automated computer vision pipeline (monocular depth estimation plus animal detection) to estimate camera-to-animal distances in camera trap videos of wild animals in a conservation area.

title: Building of an edge enabled drone network ecosystem for bird species identification
reason: Bird species are classified from MFCC features of xeno-canto audio recordings. The drone flights are only simulated, and no images or video are analysed.

title: Bird posture recognition based on target keypoints estimation in dual-task convolutional neural networks

title: Underwater target detection based on Faster R-CNN and adversarial occlusion network
reason: The authors propose a CNN detection method and test it on underwater robot images of sea cucumbers, sea urchins, starfish and scallops from a deep-sea fishing ground. These are free-living marine invertebrates. The paper does not say they are farmed.

title: Object and behavior differentiation for improved automated counts of migrating river fish using imaging sonar data
reason: Automated detection, tracking and counting of wild migrating river fish in multibeam imaging sonar video (ARIS) from a river monitoring site; image/video-based processing of wild animals.

title: Use of manned submersible and autonomous stereo-camera array to assess forage fish and associated subtidal habitat
reason: Stereo-camera images of wild Pacific sand lance in situ are analysed (stereo triangulation, counting, length measurement) to assess a wild forage fish population.

title: Automatic, operational, high-resolution monitoring of fish length and catch numbers from landings using deep learning
reason: Computer vision is applied to images of dead, landed dolphinfish in boxes at a commercial fish auction (fishery landings monitoring); no images of wild, free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Comparing workflow application designs for high resolution satellite image analysis

title: Giant panda behaviour recognition using images

title: Using UAVs to assess the relationship between alpine meadow bare patches and disturbance by pikas in the source region of Yellow River on the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau
reason: Applies image analysis to UAV aerial photos to detect and count burrow holes (direct signs) of wild plateau pikas in alpine meadows and relate them to bare patches.

title: Persistence of a locally endangered mouse-deer amidst the re-emergence of two larger ungulates in small urban rainforest fragments
reason: Ecological camera-trap study of wild ungulates in Singapore. Videos are analysed with statistical models (random encounter model, GLM, occupancy models, activity overlap); no computer vision or automated image analysis is applied.

title: The use of drone-based aerial photogrammetry in population monitoring of Southern Giant Petrels in ASMA 1, King George Island, maritime Antarctica
reason: Drone-based aerial photogrammetry (orthophoto generation from image series) used to count and monitor wild Southern Giant Petrel adults, chicks and nests in Antarctica; primary research with image data of wild animals.

title: Application of IOT and machine learning in crop protection against animal intrusion
reason: Applies CNN detectors (R-CNN, SSD) to images of animals intruding on crop fields, including wild species (zebra, cheetah, elephant) alongside domestic cow and horse; human-wildlife conflict application.

title: Deep Learning based Detection, Segmentation and Counting of Benthic Megafauna in Unconstrained Underwater Environments
reason: Deep learning detection, segmentation and counting of wild benthic megafauna in towed-camera seafloor imagery from the Weddell Sea.

title: CIRAL: a hybrid active learning framework for plankon taxa labeling
reason: Proposes an active learning framework for classifying plankton taxa images (Kaggle NDSB plankton dataset) to reduce expert labelling effort for in-situ underwater plankton analysis; the application domain is free-living marine plankton.

title: Optical sensing in Tibet Plateau wildlife observation based on tethered balloon
reason: Thermal video of wild Tibetan antelopes from a tethered balloon, processed with frame differencing for motion detection and counting.

title: Bumblebees land rapidly and robustly using a sophisticated modular flight control strategy
reason: Bumblebees from a commercially supplied colony were trained to fly in an indoor flight arena and tracked there with machine vision. This is a laboratory set-up, not wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Automatic large scale detection of red palm weevil infestation using street view images

title: Multi-level residual network VGGNet for fish species classification

reason: Proposes a CNN (MLR-VGGNet) for fish species classification, evaluated partly on the Fish4-Knowledge dataset of live fish filmed underwater in the open sea.

title: Phylogenetic morphometrics, geometric morphometrics and the Mexican fossils to understand evolutionary trends of enchodontid fishes
venue: Journal of South American Earth Sciences
reason: Palaeontological study of fossil museum specimens. Landmarks were digitised by hand and analysed with geometric and phylogenetic morphometrics; no computer vision method was developed or applied, and the animals are not living wild animals.

title: An explainable deep vision system for animal classification and detection in trail-camera images with automatic post-deployment retraining
reason: Primary study developing a CNN pipeline for animal/no-animal classification and bird detection in trail-camera images of free-ranging wildlife at field sites in Texas.

title: The role of the vegetation structure, primary productivity and senescence derived from airborne LiDAR and hyperspectral data for birds diversity and rarity on a restored site
reason: Bird data come from field point counts by ornithologists (sight or sound); the airborne LiDAR and hyperspectral data are used only to derive vegetation structure and indices as predictors in boosted regression trees. No image analysis of animals is performed.

title: Integrating remote sensing methods during controlled exposure experiments to quantify group responses of dolphins to navy sonar
reason: Drone aerial images of free-ranging long-beaked common dolphins are analysed by photogrammetry. Individuals are located and tracked across frames and projected to geographic coordinates to measure group movement responses to sonar.

title: One-stage CNN detector-based benthonic organisms detection with limited training dataset
reason: Detection of benthic organisms (echinus, scallop, starfish, holothurian) for harvesting by fishing robots in marine ranching, i.e., an aquaculture/production application rather than wildlife.

title: Automated classification of fauna in seabed photographs: The impact of training and validation dataset size, with considerations for the class imbalance
reason: Applies a CNN classifier to crops of wild benthic invertebrate megafauna in seabed photographs taken by an AUV at an abyssal plain observatory; primary research.

reason: Ecological study of zooplankton community composition; the animal images are laboratory Zooscan scans of formaldehyde-preserved net samples, classified semi-automatically in Ecotaxa. No images of live free-ranging animals are analysed (UVP5 in situ imaging is used only for particle flux).

title: Honey sources: neural network approach to bee species classification
reason: Primary study applying object detection and species classification (Faster R-CNN) to crowdsourced photographs of bees in their natural environment.

reason: Applies CoralNet machine-learning image classification to field photoquadrats of wild coral reef benthic communities (hard corals, soft corals) in Indonesia to estimate cover.

title: Vector mosquito image classification using novel RIFS feature selection and machine learning models for disease epidemiology
reason: Computer vision classification of images of non-domestic disease-vector mosquitoes (Aedes, Culex). The paper does not say whether the images show wild-caught, lab-reared or specimen mosquitoes.

title: Underwater dual-magnification imaging for automated lake plankton monitoring
reason: Presents an in-situ underwater imaging system with image processing and a CNN classifier for lake plankton; wild zooplankton are imaged in Lake Greifensee, alongside laboratory cultures used for calibration.

title: Satellite Remote Sensing of Herring (Clupea pallasii) Spawning Events: A Case Study in the Strait of Georgia

title: Rapid phenotypic change in a polymorphic salamander over 43 years

title: Automating the assessment of biofouling in images using expert agreement as a gold standard

title: Zebrafish tracking using YOLOv2 and Kalman filter

reason: CNN classification of bumble bee species from community-science photographs of free-ranging bumble bees in North America, aimed at pollinator conservation and monitoring.

reason: Mosquito samples are imaged individually in a Petri dish inside a purpose-built imaging device (Aedes Detector) under controlled illumination; no images of wild, free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Monitoring abundance of aggregated animals (Florida manatees) using an unmanned aerial system (UAS)

title: Mosquito species identification using convolutional neural networks with a multitiered ensemble model for novel species detection

title: Hyperspectral data as a biodiversity screening tool can differentiate among diverse Neotropical fishes
reason: Data are point reflectance spectra from a contact-probe spectroradiometer, not images or video, so there is no image analysis. The fish came from the pet trade or were measured in holding aquaria and labs after collection.

reason: Individual identification of farmed Atlantic salmon photographed in a photo tent and aquarium at an aquaculture research facility; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Weakly supervised underwater fish segmentation using affinity LCFCN

title: DeepLabStream enables closed-loop behavioral experiments using deep learning-based markerless, real-time posture detection
reason: Real-time pose estimation of laboratory C57BL/6 mice in indoor arenas for closed-loop neuroscience experiments; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Evaluation of the use of drones to monitor a diverse crocodylian assemblage in West Africa
reason: Drone survey of wild crocodiles; images were only mosaicked and crocodiles were counted visually by human observers. No automated computer vision analysis was performed.

title: Drone thermal imaging technology provides a cost-effective tool for landscape-scale monitoring of a cryptic forest-dwelling species across all population densities

title: Size structure of broadnose sevengill sharks ( Notorynchus cepedianus ) in Sawdust Bay, Rakiura/Stewart Island, estimated using underwater stereo‐photogrammetry

reason: Primary study that trains CNN patch classifiers on aerial survey photographs to detect wild Cumberland Sound belugas for population counts.

title: Quantifying plant mimesis in fossil insects using deep learning
reason: Deep learning (Siamese CNN) applied to images of wild extant insects from iNaturalist and fossil insect specimens to quantify plant mimesis.

title: Introducing Theil-Sen estimator for sun glint correction of UAV data for coral mapping

title: A screening approach for the correction of distortion in UAV data for coral community mapping
reason: Primary study that classifies UAV multispectral imagery of wild reef corals (patch, branching and tabular coral growth forms) with machine learning. Borderline with benthic habitat mapping, but the mapped classes are coral animals in situ.

title: Activity Budget and Postural Behaviors in Orangutans on Bukit Merah Orang Utan Island for Assessing Captive Great Ape Welfare

reason: Behavioural study of semi-captive orangutans in enclosures. The data come from direct focal-animal observation, with no image or video analysis.

title: Silence is Golden: Auditory Preferences in Zoo-housed Gorillas

reason: Behavioural study of auditory preferences in zoo-housed gorillas using touchscreen choices; no image or video analysis or computer vision is performed.

title: Using object-based image analysis to detect laughing gull nests
reason: Primary study applying object-based image analysis to aerial imagery to detect nests (direct signs) of a wild, free-ranging laughing gull colony in a salt marsh.

title: Spatio-temporal distribution ofGymnocypris przewalskiiduring migration with UAV-based photogrammetry and deep neural network
reason: Primary study applying a U-net deep neural network and SfM photogrammetry to UAV images of wild migrating naked carp in a river back channel.

title: Research on Recognition Technology of Amur Tiger Gait Features Based on Video

title: An Automated Mammals Detection Based on SSD-Mobile Net
reason: Generic mammal vs. no-animal object detection on images taken from a standard benchmark (Caltech 101) and the internet; classes include pets (dog, cat) and wildlife is not the stated subject or application, and the paper does not state that the animals are wild or free-ranging.

title: Research on The Method of Grass Mouse Hole Target Detection Based on Deep Learning
reason: Deep learning detection of rodent burrows (direct signs of wild animals) in grassland UAV and phone images.

reason: Primary study training a CNN to classify web-crawled images of snub-nosed monkeys versus other monkeys for rare-animal conservation. title: Remote sensing for coral reef and seagrass cover mapping to support coastal management of small islands

reason: Satellite-based benthic habitat mapping (coral reef, seagrass, macroalgae, substrate classes); habitat/land-cover mapping, not analysis of animals.

reason: Primary study applying CNN image classification to three non-domestic catfish genera (Siluriformes) for biodiversity identification. title: Smart aerial monitoring system to prevent human wildlife intervention

title: BettaNet: A Deep Learning Architecture for Classification of Wild Siamese Betta Species

reason: Images of betta fish photographed through glass at a pet market and a betta fish contest in Bangkok; animals are captive/kept, not free-ranging.

reason: Editorial/perspective introducing a special section on citizen science and community-based monitoring; no computer vision or image analysis.

title: A deep learning-based method to identify and count pelagic and mesopelagic fishes from trawl camera images
reason: Deep learning object detection (RetinaNet) applied to in-trawl camera images of wild pelagic and mesopelagic fishes collected during survey cruises in the Northeast Atlantic.

title: Combined video–hydroacoustic survey of nearshore semi-pelagic rockfish in untrawlable habitats
reason: Wild rockfish were filmed with an underwater stereo video system, but species identification, counts and length measurements were done by human reviewers in EventMeasure software. title: Pretrained Convolutional Neural Networks Perform Well in a Challenging Test Case: Identification of Plant Bugs (Hemiptera: Miridae) Using a Small Number of Training Images
reason: CNN-based species identification of plant bugs (Miridae). Most data are pinned museum specimens, but the paper also tests on field photographs of live insects from iNaturalist and BugGuide, so part of the data shows wild animals.

reason: Termites were collected from field colonies but all analysed images were taken in a controlled laboratory set-up (acrylic ring on a black panel); no images show free-ranging animals in situ.

title: Drones and deep learning produce accurate and efficient monitoring of large-scale seabird colonies
reason: Primary study applying CNN object detection to drone imagery of wild breeding seabird colonies (albatrosses and penguins) in the Falkland Islands.

title: Exceptional variation in the appearance of Common Murre eggs reveals their potential as identity signals
reason: Image analysis (colour measurement and thresholding) of photographs of eggs laid by free-living Common Murres on Skomer Island; eggs are direct signs of wild animals.

title: High-throughput visual assessment of sleep stages in mice using machine learning
reason: Video-based sleep stage classification of laboratory mice in home cages with implanted EEG/EMG electrodes; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Image-Based Automated Species Identification: Can Virtual Data Augmentation Overcome Problems of Insufficient Sampling?
reason: Images are of dissected genitalia of collection specimens of scarab beetles; no images of wild, free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Identification of Species by Combining Molecular and Morphological Data Using Convolutional Neural Networks
reason: Only one figure page of the paper is available. title: Forecasting dynamic body weight of nonrestrained pigs from images using an RGB-D sensor camera
reason: Computer vision pipeline for predicting body weight of domestic pigs housed in a swine facility; livestock, no wild animals.

title: Automatic identification of bird females using egg phenotype

reason: Image analysis (pattern, shape, luminance) of photographs of eggs laid by wild common cuckoo females in host nests, used with machine learning to identify the individual laying female; eggs are treated as direct signs of wild birds.

title: A Deep Learning‐based Computer Vision Approach for Comparative Monarch Butterfly Phenotype Identification in Citizen Science
reason: Presents a web-collected image dataset of monarch butterflies and five look-alike species and trains a CNN classifier for conservation monitoring; the paper does not state whether the photographed butterflies are wild or captive.

title: Raptor wing morphing with flight speed

reason: 3D photogrammetric reconstruction of captive-bred, trained raptors gliding in an indoor flight corridor; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Re-identification of individuals from images using spot constellations: a case study in Arctic charr (Salvelinus alpinus)
reason: Develops a computer vision pipeline (U-Net segmentation and spot-constellation matching) to re-identify individual wild Arctic charr from photographs taken during a capture-mark-recapture study in Icelandic lava caves.

title: Integrating real-time data analysis into automatic tracking of social insects
reason: Real-time video tracking of tagged ants from a colony fragment kept in the laboratory, filmed in an artificial acrylic arena; no images of wild, free-ranging animals.

title: Domestic egg-laying hens,Gallus gallus domesticus, do not modulate flapping flight performance in response to wing condition
