title: A multi‐state occupancy model to non‐invasively monitor visible signs of wildlife health with camera traps that accounts for image quality
reason: Borderline include. Camera-trap images of free-ranging urban coyotes; species and mange were labelled manually, but an OpenCV Laplacian-variance blur metric was computed on every image and used as a detection covariate in the occupancy model.

title: Eagle fatalities are reduced by automated curtailment of wind turbines
reason: Field evaluation of a deployed automated camera system (IdentiFlight) that detects, tracks and classifies free-flying birds as eagle/non-eagle to curtail wind turbines; outcome measured as wild eagle fatalities. Borderline because the authors analyse carcass counts, not images.

title: Assessing the camera trap methodologies used to estimate density of unmarked populations
reason: Compares three statistical density estimators (REM, REST, CT-DS) on camera trap data from wild populations; images were processed manually and no computer vision or automated image analysis is applied.

title: Estimation of body weight in captive Amur tigers (Panthera tigris altaica)
reason: Image-based body weight estimation of Amur tigers that were all bred and reared in captivity in the Siberian Tiger Park; no wild animals in the analysed data.

title: DiversityScanner: Robotic handling of small invertebrates with machine learning methods
reason: CNN classification and image-based detection/measurement of ethanol-preserved insects collected with Malaise traps in the field in Germany and Italy; the animals are wild-caught invertebrates imaged as preserved specimens in a robot, not museum specimens.

title: Spot size, distance and emissivity errors in field applications of infrared thermography
reason: Methodological study of measurement error in infrared thermography (distance, spot size, emissivity). Temperatures are read from manually drawn ROIs in thermal images, with no computer vision method for detecting, classifying or analysing animals.

title: Robust ecological analysis of camera trap data labelled by a machine learning model
reason: Primary study that trains and evaluates a CNN species classifier on camera trap images of wild Central African forest mammals and birds, and tests the labels in ecological analyses.

title: Revisiting animal photo‐identification using deep metric learning and network analysis
reason: Primary study developing a CNN/SIFT pipeline for individual re-identification of wild giraffes photographed in Hwange National Park.

title: A motion‐detection based camera trap for small nocturnal mammals with low latency and high signal‐to‐noise ratio
reason: Primary study that builds a camera trap triggered by image-based motion detection (frame differencing) and deploys it on wild flying squirrels at wooded field sites. Borderline for E-NOCV: the only image analysis is the motion-detection trigger, and capture events were categorised manually.

title: Innovations in movement and behavioural ecology from camera traps: Day range as model parameter
reason: Camera-trap study of wild mammals, but no image analysis is done: animal positions and speeds are obtained manually from the images, and the 'machine learning procedure' (k-means clustering plus log-normal mixture models) is applied to speed values to separate movement behaviours and estimate day range.

title: PICT: A low‐cost, modular, open‐source camera trap system to study plant–insect interactions
reason: Primary study presenting a DIY camera trap for filming wild insects visiting flowers in Cameroon; the videos are filtered with motion-detection algorithms (classical image analysis) in post-processing, then insects are identified manually.

title: Understanding the reliability of citizen science observational data using item response models
reason: The paper proposes Bayesian spatial item response models to estimate citizen scientists' abilities and item difficulties from manual classifications of Serengeti camera-trap images. No computer vision or automated image analysis is applied.

title: BatRack: An open‐source multi‐sensor device for wildlife research
reason: Multi-sensor device for wild bats; video recordings are only manually screened, automated analysis applies to audio and VHF signals, not to images.

title: A method for low‐cost, low‐impact insect tracking using retroreflective tags
reason: Camera-based detection and tracking of retroreflector-tagged wild bees foraging in the field; image subtraction plus SVM classifier. Also includes workers from a commercial nest.

title: Sashimi : A toolkit for facilitating high‐throughput organismal image segmentation using deep learning
reason: Trains and evaluates a Mask R-CNN segmentation model on fish images: standardized digitized specimen photographs plus naturalistic iNaturalist images of fish in their natural contexts, so part of the data shows wild animals.

title: Tracking wildlife energy dynamics with unoccupied aircraft systems and three‐dimensional photogrammetry
reason: Primary study applying structure-from-motion 3-D photogrammetry to drone imagery of free-living grey seals to measure body volume and estimate mass.

title: Cost‐effective seafloor habitat mapping using a portable speedy sea scanner and deep‐learning‐based segmentation: A sea trial at Pujada Bay, Philippines
reason: Applies U-Net segmentation to seafloor orthophotos from a towed camera array to estimate cover of wild corals and sea urchins (plus seagrass) in Pujada Bay.

title: Hierarchy‐guided neural network for species classification
reason: Species classification of fish from images of preserved museum collection specimens; no images of wild, free-ranging animals.

title: Bulk arthropod abundance, biomass and diversity estimation using deep learning for computer vision
reason: Images show dead, ethanol-preserved arthropod specimens from Malaise traps, photographed in petri dishes and trays in a laboratory set-up; no images of live free-ranging animals.

title: Deep learning and satellite imagery predict genetic diversity and differentiation
reason: A CNN is applied to satellite image sections of coastal dune landscape to predict population genetic metrics (FST, allele richness) of a rodent; the images show habitat/landscape only, not animals or their direct signs.

title: Argos: A toolkit for tracking multiple animals in complex visual environments
reason: Presents a computer vision toolkit for multi-animal tracking, tested on stock videos of animals in natural settings (elephants, birds, sparrows) as well as on laboratory locusts and flies, dogs and horses.

title: Leveraging social media and deep learning to detect rare megafauna in video surveys
reason: Primary study training an object-detection CNN on social media drone videos and field aerial video surveys to detect wild dugongs.

title: On the importance of defendable resources for social evolution: Applying new techniques to a long‐standing question
reason: Computer vision (SfM/MVS reconstruction and Mask R-CNN stone segmentation) is applied only to the habitat (stones and sand) in underwater video. Fish counts came from direct visual surveys by divers, not from image analysis. Because the animals are not the subject of the image analysis, the paper falls under habitat-only.

title: Deciphering choreographies of elaborate courtship displays of golden‐collared manakins using markerless motion capture
reason: Primary study applying CNN-based markerless tracking and multi-camera 3D reconstruction to field video of wild golden-collared manakins performing courtship displays in Panamanian rainforest.

title: Internet of things‐based deeply proficient monitoring and protection system for crop field
reason: IoT crop field protection system focused on agricultural production (crop disease detection and generic animal/bird intrusion alerts in farmed fields); animals are unspecified intruders and wildlife is not the stated subject.

title: Rapid drone semi‐automated counts of wintering Greater Flamingos (Phoenicopterus roseus) as a tool for amateur researchers
reason: Primary study applying semi-automated image analysis (ImageJ) to drone imagery of wild wintering Greater Flamingos to count them, compared with ground counts.

title: Estimating bird flight height using 3‐D photogrammetry
reason: Primary study developing a stereophotogrammetric (image-based 3-D reconstruction) approach to measure flight heights of free-flying wild birds photographed in the field.

title: Sensory‐based quantification of male colour patterns in Trinidadian guppies reveals no support for parallel phenotypic evolution in multivariate trait space
reason: Wild-caught guppies were photographed live in a custom UV-transparent chamber after being held in laboratory aquaria. The image analysis (QCPA colour pattern quantification) was therefore done only in a laboratory set-up, not on free-ranging animals in the field.

title: Drone photogrammetry allows refinement of acoustically derived length estimation for male sperm whales
reason: Drone photogrammetry of free-ranging sperm whales in which total length is measured manually by an operator marking points in a MATLAB GUI; no automated computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated. The main analysis is a regression of acoustic interpulse interval against length.

title: Sexually dimorphic measurements from stranded and bycaught specimens contribute to the characterization of group composition in free‐ranging common dolphins (Delphinus spp.) from aerial images
reason: The main analysis uses tape measurements from stranded and bycaught specimens. The drone part is one example image of free-ranging dolphins measured by hand with photogrammetry. No computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Influence of krill ( Euphausia superba ) availability on humpback whale ( Megaptera novaeangliae ) reproductive rate
reason: Ecological study correlating krill acoustic density with humpback whale birth rates from visual vessel surveys; photo-identification is manual, and the paper uses no computer vision method.

title: Use of satellite imagery to identify southern right whales (Eubalaena australis) on a Southwest Atlantic Ocean breeding ground
reason: Primary study that detects and counts wild southern right whales in satellite images by visual interpretation and QGIS pixel-classification plug-ins, checked against aerial survey data.

title: finFindR : Automated recognition and identification of marine mammal dorsal fins using residual convolutional neural networks
reason: Primary study developing a CNN-based photo-identification tool for free-ranging bottlenose dolphins from field survey photographs.

title: Lords of the Rings: Mud ring feeding by bottlenose dolphins in a Caribbean estuary revealed from sea, air, and space
reason: Behavioural note on dolphin mud ring feeding. Satellite, aerial, UAV and boat imagery was searched and reviewed visually by people; no computer vision method is applied.

title: Stressed and slim or relaxed and chubby? A simultaneous assessment of gray whale body condition and hormone variability
reason: Drone-video photogrammetry is used to measure the body condition (Body Area Index) of wild gray whales, and these measurements are related to fecal hormones.

title: Relative influence of predators, competitors and seascape heterogeneity on behaviour and abundance of coral reef mesopredators
reason: Ecological study of wild coral reef fishes using stereo-BRUV video, but videos were annotated manually by human annotators (MaxN, behaviours) and analysed with GAMMs; no computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Awakening a taxonomist's third eye: exploring the utility of computer vision and deep learning in insect systematics
reason: Opinion piece with a case study classifying pinned museum specimens of Oxythyrea beetles; no wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Feathers dataset for fine-grained visual categorization
reason: Images show feathers from collectors' feather collections (specimens) photographed and posted online, not free-ranging animals in the wild; specimen data falls under E-CAPTIVE.

title: Self-organization in natural swarms of Photinus carolinus synchronous fireflies
reason: Primary study that video-records natural swarms of wild fireflies in a national park and uses image analysis (intensity thresholding, stereo triangulation, 3D reconstruction, streak matching) to localise flashes.

title: Automated audiovisual behavior recognition in wild primates
reason: Primary study developing a deep CNN pipeline for detection, tracking and audiovisual action recognition of wild chimpanzees in camera trap and camcorder video.

title: Big or small, patchy all: Resolution of marine plankton patch structure at micro- to submesoscales for 36 taxa
reason: Applies CNN classification to in situ underwater images of wild marine plankton (including larval fishes and zooplankton) to study patch structure.

title: Operational Video Surveillance of the Vertical Distribution of Zooplankton in Situ
reason: Describes the hardware of a probe video system for watching zooplankton in situ in the Kara Sea. The images are only assessed visually by an operator; no computer vision or automated image analysis is applied.

title: Automated Visual Large Scale Monitoring of Faunal Biodiversity
reason: Primary study developing computer vision for automated biodiversity monitoring stations: RGB-D camera-trap instance segmentation and tracking (evaluated on zoo deer) and detection and classification of moths attracted to a light-trap screen. Wild-origin of the moth images is not stated explicitly, so inclusion rests on the light-trap moth scanner being the stated image source.

title: A New Method for Calculating the Population Density of Terrestrial Animals Using Camera Traps with an Assessment of the Roe Deer (Capreolus pygargus Pallas, 1771) (Cervidae, Mammalia) Population Density in Khingan Nature Reserve as an Example
reason: Statistical method for estimating population density from camera-trap video records of wild roe deer; registrations and residence times are tabulated without any computer vision or automated image analysis.

title: Foraging modes and movements of Oncorhynchus mykiss as flow and invertebrate drift recede in a California stream
venue: Canadian Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences
reason: Field study of wild juvenile O. mykiss in a California stream using stereo GoPro video and 3-D videogrammetry (VidSync triangulation) to track foraging movement and score foraging modes.

title: Early lessons in deploying cameras and artificial intelligence technology for fisheries catch monitoring: where machine learning meets commercial fishing
venue: Canadian Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences
reason: Primary study applying CNN detection and tracking to on-vessel video of wild-caught fish and bycatch in a commercial longline fishery (wild capture, not aquaculture).

title: Video analysis for the detection of animals using convolutional neural networks and consumer-grade drones
reason: Proof-of-concept drone detection of rhinos and cars; the field trial and the authors' own data come from a safari park rhino enclosure, supplemented by Google/YouTube images whose wild status is not established. No data clearly shows wild, free-ranging animals.

title: Individual Identification Method of Leopard in Multiple Scenarios
reason: Proposes a CNN-based individual re-identification method for leopards using images from a wild animal park and protected areas, partly taken in the wild.

title: Bio Sketchbook
reason: The system recognises and sketches plants photographed by children in a botanical park; no animal images are analysed.

title: ElephantBook: A Semi-Automated Human-in-the-Loop System for Elephant Re-Identification
venue: ACM SIGCAS Conference on Computing and Sustainable Societies (COMPASS)
reason: Human-in-the-loop system combining manual attribute coding with computer vision (ear detection and contour matching) to re-identify wild African elephants from ranger photographs; deployed in the Greater Mara Ecosystem.

title: Authoring Platform for Mobile Citizen Science Apps with Client-side ML
venue: ACM Conference on Computer-Supported Cooperative Work and Social Computing (CSCW)
reason: Platform paper applying client-side object detection to images of seals and sea lions (marine wildlife) for biodiversity citizen science, alongside a non-animal rip current use case.

title: Scaling Biodiversity Monitoring for the Data Age
venue: XRDS Crossroads The ACM Magazine for Students
reason: Magazine feature/perspective article discussing challenges and opportunities of machine learning for biodiversity monitoring; no primary experiments or image analysis performed.

title: Underwater target detection system based on YOLO v4
reason: Applies YOLO v4 to detect fish (clownfish, snapper) in underwater images/video from the Labeled Fishes in the Wild dataset captured by an underwater ROV.

title: Chinese White Dolphin Detection in the Wild
reason: Develops a deep-learning detection system and dataset for wild Chinese White Dolphins filmed from survey vessels.

title: Effective Insect Recognition Based on Deep Neural Network Models in Complex Background
venue: International Conference on High Performance Compilation, Computing and Communications (HP3C)
reason: CNN classification of insect images including images taken in the natural ecological environment, alongside specimen and web images.

title: RAMS-Trans: Recurrent Attention Multi-scale Transformer for Fine-grained Image Recognition
venue: ACM International Conference on Multimedia (ACM MM)
reason: This is a generic fine-grained image recognition method (a transformer). It is only evaluated on general FGIR benchmarks (CUB-200-2011, Stanford Dogs, iNaturalist2017). Wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Underwater Species Detection using Channel Sharpening Attention
venue: ACM International Conference on Multimedia (ACM MM)
reason: Underwater detection of cultured aquatic products (sea cucumbers, sea urchins, scallops) for fishing/aquaculture robots; framed as aquaculture production, not wild animals.

title: Classification of Starling Image Using Artificial Neural Networks
venue: International Conference on Sustainable Information Engineering and Technology (SIET)
reason: Classifies photographed starling types to help people choose birds to keep or cultivate (pet-bird trade). The paper never says the birds were wild or free-ranging, or where they were photographed.

title: Point cloud capture and segmentation of animal images using classification and clustering
reason: All analysed data are RGB-D captures of a single taxidermy raccoon placed in a controlled outdoor setting; no wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Enhanced Deep Learning Feature Extraction for Plankton Taxonomy
reason: Proposes a CNN ensemble feature extractor for classifying plankton images (wild marine organisms) from EcoTaxa projects.

title: Intelligent Detection of Marine Organisms with Deep Learning based on Attention Mechanism
reason: Deep learning object detection of fish in underwater video from the marine environment (marine pastures); the fish are in open sea, not held in a production enclosure.

title: Individual Feral Cat Identification through Deep Learning
venue: IEEE/ACM International Conference on Big Data Computing, Applications and Technologies (BDCAT)
reason: Applies YOLOv5 to camera-trap images of free-ranging feral cats in Australian forests for individual identification; primary research.

title: Payload Drones and ACI: Drone Navigation System Prototype
reason: Drone navigation prototype that uses OpenCV to detect coloured cardboard target squares for payload delivery in enclosures; no images or video of animals are analysed.

title: Chameleo: walk like a chameleon detection with AI
reason: Wild-caught chameleons were temporarily housed in cages and filmed on a stretched rope in an experimental set-up on a university campus; no images of free-ranging animals are analysed. The paper is a work-in-progress proposal and no model was trained yet.

title: Hierarchical Clustering of Corals using Image Clustering
reason: Analyses only coral museum specimen images taken in a laboratory environment (Queensland Museum collection); no free-ranging animals in analysed data.

title: Deep Transfer Learning for Biology Cross-Domain Image Classification
venue: Journal of Control Science and Engineering
reason: Proposes multistage cross-domain transfer learning for biology image classification, evaluated partly on in situ plankton and fish image datasets (QUT Fish includes in situ images), motivated by biodiversity conservation.

title: Accurate Multilevel Classification for Wildlife Images
reason: Primary study evaluating CNN multilevel (taxonomic) classification on iNaturalist 2019 images of wild animals and plants; wildlife recognition is the stated application.

title: Object Detection and Movement Tracking Using Tubelets and Faster RCNN Algorithm with Anchor Generation
reason: Develops a Faster RCNN and tubelet method to detect and track elephants in video recorded in forest areas (Hosur forest) and at Theppakadu elephant camp, so wild and camp elephants appear together.

title: Detecting African hoofed animals in aerial imagery using convolutional neural network
venue: IAES International Journal of Robotics and Automation (IJRA)
reason: Proposes a Faster R-CNN variant with atrous convolutions to detect wild African hoofed animals in UAV imagery collected in Namibia.

title: Computational classification of animals for a highway detectiosystem
venue: Brazilian Journal of Veterinary Research and Animal Science
reason: Object detection (YOLOv4) applied to web images of capybaras (wild species) together with donkeys and horses (domestic/free-roaming) for a highway animal-vehicle collision warning system.

title: The Obs-Services and their potentials for biodiversity data assessments with a test of the current reliability of photo-identification of Coleoptera in the field
reason: Primary evaluation of a deep-learning image recognition app (ObsIdentify / Nature Identification API) on smartphone photographs of wild beetles taken in the field in Germany. Labelled 'Opinion' but contains an original empirical test.

title: Deep learning-based visual identification of signs of bat presence in bridge infrastructure images: A transfer learning approach
reason: Primary study that trains CNN image classifiers to recognise direct signs of wild bats (guano, urine staining, and bats themselves) in photographs of bridges and culverts taken during field studies.

title: Underwater image segmentation in the wild using deep learning
venue: Journal of the Brazilian Computer Society
reason: Generic foreground/background segmentation of underwater images; marine life appears only as one kind of foreground alongside divers and objects, and wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Counting sea lions and elephants from aerial photography using deep learning with density maps
reason: Primary study proposing a UNet density-map deep learning method to count wild Steller sea lions and African bush elephants in aerial images.

title: A new innovative real-time tracking method for flying insects applicable under natural conditions
reason: Image-based SWIR tracking of tagged bumblebees (hive placed inside the arena) and laboratory-reared hawkmoths confined in a 2 m netted outdoor flight arena; no wild, free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Continuous body 3-D reconstruction of limbless animals
reason: Laboratory locomotion experiment: marker-tagged kingsnakes filmed on a constructed step obstacle with a multi-camera high-speed rig; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Wing damage affects flight kinematics but not flower tracking performance in hummingbird hawkmoths
reason: Laboratory flight-cage experiment on lab-reared hawkmoths tracking a robotic flower; no images of wild, free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Motion parallax via head movements modulates visuo-motor control in pigeons
reason: Behavioural laboratory experiment on three captive pigeons in an operant chamber; computer vision is only used to track a head marker. No wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Attack behaviour in naive gyrfalcons is modelled by the same guidance law as in peregrine falcons, but at a lower guidance gain
reason: Flight trajectories were recorded with GPS loggers and modelled with guidance laws. Video served only to identify intercept time by eye, so there is no computer vision analysis. The subjects are captive-bred falconry birds.

title: Drosophila acquires seconds-scale rhythmic behavior
reason: Laboratory strain of Drosophila melanogaster filmed in a conditioning arena with electric shocks; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Wild Animal Detection Based on Swin-Transformer
reason: Applies Swin-Transformer object detection to infrared camera-trap images and video of wild animals from the Wuling Mountain area and compares it with other detectors.

title: Sampling flying bats with thermal and near-infrared imaging and ultrasound recording: hardware and workflow for bat point counts
reason: Wild free-flying bats are imaged with a thermal scope and near-infrared photographs, but the images are only inspected by hand: an observer spots the bats and features are scored manually. Photos are matched to detections by timestamps. No computer vision or automated image analysis is developed or applied.

title: FastTrack: An open-source software for tracking varying numbers of deformable objects
reason: General-purpose 2D tracking software tested on a compiled set of movies of laboratory model animals, cells, particles, robots, humans and traffic; no wild or free-ranging animals are stated.

title: WormPose: Image synthesis and convolutional networks for pose estimation in C. elegans
reason: Pose estimation method for the laboratory model organism C. elegans, recorded on agar plates under a tracking microscope; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Tracking individual honeybees among wildflower clusters with computer vision-facilitated pollinator monitoring
reason: Primary study proposing a hybrid detection and tracking method applied to video of unmarked, freely foraging honeybees outdoors among flowering groundcover; not a hive or beekeeping set-up.

title: Real-time dispersal of malaria vectors in rural Africa monitored with lidar
reason: Field entomological lidar with a CMOS linescan camera records wild free-flying mosquitoes and other insects over rice fields in Tanzania. Insects are detected in the range-time image data with background subtraction, thresholding and erosion/dilation, then classified by hierarchical clustering of their modulation spectra.

title: Estimating reef fish size distributions with a mini remotely operated vehicle-integrated stereo camera system
reason: Stereo-camera photogrammetry (StereoMorph calibration and 3D landmark measurement) applied to ROV video of wild reef fishes to estimate lengths; landmarks are digitized manually, so it is a borderline case of computer vision. A pool experiment with paper fish models precedes the field trials.

title: Egg recognition: The importance of quantifying multiple repeatable features as visual identity signals
reason: Image analysis (SpotEgg segmentation and feature extraction plus SVM) of eggs of wild Eurasian coots photographed at field nests; eggs are direct signs of wild animals.

title: Identifying geographically differentiated features of Ethopian Nile tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus) morphology with machine learning
reason: Computer vision (CNN, GP-LVM) applied to images of wild-caught Nile tilapia from six Ethiopian lakes to identify population-specific morphology; the fish come from wild lake populations caught by fishermen, not aquaculture.

title: Field testing an “acoustic lighthouse”: Combined acoustic and visual cues provide a multimodal solution that reduces avian collision risk with tall human-made structures
reason: Field study using stereo video and 3D reconstruction of wild migrating birds' flight trajectories near communication towers to assess collision risk under acoustic treatments.

title: Aerial survey estimates of polar bears and their tracks in the Chukchi Sea
reason: Aerial survey of wild polar bears on sea ice using thermal and colour imagery with an automated hot spot detection algorithm, used to estimate abundance.

title: Potential effects of GPS collars on the behaviour of two red pandas (Ailurus fulgens) in Rotterdam Zoo
reason: Behaviour of two zoo red pandas was recorded by direct human observation and analysed with statistical tests. No computer vision or image analysis is used, and the animals are captive.

title: Towards sustainable demersal fisheries: NepCon image acquisition system for automatic Nephrops norvegicus detection
reason: Computer vision for Norway lobster segmentation, detection, tracking and counting, but all images and videos come from an indoor experimental tank with dead or released individuals; no data from wild, free-ranging animals.

title: Automatic ladybird beetle detection using deep-learning models
reason: Primary study proposing a computer vision detector for ladybird beetles in citizen-science (iNaturalist) photographs taken in uncontrolled environments in Ecuador and Colombia.

title: Mapping Arctic cetaceans from space: A case study for beluga and narwhal
reason: Whales are detected and counted by human observers visually reading satellite images in QGIS; no automated computer vision method is applied (only pansharpening as visual enhancement, automated detection is named as future work).

title: Passive citizen science: The role of social media in wildlife observations
reason: Primary study that applies an image-labelling service (Google Cloud Vision API) to Flickr photographs to verify observations of UK wildlife species, including many wild birds, mammals and insects alongside plants and fungi.

title: Steps to build a DIY low-cost fixed-wing drone for biodiversity conservation
reason: Paper describes building and flight-testing a low-cost DIY fixed-wing drone; images were inspected visually (deforestation spots, trails, a domestic dog) and no computer vision method is applied to animal imagery.

title: Deep neural networks based automated extraction of dugong feeding trails from UAV images in the intertidal seagrass beds
reason: Primary study applying deep neural network segmentation to UAV images of feeding trails (direct signs) left by wild dugongs in an intertidal seagrass bed.

title: ESIDE: A computationally intelligent method to identify earthworm species (E. fetida) from digital images: Application in taxonomy
reason: Earthworms were collected from the field, washed and photographed ex situ as collected samples; no images show free-ranging animals in their habitat.

title: A drone-based survey for large, basking freshwater turtle species
reason: Drone photographs of wild freshwater turtles were detected, identified and counted manually by people; no computer vision method was applied to the animals. Photogrammetric stitching was tried and abandoned.

title: Identification of public submitted tick images: A neural network approach
reason: A CNN classifies public-submitted photographs of three wild tick species; an additional test set shows tick specimens photographed in a laboratory.

title: Quantitative photogrammetric methodology for measuring mammalian belly score in the painted dog
reason: Belly-score measurements are taken by hand with Adobe Photoshop's measurement tool on photographs of wild painted dogs; no automated computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Coleoptera Classification Using Convolutional Neural Network and Transfer Learning
venue: International Journal of Engineering Trends and Technology
reason: Classifies images of beetle specimens (collection/repository images) into four families; the paper never shows that the images are of live, free-ranging animals.

title: Human and Animal Movement Detection in Agricultural Fields
venue: International Journal of Computer Science and Engineering
reason: IoT system detecting animal intrusion in crop fields with PIR, LDR and flame sensors. The camera only streams live video to a laptop, and no images are analysed.

title: Automatically Identifying Wild Animals In Camera-Trap Images With Deep Learning
venue: International Journal of Computer Science and Engineering
reason: Although framed around camera-trap wildlife, the CNN is trained and tested only on images of cats and dogs (domestic pets); no wild animal data is analysed.

title: FishDeTec: A Fish Identification Application using Image Recognition Approach
venue: International Journal of Advanced Computer Science and Applications
reason: Applies a CNN (VGG16 with transfer learning) to images to classify Malaysian freshwater fish species, which are non-domestic animals. The paper does not say whether the imaged fish were wild or farmed, so they are coded as not_reported and the paper is included.

title: Birds Identification System using Deep Learning
venue: International Journal of Advanced Computer Science and Applications
reason: Primary study applying CNN feature extraction and classifiers to images of 434 bird species of Jordan for species identification aimed at birdwatching; the paper does not state whether the photographed birds were wild or captive.

title: Infrared thermography as a technique to measure physiological stress in birds: Body region and image angle matter
reason: Experimental study on domestic pigeons from a breeder, held in individual enclosures in a controlled room, with catheters fitted and handled as a stressor. The thermal imaging and head-pose estimation were done only on these domestic animals in a laboratory-style set-up. No wild or free-ranging animals are in the data.

title: Automatic Recognition of Macaque Facial Expressions for Detection of Affective States
reason: Automatic facial action unit recognition on videos of head-fixed laboratory macaques in neuroscience experiments; no wild or free-ranging animals in the data.

title: The Science of Citizen Science
venue: Proceedings of the Nova Scotian Institute of Science
reason: Book review of a volume on citizen science; no computer vision, no image data analysed, not primary research.

title: Citizen science, computing, and conservation: How can “Crowd AI” change the way we tackle large-scale ecological challenges?
reason: Case study that trains and evaluates CNN classifiers on camera trap images of wild African wildlife (Snapshot Safari) and integrates them with citizen science.

title: Unmanned aerial vehicle, and GIS tools, to monitor the reproduction of the flamingo Phoenicopterus chilensis (Aves: Phoenicopteridae)
reason: Primary study applying GIS-based image processing (principal components and pixel-value reclassification) to UAV photographs of wild Chilean flamingo breeding colonies to count individuals and eggs.

title: A Comparison of Convolutional Neural Network Architectures for Automated Detection and Identification of Waterfowl in Complex Environments
reason: Compares CNN object detectors for detecting and identifying wild waterfowl in sUAS imagery from a wildlife refuge.

title: Finally Within Reach: A Drone Census of an Important, But Practically Inaccessible, Antarctic Fur Seal Colony
reason: Drone imagery of wild Antarctic fur seal pups, but the pups were identified and counted by hand with Photoshop's Count Tool. No computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Viability of sex identification of the blue-fronted Amazon parrot (Amazona aestiva) based on iris color sexual dichromatism
venue: Anais da Academia Brasileira de Ciências
reason: Iris colorimetry from photographs of apprehended parrots held at a wildlife screening center; only captive animals analysed.

title: Path to Automating Ocean Health Monitoring
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
reason: Applies a CNN (Inception v3 with transfer learning) to classify wild deep-sea coral species from photographs of specimens collected in a field trawl survey off the US west coast. These are field-collected wild animals, not museum specimens.

title: Snapshot Safari: A large-scale collaborative to monitor Africa’s remarkable biodiversity
reason: Commentary describing the authors' own camera-trap monitoring network, in which CNN classifiers are applied to images of wild African mammals. It is not a literature review, though it reports no experiments of its own.

title: Batch extraction of morphological and color metrics from invertebrate samples. v1
reason: This is a protocol for imaging preserved invertebrate specimens from pitfall trap samples in a lab set-up. No living free-ranging animals are imaged, and the specimens are treated like museum specimens.

title: Small Sample Underwater Target Recognition Based on Mobilenet_ YOLOV4 Algorithm
reason: Object detection (Mobilenet-YOLOv4) of marine invertebrates in real seabed images; the animals are on the seabed and the paper does not say they come from a farm.

title: Fossil Texture Mapping With Computeriation Techniques As A Tool In Paleontology With Pheomelanin Pigment Method
venue: Turkish Journal of Computer and Mathematics Education (TURCOMAT)
reason: Image processing applied to fossil images (specimens taken from the internet), not wild free-ranging living animals; fossils treated as specimens.

reason: Applies YOLOv3 object detection to drone imagery of wild sea cucumbers on a coral reef flat to estimate density.

title: Assessing the Potential of Remotely-Sensed Drone Spectroscopy to Determine Live Coral Cover on Heron Reef
reason: Borderline include: drone point spectroscopy and supervised classification of an RGB drone mosaic are used to estimate live coral cover (corals are wild sessile animals) on a natural reef. The work is benthic substrate mapping, so E-PLANT (habitat cover only) is the alternative reading.

title: Area-Wide Prediction of Vertebrate and Invertebrate Hole Density and Depth across a Climate Gradient in Chile Based on UAV and Machine Learning
reason: Primary study that uses UAV RGB imagery with image-derived predictors and random forest models to predict the density and depth of burrow holes (direct signs) made by wild burrowing vertebrates and invertebrates in Chile. Holes are not detected in the images directly but predicted from image-derived vegetation and texture layers.

title: Surveys of Large Waterfowl and Their Habitats Using an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle: A Case Study on the Siberian Crane
reason: UAV survey of wild Siberian cranes in which the birds were identified and counted manually by visual interpretation. The authors state they did not use automatic identification; photogrammetry software was used only to build the habitat orthomosaic and 3D mesh.

title: From Coastal to Montane Forest Ecosystems, Using Drones for Multi-Species Research in the Tropics
reason: Primary study using drone RGB and thermal imagery of wild waterbirds, ungulates and primates in Indonesian protected areas, including machine-learning species detection on the imagery.

title: Underwater Target Recognition Based on Improved YOLOv4 Neural Network
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv4 detector for underwater marine animals (echinus, starfish, holothurian, scallop) in underwater images; the paper does not say whether the animals are wild or farmed.

title: Wild Animal Information Collection Based on Depthwise Separable Convolution in Software Defined IoT Networks
reason: Proposes a lightweight CNN object detection network for wild animal detection, trained and evaluated on images of wild animals from the Oregon Wildlife dataset.

title: Implementation of an Award-Winning Invasive Fish Recognition and Separation System
reason: Computer vision fish species recognition for invasive carp removal, but the analysed data are a pre-existing fish image dataset whose capture conditions are not described, and the system was tested only in an indoor water tank; no images of wild free-ranging fish are shown to be analysed.

title: Real-time automatic investigation of indian roadway animals by 3D reconstruction detection using deep learning for R-3D-YOLOV3 image classification and filtering
reason: Primary study proposing a YOLOv3-based detector and 3D reconstruction for stray and wild animals on Indian roads. The paper says its images show stray and wild animals, but the only taxa it names are cats and cows, so inclusion is borderline (E-AGRI would apply if only domestic animals count).

title: Train Fast While Reducing False Positives: Improving Animal Classification Performance Using Convolutional Neural Networks
reason: All analysed images show farmed red deer held in enclosures on a deer farm; no wild or free-ranging animals are in the data, although the motivation is wildlife surveys.

title: Contrasting Manual and Automated Assessment of Thermal Stress Responses and Larval Body Size in Black Soldier Flies and Houseflies
reason: Laboratory phenotyping of laboratory-reared and commercially produced black soldier flies and houseflies in well plates and vials using video tracking software; no wild, free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Swallowtail Butterflies Use Multiple Visual Cues to Select Oviposition Sites
reason: Behavioural study of laboratory-reared, hand-mated butterflies filmed in a small indoor cage; no wild or free-ranging animals in the analysed data.

title: A Temporal Boosted YOLO-Based Model for Birds Detection around Wind Farms
reason: Proposes YOLOv4-based detection models for free-flying wild birds in videos recorded around wind farm sites in Denmark.

title: Coral Image Segmentation with Point-Supervision via Latent Dirichlet Allocation with Spatial Coherence
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Proposes a point-supervised segmentation method evaluated on images of wild corals (animals) collected in situ at Pulley Ridge, Gulf of Mexico.

title: Plankton Detection with Adversarial Learning and a Densely Connected Deep Learning Model for Class Imbalanced Distribution
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Proposes a CycleGAN augmentation plus densely connected YOLOv3 for detecting and classifying marine plankton taxa in images from the WHOI-Plankton dataset (Imaging FlowCytobot). Borderline: the analysed taxa are mostly phytoplankton/protists.

title: Using Drones to Measure Jellyfish Density in Shallow Estuaries
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Primary study (technical report, labelled 'Perspective' by the journal) that develops a semiautomated image-processing program to count wild jellyfish in drone pictures taken in a Danish fjord.

title: On the Importance of Passive Acoustic Monitoring Filters
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: The study classifies marine mammal species from audio recordings (passive acoustic monitoring). The only images are spectrograms generated from sound, so no images or video of animals are analysed.

title: Applying Artificial Intelligence Methods to Detect and Classify Fish Calls from the Northern Gulf of Mexico
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Passive acoustic monitoring study: fish calls from hydrophone recordings are detected with an energy detector and classified from spectrogram images with ResNet-50. The data are sound only, with no images or video of animals.

title: Application of Feature Point Matching Technology to Identify Images of Free-Swimming Tuna Schools in a Purse Seine Fishery
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Applies feature point matching (ORB/SIFT/SURF + KNN) to video of wild free-swimming tuna schools in the open ocean to recognise fish shoals.

title: Insights into Activity of Zoo Housed Asian Elephants (Elephas maximus) during Periods of Limited Staff and Visitor Presence, a Focus on Resting Behaviour
venue: Journal of Zoological and Botanical Gardens
reason: Behaviour of zoo-housed Asian elephants was coded manually by an observer from CCTV footage. No computer vision or automated image analysis was used, and the animals are captive only.

title: Gaps in Live Inter-Observer Reliability Testing of Animal Behavior: A Retrospective Analysis and Path Forward
venue: Journal of Zoological and Botanical Gardens
reason: Retrospective analysis of live inter-observer reliability tests of zoo animal behaviour recorded by human observers with the ZooMonitor app; no image or video analysis, and the animals are captive zoo animals.

title: Use of Interactive Technology in Captive Great Ape Management
venue: Journal of Zoological and Botanical Gardens
reason: Online questionnaire survey of zoo carers about interactive technology use with captive great apes; no image or video analysis and no computer vision; animals are captive only.

title: Investigation of Environmentally Dependent Movement of Bottlenose Dolphins (Tursiops truncatus)
venue: Journal of Zoological and Botanical Gardens
reason: Computer vision tracking of four managed bottlenose dolphins in a lagoon at Dolphin Quest Oahu; captive animals only.

title: A Method for Detection of Small Moving Objects in UAV Videos
reason: Detects flying honeybees from beehives placed by the authors (managed honeybees, beekeeping) in UAV videos; no wild free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Repeatable semantic reef-mapping through photogrammetry and label-augmentation
reason: Semantic segmentation of underwater photomosaics of wild sessile reef animals (scleractinian corals, sponges, soft corals) in natural reefs; primary research with a computer vision method.

title: Individual Identification of Cheetah (Acinonyx jubatus) Based on Close-Range Remote Sensing: First Steps of a New Monitoring Technique
reason: Tracks were collected only from eight semi-captive cheetahs kept in a wildlife sanctuary, walking over prepared sand patches. No wild or free-ranging animals are in the data.

title: Using Aerial Photogrammetry to Assess Stock-Wide Marine Turtle Nesting Distribution, Abundance and Cumulative Exposure to Industrial Activity
reason: Aerial photographs of wild marine turtle nesting tracks were reviewed and counted manually by human observers in a QGIS interface. No automated image analysis or computer vision method is applied; the paper only suggests machine learning as future work.

title: Feasibility Analyses of Real-Time Detection of Wildlife Using UAV-Derived Thermal and RGB Images
reason: UAV thermal/RGB detection method developed and tested only on farm-kept animals (mainly alpaca) at an animal farm; no wild or free-ranging animals in the analysed data.

title: Deep Learning for Automated Detection and Identification of Migrating American Eel Anguilla rostrata from Imaging Sonar Data
reason: The analysed data are imaging sonar (ARIS) recordings only; the optical camera served only to verify eel behaviour. Eels were tethered in a laboratory tank and tethered in a river near a dam.

title: Coral Reef Mapping with Remote Sensing and Machine Learning: A Nurture and Nature Analysis in Marine Protected Areas
reason: Supervised SVM classification of WorldView-3 satellite imagery maps benthic habitats of wild coral reefs, including a class for the hydrocoral Millepora alcicornis. The map feeds a species distribution model for this wild, free-living animal.

title: Machine Learning for the Fast and Accurate Assessment of Fitness in Coral Early Life History
reason: Develops a machine learning pixel-classification pipeline to segment, count and measure coral juveniles in images. Part of the data comes from field-deployed tiles on the Great Barrier Reef and part from laboratory slides.

title: How the Small Object Detection via Machine Learning and UAS-Based Remote-Sensing Imagery Can Support the Achievement of SDG2: A Case Study of Vole Burrows
reason: Deep-learning object detection on UAS imagery of burrows (direct signs) of free-ranging wild Levant voles in an alfalfa field; primary research.

title: Automated Detection of Animals in Low-Resolution Airborne Thermal Imagery
reason: Proposes D-YOLO to detect free-ranging rabbits, feral pigs and kangaroos (and rabbit warrens) in airborne thermal imagery from Australia; the pest species are feral/free-ranging and kangaroos are wild.

title: Regional High-Resolution Benthic Habitat Data from Planet Dove Imagery for Conservation Decision-Making and Marine Planning
reason: Satellite-based benthic habitat (coral reef, seagrass, hardbottom, sand) mapping; the paper maps habitat or land cover classes, not individual animals or their signs.

title: Evaluation of Satellite Imagery for Monitoring Pacific Walruses at a Large Coastal Haulout
reason: Wild Pacific walrus haulouts imaged by satellite, but walrus aggregations were detected and delineated only by manual visual interpretation by human observers; no computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Regional Ranking of Marine Turtle Nesting in Remote Western Australia by Integrating Traditional Ecological Knowledge and Remote Sensing
reason: Aerial photographs of wild marine turtle nesting tracks were only interpreted and counted by human viewers. No computer vision method was applied to the animal images; the only automated processing was brightness thresholding of Landsat imagery to map beaches.

title: Lightweight Underwater Object Detection Based on YOLO v4 and Multi-Scale Attentional Feature Fusion
reason: Proposes a lightweight YOLO v4-based detector and evaluates it on underwater datasets of marine organisms (fish, crabs, jellyfish, starfish, sea cucumbers, etc.) filmed in real underwater environments.

title: Retreating Shorelines as an Emerging Threat to Adélie Penguins on Inexpressible Island
reason: Primary study applying object-based image analysis to UAV and aerial images of a wild Adélie penguin colony to estimate abundance and colony extent.

title: Animal Migration Patterns Extraction Based on Atrous-Gated CNN Deep Learning Model
reason: Deep learning semantic segmentation of rendered weather radar images to extract biological (bird migration) echoes from free-flying animals.

title: Feasibility of Using Small UAVs to Derive Morphometric Measurements of Australian Snubfin (Orcaella heinsohni) and Humpback (Sousa sahulensis) Dolphins
reason: UAV photogrammetry of wild dolphins, but body lengths are obtained by manually measuring pixel distances in software (AragoJ) and analysed with linear mixed models; no automated computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Comprehensive Bird Preservation at Wind Farms
reason: Stereo-vision system with motion detection and a CNN to detect, localize and size-classify wild birds flying around a wind turbine; validated against ornithologists' field observations.

title: An Automated Light Trap to Monitor Moths (Lepidoptera) Using Computer Vision-Based Tracking and Deep Learning
reason: Primary study proposing a light trap and computer vision pipeline (blob detection, tracking, CNN classification) on images of live, free-flying wild moths attracted to a trap in the field.

title: ALMI—A Generic Active Learning System for Computational Object Classification in Marine Observation Images
reason: Proposes an active learning image classification method evaluated on image patches of wild marine fauna from a deep-sea towed camera system and a cabled underwater observatory.

title: A Runway Safety System Based on Vertically Oriented Stereovision
reason: Stereovision and CNN based system for detecting, localizing and size-classifying free-flying birds at an airport runway; field prototype reported real birds, although quantitative validation used bird-like drones.

title: Development of Coral Investigation System Based on Semantic Segmentation of Single-Channel Images
reason: CNN semantic segmentation of coral images; data combine laboratory aquarium corals, corals imaged in the sea at a conservation base, and web-crawled coral images.

title: U-Infuse: Democratization of Customizable Deep Learning for Object Detection
reason: Software tool for training RetinaNet object detectors, evaluated in a case study on camera trap images of free-ranging feral cats and other wildlife in Australia and New Zealand.

title: Visual diagnosis of the varroa destructor parasitic mite in honeybees using object detector techniques
reason: The study detects Varroa mites on managed honey bees for beekeeping colony health monitoring; no wild, free-ranging animals are the subject.

title: Ethoflow: Computer vision and artificial intelligence-based software for automatic behavior analysis
reason: Software for behaviour tracking validated with laboratory bioassays (Petri dish, pesticide exposure) on stingless bees; no clearly wild, free-ranging data described in the analyses.

title: Towards Lifespan Automation for Caenorhabditis elegans Based on Deep Learning: Analysing Convolutional and Recurrent Neural Networks for Dead or Live Classification
reason: Laboratory lifespan assays of cultured C. elegans in Petri plates; no wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: A Deep Dive of Autoencoder Models on Low-Contrast Aquatic Images
reason: The data are videos of fish kept in an aquarium compartment at the Aquatic Animal Center. No wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Cascade and Fusion: A Deep Learning Approach for Camouflaged Object Sensing
reason: Deep learning method for pixel-level camouflaged object detection, evaluated on camouflaged-animal datasets and on field photos of camouflaged creatures. The stated application is biological monitoring with camera traps.

title: Caenorhabditis elegans Multi-Tracker Based on a Modified Skeleton Algorithm
reason: Tracking of laboratory-cultured C. elegans nematodes on Petri dishes; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Improving Animal Monitoring Using Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (sUAS) and Deep Learning Networks
reason: Deep learning classification of sUAS images of animals; data include free-ranging wild species (white-tailed deer, Canada Geese) together with domestic cattle and horses.

title: An NB-IoT-Based Edge-of-Things Framework for Energy-Efficient Image Transfer
reason: The paper is about sending images of vehicles at a campus entrance over NB-IoT in an energy-efficient way. No animals appear in the data.

title: Comparing Class-Aware and Pairwise Loss Functions for Deep Metric Learning in Wildlife Re-Identification
reason: Compares deep metric learning loss functions and CNN backbones for image-based individual re-identification of wild animals (lions, nyala, zebra, tiger) alongside zoo chimpanzee and panda datasets.

title: Detection of the Deep-Sea Plankton Community in Marine Ecosystem with Underwater Robotic Platform
reason: Classical computer vision (optical flow) method to detect and count free-living deep-sea plankton in in-situ underwater video from the western Pacific.

title: A Marine Organism Detection Framework Based on the Joint Optimization of Image Enhancement and Object Detection
reason: Proposes a CNN-based detection framework for marine organisms (sea urchin, sea cucumber, scallop, starfish) in underwater seabed images taken by underwater robots (URPC dataset).

title: Automated Quantification of Brittle Stars in Seabed Imagery Using Computer Vision Techniques
reason: Primary study applying deep-learning semantic segmentation and blob counting to ROV seabed mosaics showing wild brittle stars in an Arctic bay.

title: Real-Time Jellyfish Classification and Detection Based on Improved YOLOv3 Algorithm
reason: Improved YOLOv3 for detecting and classifying seven jellyfish species and fish. Data combine a published jellyfish dataset, web-crawled images and laboratory/aquarium jellyfish. The paper does not explicitly state that any images show wild animals; inclusion rests on the web and published-dataset images, so subject type is coded as mixed.

title: The Role of Citizen Science and Deep Learning in Camera Trapping
reason: Conceptual framework and data model for a web-based camera trap database combining citizen science and deep learning; no images are analysed and no computer vision method is implemented or evaluated.

title: A Deep Learning Approach to Assist Sustainability of Demersal Trawling Operations
reason: Applies Mask R-CNN detection, classification, tracking and counting to in-trawl underwater video of wild-caught Nephrops and fish in a commercial demersal trawl fishery.

title: MRDA-MGFSNet: Network Based on a Multi-Rate Dilated Attention Mechanism and Multi-Granularity Feature Sharer for Image-Based Butterflies Fine-Grained Classification
reason: Proposes a CNN for fine-grained species classification of butterfly images, almost all captured in the natural environment (web-collected).

title: Underwater biological detection algorithm based on improved faster-rcnn
reason: Proposes an improved Faster-RCNN to detect underwater organisms (sea cucumber, sea urchin, scallop, starfish) in underwater robot images that the paper says reflect real underwater conditions.

title: Machine Learning Applications of Convolutional Neural Networks and Unet Architecture to Predict and Classify Demosponge Behavior
reason: Primary study applying a modified Unet for semantic segmentation to in situ time-lapse images of a wild marine demosponge recorded by a seafloor cabled observatory.

title: Rapid quantification of biofouling with an inexpensive, underwater camera and image analysis
reason: Viewpoint article describing a citizen-science early-detection program design (Invader Detectives) using iNaturalist records; no computer vision or image analysis is performed.

title: Experience and perspectives of small unmanned aerial vehicles application for marine coastal biological studies
reason: Drone survey of wild seals and fish in the Tatar Strait. Animals were counted by eye on photos and orthophotos in GIS. The only processing was photogrammetric orthophoto assembly; no computer vision analysis of the animals was developed or applied.

title: Long-tailed Visual Recognition via Gaussian Clouded Logit Adjustment
reason: Generic long-tailed visual recognition method evaluated on general benchmarks (CIFAR-LT, ImageNet-LT, Places-LT, iNaturalist 2018). The paper does not state wildlife as its subject or application.

title: Semi-automated photo-identification of Bahamian Racers (Cubophis vudii vudii)
reason: Primary study testing semi-automated photo-identification software (APHIS) on photographs of wild, opportunistically captured Bahamian Racers for individual identification.

title: Multi-scale CNN Approach for Accurate Detection of Underwater Static Fish Image
venue: Journal of Artificial Intelligence and Capsule Networks
reason: Proposes a multi-scale CNN to detect and classify fish species in underwater images from the Fish4Knowledge dataset; these are free-ranging fish.

title: Computerized assessment of dominance hierarchy in baboons (Papio papio)
reason: Dominance hierarchy is inferred from RFID-identified trial logs of automated touchscreen workstations and from manual behavioural observation; no image or video analysis by computer vision. The animals are a captive group in a primate centre enclosure.

title: Advanced Ecosystem Monitoring using Camera and Image Processing Technology
reason: Editorial preface to a special issue on camera and image-processing ecosystem monitoring; summarises the issue's papers and literature trends without primary image analysis.

title: An open-source, citizen science and machine learning approach to analyse subsea movies
reason: Software pipeline that trains a YOLOv3 object detector on ROV video frames of wild cold water corals (animals) in a marine protected area; primary research.

title: Life beneath the ice: jellyfish and ctenophores from the Ross Sea, Antarctica, with an image-based training set for machine learning
reason: Taxonomic paper that also publishes a taxonomist-ratified, annotated COCO image training set of wild under-ice jellyfish and ctenophores for machine learning. No computer vision model is trained or evaluated in the paper itself, so inclusion rests on the dataset contribution; this is a borderline case against E-NOCV.

title: Reducing Manual Supervision Required for Biodiversity Monitoring with Self-Supervised Learning
reason: Conference abstract presenting primary work on self-supervised learning for species classification in camera trap imagery of wild animals.

title: The Waterston’s evaporatorium of Ceraphronidae (Ceraphronoidea, Hymenoptera): A morphological barcode to a cryptic taxon
reason: Morphological and phylogenetic study of parasitoid wasp specimens imaged with microscopy (brightfield, CLSM, SEM). The images are used for manual description of anatomy, and no computer vision analysis is applied.

title: Automatic Camera-Trap Classification Using Wildlife-Specific Deep Learning in Nilgai Management
venue: Journal of Fish and Wildlife Management
reason: Deep learning classification of camera-trap images of free-ranging wildlife (nilgai and other groups) in south Texas; data also include cattle, dogs and horses.

title: NorFisk: fish image dataset from Norwegian fish farms for species recognition using deep neural networks
venue: Modeling Identification and Control A Norwegian Research Bulletin
reason: Fish detection dataset and semi-automatic annotation method built from underwater video at a Norwegian fish farm; the footage shows wild saithe outside the net pens together with farmed salmonids inside them.

title: Fish Species Detection Application (FiSDA) in Leyte Gulf Using Convolutional Neural Network
venue: Proceedings of Engineering and Technology Innovation
reason: Primary study that trains a CNN to classify images of wild marine fish species from Leyte Gulf for a mobile identification app. Images come from BFAR publications and Fishbase; the paper does not state whether they show live, free-ranging fish or caught specimens.

title: CONVOLUTIONAL NEURAL NETWORK ARCHITECTURES PERFORMANCE EVALUATION FOR FISH SPECIES CLASSIFICATION
venue: Journal of Sustainability Science and Management
reason: Benchmarks CNN architectures for species classification of 18 marine fish species. The images are real-world photos, including in-situ ones, taken from the web and the QUT fish dataset.

title: Body condition of gray whales (Eschrichtius robustus) feeding on the Pacific Coast reflects local and basin-wide environmental drivers
venue: The journal of cetacean research and management. Special issue
reason: Wild gray whales were photographed, but a single researcher scored body condition by eye from the photographs. No computer vision or automated image analysis method is developed or applied.

title: Towards Accurate Camouflaged Object Detection with Mixture Convolution and Interactive Fusion
reason: Generic camouflaged object detection method evaluated on COD benchmarks (and polyp segmentation); wildlife conservation is not the stated subject or application.

title: Class balanced underwater object detection dataset generated by class-wise style augmentation
reason: The authors use CycleGAN style transfer on underwater images of marine invertebrates (sea cucumber, sea urchin, scallop, starfish) from URPC2018 to build a class-balanced detection dataset. The paper does not say whether these animals are wild or farmed, but nothing indicates they are captive.

title: Semi-supervised Keypoint Localization
reason: Semi-supervised keypoint localization method motivated by wild animals, evaluated on bird (CUB-200-2011) and Amur tiger (ATRW) images alongside human pose benchmarks; tigers are from zoos, birds are not specified as captive.

title: Deep CNNs for large scale species classification
reason: Evaluates standard CNN architectures for large-scale image classification on the iNaturalist 2019 challenge dataset (amphibians, birds, fungi, insects, plants, reptiles); the stated aim is large-scale classification in general, not wildlife conservation, and the paper does not describe whether the animals are wild.

title: Absolute 3D Pose Estimation and Length Measurement of Severely Deformed Fish from Monocular Videos in Longline Fishing
reason: Computer vision method estimating 3D pose and length of wild-caught Pacific Halibut from monocular videos recorded during longline fishing (capture fishery, not aquaculture).

title: Exploiting Depth Information for Wildlife Monitoring
reason: The method is trained and evaluated only on rendered synthetic animal scenes and on video of deer inside a zoo enclosure; no wild or free-ranging animals are in the analysed data (Caltech Camera Traps images appear only as an illustration in Figure 1).

title: The Semi-Supervised iNaturalist-Aves Challenge at FGVC7 Workshop
reason: Presents a new bird species recognition dataset (Semi-Aves) built from iNaturalist images, with ResNet-50 classification baselines; birds are the stated subject of the benchmark.

title: Geo-Spatiotemporal Features and Shape-Based Prior Knowledge for Fine-grained Imbalanced Data Classification
reason: Develops fine-grained image classification with geo-spatiotemporal priors on citizen-science photos of wild butterflies/insects in North America.

title: From Synthetic to Real: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for Animal Pose Estimation
reason: Proposes a CV method (unsupervised domain adaptation) for animal pose estimation, evaluated on real images that include wild animals (tigers from documentaries, Grevy's zebras from Kenya) as well as domestic ones (horses, dogs, cats, sheep, cows).

title: Object detection for crabs in top-view seabed imagery
reason: Applies a CNN-LSTM object detector to underwater seabed images of wild crabs and mussels and to aerial images of wild Steller sea lions. Pascal VOC is used only as an extra benchmark.

title: The iWildCam 2021 Competition Dataset
reason: Competition dataset paper on species classification and counting of wild animals in camera trap image sequences, with baseline results.

title: Detecting Biological Locomotion in Video: A Computational Approach
reason: Proposes a computer vision method to detect locomoting animals in video and evaluates it on web videos of many animal groups (wild animals such as snakes, fish, cetaceans, birds, together with humans, cats and dogs) and on a camouflaged-animals dataset; wildlife monitoring is a stated application.

title: The Semi-Supervised iNaturalist Challenge at the FGVC8 Workshop
reason: Dataset/benchmark paper for semi-supervised fine-grained classification spanning animals, plants and fungi from iNaturalist; the stated subject is semi-supervised learning methodology, not wildlife or conservation.

title: The Fishnet Open Images Database: A Dataset for Fish Detection and Fine-Grained Categorization in Fisheries
reason: The paper presents a dataset of images from electronic monitoring cameras on commercial fishing vessels and benchmarks detection and classification of wild-caught fish species. This is capture fisheries, not aquaculture.

title: The Animal ID Problem: Continual Curation
reason: Position/perspective paper that proposes a problem formulation (continual curation) and performance metrics for individual animal ID; it reports no experiments and analyses no image data.

title: Image-to-Image Translation of Synthetic Samples for Rare Classes
reason: Primary study applying image-to-image translation of synthetic images to improve rare-species classification in camera trap images of wild animals.

title: Florida Wildlife Camera Trap Dataset
reason: Introduces a camera-trap image classification dataset of free-ranging Florida wildlife (with some cattle and dogs) and trains a ResNet-50 baseline.

title: Detecting Cattle and Elk in the Wild from Space
reason: Deep learning counting and localization of free-ranging elk and cattle in very high-resolution satellite imagery of Point Reyes National Seashore; wild elk appear together with domestic cattle.

title: Self-Supervised Learning for Fine-Grained Image Classification
reason: Self-supervised fine-grained classification of cassava leaf disease images; no animals are the subject.

title: Trade-off between deep learning for species identification and inference about predator-prey co-occurrence: Reproducible R workflow integrating models in computer vision and ecological statistics
reason: Deep learning species classification of camera trap images of wild lynx and its prey in the Jura mountains, France; data also include domestic animals (dogs, cats, cows).

title: An Underwater Image Semantic Segmentation Method Focusing on Boundaries and a Real Underwater Scene Semantic Segmentation Dataset
reason: Proposes a semantic segmentation method and dataset for real-scene underwater images of marine organisms (sea cucumber, sea urchin, scallop, starfish). The paper does not say the animals are farmed, so they are coded as free-ranging.

title: AP-10K: A Benchmark for Animal Pose Estimation in the Wild
reason: Introduces AP-10K, a mammal pose estimation dataset and benchmark compiled from public animal image datasets; it covers wild species together with domestic ones (dog, cat, cow, sheep, horse, pig) and some zoo backgrounds, and names wildlife conservation as an application.

title: A Novel Dataset for Keypoint Detection of quadruped Animals from Images
reason: Dataset paper introducing keypoint (pose) annotations for images of 35 quadruped species, including wild species (e.g. giant panda, giraffe, elephant) and domestic ones (persian and siamese cat). Animals are the stated subject.

title: A deep neural network for multi-species fish detection using multiple acoustic cameras
reason: Develops a CNN-based detector for fish in acoustic-camera (imaging sonar) video for fish monitoring, including Atlantic salmon and European eel, tested on a real-world scenario. Only pages 1, 2, 19 and 20 were available, so the wild status rests on the abstract's monitoring context.

title: Fine-Grained Zero-Shot Learning with DNA as Side Information
reason: Proposes a zero-shot method for fine-grained species classification of images (insects from BOLD, birds from CUB), using DNA as side information. The images are of non-domestic species, but the paper does not say how or where they were taken.

title: Domain Adaptation for Rare Classes Augmented with Synthetic Samples
reason: Domain adaptation method for species classification of camera trap images (Caltech Camera Traps) of wild animals, augmented with synthetic deer; dataset also includes cats and dogs.

title: Unified 3D Mesh Recovery of Humans and Animals by Learning Animal Exercise
reason: 3D mesh recovery of humans and domestic quadrupeds (dog, horse, cow) from generic pose datasets; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Coarse-to-fine Animal Pose and Shape Estimation
reason: 3D pose and shape estimation of domestic dogs (pets); no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Pose Recognition in the Wild: Animal pose estimation using Agglomerative Clustering and Contrastive Learning
reason: Proposes an unsupervised computer vision method for animal pose estimation / body-part segmentation on videos of wild animals from nature documentaries (tigers, koalas, langurs, ostriches) together with domestic dogs and horses.

title: The CSIRO Crown-of-Thorn Starfish Detection Dataset
reason: Releases an annotated underwater image dataset of wild Crown-of-Thorns Starfish on the Great Barrier Reef for object detection.

title: Counting breeding gulls with unmanned aerial vehicles: camera quality and flying height affects precision of a semi-automatic counting method
reason: Applies a semi-automatic supervised image classification method to UAV imagery to count wild breeding gulls in a colony on a Danish Wadden Sea island.

title: Human Attention in Fine-grained Classification
reason: The paper is a generic fine-grained classification method that uses human gaze. Birds appear only through the CUB benchmark, and the method is also tested on chest X-rays. Wildlife is not the stated subject.

title: Feature Fusion Vision Transformer for Fine-Grained Visual Categorization
reason: Generic fine-grained visual categorization method evaluated on benchmarks (CUB birds, Stanford Dogs, soy and cotton cultivars); wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Endemic and endangered Short-crested Coquette (Lophornis brachylophus): floral resources and interactions
reason: Field ecology study using point counts, focal behavioural observations and network analysis of hummingbird-plant interactions; no image or video analysis.

title: Robust Underwater Fish Detection Using an Enhanced Convolutional Neural Network
venue: International Journal of Image Graphics and Signal Processing
reason: Proposes a simplified VGGNet CNN to classify underwater fish images (ImageCLEF Fish_ts), also evaluated on plankton, coral and coral reef fish datasets. The paper does not explicitly state the animals are wild; this is inferred from the underwater and coral reef context.

title: Content-based Fish Classification Using Combination of Machine Learning Methods
venue: International Journal of Information Technology and Computer Science
reason: Proposes a content-based fish species classification method using image features and an ensemble of ML classifiers on the QUT fish image dataset; animals are non-domestic fish and nothing indicates captivity.

title: Fish Image Classification by XgBoost Based on Gist and GLCM Features
venue: International Journal of Information Technology and Computer Science
reason: Classifies fish species from images of fish, including underwater images (F4K) of non-domestic fish species, using hand-crafted features and machine learning.

title: Identification of Potential Predators for Asari Clam Ruditapes philippinarum Using Time-lapse Camera Observations
reason: Wild fish predators were recorded with field time-lapse underwater cameras, but people identified and counted them by looking at the images on a monitor. No computer vision or automated image analysis was used.

title: Clasificación automática para animales en peligro de extinción de Colombia usando redes neuronales convolucionales
reason: Applies a CNN (AlexNet) to classify images of 11 endangered wild Colombian animal species collected from the web.

title: Biodiversitätsdaten, Citizen Science und Online-Erfassungssysteme – Überblick und Erfahrungsbericht
reason: Experience report comparing citizen-science biodiversity recording platforms; no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated. The image-recognition app ObsIdentify is only mentioned, and photos are validated manually by experts.

title: A Comparative Study of Underwater Marine Products Detection based on YOLOv5 and Underwater Image Enhancement
reason: Applies YOLOv5 detection combined with underwater image enhancement to underwater images of marine invertebrates (echinus, holothurian, scallop, starfish) from the URPC dataset in a marine environment.

title: Can eye surface temperature be used to indicate a stress response in harbour seals (Phoca vitulina)?
reason: Thermal images of orphaned harbour seal pups held in pens at a rehabilitation facility. All the animals were in captivity, and eye temperature was read off the images by hand in FLIR software, with no computer vision method.

title: Butterfly Species Identification from Natural Environment Based on Improved RetinaNet
venue: Journal of Computer Research and Development
reason: Proposes an improved RetinaNet to detect and identify butterfly species in images taken in the natural environment. Specimen photos are added to the training set, which makes the data mixed.

title: Propelling and perturbing appendages together facilitate strenuous ground self-righting
reason: Biomechanics study of self-righting in commercially supplied discoid cockroaches filmed in a laboratory arena with high-speed cameras, plus a robot physical model; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: DeepEthogram, a machine learning pipeline for supervised behavior classification from raw pixels.
reason: Behaviour classification software evaluated only on videos of laboratory mice and tethered Drosophila in neuroscience arenas; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: The Mouse Action Recognition System (MARS) software pipeline for automated analysis of social behaviors in mice
reason: Pose estimation and social behavior classification of laboratory mice filmed in a resident-intruder assay in a home cage; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: TRex, a fast multi-animal tracking system with markerless identification, and 2D estimation of posture and visual fields
reason: Tracking and identification software evaluated only on laboratory videos of fish and insects in experimental set-ups; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: scAnt —an open-source platform for the creation of 3D models of arthropods (and other small objects)
reason: Photogrammetric 3D reconstruction of dried, pinned arthropod specimens (museum-style specimens) inside a lab scanner; no wild free-ranging animals imaged.

title: Cephalopod species identification using integrated analysis of machine learning and deep learning approaches
reason: Images are of beaks extracted from dead cephalopod specimens bought at fisheries landing sites and photographed in a laboratory lightbox; no images of wild, free-ranging animals or their field signs.

title: Capturing and analyzing pattern diversity: an example using the melanistic spotted patterns of leopard geckos
reason: Image analysis of melanistic patterns of captive-bred leopard geckos photographed sedated in a controlled set-up; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Characterizing the spatial distribution of coral reefs in the South-Central Coast region of Viet Nam using Planetscope imagery
reason: Primary study applying supervised pixel classification to satellite imagery to map live coral cover (corals are wild animals) on natural reefs. Borderline with benthic habitat mapping, but live coral is the stated subject.

title: Non‐local effects of human activity on the spatial distribution of migratory wildlife in Serengeti National Park, Tanzania
reason: Applies a deep learning object detector (YOLO) to camera trap images of free-ranging wildebeest and zebra in Serengeti National Park to study spatial distribution relative to park boundaries.

title: Large‐scale mammal monitoring: The potential of a citizen science camera‐trapping project in the United Kingdom
reason: Describes a citizen-science camera-trapping platform in which humans classify the images; no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated. Automated classification is only discussed as future potential.

title: Application of a parallel laser apparatus to measure forearms and flanges of wild Bornean orangutans (Pongo pygmaeus wurmbii)
reason: Develops and validates an image-based laser photogrammetry method to measure body parts of wild Bornean orangutans from digital photographs.

title: Analyzing and visualizing morphological features using machine learning techniques and non‐big data: A case study of macaque mandibles
reason: Deep learning sex classification on CT scans of dried museum mandible specimens of macaques (museum specimens), not images of free-ranging animals.
