title: Coordination of trunk motion during bipedal walking in the frontal plane: A comparison between Homo sapiens , Macaca fuscata , and an exploratory study on a gibbon
reason: Biomechanics study using marker-based 3D motion capture of laboratory-housed macaques and human volunteers walking on a runway or treadmill; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Identifying key factors for coral survival in reef restoration projects using deep learning
venue: Aquatic Conservation Marine and Freshwater Ecosystems
reason: Primary study applying CNN detection and segmentation to underwater monitoring pictures of transplanted coral colonies (animals) living on reefs in the Maldives.

title: MoFiM: A morphable fish modeling method for underwater binocular vision system
reason: 3D fish modelling from underwater binocular images of grass carp, motivated by fishery management; fish were manually measured on a measuring plate. The paper does not state that the fish were wild or free-ranging, and the origin of the animals is not reported.

title: Eyes on the herd: Quantifying ungulate density from satellite, unmanned aerial systems, and GPS collar data
reason: Elk were located and counted in satellite and UAS imagery by manual photo interpretation (digitizing in ArcGIS); the paper states automated detection could not be used, so no computer vision method is applied.

title: A general deep learning model for bird detection in high‐resolution airborne imagery
reason: Develops and evaluates a deep learning detector for wild birds in airborne (UAV) imagery from 13 monitoring projects.

title: Bee Tracker—an open‐source machine learning‐based video analysis software for the assessment of nesting and foraging performance of cavity‐nesting solitary bees
reason: All analysed videos show marked Osmia bicornis females released into enclosed flight cages; no free-ranging animals were imaged.

title: FishSizer: Software solution for efficiently measuring larval fish size
reason: Software segments and measures images of anesthetized fish larvae on microscope slides taken under a stereomicroscope in a laboratory setting; no wild, free-ranging animals imaged.

title: BOVIDS: A deep learning‐based software package for pose estimation to evaluate nightly behavior and its application to common elands (Tragelaphus oryx) in zoos
reason: All analysed video shows common elands and other African ungulates kept in zoo stables; no wild or free-ranging animals are in the data.

title: SizeExtractR: A workflow for rapid reproducible extraction of object size metrics from scaled images
reason: Semi-automated ImageJ/R workflow in which users outline objects by hand; size metrics are computed from manual outlines, with no automated computer vision analysis of the images. Subject is wild hard corals in seafloor photographs.

title: SEALNET: Facial recognition software for ecological studies of harbor seals
reason: Develops a CNN-based face detection and individual recognition pipeline on photographs of a wild harbor seal population at haul-out sites.

title: Assessing the effect of complex ground types on ground‐dwelling arthropod movements with video monitoring: Dealing with concealed movements under a layer of plant residues
reason: Video tracking of wild-caught earwigs kept in the laboratory and filmed in artificial mesocosm arenas inside a climatic chamber; no images of free-ranging animals.

title: Combining stereo‐video monitoring and physiological trials to estimate reef fish metabolic demands in the wild
reason: Stereo-video recordings of wild reef fish in situ are analysed using 3D video measurement software (VidSync) to measure body lengths and swimming speeds of individuals.

title: The potential of Jellytoring 2.0 smart tool as a global jellyfish monitoring platform
reason: CNN-based detection and species classification of jellyfish in underwater video frames; most images from natural environments, some from aquaria.

title: Giant panda age recognition based on a facial image deep learning system
reason: Age group classification from facial images of captive giant pandas only (breeding bases and zoos); no wild or free-ranging animal images are analysed.

title: Estimating wolf abundance from cameras
reason: Camera-trap images of wild wolves were categorised manually by technicians and analysed with a statistical space-to-event abundance model; no computer vision or automated image analysis is applied.

title: Applying and testing a novel method to estimate animal density from motion‐triggered cameras
reason: Statistical density estimation (TIFC) from camera-trap images that were manually tagged; no automated image analysis or computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Multi‐image flock size estimation with CountEm : A case study with half a million Common Eiders and Greater Snow Geese
reason: CountEm estimates flock size by systematic quadrat sampling with manual counting by a human observer; no automated image analysis or computer vision is applied to the aerial images of wild birds.

title: Regional walrus abundance estimate in the United States Chukchi Sea in autumn
reason: UAS imagery of wild Pacific walruses was stitched into an orthoimage with structure from motion, but walruses were counted by hand and the paper's main contribution is Bayesian abundance estimation using telemetry. No computer vision analysis of the animals is developed or applied.

title: Estimating roe deer density using motion‐sensitive cameras in Switzerland
reason: Camera-trap survey of wild roe deer in which sexing and individual identification of photos were done manually by human observers; density is estimated with statistical capture-recapture models. No computer vision method is applied to the images.

title: Selective foraging behavior of seabirds in small‐scale slicks
reason: Drone video of wild foraging terns tracked and analysed with computer vision techniques together with slick extraction to study foraging behaviour.

title: Predicting dreissenid mussel abundance in nearshore waters using underwater imagery and deep learning
reason: Develops a deep-learning semantic segmentation method on underwater images of free-living invasive dreissenid mussels on the lakebed of Lake Erie and Lake Ontario to estimate coverage, abundance and biomass.

title: Image‐based analyses from an online repository provide rich information on long‐term changes in morphology and human perceptions of rhinos
reason: Images of rhinos from an online repository are categorised by visual inspection and measured manually in Fiji/ImageJ; no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Community‐based mosquito surveillance: an automatic mosquito‐on‐human‐skin recognition system with a deep learning algorithm
reason: Images show laboratory-reared colony mosquitoes photographed in a netted cage on a volunteer's hand; no wild or free-ranging animals in the analysed data.

title: TagLab: AI-assisted annotation for the fast and accurate semantic segmentation of coral reef orthoimages
reason: Presents an AI-assisted annotation tool evaluated on semantic segmentation of wild coral reef colonies in underwater orthoimages from field surveys.

title: Spy in the sky: a method to identify pregnant small cetaceans
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: UAS and laser photogrammetry of wild bottlenose dolphins, but all image measurements and photo-ID matches are made manually by a researcher in measurement software; the only automated analysis is statistical (discriminant analysis, regression) on the manual measurements, so there is no computer vision method applied to the images. Borderline case: would be included if manual photogrammetry counts as image analysis.

title: Camera trap distance sampling for terrestrial mammal population monitoring: lessons learnt from a UK case study
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Camera trap distance sampling study of wild UK mammals. Images were screened, tagged and measured manually (DigiKam, Photoshop grid overlay) and densities were estimated with statistical distance-sampling models; no computer vision method is used.

title: Structure‐from‐motion photogrammetry demonstrates that fine‐scale seascape heterogeneity is essential in shaping mesophotic fish assemblages
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: The image analysis (SfM photogrammetry and maximum likelihood classification of orthomosaics) is applied only to the benthic habitat. Wild reef fish were identified and counted manually from video in EventMeasure, so no computer vision is applied to the animals.

title: Remote sensing‐supported mapping of the activity of a subterranean landscape engineer across an afro‐alpine ecosystem
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Primary study that classifies Sentinel-2 satellite imagery (spectral indices and texture metrics, random forest) to map the mounds, i.e. direct above-ground signs, of the wild giant root-rat in the Bale Mountains.

title: A camera trap‐based assessment of climate‐driven phenotypic plasticity of seasonal moulting in an endangered carnivore
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Camera trap images of wild Arctic foxes were scored for moult stage and individual identity by a human observer and then analysed with linear mixed models. No computer vision or automated image analysis was used.

title: Using Unoccupied Aerial Vehicles to estimate availability and group size error for aerial surveys of coastal dolphins
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: UAV video of wild humpback dolphins was reviewed manually by human reviewers to record surfacing times and group sizes; no computer vision or automated image analysis is applied.

title: Antler detection from the sky: deer sex ratio monitoring using drone‐mounted thermal infrared sensors
reason: Thermal UAV and camera-trap imagery of wild sika deer and wild boar was interpreted visually by the pilot/observers; no computer vision or automated image analysis method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Utility of machine learning for segmenting camera trap time‐lapse recordings
reason: Primary study that develops and evaluates a CNN-based detector on camera trap time-lapse images of wild gopher tortoises at their burrows in a nature preserve.

title: Estimating species richness with camera traps: modeling the effects of delay period, deployment length, number of sites, and interference imagery
reason: Camera-trap study-design and simulation paper on delay period, deployment length and number of sites; species in images were identified by people and no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Optimizing surveys of fall‐staging geese using aerial imagery and automated counting
reason: Primary study applying an automated machine-learning counting algorithm to aerial photographs of wild fall-staging geese at Izembek Lagoon, Alaska, and evaluating its accuracy.

title: Testing the detection of large, secretive snakes using camera traps
reason: Applies a pixel change detection algorithm to time-lapse camera trap images of free-ranging snakes (translocated Louisiana Pinesnake population and other wild snakes) in a national forest.

title: Differing animal welfare conceptions and what they mean for the future of zoos and aquariums, insights from an animal welfare audit
reason: Animal welfare audit of zoo habitats based on carer, veterinary and visitor rank scores; no image or video analysis is performed, and the animals are captive.

title: From left to right all through the night: Characteristics of lying rest in zoo elephants
reason: Zoo elephants' lying behaviour was scored by people watching video or observing directly, then analysed with statistical models. No computer vision method is used, and all animals are captive.

title: Effects of a modern exhibit design on captive tiger welfare
reason: Behavioural welfare study of four zoo tigers; camera-trap pictures were reviewed manually for tiger presence and no computer vision method was used. The animals are also captive only (E-CAPTIVE applies too).

title: Monitoring Human-Wildlife Interactions in National Parks with Crowdsourced Data and Deep Learning
reason: Primary study applying object detection, image captioning and distance calculation to crowd-sourced photos of wildlife and visitors in national parks; animals are detected and categorised alongside humans.

title: A Whale’s Tail - Finding the Right Whale in an Uncertain World
reason: Primary study proposing a landmark-based attention CNN for individual identification of humpback whales from fluke photographs, with sensitivity and uncertainty analysis.

title: I-MuPPET: Interactive Multi-Pigeon Pose Estimation and Tracking
reason: Pose estimation and tracking of pigeons recorded in an indoor motion-capture facility, with extra tests on cowbirds from outdoor aviaries and laboratory mice. None of the analysed data shows free-ranging wild animals.

title: Grounding Visual Representations with Texts for Domain Generalization
reason: Generic domain generalization method for image classification, evaluated on CUB birds and the DomainBed benchmarks (VLCS, PACS, OfficeHome, TerraIncognita, DomainNet). The paper never states wildlife as its subject or application.

title: Where to Focus: Investigating Hierarchical Attention Relationship for Fine-Grained Visual Classification
reason: Generic fine-grained visual classification method evaluated on CUB, Butterfly-200, VegFru, FGVC-Aircraft and Stanford Cars benchmarks; wildlife is not the stated application.

title: Exploring Fine-Grained Audiovisual Categorization with the SSW60 Dataset
reason: Presents a benchmark dataset (SSW60) of images, video and audio of 60 bird species and benchmarks species classification on it; the videos are described as in-the-wild recordings from the Macaulay Library.

title: On Label Granularity and Object Localization
reason: Generic weakly supervised object localization study on label granularity; animal images from iNaturalist serve as a fine-grained benchmark, and wildlife or conservation is not the stated application.

title: Stingless bee (Apidae: Meliponini) foraging and predation at trunk resin sources: Rare observations captured with microcontroller-based camera traps in a lowland dipterocarp forest
reason: Camera-trap photos of wild insects at resin wounds were filtered and identified manually; the paper states automated image analysis was untenable, so no computer vision method is applied.

title: Aerial photogrammetry of whale sharks (Rhincodon typus) in the Bay of La Paz, using an unoccupied aerial vehicle
reason: UAV photogrammetry of wild whale sharks in which body length and widths are measured manually on still frames with a custom R script and scaled by a reference pole; no automated image analysis or computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Operational sex ratio estimated from drone surveys for a species threatened by climate warming
reason: Wild green and loggerhead turtles were filmed by drone, but people reviewed and annotated the video by hand in BORIS and measured body ratios by hand in ImageJ. No automated computer vision method was developed or applied.

title: Application of underwater imagery for the description of upper sublittoral benthic communities in glaciated and ice-free Arctic fjords
reason: Ecological study of wild Arctic benthic fauna from underwater video mosaics; organisms were identified and counted by manual visual annotation (Labelbox). Mosaicking is only image preparation; no computer vision analysis of the animals is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Reef complexity influences distribution and habitat choice of the corallivorous seastar Culcita schmideliana in the Maldives
reason: The only computer vision is Structure-from-Motion photogrammetry, used to rebuild reef topography (habitat complexity: LRI and slope). Seastars were counted by divers on belt transects, not from images, and juvenile corals were measured by hand in ImageJ. The image analysis is about habitat structure, not about detecting or analysing animals.

title: Sea snake diversity at the Entrecasteaux atolls, Coral Sea, as revealed by video observations at unbaited stations
reason: Ecological survey of wild sea snakes with remote unbaited underwater video; species were identified and counted manually by the authors, with no computer vision or automated image analysis.

title: Mushroom to manoeuvre? Using photogrammetry to track the movement and survival of free-living corals
reason: Applies structure-from-motion photogrammetry to underwater images to reconstruct a reef and track movement and survival of wild free-living mushroom corals in a remote lagoon.

title: Properties of an attention-grabbing motion signal: a comparison of tail and body movements in a lizard
reason: Primary behavioural study that tracks body and tail points in two-camera video of wild, free-roaming lizards and reconstructs their motion in 3D. The image analysis is frame-by-frame point location in Matlab plus direct linear transformation, so the computer vision content is modest and borderline.

title: SSoB: searching a scene-oriented architecture for underwater object detection
reason: Proposes a NAS-based detector for underwater images of marine animals (echinus, holothurian, scallop, starfish) on URPC2020 and UODD. The paper does not say whether these animals are wild; they are coded as free-ranging underwater benthic animals.

title: Attentive fine-grained recognition for cross-domain few-shot classification
reason: Generic cross-domain few-shot classification method tested on general benchmarks (mini-ImageNet, CUB, Cars, Places, Plantae); birds appear only as classes of the CUB fine-grained benchmark and wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Refined marine object detector with attention-based spatial pyramid pooling networks and bidirectional feature fusion strategy
reason: CNN-based detector for marine animals (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish) in underwater images, partly captured by an underwater robot in a natural ocean environment.

title: Computational metadata generation methods for biological specimen image collections
reason: Computer vision is applied to images of preserved museum fish specimens from natural history collections (INHS, UWZM), not to wild free-ranging animals.

title: Studying feral horse behavior from the sky
reason: Invited review article summarising earlier drone-based behavioural studies of feral horses. Positions and identities were marked manually in the imagery; no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated, and automation is only named as future work.

title: Automated entrance monitoring of managed bumble bees
reason: Hardware and image-processing system for monitoring hive entrances of managed (commercial) bumble bee colonies; the subject is managed pollinators, not wild animals.

title: Long-term tracking and quantification of individual behavior in bumble bee colonies
reason: Tag tracking and pose estimation are applied to bumble bee colonies reared in the lab and filmed in a robotic imaging rig; no images of free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Large-scale underwater fish recognition via deep adversarial learning
reason: Proposes an adversarial training framework for fish species classification from underwater images, including footage from underwater observatories in Taiwan (free-ranging fish) alongside web-collected and other fish image datasets.

title: Using machine learning and DeepLabCut in animal behavior
reason: Commentary on DeepLabCut; the only analysed data are laboratory videos of Poecilia mexicana in a fish tank under controlled conditions, no wild free-ranging animals.

title: Parallel lasers and digital photography to estimate limb size of chimpanzees (Pan troglodytes) at Ngogo, Kibale National Park, Uganda
reason: Applies photogrammetric image analysis (parallel lasers as scale, pixel measurements in ImageJ) to digital photographs of wild chimpanzees to estimate limb size.

title: Taxonomic resolution of coral image classification with Convolutional Neural Network
reason: Primary study that fine-tunes a CNN to classify underwater images of hard corals (animals, order Scleractinia) from reefs worldwide at species, genus and family level.

title: Geometric algebra graph neural network for cross-domain few-shot classification
reason: Generic few-shot cross-domain classification method (GA-GNN); birds appear only as classes of the CUB fine-grained benchmark alongside cars, scenes and plants; wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Multiple attentional path aggregation network for marine object detection
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for marine animals (echinus, holothurian, scallop, starfish) in underwater images taken in the sea at a marine ranch, and tests it on the MUED marine life dataset. A marine ranch might count as aquaculture, but the animals live on the open seabed. A pool test with model animals and a PASCAL VOC test are extra parts.

title: Detecting spider monkeys from the sky using a high-definition RGB camera: a rapid-assessment survey method?
reason: Drone RGB videos of wild spider monkeys were reviewed manually by human coders in a video player; no computer vision or automated image analysis method was developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Flight speed and time of day heavily influence rainforest canopy wildlife counts from drone-mounted thermal camera surveys
reason: Drone thermal/RGB video of wild rainforest canopy animals is reviewed manually by human observers; no computer vision or automated image analysis is applied, only statistical modelling (GLMMs) of human detections.

title: Evaluation of thermal infrared imaging from uninhabited aerial vehicles for arboreal wildlife surveillance
reason: All animal imagery comes from semi-free-ranging Japanese macaques kept in a four-hectare enclosure at a monkey park; no wild free-ranging animals analysed.

title: Detection of Bonobos (Pan Paniscus) in Tropical Rainforest Canopies Using Drone-Based Thermal Imaging: A First Step Towards Accurately Estimating Population Sizes?
reason: Applies drone-based thermal imaging, with thermal image processing software, to detect wild bonobos in their natural rainforest habitat.

title: Novel modified convolutional neural network and FFA algorithm for fish species classification
reason: Primary study proposing a computer vision pipeline (segmentation, SURF, modified CNN) for classifying five reef fish species from images; the stated motivation is monitoring fish in native environments. The paper does not state whether the images show wild or captive fish.

title: An ultra-specific image dataset for automated insect identification
reason: Dataset and benchmark for image classification of wild tiger beetle genera from field, photographer and web images.

title: Fish recognition in complex underwater scenes based on targeted sample transfer learning
reason: Proposes a CNN transfer-learning method to classify fish species in images from underwater observatories in Taiwan (free-ranging reef fish).

title: Underwater images quality improvement techniques for feature extraction based on comparative analysis for species classification
reason: Proposes underwater image enhancement (ALE) and compares feature extractors (SURF, SIFT, PCA) as preprocessing for underwater species classification. The animals shown are never described, so the subject type is not reported. Inclusion is borderline: it rests on the paper's stated aim of species classification in seawater.

title: Automatic fish counting via a multi-scale dense residual network
reason: Proposes a CNN density-regression method to count fish in underwater images. The images are web-collected underwater fish pictures (goldfish, carp, hairtail and others) plus phone photos of ornamental fish in a park, so wild fish are plausibly mixed with captive or ornamental ones.

title: Identification and classification of wild animals from video sequences using hybrid deep residual convolutional neural network
reason: Proposes a hybrid deep residual CNN (DRCNN-TSOA) to classify wild animals in camera-trap imagery from the Snapshot Serengeti dataset.

title: Occlusion aware underwater object tracking using hybrid adaptive deep SORT -YOLOv3 approach
reason: Proposes a deep learning detection and tracking method for fish in underwater videos, including the Fish4Knowledge coastal footage from Taiwan.

title: A deep learning-based pipeline for mosquito detection and classification from wingbeat sounds
reason: The paper detects and classifies mosquito species and sex from wingbeat audio recordings of laboratory-strain mosquitoes; no image or video data are analysed.

title: OpenMonkeyChallenge: Dataset and Benchmark Challenges for Pose Estimation of Non-human Primates
reason: Pose estimation dataset and benchmark for non-human primates; images come from the Internet (Flickr, YouTube, natural contexts) together with primate research centers and a zoo, so wild/free-ranging and captive animals are mixed.

title: AnimalTrack: A Benchmark for Multi-Animal Tracking in the Wild
reason: Introduces a multi-animal tracking benchmark of YouTube videos and evaluates 14 trackers on it; the 10 categories mix wild animals (deer, dolphin, penguin, zebra) with domestic ones (chicken, pig, horse).

title: Overcoming the Domain Gap in Neural Action Representations
reason: Self-supervised neural action decoding on tethered transgenic laboratory Drosophila recorded with two-photon microscopy and infrared cameras, plus human ECoG and H3.6M data; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: A deep neural network framework for detection and identification of bengal tigers
venue: Innovations in Systems and Software Engineering
reason: Proposes a CNN-based system for detecting and individually identifying Royal Bengal Tigers for wild population monitoring in the Sundarbans; images were collected from online sources and whether the pictured tigers are wild or captive is not stated.

title: Fractal adaptive weight synthesized–local directional pattern–based image classification using enhanced tree seed algorithm
reason: Proposes a texture descriptor and optimised ELM classifier, evaluated on in-situ underwater coral reef image datasets (corals and urchins on wild reefs), plus two generic texture benchmarks.

title: Prototype-based classifier learning for long-tailed visual recognition
reason: Generic long-tailed visual recognition method evaluated on general benchmarks (CIFAR, ImageNet-LT, Places-LT, iNaturalist 2018); wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Lightweight Transformers make strong encoders for underwater object detection
reason: Proposes a transformer-CNN detector for underwater marine organisms (holothurian, scallop, starfish, echinus) in URPC 2021 underwater images; aquaculture origin not stated.

title: Research on fish identification in tropical waters under unconstrained environment based on transfer learning
reason: ResNet50 transfer learning is applied to classify tropical fish in underwater surveillance video filmed in open sea at artificial reefs and coral reef areas; the fish are free-ranging.

title: Noninvasive Tracking of Every Individual in Unmarked Mouse Groups Using Multi-Camera Fusion and Deep Learning
reason: Tracking of laboratory C57BL/6J mice in an acrylic experimental box with a multi-camera set-up; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: KSRFB-net: detecting and identifying butterflies in ecological images based on human visual mechanism
venue: International Journal of Machine Learning and Cybernetics
reason: Proposes an object detection network for detecting and identifying butterflies in ecological images taken in the butterfly habitat; specimen images are added to training.

title: Drones and Bathymetry Show the Importance of Optimal Water Depth for Nest Placement Within Breeding Colonies of Western and Clark’s Grebes
reason: Drone images were stitched into an orthomosaic and the grebe nests were marked by hand in ArcGIS. The analysis is a resource selection function (logistic regression) on habitat variables. No automated image analysis or computer vision method is developed or applied to the animals.

title: Classifying and Mapping Cultural Ecosystem Services Using Artificial Intelligence and Social Media Data
reason: A CNN classifies Flickr photographs into cultural ecosystem service categories. Animals appear only inside a broad 'Nature Appreciation' class together with plants; wildlife is not the subject or application of the study.

title: Detecting Changes in Dynamic Social Networks Using Multiply-Labeled Movement Data
venue: Journal of Agricultural Biological and Environmental Statistics
reason: The paper builds a Bayesian statistical movement and social-network model and fits it to dolphin positions that were already derived from drone images. Image collection and tracking are described in a separate paper (Durban et al., 2022), and this paper does no image analysis of its own.

title: Population density, habitat use and activity patterns of endangered hog deer in Cambodia
reason: Camera-trap ecological survey of wild hog deer (density, habitat use, activity patterns) using a random encounter model; species were identified manually with a field guide and no computer vision or automated image analysis was applied.

title: Estimating the density of small mammals using the selfie trap is an effective camera trapping method
reason: Field-ecology comparison of selfie-trap camera trapping with live trapping for small mammals. Videos were sorted to species and individuals manually by human observers; no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Reducing identification errors of African carnivores from photographs through computer-assisted workflow
reason: Applies the HotSpotter pattern recognition algorithm (via African Carnivore Wildbook) to camera-trap images of wild cheetahs and leopards in Namibia to revise individual identifications.

title: Comparison of Two Stereo-Video Software for the Assessment of Marine Resources
venue: Thalassas An International Journal of Marine Sciences
reason: Stereo-video videogrammetry (image-based 3D measurement) applied to footage of free-swimming wild common dolphinfish recorded by a stereo-BRUV in open ocean, plus calibration tests in a pool.

title: Deep-learning with context sensitive quantization and interpolation for underwater image compression and quality image restoration
reason: Proposes a deep-learning compression and restoration method for underwater images of fish from Fish4Knowledge underwater cameras. The reconstructed images are then classified by fish type. The paper does not explicitly say the fish are wild.

title: An open-set framework for underwater image classification using autoencoders
reason: Proposes an autoencoder plus EfficientNet open-set classifier for fish species images, evaluated on the WildFish dataset of real fish images; the paper does not state whether the fish are wild or captive.

title: Reidentifying Asian Elephants from Ear Images Using a Cascade of Convolutional Neural Networks and Explaining with GradCAM
reason: Primary study proposing a YOLO + Xception CNN cascade to re-identify individual wild Asian elephants from ear images taken in Udawalawe National Park, Sri Lanka.

title: Multispecies facial detection for individual identification of wildlife: a case study across ursids
reason: Develops a CNN-based multispecies bear face detector and individual ID pipeline; trained on captive bears but also evaluated on a test set of wild brown bears.

title: Automated, high-throughput image calibration for parallel-laser photogrammetry
reason: Primary study presenting two automated image-analysis methods (machine-learning masking plus image processing) to locate laser spots in parallel-laser photogrammetry photographs of wild mountain gorillas and wild savannah baboons.

title: Morphometrics and body condition of southern right whales on the calving grounds at Port Ross, Auckland Islands
reason: UAV photogrammetry of wild southern right whales. Lengths and widths were measured manually in a GUI and individuals were identified manually from callosities. The paper uses no automated computer vision method; its analysis is PCA on the measurements.

title: Evaluating the use of thermal imagery to count harbor seals in aerial surveys
reason: Aerial colour and thermal imagery of wild harbor seals is reviewed and counted manually by a biologist; the analysis is a Bayesian statistical model of counts, with no computer vision method applied to the animal images.

title: Feasibility of using convolutional neural networks for individual-identification of wild Asian elephants
reason: Primary study evaluating CNN models for individual identification from hand-held photographs of wild Asian elephants in a national park.

title: Extreme moulting site fidelity of the Saimaa ringed seal
reason: Ecological site-fidelity study of wild Saimaa ringed seals using photo-identification; individuals were matched manually by eye against a catalogue, and no computer vision method was developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Similarity learning networks for animal individual re-identification: an ecological perspective
reason: Primary study evaluating CNN similarity networks for individual re-identification on images of chimpanzees, humpback whales, Siberian tigers, fruit flies and humans; part of the data (whale flukes, tigers 'in the Wild') concerns wild animals, though the paper does not state the capture conditions of each dataset.

title: Flukebook: an open-source AI platform for cetacean photo identification
reason: Describes a platform applying detection and individual photo-identification algorithms to photographs of free-ranging whales and dolphins.

title: Evaluating likelihood-based photogrammetry for individual recognition of four species of northern ungulates
reason: All photographs are of captive ungulates held at a wildlife preserve and a research station; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed. The method is semi-manual photogrammetry (landmark distances measured by hand in ImageJ) followed by likelihood-based matching.

title: Pre-trained models are not enough: active and lifelong learning is important for long-term visual monitoring of mammals in biodiversity research—Individual identification and attribute prediction with image features from deep neural networks and decoupled decision models applied to elephants and great apes
reason: Primary study applying deep-feature-based individual identification and attribute prediction to images and camera-trap videos of wild elephants, gorillas and chimpanzees recorded in national parks and forests.

title: Drone-based photogrammetry assessments of body size and body condition of Antillean manatees
reason: Drone photogrammetry of body size was tested only on captive manatees housed in aquarium pools, with no free-ranging animals in the analysed data.

title: Matching individual Ladoga ringed seals across short-term image sequences
reason: Develops a computer vision pipeline (instance segmentation, grouping, pattern extraction, re-identification) on field images of wild Ladoga ringed seals taken with game cameras and handheld cameras.

title: A novel technique for aging male African elephants (Loxodonta africana) using craniofacial photogrammetry and geometric morphometrics
reason: Borderline exclusion. Wild elephants are photographed, but landmarks are placed by hand and measurements come from manual photogrammetry and statistics; no automated computer vision method is applied, and the paper names computer vision only as future work.

title: Artificial intelligence for right whale photo identification: from data science competition to worldwide collaboration
reason: Primary study applying and evaluating computer vision algorithms (detection and individual photo identification) on aerial and lateral photographs of wild North Atlantic and southern right whales.

title: Individual identification of armadillos (Mammalia, Cingulata) using a photo-identification software
reason: Applies computer-assisted photo-ID (Wild-ID, SIFT) to head-shield images of armadillos. The data mix wild individuals captured in the field with captive animals and museum specimens.

title: Growth trajectories of wild Assamese macaques (Macaca assamensis) determined from parallel laser photogrammetry
reason: Applies digital photogrammetry (parallel laser and distance meter methods) to photographs of wild Assamese macaques to measure forearm length and estimate growth trajectories.

title: Manatee population traits elucidated through photo-identification
reason: Review of manual photo-identification of Florida manatees using the MIPS catalog; no computer vision method is developed or applied (matching is manual by feature codes).

title: Assessing neophobia and exploration while accounting for social context: an example application in scimitar-horned oryx
reason: Study analyses aerial video of a captive herd of scimitar-horned oryx in an enclosure at SCBI; behaviour was annotated manually with BORIS, no wild animals and no automated computer vision.

title: Body length and growth pattern of free-ranging Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins off Mikura Island estimated using an underwater 3D camera
reason: Applies stereo-photogrammetry on underwater 3D photographs to measure body length of free-ranging wild dolphins.

title: A photogrammetric method to estimate total length of the largest mammal, the blue whale (Balaenoptera musculus)
reason: Boat-based photogrammetry of free-ranging blue whales in which photographs are joined and measured manually with Photoshop and SigmaScan software, followed by a Bayesian statistical model; no automated computer vision / image analysis algorithm is developed or applied.

title: Remote and non-invasive quantification of ‘Tattoo Skin Disease-Like’ dermatopathy in endangered Arabian Sea humpback whales using drone photography
reason: Wild Arabian Sea humpback whales photographed by drone, but lesions are diagnosed visually by an expert and outlined by hand with Photoshop selection tools to count pixels. No computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Individual identification and photographic techniques in mammalian ecological and behavioural research—Part 2: Field studies and applications
reason: Editorial preface to a journal special issue on photo-identification in mammalian field studies; it discusses methodological issues and introduces the collected papers but presents no primary computer vision research and analyses no image data.

title: Application of multi-species photo-ID database management systems: a user’s perspective
reason: Editorial / user's perspective on photo-ID database management systems (Wildbook, catRlog, DISCOVERY). It runs no computer vision experiments and analyses no image data; the system described in the appendix (DISCOVERY) relies on manual matching without automated image recognition.

title: Perception for Underwater Robots
reason: The paper is a literature survey of perception methods for underwater robots, such as sonar, vision, SLAM and bathymetry. It contains no primary study of wild animals.

title: Fish recognition model for fraud prevention using convolutional neural networks
reason: Images show dead commercial fish photographed at fish sales establishments for food-fraud prevention in the fisheries supply chain, not wild free-ranging animals.

title: Automated detection of microfossil fish teeth from slide images using combined deep learning models
reason: Detects microfossil fish teeth (ichthyoliths) on glass slides imaged with a digital microscope. The subjects are fossil specimens in a laboratory microscopy set-up, not wild free-ranging animals.

title: Automatically recognizing four-legged animal behaviors to enhance welfare using spatial temporal graph convolutional networks
reason: Video-based behaviour recognition (skeleton via pose estimation + NAS-designed GCN) on a multispecies dataset of non-domestic four-legged animals (e.g., lion), aimed at zoos and natural reserves. The paper does not say where the videos came from, so subject type is not reported.

title: A deep transfer learning model for head pose estimation in rhesus macaques during cognitive tasks: Towards a nonrestraint noninvasive 3Rs approach
reason: Head pose classification on video of research-colony rhesus macaques housed at a breeding/research facility during cognitive experiments; no wild or free-ranging animals in the analysed data.

title: Multi-scale Sparse Network with Cross-Attention Mechanism for image-based butterflies fine-grained classification
reason: CNN-based fine-grained classification of butterfly images, almost all taken in natural habitat (some specimen images); wildlife conservation is the stated application.

title: Machine-based mosquito taxonomy with a lightweight network-fused efficient dual ConvNet with residual learning and Knowledge Distillation
reason: Proposes a lightweight CNN with knowledge distillation to classify mosquito species (non-domestic insects) from images; the paper does not say how or where the images were taken.

title: A Purely Visual Re-ID Approach for Bumblebees (Bombus terrestris)
reason: Visual re-identification of bumblebees from two commercial hives (precision beekeeping context); no wild or free-ranging animals in the analysed data.

title: Putting eagle rays on the map by coupling aerial video-surveys and deep learning
reason: Primary study applying a CNN object detector to aerial video images of wild eagle rays in a coral lagoon.

title: Recent advances of target tracking applications in aquaculture with emphasis on fish
reason: Review article on fish tracking algorithms in aquaculture; it is not primary research and states that no data was used.

title: Customized deep neural network model for autonomous and efficient surveillance of wildlife in national parks
reason: Develops a custom CNN object detector for wild animals (lion, tiger, elephant) and vehicles, aimed at surveillance of wildlife in national parks; images come from Open Images and the paper does not say whether the animals are wild or captive.

title: Underwater object detection using collaborative weakly supervision
reason: Proposes a deep learning detector for underwater marine organisms (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish) in underwater images.

title: Light weight convolutional neural network and low-dimensional images transformation approach for classification of thermal images
reason: Generic thermal image classification method; animals (cat, dog) appear only as classes alongside car, man and drone, and wildlife is not the stated subject.

title: Behavioral signatures of structured feature detection during courtship in Drosophila
reason: Laboratory-reared Drosophila melanogaster pairs filmed in acrylic arenas inside fly incubators; pose estimation is used for a neuroethology study, with no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Isolation disrupts social interactions and destabilizes brain development in bumblebees
reason: Laboratory study of commercially purchased bumblebee colonies reared in chambers and filmed in a Petri dish arena; pose tracking is used for behavioural neuroscience, no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Active vision during prey capture in wild marmoset monkeys
reason: Primary study applying markerless pose tracking (SLEAP) to field videos of wild marmosets hunting insects.

title: Population structure of Asconema setubalense Kent, 1870 at Concepción Seamount, Canary Islands (Spain). Methodological approach using non-invasive techniques
venue: Deep Sea Research Part I Oceanographic Research Papers
reason: Applies image analysis (threshold-based wand segmentation in ImageJ and Structure-from-Motion 3D reconstruction in Pix4D) to towed-vehicle video of wild deep-sea sponges on a seamount to measure size and population structure.

title: Using Web images to train a deep neural network to detect sparsely distributed wildlife in large volumes of remotely sensed imagery: A case study of polar bears on sea ice
reason: Primary study training a CNN (ResNet-50) with Web images to detect wild polar bears in aerial survey imagery over sea ice in Baffin Bay.

title: Graph ranking based butterfly segmentation in ecological images
reason: Proposes a graph-based computer vision method to segment butterflies in ecological images of natural environments.

title: Automated detection and classification of southern African Roman seabream using mask R-CNN
reason: Applies Mask R-CNN to BRUV underwater video of wild roman seabream in South African coastal waters for detection, counting and tracking.

title: Tag Frequency Difference: Rapid estimation of image set relevance for species occurrence data using general-purpose image classifiers
reason: Proposes a method using general-purpose image classifiers to estimate the fraction of images in online sources that show wild invasive fauna (cane toads, German wasps, wild rabbits). Some social media rabbit images showed domestic rabbits.

title: A case study of utilizing YOLOT based quantitative detection algorithm for marine benthos
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv4 (YOLOT) for detecting and counting wild marine benthic organisms in real seafloor images.

title: A two-stage adaptive thresholding segmentation for noisy low-contrast images
reason: Proposes a 2-stage adaptive thresholding segmentation method and tests it on in situ underwater images of wild jellyfish in coastal waters.

title: A novel age-group classification method for Irrawaddy dolphins based on dorsal fin shape features
reason: Primary study proposing an image-based age-group classification method using dorsal fin shape features from photographs of free-ranging Irrawaddy dolphins in the Mekong River.

title: Motion vectors and deep neural networks for video camera traps
reason: Primary study developing a camera-trap video filtering pipeline (motion vectors plus a YOLOv4-tiny animal detector), trained on WCS camera trap data and evaluated on static-camera animal videos from GBIF.

title: Shark detection and classification with machine learning
reason: Develops CNN-based detection and classification of sharks in crowd-sourced images, Instagram images, baited remote underwater video and YouTube videos showing sharks in nature.

title: Passive acoustic monitoring of animal populations with transfer learning
reason: The study classifies animal vocalisations in passive acoustic recordings (spectrograms of audio); no images or video of animals are analysed.

title: Prospects for the monitoring of the great cormorant (Phalacrocorax carbo sinensis) using a drone and stationary cameras
reason: Automated detection and counting of wild migratory great cormorants on carp ponds from UAV (thermal, RGB, multispectral) images and stationary 360° camera video.

title: Automated distance estimation for wildlife camera trapping
reason: Camera-to-animal distance estimation method for camera trapping, but the only animal imagery analysed is from a zoo enclosure (Lindenthal Zoo: geese, goats, donkeys, deer); the training datasets contain no wild animals.

title: Class incremental learning for wildlife biodiversity monitoring in camera trap images
reason: Proposes a class incremental learning method for species classification in camera trap images of wild animals from Serengeti National Park.

title: A text and image analysis workflow using citizen science data to extract relevant social media records: Combining red kite observations from Flickr, eBird and iNaturalist
reason: Applies CNN image classification (with text metadata) to Flickr, eBird and iNaturalist images to retrieve observations of wild red kites in the Chilterns.

title: Fast and accurate mapping of fine scale abundance of a VME in the deep sea with computer vision
reason: Primary study applying a YOLOv4 CNN to AUV seabed images to detect, count and measure the wild deep-sea xenophyophore Syringammina fragilissima in situ. The organism is single-celled, but the paper treats it as benthic megafauna and a VME indicator taxon, and no exclusion criterion fits.

title: Wildlife 3D multi-object tracking
reason: The 3D multi-object tracking method is developed and evaluated only on video of goats kept at a zoo (Lindenthal Zoo, Cologne); no wild or free-ranging animals appear in the analysed data.

title: Instance segmentation and tracking of animals in wildlife videos: SWIFT - segmentation with filtering of tracklets
reason: All analysed video shows red deer and fallow deer recorded inside a wildlife park (Wildpark Rolandseck), i.e. park-held animals. Borderline: the paper frames this as wildlife monitoring 'in their natural environment' and never states an enclosure, but no free-ranging wild population outside the park is analysed.

title: Environmentally adaptive fish or no-fish classification for river video fish counters using high-performance desktop and embedded hardware
reason: Computer vision pipeline classifying underwater fish counter videos of wild migrating freshwater fish in European river fishways as fish or no-fish.

title: An approach to multi-class imbalanced problem in ecology using machine learning
reason: The study classifies fish species from a tabular count dataset with 4 variables using ensemble machine learning. It does not analyse any images or video.

title: Optimized lightweight CA-transformer: Using transformer for fine-grained visual categorization
reason: Generic fine-grained transformer method evaluated on ImageNet, a plant disease dataset and the bird benchmarks Birds and CUB-Birds. The birds are only benchmark classes, and the paper gives no wildlife data or field context for them.

title: Improved seabird image classification based on dual transfer learning framework and spatial pyramid pooling
reason: Proposes a CNN-based dual transfer learning framework that classifies images of 10 wild seabird species.

title: YOLO-Fish: A robust fish detection model to detect fish in realistic underwater environment
reason: Proposes YOLO-based fish detection models evaluated on underwater images of free-ranging fish in natural Australian marine habitats.

title: An image enhancement approach for coral reef fish detection in underwater videos
reason: Proposes a saliency-based image enhancement method for deep learning detection of wild coral reef fish in underwater videos (LCF-15 / Fish4Knowledge).

title: Automatically detecting the wild giant panda using deep learning with context and species distribution model
reason: Proposes a deep-learning detection method (modified YOLOv5 with context memory bank and species distribution model) for wild giant pandas in infrared camera-trap images from a nature reserve.

title: Fish image recognition method based on multi-layer feature fusion convolutional network
reason: Proposes a CNN (Tripmix-Net) for fine-grained species classification of wild fish images from the WildFish and Fish4Knowledge datasets, motivated by conserving fish diversity.

title: Identification of free-ranging mugger crocodiles by applying deep learning methods on UAV imagery
reason: Primary study applying CNNs to UAV imagery for individual identification of free-ranging mugger crocodiles; captive gharials and saltwater crocodiles are used only as negative test classes.

title: Human vs. machine: Detecting wildlife in camera trap images
reason: Primary study evaluating the MegaDetector object detection model against manual human review on camera trap images of wild caribou and other wildlife in Arctic Alaska.

title: Embracing imperfection: Machine-assisted invertebrate classification in real-world datasets
reason: Images are of collected, vouchered invertebrate specimens from pitfall traps photographed in bulk against a white background; no images of live free-ranging animals.

title: YoloXT: A object detection algorithm for marine benthos
reason: Proposes a CNN/transformer object detector for marine benthic organisms in real seafloor underwater images (URPC 2020, IOC seamount images, Brackish dataset).

title: ‘I know the tiger by his paw’: A non-invasive footprint identification technique for monitoring individual Amur tigers (Panthera tigris altaica) in snow
reason: Image-based footprint identification technique (landmark morphometrics from footprint photographs) to identify individual Amur tigers; trained on captive tigers and applied to free-ranging tiger footprint trails in Northeast China.

title: Video-based bird posture recognition using dual feature-rates deep fusion convolutional neural network
reason: Proposes a video-based deep learning model for recognising behaviours of various bird species in web-collected videos (birds perching on trees, flying, swimming); the paper does not say whether the birds are wild or captive, but the stated application is bird protection.

title: Assessing drivers of intra-seasonal grassland dynamics in a Kenyan savannah using digital repeat photography
reason: Primary study that applies a pre-trained detector (MegaDetector) to camera-trap photographs to count wild and domestic grazers in a Kenyan savannah grassland; the animal counts serve as a grazing-intensity proxy in a study mainly about grassland greenness.

title: Classifying the content of social media images to support cultural ecosystem service assessments using deep learning models
reason: CNN classification of social media images into cultural ecosystem service content categories (natural/human, landscape, posing, etc.). Animals appear only inside a broad 'Species' class shared with plants; wildlife is not the stated subject.

title: Coastal fisheries resource monitoring through A deep learning-based underwater video analysis
reason: Primary study that creates an annotated underwater video dataset of wild fish from a sub-sea observatory and retrains Mask R-CNN for fish detection and instance segmentation.

title: Deep learning-assisted high resolution mapping of vulnerable habitats within the Capbreton Canyon System, Bay of Biscay
reason: Primary study applying deep-learning object detection to underwater photographs of wild cold-water coral colonies (Dendrophyllia cornigera) taken in situ, feeding a species distribution model.

title: Methods studies for attached marine organisms detecting based on convolutional neural network
reason: Proposes an improved YOLO v5 to detect attached marine fouling organisms (non-domestic invertebrates such as barnacles, mussels, tubeworms) in images; primary research.

title: Motion parameters measurement of user-defined key points using 3D pose estimation
reason: 3D pose estimation method; the only animal data are a Koi swimming in a lab water tank and cheetahs filmed at captive breeding/outreach centres (AcinoSet). No wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Smart Oceans: Artificial intelligence and marine protected area governance
reason: Governance perspective paper on AI-enabled mobile marine protected areas based on interviews and literature review; no primary computer vision analysis of image or video data.

title: Improving importance estimation in covariate shift for providing accurate prediction error
reason: Generic machine-learning paper on importance estimation for covariate shift. The plankton application uses deep features that another paper extracted beforehand and treats them as tabular covariates, so this paper does no image analysis of its own. The other experiments use UCI tabular datasets.

title: Odonata identification using Customized Convolutional Neural Networks
reason: CNN-based species classification of photographs of wild dragonflies and damselflies (Odonata) gathered from web and photographer sources.

title: Use of object detection in camera trap image identification: Assessing a method to rapidly and accurately classify human and animal detections for research and application in recreation ecology
reason: Applies and evaluates an existing object-detection model (MegaDetector) on camera trap images of wild animals and humans from a provincial park.

title: Automatic detection for the world's rarest primates based on a tropical rainforest environment
reason: Proposes an image-filter YOLO detector for wild Hainan gibbons in infrared-triggered camera footage from Bawangling Nature Reserve.

title: Human expertise combined with artificial intelligence improves performance of snow leopard camera trap studies
reason: All analysed images show captive snow leopards photographed in US and European zoos; no wild or free-ranging animals are in the data.

title: High-accuracy in the classification of butchery cut marks and crocodile tooth marks using machine learning methods and computer vision algorithms
reason: The images show bone surface marks under a microscope: crocodile tooth marks made by captive crocodiles in a zoo experiment, and experimental cut marks on cow bones. No wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: A Communication Interface for Multilayer Cloud Computing Architecture for Low Cost Underwater Vehicles*
reason: The paper proposes a cloud communication interface for underwater vehicles. Semantic segmentation with SUIM-Net on the SUIM benchmark is only a workload to test latency; fish and invertebrates appear only as benchmark classes and wildlife is not the stated subject.

title: Audio-Visual Low Power System for Endangered Waterbirds Monitoring
reason: Primary study proposing an audio-triggered camera sensor network for wild waterbirds in wetlands. It applies image ROI detection (KAZE features) and compression to the captured bird images.

title: Computer vision for assessing species color pattern variation from web-based community science images
reason: CNN classification of colour morphs of a wild salamander species from iNaturalist community science photographs; primary research.

title: Acoustic camera system for measuring ultrasound communication in mice
reason: Laboratory mice (C57BL/6J and ICR strains) recorded in home cages inside a soundproof box; the system localizes ultrasonic vocalizations and uses video tracking of snouts. No wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Behavioral variation across the days and lives of honey bees
reason: Barcode-based automated tracking of managed honey bees (Apis mellifera) in an observation hive; domestic/managed bees (beekeeping), not wild free-ranging animals.

title: Artificial intelligence versus natural selection: Using computer vision techniques to classify bees and bee mimics
reason: CNN classification of citizen-science (iNaturalist Research Grade, non-captive) images of wild bees, bumble bees and bee-mimic insects; primary research.

title: Reassessing the role of carnivores in the formation of FLK North 3 (Olduvai Gorge, Tanzania): A pilot taphonomic analysis using Artificial Intelligence tools
reason: Computer vision classifies microscope images of tooth pits on fossil bone specimens, using a model trained on marks made by semi-captive lions and hyenas. No images of living wild or free-ranging animals are analysed, only specimens and captive experimental material.

title: Big spots in a small population: Analyzing characteristics and temporality of coat patterns in Croatian lynx population
reason: Applies ImageJ image processing (thresholding, particle analysis) to photographs of wild Eurasian lynx from Croatia, including camera-trap images of live free-ranging lynx alongside trophy pelt photographs.

title: Conservation benefits of a marine protected area on South African chondrichthyans
reason: Ecological survey of wild sharks, rays and chimaeras with baited remote underwater stereo-video. Species identification, MaxN counts and length measurements were done by human observers in EventMeasure software; no automated computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Semi-automated detection of ungulates using UAV imagery and reflective spectrometry
reason: Develops an object-based image analysis ruleset to detect reintroduced free-roaming Arabian oryx in UAV imagery of a desert protected area; captive animals supplied only hair samples, not images.

title: Machine learning based assessment of small-bodied fish tracking to evaluate spoiler baffle fish passage design
reason: Wild-caught Galaxias maculatus were housed and filmed only in a laboratory recirculating flume; no images of free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Using computer vision, image analysis and UAVs for the automatic recognition and counting of common cranes (Grus grus)
reason: Primary study developing image-analysis and YOLO v3 methods to count wild wintering common cranes in UAV thermal and RGB imagery.

title: Validating the automation of different measures of high temperature tolerance of small terrestrial insects
reason: Laboratory thermal tolerance assays on mass-bred Drosophila (plus a few field-collected arthropods and a lab housefly culture) filmed in plexiglass arenas inside a temperature cabinet and tracked with commercial software; no images of free-ranging animals.

title: Wide-angle, monocular head tracking using passive markers
reason: Marker-based monocular head-pose tracking system for laboratory rats in a behavioural arena; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: On the use of deep learning for fish species recognition and quantification on board fishing vessels
reason: Applies deep learning instance segmentation and length estimation to images of wild-caught fish on trawler conveyor belts for fisheries catch monitoring; wild marine fish, not aquaculture.

title: In an octopus's garden in the shade: Underwater image analysis of litter use by benthic octopuses
reason: The images are wild octopuses from citizen-science and web sources, but people annotated them by hand and used chi-squared tests. No computer vision or automated image analysis is developed or applied.

title: A 3D perspective on sediment turnover and feeding selectivity in blennies
reason: Image analysis (structure-from-motion photogrammetry) builds orthomosaics and elevation models of the reef habitat. Blenny locations come from divers' hand-drawn maps and are transcribed manually, so the animals are not the subject of the image analysis.

title: Is the use of deep learning an appropriate means to locate debris in the ocean without harming aquatic wildlife?
reason: Applies a CNN to underwater images to distinguish natural aquatic life (wild marine animals) from man-made debris, with the stated aim of protecting marine wildlife.

title: Deploying deep learning to estimate the abundance of marine debris from video footage
reason: The paper is about detecting and counting marine debris. Fish appear only as one auxiliary class added for context, and wildlife is not the stated subject.

title: ‘Eye in the sky’: Off-the-shelf unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) highlights exposure of marine turtles to floating litter (FML) in nearshore waters of Mayo Bay, Philippines
reason: Wild marine turtles are filmed with a UAV, but the videos are only reviewed by eye and annotated by hand. No computer vision method is developed or applied; the analysis is spatial statistics.

title: Animal image identification and classification using deep neural networks techniques
reason: Proposes a deep learning method robust to noisy labels for classifying wild animal species in camera-trap images (Snapshot Serengeti, Panama-Netherlands). A small dataset that includes pets is also described.

title: ChickTrack – A quantitative tracking tool for measuring chicken activity
reason: The study detects, counts and tracks domesticated chickens on poultry farms; no wild or free-ranging non-domestic animals are analysed.

title: In situ measurement of fish color based on machine vision: A case study of measuring a clownfish’s color
reason: Machine-vision colour measurement of ornamental clownfish kept in a small aquarium inside a studio box, motivated by fish farming and the ornamental fish industry; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: A protocol for developing a classification system of mosquitoes using transfer learning
reason: Transfer-learning classification of two Aedes mosquito species from a Kaggle image set taken with one device, the same background and the same lighting (a controlled set-up); no images of wild, free-ranging animals. The paper does not explicitly say the mosquitoes were laboratory-reared, so E-LAB rests on the controlled imaging conditions.

title: Hybridization of Deep Convolutional Neural Network for Underwater Object Detection and Tracking Model
reason: Proposes a hybrid deep CNN for detecting and tracking underwater objects, mainly marine animals such as fish, crabs, starfish and scallops, in public underwater video datasets.

title: The IoT-based real-time image processing for animal recognition and classification using deep convolutional neural network (DCNN)
reason: CNN classification of elephant, leopard, gaur and bear images for human-wildlife conflict early warning; elephant images come from a captive camp, the other species from forest officials and online sources (described as camera trap images), so wild and captive animals are mixed.

title: Rethinking general underwater object detection: Datasets, challenges, and solutions
reason: Presents a real-world underwater object detection dataset (RUOD) of marine organisms (fish, turtles, starfish, corals, etc.) from web images and benchmarks detectors on it; computer vision on images of free-ranging marine animals.

title: AntVideoRecord: Autonomous system to capture the locomotor activity of leafcutter ants
reason: Open-hardware paper describing an autonomous video recorder for leafcutter ant trails. Ant counting is mentioned only as done later with separate software; no image-analysis method is developed, applied or evaluated here.

title: Robust learning from noisy web data for fine-Grained recognition
reason: Generic web-supervised fine-grained classification method evaluated on bird, aircraft and car benchmarks; wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Detection confidence driven multi-object tracking to recover reliable tracks from unreliable detections
reason: Proposes a multi-object tracking algorithm and a new dataset of real-world underwater video of wild fish recorded off Hawai'i. Car and pedestrian datasets are also used, but wild fish tracking is a stated application.

title: Mix-ViT: Mixing attentive vision transformer for ultra-fine-grained visual categorization
reason: Generic ultra-fine-grained classification method aimed at crop cultivar leaves; animals appear only via the CUB-200-2011 bird benchmark and Leeds Butterfly visualisation, wildlife is not the stated application.

title: Applying image clustering to phylogenetic analysis: A trial
reason: The study clusters images of Corybas orchids, which are plants, to reconstruct their phylogeny. No animals are analysed.

title: Long-term monitoring reveals unprecedented stability of a vent mussel assemblage on the Mid-Atlantic Ridge
reason: Ecological time-series study of a wild deep-sea hydrothermal vent assemblage using seafloor observatory imagery; applies image processing (SURF/homography registration, ImageJ segmentation and automated counting of zoanthids) alongside manual annotation.

title: Machine Learning interspecific identification of mouse first lower molars (genus Mus Linnaeus, 1758) and application to fossil remains from the Estrecho Cave (Spain)
reason: Analyses photographs of isolated molars from museum collection specimens and fossil remains (manually digitised landmarks, ML on morphometric data); no living wild animals imaged.

title: Animal species detection and classification framework based on modified multi-scale attention mechanism and feature pyramid network
reason: Proposes a CNN detection and classification framework evaluated on animal image datasets including African wildlife (buffalo, elephant, rhino, zebra) alongside domestic animal classes; wildlife detection is the stated application.

title: Anchor scour from shipping and the defaunation of rocky reefs: A quantitative assessment
venue: The Science of The Total Environment
reason: Ecological impact study of wild sessile reef invertebrates. Stereo-ROV imagery was annotated manually in EventMeasure software, and no computer vision method was developed or applied.

title: A Video Plankton Recorder user guide: Lessons learned from in situ plankton imaging in shallow and turbid coastal waters in the Belgian part of the North Sea
reason: In situ imaging of wild zooplankton in the North Sea with a Video Plankton Recorder. Automated ROI segmentation (AutoDeck) is evaluated across tow types, magnification settings and turbidity, and plankton densities are derived from the images.

title: Temporal characteristics of plankton indicators in coastal waters: High-frequency data from PlanktonScope
reason: Applies an in situ imaging system with deep learning (Mask R-CNN, ResNet) to classify and count wild plankton, including zooplankton such as copepods, jellyfish and mysids, in Chinese coastal waters.

title: Protocol for quantitative ethology on natural social interactions in Drosophila
reason: Laboratory protocol for pose estimation and behaviour annotation of lab-reared Drosophila melanogaster in acrylic chambers; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Bipedal locomotion in zoo apes: Revisiting the hylobatian model for bipedal origins
reason: Questionnaire survey of zoo primate caretakers about bipedal locomotion frequency; there is no image or video analysis and no computer vision. The animals are also zoo-housed only.

title: Automatic taxonomic identification based on the Fossil Image Dataset (>415,000 images) and deep convolutional neural networks
reason: Images show fossil specimens (and fossil plants) collected from the web, not living wild free-ranging animals; specimens fall under E-CAPTIVE.

title: Unmanned aerial vehicle surveys reveal unexpectedly high density of a threatened deer in a plantation forestry landscape
