title: Applying computer vision to digitised natural history collections for climate change research: Temperature‐size responses in British butterflies
reason: Computer vision is applied to digitised images of pinned museum specimens (NHM iCollections), not to live wild animals; museum specimens are excluded under E-CAPTIVE.

title: In situ size and motility measurement of aquatic invertebrates with an underwater stereoscopic camera system using tilted lenses
reason: Underwater stereo camera system with image segmentation, 3D tracking and size measurement applied to wild water boatmen filmed in situ in a saltmarsh channel.

title: A deep neural network for high‐throughput measurement of functional traits on museum skeletal specimens
reason: Computer vision is applied only to photographs of museum bird skeletal specimens; no images of wild, free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Automated call detection for acoustic surveys with structured calls of varying length
reason: The study detects Hainan gibbon calls in passive acoustic recordings; spectrogram images are derived from sound only, with no camera images or video of animals.

title: Estimating animal size or distance in camera trap images: Photogrammetry using the pinhole camera model
reason: Photogrammetric size/distance estimation from camera trap images, evaluated only on stationary 3D animal targets and captive reindeer in research station enclosures; no wild or free-ranging animals in the analysed data.

title: Long‐term automated visual monitoring of Antarctic benthic fauna
reason: Primary study applying computer vision (image differencing, Hough transform, YOLO-V5) to underwater time-lapse images of wild Antarctic benthic fauna.

title: Estimating animal density for a community of species using information obtained only from camera‐traps
reason: Statistical density-estimation method (Bayesian multi-species Random Encounter Model) on camera-trap data. Animal positions were digitised manually in Blender and converted to distances with a calibration model; no automated image analysis is applied.

title: Integrating 3D models with morphometric measurements to improve volumetric estimates in marine mammals
reason: Photogrammetric measurements from UAV images of free-ranging humpback whales are used to scale 3D models and estimate body volume. This is image-based morphometric reconstruction of wild animals.

title: CollembolAI , a macrophotography and computer vision workflow to digitize and characterize samples of soil invertebrate communities preserved in fluid
reason: Computer vision workflow evaluated only on ethanol-preserved springtail and mite specimens picked from the authors' taxonomic collection (a mock community) and photographed in a petri dish; no images of wild, free-ranging animals.

title: Digitizing the coral reef: Machine learning of underwater spectral images enables dense taxonomic mapping of benthic habitats
reason: Machine-learning segmentation of in-situ underwater hyperspectral images of a wild coral reef; classes include corals, soft corals and sponges (animals) at family, genus or species level, alongside algae and substrate.

title: Can CNN‐based species classification generalise across variation in habitat within a camera trap survey?
reason: Primary study evaluating CNN species classification on camera trap images of wild mammals in tropical forest in Malaysian Borneo.

title: An evaluation of platforms for processing camera‐trap data using artificial intelligence
reason: Although labelled a review of AI platforms, the paper carries out its own primary evaluation of detection and species classification models on four out-of-sample camera-trap datasets of wild animals.

title: Effectiveness of using drones and convolutional neural networks to monitor aquatic megafauna
reason: Primary study applying a CNN object detector to drone imagery of free-ranging Nile crocodiles (and manual drone counts of hippos) in two South African protected areas.

title: Deriving observation distances for camera trap distance sampling
reason: All analysed camera trap images show animals in an outdoor savannah enclosure at Zoo Leipzig; no wild free-ranging animals are in the data.

title: Human impacts on mammals in and around a protected area before, during, and after COVID ‐19 lockdowns
reason: Camera-trap study of wild mammals in a protected area and adjacent research forest. Automated detection software is applied to sort images into human, vehicle and animal categories before manual species identification. The computer vision component is minor; the paper is mainly an ecological statistical analysis.

title: Automatic individual recognition of Japanese macaques (Macaca fuscata) from sequential images
reason: Primary study applying CNN-based individual recognition with a sequential Bayesian filter to images and video of free-ranging Japanese macaques.

title: Are fish communities on coral reefs becoming less colourful?
reason: Image analysis (colour quantification with colordistance) of photographs of wild reef fishes collected from the Great Barrier Reef, used to study community colouration; animals are wild-caught, photographed as fresh specimens.

title: Quantifying long‐term phenological patterns of aerial insectivores roosting in the Great Lakes region using weather surveillance radar
reason: Applies a Faster R-CNN deep-learning detector and tracker to weather surveillance radar imagery to detect wild swallow and martin roosts and study their phenology.

title: Semi‐automated detection of tagged animals from camera trap images using artificial intelligence
reason: Deep-learning object detection of wing tags on wild Lappet-faced Vultures in camera trap images from Namibia; primary research.

title: Into the lion’s den: spawning success of lionfish (Pterois miles) in the Mediterranean Sea
reason: Editorial commentary summarising a histological study of lionfish reproduction; no primary computer vision research or image analysis.

title: Swimming kinematics of the Caribbean reef shark, Carcharhinus perezi
reason: The study films wild Caribbean reef sharks, but the kinematics come from landmarks tracked frame by frame in Loggerpro video-analysis software. The paper names no automated computer vision method, so the analysis is manual digitisation rather than computer vision.

title: Aposematic patterns shift continuously throughout the life of poison frogs
reason: Image analysis of pattern change in poison frogs kept in colonies at the National Aquarium; there are no wild or free-ranging animals in the analysed data.

title: Evaluating the prevalence and spatial distribution of giraffes injured by non‐target poaching
reason: Photographs of wild giraffes in a national park; individuals identified via automated pelage pattern matching (Wild-ID) for spatial capture-recapture.

title: Body volume and mass estimation of southern elephant seals using 3D range scanning and neural network models
reason: Primary study developing automated processing of 3D depth scans (infrared time-of-flight sensor) of wild southern elephant seals at a colony to reconstruct body models and estimate volume and mass.

title: Morphometrics of mammal‐eating killer whales from drone photogrammetry, with comparison to sympatric fish‐eating killer whales in the eastern North Pacific
reason: Drone photogrammetry of free-ranging Bigg's killer whales: length and body condition are measured from aerial images. The image analysis is manual (ImageJ pixel measurements).

title: Skin condition of fin whales at Antarctic feeding grounds reveals little evidence for anthropogenic impacts and high prevalence of cookiecutter shark bite lesions
reason: Aerial video of wild fin whales was screened manually by a person for skin features; no computer vision or automated image analysis method is developed or applied.

title: Individual North Atlantic right whales identified from space
reason: Whales in satellite imagery were found and identified by a trained human observer scanning the imagery in QGIS and confirmed by marine biologists; no computer vision or automated image analysis method is used.

title: Estimating body mass of sperm whales from aerial photographs
reason: UAV photogrammetry (image-based morphometric measurement) of free-ranging sperm whales to estimate body volume and mass.

title: Enhancing UAV images to improve the observation of submerged whales using a water column correction method
reason: Primary study applying an image processing method (water column correction) to UAV images of wild humpback whales to enhance their visibility for detection.

title: Fish use of restored mangroves matches that in natural mangroves regardless of forest age
reason: Primary study applying a deep learning detection model to underwater video of wild fish in restored and natural mangroves to estimate abundance.

title: Machine learning for expert‐level image‐based identification of very similar species in the hyperdiverse plant bug family Miridae (Hemiptera: Heteroptera)
reason: CNN species classification of plant bugs; trained on museum specimen photos but evaluated on web images of live, free-ranging Adelphocoris bugs, so part of the data shows wild animals.

title: Fetal growth, birth size and energetic cost of gestation in southern right whales
reason: Applies UAV aerial photogrammetry (image-based body length and width measurement) to wild southern right whales on breeding grounds in Argentina and Australia, to estimate calf birth size and the cost of gestation.

title: Chimera states among synchronous fireflies
reason: Stereo video of wild Photuris frontalis firefly swarms in a national park is analysed with flash detection, 3D reconstruction and tracking to study their collective flashing behaviour.

title: Territories within groups: the dynamic competition of drift-feeding juvenile Chinook salmon in 3-dimensional space
venue: Canadian Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences
reason: Uses stereo video and 3-D video measurement (VidSync) to track the positions and behaviour of wild juvenile Chinook Salmon in the Chena River.

title: Plastron color patterns allow for individual photo-identification in two different chelonian species
reason: Primary study testing photo-identification software (image template matching and spot pattern matching) on plastron photographs of wild tortoises and pond turtles captured and released in the field.

title: Drones reveal spatial patterning of sympatric Alaskan pinniped species and drivers of their local distributions
reason: Drone RGB and thermal survey of wild pinnipeds, but animals were located, counted and classified to species manually by an expert analyst in GIS. The only automated image processing is standard photogrammetry (orthomosaics and DSM) feeding statistical distribution models; no computer vision method is applied to the animals.

title: Detection and tracking of belugas, kayaks and motorized boats in drone video using deep learning
reason: Applies YOLOv4 detection and DeepSORT tracking to drone video of wild belugas in the Churchill River estuary.

title: A real-time edge-AI system for reef surveys
venue: Proceedings of the 28th Annual International Conference on Mobile Computing And Networking
reason: Deep learning detection and tracking of wild Crown-of-Thorns Starfish in underwater reef survey video on the Great Barrier Reef.

title: SIM-Trans: Structure Information Modeling Transformer for Fine-grained Visual Categorization
venue: ACM International Conference on Multimedia (ACM MM)
reason: Generic fine-grained visual categorization method (vision transformer) tested on CUB-200-2011 and iNaturalist 2017 as benchmarks; wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: MAVT-FG
venue: ACM International Conference on Multimedia (ACM MM)
reason: Proposes an audio-visual transformer for fine-grained bird species recognition from real-world videos of birds in natural scenes; introduces a new bird video benchmark.

title: Hierarchical Few-Shot Object Detection
venue: ACM International Conference on Multimedia (ACM MM)
reason: Proposes a hierarchical few-shot detection method and builds a new detection dataset of wild-bird images; wild birds are the stated subject, with monitoring of endangered birds as the application.

title: Towards battery-free machine learning and inference in underwater environments
reason: The paper classifies marine mammals from sound recordings (audio spectrograms) on a battery-free underwater device. No images or video are analysed.

title: Marine-tree: A Large-scale Marine Organisms Dataset for Hierarchical Image Classification
venue: Proceedings of the ... ACM International Conference on Information & Knowledge Management
reason: Presents a dataset and CNN-based hierarchical classification of in-situ underwater photoquadrat images of wild benthic organisms (corals, sponges, other sessile invertebrates) alongside algae and substrate.

title: Artemis
reason: Neural rendering of CGI animal assets and motion capture of pets and zoo/circus animals; no wild free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Detecting Hotspots of Human-Wildlife Conflicts in India using News Articles and Aerial Images
venue: ACM SIGCAS/SIGCHI Conference on Computing and Sustainable Societies (COMPASS)
reason: The only image analysis is land use / land cover classification of Sentinel-2 satellite imagery to find forest-settlement proximity zones; no animals or animal signs are imaged. The rest is news-text mining.

title: Weakly Supervised Faster-RCNN+FPN to classify animals in camera trap images
venue: International Conference on Image, Video and Signal Processing (IVSP)
reason: Proposes a weakly supervised Faster-RCNN+FPN workflow to classify wild animals in camera trap images from Papua New Guinea and Missouri monitoring campaigns.

title: Do Monkeys Want Audio or Visual Stimuli? Interactive Computers for Choice with White-Faced Sakis in Zoos
reason: Study of three zoo-housed white-faced sakis using an IR-sensor-triggered enrichment device; animals are captive only, and video was labelled manually with no computer vision analysis.

title: Deep Learning based Animal Detection and Tracking in Drone Video Footage
venue: International Conference on Computing and Artificial Intelligence (ICCAI)
reason: Applies YOLO-V5 detection and centroid tracking to drone video of free-ranging Arabian oryx in desert areas of the UAE.

title: Fish Target Detection Method Based on EPSA-CenterNet2
reason: Proposes a CNN detector (EPSA-CenterNet2) for detecting fish (Oplegnathus punctatus) in images with complex backgrounds such as water grass and reef. The paper does not say whether the fish are wild or farmed. The reef and water-grass backgrounds suggest a natural setting, so the paper is included.

title: A Face Recognition System for Bears
reason: Conceptual proposal for a bear face recognition system in the Alps, based on literature research and an expert interview. The authors analyse no images or video and run no experiments; the BearID results are quoted from another study.

title: Convolutional neural network-based image recognition for animals
venue: International Symposium on Artificial Intelligence for Medicine Sciences (ISAIMS)
reason: CNN transfer learning for cat-versus-dog image classification on a Kaggle dataset; only pets, no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Improved Inception Network for wild mammal Behavior Recognition
venue: International Conference on Electronic Information Technology and Computer Engineering (EITCE)
reason: Proposes a CNN-based behaviour recognition method applied to video of wild mammals from an existing wild mammal dataset plus web-collected video sequences.

title: Exploring Semi-Supervised Learning for Camera Trap Images from the Wild
venue: Artificial Intelligence and Cloud Computing Conference (AICCC)
reason: Evaluates semi-supervised image classification (FixMatch, ABC) on a real camera trap dataset containing wild species (fox, birds, rodents) together with domestic animals (goat, donkey, sheep, dog, cat, camel).

title: Research on underwater object detection of improved YOLOv7 model based on attention mechanism
venue: International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv7 detector for underwater images of marine benthic animals (scallops, sea urchins, sea cucumbers, starfish). The paper does not say whether the animals are wild or farmed, but the data shows free-living marine invertebrates underwater.

title: Fine-grained classification network for fish based on the attention mechanism and EfficientNet
venue: International Conference on Robotics, Intelligent Control and Artificial Intelligence (RICAI)
reason: Proposes CNN-based fine-grained classification of wild-caught fish from fishing-boat camera images and underwater fish photos for fisheries monitoring.

title: A Novel Attention-Based Lightweight Network for Multiscale Object Detection in Underwater Images
reason: Proposes a lightweight deep detection network for underwater images whose classes are mostly marine animals (fish, holothurian, sea urchin, turtle, manta ray, octopus, starfish). The images come from public underwater datasets. The paper is a retracted publication.

title: Identifying Animals in Camera Trap Images via Neural Architecture Search
reason: Proposes a neural architecture search method (NASRT) and evaluates the resulting CNN for species classification on two camera trap wildlife datasets (ENA24, MCTI); classes are mostly wild animals with a few domestic ones (dog, domestic cat, chicken).

title: Deep convolutional neural network-based system for fish classification
venue: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
reason: Proposes a CNN to classify images of eight indigenous (native) fish species from Bangladesh. The paper does not say whether the fish are wild, farmed or market specimens. Included because the species are native and the paper frames the work around conservation.

title: Fish classification using extraction of appropriate feature set
venue: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
reason: Proposes a hybrid GA-SA-backpropagation classifier for classifying images of wild fish (LifeCLEF 2015 fish task and FishBase images) into families/classes.

title: Effective classification of birds’ species based on transfer learning
venue: International Journal of Power Electronics and Drive Systems/International Journal of Electrical and Computer Engineering
reason: Compares traditional ML, CNNs and transfer-learning CNNs for bird species classification on a Kaggle bird image dataset. The stated motivation is bird conservation.

title: Population abundance of Greater Flamingo Phoenicopterus roseus (Aves: Phoenicopteridae) in district Gurugram of Haryana, India
reason: Population survey of wild Greater Flamingos where drone photos and videos were counted manually (photo interpretation, tally counter); no computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: The Specimen Data Refinery: A Canonical Workflow Framework and FAIR Digital Object Approach to Speeding up Digital Mobilisation of Natural History Collections
reason: Describes a workflow framework (Specimen Data Refinery) for digitising preserved museum specimens (herbarium sheets, microscope slides, pinned insects) and their labels; no wild free-ranging animals and no experimental CV results.

title: To tag ornot to tag: comparative performance of tagging and photo-identification in a long-term mark-recapture of Juvenile Green Turtles (Chelonia mydas)
reason: Primary study evaluating software-assisted photo-identification (Wild-ID image matching) of wild green turtles captured in a long-term mark-recapture programme, compared against artificial tags.

title: Fish species classification using a collaborative technique of firefly algorithm and neural network
venue: EURASIP Journal on Advances in Signal Processing
reason: Primary study proposing a computer vision pipeline (enhancement, SURF, firefly optimisation, PatternNet) to classify five marine fish species in underwater images from the Fish Recognition Ground Truth dataset.

title: Scheimpflug lidar range profiling of bee activity patterns and spatial distributions
reason: Entomological Scheimpflug lidar with line-scan camera records free-flying insects in a crop field; managed honeybees are separated from wild insects, and both groups are counted. Optical sensor data analysed automatically, so it is included as remote-sensing vision of free-flying wild and managed insects.

title: Bumblebees display characteristics of active vision during robust obstacle avoidance flight
reason: Laboratory flight-tunnel experiment with bumblebees from a commercially bred colony kept in the lab; marker positions digitized from high-speed video to study flight behaviour, no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Scaling of maneuvering performance in baleen whales: larger whales outperform expectations
reason: Biomechanics study of free-swimming baleen whales based on bio-logger (accelerometer, magnetometer, depth) data. Drone photographs are used only to measure body length by converting pixels to metres with altimeter and camera parameters; no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Vocalization-associated respiration patterns: thermography-based monitoring and detection of preparation for calling
reason: Thermal video of free-ranging wild meerkats analysed with a deep-learning nostril keypoint detector and tracking to extract respiration patterns.

title: Divergence of climbing escape flight performance inMorphobutterflies living in different microhabitats
reason: Biomechanics study of wild-caught Morpho butterflies filmed in an outdoor insectary; kinematics were obtained by manual digitizing in DLTdv6 and Kine, with no automated computer vision method developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Biomechanical energetics of terrestrial locomotion in California sea lions ( Zalophus californianus )
reason: Biomechanics study in which anatomical points were digitized manually, frame by frame, in Tracker/ImageJ to compute energetics. No computer vision method is developed or applied. The data mix captive sea lions and seals with wild elephant seals.

title: Gap selection and steering during obstacle avoidance in pigeons
reason: Domestic homing pigeons tracked with a marker-based motion capture system in an indoor experimental flight hall. This is a laboratory-style behavioural set-up with domestic animals, not wild animals imaged in the field.

title: Study on Underwater Video Detection Method of Chinese Sturgeon
reason: Improves YOLOv5 to detect Chinese sturgeon, an endangered non-domestic species, in underwater video for conservation. The paper does not say whether the filmed animals were wild or captive.

title: REALIZATION OF A YOLO-V3-BASED APPLICATION FOR THE DETECTION OF TICK-BORNE CASES
reason: Applies YOLOv3 object detection to images of ticks (non-domestic arthropods) downloaded from the internet; primary research with animals as subject.

title: Development of a protected birds identification system using a convolutional neural network
reason: Primary study applying a CNN to images of ten protected, non-domestic Indonesian bird species collected from eBird and Oriental Bird Images; the paper does not state whether the photographed birds were wild or captive.

title: Passive optical detection and classification of flying objects
reason: Computer vision (motion detection plus SIFT/SVM classification) applied to video of flying wild birds in the sky near an airport, recorded by a static outdoor camera.

title: The aesthetic value of reef fishes is globally mismatched to their conservation priorities
reason: Applies a fine-tuned CNN to web photographs of wild reef fish species to predict their aesthetic value, then relates that value to conservation status.

title: Sticky Pi is a high-frequency smart trap that enables the study of insect circadian activity under natural conditions
reason: Develops a camera-based smart trap and deep learning pipeline (segmentation, tracking, classification) applied to wild free-moving insects in berry fields, plus a laboratory validation with Drosophila melanogaster.

title: An artificial intelligence model to identify snakes from across the world: Opportunities and challenges for global health and herpetology
reason: Develops a Vision Transformer model to classify snake species from photos. Most photos show free-ranging snakes from citizen-science platforms; a small share shows captive snakes.

title: Computer-vision object tracking for monitoring bottlenose dolphin habitat use and kinematics
reason: CNN detection and tracking of bottlenose dolphins housed in a zoo habitat (Brookfield Zoo); no wild or free-ranging animals in the analysed data.

title: Interclutch variability in egg characteristics in two species of rail: Is maternal identity encoded in eggshell patterns?
reason: Applies image pattern matching (NaturePatternMatch, SIFT features) to field photos of eggs from wild King Rail and Common Moorhen nests. Eggs count as direct signs of the animals, and the aim is to identify mothers (re-identification).

title: Evaluating the effectiveness of drones for quantifying invasive upside-down jellyfish (Cassiopea sp.) in Lake Macquarie, Australia
reason: Drone video of wild jellyfish was reviewed and counted manually in video-player software and compared with kayak counts; no computer vision method was developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Automated image analysis to assess hygienic behaviour of honeybees
reason: Image processing pipeline counting uncapped brood cells in comb images of managed honeybee colonies photographed by beekeepers; beekeeping application, no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: A low-cost, long-term underwater camera trap network coupled with deep residual learning image analysis
reason: Primary study that deploys underwater camera traps on a tropical reef and trains a ResNet-50 CNN to classify images of wild, free-ranging fishes as Fish/NoFish.

title: 3D reconstruction of bird flight trajectories using a single video camera
reason: Trained laboratory Budgerigars filmed flying through an indoor experimental tunnel; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Caught on camera: Field imagery reveals the unexpected importance of vertebrates for biological control of the banana weevil (Cosmopolites sordidus Col. Curculionidae)
reason: Background subtraction is applied to field time-lapse images to detect free-ranging wild vertebrates and invertebrates visiting sentinel prey tiles in banana plots. The study is set in agriculture, but the detected animals are wild predators, not livestock or the crop pest alone.

title: Design and fabrication of a stereo-video camera equipped unoccupied aerial vehicle for measuring sea turtles, sharks, and other marine fauna
reason: Stereo-video photogrammetry from a UAV is used to measure body size of free-swimming wild green sea turtles and a nurse shark in the Bahamas. Measurement points are selected manually in software, so the computer vision component is stereo calibration and triangulation rather than automated recognition.

title: Next generation insect taxonomic classification by comparing different deep learning algorithms
reason: All analysed images are of preserved, pinned museum-collection insect specimens photographed in a lightbox under laboratory conditions; no wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: I Spy Through a Camera’s Eye: Divii in the Gwich’in Settlement Area
reason: Camera-trap images of wild Dall sheep and other mammals in the Northern Richardson Mountains are processed with MegaDetector to find images containing animals, which then supports demographic monitoring.

title: Fish Species Classification using Optimized Deep Learning Model
venue: International Journal of Advanced Computer Science and Applications
reason: Fish species classification on 1000 images downloaded from GitHub and internet sources; the five classes are ornamental/aquarium-type fish (aulonocara fire, discus, flame fish, molly, king fish) and the paper gives no evidence that any image shows wild, free-ranging animals or where the images were taken.

title: Fish Detection in Seagrass Ecosystem using Masked-Otsu in HSV Color Space
venue: International Journal of Advanced Computer Science and Applications
reason: Classical image-processing fish detection on in-situ underwater images of wild fish in a seagrass ecosystem.

title: A Layered, Hybrid Machine Learning Analytic Workflow for Mouse Risk Assessment Behavior
reason: Laboratory C57Bl/6 mice filmed in a customized two-chamber arena for behavioural neuroscience; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: AN EFFECTIVE DEEP LEARNING MODEL FOR RECOGNITION OF ANIMALS AND PLANTS
venue: Journal of Computer Science and Cybernetics
reason: Proposes a lightweight CNN to classify images of 36 rare animal species (and 20 plants) for wildlife protection; images come from the Internet and from places in Thanh Hoa province, so the wild or captive status of the animals is not stated.

title: IsVoNet8: A Proposed Deep Learning Model for Classification of Some Fish Species
reason: CNN classification of dead fish photographed as seafood items collected from a supermarket; no images of wild, free-ranging animals.

title: Role of Human-AI Interaction in Selective Prediction
venue: AAAI Publications (The Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence (AAAI))
reason: Primary study evaluating a selective prediction system (AI ensemble with deferral to humans) for detecting whether animals are present in Snapshot Serengeti camera trap images of wild animals.

title: First description of the breeding biology of the North Philippine Hawk-Eagle ( Nisaetus philippensis )
reason: Primary breeding-biology study that trains a CNN to classify remote nest-camera images of a wild North Philippine Hawk-Eagle pair and chick.

title: Ventral and lateral spot patterns differentiation between three smooth newt species (Amphibia: Salamandridae: Lissotriton)
reason: The authors photographed preserved voucher specimens kept in herpetological collections and analysed their spot patterns with ImageJ. The data are museum specimens, not images of free-ranging animals.

title: Development of Wild Animal Ward-Off System
reason: Describes a PIR-triggered camera system that classifies intruding wild animals (elephants, deer, boar) on farmland to trigger repellents; cow and goat are also recognised. No dataset or experiment is reported, so inclusion rests on the described system only.

title: Sustainable development of green energy-automated bird protection at wind farms
reason: Field evaluation of a camera-based stereo-vision system detecting and size-classifying wild birds at a wind turbine in Poland.

title: Modernized Wildlife Surveillance and Behaviour Detection using a Novel Machine Learning Algorithm
venue: International Journal on Recent and Innovation Trends in Computing and Communication
reason: Proposes a HOG + DCNN + seagull-optimisation framework to classify wild animals (tiger, cheetah, elephant) in images collected from the internet for wildlife surveillance. The paper calls the data wild animal images but does not state whether the animals are free-ranging or captive.

title: A Study on Fish Classification Techniques using Convolutional Neural Networks on Highly Challenged Underwater Images
venue: International Journal on Recent and Innovation Trends in Computing and Communication
reason: Besides reviewing prior work, the paper trains and evaluates a CNN that classifies fish species in underwater images of fish in their natural habitat, so it counts as primary research.

title: 3D models related to the publication: Hide and seek shark teeth in Random Forests: Machine learning applied to Scyliorhinus canicula
reason: Dataset paper of laboratory micro-CT scans of dead shark specimens' heads; teeth landmarked manually and classified with Random Forests on morphometric coordinates, not field imagery of free-ranging animals.

title: Self-organisation of zooplankton communities produces similar food chain lengths throughout the ocean
reason: Ecological study using particle size measurements from optical plankton counters and a size-spectrum model; no image or video analysis or computer vision method.

title: Computer Vision Reveals Fish Behaviour Through Structural Equation Modelling of Movement Patterns
reason: Deep-learning detection and tracking of wild fish in underwater field video at an estuarine tidal weir, used to infer behaviour.

title: Development of a new 3D tracking system for multiple marmosets under free-moving conditions
reason: 3D tracking, face identification and grooming detection of laboratory common marmosets housed in a home cage at an experimental animal facility; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Individual experience influences reconstruction of division of labour under colony disturbance in a queenless ant species (Diacamma cf. indicum)
reason: Behavioural ecology experiment on laboratory-reared ant colonies; photographs were only used for manual recording of worker location, with no computer vision analysis.

title: Animal Pose Estimation Algorithm Based on the Lightweight Stacked Hourglass Network
reason: Proposes a lightweight stacked hourglass network for animal pose estimation, evaluated on TigDog (tigers from a wildlife documentary and horses from YouTube) plus synthetic animals.

title: Fish Species Classification Using a Collaborative Technique Of Firefly Algorithm & Neural Network
reason: Primary study proposing an image-processing and neural-network pipeline to classify five marine fish species in underwater images taken from the Fish Recognition Ground Truth dataset.

title: Design and implement of the automatic wetland waterfowl identification system based on YOLOv5 algorithm
reason: Applies YOLOv5 to detect, identify and count native wild waterfowl in the Quanzhou Bay Estuary Wetland from images and camera video.

title: A 16p11.2 deletion mouse model displays quantitatively and qualitatively different behaviours in sociability and social novelty over short- and long-term observation
reason: Behavioural phenotyping of a genetically modified laboratory mouse model in a test cage using the Live Mouse Tracker system; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Updated estimate of the breeding population of Adélie penguins (Pygoscelis adeliae) at Penguin Point, Marambio / Seymour Island within the proposed Weddell Sea Marine Protected Area
reason: Population census of wild Adélie penguins by direct field counts of nests; no image or video analysis.

title: Fish Species Identification on Low Resolution - A Study with Enhanced Super Resolution Generative Adversarial Network (ESRGAN), YOLO and VGG-16
reason: Species identification of caught/commercial fish for automated sorting in the fishing industry. The images are photos of harvested fish from a published dataset, not free-ranging animals in the wild.

title: Fish Species Classification from Underwater Images using Large-Scale Dataset via Deep Learning
reason: Primary study proposing a computer vision pipeline (FFA segmentation, SURF features, DNN) to classify fish species in underwater images collected in the marine environment.

title: Novel Approach of Animal Recognition Using Deep Learning Algorithm
venue: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)
reason: Primary study applying a CNN to classify images of wild animal species (elephant, cheetah) for wildlife monitoring; the paper does not state whether the pictured animals are free-ranging or captive.

title: Conservation Benefits of a Marine Protected Area on South African Chondrichthyans
reason: Ecological survey of wild sharks, rays and chimaeras with baited stereo-video; species identification, MaxN counts and length measurements were done manually by observers in EventMeasure software, with no computer vision method.

title: Automatic Identification of Individual Yaks in In-the-Wild Images Using Part-Based Convolutional Networks with Self-Supervised Learning
reason: Identifies individual domestic yaks (livestock) for precision livestock management; not wild animals.

title: Automatic Fish Identification Using Single Shot Detector
reason: Applies an SSD-MobileNet detector to images of wild-caught marine fish, photographed after capture by fishermen, to identify 10 genera.

title: DEVELOPMENT OF SYMBIOTIC TECHNOLOGY OF SEA URCHIN AND SEA WEED IN THE EARTHQUAKE DISASTER AREA
venue: Journal of Japan Society of Civil Engineers Ser B3 (Ocean Engineering)
reason: Applies YOLOv5 object detection to underwater images/video of wild sea urchins in the coastal fishing grounds of Iwate to estimate their density.

title: Mobile-based Primate Image Recognition using CNN
venue: IJCCS (Indonesian Journal of Computing and Cybernetics Systems)
reason: Primary study applying a CNN (MobileNet) in an Android app to classify images of two non-domestic primate species for conservation; the paper does not state whether the pictured animals are wild or captive.

title: Smart Farming Application for Protecting Animal Intrusion Using AI
venue: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
reason: Primary study proposing a CNN-based vision system to detect and recognise wild animals intruding on farmland in order to repel them. The stated subject is wildlife, but the paper does not describe the animals in the images it actually analyses (datasets E1/E2).

title: Observation and Classification of Fauna for Forest Survey
venue: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
reason: Raspberry Pi smart camera with pre-trained TensorFlow detection model applied in field trials to detect and label wild animals (giraffes, bears, elephants).

title: Animal Detector System for Forest Monitoring Using OpenCV and Raspberry-pi
venue: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
reason: Descriptive prototype paper for a YOLO/GSM animal alert system. It describes the YOLO algorithm in general terms but analyses no images or video, names no dataset and reports no experiments or results, so no data showing wild animals is analysed.

title: Bird Species Identifier using Convolutional Neural Network
venue: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
reason: Primary study that trains a CNN to classify bird species from images (CUB-200-2011); birds are the stated subject and the images are described as captured in their natural habitat.

title: Underwater biotope mapping: automatic processing of underwater video data
reason: Primary study presenting a deep-learning pipeline (classification, few-shot segmentation, counting, 3D reconstruction) on underwater seabed video from the White Sea showing free-living marine organisms.

title: Rapid Prototyping of Species Classifiers using Deep Learning
reason: Applies a CNN (ResNet-34) to classify images of three non-domestic sea star species. Where the images came from is not reported, but these are wild marine taxa and nothing in the text points to captive, lab or farm animals.

title: Prototyping Artificial Intelligent Classifiers using Deep Learning
reason: Applies a deep CNN classifier to images of three wild sea star species. The image source is not stated, but the species are non-domestic marine invertebrates.

title: Multiresolution DECOLOR for camouflaged moving foreground detection using a redundant wavelet transform
reason: Proposes a foreground-extraction method (MR-DECOLOR) evaluated on camera-trap image sequences of wild snow leopards.

title: Detection of Moving Object with Dynamic Mode Decomposition and Yolov5
reason: Generic moving-object detection method (DMD + Yolov5) tested on pedestrians in a corridor and an unspecified underwater web video; no animals are stated as the subject or the application.

title: Underwater Target Detection Based on Improved YOLOv4
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv7 detector evaluated on underwater optical images of marine animals (sea urchins, starfish, scallops, sea cucumbers, fish, crabs, shrimp, jellyfish). The paper does not state whether the animals are wild or farmed; the datasets are described only as underwater/seafloor images.

title: Animal Intrusion Detection in Farming Area using YOLOv5 Approach
venue: International Conference on Control, Automation and Systems (ICCAS)
reason: Applies YOLOv5 to images to detect wild animals (elephant, monkey, tiger, wild boar) that intrude into farming areas. This is human-wildlife conflict monitoring, not livestock.

title: Automated and non-invasive UAV-based system for the monitoring and the group size estimation of dolphins
venue: International Conference on Smart and Sustainable Technologies (SpliTech)
reason: Primary study applying object detection models to UAV video frames of free-ranging dolphins in the Gulf of Taranto to estimate group size.

title: Exploring the necessity of mosaicking for underwater imagery semantic segmentation using deep learning
reason: Deep-learning semantic segmentation of seabed video from the Baltic Sea; one of the three classes is the wild blue mussel Mytilus edulis trossulus (the others are a red alga and boulders), so part of the data shows wild animals.

title: MonkeyTrail: A scalable video-based method for tracking macaque movement trajectory in daily living cages
reason: Tracks laboratory macaques housed individually in daily living cages in an animal room for neuroscience research; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: A Robust Feature Construction for Fish Classification Using Grey Wolf Optimizer
reason: Primary study proposing an image-based fish species classification workflow (NCACC enhancement, GLCM features, GWO feature construction, BPNN) on the Fish4Knowledge dataset, framed as underwater fish recognition with images collected from the fish's habitat.

title: Drone monitoring improves nest detection of Squacco Herons Ardeola ralloides , but fails to assess its productivity
reason: Drone survey of wild Squacco Heron nests; nests were counted manually by human observers on drone images (DotDotGoose count tool). The paper uses no automated computer vision analysis.

title: KLASIFIKASI CITRA IKAN MENGGUNAKAN CONVOLUTIONAL NEURAL NETWORK
venue: Jurnal Ilmu Komputer dan Sistem Informasi
reason: Applies a CNN to classify images of 20 non-domestic (Mediterranean) fish species. The data come from Kaggle and the paper does not say whether the images show wild, captured or farmed fish. There is no indication of aquaculture, lab or captive animals.

title: Webly-Supervised Fine-Grained Recognition with Partial Label Learning
venue: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
reason: Generic webly-supervised fine-grained recognition method evaluated on aircraft, car, bird and iNat web benchmarks; wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: "Corvid Tracking Studio": A custom-built motion capture system to track head movements of corvids.
reason: Marker-based infrared motion capture of four wild-caught large-billed crows kept in an outdoor cage and recorded in a purpose-built indoor motion-capture room; no images of free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Birds Images Prediction with Watson Visual Recognition Services from IBM-Cloud and Conventional Neural Network
venue: Advances in Science Technology and Engineering Systems Journal
reason: Applies CNN and IBM Watson visual recognition to classify images of about 210 endemic (non-domestic) bird species; primary application study.

title: Photogrammetric counts of pacific salmon by means of unmanned aerial vehicles of consumer grade
reason: Develops a UAV photogrammetric (SfM orthomosaic and DEM) image-processing pipeline for counting wild Pacific salmon spawners and their redds in rivers of Khabarovsk Krai.

title: Which index should I use? A comparison of indices for enclosure use studies
reason: Simulation study comparing enclosure use indices on artificial data sets; no images or video analysed and no computer vision. Context is captive animal welfare.

title: A Comparative Study of Various Edge Detection Techniques for Underwater Images
venue: Journal of Telecommunications and Information Technology
reason: The paper compares edge detection methods on underwater video images of wild Acropora corals (which are animals), filmed on reefs at the Redang islands.

title: Multi-species Fish Identification using Hybrid DeepCNN with Refined Squeeze and Excitation Architecture
reason: Proposes a CNN-based fish species classifier evaluated on images from underwater videos of fish recorded off the coast of Taiwan (Fish4Knowledge) and on the Croatian fish dataset.

title: Towards the Conservation of Endangered Mammals using Single-stage Deep Neural Network
venue: Direct Research Journal of Agriculture and Food Science
reason: Primary study training YOLOv4 to detect four wild mammal classes (buffalo, rhino, elephant, zebra) in images for conservation; the paper does not state whether the photographed animals were wild or captive, but wildlife is the stated subject.

title: Automating Bird Detection Based on Webcam Captured Images using Deep Learning
reason: Primary study evaluating CNN object detectors for detecting birds in webcam images from Cornell Lab of Ornithology live feeds at outdoor locations.

title: Update on the development of the Agouti platform for collaborative science with camera traps and a tool for wildlife abundance estimation
reason: Progress report on developing a camera-trap data management platform (Agouti) and an R package for density estimation. Animal positions are recorded by manual annotation, and the report applies or evaluates no computer vision method.

title: Data generated by camera trapping in 40 areas in Europe including East and South Europe: report of the field activities (May 2022)
reason: Progress report on a planned camera-trap field protocol and an observatory website. No images are analysed. AI processing in AGOUTI is only planned for later.

title: KLASIFIKASI TIGA GENUS IKAN KARANG MENGGUNAKAN CONVOLUTION NEURAL NETWORK
venue: Jurnal Ilmu dan Teknologi Kelautan Tropis
reason: CNN classification of three fish genera from photos downloaded from a Kaggle dataset; the paper does not state whether the images show wild, free-ranging fish, so the wild-animal requirement cannot be confirmed from the text.

title: Jumping Motion of Gourami Fish Using Tracker Software as a Mechanical Energy Conservation Practicum
reason: Video tracking of individual gourami fish that people handled and provoked to jump for a physics practicum. None of the data shows wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Detection of animal intrusion using CNN and image processing
venue: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews
reason: CNN-based classification of animal images to detect intrusion of wild animals (deer, wild boar, elephants, monkeys) alongside cows into farm fields; human-wildlife conflict application.

title: Development of a Detection System for Endangered Mammals in Negros Island, Philippines Using YOLOv5n
reason: Applies YOLOv5n object detection to images of four wild endangered mammal species of Negros Island, collected from web images.

title: Can a leopard seal, Hydrurga leptonyx de Blainville, 1820 (Mammalia Phocidae), change its spots? (Spoiler alert: at least one adult female can)
reason: Researchers matched the spots of one wild leopard seal across photographs by eye. The AI software was used only to enhance image quality, not for computer vision analysis.

title: Multiple pathways to dissipate body heat excess and the infrared thermography effectiveness
venue: Journal of Animal Behaviour and Biometeorology
reason: Editorial briefly discussing prior infrared thermography studies of wild rodents and naked-neck chickens; not a primary computer vision study and no image analysis method is developed or evaluated.

title: An Improved Transfer-Learning for Image-Based Species Classification of Protected Indonesians Birds
reason: Primary study proposing a CNN transfer-learning framework for image-based species classification of protected Indonesian birds; images were photographed by the authors or retrieved from the internet, and the paper does not state whether the birds are wild or captive.

title: Large Scale Fish Images Classification and Localization using Transfer Learning and Localization Aware CNN Architecture
reason: Applies a CNN to classify and localize fish species in the QUT fish dataset, which includes in-situ underwater images of fish in their natural environment.

title: An Efficient Method for Underwater Video Summarization and Object Detection Using YoLoV3
reason: Applies keyframe extraction and YOLOv3 object detection to underwater videos of free-ranging marine animals (fish, crabs, jellyfish, shrimp, starfish) recorded in a Danish brackish waterway.

title: Cephalopods Classification Using Fine Tuned Lightweight Transfer Learning Models
reason: CNN-based species classification of images of wild-caught cephalopods photographed at Indian coastal areas; animals are wild (not farmed), images analysed with computer vision.

title: Klasifikasi Hewan Mamalia Berdasarkan Bentuk Wajah Menggunakan Fitur Histogram of Oriented dan Metode Support Vector Machine
reason: Primary study applying HOG + SVM to classify mammal face images from the LHI-Animal-Faces dataset. The 15 classes mix wild species (tiger, lion, panda, wolf, elephant, deer, bear, monkey) with domestic ones. The capture context is not stated.

title: Artificial intelligence applications for proactive environmental monitoring and asset management
reason: Applies a deep learning detector to video of wild egrets at a Hong Kong egretry to count birds and analyse their behaviour. The paper also has a second, non-animal concrete-defect study.

title: A novel approach for wild fish monitoring at aquaculture sites: wild fish presence analysis using computer vision
reason: Applies YOLOv4-based detection and counting to underwater video of wild fish aggregating around salmon sea cages; the farmed salmon were excluded from counts.

title: Investigating the thermal physiology of Critically Endangered North Atlantic right whales Eubalaena glacialis via aerial infrared thermography
reason: Drone thermal and RGB videos of free-ranging right whales were reviewed qualitatively and aligned manually by humans; no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Discovery and dynamics of a cryptic marine copepod-parasite interaction
reason: Primary study applying a CNN classifier to in situ microscope images of free-living marine copepods (Oithona spp.) and their parasite, collected in undisturbed seawater at a pier.

title: Automated Video Monitoring of Unmarked and Marked Honey Bees at the Hive Entrance
reason: Video monitoring of managed honey bees at the entrance of a hive at an agricultural experimental station (beekeeping); no wild, free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Detecting illegal wildlife trafficking via real time tomography 3D X-ray imaging and automated algorithms
reason: The analysed data are 3D X-ray CT scans of dead animal carcasses (wildlife-hospital specimens and market-bought fish) scanned at a mail facility; no images of wild, free-ranging animals.

title: High-resolution 3D mapping of cold-water coral reefs using machine learning
reason: Primary study applying machine-learning classification to SfM point clouds reconstructed from ROV video of a wild cold-water coral reef (live/dead coral framework, rubble, sediment).

title: Deer Behavior Affects Density Estimates With Camera Traps, but Is Outweighed by Spatial Variability
reason: Camera-trap photos of free-ranging red and roe deer were tagged manually in digiKam and fed into statistical density models (REM, CTDS); no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: An automated work-flow for pinniped surveys: A new tool for monitoring population dynamics
reason: Primary study applying CNN-based segmentation to drone orthomosaics of wild harbour seals at haul-out sites to count and measure them.

title: Modern approaches for leveraging biodiversity collections to understand change in plant-insect interactions
reason: The computer vision part classifies light-microscope images of pollen grains taken from herbarium plant specimens. No animal images are analysed; butterfly museum specimens are only the source of pollen for the network analysis.

title: Color in motion: Generating 3-dimensional multispectral models to study dynamic visual signals in animals
reason: The workflow builds 3D multispectral models from mounted museum bird specimens; a wild-bird video is used only as an animation reference and is not analysed with computer vision.

title: Modified Mosquito Programs’ Surveillance Needs and An Image-Based Identification Tool to Address Them
reason: Computer vision species identification of dead, wild-caught mosquito specimens imaged in an enclosed tabletop lab device; no images of free-ranging animals. The paper calls itself a perspective but reports original experiments.

title: Automated Detection, Classification and Counting of Fish in Fish Passages With Deep Learning
reason: Applies deep learning detection, classification and tracking to imaging-sonar and optical video of free-ranging fish in a river and a dam fish ladder.

title: PSS-net: Parallel semantic segmentation network for detecting marine animals in underwater scene
reason: Primary study proposing a CNN semantic segmentation network for marine animals in underwater scenes, evaluated on the open MAS3K marine animal segmentation dataset; the paper does not state whether the animals are wild or captive.

title: Robust segmentation of underwater fish based on multi-level feature accumulation
reason: Proposes CNN segmentation networks for fish in underwater images from natural marine habitats (DeepFish, SUIM); primary research on free-ranging fish imagery.

title: RMP-Net: A structural reparameterization and subpixel super-resolution-based marine scene segmentation network
reason: Proposes a semantic segmentation network evaluated on underwater marine-scene datasets (SUIM, DeepFish) whose classes include fish and other marine animals in the marine environment.

title: Seasonal gain in body condition of foraging humpback whales along the Western Antarctic Peninsula
reason: Applies drone-based image photogrammetry to measure body length and body condition of wild humpback whales on Antarctic foraging grounds.

title: UMOTMA: Underwater multiple object tracking with memory aggregation
reason: Proposes a vision-based multi-object tracking method evaluated on underwater videos of fish, including fish schools in a marine pasture; MOT17 pedestrians is used only as an extra benchmark.

title: Using Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) Imagery to Characterise Pursuit-Diving Seabird Association With Tidal Stream Hydrodynamic Habitat Features
reason: Wild seabirds (auks) in UAV imagery, but they were found, classified and measured by hand by a human observer using a GUI. The image processing was georectification and manual annotation followed by spatial statistics; no computer vision method was developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Assessing the Image Concept Drift at the OBSEA Coastal Underwater Cabled Observatory
reason: Primary study applying deep-learning fish detection and classification to images of free-ranging fish acquired at a coastal underwater cabled observatory, quantifying concept drift over one year.

title: Machine learning applied to big data from marine cabled observatories: A case study of sablefish monitoring in the NE Pacific
reason: Primary study applying a YOLO detector and tracking algorithm to deep-sea cabled observatory video of wild sablefish to detect and count them.

title: A Pyramidal Feature Fusion Model on Swimming Crab Portunus trituberculatus Re-identification
reason: Individual re-identification of farmed swimming crabs collected from a crab farm for product tracing in aquaculture; no wild or free-ranging animals in the data.

title: Rise of the Machines: Best Practices and Experimental Evaluation of Computer-Assisted Dorsal Fin Image Matching Systems for Bottlenose Dolphins
reason: Primary study that experimentally evaluates computer vision dorsal fin matching systems (finFindR, CurvRank, CurvRank v2) on photographs of wild, free-ranging bottlenose dolphins from Sarasota Bay.

title: Range-Wide Comparison of Gray Whale Body Condition Reveals Contrasting Sub-Population Health Characteristics and Vulnerability to Environmental Change
reason: Applies image-based photogrammetry (body measurements from UAS and aerial images) to wild gray whales to assess body condition.

title: Automated Plankton Classification With a Dynamic Optimization and Adaptation Cycle
reason: Develops a CNN-based adaptive classification pipeline for images of wild marine plankton (including copepods, bivalve larvae, gastropods, appendicularians) sampled at sea in North Sea surveys.

title: Content-Aware Segmentation of Objects Spanning a Large Size Range: Application to Plankton Images
reason: Primary study comparing computer vision segmentation/detection methods on in situ images of free-living planktonic organisms collected at sea.

title: Low-Cost, Deep-Sea Imaging and Analysis Tools for Deep-Sea Exploration: A Collaborative Design Study
reason: Participatory design study based on interviews with marine professionals; describes a low-cost camera prototype and planned AI video analysis tool, but performs no image analysis of animals.

title: Global Distribution of Zooplankton Biomass Estimated by In Situ Imaging and Machine Learning
reason: In situ underwater images of free-living ocean zooplankton are measured by image analysis and classified taxonomically with supervised learning plus manual validation; the results feed habitat models of global biomass.

title: Comparison of an In Situ Imaging Device and Net-Based Method to Study Mesozooplankton Communities in an Oligotrophic System
reason: The study images wild marine mesozooplankton in situ with a UVP5 and scans net-collected samples with a ZooScan. Images are segmented, then classified with a random forest in Ecotaxa, and the results are used to estimate abundance and biomass.

title: Fish surveys on the move: Adapting automated fish detection and classification frameworks for videos on a remotely operated vehicle in shallow marine waters
reason: Primary study applying CNN object detectors to underwater drone video of wild fish in an estuary to detect and count two fisheries species.

title: Research on target detection of Engraulis japonicus purse seine based on improved model of YOLOv5
reason: Detects fishing-operation objects on a vessel deck (persons, buoys, fish tanks, baskets, nets, processing vessels) to compile fishery statistics. No wild animals are the image subject.

title: Accelerating Species Recognition and Labelling of Fish From Underwater Video With Machine-Assisted Deep Learning
reason: Deep learning object detection and species classification of wild fish in Baited Remote Underwater Video Station (BRUVS) footage; primary research.

title: Diver-generated photomosaics as a tool for monitoring temperate rocky reef ecosystems
reason: Primary study that applies structure-from-motion photogrammetry to diver-collected underwater images of temperate rocky reefs to build photomosaics, from which wild sea urchin densities and benthic cover are extracted (the extraction itself is manual annotation).

title: Citizen science and machine learning: Interdisciplinary approach to non-invasively monitoring a northern marine ecosystem
reason: CNNs classify underwater video frames of wild beluga whales (presence/absence) from a boat-mounted camera in the Churchill River estuary; primary research.

title: Assessing the ability of deep learning techniques to perform real-time identification of shark species in live streaming video from drones
reason: Primary study training deep-learning object detectors on drone video of free-ranging sharks and other marine fauna off New South Wales beaches.

title: Maka Niu: A low-cost, modular imaging and sensor platform to increase observation capabilities of the deep ocean
reason: Hardware paper describing a low-cost deep-sea camera and sensor platform. Footage of wild marine animals is recorded, but no computer vision analysis is performed; machine-learning localization and classification via Tator/FathomNet is stated as future integration.

title: The Remote Emerging Disease Intelligence—NETwork
reason: Programme overview of a pathogen surveillance consortium (metagenomics, SOPs, data pipeline). A computer-vision tick identification tool is only mentioned as developed from images of collected tick specimens taken with a laboratory device; no image analysis method, data or results are reported.

title: Siamese Network-Based All-Purpose-Tracker, a Model-Free Deep Learning Tool for Animal Behavioral Tracking
reason: General-purpose behavioural tracking tool evaluated mainly on head-fixed laboratory mice, plus published laboratory/behavioural videos (zebrafish, mouse pupil, chimpanzee on a keyboard, peacock spider, cordon-bleu); no data are stated to show wild, free-ranging animals.

title: A Markerless Pose Estimator Applicable to Limbless Animals
reason: Markerless pose tracker demonstrated only on laboratory-reared Drosophila larvae under a microscope and adult zebrafish in a Plexiglas aquarium; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Giant Panda Video Image Sequence and Application in 3D Reconstruction
reason: 3D reconstruction of giant pandas from video. The paper does not state where the videos were recorded and gives no indication of wild or free-ranging animals; the only context is a giant panda breeding base (author affiliation and funder), so the wild-data condition is not met.

title: A Dataset for Forestry Pest Identification
reason: Builds and benchmarks an object detection dataset of forest insect pests photographed in the wild. These are not crop pests in production.

title: Rodent hole detection in a typical steppe ecosystem using UAS and deep learning
reason: Primary study applying deep-learning object detection to UAS images of burrow holes (direct signs) of wild Brandt's voles in a steppe.

title: Group-based, autonomous, individualized training and testing of long-tailed macaques (Macaca fascicularis) in their home enclosure to a visuo-acoustic discrimination task
reason: Captive research-colony long-tailed macaques trained on a touchscreen in their home enclosure at a primate research centre; CNN-based individual identification serves a neuroscience training protocol. No wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Automated 2D, 2.5D, and 3D Segmentation of Coral Reef Pointclouds and Orthoprojections
reason: Primary study evaluating 2D, 2.5D and 3D neural-network segmentation of the coral genus Porites on image-derived pointclouds and orthoprojections of a wild reef site at Palmyra Atoll.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Social Networks Can Help to Protect the Famous Dugong
reason: Popular-science (young readers) summary of a previously published original study on dugong detection in aerial video; it is a secondary account, not primary research. The underlying work is computer vision on wild dugongs.

title: Evaluating Cognitive Enrichment for Zoo-Housed Gorillas Using Facial Recognition
reason: Facial recognition of a troop of seven zoo-housed Western lowland gorillas at Bristol Zoo Gardens; no wild or free-ranging animals in the data.

title: DepthFormer: A High-Resolution Depth-Wise Transformer for Animal Pose Estimation
reason: Proposes a lightweight pose estimation network evaluated on AP-10K, which the paper describes as mammals in wild environments.

title: Computer Vision for Detection of Body Posture and Behavior of Red Foxes
reason: Red foxes kept individually in cages as laboratory animals during an oral rabies vaccine experiment; no wild or free-ranging animals in the analysed data.

title: Domain-Aware Neural Architecture Search for Classifying Animals in Camera Trap Images
reason: Proposes a neural architecture search method (DANAS) to design lightweight CNNs for species classification of wildlife camera trap images, evaluated on two camera trap datasets.

title: A Multi-Point Identification Approach for the Recognition of Individual Leopards (Panthera pardus kotiya)
reason: Individual leopards are identified by human visual comparison of spot and rosette patterns in DSLR photographs; spot counts are made by eye and analysed statistically (PCA, cluster analysis). No computer vision method is applied to the images.

title: Automated Video-Based Analysis Framework for Behavior Monitoring of Individual Animals in Zoos Using Deep Learning—A Study on Polar Bears
reason: The framework is developed and evaluated only on two captive polar bears in a zoo enclosure; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Unmanned Aircraft Systems as a Powerful Tool to Detect Fine-Scale Spatial Positioning and Interactions between Waterbirds at High-Tide Roosts
reason: Wild waterbirds were photographed by UAS, but each bird was identified and counted by hand in GIS. The only automated image analysis is habitat segmentation, so no computer vision is applied to the animals.

title: Behavioral Assessment of Six Reptile Species during a Temporary Zoo Closure and Reopening
reason: Behavioural observations of zoo reptiles were recorded live by human observers using the ZooMonitor app. No images or video were analysed and no computer vision was used. The animals are also captive only.

title: Multiobject Tracking of Wildlife in Videos Using Few-Shot Learning
reason: Proposes a few-shot multiobject-tracking framework (Few-MOT) for endangered wildlife in video; the paper presents the data as wildlife video for tracking in the wild, although it does not state where or how the videos were recorded.

title: Robust Algorithms for Drone-Assisted Monitoring of Big Animals in Harsh Conditions of Siberian Winter Forests: Recovery of European elk (Alces alces) in Salair Mountains
reason: Primary study that processes drone thermal infrared and RGB imagery with software to detect wild European elk in a Siberian nature reserve.

title: Development of a Slow Loris Computer Vision Detection Model
reason: All analysed images are of captive Bengal slow lorises kept in cages at wildlife rescue centers; no wild or free-ranging animals are in the data.

title: Power Up: Combining Behavior Monitoring Software with Business Intelligence Tools to Enhance Proactive Animal Welfare Reporting
reason: Commentary on using business intelligence software (Power BI) to visualise manually recorded ZooMonitor behaviour data of zoo animals; no image or video analysis.

title: Apex and ApeTouch: Development of a Portable Touchscreen System and Software for Primates at Zoos
reason: Develops a touchscreen apparatus and software for zoo-housed macaques; no computer vision or image analysis is performed, and all animals are captive.

title: Automated Cardiac Chamber Size and Cardiac Physiology Measurement in Water Fleas by U-Net and Mask RCNN Convolutional Networks
reason: Laboratory-cultured water fleas imaged under an inverted microscope for cardiac chamber segmentation in an ecotoxicity assay; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: The Future of Artificial Intelligence in Monitoring Animal Identification, Health, and Behaviour
reason: The primary work trains detection and individual recognition on Sumatran orangutans in an indoor enclosure at the Toronto Zoo; the additional online images are not described as showing wild animals, and the rest of the paper is a literature overview.

title: Animal Detection and Classification from Camera Trap Images Using Different Mainstream Object Detection Architectures
reason: Evaluates object detection models on camera trap images and videos of wild animals (plus two domestic species) from a national park; primary research.

title: Contour-Based Wild Animal Instance Segmentation Using a Few-Shot Detector
reason: Proposes a few-shot detection plus contour-based instance segmentation method for wild mammals, evaluated on an image dataset of 12 mammal species (mostly wild species, plus cow and horse) taken from COCO/PASCAL VOC and wildlife documentaries.

title: Diurnal and Nocturnal Behaviour of Cheetahs (Acinonyx jubatus) and Lions (Panthera leo) in Zoos
reason: Behaviour of zoo lions and cheetahs was manually annotated from video in BORIS with continuous sampling. No computer vision method was used, and all animals were captive.

title: The Relationship between Burrow Opening Dimensions and Biomass of Intertidal Macroinvertebrates by Feeding Mode (Surface Deposit Feeders vs. Suspension Feeders)
reason: Burrow opening diameters were measured with calipers in the field and related to biomass by regression. No image or video analysis is performed; drone-based object detection is only mentioned as future work.

title: Fine-Grained Butterfly Recognition via Peer Learning Network with Distribution-Aware Penalty Mechanism
reason: Proposes a CNN-based fine-grained classification method for butterflies, using web-collected natural field images of butterflies together with specimen images; also evaluated on the IP102 insect pest dataset.

title: Eyebirds: Enabling the Public to Recognize Water Birds at Hand
reason: Primary study proposing an attention-based CNN to classify water bird species from web-crawled bird images and CUB200-2011, with wildlife conservation as the stated application; the paper does not state whether the photographed birds are wild or captive.

title: Different Traits, Different Evolutionary Pathways: Insights from Salamandrina (Amphibia, Caudata)
reason: Wild salamanders were caught in the field and photographed. The head colour pattern in the photographs was analysed at pixel level with unsupervised and supervised clustering, after geometric morphometric standardisation. This counts as image analysis of wild animals.

title: Wild Terrestrial Animal Re-Identification Based on an Improved Locally Aware Transformer with a Cross-Attention Mechanism
reason: Proposes a transformer-based re-identification method evaluated on Amur tiger (ATRW), Tri-AI face and chimpanzee face (C-Zoo, C-Tai) datasets; wildlife re-identification is the stated subject, with zoo and wild chimpanzee data combined.

title: Size-Mediated Sea Turtle Behavioral Responses at Artificial Habitats in the Northern Gulf of Mexico
reason: Wild sea turtles filmed with stereo-video cameras, but the analysis was done by hand: reviewers coded behaviours and selected points manually in EventMeasure for length and distance measurements. No automated computer vision method was developed or applied.

title: A Novel, Automated, and Real-Time Method for the Analysis of Non-Human Primate Behavioral Patterns Using a Depth Image Sensor
reason: Behaviour analysis of laboratory monkeys in home cages at a primate research centre; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: A Comparative Assessment of Mid-Water Trawl and Deep Vision for Investigating Fishery Resources in the Coastal Waters off Jeju Island, Korea
reason: Stereo camera images of wild pelagic fish passing through a mid-water trawl are analysed with software (image filtering, tracking, counting, length measurement) for a fishery resource survey.

title: Dual-Fusion Active Contour Model with Semantic Information for Saliency Target Extraction of Underwater Images
reason: Generic underwater image segmentation method (active contour model) for salient target contour extraction; wildlife is not the stated subject or application, and the animals in the test images are not described.

title: Investigating Shape Variation Using Generalized Procrustes Analysis and Machine Learning
reason: Images show dead, mounted Nile tilapia specimens (caught in commercial fishing, partly from farms), not free-ranging animals; specimen imaging is treated like museum specimens.

title: Grouping Bilinear Pooling for Fine-Grained Image Classification
reason: Generic fine-grained classification method (compact bilinear pooling) evaluated on CUB-200-2011 and Stanford Cars; birds appear only as classes of a benchmark, and wildlife is not the stated subject.

title: Infrared Bird Target Detection Based on Temporal Variation Filtering and a Gaussian Heat-Map Perception Network
reason: Proposes a computer vision detection method (TVF + GHPNet) for free-flying birds and bats in thermal infrared video recorded outdoors.

title: Autonomous Temporal Pseudo-Labeling for Fish Detection
reason: Proposes an automatic pseudo-labeling pipeline for fish detection in baited remote underwater video of wild marine fish off the Algarve coast, with YOLOv4 as detector.

title: Birds Detection in Natural Scenes Based on Improved Faster RCNN
reason: Proposes an improved Faster RCNN for detecting birds in camera images from Hengshui Lake, a natural wetland scene; primary research on free-ranging birds.

title: Application of Low-Altitude UAV Remote Sensing Image Object Detection Based on Improved YOLOv5
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv5s detector for six wild grassland animals in aerial/UAV-perspective images for wildlife monitoring.

title: Underwater Sea Cucumber Identification Based on Improved YOLOv5
reason: Detection of farmed sea cucumbers in aquaculture waters (bottom sowing culture) for a harvesting robot; the animals are aquaculture stock, not wild free-ranging wildlife.

title: Identification of Shark Species Based on Their Dry Dorsal Fins through Image Processing
reason: Images show dried dorsal fins of sharks taken from the fin trade. These are processed specimens or products, not living wild or free-ranging animals.
