reason: Proposes a deep-feature fusion and optimized RNN classifier for fish species images; data include in-situ underwater images of fish in natural habitat (QUT FISH, DeepFish) alongside controlled and out-of-water specimen images.

title: Cues to individuality in Greylag Goose faces: algorithmic discrimination and behavioral field tests
reason: Primary study developing facial recognition software to identify individual Greylag Geese from photographs of a free-flying, habituated, supplementally fed flock.

title: The DeepFaune initiative: a collaborative effort towards the automatic identification of European fauna in camera trap images
reason: Develops a detection + CNN classification pipeline for camera-trap images of French wild fauna; the data also include domestic classes (cow, dog, sheep).

title: AcousticIA, a deep neural network for multi-species fish detection using multiple models of acoustic cameras
reason: Develops a CNN-based detector for wild migratory fish in imaging-sonar (acoustic camera) video recorded in rivers; the data are images analysed with computer vision, not sound-only signals.

title: A deep learning approach to detect and identify live freshwater macroinvertebrates
reason: Object detection of live freshwater macroinvertebrates sampled from outdoor experimental mesocosms and photographed in trays; no wild, free-ranging communities are analysed (the paper names wild communities only as a future application).

title: Social media image classification for jellyfish monitoring
reason: Primary study training CNNs to classify social media and iNaturalist images of wild Portuguese man-of-war, mostly stranded on beaches, for jellyfish monitoring.

title: A weakly supervised spatial group attention network for fine-grained visual recognition
reason: Proposes a CNN method for fine-grained bird species classification, evaluated on bird image datasets including a custom dataset from the Poyang Lake area; bird recognition is the stated subject and is motivated by conservation.

title: T-KD: two-tier knowledge distillation for a lightweight underwater fish species classification model
reason: Proposes a knowledge-distillation method for underwater fish species classification; data include wild fish images (Fish4knowledge underwater videos, WildFish, WildFish++) together with web-collected images and supermarket fish.

title: Spatial variation on the abundance of a threatened South American large herbivore using spatiotemporally replicated drone surveys
reason: Drone images of wild marsh deer were reviewed manually by human observers and the counts analysed with statistical N-mixture models; no computer vision method is applied to the images.

title: Identifying the drivers of silky shark distribution and an evaluation of protection measures
reason: Baited underwater video of wild silky sharks is annotated manually by video analysts (identification, MaxN, length); analysis is statistical (GLMs). No computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Research on Grassland Rodent Infestation Monitoring Methods Based on Dense Residual Networks and Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Remote Sensing
reason: UAV hyperspectral imaging with a deep CNN to classify wild grassland rodent holes (direct signs of free-ranging animals), vegetation and soil in natural grassland.

title: Comparing performance between a deep neural network and monkeys with bilateral removals of visual area TE in categorizing feature-ambiguous stimuli
reason: Neuroscience study comparing AlexNet layers with laboratory monkeys (control and TE-lesioned) on categorising photos of cats, dogs, human faces and monkey faces; no wild or free-ranging animals and no wildlife application.

title: Pitfall trapping outperforms other methods for surveying ground-dwelling large-bodied alpine invertebrates
reason: Field comparison of invertebrate survey methods (pitfall traps, tracking tunnels, visual surveys, trail cameras). Trail-camera images were counted and identified manually by the authors in Timelapse2; no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Analysis of Antennal Responses to Motion Stimuli in the Honey Bee by Automated Tracking Using DeepLabCut
reason: Laboratory behavioural assay on managed honey bees fixed in pipette tips; antennal movements tracked with DeepLabCut under controlled stimuli. No wild, free-ranging animals imaged.

title: Investigating the land-to-sea transition in carnivorans from the evolution of sacrum morphology in pinnipeds
reason: 3D geometric morphometric study of museum skeletal specimens (sacra) with manually digitized landmarks; no images of wild, free-ranging animals and no computer vision on such data.

title: Computer vision model with novel cuckoo search based deep learning approach for classification of fish image
reason: Classifies fish species presented as food/seafood items (incl. shrimp) in a public dataset; the paper frames the work around diet and agriculture/marine industry and never says that any images show wild, free-ranging animals.

title: SWIN transformer based contrastive self-supervised learning for animal detection and classification
reason: Proposes a self-supervised Swin Transformer method with animal classification as the stated application; evaluated on the Snapshot Serengeti camera-trap dataset of wild animals alongside domestic dog and generic benchmarks.

title: Bird-Count: a multi-modality benchmark and system for bird population counting in the wild
reason: Introduces a bird population counting dataset of birds in real-world ecological scenes and a CNN density-map counting method, deployed in wetland nature reserves.

title: Classification methods of butterfly images based on U-net and STL-MSDNet
reason: Proposes a CV method (U-Net segmentation + STL-MSDNet classification) for butterfly species identification on specimen images and ecological images of butterflies in the natural environment.

title: Optimzied resnet model of convolutional neural network for under sea water object detection and classification
reason: Proposes a CNN method for detecting and classifying underwater objects including fish, corals and sea urchins in marine images from public underwater datasets.

title: An objectness-aware network for wildlife detection
reason: Proposes a YOLOv3-based detector (OA-YOLO) and evaluates it on wildlife images from online resources, cameras in the wild and camera-trap datasets.

title: JF-YOLO: the jellyfish bloom detector based on deep learning
reason: Proposes a deep learning detector (JF-YOLO) for jellyfish in web-crawled underwater videos that the paper describes as real-world/real-environment footage. Whether any footage comes from aquaria is not stated.

title: Underwater video consistent enhancement: a real-world dataset and solution with progressive quality learning
reason: Generic underwater video enhancement paper (dataset plus quality-comparison network and colour-transfer enhancement). Animals appear only as content of the underwater videos; wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Underwater occluded object recognition with two-stage image reconstruction strategy
reason: Generic underwater object reconstruction/recognition for AUVs; targets are frogmen, torpedoes, submarines and AUVs; fish appear only incidentally and wildlife is not the stated subject.

title: Deep learning with invariant feature based species classification in underwater environments
reason: Proposes a computer vision pipeline (enhancement, segmentation, SURF features, GA selection, CNN) to classify octopus and crab classes in unconstrained underwater images that the paper says were captured with stationary cameras; nothing indicates captive animals.

title: Criss-cross global interaction-based selective attention in YOLO for underwater object detection
reason: Proposes attention modules for YOLO to detect underwater marine animals (holothurians, echinus, scallops, starfish, fish, crabs, etc.) in real marine imagery from URPC and Brackish datasets.

title: Smart bird identification system based on a hybrid approach: Petri nets, convolutional neural and deep residual networks
reason: Primary study that develops a YOLOv5 + ResNet-50 system to detect and classify images of 30 Taiwan endemic wild bird species, using images from Open Images, eBird Taiwan and the Internet.

title: Snake species classification using deep learning techniques
reason: Deep learning classification of snake species images from biodiversity citizen-science platforms (iNaturalist, HerpMapper) showing snakes in natural surroundings.

title: Object detection and classification of butterflies using efficient CNN and pre-trained deep convolutional neural networks
reason: Proposes a CNN-based detection (YOLOv3) and species classification (Effi-CNN) pipeline applied to images of wild butterfly species; primary research.

title: Underwater object detection based on enhanced YOLOv4 architecture
reason: Proposes an enhanced YOLOv4 detector for underwater marine invertebrates (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish) on the DUO dataset. The paper does not say where the images come from, but the subject is underwater animal detection.

title: Fine-grained bird image classification based on counterfactual method of vision transformer model
reason: Primary study proposing a Vision Transformer-based fine-grained bird species classification model, evaluated on two bird image datasets (CUB-200-2011, NABirds); birds are the stated subject and application. The paper does not describe how or where the bird images were taken.

title: Animal Pose Tracking: 3D Multimodal Dataset and Token-based Pose Optimization
reason: The paper introduces a laboratory rodent multimodal dataset and a 3D pose refinement model; other data are laboratory rats, tethered flies and cheetahs at wildlife-enclosure scale. No wild free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: WATB: Wild Animal Tracking Benchmark
reason: Introduces a visual object tracking benchmark of wild animal video sequences (from documentaries and the Internet) and evaluates 38 trackers on it.

title: Through Hawks’ Eyes: Synthetically Reconstructing the Visual Field of a Bird in Flight
reason: Captive-bred Harris' hawks flown in an indoor motion capture laboratory; the visual field is rendered synthetically from marker-based head tracking and a 3D lab model. No wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Dynamic Curriculum Learning for Great Ape Detection in the Wild
reason: Proposes a semi-supervised detection method evaluated mainly on camera-trap footage of wild great apes and on Snapshot Serengeti; it also uses a dataset of bees in hives and generic benchmarks, so subjects are mixed.

title: Context-Driven Detection of Invertebrate Species in Deep-Sea Video
reason: Presents a dataset and detection/counting methods for wild deep-sea invertebrates in ROV video from the ocean floor.

title: Improved 3D Markerless Mouse Pose Estimation Using Temporal Semi-supervision
reason: 3D pose estimation of laboratory mice recorded in a multi-camera cylindrical arena; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Semi-supervised Visual Tracking of Marine Animals Using Autonomous Underwater Vehicles
reason: Primary study that introduces an underwater video dataset of marine animals in their natural environment, benchmarks 13 visual trackers on it and deploys a tracker on an AUV to follow wild marine animals.

title: Multi-view Tracking, Re-ID, and Social Network Analysis of a Flock of Visually Similar Birds in an Outdoor Aviary
reason: Computer vision tracking and re-identification of a flock of 15 cowbirds housed in an enclosed outdoor aviary; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: BARC: Breed-Augmented Regression Using Classification for 3D Dog Reconstruction from Images
reason: The paper reconstructs 3D shape and pose of domestic dogs (pets) from images; no wild or free-ranging non-domestic animals are analysed.

title: Towards Automated Ethogramming: Cognitively-Inspired Event Segmentation for Streaming Wildlife Video Monitoring
reason: Proposes a self-supervised event segmentation and localization method and evaluates it on continuous nest-monitoring video of a wild Kagu collected in its natural habitat.

title: Self-supervised Secondary Landmark Detection via 3D Representation Learning
reason: Landmark (pose) detection method evaluated on caged laboratory macaques, laboratory Drosophila and humans; no wild or free-ranging animals in the analysed data.

title: DOVE: Learning Deformable 3D Objects by Watching Videos
reason: Computer vision method for 3D reconstruction of animals (birds, horses) learned from online YouTube videos; data is described as real animals without stating whether wild or domestic, plus toy bird models, so coded as mixed.

title: An Optimal Transport View of Class-Imbalanced Visual Recognition
reason: Generic class-imbalanced visual recognition method (optimal transport, Adaptive Bias Loss) tested on general long-tailed benchmarks; iNaturalist 2018 is used only as a benchmark and wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Automatic Generation of 3D Scene Animation Based on Dynamic Knowledge Graphs and Contextual Encoding
reason: The paper generates 3D human-centric scene animations from single images; people are the subject, and the only animals are domestic horses and dogs appearing as interaction partners in web videos. No wild, free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Exploring Vision-Language Models for Imbalanced Learning
reason: Generic long-tailed classification study with vision-language models; animals appear only as classes of general imbalanced benchmarks (ImageNet-LT, iNaturalist18, Places-LT) and wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Accurate Fine-Grained Object Recognition with Structure-Driven Relation Graph Networks
reason: Generic fine-grained object recognition method (SRGN) tested on bird, car, aircraft, person, vehicle and face benchmarks; wildlife is not the stated subject or application, and animals appear only as benchmark classes.

title: The Curious Layperson: Fine-Grained Image Recognition Without Expert Labels
reason: General fine-grained recognition method (image captioning plus document retrieval without expert labels) tested on the CUB-200 bird and Oxford-102 flower benchmarks; wildlife is not the stated subject or application, and the paper does not say how or where the bird images were taken.

title: Direct application of residual neural network to riverine aerial photography for estimating fish distribution
reason: A CNN is applied to aerial photographs of river sections (habitat/river morphology) to predict fish presence/absence from census data; no animals or their direct signs are visible in the analysed images.

title: Automated software for counting and measuring Hyalella genus using artificial intelligence
reason: Field-collected Hyalella amphipods are imaged as alcohol-preserved specimens in a Petri dish in a laboratory set-up; no images show free-ranging animals.

title: A real-time object detection method for underwater complex environments based on FasterNet-YOLOv7
reason: Detection of sea urchin, sea star, scallop and sea cucumber in images taken by an underwater robot in a marine pasture (marine ranching, a form of aquaculture production) for harvesting. It is not a study of wild, free-ranging animals for conservation.

title: An efficient network for multi-scale and overlapped wildlife detection
reason: Proposes a YOLOv3-based detector (WD-YOLO) for wildlife detection, trained and tested on a self-built wildlife dataset that includes web images and surveillance-camera images from the real wild environment.

title: Smoothness-based consistency learning for macaque pose estimation
reason: Semi-supervised pose estimation for macaques used as laboratory stand-ins for humans, evaluated only on the OpenMonkeyPose dataset, which the paper describes as obtainable only under an experimental environment; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Down the rabbit-hole: satellite-based analysis of spatiotemporal patterns in wild European rabbit burrows for better coastal dune management
reason: Burrow entrances of wild rabbits were digitised by hand from satellite, aerial and drone imagery and then analysed with spatial statistics. The paper uses no computer vision method; automated segmentation is mentioned only as a future option.

title: TEGAN: Transformer Embedded Generative Adversarial Network for Underwater Image Enhancement
reason: Generic underwater image enhancement method (TEGAN) evaluated with image-quality metrics. Animals appear only as object classes in a small downstream detection test; wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: A Dynamic Occupancy Model for Interacting Species with Two Spatial Scales
venue: Journal of Agricultural Biological and Environmental Statistics
reason: Borderline include: the paper is mainly a statistical occupancy model, but it applies an automatic image classification model (MLWIC) to camera trap photographs of wild small rodents and mustelids to produce the detection data.

title: Deep Neural Network Identification of Limnonectes Species and New Class Detection Using Image Data
venue: Journal of Agricultural Biological and Environmental Statistics
reason: CNN classification and new-class detection on photographs of preserved museum specimens of Limnonectes frogs (hind-leg skin texture); no images of free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Hybrid drone-based survey of riverine habitat and crocodiles in complex landscapes
venue: International Journal of Environmental Science and Technology
reason: UAV survey of wild crocodiles in which individuals were identified, counted and measured by hand on photogrammetric orthomosaics. No computer vision method is applied to detect or analyse the animals; image processing is limited to stitching images into maps.

title: Automated Freshwater Fish Species Classification using Deep CNN
venue: Journal of The Institution of Engineers (India) Series B
reason: CNN classification of images of freshwater fish; the authors' own samples were caught with nets from local ponds in Assam (wild-caught indigenous species, photographed after capture), combined with Fish-Pak images of cultured carps. Aquaculture framing is strong, but part of the data shows wild-caught indigenous fish.

title: Evaluation of pre-trained convolutional neural networks for the development of web/mobile-based bird species identification applications under Indian Bioresource Information Network (IBIN) framework
reason: Primary study evaluating pre-trained CNNs for classifying Indian bird species from web-collected photographs (eBird, Flickr), intended for field identification of birds; the paper does not explicitly state whether the photographed birds are wild or captive.

title: An Auto Encoder-Decoder Approach to Classify the Bird Sounds Using Deep Learning Techniques
reason: The study classifies bird species from audio recordings converted to Mel spectrograms; no images or video of animals are analysed.

title: A Novel Framework for Detection of Harmful Snakes Using YOLO Algorithm
reason: Applies YOLO-based computer vision to detect wild snakes in images and video, aimed at agricultural fields. The snakes are free-ranging wild animals, not livestock.

title: Interaction rules guiding collective behaviour in echolocating bats
reason: Thermal video of wild Brazilian free-tailed bats emerging from a cave; anatomical landmarks were tracked across frames to measure flight behaviour.

title: Qualitative Behaviour Assessment for zoo-housed polar bears (Ursus maritimus): Intra- and inter-day consistency and association to other indicators of welfare
reason: Qualitative Behaviour Assessment of zoo-housed polar bears done by human observers (direct and from video), followed by statistical analysis. No computer vision or automated image analysis, and the animals are captive only.

title: Koalas showed limited behavioural response and no physiological response to drones
reason: Behavioural and physiological responses of captive koalas to drones; the videos were scored by hand in Solomon Coder and no computer vision method was used. The animals are also captive in enclosures at a wildlife park.

title: A comparative taphonomic study of tooth marks caused by Iberian wolves (Canis lupus signatus) and domestic hunting dogs (Rehala) (Canis familiaris) on bovine scapulae, for taxonomic differentiation
reason: Taphonomic study of tooth marks by captive Iberian wolves and domestic dogs on bovine scapulae; marks are measured manually by observers and analysed with univariate statistics, with no computer vision method. The animals are also captive or domestic only.

title: Deep-worm-tracker: Deep learning methods for accurate detection and tracking for behavioral studies in C. elegans
reason: Detection and tracking of laboratory-cultured C. elegans worms on agar plates imaged under a stereo microscope; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Resting pattern and preferences when lying down at night in a semi-captive population of African elephants
reason: Trained human observers manually coded CCTV footage of semi-captive elephants and then ran statistical analyses (GLMM, Chi-square). No computer vision method is used. The animals are also semi-captive and housed in a boma.

title: A progressive deep learning framework for fine-grained primate behavior recognition
reason: Deep learning method for fine-grained primate behavior recognition in still images; dataset includes wild forest images alongside zoo, residential and domestic settings.

title: AntTracker: A low-cost and efficient computer vision approach to research leaf-cutter ants behavior
reason: Proposes a computer vision pipeline (segmentation, tracking, load classification) on video of free-ranging leaf-cutter ants recorded on natural trails near their nests. The ants are framed as agroecosystem pests, but the animals are wild and the study is about their behaviour in the field.

title: Feline faces: Unraveling the social function of domestic cat facial signals
reason: Behavioural study of domestic pet cats in a cat café; facial signals coded by hand with catFACS and analysed statistically. The animals are domestic and no computer vision is used.

title: Detecting wildlife trafficking in images from online platforms: A test case using deep learning with pangolin images
reason: CNN classification and detection applied to online images of pangolins, including live wild individuals in natural habitats as well as traded/dead animals and parts.

title: Towards automatic detection of wildlife trade using machine vision models
reason: Deep-learning image classification distinguishing exotic mammals in captive/sale contexts from the same species photographed in the wild (iNaturalist), for monitoring online wildlife trade; part of the data shows wild free-ranging animals.

title: Lost in the ashes? Broadscale passive monitoring provides limited insight into the impacts of Australia's megafires on biodiversity
reason: Ecological occupancy study of camera-trap data on wild mammals; images were identified manually by trained analysts and no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: SketchANIMAR: Sketch-based 3D animal fine-grained retrieval
reason: SHREC challenge on sketch-based retrieval of 3D animal mesh models sourced from online resources and video games; no images or video of wild, free-ranging animals are analysed and wildlife is not the application.

title: Wizard: Unsupervised goats tracking algorithm
reason: Tracking algorithm developed and evaluated on videos of farmed Creole goats on pasture at an agricultural research facility; no wild or free-ranging non-domestic animals.

title: Fast prediction in marmoset reach-to-grasp movements for dynamic prey
reason: Laboratory reach-to-grasp study of colony-housed marmosets and feeder crickets filmed in an experimental apparatus; no wild or free-ranging animals in the analysed data.

title: Obstacle avoidance in aerial pursuit
reason: Behavioural guidance study of four captive-bred, falconry-trained Harris' hawks flown in an indoor flight hall and tracked with marker-based motion capture; no wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Segmentation of butterflies from complex agro-ecological images using quantum mechanics and spatial refinement
reason: Proposes an unsupervised graph/quantum-cuts segmentation method for butterflies in natural agro-ecological images (Leeds Butterfly database).

title: Multi-sensor observation of a rapidly dispersing micronekton thin layer
venue: Deep Sea Research Part I Oceanographic Research Papers
reason: Primary study applying a classical computer vision pipeline (segmentation, SIFT stereo matching) to in situ stereo imagery of wild pelagic red crabs in the open ocean.

title: A baseline for the monitoring of Mediterranean upper bathyal biogenic reefs within the marine strategy framework directive objectives
venue: Deep Sea Research Part I Oceanographic Research Papers
reason: ROV video of wild deep-sea cold-water corals analysed with SfM photogrammetry (3D reconstruction) to measure colony density and height; computer vision applied to wild animals.

title: An experiment on animal re-identification from video
reason: Re-identification experiment on five web-sourced video clips of ornamental koi fish, street pigeons and farm pigs; the paper does not state that any of the animals are wild, non-domestic animals, and the named subjects are ornamental, urban or farm animals.

title: Re-identification of fish individuals of undulate skate via deep learning within a few-shot context
reason: Primary study developing a siamese-network photo-identification method on images of wild undulate skates photographed underwater or on board during tagging surveys.

title: Bag of tricks for long-tail visual recognition of animal species in camera-trap images
reason: Proposes and evaluates a long-tail classification framework for animal species in four camera-trap datasets of wild animals.

title: DeepWILD: Wildlife Identification, Localisation and estimation on camera trap videos using Deep learning
reason: Primary study that fine-tunes an object detection model to detect, classify and count wild species (plus humans, dogs, bikes) on camera trap videos from a French national park.

title: A comparative study on CNN-based semantic segmentation of intertidal mussel beds
reason: Applies CNN semantic segmentation to field images of wild intertidal mussel beds on Hong Kong rocky shores.

title: A semi-automatic workflow to process images from small mammal camera traps
reason: Primary study training a deep learning classifier on camera trap images of wild Arctic small mammals within a semi-automatic processing workflow.

title: Modelling dynamic fish-waterfall interactions with digital image field data: From rescaling to weir removal for migratory freshwater fish
reason: Wild barbels are filmed at a weir, but the paper is about biophysical and hydraulic modelling. The only image analysis is manual kinematic digitisation of video frames, summarised from earlier work; no computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Deep residual convolutional neural network based on hybrid attention mechanism for ecological monitoring of marine fishery
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for marine organisms in ROV underwater images of wild fish and invertebrates off Southern California; also tested on an open-sea farm dataset.

title: Comparison of two individual identification algorithms for snow leopards (Panthera uncia) after automated detection
reason: Evaluates individual identification algorithms (PIE v2, HotSpotter) on camera-trap images of free-ranging snow leopards in Afghanistan together with captive zoo images.

title: Giant panda face recognition based on PandaFaceNet
reason: Proposes a CNN-based face re-identification method for giant pandas, trained on captive images and tested on wild camera-trap images.

title: Automated wildlife image classification: An active learning tool for ecological applications
reason: Primary study proposing an object-detection plus image-classification pipeline with active learning on camera trap images of wild European mammals in Bavarian forests.

title: A few-shot rare wildlife image classification method based on style migration data augmentation
reason: Proposes a CycleGAN-based data augmentation method for few-shot classification of rare wild animals in camera images from a nature reserve.

title: Empowering novel scholarship at the intersection of machine learning/deep learning and ecology
reason: Editorial note on machine/deep learning in ecology; no primary research, no image data analysed.

title: Evaluating a tandem human-machine approach to labelling of wildlife in remote camera monitoring
reason: Primary study evaluating an object detection model (MegaDetector) on trail camera images of wild mammals and birds in Vermont and Maine, and its effect on human labelling efficiency.

title: A method for automatic identification and separation of wildlife images using ensemble learning
reason: Deep learning ensemble applied to camera trap images of wild animals in a nature reserve; the images also show humans and livestock.

title: Image background assessment as a novel technique for insect microhabitat identification
reason: Primary study applying instance segmentation and CNN+SVM classification to online photographs of free-ranging insects in Australia to classify the microhabitat shown in the image background.

title: Hierarchical classification of insects with multitask learning and anomaly detection
reason: Proposes a hierarchical CNN classifier with anomaly detection for images of live insects recorded in situ with time-lapse cameras and from GBIF observations.

title: Semi-supervised and weakly-supervised deep neural networks and dataset for fish detection in turbid underwater videos
reason: Primary study that develops deep learning models and a dataset for fish presence classification in underwater videos of wild fish recorded in turbid port waters.

title: Research on facial recognition of sika deer based on vision transformer
reason: Facial recognition of individual juvenile sika deer photographed at a deer breeding farm, so the animals are farmed. Generalization tests use a sheep face dataset and a seabird image set whose origin is not described.

title: An efficient segmentation method based on semi-supervised learning for seafloor monitoring in Pujada Bay, Philippines
reason: Semi-supervised semantic segmentation of field seafloor images of wild corals, sea urchins and sea stars (plus seagrass) in Pujada Bay.

title: Deer survey from drone thermal imagery using enhanced faster R-CNN based on ResNets and FPN
reason: Primary study that develops an enhanced Faster R-CNN to detect wild deer in UAV thermal images from Chitwan National Park, Nepal.

title: Membership inference attack for beluga whales discrimination
reason: Primary study applying CNN-based membership inference attacks to photographs of wild beluga and humpback whales to discriminate known from unknown individuals for photo-identification.

title: YWnet: A convolutional block attention-based fusion deep learning method for complex underwater small target detection
reason: Proposes a YOLOv5-based detector for underwater marine organisms (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish) in the URPC dataset. It also tests generalisation on an Aquarium dataset, so the data mix underwater marine benthos with aquarium animals.

title: Cellphone picture-based, genus-level automated identification of Chagas disease vectors: Effects of picture orientation on the performance of five machine-learning algorithms
reason: Genus-level image classification of dried, pinned triatomine bug specimens photographed on a white base with a tripod-mounted cellphone; no images of wild, free-ranging animals.

title: Development of a non-invasive method for species and sex identification of rare forest carnivores using footprint identification technology
reason: Image-based footprint identification (FIT) on photographed tracks (direct signs) of free-ranging fisher and marten collected at track plates, for species and sex classification.

title: A novel approach for surveying flowers as a proxy for bee pollinators using drone images
reason: Image analysis classifies flower pixels versus grass/soil in UAV orthomosaics; bees are not visible in the images and are only surveyed in the field and related to flower cover by regression.

title: Drone lidar-derived surface complexity metrics as indicators of intertidal oyster reef condition
reason: Primary study that analyses a UAS lidar-derived DSM (image raster) of natural, wild intertidal oyster reefs. It uses texture analysis (GLCM) and surface metrics to predict live oyster counts.

title: Age-groups classification of Irrawaddy dolphins based on dorsal fin geometric morphological features
reason: Image-based classification of age groups of wild Irrawaddy dolphins photographed in the Mekong River, using dorsal fin shape features.

title: Toward broad-scale mapping and characterization of prairie dog colonies from airborne imagery using deep learning
reason: Applies a deep CNN to UAS imagery to detect burrows (direct signs) of wild black-tailed prairie dogs and delineate colonies.

title: Stereo-ROV surveys of tropical reef fishes are comparable to stereo-DOVs with reduced behavioural biases
reason: Wild reef fish were filmed with stereo-video, but an experienced analyst identified, counted and measured the fish by hand in EventMeasure. No automated computer vision method was developed or evaluated; the study compares survey methods and fish behaviour using statistics.

title: A swimming crab portunus trituberculatus re-identification method based on RNN encoding of striped key regions
reason: Re-identification of farmed swimming crabs from a crab farm for aquaculture product tracing; no wild animals.

title: Joint image enhancement learning for marine object detection in natural scene
reason: Proposes a deep learning detector for marine organisms (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish) in natural underwater scene images; primary method research.

title: Semantic attention and relative scene depth-guided network for underwater image enhancement
reason: Generic underwater image enhancement method (SARSDN) evaluated on underwater image benchmarks; animals (fish, benthic organisms) appear only as scene content and wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: WILDetect: An intelligent platform to perform airborne wildlife census automatically in the marine ecosystem using an ensemble of learning techniques and computer vision
reason: Primary study developing a computer vision platform to detect, split and count free-ranging Northern gannets in airborne offshore survey images.

title: Analyzing the pregnancy status of giant pandas with hierarchical behavioral information
reason: Behaviour recognition and pregnancy analysis using video of captive, artificially inseminated giant pandas at a breeding centre only; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Augmented weighted bidirectional feature pyramid network for marine object detection
reason: Proposes a CNN detection network for marine organisms in underwater images, evaluated on sea ranch (UTDAC), aquarium (AMLD) and natural underwater (RUOD) data. Part of the data shows free-living marine animals.

title: DP-FishNet: Dual-path Pyramid Vision Transformer-based underwater fish detection network
reason: Proposes a vision transformer-based detector for wild coral reef fish in real underwater videos (SeaCLEF2017).

title: Fish behavior in response to an approaching underwater camera
reason: Stereo image analysis (3D positions, KLT point tracking, camera motion estimation) applied to underwater images of wild demersal fish in Alaska to study behaviour.

title: Face recognition of a Lorisidae species based on computer vision
reason: All analysed images show Bengal slow lorises housed in iron cages at a wildlife rescue center; no images of free-ranging animals are used, although the individuals are assumed wild-caught.

title: Undertaking wildlife surveys with unmanned aerial vehicles in rugged mountains with dense vegetation: A tentative model using Sichuan Snub-nosed monkeys in China
reason: UAV thermal survey of wild Sichuan snub-nosed monkeys; video records were checked manually to count individuals, and no computer vision or automated image analysis method was applied.

title: Automatic segmentation of Caenorhabditis elegans skeletons in worm aggregations using improved U-Net in low-resolution image sequences
reason: Laboratory model organism (C. elegans) cultured on Petri dishes and imaged in a lab capture system; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Fish-TViT: A novel fish species classification method in multi water areas based on transfer learning and vision transformer
reason: Vision-transformer fish species classification on images of marine fish from fishery electronic monitoring (wild-caught fish) together with a freshwater fish image dataset (farmed carp species); primary method paper.

title: Efficient unsupervised learning of biological images with compressed deep features
reason: Unsupervised clustering method for biological images evaluated on wild plankton and coral image datasets (e.g., coral images from the Red Sea), together with laboratory cell datasets.

title: Semi-supervised classification with pairwise constraints: A case study on animal identification from video
reason: Proposes a semi-supervised classification method with pairwise constraints for individual animal re-identification from video; data include free-ranging pigeons (square, pavement, curb) together with koi fish and pigs, so wild animals appear alongside domestic/captive ones.

title: Improving long-tailed classification by disentangled variance transfer
reason: Generic long-tailed image classification method tested on CIFAR-LT, ImageNet-LT and iNaturalist 2018 as benchmarks; wildlife is not the stated subject or application (the framing is IoT).

title: Constitutive depletion of brain serotonin differentially affects rats’ social and cognitive abilities
reason: Behavioural neuroscience study of laboratory knockout rats in operant cages and a visible burrow system; videos were scored manually by observers, with no wild animals.

title: Social and sexual consequences of facial femininity in a non-human primate
reason: Develops a DCNN-based face-space method to estimate facial femininity from field portraits of a free-ranging wild mandrill population in Gabon, linking it to behaviour.

title: Optical multiband polarimetric modulation sensing for gender and species identification of flying native solitary pollinators
reason: Laboratory flight-chamber study of bees hatched from purchased cocoons; classification uses photodetector lidar-like signals (optical cross-section, polarization, wingbeat spectra), with a camera used only for 3D trajectory description.

title: From crowd to herd counting: How to precisely detect and count African mammals using aerial imagery and deep learning?
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
reason: The analysed aerial images contain only domestic livestock (camels, donkeys, sheep, goats) of semi-nomadic herders in a protected area; no wild animals are in the data analysed in the main text.

title: Sphere2Vec: A general-purpose location representation learning over a spherical surface for large-scale geospatial predictions
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
reason: Proposes a spherical location encoder evaluated on geo-aware image classification, with fine-grained species recognition on iNaturalist and bird image datasets as a stated application, alongside Flickr and remote sensing tasks.

title: ARIANNA: A novel deep learning-based system for fin contours analysis in individual recognition of dolphins
reason: Proposes a semantic-segmentation-based fin contour system for photo identification of individual wild Risso's dolphins photographed during marine research expeditions.

title: Photo identification for sea turtles: Flipper scales more accurate than head scales using APHIS
venue: Journal of Experimental Marine Biology and Ecology
reason: Primary study applying semi-automated photo-identification software (APHIS) to photographs of wild-caught green turtles to identify individuals.

title: Computer-aided fish assessment in an underwater marine environment using parallel and progressive spatial information fusion
venue: Journal of King Saud University - Computer and Information Sciences
reason: Proposes CNN segmentation networks for fish in underwater marine imagery (SUIM, DeepFish), plus a supermarket seafood dataset; wild underwater fish form part of the data.

title: MAPoseNet: Animal pose estimation network via multi-scale convolutional attention
venue: Journal of Visual Communication and Image Representation
reason: Proposes a pose estimation network evaluated on AP-10K (wild animals in native habitats) and Animal Pose (domestic animals); wild animals are part of the analysed data.

title: Edge-guided oceanic scene element detection
reason: Detects oceanic scene elements (bays, beaches, buoys, islands, sea stacks, etc.) in scene images. Animals are not the subject; this is about scene and landform detection.

title: Coral Detection, Ranging, and Assessment (CDRA) algorithm-based automatic estimation of coral reef coverage
reason: Proposes a CV pipeline (YOLOv5 detection, stereo ranging, StrongSORT tracking) to estimate coral coverage. It is evaluated in a coral breeding pool and on wild fringing reefs at Xidao.

title: CNN based color balancing and denoising technique for underwater images: CNN-CBDT
reason: Generic underwater image enhancement/restoration method; animals are not the subject and no wildlife analysis is performed.

title: A binocular vision-based underwater object size measurement paradigm: Calibration-Detection-Measurement (C-D-M)
reason: Generic underwater binocular object size measurement method tested on static, non-animal objects in an outdoor pool; no animals are the subject.

title: Annotating very high-resolution satellite imagery: A whale case study
reason: Step-by-step protocol for manually annotating VHR satellite images of whales in GIS software; no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated, and no data are analysed.

title: Automating mosquito taxonomy by compressing and enhancing a feature fused EfficientNet with knowledge distillation and a novel residual skip block
reason: Proposes a CNN method that classifies images of mosquito species, which are non-domestic insects. The paper does not say where the images come from or whether the mosquitoes were wild.

title: Achieving domain generalization for underwater object detection by domain mixup and contrastive learning
reason: Proposes a domain generalization method for underwater object detection of marine invertebrates (echinus, holothurian, starfish, scallop). The origin of the images (wild or farmed) is not stated, but the animals are the detection subjects in underwater scenes.

title: Boosting R-CNN: Reweighting R-CNN samples by RPN’s error for underwater object detection
reason: Proposes an underwater object detector evaluated on images of aquatic organisms (echinus, holothurian, starfish, scallop, fish, crab, jellyfish, shrimp); the Brackish dataset was collected in natural brackish waters. Generic benchmarks (VOC, COCO) are used only to show generalisation.

title: Curricular-balanced long-tailed learning
reason: Generic long-tailed image classification loss (CurB Loss) evaluated on general benchmarks; iNaturalist18 is used only as a long-tailed benchmark and wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Automatic classification of biofouling images from offshore renewable energy structures using deep learning
reason: Primary study applying CNN image classification to images of free-living marine fouling invertebrates (mussels, barnacles, calcareous worms) from web/naturalist sources and offshore structures.

title: EFP-YOLO: A quantitative detection algorithm for marine benthic organisms
reason: Proposes a YOLOX-based detector for marine benthic organisms (sea cucumbers, sea urchins, scallops, starfish) in underwater images. The data includes naturally grown organisms as well as cultured ones.

title: The Open-source Camera Trap for Organism Presence and Underwater Surveillance (OCTOPUS)
reason: Open-source underwater camera trap that uses computer-vision motion detection (MOG background subtraction) to trigger image capture. It was field-deployed on wild ruby octopuses in Puget Sound.

title: Weakly-supervised butterfly detection based on saliency map
reason: Proposes a weakly-supervised CNN detector for butterflies in natural ecological images (field photography and web). It also runs an extra test on the Oxford-IIIT Pet dataset of domestic animals, so subject_type is mixed.

title: Underwater object detection algorithm based on feature enhancement and progressive dynamic aggregation strategy
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for underwater images of marine animals (holothurian, echinus, starfish, scallop). The paper does not describe the animals as farmed or captive, so they are coded as wild.

title: LCReg: Long-tailed image classification with Latent Categories based Recognition
reason: Generic long-tailed image classification method evaluated on general benchmarks (CIFAR-LT, ImageNet-LT, iNaturalist 2018, Places-LT); wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Separated Fan-Beam Projection with Gaussian Convolution for Invariant and Robust Butterfly Image Retrieval.
reason: Handcrafted image descriptor for butterfly image retrieval, evaluated on the Leeds dataset of butterflies photographed in natural environments and on museum Heliconius specimens.

title: A gated cross-domain collaborative network for underwater object detection
reason: Proposes an underwater object detection network evaluated on underwater datasets with marine organisms (echinus, holothurian, starfish, scallop, fish, crab, jellyfish, shrimp) in natural waters.

title: BeeNet: An End-To-End Deep Network For Bee Surveillance
reason: Deep learning classification of bee species from iNaturalist images, including wild bumble bees and carpenter bees, plus honey bee health datasets (varroa and pollen).

title: Wild Animal Detection using YOLOv8
reason: Applies YOLOv8 object detection to images of wild animals (lions, tigers, leopards, bears) gathered from documentaries, YouTube and Kaggle, aimed at reducing human-wildlife conflict.

title: Automatic detection of brown hens in cage-free houses with deep learning methods
reason: The study detects domestic laying hens (poultry) in cage-free houses on a research farm; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Validation of satellite imagery for quantitative population assessment and monitoring of Atlantic walrus
venue: Remote Sensing Applications Society and Environment
reason: Wild Atlantic walrus are imaged by satellite and from an aircraft, but people counted the animals and digitized the haul-out area by hand. The images are interpreted visually, with no computer vision method applied to the animals.

title: Deep learning based whale detection from satellite imagery
reason: Proposes a modified Tiny YOLOv3 detector for whales in very high resolution satellite imagery of free-ranging whales at ocean hotspots.

title: Maternal behavioural analysis during a successful captive breeding of jaguars Panthera onca
reason: Behaviour of a single captive jaguar was coded by hand from camera-trap/infrared video and analysed with GLMs. No computer vision method is used, and the animal is captive.

title: Environmental enrichment for reptiles in European zoos: Current status and perspectives
reason: Questionnaire survey of European zoos about environmental enrichment for captive reptiles; no image or video data and no computer vision method.

title: Toward low-cost automated monitoring of life below water with deep learning
reason: Applies YOLOv4 and YOLOv7 to detect and classify wild fish in baited deep-sea video from a marine refuge off Newfoundland.

title: Time-lapse recording of yearly activity of the sea star Odontaster validus and the sea urchin Sterechinus neumayeri in Tethys Bay (Ross Sea, Antarctica)
reason: Time-lapse underwater images of wild Antarctic benthos were identified, counted and scored for activity manually by an author; no computer vision method is described.

title: The contribution of penguin guano to the Southern Ocean iron pool
reason: Applies a Faster R-CNN deep learning model to drone imagery to detect and count wild Chinstrap penguins in an Antarctic rookery.

title: Deep learning enables satellite-based monitoring of large populations of terrestrial mammals across heterogeneous landscape
reason: Primary study developing a U-Net-based deep learning pipeline to detect and count wild migratory wildebeest and zebra in fine-resolution satellite imagery of the Serengeti-Mara ecosystem.

title: Automatically annotated motion tracking identifies a distinct social behavioral profile following chronic social defeat stress
reason: Open-source tool for behavioural profiling of laboratory mice from DeepLabCut pose estimation in open field arenas after chronic social defeat stress; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Fine-scale collective movements reveal present, past and future dynamics of a multilevel society in Przewalski’s horses
reason: Drone video of free-ranging Przewalski's horses in a 3000-ha natural steppe reserve, processed with image-based motion tracking to get individual trajectories for social network analysis.

title: Large-scale capture of hidden fluorescent labels for training generalizable markerless motion capture models
reason: Markerless pose tracking method developed and evaluated on laboratory mice in behavioural set-ups and on a human hand; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: replicAnt: a pipeline for generating annotated images of animals in complex environments using Unreal Engine
reason: Synthetic-data pipeline for animal detection, tracking, pose estimation and segmentation; evaluated on laboratory insect recordings and on field recordings of free-ranging desert termites.

title: Facemap: a framework for modeling neural activity based on orofacial tracking
reason: Keypoint tracking of orofacial movements in head-fixed transgenic laboratory mice during two-photon neural recordings; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: CherryChèvre: A fine-grained dataset for goat detection in natural environments
reason: Dataset paper on detection of farmed goats and sheep on experimental farm pastures and indoor pens; no wild, free-ranging non-domestic animals are the subject.

title: Three-dimensional unsupervised probabilistic pose reconstruction (3D-UPPER) for freely moving animals
reason: Pose reconstruction method validated on laboratory C57BL/6J mice in open-field arenas with brain implants, plus simulated shapes; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Automated monitoring of honey bees with barcodes and artificial intelligence reveals two distinct social networks from a single affiliative behavior
reason: Behaviour detection on barcoded honey bees (a managed species) kept in a glass-walled observation hive in a dark, climate-controlled room; a laboratory set-up, not wild free-ranging animals.

title: New machine learning-based automatic high-throughput video tracking system for assessing water toxicity using Daphnia Magna locomotory responses
reason: Video tracking of laboratory-cultured Daphnia magna in flow cells for ecotoxicity testing; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Artificial intelligence for automated detection of large mammals creates path to upscale drone surveys
reason: Primary study training a Faster-RCNN to detect and count wild caribou in drone orthomosaics from Wapusk National Park.

title: Evaluating the effects of giraffe skin disease and wire snare wounds on the gaits of free-ranging Nubian giraffe
reason: Gait kinematics of wild and zoo giraffe measured by manual digitizing of video frames (GaitKeeper, ImageJ angle tool) followed by linear mixed models; the paper uses no automated computer vision method.

title: Learning from algorithm-generated pseudo-annotations for detecting ants in videos
reason: Proposes a deep learning method for detecting ants in videos recorded under natural conditions in a tropical rainforest; wild free-ranging animals analysed with computer vision.

title: DeepAction: a MATLAB toolbox for automated classification of animal behavior in video
reason: Behaviour classification toolbox evaluated only on laboratory mouse videos and videos of single-housed octopus in a lab tank; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Insect recognition based on complementary features from multiple views
reason: The paper proposes a feature-fusion classification method for insect crop pests, evaluated only on the IP102 pest dataset; the subject is agricultural pest recognition, not wildlife.

title: Decadal decline in maternal body condition of a Southern Ocean capital breeder
reason: Aerial photogrammetry (image-based body measurements) of wild southern right whales from helicopter and UAV images to assess body condition.

title: EXPLORE: a novel deep learning-based analysis method for exploration behaviour in object recognition tests
reason: Deep-learning behaviour classification of laboratory mice in object recognition test arenas; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Hydrodynamics of the fast-start caridoid escape response in Antarctic krill, Euphausia superba
reason: Wild-caught krill were filmed in a laboratory glass test tank with a tomo-PIV set-up. All analysed images come from a lab set-up, not from free-ranging animals.

title: Photogrammetry as a promising tool to unveil marine caves’ benthic assemblages
reason: Primary study applying Structure from Motion photogrammetry to diver-collected underwater images of wild sessile benthic animals (sponges, hydroids, date mussel holes) in a natural marine cave. Annotation of the orthomosaics was manual.

title: An automated image-based workflow for detecting megabenthic fauna in optical images with examples from the Clarion–Clipperton Zone
reason: Primary study proposing an object detection workflow (FaunD-Fast) for wild deep-sea megabenthic fauna in seafloor images recorded by a towed camera in the Clarion-Clipperton Zone.

title: Horses (Equus caballus) facial micro-expressions: insight into discreet social information
reason: Studies facial micro-expressions of domestic horses kept in stables, coded manually from video with EquiFACS in BORIS; domestic animals and no automated computer vision.

title: A collaborative and near-comprehensive North Pacific humpback whale photo-ID dataset
reason: Dataset paper on photo-ID of wild North Pacific humpback whales; fluke images are matched to individuals with an automated machine-learning image recognition system.

title: Fusion of visible and thermal images improves automated detection and classification of animals for drone surveys
reason: Drone visible/thermal fusion study on white-tailed deer held in research enclosures plus domestic cows and horses in paddocks; no wild, free-ranging animals in the analysed data.

title: WormSwin: Instance segmentation of C. elegans using vision transformer
reason: Instance segmentation of the laboratory model organism C. elegans in microscope/petri-dish recordings; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Quantifying the behavioural consequences of shark ecotourism
reason: Primary study applying a deep learning pose/tracking system (SLEAP) to UAV video of wild whale sharks to quantify behaviour under ecotourism.

title: Real-time jellyfish classification and detection algorithm based on improved YOLOv4-tiny and improved underwater image enhancement algorithm
reason: Jellyfish detection with an improved YOLOv4-tiny on a dataset combining a public field jellyfish dataset, web-crawled images and images collected in the authors' lab; at least part shows free-ranging jellyfish.

title: Individual identification of endangered amphibians using deep learning and smartphone images: case study of the Japanese giant salamander (Andrias japonicus)
reason: Individual identification of Japanese giant salamanders using deep learning, but all images are of 11 captive individuals kept at a zoo breeding facility; no wild or free-ranging animals are in the analysed data.

title: Quantifying agonistic interactions between group-housed animals to derive social hierarchies using computer vision: a case study with commercially group-housed rabbits
reason: The study analyses video of commercially group-housed farm rabbits in pens; no wild or free-ranging animals are involved.

title: Migratory destinations and spatial structuring of humpback whales (Megaptera novaeangliae) wintering off Nicaragua
reason: Applies automated image recognition (Happywhale fluke matching) to photo-identify wild humpback whales from boat-based and citizen science photographs.

title: A fast and accurate identification model for Rhinolophus bats based on fine-grained information
reason: Deep learning classification of images of seven Rhinolophus bat species photographed during field surveys in South China; primary research on wild bats.

title: YOLO object detection models can locate and classify broad groups of flower-visiting arthropods in images
reason: Trains and evaluates YOLO object detectors on citizen-science photographs of flower-visiting arthropods (GBIF-indexed iNaturalist and Observation.org images) for pollinator monitoring; primary research on free-ranging animals.

title: Wing Interferential Patterns (WIPs) and machine learning for the classification of some Aedes species of medical interest
reason: Dissected mosquito wings (collection specimens and lab colony) photographed under a microscope for species classification; this is a laboratory microscopy set-up, not imaging of free-ranging animals.

title: Counting manatee aggregations using deep neural networks and Anisotropic Gaussian Kernel
reason: Proposes a deep-learning density-estimation counting method for manatees in webcam surveillance video from Blue Spring State Park; wild free-ranging animals are the subject.

title: An automated rat grimace scale for the assessment of pain
reason: Automated rat grimace scale developed on images of laboratory Sprague Dawley and Wistar rats in pain research set-ups; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Gender identification of the horsehair crab, Erimacrus isenbeckii (Brandt, 1848), by image recognition with a deep neural network
reason: CNN-based sex classification on photographs of wild-caught horsehair crabs collected in Funka Bay; the animals are wild-caught and photographed after capture, with a fisheries-management aim.

title: Machine learning framework for precise localization of bleached corals using bag-of-hybrid visual feature classification
reason: Computer vision classification of bleached versus unbleached corals (sessile animals) in underwater images from the Great Barrier Reef; primary research.

title: Anomalous behavior recognition of underwater creatures using lite 3D full-convolution network
reason: Behaviour recognition of farmed fish (tilapia, cobia) kept in tanks/pools during breeding experiments, aimed at the breeding and aquaculture industry; no wild free-ranging animals in the analysed data.

title: Classifying stages in the gonotrophic cycle of mosquitoes from images using computer vision techniques
reason: All images are of mosquitoes reared in captivity in two laboratories, anesthetized and photographed on a plain background; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Assessment of the utility of underwater hyperspectral imaging for surveying and monitoring coral reef ecosystems
reason: Primary study applying a deep-learning classifier to underwater hyperspectral imagery of wild reef benthos (scleractinian corals, sponges, other invertebrates, alongside algae) in Guam.

title: The first use of a photogrammetry drone to estimate population abundance and predict age structure of threatened Sumatran elephants
reason: Drone RGB imagery of wild Sumatran elephants is analysed with a CNN segmentation platform to count animals and measure body length for abundance and age structure estimation.

title: Deep learning-based image classification of turtles imported into Korea
reason: Primary study applying SSD object detection models to Internet-collected images of 36 non-domestic turtle species to support trade control and invasive species detection in the wild; images include turtles in marine, freshwater and grassland habitats, though the paper does not state whether individuals are wild or captive.

title: OSAP‐Loss: Efficient optimization of average precision via involving samples after positive ones towards remote sensing image retrieval
reason: Generic image-retrieval loss function aimed at remote sensing scene retrieval; animals appear only as classes of the fine-grained benchmarks CUB-200-2011 and INaturalist-2018, and wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Health evaluation and dangerous reptile detection using a novel framework powered by the YOLO algorithm to design high‐content cellular imaging systems
reason: Applies YOLOv5 and ResNeXt to images and videos of snakes, which are non-domestic animals, to detect and classify them for farmer safety. The paper does not say where the images come from.

title: Smart Agriculture Land Crop Protection Intrusion Detection Using Artificial Intelligence
reason: Camera-based CNN detection of animals, including wild elephants and bears, entering farmland to reduce human-wildlife conflict. Domestic cows and sheep are also detected, so the subject type is mixed.

title: Crop protection from animals based on machine learning
reason: Applies a deep-learning object detector (YOLOv3) to camera footage to detect wild animals intruding into crop fields (human-wildlife conflict). The paper does not say whether the animals in the analysed footage were wild or free-ranging; the examples shown are an elephant, a horse and a cow, so inclusion rests on the stated wildlife application.

title: Automated Tasmanian devil segmentation and devil facial tumour disease classification
reason: Develops a segmentation and disease classification pipeline on camera images of wild Tasmanian devils captured during field monitoring.

title: Comparisons of morphometrics and body condition between two breeding populations of Australian humpback whales
reason: UAV video stills of wild migrating humpback whales analysed by photogrammetry to measure morphometrics and body condition.

title: Wild animals suppress the spread of socially transmitted misinformation
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
reason: Applies automated video tracking and visual field reconstruction to wild coral reef fish groups filmed in the field to study escape behaviour.

title: Evolutionary predictors of the specific colors of birds
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
reason: Primary study applying pixel-level colour image analysis to images (handbook plates) of nearly all wild bird species to quantify plumage colour categories; borderline because images are illustrations rather than photographs.

title: Convergence in sympatric swallowtail butterflies reveals ecological interactions as a key driver of worldwide trait diversification
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
reason: Computer vision (SimCLR, Mask-RCNN) is applied to photographs of museum specimens of swallowtail butterflies, not to images of live free-ranging animals.

title: Evaluation of mouse behavioral responses to nutritive versus nonnutritive sugar using a deep learning-based 3D real-time pose estimation system
reason: Laboratory C57BL/6J mice recorded in an indoor multi-camera behaviour chamber for 3D pose estimation; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: RETRACTED ARTICLE: A Deep Learning Approach to Detecting Objects in Underwater Images
reason: Retracted paper presenting a generic CNN-based underwater object detection pipeline on an unspecified Kaggle image set. The detected object classes are never named, and wild animals are not the stated subject of the experiments; marine life appears only in the background and related-work sections.

title: High-resolution benthic habitat mapping from machine learning on PlanetScope imagery and ICESat-2 data
reason: Satellite-based benthic habitat / bottom-cover mapping (seagrass, coral cover, sand, hard bottom) with pixel-based classification; habitat and substrate classes only, no animals as individual subjects.

title: Toward the automatic detection of effective gerbil holes in desert grasslands through unmanned aerial vehicle imagery
reason: Primary study applying object-based image analysis to UAV imagery to identify burrow holes (direct signs) of wild Mongolian gerbils in desert grassland.

title: Three-dimensional (3D) modelling to determine the weight of massive corals in Gili Labak Island, Sumenep, Madura, East Java, Indonesia
reason: Photogrammetric 3D reconstruction from underwater photographs of wild massive corals at Gili Labak Island to estimate colony volume and weight.

title: The development of object play in wolf puppies (Canis lupus)
reason: Ethological study of hand-reared captive wolf pups. The videos were coded by hand by human observers in Noldus Observer XT and no computer vision method is applied. The animals are also captive only (E-CAPTIVE would apply too).

title: Honeybee flight dynamics and pair separation in windy conditions near the hive entrance
reason: Flight tracking of managed honeybees at the entrance of a kept hive (beekeeping); the animals fly freely outdoors but are domestic, not wild.

title: New insights into the influence of turbines on the behaviour of migrant birds: implications for predicting impacts of offshore wind developments on wildlife
reason: Applies automatic target detection and stereo-thermographic tracking to video of wild migrant birds and bats around offshore wind turbines.

title: Research on an underwater image segmentation algorithm based on YOLOv8
reason: Generic underwater instance segmentation of boats, divers, seagrass, coral, debris, fish, humans and robots; animals appear only as some of the classes, and wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Contact feedback helps snake robots propel against uneven terrain using vertical bending
reason: Robotics study of feedback controllers for a snake robot traversing bumps; cameras only track ArUco markers on the robot and terrain. No images of animals are analysed; snakes are only biological inspiration from earlier studies.

title: Active wing-pitching mechanism in hummingbird escape maneuvers
reason: Hummingbirds filmed with high-speed cameras inside a transparent lab chamber for kinematic reconstruction and CFD; no wild or free-ranging animals in the data.

title: The use of stereo cameras and artificial intelligence data to support capture fisheries landing data monitoring
venue: IOP Conference Series Earth and Environmental Science
reason: The system detects, counts and measures fish baskets (man-made containers) at a fishing port; no wild, free-ranging animals are analysed, only landed catch inside baskets. No criterion fits exactly; E-HUMAN is the closest for non-animal, human-related objects.

title: Comparative image analysis approaches to assess ecological effects of macroalgal removal on inshore reefs of Magnetic Island, Australia
venue: IOP Conference Series Earth and Environmental Science
reason: Applies the automated image annotation tool CoralNet to underwater photographs of wild inshore reef benthos, including coral and sponge cover, and compares it with manual annotation.

title: Coral Reefs Detecting with Artificial Neural Network Classification and PlanetScope Imagery in Cu Lao Xanh Island, Binh Dinh province
venue: IOP Conference Series Earth and Environmental Science
reason: Applies image classification (ANN, MLC) to PlanetScope satellite imagery to map wild hard and soft coral reefs (animals) around Cu Lao Xanh Island; primary research.

title: Robust detection of marine life with label-free image feature learning and probability calibration
reason: Primary study that trains deep image classifiers on in situ underwater images of free-living plankton and particles collected at sea. Class names are only given in a figure, so the animal share of the classes is not stated in the text.

title: A picture is worth a thousand dollars: a photographic approach to studying colour in anoles
venue: Biological Journal of the Linnean Society
reason: Validates an image-analysis method that measures RGB colour from field photographs of wild-caught Anolis lizards, sampled in urban and forest habitats. The lizards were caught, photographed and released at the point of capture.

title: Collective decision-making and spatial patterns in orientation of an endemic ungulate on the Tibetan Plateau
reason: Drone videos of wild kiang were analysed by manual tracking, manual behaviour scoring and manual coordinate extraction in ImageJ. The only automated image processing is a perspective correction, and no computer vision method analyses the animals.

title: Scaling of Gait, Limb Posture, Forces, and Inertial Properties in Terrestrial Locomotion of American Alligators Across a Thousand-Fold Increase in Body Mass
reason: Biomechanics study of American alligators kept in a zoo enclosure (adults) plus earlier lab juveniles. Video was digitized by hand and photogrammetry was used for 3D meshes. No wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Using machine learning to alleviate the allometric effect in otolith shape-based species discrimination: the role of a triplet loss function
reason: Species classification from microscope images of otoliths extracted from dead bycatch fish in the laboratory; no images of wild, free-ranging animals or their field signs.

title: An integrated end-to-end deep neural network for automated detection of discarded fish species and their weight estimation
reason: Primary study proposing a modified YOLOv5 for detection, species classification and weight estimation of wild-caught discarded fish imaged on the conveyor belt of North Sea beam trawlers (fisheries monitoring). The animals are wild, non-farmed fish, but they are imaged as catch after capture, not free-ranging, so inclusion is a borderline call.

title: Shaped by Their Environment: Variation in Blue Whale Morphology across Three Productive Coastal Ecosystems
reason: Applies UAS-image photogrammetry to measure the morphology of wild blue whales in three foraging grounds. This is image analysis of free-ranging animals.

title: Automatic estimation of lipid content from in situ images of Arctic copepods using machine learning
reason: CNN segmentation of lipid sacs in in situ images of free-living Arctic copepods taken by a towed underwater imaging system; primary research.

title: Automatic recording of rare behaviors of wild animals using video bio-loggers with on-board light-weight outlier detector
reason: The rare-behaviour detector runs on accelerometer and water-depth sensor data, not on images. The bio-logger video it triggers was categorised manually, so no computer vision is applied to images.

title: Downsized: gray whales using an alternative foraging ground have smaller morphology
reason: Drone-based photogrammetric measurement of body morphology of free-ranging gray whales from UAS video snapshots; image-based analysis of wild animals.

title: Visual versus visual-inertial guidance in hawks pursuing terrestrial targets
venue: Journal of The Royal Society Interface
reason: Behavioural guidance-law modelling of captive-bred Harris' hawks flown indoors in a flight hall, tracked with marker-based motion capture; no wild or free-ranging animals in the analysed data.

title: Hummingbirds use wing inertial effects to improve manoeuvrability
venue: Journal of The Royal Society Interface
reason: Hummingbird escape maneuvers were filmed with high-speed cameras inside a laboratory flight chamber. The study then reconstructs 3D kinematics for CFD analysis. No wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: How honeybees respond to heat stress from the individual to colony level
venue: Journal of The Royal Society Interface
reason: Behavioural study of a managed western honeybee colony housed in an indoor observation hive, tracked with barcode tags (BeesBook); beekeeping / managed domestic animals, not wild free-ranging wildlife.

title: Recognizability bias in citizen science photographs
reason: Primary study training CNN image recognition models on citizen science photographs of wild species (birds, insects, plus plants and fungi) to analyse recognizability bias.

title: Female–female aggression in the Gila monster ( Heloderma suspectum )
reason: Behavioural ethogram and bite-force study of captive Gila monsters; the only image use is manual angle measurement on video frames in ImageJ, with no computer vision method. The animals are also captive only.

title: Stay close, but not too close: aerial image analysis reveals patterns of social distancing in seal colonies
reason: Ecological study of spacing in wild seal colonies from aerial images. All seals were labelled manually and analysed with spatial statistics; no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated (automated detection is only suggested as future work).

title: Group-level differences in social network structure remain repeatable after accounting for environmental drivers
reason: Automated camera-based barcode tracking of captive zebra finch colonies housed in outdoor aviaries; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Assessment of a non-invasive approach to pregnancy diagnosis in gray whales through drone-based photogrammetry and faecal hormone analysis
reason: Drone-based photogrammetry (image measurement) of free-ranging Pacific Coast Feeding Group gray whales used to classify pregnancy status; field study of wild animals.

title: Early-life sleep disruption impairs subtle social behaviours in prairie voles: a pose-estimation study
reason: Pose estimation applied to colony-bred prairie voles in divided home cages in a laboratory neuroscience experiment; no wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Strategic predatory pursuit of the stealthy, highly manoeuvrable, slow flying bat Corynorhinus townsendii
venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences
