reason: The main animal data is museum and literature images of beetle specimens, used for retrieval from natural history collections. The bird and butterfly web datasets serve only as extra test sets and are never described as wild animals.

title: Sherlock—A flexible, low‐resource tool for processing camera‐trapping images
reason: Presents a computer vision algorithm (background comparison) to filter camera trap images of wild European badgers on farms in Cornwall; images also contain livestock.

title: Drones are an effective tool to assess the impact of feral horses in an alpine riparian environment
reason: Drone RGB orthomosaics of feral horse signs (tracks, dung, pugging) were classified by hand in ArcMap and then analysed with statistics. No computer vision method was developed or applied.

title: Tadpole fingerprinting: Using tail venation patterns to photo‐identify tadpole individuals of a threatened frog
reason: Individual tadpoles are identified by people matching photographs by eye, with no computer vision method. The tadpoles were also captive-bred and kept in tanks.

title: Computer vision system using deep learning to predict rib and loin yield in the fish Colossoma macropomum
reason: Computer vision phenotyping of farmed tambaqui (and pacu) in an aquaculture breeding programme; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: An AI‐based platform to investigate African large carnivore dispersal and demography across broad landscapes: A case study and future directions using African wild dogs
reason: Applies an AI-based detection and individual identification platform (African Carnivore Wildbook) to photographs of a free-ranging African wild dog population.

title: Vegetation cover and biodiversity reduce parasite infection in wild hosts across ecological levels and scales
reason: Ecological/epidemiological study of T. cruzi infection in captured wild small mammals using tabular machine learning (gradient boosting) and structural equation models on trait, biodiversity and land-cover variables; no analysis of animal images or video.

title: Getting the bugs out of AI : Advancing ecological research on arthropods through computer vision
reason: Synthesis/review and perspective article on deep learning for computer vision in entomology; it summarises other studies and gives guidelines, with no primary image analysis of its own.

title: Nature 4.0: A networked sensor system for integrated biodiversity monitoring
reason: Presents a networked biodiversity monitoring system that includes a camera trap pipeline (MegaDetector + EfficientNetV2 species classifier) applied to wild animals in the Marburg Open Forest.

title: Three major mesoplanktonic communities resolved by in situ imaging in the upper 500 m of the global ocean
reason: In situ UVP5 images of wild plankton were sorted in EcoTaxa, and every object was manually validated or corrected. The study is an ecological analysis (PCA, clustering and RDA) of concentration data; it does not develop, apply or evaluate a computer vision method on the images.

title: Scanning sympatric sika deer and Japanese serows using drones: A methodological trial in Mt. Asama, Central Japan
reason: UAV thermal and RGB survey of wild sika deer and Japanese serows in which detection, species identification and counting were done manually by a pilot and two researchers; no computer vision method is applied.

title: Towards reliable estimates of abundance trends using automated non‐lethal moth traps
reason: Wild moths were photographed by automated traps, but they were counted by hand from the photos. No computer vision method was applied; AI analysis was explicitly left out of scope.

title: Increasing Trust in New Data Sources: Crowdsourcing Image Classification for Ecology
reason: Coral reef images are classified by human crowd workers on Amazon Mechanical Turk. The paper's method is a Bayesian item response model that aggregates these human labels. No computer vision or automated image analysis is applied.

title: Geometric morphometric analysis of Pleuronectiformes vertebrae: A new tool to identify archaeological fish remains?
reason: Landmark-based geometric morphometrics on photographs of fish vertebrae from museum/reference bone collections and archaeological remains; no images of wild, free-ranging animals.

title: Hidden in plain sight: unveiling the distributions of green‐winged grasshoppers (Aiolopus spp.) with citizen‐science data
reason: Wild grasshoppers in citizen-science photos, but the traits were measured by hand in ImageJ and then classified with discriminant analysis on the ratio values. No computer vision or automated image analysis method is developed or applied.

title: Growth and opportunities for drone surveillance in pinniped research
reason: Perspective article discussing opportunities of drone methods in pinniped research; it only illustrates them with example drone orthomosaics and develops or evaluates no computer vision method.

title: A three‐dimensional, dynamic blue whale model for research and scientific communication
reason: Builds a 3D reconstruction of wild blue whales from aerial, underwater, tag-camera and web images, using Blender motion tracking that automatically detects and tracks visual features in video.

title: Aerial photogrammetry techniques using drones to estimate morphometric measurements and body condition in South American small cetaceans
reason: Drone video frames of free-ranging dolphins analysed by image-based photogrammetry to estimate morphometrics and body condition.

title: Color pattern complexity in dwarf minke whales (Balaenoptera acutorostrata) of the northern Great Barrier Reef of Australia
reason: Wild dwarf minke whales are photographed, but colour pattern character states are assigned visually by a human assessor and analysed statistically (clustering, MCA); no computer vision method is applied to images.

title: Satellite image survey of beluga whales in the southern Kara Sea
reason: Belugas in satellite imagery were counted manually by a human expert in ArcGIS; no computer vision or automated image analysis method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Cost of migration and migratory timing in Western Australian humpback whales
reason: Primary study applying UAV aerial photogrammetry (image-based morphometric measurement) to wild migrating humpback whales to estimate body condition.

title: How otariids walk: a comparative axial analysis of the hind limb movements of California and South American sea lions
reason: All filmed animals are kept in an aquarium, a sea-world park or zoos (one sea lion was caught in the wild but is now captive). Joint positions were also marked by hand rather than by any automated computer vision method.

title: Using audio and UAS ‐based video for estimating tidal lung volumes of resting and active adult gray whales (Eschrichtius robustus)
reason: Wild gray whales are filmed from UAS, but the videos are only timed by hand (frames played at reduced speed) to estimate breathing durations. No computer vision method is developed or applied. The comparison data are audio spectrograms.

title: Computer vision‐assisted photogrammetry and one‐image 3D modeling in marine mammals
reason: The computer vision method is developed and tested only on images of bycaught porpoise carcasses photographed on a gridded plank at a research institute; no images of live, free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Species classification of Antarctic pack‐ice seals using very high‐resolution imagery
reason: Primary study classifying wild Antarctic pack-ice seals to species from satellite and aerial imagery, using CNN-detected/manual seal locations, CNN sea-ice segmentation and a Random Forest on image-derived spatial features.

title: African bovid tribe classification using transfer learning and computer vision
venue: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
reason: The images show the occlusal surfaces of bovid teeth from a reference specimen database (dental specimens), not wild, free-ranging animals. The aim is to identify fossil tribes for paleoecology.

title: Image‐based taxonomic classification of bulk insect biodiversity samples using deep learning and domain adaptation
reason: Images are of collected, ethanol-preserved beetle specimens extracted from bulk samples and photographed under stereo microscopes in the laboratory; no images of live free-ranging animals.

title: Multisensor data fusion for automatized insect monitoring (KInsecta)
reason: Primary study presenting a multisensor live insect monitoring system with camera-image classification of insects passing through a trap-connected arena alive; tested in laboratory and field.

title: Gaze following in Archosauria—Alligators and palaeognath birds suggest dinosaur origin of visual perspective taking
reason: Behavioural cognition study of gaze following in captive archosaurs. The videos were coded manually in Solomon Coder and no computer vision method was applied.

title: SMART-BARN: Scalable multimodal arena for real-time tracking behavior of animals in large numbers
reason: Indoor tracking arena (SMART-BARN) built from motion capture and video. All animals are held in the enclosure: wild-caught starlings kept in aviaries, loft-bred homing pigeons, lab-reared moths and bats. No free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: CATER: Combined Animal Tracking & Environment Reconstruction
reason: Develops a computer vision tracking and environment reconstruction framework and applies it to field video of freely foraging wild desert ants in their natural habitat.

title: Abyssal hydrothermal springs—Cryptic incubators for brooding octopus
reason: Ecological study of wild deep-sea octopus. Octopus were counted and classified by hand in a photomosaic. Image processing was limited to mosaicking and to locating the manual marker codes, so no computer vision was applied to the animals themselves.

title: Automatic classification of the phenotype textures of three Thunnus species based on the machine learning SVM algorithm
venue: Canadian Journal of Fisheries and Aquatic Sciences
reason: Computer vision classification (GLCM/VGG16 features + SVM) of images of wild-caught tuna photographed by marine observers during a Pacific fishery survey; primary research on non-domestic wild fish.

title: Automated Fish Detection and Tracking System Using Pre-Trained Mask R-CNN for Ecological Biodiversity
venue: International Journal of Uncertainty Fuzziness and Knowledge-Based Systems
reason: Fish detection and tracking with Mask R-CNN on videos of fish held in aquariums, a pool and a glass container; no wild, free-ranging animals in the analysed data.

title: Discovering Novel Biological Traits From Images Using Phylogeny-Guided Neural Networks
venue: ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (KDD)
reason: Generative trait-discovery method applied only to fish specimen images from ichthyological research collections (museum specimens); no images of wild free-ranging animals.

title: Category-Specific Prompts for Animal Action Recognition with Pretrained Vision-Language Models
venue: Mm 2023 Proceedings of the 31st ACM International Conference on Multimedia
reason: Proposes a CLIP-based method for video action recognition of animals, evaluated on the Animal Kingdom dataset, which the paper describes as covering many animals in natural environments (grasslands, forests, rivers, oceans).

title: Data-Scarce Animal Face Alignment via Bi-Directional Cross-Species Knowledge Transfer
venue: ACM International Conference on Multimedia (ACM MM)
reason: Proposes a CV method for animal facial landmark alignment evaluated on AnimalWeb (350 species incl. wild taxa), a horse dataset and Japanese macaques; mixes wild and domestic animals.

title: Poster: Towards Battery-Free Machine Learning Inference and Model Personalization on MCUs
venue: International Conference on Mobile Systems, Applications, and Services
reason: Primary study applying a lightweight neural network to fish image recognition on a field-recorded underwater marine dataset (DeepFish), deployed on microcontrollers.

title: Edge-based Privacy-Sensitive Live Learning for Discovery of Training Data
reason: Generic edge-computing system for interactive labeling and training-set discovery; animals (deer, Common Yellowthroat, antelope) appear only as example target classes alongside Taj Mahal, fire hydrant and a military drone in general image datasets. Wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Progress toward automated migratory waterfowl census using drones and deep learning
reason: Work-in-progress primary study applying CNN detection and classification to UAS imagery of wild overwintering migratory waterfowl at wildlife refuges.

title: Comparison of Convolutional Neural Network Architectures for Sea Turtle Individual's Recognition
venue: International Conference on Frontiers of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning (FAIML)
reason: Applies CNNs to images of wild sea turtles' facial scutes, sampled at Redang Island, to recognise individual turtles.

title: Efficient-YOLOv8: Multi-Scale ConvNet for Underwater Object Detection
venue: International Conference on Sustainable Information Engineering and Technology (SIET)
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv8 detector, tested on underwater video frames of wild cuttlefish that the authors recorded in the field in South Australia.

title: Bayesian method for bee counting with noise-labeled data
venue: International Symposium on Information and Communication Technology
reason: Counts managed honey bees at beehive entrances in a beekeeping research center; beekeeping is excluded as agriculture.

title: Digital Eye on Endangered Wildlife: Crafting Recognition Datasets through Semi-Automated Annotation
venue: International Conference on Advances in Image Processing (ICAIP)
reason: Primary study that builds a bounding-box and keypoint dataset of six African wild animal classes using a YOLOv5-based semi-automatic annotation framework; images are web-scraped and the paper does not state whether the animals are wild or captive.

title: CMAF: Cross-Modal Augmentation via Fusion for Underwater Acoustic Image Recognition
venue: ACM Transactions on Multimedia Computing Communications and Applications
reason: Proposes a computer vision framework classifying fish species in acoustic camera (imaging sonar) images from the DIDSON fishery dataset, which was collected in a real-world environment.

title: A Drawing-type Observation and Retrieval Method Focusing on the Abdominal Pattern of Penguins
reason: HCI study analysing the coordinates of human drawings of penguin abdominal patterns, not photos or video of the animals. The penguins are captive aquarium animals.

title: Underwater Fish Target Detection Based on YOLOv5 Fusion CBAM
venue: International Conference on Machine Learning and Computer Application (ICMLCA)
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv5s detector for marine fish in underwater images from the public Deep Fish dataset. The paper does not state that the fish are captive or farmed.

title: Drone-Based Thermal Imaging in the Detection of Wildlife Carcasses and Disease Management
reason: Field study of drone thermal imaging to find deployed wild boar carcasses. Detection relies on the camera's built-in hottest-point function watched by an operator, and the analysis is statistical (GLMMs, conditional inference trees) on detection outcomes; no computer vision method is developed or evaluated on the images.

title: Not Just Pictures: Utility of Camera Trapping in the Context of African Swine Fever and Wild Boar Management
reason: Camera-trap ecology study of wild boar, roe deer and wolf. Images were processed manually (manual pixel digitising for photogrammetry, manual counts); no automated computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Comparative study of ensemble deep learning models to determine the classification of turtle species
reason: CNN ensemble classification of sea turtle species from images of turtles photographed on the coast and at sea, partly collected at a turtle conservation site in Indonesia.

title: Robust features extraction from shape signature for fish images classification
venue: Indonesian Journal of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science
reason: Proposes a shape-signature feature extraction and classification method for fish species images taken from a live-video fish dataset. The images show non-domestic fish species. The paper does not state whether the fish were wild or captive.

title: Dual-Band Infrared Scheimpflug Lidar Reveals Insect Activity in a Tropical Cloud Forest
reason: Field deployment of a dual-band Scheimpflug lidar with a linear CMOS camera sensor to observe free-flying wild insects and bats in an Ecuadorian cloud forest. Insects are detected in time-range maps and their wingbeat signals are analysed. This is primary research on image-sensor data of wild animals.

title: Real-time marine target recognition method of underwater inspection robot based on computer vision
venue: International Journal of Advanced Robotic Systems
reason: Computer vision detection of benthic marine organisms (sea urchin, starfish, scallop, sea cucumber) in images taken by an underwater robot in offshore marine ranches. These are free-ranging animals on the seabed, though some may be ranched.

title: Non-invasive measurements of respiration and heart rate across wildlife species using Eulerian Video Magnification of infrared thermal imagery
reason: All infrared and RGB video was recorded of animals held at four zoological institutions (immobilized or trained); no wild or free-ranging animals were imaged.

title: An automated, low-latency environment for studying the neural basis of behavior in freely moving rats
reason: Laboratory rats tracked and pose-estimated in an indoor experimental arena for neuroscience; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: A pilot study to estimate the population size of endangered Galápagos marine iguanas using drones
reason: Drone survey of wild marine iguanas in which animals were counted manually by experts on orthophotographs; no automated image analysis of animals is applied (AI is only named as future work).

title: Deep learning based deep-sea automatic image enhancement and animal species classification
reason: Primary study proposing a deep-learning image enhancement and species classification pipeline on deep-sea crawler images of wild benthic fauna at Barkley Canyon.

title: Camera traps link population-level activity patterns with wildfire smoke events for mammals in Eastern Washington State
reason: Ecological study that applies MegaDetector to camera-trap images of wild mammals before manual species labelling; the computer vision step is minor but is applied to wild, free-ranging animals.

title: Arthropod Taxonomy Orders Object Detection in ArTaxOr dataset using YOLOX
venue: Journal of Engineering and Applied Science
reason: Primary study applying a YOLOX object detector to images of arthropods at order level; the paper describes the images as having natural complexity and complex backgrounds, but does not state how or where the images were taken.

title: From quadrupedal to bipedal walking ‘on the fly’: the mechanics of dynamical mode transition in primates
reason: Biomechanics study of captive olive baboons at a primatology station; 25 body points were digitized by hand, frame by frame, from video. There is no computer vision method, and the animals are captive.

title: Drink safely: common swifts (Apus apus) dissipate mechanical energy to decrease flight speed before touch-and-go drinking
reason: Video-based 3D optical tracking (rotational stereo-videography) of free-flying wild common swifts drinking at waterbodies in France.

title: Nectophore coordination and kinematics by physonect siphonophores
reason: Nectophore kinematics were quantified by manually observing videos frame by frame, so no computer vision was applied to the animals. The only automated image analysis is particle image velocimetry (PIV) of fluid flow in one laboratory sequence.

title: Butterfly Species Detection Based on YOLOv5s
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv5s detector for species detection of butterflies in natural-environment images.

title: The use of an unmanned aerial vehicle to investigate habitat use and behavior of invasive blue crab in Mediterranean microhabitats
reason: UAV photographs of buoy-tagged wild blue crabs were georeferenced and trajectories traced manually in QGIS; no computer vision or automated image analysis method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Validation of the Effectiveness of Detic as a Zero-shot Fish Catch Recognition System
venue: IIAE International Conference on Industrial Application Engineering (ICIAE)
reason: Images show dead fish bought at a supermarket and photographed in a laboratory set-up that simulates a conveyor belt. No wild, free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Marine Life Detection Algorithm Based on Deep Convolutional Generative Adversarial Network and ResNeXt50 with FPN Faster R-CNN Network
venue: IIAE International Conference on Industrial Application Engineering (ICIAE)
reason: Proposes a detection method (DCGAN augmentation + ResNeXt50-FPN Faster R-CNN) for marine life (sea cucumber, sea urchin, starfish) in underwater images collected from Kaggle and the internet; marine wildlife is the stated subject, although the paper does not state whether the animals are wild or captive.

title: Few-Shot Learning for CNN-based Animal Classification in Camera Traps using an Infrared Camera
venue: International Conference on Intelligent Systems and Image Processing (ICISIP)
reason: Evaluates CNN few-shot learning (transfer learning, data augmentation) for animal classification on infrared camera-trap images from Caltech Camera Traps; categories are wild animals plus cat and dog.

title: A Deep Transfer Learning Framework for the Multi-Class Classification of Vector Mosquito Species
reason: Images are of mosquito specimens from a laboratory colony; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: IMPLEMENTATION OF ANIMAL FACE’S RECOGNITION BY CONVOLUTIONAL NEURAL NETWORK (CNN) ALGORITHM
reason: Applies a CNN to classify animal face images into cat, dog and wild-animal classes. The wild class shows non-domestic animals, mixed with domestic cats and dogs.

title: Camera Vision Based Animal Beat Back System for Agriculture using Machine Learning
reason: Applies CNN-based animal detection/classification from camera images to repel crop-raiding wild animals (elephants, wild pig, deer); the data mixes wild species with domestic ones (goat, cow, horse, cat, hamster).

title: Spatial distribution of benthic habitats in Kapota Atoll (Wakatobi National Park, Indonesia) using remote sensing imagery
reason: Pixel-based classification of Sentinel-2A satellite imagery into benthic habitat / substrate cover classes (sand, coral, rubble, seagrass); habitat mapping only, no animals as individual subjects.

title: Using pose estimation to identify regions and points on natural history specimens
reason: Pose estimation applied only to images of museum bird specimens and Littorina shells imaged under a microscope; no images of live free-ranging animals.

title: A network-based analysis detects cocaine-induced changes in social interactions in Drosophila melanogaster
reason: Laboratory-bred Drosophila melanogaster recorded in an indoor arena to study cocaine-induced changes in social interaction networks; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: BatCount: A software program to count moving animals
reason: Presents and evaluates software that counts wild bats emerging from maternity cave roosts in thermal video, using background subtraction and tracking.

title: Effectiveness of an artificial intelligence-based system to curtail wind turbines to reduce eagle collisions
reason: Evaluates an AI-based camera system that detects, identifies and tracks free-flying wild eagles and other birds at a wind farm.

title: Detection and measurement of butterfly eyespot and spot patterns using convolutional neural networks
reason: The paper uses CNNs to detect and measure spots and eyespots on digital images of butterfly wings, mostly with one wing shown or digitally erased. It is a developmental and evolutionary biology tool working on wing specimens. None of the data shows wild, free-ranging animals photographed in the field.

title: A data science approach for multi-sensor marine observatory data monitoring cold water corals (Paragorgia arborea) in two campaigns
reason: Paper describes the PyTorch deep learning library and benchmarks its training throughput; no animal imagery or wildlife application is analysed.

title: Identification of Crown of Thorns Starfish (COTS) using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) and attention model
reason: CNN with attention module to classify and detect Crown of Thorns Starfish in underwater images, including photos taken by the authors in the Mauritian lagoon.

title: Do you get what you see? Insights of using mAP to select architectures of pretrained neural networks for automated aerial animal detection
reason: Aerial detection of red deer kept in enclosures on a private deer farm; no wild or free-ranging animals in the analysed data.

title: Innate attraction and aversion to odors in locusts
reason: Laboratory-reared locust hatchlings tracked in an indoor behaviour arena for an olfactory preference study; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Multi-classification deep neural networks for identification of fish species using camera captured images
reason: The only data analysed are photographs of dead seafood specimens bought at a grocery-store fish counter; no images of wild, free-ranging animals are used. E-CAPTIVE (specimens) fits best; E-AGRI is a possible alternative given the aquaculture framing.

title: Using ecotourism boats for estimating the abundance of a bottlenose dolphin population in south-eastern Australia
reason: Applies computer-vision photo-identification (Flukebook with CurvRank v2 and finFindR) to images of wild bottlenose dolphins to identify individuals for abundance estimation.

title: MBT3D: Deep learning based multi-object tracker for bumblebee 3D flight path estimation
reason: Multi-object tracker for bumblebees filmed in a plexiglass tunnel under controlled laboratory conditions; no images of wild, free-ranging animals in a natural environment.

title: Accurate detection and identification of insects from camera trap images with deep learning
reason: Primary study presenting an annotated image dataset and YOLO models for detecting and classifying free-ranging flower-visiting insects recorded in situ by time-lapse cameras on a green roof.

title: Internet of Wild Things with the Integration of Vision Technology and LoRa Network
venue: International Journal of Electrical and Electronics Engineering
reason: Proposes and deploys a camera-based vision node that detects wild animal movement on a forest road in an animal corridor and sends alerts via LoRa.

title: Advanced Detections of Norway Lobster (Nephrops Norvegicus) Burrows using Deep Learning Techniques
venue: International Journal of Advanced Computer Science and Applications
reason: Applies deep learning object detection to underwater survey video to detect burrows (direct signs) of wild Norway lobster.

title: Bird Image Classification using Convolutional Neural Network Transfer Learning Architectures
venue: International Journal of Advanced Computer Science and Applications
reason: Primary study comparing CNN transfer-learning models for bird species classification from images, framed for conservation; the paper does not state whether the birds in the Kaggle dataset are wild or captive.

title: Bird Detection and Species Classification: Using YOLOv5 and Deep Transfer Learning Models
venue: International Journal of Advanced Computer Science and Applications
reason: Primary study applying YOLOv5 detection and CNN transfer learning to images of 525 bird species, with bird monitoring and conservation as the stated application. The paper does not describe how the images were taken; the wild status rests on the non-domestic bird species and one eBird example image.

title: VOCALExplore: Pay-as-You-Go Video Data Exploration and Model Building
reason: Proposes a video exploration and model-building system and evaluates it on collar-camera video of wild deer (activity classification) and camera-trap video of bears, alongside generic human-action and driving benchmarks.

title: PyMouseTracks: Flexible Computer Vision and RFID-Based System for Multiple Mouse Tracking and Behavioral Assessment
reason: Computer vision and RFID tracking system for laboratory mice in home cages and behavioural arenas; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Structures of coexisting marine snow and zooplankton in coastal waters of Svalbard (European Arctic)
reason: Applies in situ underwater imaging (UVP) with automated deep-learning classification (EcoTaxa) and manual validation to quantify wild zooplankton and marine snow in Svalbard waters.

title: Non-invasive monitoring of endangered Ladoga ringed seal (Pusa hispida ladogensis) (Carnivora: Phocidae) using photo-identification
reason: Photo-identification of wild Ladoga ringed seals was done entirely by manual visual comparison of photographs; no computer vision method was developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Artificial intelligence in wildlife conservation
venue: International Journal of Avian & Wildlife Biology
reason: Editorial perspective on AI in wildlife conservation; no primary research or image analysis.

title: Covariation in Shapes Between the Sternum and Pelvis in Aquatic Birds with Different Locomotor Modes
reason: Geometric morphometric study of museum skeletal specimens using manually digitised landmarks on photographs; there is no computer vision method and no images of live wild animals.

title: Migratory destinations of endangered humpback whales, Megaptera novaeangliae (Cetartiodactyla: Balaenopteridae), from El Salvador
reason: Applies automated image recognition (Happywhale) to match fluke photo-identification images of wild humpback whales for individual re-identification and migration analysis.

title: Bugs in the Data: How ImageNet Misrepresents Biodiversity
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
reason: The paper audits the wildlife classes and validation images of ImageNet-1k using human expert annotation. No computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Wildlife Detection and Intrusion Alert System
reason: Primary study that builds a computer vision pipeline (segmentation plus CNN classification) to detect wild animal intrusion from surveillance video. Wild animals are the stated subject, but the paper does not describe where its images come from.

title: Evaluating the use of a quad-copter drone to detect Siamese Crocodile nests in Lao PDR, with incidental observations of female nest attendance
reason: Drone imagery of wild Siamese crocodile nests was inspected visually by observers; no computer vision or automated image analysis was applied.

title: Application of neural networks for the classification of objects in video data in the tasks of automatic monitoring of the condition of biological objects
reason: The study builds a video-monitoring system for the health and behaviour of dairy cattle (livestock) on dairy farms. No wild animals are analysed.

title: Optimizing Region Detection in Enhanced Infrared Images Using Deep Learning
reason: Fine-tunes an R-CNN to detect animal regions in infrared images from Wildlife Conservation Society field surveys and monitoring programs.

title: A Comparison of Adaptive Moment Estimation (Adam) and RMSProp Optimisation Techniques for Wildlife Animal Classification Using Convolutional Neural Networks
reason: Compares Adam and RMSProp optimisers for CNN classification of wild animals in Snapshot Serengeti camera-trap images.

title: NAM-YOLOV7: An Improved YOLOv7 Based on Attention Model for Animal Death Detection
reason: Applies object detection (improved YOLOv7) to web and drone images to detect dead animals (roadkill) on roads, highways and forests. The paper does not say whether the animals are wild or domestic. Roadkill of free-ranging animals is a wildlife-relevant application, so the paper is included.

title: Hybrid Deep Learning Approach for Enhanced Animal Breed Classification and Prediction
reason: Proposes a CNN-based classifier for animal images from the Animals-10 web dataset, which contains wild animals (elephant, squirrel, butterfly, spider) together with domestic ones (cat, dog, cow). The stated motivation is animal monitoring in forest ecosystems.

title: Near real-time animal action recognition and classification
reason: Action recognition from keypoints trained and tested on the Animal Pose dataset of domestic animals (cats, cows, dogs, horses, sheep); the analysed data contains no wild animals.

title: Detecting Eating Behavior of Elephants in a Zoo Using Temporal Action Localization
reason: The method detects the eating behaviour of Asian elephants filmed by surveillance cameras in an indoor zoo enclosure. No wild animals appear in the data.

title: Prompting Scientific Names for Zero-Shot Species Recognition
venue: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP)
reason: Proposes a prompting method for zero-shot species recognition with CLIP, evaluated on species datasets (semi-iNat, semi-Aves, CUB200) of organisms including wild birds and mammals; species recognition for ecological/biodiversity research is the stated application.

title: A deep learning algorithm and software for photo identification of the Indo-Pacific humpback dolphin (Sousa chinensis)
reason: Primary study proposing a deep learning re-identification method on photographs of wild Indo-Pacific humpback dolphins from Xiamen Bay.

title: Using Drone Imagery to Map Intertidal Oyster Reefs along Florida’s Gulf of Mexico Coast
reason: Applies image segmentation to drone multispectral imagery to delineate wild intertidal eastern oyster reefs for monitoring.

title: AddaxAI: A no-code platform to train and deploy custom YOLOv5 object detection models
venue: The Journal of Open Source Software
reason: Software paper describing a GUI for annotating, training and deploying object detection models; aimed at camera-trap ecologists but analyses no animal image data and reports no experiments.

title: Design and implementation of the intelligent system for automatically monitoring waterbirds in Quanzhou Bar Wetland
reason: Applies YOLOv5 to detect, identify and count wild native waterbirds from surveillance cameras in the Quanzhou Bay Estuary Wetland.

title: Real-time Jellyfish Classification and Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv4-Tiny and Improved Underwater Image Enhancement Algorithm
reason: Jellyfish detection with an improved YOLOv4-tiny. Images come from a web crawler, a public dataset and the authors' laboratory; the paper never states that any of the images show wild, free-ranging animals, and the only described acquisition is in the laboratory.

title: Population data of the Heron Colonies in the Reedbed of Lake Kolon from a Non- Disturbance high altitude Aerial Photogrammetry based Survey
reason: Aerial photogrammetric survey of wild heron colonies; birds and nests are counted and identified by manual visual interpretation of orthophotos in GIS software, with no automated computer vision analysis of the animals.

title: A Robust Fish Species Classification Framework: FRCNN-VGG16-SPPNet
reason: Primary study proposing a CNN framework to classify five non-domestic marine fish species for marine conservation. Images come from internet databases; the paper does not state whether the fish were photographed alive in the wild, caught or as specimens.

title: Analysis of the daily activities of dromedary camel (Camelus dromedaries) kept under farm conditions using deep learning technology
reason: Study analyses videos of domestic dromedary camels kept in a farm pen; no wild or free-ranging animals in the data.

title: An Automated Rat Grimace Scale for the Assessment of Pain
reason: Automated rat grimace scale on images of laboratory Sprague Dawley and Wistar rats in a pain/blast traumatic brain injury study; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Bimodal distribution of inter-individual distance in free-ranging narrow-ridged finless porpoises—Potential use of visual and auditory cues
reason: Drone video of free-ranging finless porpoises analysed with calibrated image measurement (photogrammetry) to measure inter-individual distances; the image analysis is mostly measurement rather than automated recognition, so inclusion is borderline.

title: 3D tracking reveals energy-distance trade-offs in two dominant grazers on a degraded coral reef
reason: Applies YOLOv5 detection, CNN species classification and DeepSORT 3D tracking to remote underwater stereo-video of free-ranging coral reef fishes in the Red Sea.

title: Energy-use strategies on a degraded coral reef: insights from remote underwater stereo-video and AI-driven 3D tracking
reason: Applies CNN detection, species classification and 3D multi-object tracking to stereo-video of free-ranging coral reef fishes in the Red Sea to derive energy expenditure.

title: Genetic control of changes in locomotor activity caused by social experience in Drosophila males
reason: Laboratory study of locomotor activity in Drosophila melanogaster stocks tracked by webcam in experimental chambers; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Multimodal system for recording individual-level behaviors in songbird groups
reason: The paper describes a multimodal recording system (radio, audio, video) for colony-bred zebra finches in a laboratory sound-isolation chamber. Video is recorded and encoded, but no computer vision analysis is performed; the analysis is manual segmentation of vocalizations from spectrograms. The animals are also laboratory animals, so E-LAB would equally apply.

title: Using Citizen Science to Infer Characteristics and Habitat Use of Reef Manta Rays (Mobula Alfredi) in New Caledonia
reason: Wild reef manta rays are photo-identified, but the matching is done by eye. The images are not analysed with any computer vision method; the analyses are statistical (accumulation curves, residency models).

title: Advancing Ecological Research with MobileNet-SSD V2 CNN: A Leap in Machine Learning
reason: Applies a MobileNet-SSD V2 CNN to detect wild lions, tigers and elephants in images from Kaggle and from live footage recorded in Ramnagar forest, aimed at reducing human-wildlife conflict.

title: Advances in Ecological Surveillance: Real-Time Wildlife Detection using MobileNet-SSD V2 CNN
reason: Applies a CNN detector (MobileNet-SSD V2) to images of wild elephants, tigers and lions. The data include live footage from Ramnagar forest.

title: Animal Detection for Vehicle
venue: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
reason: The only target animal is the cow, a domestic livestock animal filmed on roads for avoiding vehicle collisions. No wild animals are analysed.

title: Endangered Bird Species Classification Using Machine Learning Techniques
venue: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
reason: Applies CNN/SVM image classification to images of endangered bird species, which are wild taxa, for conservation. The paper does not say where the images come from.

title: Wild Animal Detection Using CNN
venue: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
reason: CNN-based classification of camera-trap images of wild animals (Wildlife Spotter, Australia); primary study.

title: Deep Blue Discoveries: Advancements in Fish Detection and Species Taxonomy Using Deep Learning in the Subaquatic Realm
venue: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
reason: Primary study applying deep learning (R-CNN, ResNet, YOLO V7) to detect and classify fish in underwater images from different underwater locations. The paper does not explicitly say whether the fish are wild or captive; included because the images are described as coming from underwater environments.

title: Camera Vision Based Animal Repellent System for Agriculture using Machine Learning
venue: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
reason: Primary study applying a CNN to camera images to recognise crop-raiding wild animals (elephants, wild boar, deer) for a repellent system; the composition of the image database is not described.

title: Advances in Ecological Surveillance: Real-Time Wildlife Detection using MobileNet-SSD V2 Convolutional Neural Network
venue: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
reason: Builds and deploys a MobileNet-SSD V2 detector for lions, tigers and elephants. It is trained on Kaggle images and live footage from Ramanagar forest, and the deployed system is tested for elephant intrusion.

title: Optimising the automated recognition of individual animals to support population monitoring
reason: Develops a CNN-based pre-processing framework and compares image-matching software for individual identification of free-ranging African wild dogs photographed in long-term monitoring programmes in Kenya and Zimbabwe.

title: Animating the Dead: Creating Site Specific Synthetic Datasets to Train Machine Learning Models for Ecology and Conservation
reason: Trains image classifiers on synthetic images built from museum specimen photographs and tests them on real-world opportunistic images of the target salamander and lizard taxa, aimed at camera-trap wildlife monitoring.

title: Behavioral analysis of a captive male Bornean orangutan (Pongo pygmaeus) when exposed to environmental changes
reason: Behaviour of one zoo orangutan was coded manually from camera recordings using an ethogram and statistics. The paper uses no computer vision method, and the animal is captive only.

title: Pupil Dynamics-derived Sleep Stage Classification of a Head-fixed Mouse Using a Recurrent Neural Network
reason: Sleep-stage classification from pupil video of head-fixed laboratory mice in a darkroom set-up; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Challenges and constraints when applying few shot learning to a real-world scenario: In-the-wild camera-trap species classification
reason: Evaluates few-shot learning networks for species classification on camera-trap images of wild animals in Senegal.

title: Utilization of UAV-Borne RGB Data for Monitoring Horses: Comparison of Classification Methods
venue: Iberian Conference on Information Systems and Technologies (CISTI)
reason: Compares pixel- and object-based classifiers on UAV RGB imagery to identify free-ranging wild horses released in a nature reserve.

title: Ensemble Fusion for Small Object Detection
reason: Ensemble detection method for small flying birds (SOD4SB challenge). The birds are the detection target, and the paper names wildlife monitoring as an application. The paper does not say outright that the birds are wild; free-flying birds are assumed here.

title: MVA2023 Small Object Detection Challenge for Spotting Birds: Dataset, Methods, and Results
reason: Introduces a drone-captured dataset of wild birds for small object detection and reports challenge methods evaluated on it.

title: Small Object Detection for Birds with Swin Transformer
reason: Primary method paper on detecting birds as small objects in images; birds are the stated subject. The paper does not say whether they are wild or captive, but birds in sky scenes from drone and challenge datasets are the target, so it is not a generic benchmark paper.

title: A Zero Shot Detection Based Approach for Fish Species Recognition in Underwater Environments
reason: Zero-shot object detection of reef fish species in underwater survey images from the Gulf of Mexico; wild fish are the subject.

title: Portable Stereo Chute Box Imaging System Design and Development for Fisheries
reason: System design paper for a stereo imaging chute box on a research vessel conveyor belt. It collects colour and depth images of trawl-caught fish but applies no image-analysis method; the data have not yet been used for AI/ML.

title: ROVIA: Automated Underwater Video Highlight Generation using Deep Neural Network
reason: A 3D-CNN finds highlight clips in deep-sea ROV video of wild marine organisms. Highlights include organism movement and fish, alongside geological and operational events.

title: Development and Characterization of an Underwater Motion-Triggered Camera Trap
reason: Develops a motion-triggered underwater camera trap that uses image differencing. It is evaluated on DeepFish videos of wild fish in mangrove and coral reef scenes and also in a museum aquarium with cichlids.

title: Aquaeye.ai: Towards Development, Deployment and Distribution of Novel Artificial Intelligence for Aquariums
reason: Fish detection and classification for public aquarium exhibits (California Academy of Sciences Reef Lagoon and Philippine Coral Reef). The images come from the exhibit livestream, supplemented with web-scraped and synthetic images. The paper never says that any analysed images show wild animals.

title: Whale Detection Enhancement Through Synthetic Satellite Images
reason: Develops a synthetic image simulator and trains segmentation networks to detect whales in real satellite images of free-ranging whales.

title: Probabilistic Model-Based Active Learning with Attention Mechanism for Fish Species Recognition
reason: Deep active learning object detector applied to underwater video frames of reef fish in their natural habitat (fisheries-independent survey data).

title: Optimizing and Gauging Model Performance with Metrics to Integrate with Existing Video Surveys
reason: Evaluates automated deep-learning fish detection/classification counts against manual counts on baited underwater survey video of wild reef fish (Red Snapper) in the Gulf of Mexico.

title: Plankton Classification with Deep Learning
venue: Signal Processing: Algorithms, Architectures, Arrangements, and Applications
reason: Deep learning classification of in situ underwater images of wild marine plankton (copepods, larval fish, protists) from the Kaggle National Data Science Bowl dataset.

title: Automatic Individual Identification of Patterned Solitary Species Based on Unlabeled Video Data
reason: Develops and evaluates a computer vision pipeline for individual identification of wild leopards from camera trap videos.

title: Deep learning-based activity recognition and fine motor identification using 2D skeletons of cynomolgus monkeys
reason: Action recognition and pose estimation on laboratory cynomolgus monkeys housed in single cages in a primate biomedical research facility, including MECP2 mutant disease-model animals; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Density estimation of the main structuring sessile species in underwater marine caves with a deep learning approach
reason: Applies deep learning semantic segmentation to video frames of wild sessile benthic animals (sponges, corals, bryozoans, tunicates) in a Mediterranean marine cave to estimate how dense they are.

title: Optimization of Animal Detection in Thermal Images Using YOLO Architecture
venue: International Journal of Electronics and Telecommunications
reason: YOLOv5 detection of deer and wild boar in thermal images taken in natural environments; primary research on wild animals.

title: Research on Object Detection in Animal Images Based on Convolutional Neural Networks
venue: International Journal of Advanced Network Monitoring and Controls
reason: YOLOv5 is applied to a small set of animal classes (cats, dogs, birds, horses, sheep) taken from the generic COCO and Cats vs Dogs benchmarks. Wildlife appears only as motivation, and no free-ranging wildlife data are identified.

title: Tracking Different Ant Species: An Unsupervised Domain Adaptation Framework and a Dataset for Multi-object Tracking
venue: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
reason: Multi-object tracking of ants filmed in a laboratory experimental setup; no wild free-ranging animals.

title: Find Rhinos without Finding Rhinos: Active Learning with Multimodal Imagery of South African Rhino Habitats
venue: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
reason: Primary study applying deep learning image classification to drone thermal, RGB and LiDAR imagery to find rhino middens (direct signs of wild rhinos) in Kruger National Park.

title: Long-term Monitoring of Bird Flocks in the Wild
venue: International Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence
reason: Primary study presenting a point-annotated image/video dataset of a wild flock of Demoiselle cranes and benchmarking counting, detection and segmentation models on it.

title: Landmarking Technique for Improving YOLOv4 Fish Recognition in Various Background Conditions
venue: Advances in Science Technology and Engineering Systems Journal
reason: Proposes a landmarking labelling technique with YOLOv4 for fish detection and classification. It is evaluated on the BYU dataset, which includes fish photographed in nature and underwater as well as fish on a processing table.

title: Aero-morphological Analysis of Nankeen Kestrels (Falco cenchroides) in Wind Hover Flight within Wind Tunnel
reason: Stereo-camera 3D reconstruction of a captive-reared, trained Nankeen Kestrel flying in a wind tunnel; no wild or free-ranging animals in the data.

title: NeRF IN REINFORCEMENT LEARNING FOR IMAGE RECOGNITION
reason: Primary study that classifies photographs of eight non-domestic forest animal classes with NeRF-RL / Q-Learning models, with camera-trap wildlife monitoring as the stated application. The paper does not say where the photographs come from or whether the animals are free-ranging.

title: Foraging behavior in the ant genus Messor (Hymenoptera: Formicidae: Myrmicinae)
reason: The paper is a literature review of foraging strategies and chemical ecology in Messor ants. It applies no computer vision or image analysis.

title: Automated staging of zebrafish embryos with deep learning
reason: Deep learning staging of laboratory zebrafish embryos from brightfield microscopy images in multi-well plates; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: New Zealand Inventory of Biodiversity
reason: This is a book review of the New Zealand Inventory of Biodiversity. It contains no primary research and no computer vision or image analysis.

title: Wild ungulate density data generated by camera trapping in 37 European areas: first output of the European Observatory of Wildlife (EOW)
reason: Camera-trap survey of wild ungulates across European study areas; images processed with the Agouti platform, including AI annotation and a computer-vision photogrammetry process to derive animal positions and speed for REM density estimation.

title: Night Vision Thermal sensor based Animal Movement Observation using CNN and YOLO v3
venue: International Journal of Advances in Computer Science and Technology
reason: Applies a CNN and YOLOv3 to thermal images and video of animals. The detected animals include wild species (elephant, giraffe, zebra) as well as domestic ones (cat, dog, sheep), and the stated application is wildlife conservation and protecting domestic animals from wild ones.

title: Preventing Animals Interference using Intelligence Camera and RFID System
venue: International Journal of Emerging Trends in Engineering Research
reason: Proposes an RFID and thermal CCTV monitoring framework plus physical barriers to keep animals off power distribution sites. Staff watch the CCTV footage by hand; the paper develops or evaluates no computer vision method on animal images.

title: Stressed Coral Reef Identification Using Deep Learning CNN Techniques
reason: CNN classification of coral reef images (corals are marine invertebrate animals) into healthy vs stressed; images collected from the internet, whether wild or aquarium corals is not stated.

title: MDM-YOLO: Research on Object Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv4 for Marine Organisms
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv4 detector for marine organisms (sea cucumber, sea urchin, scallop, starfish) in images taken in real underwater environments. The paper does not say whether these animals are wild or farmed; they are coded as free-ranging marine animals.

title: Towards Species-Specific Coral Classification in Reef Monitoring Efforts
venue: Proceedings of the ... International Florida Artificial Intelligence Research Society Conference
reason: CNN classification of stony and fire coral species (animals) in underwater images and reef photomosaics captured in situ in the Caribbean Sea.

title: Early Warning System to Prevent Animal-Train Collision
venue: International Journal of Scientific Research in Science and Technology
reason: Applies YOLOv3 detection to camera images of animals on railway tracks, including wild deer as well as domestic dogs and cows, to give collision warnings.

title: A computer vision toolkit for the dynamic study of air sacs in Siamang with a general application to the study of elastic kinematics in other animals
reason: Computer vision toolkit for air sac tracking applied to a captive siamang family recorded at a zoo/park; no wild free-ranging animals analysed.

title: Cross-modal constraints in multimodal vocalizations in Siamang (Syndactylus symphalangus)
reason: Computer vision (DeepLabCut keypoint tracking) applied to video of captive siamangs recorded only at a zoo; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Automated tracking of avian parental care behavior
reason: Sensor and video-based tracking of parental care behaviour applied only to captive zebra finches kept in cages inside sound attenuation chambers; no wild animals.

title: Comparison Efficacy of VGG16 and VGG19 Insect Classification Models
reason: Insect classification with VGG16/VGG19 on Google Images, framed around agricultural pest identification and crop protection; the stated target is agricultural research, not wildlife.

title: Exploring YOLOv8 Pretrain for Real-Time Detection of Indonesian Native Fish Species
reason: Applies YOLOv8 to images of native fish in Indonesian waters for head/tail detection with a fisheries and marine conservation motivation. The image source is not described in detail.

title: Drones and machine-learning for monitoring dugong feeding grounds and gillnet fishing
reason: Drone imagery and U-net segmentation of feeding trails (direct signs) of wild dugongs at Inhaca Island, Mozambique.

title: DEVELOPMENT OF ANIMAL TRACKING SYSTEM USINGCOMPUTER VISION
venue: International Journal of Engineering Applied Sciences and Technology
reason: Primary study that builds a motion-triggered camera prototype using YOLOv5 / Cascade R-CNN detection and CSRT tracking to detect wildlife entering human areas. The training and test images are not described, so the wild status of the animals rests on the paper's stated wildlife application.

title: Butterflies Recognition using Enhanced Transfer Learning and Data Augmentation
venue: Journal of Computing Theories and Applications
reason: Applies CNN image classification to 100 species of wild, non-domestic butterflies and moths from a public dataset. The paper does not say how the images were taken.

title: The re-discovery in Sumatra of a rarely seen moth, Heterosphecia tawonoides, and its identification using citizen science platform iNaturalist.
venue: Indonesian Journal of Applied Environmental Studies
reason: Field record of a wild moth identified by human community members on iNaturalist from photographs; no computer vision or automated image analysis is applied or evaluated.

title: An IoT-based smart mosquito trap system embedded with real-time mosquito image processing by neural networks for mosquito surveillance
reason: Mosquito images were collected in lab imaging set-ups, insect cages and a simulated living room. No images of wild, free-ranging animals were analysed.

title: Development of an automated biomaterial platform to study mosquito feeding behavior
reason: Object detection is applied to videos of laboratory-reared mosquitoes feeding on bioprinted hydrogels inside a glass cage; no wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: A convolutional neural network to characterize mouse hindlimb foot strikes during voluntary wheel running
reason: CNN applied to video of laboratory C57BL/6 mice running on wheels inside a monitoring cabinet; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Supplementing aerial drone surveys with biotelemetry data validates wildlife detection probabilities
reason: Feral pigs in drone thermal and RGB imagery were detected manually by a human analyst; no computer vision method is applied to animal images. Automated processing is limited to land-cover classification and orthomosaic generation. The animals are wild-caught feral pigs held in a fenced 20-acre natural-habitat enclosure.

title: A software pipeline for automated wildlife population sampling
reason: The pipeline is only tested on drone images of a domestic cattle herd on rangeland. No wild animals appear in the analysed data.

title: Automatic identification of conodont species using fine-grained convolutional neural networks
reason: The study classifies SEM images of fossil conodont specimens (Hindeodus). These are specimens, not wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Dynamic identification and automatic counting of the number of passing fish species based on the improved DeepSORT algorithm
reason: Applies YOLOv5 and an improved DeepSORT to underwater video from a fishway camera to identify, track and count wild native fish species passing through a fishway.

title: Round goby [Neogobius melanostomus (Pallas, 1814)], gudgeon (Gobio gobio L.) and bullhead (Cottus gobio L.) show distinct swimming patterns in a vertical slot fish pass
reason: Wild-caught fish were recorded only in a laboratory test-rig vertical slot fish pass, not free-ranging. Species were classified from manually tracked trajectories.

title: A large-scale study on the nocturnal behavior of African ungulates in zoos and its influencing factors
reason: All analysed video shows ungulates in stables of European zoos; no wild or free-ranging animals are in the data.

title: A camera trap method for estimating target densities of grey squirrels to inform wildlife management applications
reason: Camera-trap photographs of wild grey squirrels were tagged manually by observers and analysed with linear regression in Excel; no computer vision or automated image analysis was applied.

title: Monitoring marine pollution for carbon neutrality through a deep learning method with multi-source data fusion
reason: Deep CNN feature extraction with classifiers applied to underwater images of marine organisms (plankton, fish, crab, shrimp, shark, urchin) and marine debris from public underwater datasets; primary research.

title: Surveying wildlife and livestock in Uganda with aerial cameras: Deep Learning reduces the workload of human interpretation by over 70%
reason: Deep learning model (HerdNet) applied to oblique aerial survey imagery of a Ugandan protected area to detect and count wild mammals together with livestock.

title: Spotted! Computer-aided individual photo-identification allows for mark-recapture of invasive spotted lanternfly (Lycorma delicatula)
reason: Computer-aided photo-identification (I3S spot-pattern matching) of individual spotted lanternflies; includes field photos of free-ranging insects in an urban park alongside frozen lab specimens.

title: Camera-based automated monitoring of flying insects in the wild (Camfi). II. flight behaviour and long-term population monitoring of migratory Bogong moths in Alpine Australia
reason: Applies the Camfi automated camera-based detection and tracking method to images and video of wild Bogong moths in the Australian Alps for population and flight behaviour monitoring.

title: Camera-based automated monitoring of flying insects (Camfi). I. Field and computational methods
reason: Develops a Mask R-CNN based detection and tracking method for wild flying insects (Bogong moths) imaged by wildlife cameras in the field.

title: Heterogeneity on the abyssal plains: A case study in the Bering Sea
reason: Towed-camera seafloor images of wild deep-sea megafauna were annotated and counted by hand in group sessions. No computer vision or automated image analysis method was developed or applied.

title: An integrated monitoring system for disaster-causing organisms in the water intake areas of coastal nuclear power plants
reason: A seafloor optical microscopic imager records images of wild marine organisms (Acetes chinensis, small fish) at a nuclear plant intake. Software identifies the organisms in the images and estimates their abundance. The computer vision part is minor and its algorithm is not named.

title: Deep learning-based marine big data fusion for ocean environment monitoring: Towards shape optimization and salient objects detection
reason: Generic underwater salient object detection / image classification on fused underwater image databases; the paper never states animals or wildlife as the subject, only 'prominent items' and 'underwater objects'.

title: Macrofauna community of the cold seep area at Site F, South China Sea
reason: Ecological survey of cold seep macrofauna; ROV images were stitched into a mosaic and animals were counted and identified manually, with no computer vision analysis of the animals.

title: Deep focus-extended darkfield imaging for in situ observation of marine plankton
reason: Deep learning refocusing of darkfield images of live wild marine plankton (collected from sea and imaged in situ by underwater imagers); primary method paper.

title: Surfacing rates, swim speeds, and patterns of movement of Antarctic blue whales
reason: Applies video photogrammetric tracking (image-based range/bearing measurement) and photo-identification to wild Antarctic blue whales at sea.

title: An iterative labeling method for annotating marine life imagery
reason: Develops an iterative deep-learning labeling method (Faster R-CNN with crowdsourcing) on AUV seafloor imagery of wild marine life such as rockfish, starfish and sponges.

title: Scaling whale monitoring using deep learning: A human-in-the-loop solution for analyzing aerial datasets
reason: Primary study applying deep-learning semantic segmentation to aerial photographs of wild, free-ranging belugas (and other cetaceans in the source data).

title: Towards remote surveillance of marine pests: A comparison between remote operated vehicles and diver surveys
reason: Applies ROV video surveys and a YOLOv3 detector to detect wild non-indigenous marine invertebrates (Sabella spallanzanii) in New Zealand harbours.

title: Marine mammal morphometrics: 3D modeling and estimation validation
reason: Image-based photogrammetry and 3D reconstruction (Blender) of wild East Asian finless porpoises (bycatch carcasses) to estimate body volume, validated against direct measurements; intended for free-ranging marine mammals.

title: Estimating catch rates in real time: Development of a deep learning based Nephrops (Nephrops norvegicus) counter for demersal trawl fisheries
reason: Primary study applying deep-learning detection, tracking and counting to in-trawl underwater video of wild Nephrops recorded during commercial-ground trawling at sea.

title: EchoAI: A deep-learning based model for classification of echinoderms in global oceans
reason: Deep-learning image classification of marine echinoderms (non-domestic marine animals) from WoRMS images at five taxonomic levels; primary research. The paper does not say whether the images show free-ranging animals or specimens.

title: Estimation of total population size of southern elephant seals (Mirounga leonina) on Kerguelen and Crozet Archipelagos using very high-resolution satellite imagery
reason: Wild southern elephant seals are counted on satellite images, but the counting is done manually by a human observer; no computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Few-shot fine-grained fish species classification via sandwich attention CovaMNet
reason: Proposes a few-shot fine-grained CNN classifier for marine fish species, evaluated on fish image datasets including WildFish, described as a benchmark for wild fish identification.

title: Estimating precision and accuracy of automated video post-processing: A step towards implementation of AI/ML for optics-based fish sampling
reason: Primary study evaluating automated fish detection, classification and counting models (VIAME) on baited underwater survey video of wild reef fish in the Gulf of Mexico.

title: See you somewhere in the ocean: few-shot domain adaptive underwater object detection
reason: Proposes a few-shot domain-adaptive detector for marine creatures (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish) in underwater images. The data combine underwater benchmark datasets with images from aquariums.

title: Automatic detection and classification of coastal Mediterranean fish from underwater images: Good practices for robust training
reason: Deep learning detection and classification of wild coastal Mediterranean fish in underwater images from cabled observatories and video surveys; primary research with a new labeled dataset.

title: Demystifying image-based machine learning: a practical guide to automated analysis of field imagery using modern machine learning tools
reason: The journal labels the article a Review, but it is a practical guide with an original case study: YOLO v5 is trained and evaluated on ROV imagery of wild deep-sea animals from FathomNet. Coded as primary research on that basis.

title: Drivers of plankton community structure in intermittent and continuous coastal upwelling systems–from microbes and microscale in-situ imaging to large scale patterns
reason: Primary study applying a sparse CNN to in-situ underwater imagery of free-living plankton (zooplankton, larval fishes) collected along ocean transects to study community structure.

title: An early warning model for starfish disaster based on multi-sensor fusion
reason: Applies YOLOv5 detection to underwater video from a fixed seafloor platform to count wild starfish (P. pectinifera), which are predators in a marine ranch rather than farmed animals, and uses the counts for outbreak early warning.

title: Using computer vision to identify limpets from their shells: a case study using four species from the Baja California peninsula
reason: Images are of preserved shells of field-collected limpet specimens photographed under a microscope in a controlled lab room; no images of living free-ranging animals.

title: Generalised deep learning model for semi-automated length measurement of fish in stereo-BRUVS
reason: Deep learning head/tail detection on stereo-BRUVS underwater video of wild fish to measure length in their natural habitat.

title: Token-Selective Vision Transformer for fine-grained image recognition of marine organisms
reason: Proposes a vision transformer for fine-grained classification of marine organisms (plankton, sharks, wild fish) on marine biological image datasets.

title: Rapid physiological colouration change is a challenge - but not a hindrance - to successful photo identification of giant sunfish (Mola alexandrini, Molidae)
reason: Photo identification of wild giant sunfish is done entirely by human observers comparing images side by side; no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated. Automated recognition is only discussed as future work.

title: Toward efficient deep learning system for in-situ plankton image recognition
reason: Primary study proposing a knowledge distillation method and edge enhancement for detection and classification of in-situ underwater images of free-living marine plankton (including zooplankton such as Medusae, Copepoda, Chaetognatha).

title: Edge computing at sea: high-throughput classification of in-situ plankton imagery for adaptive sampling
reason: Primary methods paper applying a segmentation and CNN classification pipeline to in-situ imagery of free-living marine plankton (including zooplankton and larval fishes) collected at sea.

title: Wild salmon enumeration and monitoring using deep learning empowered detection and tracking
reason: Primary study that trains and tests deep learning detection and multi-object tracking models on underwater video of wild migrating salmon and other freshwater fish passing river weirs.

title: Lightweight marine biological target detection algorithm based on YOLOv5
reason: Proposes a lightweight YOLOv5-based detector for marine organisms (starfish, holothurian, echinus, scallop) in underwater robot images of the URPC dataset.

title: A deep learning approach for object detection of rockfish in challenging underwater environments
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv7 detector for wild rockfish in underwater imagery from a public NOAA dataset collected by ROV.

title: Low-cost UAV monitoring: insights into seasonal volumetric changes of an oyster reef in the German Wadden Sea
reason: Consumer-grade UAV RGB imagery, SfM and Random Forest pixel classification used to map and quantify a wild Pacific oyster reef in the Wadden Sea.

title: MSGNet: multi-source guidance network for fish segmentation in underwater videos
reason: Proposes a CV segmentation network (MSGNet) evaluated on underwater videos of fish recorded in natural coastal and estuarine habitats and on videos of camouflaged underwater animals.

title: Characterizing Håkon Mosby Mud Volcano (Barents Sea) cold seep systems by combining ROV-based acoustic data and underwater photogrammetry
reason: The study maps seafloor geomorphology and benthic substrate or habitat classes (mud, bacterial mats, sediment with tubeworms) from ROV orthomosaics. Animals are not the subject of the image analysis; it is habitat mapping.

title: DeepLOKI- a deep learning based approach to identify zooplankton taxa on high-resolution images from the optical plankton recorder LOKI
reason: Primary study developing a deep learning classifier for in-situ images of wild marine zooplankton taken by the LOKI plankton recorder during research cruises in Fram Strait.

title: Marker-less tracking system for multiple mice using Mask R-CNN
reason: Marker-less tracking of laboratory C57BL/6 mice in an open-field arena for pharmacological/behavioural research; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Multi-view image-based behavior classification of wet-dog shake in Kainate rat model
reason: Behaviour classification of wet-dog shake in Kainate-treated laboratory rats filmed in a plastic cage; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Disentangling rodent behaviors to improve automated behavior recognition
reason: Behavior recognition on video-derived keypoints of laboratory Sprague-Dawley rats in PhenoTyper cages, plus artificial time-series; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Applying Few-Shot Learning for In-the-Wild Camera-Trap Species Classification
reason: Primary study evaluating few-shot learning networks for species classification on in-the-wild camera-trap images of wild animals in Senegal.

title: MAFFN_YOLOv5: Multi-Scale Attention Feature Fusion Network on the YOLOv5 Model for the Health Detection of Coral-Reefs Using a Built-In Benchmark Dataset
reason: Proposes a YOLOv5-based CNN detector for health conditions of corals (wild marine animals) in underwater images collected from the web.

title: A Fine-Grained Bird Classification Method Based on Attention and Decoupled Knowledge Distillation
reason: Proposes a CNN-based fine-grained bird species classification method on bird images (CUB-200-2011), with bird species recognition and biodiversity monitoring as the stated application.

title: Marina Observation of Sea Turtles: Establishing a Database of Intracoastal Waterway Green Sea Turtles in Northeast Florida
reason: Applies the HotSpotter pattern-matching software to photographs of wild juvenile green sea turtles at marinas to identify individual turtles.

title: PolarBearVidID: A Video-Based Re-Identification Benchmark Dataset for Polar Bears
reason: Video re-identification dataset and benchmark of 13 polar bears filmed exclusively in six zoos; no wild or free-ranging animals in the data.

title: A Lightweight Automatic Wildlife Recognition Model Design Method Mitigating Shortcut Learning
reason: Primary study proposing a data augmentation and model compression method for species classification on camera trap images of wild animals.

title: Activity Patterns of Captive Red Panda (Ailurus fulgens)
reason: Behavioural activity budgets of captive zoo red pandas from in-person observation and manually reviewed video; no computer vision method is applied, and all animals are captive.

title: Animal Species Recognition with Deep Convolutional Neural Networks from Ecological Camera Trap Images
reason: Primary study applying CNN classifiers to camera trap images of wild snakes, lizards and toads/frogs collected in Texas.

title: An Efficient Method for Monitoring Birds Based on Object Detection and Multi-Object Tracking Networks
reason: Primary study proposing an improved YOLOv7 + DeepSORT method for detecting, tracking and counting ten protected wetland bird species in internet-sourced images of birds in wetland environments.

title: Camera Trap Methods and Drone Thermal Surveillance Provide Reliable, Comparable Density Estimates of Large, Free-Ranging Ungulates
reason: Wild white-tailed deer were surveyed with camera traps and drone thermal video, but people counted the animals by hand and the analysis is statistical (mark-resight, N-mixture models). No computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Drone Observation for the Quantitative Study of Complex Multilevel Societies
reason: Review article on the use of drones to study multilevel animal societies; it analyses no image data itself and presents no primary computer vision research.

title: Optimized Small Waterbird Detection Method Using Surveillance Videos Based on YOLOv7
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv7 to detect wild waterbirds in surveillance videos from six wetlands in China.

title: Understanding Circadian and Circannual Behavioral Cycles of Captive Giant Pandas (Ailuropoda melanoleuca) Can Help to Promote Good Welfare
reason: Behaviour of zoo-housed giant pandas was coded manually by human observers watching webcam footage, and the analysis uses statistics (ZINB models, wavelet analysis). No computer vision method is used, and all animals are captive.

title: Fusing Local Shallow Features and Global Deep Features to Identify Beaks
reason: Images are of dissected beak specimens from dead, fished cephalopods, photographed on a white light board in the laboratory; no images of live free-ranging animals.

title: Bird Object Detection: Dataset Construction, Model Performance Evaluation, and Model Lightweighting
reason: Primary study that builds a web-crawled bird object detection dataset and evaluates detection models for wild bird monitoring and counting. The paper does not state whether the web images show wild or captive birds; wild is taken from the stated application.

title: A Forest Wildlife Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv5s
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv5s detector for forest wildlife in camera-trap images from a Chinese nature reserve and a subset of iWildCam 2019.

title: Monitoring Endangered and Rare Wildlife in the Field: A Foundation Deep Learning Model Integrating Human Knowledge for Incremental Recognition with Few Data and Low Cost
reason: Proposes a CLIP-based few-shot species recognition method evaluated on camera-trap images of endangered wildlife from Chinese national parks, alongside animal and generic benchmarks that include pets and livestock.

title: DJAN: Deep Joint Adaptation Network for Wildlife Image Recognition
reason: Proposes a domain adaptation network for species recognition on camera-trap images of wild animals from two public wildlife datasets.

title: Social Network Analysis as a Tool in the Care and Wellbeing of Zoo Animals: A Case Study of a Family Group of Black Lemurs (Eulemur macaco)
reason: Social network analysis of zoo black lemurs based on direct behavioural observation recorded on paper sheets; no image or video analysis (video only used in pilot for observer confirmation). Animals are also captive only.

title: Improving Known–Unknown Cattle’s Face Recognition for Smart Livestock Farm Management
reason: Individual face recognition of Hanwoo cattle in a closed livestock farm barn; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Ethogram of the Chinese Giant Salamander during the Breeding Period Based on the PAE Coding System

title: Animal Pose Estimation Based on 3D Priors

title: Underwater Object Detection Method Based on Improved Faster RCNN
reason: Proposes an improved Faster RCNN for detecting marine organisms (sea cucumbers, sea urchins, scallops, starfish) in underwater images collected from the Internet. The paper does not say whether the animals are wild or farmed, but the stated motivation is protecting marine organisms.

title: Real-Time Target Detection System for Animals Based on Self-Attention Improvement and Feature Extraction Optimization
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv5s detector for wildlife images (six wild animal classes) collected from the web; primary CV research on wild animals.
