reason: Primary study quantifying long-tailedness and evaluating a transformer object detector (DINO with BatchFormer) on camera trap images of wild animals.

title: Identification of Ratholes in Desert Steppe Based on UAV Hyperspectral Remote Sensing
reason: Applies image analysis (PCA on UAV hyperspectral images) to identify burrows (direct signs) of wild grassland rodents in a desert steppe.

title: Automated Wildlife Bird Detection from Drone Footage Using Computer Vision Techniques
reason: Applies YOLOv4 object detection to drone footage of wild birds and flocks recorded in a protected wetland.

title: WAID: A Large-Scale Dataset for Wildlife Detection with Drones
reason: Presents a drone aerial image dataset and a detector (SE-YOLO) for animal detection; classes include wild animals (seals, zebras, Tibetan wild asses) together with domestic sheep and cattle.

title: Bird Detection on Power Transmission Lines Based on Improved YOLOv7
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv7 for detecting free-ranging birds on power transmission lines in images.

title: Fish Detection under Occlusion Using Modified You Only Look Once v8 Integrating Real-Time Detection Transformer Features
reason: Proposes a modified YOLOv8 for detecting occluded fish (three reef fish species) in underwater images, aimed at monitoring fish for research and conservation. The source of the images, wild or captive, is not stated.

title: Finding a Husband: Using Explainable AI to Define Male Mosquito Flight Differences
reason: The paper classifies already-reconstructed 3D flight trajectories (coordinates over time) of wild mosquitoes with a one-class SVM on hand-built kinematic features. It does no image or video analysis itself: the stereo recordings were turned into tracks by an earlier study.

title: Detection of Hindwing Landmarks Using Transfer Learning and High-Resolution Networks
reason: Landmark detection on images of dissected hindwings of leaf beetle specimens photographed under a stereoscope; museum/lab specimens, not free-ranging animals.

title: Ontogenetic Shifts in Body Morphology of Demersal Sharks’ Species (Order: Squaliformes) Inhabiting the Western-Central Mediterranean Sea, with Implications for Their Bio-Ecological Role
reason: Morphometric study of dead trawl-caught shark specimens photographed in the laboratory. Measurements and landmarks were placed by hand in TPSDig2 and analysed with multivariate statistics, so no computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Lobster Position Estimation Using YOLOv7 for Potential Guidance of FANUC Robotic Arm in American Lobster Processing
reason: Object detection and orientation estimation on images of cooked American lobsters for robotic handling in a seafood processing line; no wild, free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Automatic Recognition of Black-Necked Swan (Cygnus melancoryphus) from Drone Imagery
reason: Primary study developing an automatic image-based recognizer (spectral threshold plus object-oriented shape classification) to detect and count wild black-necked swans in drone orthophotos of a Chilean wetland.

title: Animal Detection and Counting from UAV Images Using Convolutional Neural Networks
reason: Applies and compares CNN object detectors on UAV images to detect and count deer in a hunting ground (partly enclosed) in Serbia; additional generalisation test on cow images and internet images.

title: Evaluation of an Innovative Rosette Flight Plan Design for Wildlife Aerial Surveys with UAS
reason: The paper evaluates a rosette UAS flight plan and sampling protocol using field flights and numerical simulations. Animals on the drone images were counted manually by observers; no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: A Novel Technique for Photo-Identification of the Fin Whale, Balaenoptera physalus, as Determined by Drone Aerial Images
reason: The paper describes a manual photo-identification protocol for fin whales from drone video stills; images are categorised and matched by eye by researchers, and no computer vision method is developed or applied (AI is only suggested as future work).

title: The Use of Unoccupied Aerial Systems (UASs) for Quantifying Shallow Coral Reef Restoration Success in Belize
reason: Primary study applying object-based image segmentation to UAS imagery of outplanted and naturally spreading acroporid corals (animals) on a shallow reef in a national park.

title: A Drone Study of Sociality in the Finless Porpoise Neophocaena asiaeorientalis in the Ariake Sound, Japan
reason: Drone survey of wild finless porpoises where animals in photos were detected and counted manually; no computer vision or automated image analysis method is developed or applied.

title: Identifying Important Bird and Biodiversity Areas in Antarctica Using RPAS Surveys—A Case Study of Cape Melville, King George Island, Antarctica
reason: Drone survey of wild seabird colonies in Antarctica, but nests were counted by hand by human observers on orthophotos in GIS. No computer vision method is developed or applied; orthomosaics were only produced with photogrammetry software.

title: Observing Individuals and Behavior of Hainan Gibbons (Nomascus hainanus) Using Drone Infrared and Visible Image Fusion Technology
reason: Proposes an infrared-visible image fusion network applied to drone images of wild Hainan gibbons in a nature reserve.

title: Burrow-Nesting Seabird Survey Using UAV-Mounted Thermal Sensor and Count Automation
reason: UAV thermal imagery of a wild short-tailed shearwater colony is analysed with an image-filtering pipeline to automatically detect and count occupied burrows.

title: Drone with Mounted Thermal Infrared Cameras for Monitoring Terrestrial Mammals
reason: Thermal drone video of wild mammals (and cattle) is analysed manually: body measurements are taken by hand in ImageJ and animals are counted by reviewing videos; statistics are PCA/MANOVA on the measurements. No computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Using YOLO Object Detection to Identify Hare and Roe Deer in Thermal Aerial Video Footage—Possible Future Applications in Real-Time Automatic Drone Surveillance and Wildlife Monitoring
reason: Trains YOLOv5 object detectors on thermal drone footage of free-ranging hare and roe deer captured at night in Danish landscapes for wildlife monitoring.

title: Comparison of Different Methods of Animal Detection and Recognition on Thermal Camera Images
reason: Compares HOG/SVM, Faster R-CNN and YOLOv3 for detecting wild deer and wild boar in thermal camera images taken from the ground.

title: Wildlife Object Detection Method Applying Segmentation Gradient Flow and Feature Dimensionality Reduction
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv5s detector for wild animals (antelope, elephant, leopard, eagle, giraffe) in natural environments using wildlife images.

title: Camouflaged Insect Segmentation Using a Progressive Refinement Network
reason: Proposes a deep learning segmentation network (PRNet) for camouflaged insects in ecological images taken from the COD10K and CAMO camouflage datasets; insects in natural scenes are the stated subject.

title: An Improved YOLOv5 Underwater Detector Based on an Attention Mechanism and Multi-Branch Reparameterization Module
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv5 detector for underwater images of marine animals (echinus, starfish, holothurian, scallop) from URPC2019. The paper does not say where the animals were filmed.

title: Underwater Target Detection Algorithm Based on Feature Fusion Enhancement
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv7 detector for marine invertebrates (echinus, holothurian, starfish, scallop) in underwater robot images taken in the waters of Dalian.

title: An Underwater Dense Small Object Detection Model Based on YOLOv5-CFDSDSE
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for underwater marine organisms (sea cucumbers, sea urchins) in real-world underwater images from the URPC 2019 and UODD datasets. The paper does not say whether the animals are wild or farmed.

title: Fish Monitoring from Low-Contrast Underwater Images
reason: Computer vision toolset (fish detection, orientation classification, tracking, landmark-based shape alignment) developed and tested on underwater photographs and videos of Mediterranean fish captured by the authors in shallow sea waters in Greece; primary research.

title: Research on an Underwater Object Detection Network Based on Dual-Branch Feature Extraction
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for underwater marine organisms (echinus, holothurian, scallop, starfish) in the URPC2020 dataset. The paper says the images come from real underwater environments, so the animals are treated as free-ranging.

title: VHR-BirdPose: Vision Transformer-Based HRNet for Bird Pose Estimation with Attention Mechanism
reason: Primary study proposing a computer vision pose estimation method for birds, evaluated on bird frames of the Animal Kingdom dataset with stated application to bird monitoring and protection; the paper does not state whether the birds are wild or captive.

title: Pairwise Guided Multilayer Cross-Fusion Network for Bird Image Recognition
reason: Fine-grained classification method for bird images whose stated application is bird diversity monitoring; evaluated mainly on the CUB-200-2011 bird dataset. Cars and aircraft serve only as secondary generalisation tests.

title: DSW-YOLOv8n: A New Underwater Target Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv8n
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv8n detector for underwater targets. The authors' dataset contains marine animals (jellyfish, fish, sea urchins, scallops, sharks, sea turtles), and the stated application is underwater environment monitoring. Pascal VOC is used only as a second check.

title: Image-Fused-Guided Underwater Object Detection Model Based on Improved YOLOv7
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv7 to detect benthic marine animals (echinus, starfish, holothurian, scallop) in underwater images.

title: THANet: Transferring Human Pose Estimation to Animal Pose Estimation
reason: Proposes a vision transformer method for animal pose estimation, evaluated on AP-10K (54 mammal species) and Animal-Pose (domestic quadrupeds). Animals are the subject and the data mix wild-type mammals with domestic ones.

title: MammalClub: An Annotated Wild Mammal Dataset for Species Recognition, Individual Identification, and Behavior Recognition
reason: Dataset paper on wild mammal images/video from wildlife documentaries plus some zoo recordings, with CV models for detection, re-identification and behavior recognition.

title: MCFP-YOLO Animal Species Detector for Embedded Systems
reason: Develops an animal species detector (MCFP-YOLO) for wildlife-vehicle collision and wildlife-human conflict mitigation, evaluated on video showing wildlife (a cougar frame is shown). The paper does not explicitly state whether the animals in the test video are free-ranging; wild status is inferred from the stated application and the cougar example.

title: Detection of Forestry Pests Based on Improved YOLOv5 and Transfer Learning
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv5 detector for forestry pest insects in web-collected images of natural environments; forest pests are non-domestic, free-living insects rather than crop pests in production (borderline with E-AGRI because of the pest-management framing and agricultural pre-training data).

title: Remote Monitoring of Amur Tigers in Forest Ecosystems Using Improved YOLOX Algorithm
reason: All training and quantitative evaluation use the ATRW detection subset, which the paper says was filmed at 10 zoos in China. A further 'dataset collected from a natural reserve' is mentioned once for a qualitative figure, but the paper does not describe it or say the animals were free-ranging. The infrared camera-trap deployment is a proposed scheme, not a source of analysed data.

title: IoT-Based Object-Detection System to Safeguard Endangered Animals and Bolster Agricultural Farm Security
reason: Primary study training a YOLOv8 detector on web-collected images of wild animals (elephant, porcupine, wild boar, vulture, bat, squirrel) together with a domestic goat class, for an IoT farm alert system.

title: Automated Identification of Morphological Characteristics of Three Thunnus Species Based on Different Machine Learning Algorithms
reason: Computer vision (EFT shape features and VGG16 deep features with SVM/RF/KNN) applied to images of wild-caught tuna photographed by fishery observers on board, for species identification.

title: Semi-Automated Inquiry of Fish Launch Angle and Speed for Hazard Analysis
reason: Video of wild migrating steelhead leaping at a dam spillway is analysed with a semi-automated image annotation tool to measure launch angle, speed and length; primary field study.

title: A Fine-Grained Recognition Neural Network with High-Order Feature Maps via Graph-Based Embedding for Natural Bird Diversity Conservation
venue: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
reason: Proposes a fine-grained bird classification and detection network and evaluates it on bird benchmarks plus an author-collected dataset of wild birds photographed by remote monitoring cameras at river and lake stations in Beijing.

title: RTAD: A Real-Time Animal Object Detection Model Based on a Large Selective Kernel and Channel Pruning
reason: Proposes an animal object detection model evaluated on AP-10K, a 50-species mammal image dataset described as showing animals in an almost natural state; the result figures also show domestic animals (cow, dog), so the subject type is mixed.

title: Deep Learning-Based Image Classification for Major Mosquito Species Inhabiting Korea
reason: Live mosquitoes (wild-collected and breedable species) were manually placed with an aspirator into a prototype capture device and imaged under controlled white/UV LED lighting on a steel background; no free-ranging animals are imaged in the field.

title: SpiderID_APP: A User-Friendly APP for Spider Identification in Taiwan Using YOLO-Based Deep Learning Models
reason: Primary study training YOLO models to detect and classify spider genera in citizen-science images (iNaturalist, TBN) of spiders found in Taiwan.

title: Underwater Target Detection Lightweight Algorithm Based on Multi-Scale Feature Fusion
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Proposes a lightweight CNN-Transformer detector for underwater marine invertebrates (holothurian, echinus, scallops, starfish) in real underwater images from the URPC dataset. title: Lightweight Underwater Target Detection Algorithm Based on Dynamic Sampling Transformer and Knowledge-Distillation Optimization
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering

title: An Improved Tuna-YOLO Model Based on YOLO v3 for Real-Time Tuna Detection Considering Lightweight Deployment
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Develops a CV detection model for wild-caught tuna and billfish species in electronic monitoring video from longline fishing vessels (wild fisheries catch, not aquaculture).

title: A Real-Time Fish Target Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv5
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv5s fish detector evaluated on underwater images of free-ranging marine fish from the Fish4Knowledge dataset recorded at underwater viewing platforms in Taiwan.

title: A Biologist’s Guide to the Galaxy: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence and Very High-Resolution Satellite Imagery to Monitor Marine Mammals from Space

reason: Concept paper / perspective: a guide to very high-resolution satellite imagery for marine mammal monitoring that shares lessons learned, challenges and a vision for the GAIA initiative. title: Underwater Target Detection Based on Improved YOLOv7

reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv7 detector for underwater marine organisms (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish, fish, crab, etc.) in underwater optical image datasets; animals are the detection targets.

title: A Marine Organism Detection Framework Based on Dataset Augmentation and CNN-ViT Fusion
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Proposes a CNN-ViT detection framework for marine organisms (echinus, holothurian, scallop, starfish) in underwater images taken by underwater robots. title: A New Coastal Crawler Prototype to Expand the Ecological Monitoring Radius of OBSEA Cabled Observatory

reason: Paper presents a benthic crawler platform; fish in the videos were identified and counted manually by an operator. The only automated image processing is photo-mosaicking of the seabed, which is not an analysis of the animals.

title: Finding Nemo’s Giant Cousin: Keypoint Matching for Robust Re-Identification of Giant Sunfish

reason: Proposes a keypoint-matching re-identification pipeline for wild giant sunfish photographed by divers; also evaluated on seal and domestic cow datasets.

title: Underwater 3D Reconstruction from Video or Still Imagery: Matisse and 3DMetrics Processing and Exploitation Software
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Software paper for underwater 3D reconstruction of seafloor scenes (litter, fault scarp, hydrothermal vent, shipwreck). The subject is habitat and structures, not animals. Mussels only show up incidentally in one model.

title: Underwater-YCC: Underwater Target Detection Optimization Algorithm Based on YOLOv7
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Proposes a YOLOv7-based detector for underwater marine organisms (echinus, holothurian, scallop, starfish) in underwater optical images from the URPC2020 dataset.

title: Underwater Small Target Detection Based on YOLOX Combined with MobileViT and Double Coordinate Attention
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Proposes a deep learning detector for underwater marine animals (holothurian, echinus, starfish, scallop) evaluated on the URPC2020 underwater image dataset.

title: Particle Filter Based on Harris Hawks Optimization Algorithm for Underwater Visual Tracking

title: YOLOv6-ESG: A Lightweight Seafood Detection Method
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Proposes a lightweight CNN detector for marine invertebrates (holothurian, echinus, starfish, scallop) in underwater images taken in real marine environments.

title: Collaborative Framework for Underwater Object Detection via Joint Image Enhancement and Super-Resolution

reason: Proposes a CNN-based underwater object detection framework evaluated on underwater images/videos of marine animals (echinus, holothurian, scallop, starfish, fish, crabs, jellyfish, shrimp).

title: YOLOv7-CHS: An Emerging Model for Underwater Object Detection
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Proposes a YOLOv7-based detector for underwater marine organisms, evaluated on real underwater images of wild Crown-of-Thorns Starfish from the Great Barrier Reef and on the DUO dataset of benthic animals.

title: Performance Comparison of Sea Cucumber Detection by the Yolov5 and DETR Approach
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Sea cucumber detection for intelligent subsea fishing robots in aquaculture/marine pastures; production context (aquaculture harvesting) rather than wild animal conservation.

title: A Deep Learning-Based Lightweight Model for the Detection of Marine Fishes
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Proposes a lightweight YOLOv5s-based detector for marine coral reef fish, trained and tested on web-crawled images of fish. The paper does not explicitly say the fish are wild; this is inferred from the coral reef and marine framing.

title: A Demonstration of the Capability of Low-Cost Hyperspectral Imaging for the Characterisation of Coral Reefs
reason: Underwater hyperspectral imaging of wild corals on Bermudan reefs, with spectral classification of benthic types and 3D reconstruction (DEMs) of coral colonies.

title: High-Accuracy and Low-Latency Tracker for UAVs Monitoring Tibetan Antelopes
reason: Proposes a look-back tracker combining YOLOX detection and optical flow, evaluated on UAV video of wild Tibetan antelopes recorded in a nature reserve area in Qinghai.

title: UAS-Based Real-Time Detection of Red-Cockaded Woodpecker Cavities in Heterogeneous Landscapes Using YOLO Object Detection Algorithms
reason: YOLO object detection applied to UAS aerial images of cavity trees (direct signs/nests) of wild Red-cockaded Woodpeckers in a national forest; primary research.

title: Performance of Multiple Models for Estimating Rodent Activity Intensity in Alpine Grassland Using Remote Sensing
reason: Models applied to UAV and Sentinel-2A imagery estimate the intensity of activity by wild rodents in alpine grassland, using their direct signs (holes and mounds).

title: A Lightweight and High-Accuracy Deep Learning Method for Grassland Grazing Livestock Detection Using UAV Imagery
reason: The paper detects and counts grazing livestock (cattle, horses, sheep) in UAV imagery of a pasture; no wild, non-domestic animals are analysed.

title: Using Drones to Determine Chimpanzee Absences at the Edge of Their Distribution in Western Tanzania
reason: Drone images of wild chimpanzee nests were inspected manually by human observers; no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated. Automated nest detection is only named as future work.

title: How Do Underwater Cultural Heritage Sites Affect Coral Assemblages?
reason: Applies structure-from-motion photogrammetry to diver-collected underwater images of wild coral assemblages (corals are animals) on natural reefs and wreck sites in Guam, to quantify coral cover and 3D habitat complexity.

title: YOLO for Penguin Detection and Counting Based on Remote Sensing Images
reason: Proposes an object detection network (YoloPd) to detect and count wild Adelie penguins in aerial images taken from a helicopter over an Antarctic island.

title: Removing Human Bottlenecks in Bird Classification Using Camera Trap Images and Deep Learning
reason: Faster-RCNN detection and species classification of wild birds visiting feeders, using camera trap images from deployments in the UK and the Netherlands plus iNaturalist images.

title: Empowering Wildlife Guardians: An Equitable Digital Stewardship and Reward System for Biodiversity Conservation Using Deep Learning and 3/4G Camera Traps
reason: Faster R-CNN species detection on camera trap images of free-ranging animals in a South African game reserve; training data partly collected at a safari park.

title: Describing Polyps Behavior of a Deep-Sea Gorgonian, Placogorgia sp., Using a Deep-Learning Approach
reason: Primary study applying deep-learning semantic segmentation to in-situ time-lapse images of wild deep-sea gorgonian colonies (animals) to describe polyp feeding behaviour.

title: Development of a Google Earth Engine-Based Application for the Management of Shallow Coral Reefs Using Drone Imagery
reason: Applies supervised pixel classification to drone multispectral orthomosaics of wild shallow coral reefs. Live coral, which is an animal, is one of the mapped classes, alongside macroalgae, sand and rubble. Borderline with E-PLANT because the paper frames the work as habitat mapping.

title: Quantifying the Loss of Coral from a Bleaching Event Using Underwater Photogrammetry and AI-Assisted Image Segmentation
reason: Primary study applying AI-assisted image segmentation to underwater photogrammetric orthophotomosaics of wild reef-building corals (animals) on a natural fore reef to quantify bleaching mortality.

title: Comparison of Supervised Learning and Changepoint Detection for Insect Detection in Lidar Data
reason: Primary study comparing supervised learning and changepoint detection for detecting flying insects (honeybees near managed beehives, free-flying outdoors) in lidar range-time images; the stated subject is insect monitoring for biodiversity and population decline. title: Altering Fish Behavior by Sensing Swarm Patterns of Fish in an Artificial Aquatic Environment Using an Interactive Robotic Fish
reason: All images show 10 common carp kept in an artificial fish tank in a home garden. No wild or free-ranging animals appear in the data.

title: In Situ Sea Cucumber Detection across Multiple Underwater Scenes Based on Convolutional Neural Networks and Image Enhancements
reason: Applies CNN object detectors with image enhancement to in situ underwater images and videos of sea cucumbers on natural seabeds (sea grass, rock, sand).

title: Behavior-Based Video Summarization System for Dog Health and Welfare Monitoring
reason: The study recognises behaviours of two pet dogs recorded indoors in a laboratory room; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Yolo-Pest: An Insect Pest Object Detection Algorithm via CAC3 Module
reason: Detection of agricultural crop insect pests for pest control; images of trapped and killed insects from insect searchlight devices plus the IP102 crop pest dataset.

title: A Deep-Learning Based Pipeline for Estimating the Abundance and Size of Aquatic Organisms in an Unconstrained Underwater Environment from Continuously Captured Stereo Video
reason: Deep-learning pipeline (Yolov5 plus stereo matching) for detecting, classifying, counting and sizing free-swimming fish and jellyfish recorded in situ by a stationary underwater observatory in the Kiel Fjord.

title: An Improved YOLOv5-Based Underwater Object-Detection Framework
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv5 detector for marine organisms (echinus, starfish, holothurian, scallop) in underwater seabed images from the URPC datasets. The paper does not say whether the animals are wild or farmed; they are coded as wild seabed fauna.

title: Procapra Przewalskii Tracking Autonomous Unmanned Aerial Vehicle Based on Improved Long and Short-Term Memory Kalman Filters
reason: Computer vision (YOLOX detection plus LSTM-KF tracking) on UAV video of wild Procapra przewalskii at Qinghai Lake.

title: UWV-Yolox: A Deep Learning Model for Underwater Video Object Detection
reason: Proposes a deep learning video object detection model for underwater videos of marine animals (echinus, holothurian, starfish, fish, jellyfish) from field underwater datasets, intended for biodiversity monitoring.

title: Fine-Grained 3D Modeling and Semantic Mapping of Coral Reefs Using Photogrammetric Computer Vision and Machine Learning †
reason: Primary study that develops a multi-modal segmentation network and photogrammetric 3D reconstruction on underwater images of wild corals (animals) collected in situ at the Moorea fore reef.

title: Object Detection of Small Insects in Time-Lapse Camera Recordings
reason: Primary study proposing a motion-informed enhancement pipeline with CNN detectors for insects visiting plants in time-lapse images. Data are mainly free-flying honeybees from hives placed in greenhouses, plus some hoverflies and other incidental arthropods, so subjects are coded as mixed managed and wild.

title: Captive Animal Behavior Study by Video Analysis
reason: All three applications analyse video of captive animals only: a laboratory rat in a plastic box, a laboratory monkey in a neuroscience cage and a zoo panda bear. Two of the three are laboratory set-ups; no wild or free-ranging animals are in the data.

title: Underwater Fish Segmentation Algorithm Based on Improved PSPNet Network
reason: Proposes an improved PSPNet for semantic segmentation of fish in underwater images from the DeepFish dataset, recorded with fixed underwater cameras in natural coastal marine habitats of Australia.

title: Research on Fine-Grained Image Recognition of Birds Based on Improved YOLOv5
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv5 part-based method for fine-grained recognition of bird species, motivated by biodiversity surveys; evaluated on CUB200-2011 bird images.

title: Multi-Cat Monitoring System Based on Concept Drift Adaptive Machine Learning Architecture
reason: Individual identification of pet/domestic cats using litter-box cameras in cat cafés, streets and shelters; the application is pet health monitoring in multi-cat households, not wildlife.

title: IoT Sensor Network for Wild-Animal Detection near Roads
reason: Wild animals are detected with passive infrared (PIR) sensors in an IoT network. Camera and thermal images are used only to check sensor triggers by eye; the paper does no computer-vision analysis of the images.

title: Utility of Spectral Filtering to Improve the Reliability of Marine Fauna Detections from Drone-Based Monitoring
reason: Drone video of wild dolphins along Australian coastal beaches is analysed with a deep learning object detector to compare the detection reliability of spectrally filtered and unfiltered RGB cameras.

title: Intelligent Detection Method for Wildlife Based on Deep Learning
reason: Proposes a modified YOLOv7 detector (TMS-YOLO) evaluated on images of wild animals from national park videos, public datasets, documentaries and a Turkish wildlife dataset.

title: Design and Development of a Fog-Assisted Elephant Corridor over a Railway Track
reason: Primary study proposing a fog-computing elephant monitoring framework near railway tracks. It trains and evaluates YOLOv5 elephant detection on a custom image dataset. The elephants are wild animals near rail corridors, but the paper does not say where the training images came from.

title: Phototropic Behavioral Responses of Zooplankton in Lake Baikal In Situ and during the Anthropogenic Impact Modeling

title: A novel method for estimating avian roost sizes using passive acoustic recordings
reason: The core method is acoustic. However, the authors also built and validated an automated video-analysis technique that detects and counts free-ranging Javan mynas flying in and out of a roost tree in Singapore, so part of the work is computer vision on wild birds.

title: Measuring mantled howler monkey (Alouatta palliata) testes via parallel laser photogrammetry: Expanding the use of noninvasive methods
reason: Image-based morphometric measurement (parallel laser photogrammetry) of testes of free-living mantled howler monkeys in Costa Rica.

title: First noncontact millimeter‐wave radar measurement of heart rate in great apes: Validation in chimpanzees (Pan troglodytes)
reason: Heart rate is measured from millimeter-wave radar signals using signal processing, not computer vision on camera images or video. The two chimpanzees were anesthetized sanctuary animals, so the study is also captive-only.

title: Advancing primate surveillance with image recognition techniques from unmanned aerial vehicles
reason: Automated detection and counting of wild Sichuan snub-nosed monkeys in UAV thermal imagery from the Qinling Mountains.

title: Vertical climbing in free‐ranging bonobos: An exploratory study integrating locomotor performance and substrate compliance
reason: Field video of free-ranging bonobos analysed with video stabilization (point feature matching) and frame-by-frame digitization/tracking of body center of mass to derive speed and acceleration; image-based analysis of wild animals.

title: Pump and sway: Wild primates use compliant supports as a tool to augment leaping in the canopy
reason: Video-based kinematic tracking (digitized points on the animal and the branch) of wild colobus monkeys leaping in Kibale National Park, Uganda.

title: Automated identification of invasive rabbitfishes in underwater images from the Mediterranean Sea
venue: Aquatic Conservation Marine and Freshwater Ecosystems
reason: Deep learning classifier trained and tested on underwater video frames of wild, free-ranging Mediterranean fishes to identify invasive rabbitfishes; primary research.

title: The effectiveness of the semi‐automated Identifin software to accurately fast‐track dorsal fin photographic identifications of sharks
venue: Aquatic Conservation Marine and Freshwater Ecosystems
reason: Evaluates a semi-automated dorsal fin matching software (edge tracing and matching algorithm) on photographs of free-ranging white and bronze whaler sharks for individual identification.

title: Deep Learning for Multilabel Classification of Coral Reef Conditions in the Indo‐Pacific Using Underwater Photo Transect Method
venue: Aquatic Conservation Marine and Freshwater Ecosystems
reason: Primary study that builds a dataset of in-situ underwater photos of wild coral colonies (animals) and applies deep learning to classify coral reef condition and stressors.

title: Effect of Stocking Density on the Growth of the Endangered Amazonian Fish Hypancistrus zebra (Siluriformes: Loricariidae)
venue: Aquatic Conservation Marine and Freshwater Ecosystems
reason: Ex situ aquaculture study of captive-bred H. zebra juveniles in laboratory aquaria; images used only for manual length measurement in ImageJ; no wild free-ranging animals imaged.

title: How does the shape of the wing and hindlimb bones of aquatic birds relate to their locomotor abilities?
reason: 3D geometric morphometric study of dry museum skeletons (MNHN collection); no wild or free-ranging animals are imaged and landmarks are placed by hand, so it is museum-specimen anatomy rather than wildlife computer vision.

title: A novel DbneAlexnet with Gazelle Hunting Optimization Algorithm enabled wild animal detection in WMSN data communication in IoT environment
reason: Primary study proposing a deep learning method (GHOA-trained DbneAlexNet) to detect wild animals in images from a public animal detection image dataset. The paper calls the images wild animal images but does not state whether the animals are free-ranging or captive.

title: Individual recognition of Eurasian beavers (Castor fiber) by their tail patterns using a computer‐assisted pattern‐identification algorithm
reason: All analysed images show tails of hunted, deceased beavers photographed on a table in a mostly indoor laboratory set-up; no images of wild, free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Herbivorous fish feeding dynamics and energy expenditure on a coral reef: Insights from stereo‐video and AI ‐driven 3D tracking
reason: Applies CNN detection, species classification and 3D multi-object tracking to stereo-video of free-ranging coral reef fishes filmed on a Red Sea reef.

title: A hands‐on guide to use network video recorders, internet protocol cameras, and deep learning models for dynamic monitoring of trout and salmon in small streams
reason: Primary study training a deep learning image classifier on underwater video of free-ranging trout and salmon recorded in Swedish streams and rivers.

title: A non‐invasive approach to measuring body dimensions of wildlife with camera traps: A felid field trial
reason: Body dimensions of feral cats are measured by hand in photo-editing software on camera trap images using a pinhole camera equation; no automated computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Flight behaviour diverges more between seasonal forms than between species in Pieris butterflies
reason: Wild-caught Pieris butterflies were filmed only inside an experimental tunnel cage for 3D flight trajectory reconstruction, and the wing morphometrics come from killed, mounted specimens. No free-ranging animals were imaged in the wild.

title: Using motion‐detection cameras to monitor foraging behaviour of individual butterflies
reason: Butterflies were reared in insectaries and recorded only inside an enclosed outdoor experimental dome. Camera-trap videos were annotated manually in Timelapse 2, with no automated computer vision.

title: Bubble blasts! An adaptation for buoyancy regulation in shallow foraging gray whales
reason: Behavioural ecology study of wild gray whales using drone footage, but behaviour annotation and photo-identification were done by hand, and length measurements by manual photogrammetry. The analysis is Bayesian statistical modelling. No computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Millisecond‐scale behaviours of plankton quantified in vitro and in situ using the Event‐based Vision Sensor
reason: Applies an event-based vision sensor with particle clustering and ML classification to plankton behaviour in lab cultures and in situ in Lake Biwa and the deep sea, where free-living organisms were recorded.

title: Using convolutional neural networks to count parrot nest‐entrances on photographs from the largest known colony of Psittaciformes
reason: Applies CNN density-map regression to count nest-entrances (direct signs) of wild Burrowing Parrots on field photographs of a cliff colony.

title: Identification of plankton habitats in the North Sea
reason: The autoencoder and HDBSCAN clustering run on gridded physical variables and VPR-derived plankton densities, not on images. The paper does no image analysis of its own.

title: An Ecologist‐Friendly R Workflow for Expediting Species‐Level Classification of Camera Trap Images
reason: Develops and tests a YOLOv8-based R workflow for species-level classification of camera trap images of wild medium and large mammals in the Apuan Alps; domestic animals (cow, dog, horse, goat/sheep) also appear as categories.

title: The Field Automatic Insect Recognition‐Device—A Non‐Lethal Semi‐Automatic Malaise Trap for Insect Biodiversity Monitoring: Proof of Concept
reason: Primary study presenting a non-lethal camera-equipped Malaise trap that records wild insects in the field and classifies the extracted video frames with the iNaturalist computer vision system.

title: Automated and repeated aerial observations of GPS ‐collared animals using UAVs and open‐source electronics
reason: The analysed footage shows a herd of domestic Exmoor ponies (Equus ferus caballus) kept on a university farm and research centre. These are domestic animals in a managed farm setting, not wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Similarity learning networks uniquely identify individuals of four marine and terrestrial species
reason: Develops a deep learning pipeline (segmentation, orientation, similarity learning) for individual re-identification of wild dolphins, seals, whales and toads from photographs taken in monitoring surveys and citizen science.

title: SNAPSHOT USA 2021: A third coordinated national camera trap survey of the U nited S tates
reason: Data paper describing a national camera trap survey dataset of mammals; no computer vision or automated image analysis method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: FishAI : Automated hierarchical marine fish image classification with vision transformer
reason: Primary study training a Vision Transformer to classify marine fish images from the WoRMS photo gallery, also tested on underwater marine life images; the paper does not state whether WoRMS photos show live wild fish or specimens.

title: Protocol to record and analyze primate leaping in three dimensions in the wild
venue: Journal of Experimental Zoology Part A Ecological and Integrative Physiology
reason: Primary protocol paper: multi-camera video of wild primates is calibrated and reconstructed in 3D (photogrammetric calibration and DLT triangulation). Point digitising is manual, so the computer vision content is limited to calibration and 3D reconstruction.

title: Covariation in the Craniocervical Junction of Carnivora
reason: 3D geometric morphometric study of museum skeletal specimens (skulls and cervical vertebrae) scanned in a collection; no images of living wild animals and no computer vision analysis beyond manual landmarking.

title: Monitoring ecological dynamics on complex hydrothermal structures: A novel photogrammetry approach reveals fine‐scale variability of vent assemblages
reason: Applies structure-from-motion photogrammetry on ROV video of wild deep-sea vent fauna (Bathymodiolus azoricus mussel assemblages) to monitor cover dynamics over time.

title: Temporal evolution of plankton and particles distribution across a mesoscale front during the spring bloom
reason: In situ images of wild marine zooplankton from a UVP6 imager on a glider are classified with a CNN-feature/Random Forest pipeline to map plankton distributions.

title: In situ observations of zooplankton show changes in abundance and swimming speed in response to hypoxia and acidification
reason: Primary study applying CNN classification and video tracking to in situ underwater video of free-living zooplankton (copepods, amphipods) in a fjord.

title: A video monitoring and computational system for estimating migratory juvenile fish abundance in river systems
reason: Primary study that trains CNN models to detect and count wild emigrating juvenile river herring in underwater video collected at a fish ladder in a river.

title: Development and use of a novel diver‐operated ski for surveying nearshore rocky reef habitats
reason: The paper describes a diver-propelled ski carrying GoPro cameras for video surveys of wild fish and invertebrates. People identified, counted and scored percent cover by hand on frame grabs. No computer vision or automated image analysis was developed or applied.

title: Beyond transfer learning: Leveraging ancillary images in automated classification of plankton
reason: CNN classification of zooplankton images; two of three image sets were acquired in situ in the ocean (wild plankton), the third is net-collected preserved samples scanned in the laboratory.

title: Modular shadowgraph imaging for zooplankton ecological studies in diverse field and mesocosm settings
reason: Develops and applies shadowgraph imaging systems with image segmentation and classification to quantify wild zooplankton in situ in shelf seas and a lake mesocosm.

title: Producing plankton classifiers that are robust to dataset shift
reason: Deep learning classifiers are developed and evaluated on in situ underwater camera images of free-living lake plankton (mainly zooplankton) from a monitoring deployment.

title: Remote 3D Imaging and Classification of Pelagic Microorganisms with A Short‐Range Multispectral Confocal LiDAR
reason: The copepods were cultured in the lab and imaged in a glass cylinder with a benchtop LiDAR, so no wild or free-ranging animals are in the data.

title: Research on marine fish classification and recognition based on an optimized ResNet50 model
reason: Classification of commercial marine fish species for sorting in fish processing (fishery production context), not monitoring of wild free-ranging animals.

title: Zero‐shot insect detection via weak language supervision
reason: Applies a zero-shot vision-language detector to citizen-science (iNaturalist) photographs of insects and releases a bounding-box-annotated insect dataset; insects are the stated subject, although the framing is agricultural/plant phenomics.

title: Using spatiotemporal information in weather radar data to detect and track communal roosts
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: CNN-based detection and tracking of wild swallow/martin (and bat) roost signatures in weather radar imagery rendered as images.

title: Estimating beluga whale abundance from space: using drones to ground‐validate VHR satellite imagery
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Beluga whales in VHR satellite and drone imagery are detected and counted manually by three human observers; no computer vision method is applied to the animals (only pansharpening/HD sharpening as image preparation).

title: UAV data and deep learning: efficient tools to map ant mounds and their ecological impact
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Primary study applying a deep learning object detector to UAV imagery to detect mounds (nests) of wild wood ants, which are direct signs of free-ranging animals.

title: Mapping emergent coral reefs: a comparison of pixel‐ and object‐based methods
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Drone RGB imagery and SfM DSM used to classify and map coral cover (corals are wild, free-ranging animals) on an emergent reef bommie, comparing pixel-based and object-based random forest models.

title: Ray bioturbation rates suggest they shape estuary processes
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Drone imagery and image analysis (photogrammetric DEMs, object-based image classification) of feeding pits, which are direct signs of wild rays in an estuary.

title: Being confident in confidence scores: calibration in deep learning models for camera trap image sequences
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Primary study evaluating calibration of deep learning species classifiers on camera trap images of wild European animals.

title: Approaching a population‐level assessment of body size in pinnipeds using drones, an early warning of environmental degradation
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Develops and applies a semi-automated drone-image method (CNN segmentation plus morphometrics) to estimate body mass of wild harbour seals; calibration and testing also use captured, dead bycaught and zoo seals.

title: Near real‐time monitoring of wading birds using uncrewed aircraft systems and computer vision
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Primary study applying a RetinaNet object detector to UAS imagery of free-ranging wading bird colonies in the Everglades for detection, species classification and counting.

title: A comparison of established and digital surface model (DSM) ‐based methods to determine population estimates and densities for king penguin colonies, using fixed‐wing drone and satellite imagery
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Primary study counting wild king penguins from drone and satellite imagery. The automated count uses filtering, thresholding and clustering on a photogrammetric DSM raster derived from the drone images. The authors themselves describe the approach as 'neither manual nor computer vision-based', so inclusion is a judgement call (alternative: E-NOCV).

title: Allometric shifts in foraging site selection and area increase energy intake for Yellowstone Cutthroat Trout but are constrained by functional limits to prey capture
venue: Transactions of the American Fisheries Society
reason: Applies stereo 3D videography (calibrated stereo video measurement with VidSync) to free-ranging Yellowstone Cutthroat Trout in natural streams, measuring body size, foraging distance and foraging rates.

title: Efficacy of remote sensing technologies for burrow count estimates of a rare kangaroo rat
reason: Analyses UAS RGB imagery and derived surface models (plus NAIP imagery) to detect burrows (direct signs) of the wild Texas kangaroo rat.

title: Evaluation of drone surveys for ungulates in southwestern rangelands
reason: Thermal drone footage and trail-camera photographs were reviewed manually by human observers for distance sampling; no computer vision method was applied to animal imagery. The deer and other ungulates live on large high-fenced rangeland sites.

title: Evaluating the performance of semiautomated photographic identification programs for leopard seals
reason: Primary study evaluating semiautomated photo-ID programs (computer vision matching) on photographs of wild leopard seals hauled out along the New Zealand coast.

title: Keeper effect: Animals are more active in the presence of their caretakers
reason: Behavioural study of zoo animals using direct observer scan sampling with the ZooMonitor app; no image or video analysis, and the animals are captive.

title: Can you dig it? The impact of a movable substrate “dig pit” on naked mole rat (Heterocephalus glaber) behavior and welfare
reason: Behavioural welfare study of a zoo-housed naked mole rat colony using direct human observation with the ZooMonitor app; no image or video analysis and only captive animals.

title: Low Cost Machine Vision for Insect Classification
venue: Lecture notes in networks and systems
reason: Primary study that develops a camera-based imaging unit for live insect traps and trains CNNs to classify 16 insect species; insects are live, pass through the trap and are left unharmed.

title: Dataset Generation and Bonobo Classification from Weakly Labelled Videos
venue: Lecture notes in networks and systems
reason: Individual identification of bonobos recorded only in their enclosure at Zoo Berlin; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Automatic Coral Detection with YOLO: A Deep Learning Approach for Efficient and Accurate Coral Reef Monitoring
venue: Communications in Computer and Information Science
reason: Applies YOLOv5 object detection to underwater images of coral colonies (wild animals) recorded on reefs during field expeditions; primary research.

title: Automatic Coral Morphotypes Detection with YOLO: A Deep Learning Approach for Efficient and Accurate Coral Reef Monitoring
venue: IFIP Advances in Information and Communication Technology
reason: Primary study applying YOLOv5 object detection to underwater images of wild coral colonies (corals are animals) taken on reef expeditions.

title: Adaptive High-Frequency Transformer for Diverse Wildlife Re-identification
reason: Proposes a transformer-based re-identification method evaluated on multiple wildlife ReID image datasets; wildlife is the stated subject. The paper does not state whether the animals in the datasets are wild or captive.

title: Insect Identification in the Wild: The AMI Dataset
reason: Presents a dataset and benchmark for fine-grained classification of wild moths. It uses images from automated insect camera traps deployed in the field and from citizen-science platforms.

title: Hierarchical Conditioning of Diffusion Models Using Tree-of-Life for Studying Species Evolution
reason: Computer vision method (phylogeny-conditioned diffusion models) that generates images of fish species from museum specimen images and of bird species from CUB-200-2011, to study evolutionary traits. The bird images show non-domestic animals, so at least part of the data is wild animals.

title: Ponymation: Learning Articulated 3D Animal Motions from Unlabeled Online Videos
reason: Computer vision method (3D reconstruction and motion generation) trained on online videos of animals. The videos include zebras and giraffes, which are wild species, alongside domestic horses and cows.

title: An Adaptive Fast-RCNN Method for Fish Monitoring: From an Artificial Environment to the Ocean
venue: Lecture notes in information systems and organisation
reason: All analysed video comes from fish kept in an artificial fish tank in a controlled environment. Testing in the ocean is only proposed as future work.

title: Underwater Object Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv5
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv5 detector for underwater benthic animals (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish) in images of the real marine environment from the URPC2020 dataset. The paper does not say whether the animals are wild or farmed. It gives fishing and aquaculture as motivation but describes the images as from the real marine environment, so the paper is coded as wild.

title: An Efficient Illumination Invariant Tiger Detection Framework for Wildlife Surveillance
venue: Lecture Notes in Networks and Systems
reason: Primary study proposing an EnlightenGAN + YOLOv8 framework for tiger detection for wildlife surveillance, evaluated on the ATRW tiger dataset; the paper does not state whether the ATRW tigers are wild or captive.

title: YOLOv7-Based Object Detection Model for Effective Aquarium
venue: Lecture notes in networks and systems
reason: Applies YOLOv7 object detection to images of marine animals kept in aquariums only; no wild free-ranging animals.

title: Exploring Crown-of-Thorns Starfish and Marine Ecology: Utilizing Deep Learning for Detection and Analysis
reason: The paper compares results that other studies reported for COTS detection on the CSIRO dataset (YOLOv5 [24], YOLOv5+TFLite [26], CNN with attention [27]). It runs no experiments of its own, so it is a comparative review rather than primary research.

title: ECO-Guard: An Integrated AI Sensor System for Monitoring Wildlife and Sustainable Forest Management
venue: Lecture notes in networks and systems
reason: IoT sensor system in which a camera module runs YOLO to detect wild animals ('beasts', birds) in forests along with people and objects. It is a primary system study. The animal image data is not described.

title: Underwater image object detection based on multi-scale feature fusion
reason: Proposes a CNN-based detector for underwater fish and marine animals. It is evaluated on web-crawled fish images and on the URPC2021 dataset, which was collected in a real marine environment.

title: Natural body size variation in seabirds provides a fundamental challenge for flight height determination by single-camera photogrammetry: a comment on Humphries et al. (2023)
reason: Comment paper critiquing a photogrammetry workflow; it analyses ringing biometric data and simulations, not image or video data.

title: Quantitative analysis of body colouration in Sebastes rockfishes
reason: The study measures body colour from web photos of fresh rockfish specimens. These are photographed specimens, not free-ranging animals imaged in the wild, so the paper is excluded under the specimen rule.

title: Applications of 3D modeling in cryptic species classification of molluscs
reason: Wild-collected bivalves were preserved in ethanol and photographed as specimens in a lab set-up for 3D modelling. Only specimens were imaged, never free-ranging animals in situ.

title: Photogrammetry reveals the depth distribution of scleractinian corals in turbid waters
reason: Applies SfM photogrammetry (image-based 3D reconstruction) to underwater images of wild scleractinian coral communities in their natural habitat.

title: Exposure to Sublethal Concentrations of Lead (Pb) Affects Ecologically Relevant Behaviors in House Sparrows (Passer domesticus)
venue: Archives of Environmental Contamination and Toxicology
reason: Wild-caught house sparrows were kept and filmed in aviaries for a toxicology study, so every analysed video shows captive birds. The video analysis is 3D reconstruction from manually digitised points in Argus.

title: Wildlife Conservation on Private Land: A Social-Ecological Systems Study
reason: Citizen-science camera-trap survey of wild mammals on private land in Tasmania. The images were also classified by a deep-learning species classifier, so computer vision is applied to wild animal images, though only as a minor part of the study. Domestic livestock were detected too, hence 'mixed'.

title: Drone-based monitoring and geomorphology of southern giant petrel nests near Palmer Station, western Antarctic Peninsula
reason: Drone RGB imagery of wild southern giant petrel nests is analysed (visual nest identification, chick survival monitoring, structure-from-motion surface models) to map and model nesting habitat; primary research on wild animals.

title: Space partitioning within groups of social coral reef fish
reason: Primary study applying deep-learning detection and video-based 3D tracking to wild damselfish filmed in situ on a coral reef.

title: A dual-branch feature fusion neural network for fish image fine-grained recognition
reason: Proposes a CNN for fine-grained fish species recognition evaluated on public fish image datasets (WildFish subset, iNaturalist fish, SEAMAPD21 reef fish), covering wild fish species.

title: How to track and segment fish without human annotations: a self-supervised deep learning approach
reason: Proposes an unsupervised computer vision method for segmenting and tracking fish in underwater videos recorded in natural estuary and coastal marine habitats.

title: Automatic identification of stone-handling behaviour in Japanese macaques using LabGym artificial intelligence
reason: Applies LabGym deep learning (detector + behaviour categoriser) to video of free-ranging Japanese macaques at Japanese study sites and monkey parks to recognise stone-handling behaviour.

title: Deep learning for automatic facial detection and recognition in Japanese macaques: illuminating social networks
reason: Primary study that trains deep learning face detection and individual recognition models on video frames of free-ranging (provisioned, habituated) Japanese macaques on Kōjima Island.

title: Machine learning-based bee recognition and tracking for advancing insect behavior research
reason: Honey bees from a managed colony recorded only in a laboratory maze and an indoor room; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: UISS-Net: Underwater Image Semantic Segmentation Network for improving boundary segmentation accuracy of underwater images
reason: Proposes a semantic segmentation network evaluated on underwater image datasets showing fish in natural marine habitats (Deep Fish, SUIM); fish are a segmented target class.

title: Site fidelity of harbor seals in Casco Bay, ME, USA using facial recognition technology: a pilot study
reason: Applies facial recognition software (SealNet) to photographs of wild harbor seals at haul-out sites to estimate site fidelity, connectivity and abundance.

title: Initial effects of the expansion and enforcement of a subtropical marine reserve on threatened shark species
reason: Ecological survey of wild sharks with baited remote underwater stereo-video; videos were annotated, counted and measured manually in EventMeasure software, with no computer vision method developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Spatial ecology and philopatric tendencies of whitespotted eagle ray, Aetobatus narinari, in Cozumel, Mexico
reason: Applies computer-aided photo-identification (I3S Spot pattern matching) to photos/videos of wild free-swimming whitespotted eagle rays to re-identify individuals and study site fidelity.

title: Automated workflows using Quantitative Colour Pattern Analysis (QCPA): a guide to batch processing and downstream data analysis
reason: Presents an image-analysis batch-processing tool (QCPA) for quantifying colour patterns of animals, demonstrated on field photographs of wild sea slugs and spiders.

title: Parallel desires: unifying local and semantic feature representations in marine species images for classification
reason: Proposes a ViT+DenseNet classifier for marine species images; the self-collected data come from aquaculture tanks, but the benchmark datasets (Croatian Fish, Blue Bot) show wild marine fish recorded by divers and an underwater robot.

title: SAWIT: A small-sized animal wild image dataset with annotations
reason: Introduces a camera-trap image dataset of wild small-sized animals with bounding-box annotations and benchmarks object detectors on it.

title: Lightweight underwater object detection based on image enhancement and multi-attention
reason: Proposes a lightweight CNN detector for underwater marine animals (echinus, starfish, scallop, holothurian, fish, crab, etc.) in real underwater images. The paper does not describe any captivity or farming.

title: Identification of plants from the convolutional neural network
reason: The paper classifies and detects plant categories (trees, palms, conifers, algae, cactus, etc.). No animal images are analysed; jellyfish are named only in the abstract and related work.

title: Improving fish image detection speed with hybrid VGG16 and darknet
reason: The only analysed dataset is snapshots from video of fish in a tank seen through public viewing windows, so all animals are captive.

title: Projector deep feature extraction-based garbage image classification model using underwater images
reason: Proposes a deep-feature classification model for underwater images that separates sea animals from garbage. Part of the data (ICRA19-Trash, YouTube) shows free-living marine animals in the field.

title: Classifying aquatic organism via evolving residual convolutional neural networks by optimized random vector functional link
reason: Proposes a CNN + optimized RVFL classifier for aquatic organism images, evaluated on Fish4Knowledge underwater fish images and underwater-related ImageNet categories; the stated application is aquatic organism monitoring.

title: Automatic measurement of fish from images using convolutional neural networks
reason: Applies Mask R-CNN segmentation and length measurement to images of wild-caught freshwater fish from the Madeira River basin, photographed at a fishing market for fisheries monitoring.

title: RETRACTED ARTICLE: An optimized deep network-based fish tracking and classification from underwater images
reason: Proposes a deep network (CbGDNet) for tracking and classifying marine animals in underwater images from the Kaggle Sea Animals dataset. It is primary computer vision research on wild marine fauna.

title: OMSACC-SGRAN: an implementation of hybrid Optimized Multi-Scale Atrous Convoluted CNN with Self Guided Residual Attention Network for fish species classification
reason: Proposes a deep learning method for fish species classification on underwater fish images, including in-situ and marine underwater imagery (DeepFish, QUT Fish).

title: Revolutionizing wildlife protection: a novel approach combining deep learning and night-time surveillance
reason: Primary study proposing GAN colourisation plus YOLO-based detection/classification of forest wildlife in web and citizen-science images (iNaturalist, Unsplash, Pexels); wildlife monitoring is the stated application. The paper does not state whether any web images show captive animals.

title: Enhanced YOLOv7 with three-dimensional attention and its application into underwater object detection
reason: Proposes YOLOv7-TA for detecting marine benthic invertebrates (sea cucumbers, sea urchins, starfish, scallops) in AUV seabed images; the paper does not say the animals are farmed, so it is included.

title: Optimized wild animal detection technique through effective features selection and classification by using convolutional gated recurrent network
reason: Proposes a deep learning pipeline (wavelet features, metaheuristic feature selection, Conv-LSTM-GRU classifier) evaluated on Snapshot Serengeti images of wild animal species.

title: Enhanced fish species classification using dynamic multilayer perceptron and transformer encoders with extra distribution data
reason: Proposes a deep learning classifier for fine-grained fish species recognition from photographs of wild-caught fish with capture locations (Taiwan Fish Database) plus iNaturalist fish images; fuses geospatial survey data.

title: Deep dive into KABR: a dataset for understanding ungulate behavior from in-situ drone video
reason: Extends statistics and video-classification benchmarks for KABR, a drone video dataset of wild giraffes and zebras recorded in situ in Kenya for behaviour recognition.

title: Advancing Wild Deer Monitoring Through UAV Thermal Imaging and Modified Faster RCNN: A Case Study in Nepal’s Chitwan National Park
reason: Develops a modified Faster R-CNN to detect wild deer in UAV thermal images captured in Chitwan National Park, Nepal.

title: Underwater target detection and embedded deployment based on lightweight YOLO_GN
reason: Proposes a lightweight YOLO-based detector for underwater marine organisms (sea cucumber, sea urchin, scallop, starfish) in the URPC underwater image dataset; primary CV method research.

title: Improving underwater camouflage object segmentation with dual-decoder attention network
reason: Proposes a CNN for segmenting camouflaged objects in underwater images and evaluates it on a new dataset of underwater camouflaged creatures (starfish, seahorses, octopuses). This is a borderline call: camouflaged object segmentation is a general vision task, but the authors built a dataset made only of underwater animals.

title: PanAf20K: A Large Video Dataset for Wild Ape Detection and Behaviour Recognition
reason: Camera trap video dataset of wild chimpanzees and gorillas with benchmarks for ape detection and behaviour recognition.

title: Learning Adaptive Spatio-Temporal Inference Transformer for Coarse-to-Fine Animal Visual Tracking: Algorithm and Benchmark
reason: Proposes a transformer tracker for animal visual tracking; evaluated on zoo videos (ZOO145) and internet animal videos (MoCA, AnimalSOT), so not only captive animals.

title: WildCLIP: Scene and Animal Attribute Retrieval from Camera Trap Data with Domain-Adapted Vision-Language Models
reason: Fine-tunes a vision-language model (CLIP) on camera-trap images of wild animals from Serengeti National Park for attribute-based image retrieval.

title: Species-Agnostic Patterned Animal Re-identification by Aggregating Deep Local Features
reason: Proposes a re-identification pipeline (ALFRE-ID) evaluated on images of wild Saimaa ringed seals and whale sharks.

title: 3D-MuPPET: 3D Multi-Pigeon Pose Estimation and Tracking
reason: Computer vision framework for 3D multi-animal pose estimation and tracking of pigeons, tested on captive indoor data and on outdoor data the paper describes as recorded in the wild.

title: Open-Vocabulary Animal Keypoint Detection with Semantic-Feature Matching
reason: Method paper on zero-shot animal keypoint (pose) detection. It is evaluated on animal keypoint datasets (MP-78, including AP-10K and AnimalWeb) that contain wild species such as giraffe, panda, cheetah and antelope, alongside humans, pets, and laboratory flies and locusts.

title: Learning to Detect Novel Species with SAM in the Wild
reason: Proposes an open-world object detection framework (novelty detection + SAM + student model) evaluated on images of wild leopards, hyenas, beluga whales, zebras and giraffes; plant experiments are a second domain.

title: A modified ResNet152v2 framework for bird species classification
venue: Innovations in Systems and Software Engineering
reason: Primary study proposing a modified ResNet152v2 CNN for image-based classification of 515 bird species, framed as support for bird conservation and monitoring. The paper does not state whether the birds in the public dataset are wild or captive, so subject type is not reported.

title: Exploring the potential application of a custom deep learning model for camera trap analysis of local urban species
reason: Fine-tunes and evaluates an object detection model on camera-trap images of free-ranging urban wildlife (birds and mammals, plus cats) in South Korea.

title: A lightweight YOLOv8 integrating FasterNet for real-time underwater object detection
reason: Proposes a lightweight YOLOv8-based detector for underwater marine organisms (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish, fish, turtle, jellyfish etc.) evaluated on underwater image datasets.

title: IoT-based real-time object detection system for crop protection and agriculture field security
reason: Primary study applying a YOLOv8-based detector in an IoT system to detect animals and humans intruding into farm fields. Trained classes include wild taxa (elephant, bear, giraffe, zebra, bird) alongside domestic animals and people; the origin of the training images is not stated, and the field test shown involves people on a cricket ground, so inclusion is borderline.

title: BN-YOLO: a lightweight method for bird’s nest detection on transmission lines
reason: Proposes a YOLO-based detector for bird nests (direct signs of wild birds) on transmission line towers in UAV inspection images.

title: Real-time detection of small underwater organisms with a novel lightweight SFESI-YOLOv8n model
reason: Proposes a lightweight YOLOv8n-based detector for small marine organisms (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish) in underwater images collected from real marine environments.

title: MCR-YOLO model for underwater target detection based on multi-color spatial features
reason: Proposes a CNN-based detector for underwater marine animals (echinus, holothurian, scallop, starfish) in seabed images from public underwater datasets.

title: Underwater Image Classification Based on EfficientnetB0 and Two-Hidden-Layer Random Vector Functional Link
venue: Journal of Ocean University of China
reason: Proposes a CNN-based classifier (EfficientnetB0-TRVFL) for underwater images of marine organisms (coral reef benthos and fish). The paper does not describe where the images came from, so whether the animals are wild is not reported.

title: Feature-adaptive FPN with multiscale context integration for underwater object detection
reason: Proposes a deep-learning detector for marine animals (echinus, holothurian, starfish, scallop) in underwater images, aimed at marine biology applications. The paper does not say whether the animals were wild or farmed.

title: Mustelid mugshots: photographing facial masks of European polecats (Mustela putorius) for individual recognition and density estimation using camera traps
reason: Camera-trap study of wild European polecats. Borderline inclusion: the only computer vision element is the I3S contour pattern-matching software, which was applied to the field images for individual identification, found to fail, and replaced by manual identification.

title: Estimating body condition of Apennine brown bears using subjective scoring based on camera trap photographs
reason: Wild brown bears in camera trap photos, but body condition is scored visually by people and measured manually in TPSDig. No automated computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Population density and activity of the Gobi bear
reason: Camera-trap ecology study of wild Gobi bears; individuals were identified manually by an author and the images were analysed with statistical spatial capture-recapture and activity models. No computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Improved Yolov7 Tiny with Global Attention Mechanism for Camouflage Object Detection
venue: Journal of The Institution of Engineers (India) Series B
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv7-tiny detector for camouflaged animals, evaluated on the MoCA video dataset of camouflaged animals (arctic fox, desert fox, scorpionfish, etc.) collected from YouTube. Wildlife is the stated subject of the data.

title: Marine Ecosystem Monitoring Based on Remote Sensing Using Underwater Image Analysis for Biodiversity Conservation Model
venue: Remote Sensing in Earth Systems Sciences
reason: Proposes a machine-learning method (GSGNN + MPBN) to classify underwater images for marine biodiversity monitoring. It is evaluated on underwater datasets that contain fish and coral reefs, so the data show free-ranging marine animals. This is a borderline case: the datasets are general underwater image benchmarks.

title: Marine Ecosystem Monitoring: Applying Remote Sensing and AI to Track and Predict Coral Reef Health
venue: Remote Sensing in Earth Systems Sciences
reason: Applies a CNN-SVM hybrid to images of coral reefs (wild corals) from CoralNet and MCR LTER to classify coral health states.

title: Marine Life Analysis Based on Ocean Water Level Rise and Climate Change Using Underwater Imaging Techniques
venue: Remote Sensing in Earth Systems Sciences
reason: Proposes segmentation and classification of underwater images of marine life (corals, fish, marine animals) from benthic and SeaCLEF datasets; primary research with wild marine animals.

title: Food Security Based Marine Life Ecosystem for Polar Region Conditioning: Remote Sensing Analysis with Machine Learning Model
venue: Remote Sensing in Earth Systems Sciences
reason: The paper proposes a generic segmentation/classification pipeline and tests it on general underwater image datasets (synthetic SUEI, SUIM, OUC-VISION, UIEB). Wild animals are not the stated subject being analysed. Fish only show up as classes or scene content.

title: Enhancing Underwater Object Detection: Leveraging YOLOv8m for Improved Subaquatic Monitoring
reason: Applies YOLOv8m detection to underwater images of aquatic animals (fish, sharks, stingrays, jellyfish, penguins, puffins, starfish) for subaquatic and marine monitoring. The paper never says whether the animals are wild or captive, so the stated monitoring use was taken as the basis for inclusion.

title: Bear biometrics: developing an individual recognition technique for sloth bears
reason: Individual identification of sloth bears from chestmark images, all taken in ex-situ bear rescue facilities; no wild or free-ranging animals in the data.

title: New ecological knowledge of the bubblegum coral Paragorgia arborea (L. 1758) using computer vision
reason: Deep-learning image analysis (branch detection and diameter regression, polyp activity) of a wild cold-water coral colony photographed in situ by a seafloor observatory camera.

title: Duet of ViT and CNN: multi-scale dual-branch network for fine-grained image classification of marine organisms
reason: Proposes a ViT-CNN dual-branch network for fine-grained classification of images of marine organisms, including wild fish and shark species from public datasets.

title: Beyond texture: unveiling spiny crown-of-thorns starfish with multiresolution analysis
reason: Proposes a wavelet + GLCP texture feature and XGBoost pipeline that classifies underwater reef images as containing wild crown-of-thorns starfish or not.

title: Nightly space use of African ungulates in zoos
reason: Deep-learning video analysis of African ungulates in zoo indoor stables only; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Pretrained U-Net: in-depth analysis of binary image segmentation in underwater marine environment
venue: Machine learning for computational science and engineering
reason: Generic binary foreground/background segmentation of underwater scenes (ruins, statues, wrecks, divers, animals). Animals are only some of the foreground objects in a general underwater dataset, and wildlife is not the stated subject.

title: MarineYOLO: Innovative deep learning method for small target detection in underwater environments
reason: Proposes a YOLOv8-based detector for marine organisms (sea cucumbers, sea urchins, starfish, scallops, fish, corals) in underwater images; the stated application is marine biology research and conservation.

title: Males with high levels of oxidative damage form weak pair bonds in a gregarious bird species
reason: Behavioural physiology study on captive-bred zebra finches kept in aviaries; automated barcode tag tracking from images is used, but no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Growing into it: evidence of an ontogenetic shift in grey whale use of foraging tactics
reason: Wild grey whales filmed by drone, but behaviours were annotated manually in BORIS and body measurements were made by manual photogrammetry; the analysis is statistical regression, with no computer vision method applied to the animal images.

title: Geographical variation in signals and responses: individual identity signals linked with capacity for individual face learning across Polistes fuscatus wasp populations
reason: Wild-collected wasps were euthanized and photographed under a laboratory microscope; image analysis (alignment, colour segmentation, eigenfaces) quantifies facial pattern variation of specimens in a lab set-up, not free-ranging animals in the field.

title: The impact of enriched housing on the behaviour and welfare of captive leopard geckos (Eublepharis macularius)
reason: Behavioural welfare study of six captive leopard geckos. People coded the videos by hand with an ethogram in BORIS, so no computer vision method was used. The animals are also captive only.

title: Enhanced marine fish small sample image recognition with RVFL in Faster R-CNN model
reason: Proposes an RVFL-enhanced Faster R-CNN for detecting and recognising marine fish (clownfish, butterflyfish) in web-sourced images, with marine monitoring and conservation as the stated application. The paper does not say whether the fish were wild or captive.

title: YOLO-based marine organism detection using two-terminal attention mechanism and difficult-sample resampling
reason: Proposes a YOLO-based detector for marine organisms (sea urchins, sea cucumbers, scallops, starfish, fish, turtles, jellyfish, etc.) in underwater images from the URPC and RUOD datasets.

title: Development of a cost-efficient automated wildlife camera network in a European Natura 2000 site
reason: Primary study that deploys a camera-trap network in a Dutch dune nature reserve and tests a deep learning model for species identification on images of wild mammals.

title: Bimodal distribution of inter-individual distance in free-ranging narrow-ridged finless porpoises
reason: Drone video of wild narrow-ridged finless porpoises analysed by image-based photogrammetry (calibrated camera, pixel-based inter-individual distance measurement in MATLAB) to study social organisation.

title: Comparison of Transformers with LSTM for classification of the behavioural time budget in horses based on video data
reason: Behaviour classification of domestic horses housed in individual pens at a veterinary clinic; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Response mechanism of rodent burrow density to natural environmental factors in desert areas based on multisource data
reason: UAV images of wild rodent burrows were interpreted manually by people. No computer vision method is applied to the images; the modelling (Boruta, BRT) works on environmental factors.

title: 3D detection of flying insects from a millimeter-wave radar imaging system
reason: Radar imaging tracking of tagged bumblebees from commercial hives confined in experimental flight cages; no wild or free-ranging animals in the data.

title: A point-based method for identification and counting of tiny object insects in cotton fields
reason: Identifies and counts crop pest insects caught on yellow sticky traps in a cotton field. This is crop pest monitoring in agricultural production, which falls under E-AGRI.

title: Online_XKD: An online knowledge distillation model for underwater object detection
reason: Proposes a knowledge distillation detector for underwater marine organisms (sea urchins, sea cucumbers, starfish, scallops) using images taken on a real seabed (URPC2020).

title: Directional swimming patterns in jellyfish aggregations
reason: Primary study applying image-analysis (blob detection, tracking, thresholding/ellipse fitting) to drone videos of wild jellyfish aggregations at sea to study swimming behaviour.

title: A dataset of ground-dwelling nocturnal fauna for object detection and classification.
reason: Data paper presenting an annotated field image dataset of free-ranging ground-dwelling nocturnal fauna (carabids, mice, shrews, slugs, worms, opilions) in field plots, for deep-learning detection and classification.

title: Dataset for herding and predator detection with the use of robots
reason: Data article presenting a precision-livestock-farming dataset dominated by sheep flocks on farms and grazing fields; the only non-domestic animals are wolves kept in semi-freedom at a wolf centre, so no wild free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Underwater image classification based on image enhancement and information quality evaluation
reason: Proposes denoising and image quality screening to improve CNN classification of underwater marine animals (fish, sea cucumbers, sea urchins, scallops, starfish) from an ocean detection dataset.

title: Underwater target detection network based on differential routing assistance and bilateral attention synergy
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for underwater marine invertebrates (holothurian, echinus, starfish, scallop) in seabed images from the URPC datasets. The paper does not say whether the animals are wild or farmed, but the scenes show natural seabed, with targets hidden by rocks.

title: Jellyfish detection algorithm based on multi-gradient flow feature fusion
