reason: Proposes a YOLOv5-based detector for jellyfish in underwater images. The data come from web crawling and the authors' own fieldwork in the Qinhuangdao sea area.

title: Inferring benthic megafaunal sediment reworking activity in relation to bottom water oxygen in Barkley Canyon, NE Pacific from video and acoustic imaging analysis
venue: Deep Sea Research Part I Oceanographic Research Papers
reason: Applies image analysis (automated thresholding and feature counting in ImageJ on rotary sonar images of biogenic pits) together with video analysis of wild deep-sea benthic megafauna and their traces at a cabled observatory.

title: Biomass mapping of fjordic cold-water coral reefs reveals distinct functional role of vertical wall habitat
venue: Deep Sea Research Part I Oceanographic Research Papers
reason: Wild cold-water coral reef fauna were filmed by ROV, but the images were annotated by hand: species areas were colour-coded manually in Photoshop and the pixel area was then calculated. Machine learning (random forest, maximum-likelihood classification) runs only on terrain data and biomass values, not on images. No computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Fine-scale variability in habitat selection and niche differentiation between sponges and cold-water corals on vertical walls of the Charlie-Gibbs Fracture Zone
venue: Deep Sea Research Part II Topical Studies in Oceanography
reason: Structure-from-motion photogrammetry on ROV video of wild deep-sea corals and sponges, used to geotag organisms and study their habitat selection.

title: Automatic detection of stereotypical behaviors of captive wild animals based on surveillance videos of zoos and animal reserves
reason: Tracks and recognises stereotypical behaviour of captive animals in zoos and reserves using internet and zoo-documentary videos; no free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Object classification and visualization with edge artificial intelligence for a customized camera trap platform
reason: Primary study applying transfer-learned DNN classifiers and XAI to wildlife images, including a field camera-trap dataset of free-ranging animals from Florida; the camera-trap data also contains a domestic dog class.

title: Benchmarking wild bird detection in complex forest scenes
reason: The paper benchmarks deep-learning object detectors on camera-trap video frames of 15 wild bird species from a national park in China.

title: Marine zoobenthos recognition algorithm based on improved lightweight YOLOv5
reason: Detects farmed sea cucumbers, sea urchins and scallops in images from an open-sea aquaculture farm (AUDD). The animals are framed as aquaculture products, so this counts as aquaculture.

title: Toward an artificial intelligence-assisted counting of sharks on baited video
reason: Deep learning detection, species identification and MaxN counting of wild reef sharks on baited remote underwater videos recorded on New Caledonian reefs.

title: Bird species recognition using transfer learning with a hybrid hyperparameter optimization scheme (HHOS)
reason: Applies CNN transfer learning with hyperparameter optimization to classify bird species from images (CUB-200-2011), with conservation/ornithology motivation.

title: STARdbi: A pipeline and database for insect monitoring based on automated image analysis
reason: Pipeline applying object detection and classification to scanned sticky-trap images of field-caught flying insects, including wild insect communities in orchards and semi-natural shrubland; some data from grain stores and lab-reared insectary cages.

title: A systematic study on transfer learning: Automatically identifying empty camera trap images using deep convolutional neural networks
reason: Deep CNN transfer learning to identify empty vs. animal camera trap images of wild animals (Snapshot Serengeti and Lasha Mountain).

title: WildARe-YOLO: A lightweight and efficient wild animal recognition model
reason: Proposes a lightweight YOLOv5s-based detector for recognizing endangered wild animals (rhino, elephant, lion, cheetah, giraffe, zebra). It is also tested on a fish market dataset and on MS COCO, which includes domestic animal classes.

title: A reliable unmanned aerial vehicle multi-target tracking system with global motion compensation for monitoring Procapra przewalskii
reason: Proposes a UAV multi-object tracking system (YOLOv7 + improved Deep SORT with global motion compensation) applied to video of wild Procapra przewalskii at Qinghai Lake.

title: Monitoring vegetation patterns and their drivers to infer resilience: Automated detection of vegetation and megaherbivores from drone imagery using deep learning
reason: Applies deep learning object detection (DETR) to drone imagery to detect wild green turtles grazing in a seagrass meadow, alongside semantic segmentation of vegetation.

title: Machine learning for non-experts: A more accessible and simpler approach to automatic benthic habitat classification
reason: The paper classifies whole seabed images into broad benthic habitat classes (soft substrate, hard substrate, reef). The subject is habitat type, not the animals. Coral reef is only one of three habitat categories.

title: Evaluating error sources to improve precision in the co-registration of underwater 3D models
reason: Primary study using underwater structure-from-motion 3D reconstruction (computer vision) of wild coral reef plots on the Great Barrier Reef. The aim is to evaluate co-registration error for detecting change such as coral growth. Corals are wild animals, which is why I included it; this is borderline, because the focus is reef 3D structure and E-PLANT (habitat only) would also be defensible.

title: UAV equipped with infrared imaging for Cervidae monitoring: Improving detection accuracy by eliminating background information interference
reason: Proposes a two-stage CV pipeline (YOLOv7 + CA-Hybrid) to detect and classify wild Cervidae in UAV thermal images from national nature reserves.

title: Enhancing endangered species monitoring by lowering data entry requirements with imputation techniques as a preprocessing step for the footprint identification technology (FIT)
reason: The study runs missing-value imputation and discriminant analysis on tables of morphometric measurements. These measurements come from landmarks that experts placed by hand on footprint images. There is no automated image analysis.

title: Will artificial intelligence revolutionize aerial surveys? A first large-scale semi-automated survey of African wildlife using oblique imagery and deep learning
reason: Semi-automated deep learning detection and counting of wild African mammals in oblique aerial survey images of Comoé National Park.

title: Real-time underwater object detection technology for complex underwater environments based on deep learning
reason: Proposes a deep learning detector for marine organisms (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish, etc.) in real underwater images. Part of the data shows free-ranging marine animals, and the UDD dataset comes from open-sea farms.

title: Multi-species identification and number counting of fish passing through fishway at hydropower stations with LigTraNet
reason: Detection, tracking and counting of wild fish migrating through a real fishway at a hydropower station using underwater video and deep learning.

title: Adaptive image processing embedding to make the ecological tasks of deep learning more robust on camera traps images
reason: Proposes an adaptive image processing module integrated with YOLO-based detection for wildlife in camera trap images (NACTI).

title: Using machine learning to count Antarctic shag (Leucocarbo bransfieldensis) nests on images captured by remotely piloted aircraft systems
reason: Object detection model applied to RPAS orthomosaics to detect and count nests of wild Antarctic shags at breeding colonies.

title: Drone imagery and deep learning for mapping the density of wild Pacific oysters to manage their expansion into protected areas
reason: Applies CNN object detection to drone imagery of wild, invasive Pacific oysters on intertidal mudflats and rocky shores to detect, count and map their density.

title: Trajectory-based fish event classification through pre-training with diffusion models
reason: Deep learning classification of behaviour events from trajectories of wild nesting male corkwing wrasse, extracted with a detector and tracker from natural underwater videos.

title: Ant-observer: A new approach for automatic acquisition and autonomous analyses of individual species abundance and interactions
reason: Develops software that analyses field videos of wild ants at bait stations in Hong Kong, using object detection and line-crossing counting.

title: CEH-YOLO: A composite enhanced YOLO-based model for underwater object detection
reason: Proposes a YOLOv8-based detector for underwater marine organisms (echinus, holothurian, scallop, starfish, marine life) in underwater imagery; primary method research with wildlife-related application.

title: Automated species classification and counting by deep-sea mobile crawler platforms using YOLO
reason: Applies YOLOv8 to video from a deep-sea benthic crawler to detect, classify and count wild deep-sea fish at Barkley Canyon.

title: YOLO-SAG: An improved wildlife object detection algorithm based on YOLOv8n
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv8n object detector for wildlife images from documentaries, the internet and open camera-trap datasets (Snapshot Serengeti, Saola Working Group).

title: A joint time and spatial attention-based transformer approach for recognizing the behaviors of wild giant pandas
reason: Proposes a transformer for behaviour recognition in camera-trap videos of wild giant pandas in Wolong Nature Reserve.

title: Metadata augmented deep neural networks for wild animal classification
reason: Deep learning classification of camera-trap images of wild Norwegian animals (with some farm animals) using image and metadata fusion.

title: Reliable and efficient integration of AI into camera traps for smart wildlife monitoring based on continual learning
reason: Develops and field-tests an on-device CNN pipeline with continual learning for blank filtering of camera-trap images from a Spanish natural park (feral cats, foxes, martens, wild pigs, dogs) and Snapshot Serengeti.

title: Automated long-term monitoring of stereotypical movement in polar bears under human care using machine learning
reason: Computer vision tracking, identification and stereotypy classification of two polar bears kept in zoo enclosures; no wild or free-ranging animals in the data.

title: Discrimination between the facial gestures of vocalising and non-vocalising lemurs and small apes using deep learning
reason: Pose estimation on video of wild lemurs in Madagascar and captive gibbons, with classification of vocalising and non-vocalising facial gestures; part of the data shows wild animals.

title: Enhanced Yolov8 network with Extended Kalman Filter for wildlife detection and tracking in complex environments
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv8n detector with Extended Kalman Filter tracking for wildlife images and video collected from the web.

title: A deep learning pipeline for time-lapse camera monitoring of insects and their floral environments
reason: Deep learning pipeline detecting and classifying wild arthropods visiting Sedum plots in time-lapse insect camera trap images recorded outdoors in Denmark.

title: Efficient dual-stream neural networks: A modeling approach for inferring wild mammal behavior from video data
reason: Proposes a dual-stream CNN for recognising behaviour of wild mammals from video clips in a dataset derived from Animal Kingdom.

title: Bottlenose dolphin identification using synthetic image-based transfer learning
reason: Develops a deep-learning photo-ID pipeline (detection, keypoint extraction, triplet network) for individual identification of wild Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins photographed around Jeju Island.

title: Conservation in action: Cost-effective UAVs and real-time detection of the globally threatened swamp deer (Rucervus duvaucelii)
reason: Applies deep learning object detectors to UAV and handheld camera images of wild swamp deer in Hastinapur Wildlife Sanctuary for detection and counting.

title: SCoralDet: Efficient real-time underwater soft coral detection with YOLO
reason: Soft coral detection images come from a coral conservation and breeding center (captive). The generalisation dataset UTDAC2020 is not described as showing wild animals, so no part of the data clearly shows wild, free-ranging animals.

title: HuBot: A biomimicking mobile robot for non-disruptive bird behavior study
reason: Computer vision (detection, segmentation, depth estimation) on images of Houbara bustards, a non-domestic species of conservation concern. The detection dataset includes camera-trap and online images, which presumably show wild birds; the live robot trials used captive birds.

title: Automated skin lesion detection and prevalence estimation in Tamanend's bottlenose dolphins
reason: Trains YOLOv5 object detection models on boat-survey photographs of wild, free-ranging Tamanend's bottlenose dolphins to detect skin lesions and estimate lesion prevalence.

title: DeLoCo: Decoupled location context-guided framework for wildlife species classification using camera trap images
reason: Proposes a deep learning framework for species classification of camera trap images of wildlife (IWildCam, TerraInc). TerraInc also contains cat and dog classes, so the subject type is mixed.

title: Towards a fully automated underwater census for fish assemblages in the Mediterranean Sea
reason: Deep learning detection of wild Mediterranean fish species in diver-operated videos of underwater transects for biodiversity census.

title: Hierarchical deep learning framework for automated marine vegetation and fauna analysis using ROV video data
reason: Computer vision (instance segmentation and hierarchical classification) on ROV video of wild marine vegetation and fauna (bivalves, sea stars, hagfish) in a Norwegian fjord.

title: Machine vision approach for monitoring and quantifying fish school migration
reason: Proposes DVE-YOLO for detecting, counting and identifying migration of wild freshwater fish in a river, filmed by stationary cameras at a dam.

title: Remotely sensed spectral variability predicts reef fish diversity
reason: Images (WorldView-2 satellite, UAV FluidCam) show benthic reef habitat only; their spectral variability is correlated with fish diversity counted by SCUBA divers. No animals are analysed in the images, so this is a habitat-only image analysis.

title: Towards transparency in AI: Explainable bird species image classification for ecological research
reason: Applies deep learning and LIME explainability to classify bird species from images of birds in their natural environment (CUB 200-2011), framed as an ecological research application.

title: Exploring the potential of aerial drone imagery to distinguish breeding Adélie (Pygoscelis adeliae), chinstrap (Pygoscelis antarcticus) and gentoo (Pygoscelis papua) penguins in Antarctica
reason: Analyses drone images and orthomosaics of wild breeding penguin colonies in Antarctica. Species are told apart by image-derived features: pixel brightness in CIELAB, measured body length, nearest-neighbour spacing of individuals, and guano appearance. Much of the interpretation is manual, which makes inclusion borderline, but image analysis is performed.

title: Extreme capital breeding for giants: Effects of body size on humpback whale energy expenditure and fasting endurance
reason: Primary study that uses UAV aerial photogrammetry (body length and widths measured in pixels on images) and UAV video of wild humpback whales off Western Australia to inform a bioenergetic model.

title: A comparison of the behavioural responses of fishes to a remotely operated vehicle and diver-based stereo-video sampling
reason: Wild reef fish were filmed with stereo-video from divers and an ROV, but people identified and measured the fish by hand in EventMeasure software and the analysis is statistical. No automated computer vision method is developed or evaluated.

title: Baited rather than unbaited stereo-video provides robust metrics to assess demersal fish assemblages across deeper coastal shelf marine parks
reason: Wild demersal fish are filmed with baited and unbaited stereo-video, but all video analysis is manual annotation in EventMeasure (MaxN counts and length measurements). The paper develops or applies no computer vision method.

title: Visualization of humpback whale tracking on edge device using space-borne remote sensing data for Indian Ocean
venue: The Egyptian Journal of Remote Sensing and Space Science
reason: Deep learning segmentation, detection, classification and tracking of wild humpback whales in very high resolution satellite imagery.

title: PE-Transformer: Path enhanced transformer for improving underwater object detection
reason: Proposes a transformer detector for underwater objects, evaluated mainly on marine organism datasets (UTDAC, RUOD) showing echinus, starfish, holothurians, scallops, fish, turtles and jellyfish. The paper never says whether these animals are wild or farmed; they were coded as free-ranging marine organisms. A borderline E-GENERIC case.

title: Fractional stock exchange trading optimization trained deep learning for wild animal detection with WMSN data communication in IoT environment
reason: Proposes a deep CNN (tuned by FSETO optimization) to detect wild animals in images within an IoT-WMSN framework, evaluated on a public wild animal image dataset.

title: CATNet: Cascaded attention transformer network for marine species image classification
reason: Proposes a deep learning classifier for underwater images of marine species (fish, turtles, corals, sea urchins, etc.) in natural marine settings.

title: FBDPN: CNN-Transformer hybrid feature boosting and differential pyramid network for underwater object detection
reason: Proposes a CNN-Transformer detector for underwater object detection, tested on images of marine animals (URPC2020 holothurians, starfish, scallops, echinus) and the Aquarium dataset (fish, penguins, sharks etc.). The marine animals appear to be free-ranging, though the paper never says where the images were taken. The Aquarium images likely show captive animals, so subject_type is 'mixed'.

title: Self-supervised domain feature mining for underwater domain generalization object detection
reason: Proposes a domain-generalization object detector for underwater images of marine invertebrates (echinus, starfish, holothurian, scallop) on the S-UODAC dataset; computer vision with animals as detection targets.

title: Underwater image segmentation via the progressive network of dual iterative complement enhancement
reason: Proposes a deep learning segmentation method for underwater images, evaluated on several datasets of marine animals, including marine animal segmentation datasets and dolphin images, alongside general underwater scenes.

title: Unlocking the power of artificial intelligence for pangolin protection: Revolutionizing wildlife conservation with enhanced deep learning models
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv8 detector for pangolins using iNaturalist/web images of wild pangolins, plus public wildlife datasets; primary CV research.

title: Length estimation of fish detected as non-occluded using a smartphone application and deep learning method
reason: Deep learning (Mask R-CNN) on images of wild-caught fish in landed catch to estimate length for stock assessment; this is capture fisheries, not aquaculture.

title: YOLOv7-DCN-SORT: An algorithm for detecting and counting targets on Acetes fishing vessel operation
reason: Detects and counts fishing-operation objects on a vessel (anchors, catch baskets, nets) to monitor fishing activity. The subject is the human fishing operation, not the animals themselves.

title: Fishing event detection and species classification using computer vision and artificial intelligence for electronic monitoring
reason: Computer vision (detection, tracking, species classification) on electronic monitoring video of wild-caught fish (tunas, billfish, sharks) on commercial longline vessels; capture fishery, not aquaculture.

title: A digital twin-based energy-efficient wireless multimedia sensor network for waterbirds monitoring
reason: Waterbirds are recognised only from audio (MFCC + DTW). Images are only compressed, transmitted and scored for quality with BRISQUE inside a simulated sensor network; no vision analysis is done on the animals.

title: Aerial photography and machine learning for estimating extremely high flamingo numbers on the Makgadikgadi Pans, Botswana
reason: Applies semi-supervised machine learning (random forest pixel classification) to aerial photographs to count wild flamingos on Sua Pan, Botswana.

title: Dog invasions in protected areas: A case study using camera trapping, citizen science and artificial intelligence
reason: Applies a CNN classifier (plus citizen science) to camera-trap images from a national park to detect free-roaming domestic dogs among wild mammals; data shows wild and domestic free-ranging animals.

title: Blender as a tool for palaeoichnological research: Case study from Lark Quarry
reason: Study digitises fossil dinosaur tracks (palaeontological specimens) by photogrammetry and Blender. There are no living wild animals in the data, so it is closest to the museum-specimen exclusion.

title: MTD-YOLOv5: Enhancing marine target detection with multi-scale feature fusion in YOLOv5 model
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv5 detector for fish in underwater images, evaluated on a dataset built from Labeled Fishes in the Wild, underwater video key frames and WildFish.

title: Enhanced deep learning models for automatic fish species identification in underwater imagery
reason: Proposes deep learning detection and classification of fish species in underwater images of the Taiwanese coast (Fish4Knowledge), i.e. wild marine fish.

title: A generalized machine learning model for long-term coral reef monitoring in the Red Sea
reason: Per-pixel classification of benthic coral cover from 30 m Landsat imagery: habitat/benthic cover mapping and change detection, not image analysis of individual animals.

title: RETRACTED: MobVGG: Ensemble technique for birds and drones prediction
reason: Proposes a CNN ensemble that classifies images of flying birds versus drones. The birds are free-flying, and the stated applications include automated bird surveys. The paper does not say outright that the birds are wild.

title: U-ATSS: A lightweight and accurate one-stage underwater object detection network
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for marine organisms (echinus, holothurian, scallop, starfish) in real underwater images captured by underwater robots; primary method research.

title: Do the best of all together: Hierarchical spatial-frequency fusion transformers for animal re-identification
reason: Proposes a transformer-based re-identification method and evaluates it on animal image datasets, including wild animals (zebra, humpback whale, Amur tiger, panda, elephants), plus lab and domestic animals (fruit fly, yak, honeybee).

title: ConvFishNet: An efficient backbone for fish classification from composited underwater images
reason: Proposes a CNN for fish species classification evaluated on wild fish images (WildFish web images and Fish4Knowledge underwater footage from Taiwan).

title: Lidar as a potential tool for monitoring migratory insects
reason: Field Scheimpflug lidar with a CMOS line camera records free-flying wild insects in southern Sweden. The echo signals are thresholded to detect and count insects, estimate their size and velocity, and tell moths apart from other insects.

title: Advancing sun glint correction in high-resolution marine UAV RGB imagery for coral reef monitoring
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
reason: Computer vision pipeline (sun glint segmentation and restoration) on UAV RGB imagery of wild coral reefs in Moorea, with downstream coral semantic segmentation; corals are wild animals.

title: Variational Autoencoder with Gaussian Random Field prior: Application to unsupervised animal detection in aerial images
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
reason: Proposes a VAE with Gaussian Random Field prior for unsupervised animal detection in aerial images; evaluated on a domestic livestock dataset and on the Semmacape dataset of wild birds and dolphins at sea.

title: Satellite remote sensing and bathymetry co-driven deep neural network for coral reef shallow water benthic habitat classification
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
reason: Satellite-based benthic habitat mapping (coral, sand, rubble, background) of coral reefs; habitat/land-cover classification, not analysis of individual animals.

title: Assessing topographic features and population abundance in an Antarctic penguin colony through UAV-based deep-learning models
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
reason: Applies YOLOv8 object detection to UAV orthomosaic imagery of a wild chinstrap penguin colony in Antarctica to count adults and chicks.

title: Development of a coral and competitive alga-related index using historical multi-spectral satellite imagery to assess ecological status of coral reefs
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
reason: Proposes a satellite-image index (NRGI) to segment live-coral and competitive-alga growth zones on wild coral reefs in the South China Sea; corals are wild animals and the main subject.

title: Life history and early ontogeny determine vertical swimming behaviors in the larvae of Caribbean corals
venue: Journal of Experimental Marine Biology and Ecology
reason: Coral larvae were filmed and tracked with computer vision in laboratory aquarium observation systems; no free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: A standardized protocol for assessing the performance of automatic detection systems used in onshore wind power plants to reduce avian mortality
reason: Proposes a field protocol for assessing automatic detection systems at wind farms using human observers with laser rangefinders. The authors analyse no images or video themselves and report no ADS performance results.

title: Self-attention and long-range relationship capture network for underwater object detection
venue: Journal of King Saud University - Computer and Information Sciences
reason: Proposes a CNN-based detector for marine organisms in underwater images. The data include URPC images taken in natural underwater environments (wild marine invertebrates) and Aquarium images (captive animals), plus MS COCO as a generalisation test.

title: Photoidentification as a potential tool for individual recognition of Dendropsophus elegans (Anura: Hylidae)
reason: Wild frogs captured in the field are photographed, and individuals are recognised with software (Wild ID, which uses SIFT features) and compared with manual photo-ID and elastomer marks.

title: GLIC: Underwater target detection based on global–local information coupling and multi-scale feature fusion
venue: Journal of Visual Communication and Image Representation
reason: Proposes a CNN-transformer detector for underwater marine organisms (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish) evaluated on URPC and UDD underwater images. URPC capture context is not stated; UDD comes from an open-sea farm.

title: Blubber gene expression and cortisol concentrations reveal changing physiological stress in a Southern ocean sentinel species
reason: The study is about blubber gene expression and hormone assays in wild humpback whales. UAV photogrammetry is only used to take length and width measurements for a body condition index, and no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Improved research on coral bleaching detection model based on FCOS model
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for coral bleaching on underwater images of coral reefs (wild animals), with ROV-captured and public coral images.

title: Decoding intertidal oyster reef morphology: Insights from UAV photogrammetry and deep learning
reason: The study maps the shape of intertidal oyster reefs (footprint, height, fragmentation) from UAV orthoimages, treating it as land-cover classification. The reefs are mostly covered in sediment and carry hardly any living oysters, so this is habitat-structure mapping rather than vision on animals.

title: HD-YOLO: The hydroid of aurelia detector
reason: Proposes a YOLOv7-based detector for Aurelia hydroids. The data mix wild hydroids photographed undersea at a pier with lab-cultured and web images.

title: Feasibility study of UAV based ecological monitoring and habitat assessment of cervids in the floating meadows of Keibul Lamjao National Park in Manipur, India
reason: UAV feasibility study on wild deer; animals were detected by observers viewing RGB/thermal imagery live and through binoculars, not by a computer vision method. The only automated image analysis (SfM orthomosaics, PCA, Random Forest burnt-area classification) is applied to habitat, not animals.

title: ADD-YOLO: An algorithm for detecting animals in outdoor environments based on unmanned aerial imagery
reason: Proposes a YOLOv8-based detector for animals in UAV imagery. The data include livestock (cattle, sheep) and wild animals (wild animals in wilderness terrain; kiang and seal in WAID).

title: Coordinate-Aware Mask R-CNN with Group Normalization: A underwater marine animal instance segmentation framework
reason: Proposes an instance segmentation method for wild marine animals (fish, squid, jellies, decapods) in underwater images collected during commercial trawl deployments in the North Sea.

title: Intelligent marine detection based on spectral imaging and neural network modeling
reason: Underwater hyperspectral imaging system deployed in the sea near Weizhou Island to image wild seabed corals; neural networks classify the hyperspectral data (coral body, coral tip, water).

title: Coverage estimation of benthic habitat features by semantic segmentation of underwater imagery from South-eastern Baltic reefs using deep learning models
reason: Deep learning semantic segmentation of underwater video of wild benthic reef features, including blue mussel Mytilus edulis trossulus coverage, in the SE Baltic Sea.

title: Enhancing green sea turtle (Chelonia mydas) conservation for tourists at Little Liuqiu island, Taiwan: Application of deep learning algorithms
reason: Applies YOLO object detection to UAV, underwater and social media images of wild green sea turtles at Little Liuqiu Island.

title: Low-cost real-time aerial object detection and GPS location tracking pipeline
venue: ISPRS Open Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
reason: The paper detects and geolocates vehicles (cars, trucks, buses) in UAV imagery. No animals appear in the analysed data.

title: Autofocusing method for multifocal holograms based on connected domain analysis
reason: Autofocusing algorithm for in-line holographic microscopy of plankton samples imaged in a cuvette in a laboratory optical set-up; a microscopy/lab imaging study, though some samples are field-collected seawater.

title: Internal scanning hyperspectral imaging system for deep sea target detection
reason: Hardware/optics paper on an underwater hyperspectral imaging system with geometric distortion correction; tested only on buildings, checkerboards and color checkers. No animals are imaged or analysed.

title: Compact staring-type underwater spectral imaging system utilizing k-Nearest neighbor-based interpolation for spectral reconstruction
reason: Develops an underwater spectral imaging system and spectral reconstruction method validated only on a Munsell color card in a laboratory set-up; no animals are imaged or analysed.

title: MSDA-HLGCformer-based context-aware fusion network for underwater organism detection
reason: Proposes a deep-learning detector for underwater marine organisms (echinus, holothurian, scallop, starfish, fish, turtles, etc.) in seabed images.

title: DACBN: Dual attention convolutional broad network for fine-grained visual recognition
reason: Generic fine-grained visual classification method evaluated on CUB-200-2011 birds, aircraft and cars benchmarks; wildlife is not the stated application.

title: Deep vision-based wildlife intrusion detection with colour distribution preserved generative adversarial networks
reason: Proposes a computer vision pipeline that classifies video frames as containing wild elephants or not, to detect elephant intrusion near railway tracks; data includes Asian wild elephant images.

title: Animal Identity Recognition using Object Detection Techniques
reason: Applies YOLOv5 and Detectron2 to detect and identify individual gorillas and monkey species in images; the paper states the data include animals both in captivity and in the wild.

title: Refining Bird Species Identification through GAN-Enhanced Data Augmentation and Deep Learning Models
reason: CNN classification of ten wild warbler species from web images of birds in natural habitats, with StyleGAN3 data augmentation.

title: Multi-Label Classification with Deep Learning and Manual Data Collection for Identifying Similar Bird Species
reason: Develops a CNN to classify ten visually similar wild bird (warbler) species from web-collected images.

title: An efficient approach to detect and segment underwater images using Swin Transformer
reason: Proposes a Swin Transformer/ConvMixer UNet for semantic segmentation of underwater images in the SUIM dataset. Fish segmentation for monitoring fish habitat and the marine ecosystem is the stated application.

title: Optimum image alignment setting selection for structure-from-motion photogrammetry using Remotely Piloted Aircraft Systems (RPAS) to support coral habitat classification
venue: Remote Sensing Applications Society and Environment
reason: Drone (RPAS) imagery of wild coral reefs processed with SfM photogrammetry and SVM image classification to map coral habitat classes (live corals as animal subject).

title: A remote sensing model for coral recruitment habitat
reason: Drop-camera images of wild reef benthos (including Acropora and Porites corals) are classified with a CNN-based ReefCloud classifier. The results are combined with Sentinel 2 satellite predictors to map coral habitat on Scott Reef. Corals are wild animals and appear in the analysed images.

title: Can automatic measuring replace humans when evaluating a shrimp fishery?
reason: Computer vision (SAM segmentation on RGB-D images) used to measure carapace length of wild trawl-caught deep-water shrimp for fishery stock assessment.

title: Monitoring fish populations using stereo-DOV-based surveys and open-access tools in the Gulf of California
reason: Applies stereo-video photogrammetry (camera calibration and 3D landmark reconstruction) and image-based counting to video of wild reef and pelagic fish at a seamount in a Marine Protected Area.

title: Skinny dolphins: Can poor body condition explain population decline in Indo-Pacific humpback dolphins (Sousa chinensis)?
venue: The Science of The Total Environment
reason: Applies UAV aerial photogrammetry (image-based morphometric measurement) to free-ranging Indo-Pacific humpback dolphins to assess body condition.

title: Grazing affects ecosystem traits by regulating plateau pika activities at the landscape scale
venue: The Science of The Total Environment
reason: Applies object-oriented image classification to UAV RGB images to extract burrows (direct signs) of wild plateau pikas on the Tibetan Plateau.

title: Characterization of deep-sea sponge ground (Asconema setubalense) using structure from motion methodology.
reason: Applies structure-from-motion photogrammetry to ROTV video to reconstruct 3D models and measure wild deep-sea sponges (Asconema setubalense) in their natural habitat.

title: Butterfly segmentation by multi scaled quantum cuts in agro-ecological environment
reason: Proposes a training-free graph-based segmentation method for butterflies in photographs of their natural environment, evaluated on the Leeds Butterfly and CAMO datasets.

title: An energy efficient fog-based internet of things framework to combat wildlife poaching
reason: IoT/fog-computing framework for anti-poaching. The paper tests PIR-triggered image capture, communication, energy use and simulations. No computer vision analysis of animal images is performed or evaluated, and the system tests used human subjects.

title: An efficient densenet-based deep learning model for Big-4 snake species classification
reason: Applies a CNN (DenseNet) to classify images of free-ranging snakes (Big-4 venomous species and non-venomous colubrids) gathered from personal collections and citizen-science platforms.

title: Evaluating enrichment use in group-housed rhesus macaques (Macaca mulatta): A machine learning approach
reason: Computer vision pipelines applied to CCTV video of group-housed rhesus macaques kept in enclosures of a captive breeding colony; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Automated precision beekeeping for accessing bee brood development and behaviour using deep CNN
reason: Precision beekeeping study classifying brood stages in managed honeybee hive comb images; apiculture, not wild free-ranging animals.

title: Application of computer vision and deep learning models to automatically classify medically important mosquitoes in North Borneo, Malaysia
reason: Images are of laboratory-bred, frozen-killed mosquito specimens photographed on a white background in a lab set-up; the field test is on collected mosquitoes presented to a webcam, not free-ranging animals.

title: Why flying insects gather at artificial light
reason: The study tracks wild insects flying around artificial lights in the field in 3D, using stereo video, background subtraction and triangulation. It also records field-caught and reared insects in the lab with motion capture.

title: SuperAnimal pretrained pose estimation models for behavioral analysis
reason: Pose estimation foundation models trained and evaluated on lab mice plus in-the-wild quadruped data, including wild rodents from iNaturalist and wild animals in AP-10K; primary method research.

title: Multidimensional social influence drives leadership and composition-dependent success in octopus–fish hunting groups
reason: Applies structure-from-motion and multi-view 3D tracking to field video of wild octopus-fish hunting groups on coral reefs to study leadership and behaviour.

title: A-SOiD, an active-learning platform for expert-guided, data-efficient discovery of behavior
reason: Behaviour classification from pose data of laboratory mice (resident-intruder assay) and a singly-housed laboratory monkey; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: An annotated wing interferential pattern dataset of dipteran insects of medical interest for deep learning
reason: Dataset of microscope images of dissected wings from preserved collection specimens (lab-reared or field-caught) of dipteran insects of medical interest. This is a laboratory microscopy set-up, not imagery of free-ranging animals.

title: The Poses for Equine Research Dataset (PFERD)
reason: Dataset of domestic horses recorded with motion capture and video in an indoor riding arena; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: An image and video dataset of nesting green sea turtles with annotated data
reason: Data descriptor presenting an annotated video/image dataset of wild nesting green sea turtles on a beach, with a trained object detector used to produce bounding box annotations.

title: Grassland vertical height heterogeneity predicts flower and bee diversity: an UAV photogrammetric approach
reason: UAV RGB images are used only to reconstruct grassland vegetation height (canopy height models). Bees and flowers are counted by observers on transect walks, not from images, so no animals are analysed by computer vision.

title: Evaluating YOLO architectures for detecting road killed endangered Brazilian animals
reason: YOLO detectors are compared on web-collected images (Google Images) of five Brazilian wild mammal species and on videos recorded in an ecological park with enclosures/cages plus internet videos. The paper never states that any analysed image shows free-ranging animals; the only described recording place is a captive park, so wild data is not established.

title: A convolutional neural network to identify mosquito species (Diptera: Culicidae) of the genus Aedes by wing images
reason: Field-trapped mosquitoes were killed, and their removed wings were slide-mounted and photographed under a laboratory stereomicroscope; no images show free-ranging animals.

title: Embracing firefly flash pattern variability with data-driven species classification
reason: Stereoscopic field videos of wild firefly swarms are processed: flashes are reconstructed in 3D and linked into trajectories, then classified to species with an RNN.

title: Airborne imagery does not preclude detectability issues in estimating bird colony size
reason: Birds and nests in drone images were identified manually by human interpreters and analysed with capture-recapture statistics; no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated (only panorama stitching software was used).

title: Automated differentiation of mixed populations of free-flying female mosquitoes under semi-field conditions
reason: Species classification uses optoacoustic wingbeat-frequency signals from a photodiode (MFCC/PSD features), not image or video analysis; the mosquitoes are laboratory colonies released in a mesh tent.

title: SlumberNet: deep learning classification of sleep stages using residual neural networks
reason: Deep learning classification of sleep stages from EEG and EMG voltage time series of laboratory mice; no image or video data is analysed.

title: Computer vision enables taxon-specific identification of African carnivore tooth marks on bone
reason: Borderline case. CNN classification of microscope images of carnivore tooth marks on bone (direct animal signs) to identify the taxon that made them. Most marks come from captive zoo/reserve lions, leopards, hyenas and crocodiles, but part of the hyena sample comes from a hyena breeding den (Eyasi), which appears to be wild although the paper does not say so explicitly. If the den sample is not accepted as wild, the paper would be E-CAPTIVE.

title: ReScape: transforming coral-reefscape images for quantitative analysis
reason: Develops a computer-vision algorithm (ReScape) that rectifies perspective in underwater images of wild coral reefs in Okinawa so that coral cover can be quantified; primary research on images of wild animals (corals).

title: Edge computing based real-time Nephrops (Nephrops norvegicus) catch estimation in demersal trawls using object detection models
reason: Object detection and tracking applied to in-trawl underwater video of wild Nephrops on commercial fishing grounds to count catch in real time.

title: Markerless 3D kinematics and force estimation in cheetahs
reason: Markerless multi-camera 3D pose and force estimation on video of running cheetahs; the paper describes its data as free-running cheetahs in the wild (AcinoSet) plus a force-plate dataset of cheetahs chasing a mechanical lure, which is a controlled set-up.

title: Assessment of sustainable baits for passive fishing gears through automatic fish behavior recognition
reason: Primary study applying detection, tracking and behaviour classification to in situ underwater video of wild black seabream around baits.

title: Man versus machine: cost and carbon emission savings of 4G-connected Artificial Intelligence technology for classifying species in camera trap images
reason: Evaluates a CNN-based AI platform (eVorta) for classifying free-ranging feral cats and wild echidnas in camera trap images from a field eradication program, compared with human observers.

title: Mark-recapture validates the use of photo-identification for the widely distributed blue-spotted ribbontail ray, Taeniura lymma
reason: Primary study applying computer-aided photo-identification software (I3S) to photographs of wild-caught blue-spotted ribbontail rays to re-identify individuals.

title: Towards real-time monitoring of insect species populations
reason: Primary study training a YOLOv8 classifier on web-scraped / citizen-science images of 2584 insect species for biodiversity monitoring; whether the photographed insects are wild is not stated explicitly.

title: Leveraging deep learning and computer vision technologies to enhance management of coastal fisheries in the Pacific region
reason: Applies CV (YOLOv4, ResNet101) to photographs of wild-caught reef finfish and invertebrates landed by coastal fishers or sold at markets for species identification and length measurement; not aquaculture.

title: Towards transforming malaria vector surveillance using VectorBrain: a novel convolutional neural network for mosquito species, sex, and abdomen status identifications
reason: CNN pipeline classifies species, sex and abdomen status of wild-caught mosquitoes from field vector surveillance, imaged by smartphone. These are freshly caught wild specimens, not museum or captive animals.

title: Linking cognitive strategy, neural mechanism, and movement statistics in group foraging behaviors
reason: Primary study that records thermal and RGB video of wild birds foraging in Central Park and tracks them automatically with the SLEAP deep-learning pipeline; the trajectories are used for behavioural modelling.

title: DAMM for the detection and tracking of multiple animals within complex social and environmental settings
reason: Instance segmentation and tracking of laboratory mice and rats in experimental setups (home cages, arenas, operant chambers); no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Non-invasive methods characterise the world’s largest tiger shark aggregation in Fuvahmulah, Maldives
reason: Wild tiger sharks are identified from diver photos and video, but identification and measurement are done by hand (manual photo-ID catalogue matching and manual laser photogrammetry). No computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: UICE-MIRNet guided image enhancement for underwater object detection
reason: Proposes underwater image enhancement plus YOLOv4 detection evaluated on the Brackish dataset, which contains underwater images of living, free-ranging aquatic animals (fish, crabs, starfish, jellyfish, shrimp).

title: WingAnalogy: a computer vision-based tool for automated insect wing asymmetry and morphometry analysis
reason: Computer vision segmentation of scanned, prepared insect wing specimens. The paper does not describe free-ranging animals in the field, and the subject is specimen morphometry.

title: Wildlife target detection based on improved YOLOX-s network
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOX-s detector evaluated on about 4000 images of wild animals captured in their natural habitats in a reserve.

title: A preliminary application and its error estimates of a simple stereo-camera measure system for the far-sea fishery of Pacific saury
reason: Stereo-camera length measurement of dead Pacific saury collected from a fishing port; all images were acquired in a laboratory set-up, so no images show free-ranging animals.

title: Significant feature suppression and cross-feature fusion networks for fine-grained visual classification
reason: Generic fine-grained visual classification method evaluated on standard FGVC benchmarks (birds, aircraft, cars, dogs); wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: A Lightweight underwater detector enhanced by Attention mechanism, GSConv and WIoU on YOLOv8
reason: Proposes a YOLOv8-based detector for underwater marine invertebrates (echinus, holothurian, scallop, starfish) in underwater images of the URPC2020 dataset.

title: Automated classification in turtles genus Malayemys using ensemble multiview image based on improved YOLOv8 with CNN
reason: Primary study applying a YOLOv8-based computer vision model to photographs of wild-caught freshwater turtles (genus Malayemys) that were photographed and released, for species identification in conservation.

title: Enhancing mosquito classification through self-supervised learning
reason: Classification of archived mosquito specimens imaged under a stereomicroscope in a laboratory setting for medical entomology; no wild free-ranging animals imaged in the field.

title: Artificial intelligence correctly classifies developmental stages of monarch caterpillars enabling better conservation through the use of community science photographs
reason: YOLOv5 detection and instar classification of monarch caterpillars in iNaturalist citizen-science photographs, mostly taken in natural settings with some reared individuals.

title: Information structure of heterogeneous criticality in a fish school
reason: Ayu purchased from a fish farm were filmed in a controlled laboratory tank. Video tracking only supplies trajectories for an information-theoretic analysis of collective behaviour; no wild animals are involved.

title: Enhance fashion classification of mosquito vector species via self-supervised vision transformer
reason: Field-trapped mosquito specimens were identified under a stereomicroscope and photographed in a controlled laboratory set-up on a uniform background. The images show specimens imaged in a lab set-up, not free-ranging animals in their habitat, and the application is vector-disease surveillance.

title: Feeding kinematics of a surgeonfish reveal novel functions and relationships to reef substrata
reason: Fish sourced from commercial vendors filmed in laboratory tanks with a high-speed camera; kinematics are extracted by manual landmarking, with no wild animals.

title: Development of a 3D tracking system for multiple marmosets under free-moving conditions
reason: 3D tracking, face identification and grooming detection of laboratory common marmosets housed in a home cage at an experimental animal facility; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: VespAI: a deep learning-based system for the detection of invasive hornets
reason: Deep-learning detection and classification of free-ranging invasive hornets (Vespa velutina) and European hornets visiting field bait stations; primary research on images of wild insects.

title: Collective anti-predator escape manoeuvres through optimal attack and avoidance strategies
reason: Wild marlin and sardines are filmed by drone, but the video is only annotated and tracked by hand (custom Matlab annotation, MTrackJ manual tracking). The paper's contribution is an agent-based model; no automated computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Multi-animal 3D social pose estimation, identification and behaviour embedding with a few-shot learning framework
reason: Method for multi-animal 3D pose estimation, identification and behaviour clustering, tested on laboratory mice, two housed budgerigars and two police-base dogs in open-field arenas; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Edge‐guided representation learning for underwater object detection
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for underwater object detection evaluated on datasets of marine organisms (echinus, holothurian, starfish, scallop, fish, crabs, jellyfish) in natural underwater environments, including the Brackish dataset from temperate brackish waters.

title: FlockSeer : A portable stereo vision observer for bird flocking
reason: Develops a portable stereo vision system and applies detection, tracking and 3D trajectory reconstruction to video of free-flying wild bird flocks recorded in the field.

title: Recognition of European mammals and birds in camera trap images using deep neural networks
reason: Deep neural network classification of wild European mammals and birds in camera trap images recorded in forests in Germany and Poland; the classes also include domestic animals (house cat, domestic dog).

title: To crop or not to crop: Comparing whole-image and cropped classification on a large dataset of camera trap images
reason: Primary study comparing whole-image and detector-cropped species classification on large camera trap image datasets of wildlife.

title: Nighttime wildlife object detection based on YOLOv8‐night
reason: Proposes a YOLOv8-based detector for nighttime infrared camera images of wild animals (NTLNP dataset), which includes 15 wild and 2 domestic species.

title: Automatic classification of bird species related to power line faults using deep convolution features and ECOC‐SVM model
reason: Primary study proposing a CNN-feature + ECOC-SVM image classifier for 40 wild bird species around power lines, using inspection images from the field and Internet images.

title: A novel efficient wildlife detecting method with lightweight deployment on UAVs based on YOLOv7
reason: Proposes a lightweight YOLOv7-based detector for UAV wildlife imagery, evaluated on the WAID dataset, which contains wild animals (zebras, seals, Tibetan wild donkeys) together with captive sheep and cattle.

title: Multi‐target detection and tracking of shallow marine organisms based on improved YOLO v5 and DeepSORT
reason: Detection and tracking of shallow marine organisms in underwater videos (collected and downloaded); wild status of the animals is not explicitly stated, but the videos are described as seabed videos of shallow marine organisms.

title: YOLO‐UOD: An underwater small object detector via improved efficient layer aggregation network
reason: Proposes an underwater object detector evaluated on images of marine organisms (sea urchins, sea cucumbers, scallops, starfish) captured on a natural seabed.

title: A lightweight underwater fish image semantic segmentation model based on U‐Net
reason: Proposes a CNN segmentation model for underwater fish images from the Fish4Knowledge dataset, which was recorded at underwater viewing platforms in natural waters.

title: FishFocusNet: An improved method based on YOLOv8 for underwater tropical fish identification
reason: Fish detection method evaluated only on images of tropical fish kept in a coral and tropical fish nurturing area of a research institute; no wild, free-ranging animals in the analysed data.

title: Underwater organisms detection algorithm based on multi‐scale perception and representation enhancement
reason: Proposes a CNN-based detector for marine organisms (sea cucumber, urchin, scallop, starfish) in underwater images from a real marine environment.

title: Implementation of YOLOv8-Pose Model for Identification and Estimation of the Length of Skipjack and Tuna Like Species on the Website
reason: Applies YOLOv8-Pose to smartphone images of wild-caught marine fish (capture fisheries, not aquaculture) at fish landing sites for species identification and length estimation.

title: Mapping the distribution of sea urchin (Echinoidea) and benthic habitat using drone in the waters of Lancang Island
reason: Applies image thresholding to drone images to map and count wild sea urchins in coastal waters, and uses OBIA with SVM to classify their benthic habitat.

title: Smart Animal Repelling Device: Utilizing IoT and AI for Effective Anti-Adaptive Harmful Animal Deterrence
reason: Applies CNN-based animal detection (R-CNN, SSD) on camera images to deter wild ungulates raiding crops; primary research with experimental evaluation on 10,000 photos.

title: Multi-shift spatio-temporal features assisted deep neural network for detecting the intrusion of wild animals using surveillance cameras
reason: Proposes a spatio-temporal deep network to recognise wild animals in surveillance and camera-trap imagery, evaluated on a wild animal dataset and a camera trap dataset.

title: System for analyzing data from camera traps based on a two-stage neural network approach for operational remote monitoring
reason: Primary study training and comparing detectors and classifiers on camera-trap images of wild animals from Russian nature reserves, packaged as a software tool.

title: Ultrasonic activated energy-efficient autonomous camera system for activity observation
reason: Proof-of-concept camera system; detector trained on the Aquarium COCO dataset and tested only on printed photographs indoors. None of the analysed data shows free-ranging wild animals.

title: Identification of birds species using deep learning
reason: Applies a deep CNN to classify bird species in images from the CUB-200-2011 dataset of birds, with bird monitoring as the stated purpose.

title: Image-based recognition of parasitoid wasps using advanced neural networks
reason: Wild-collected wasps from Malaise traps are imaged as preserved specimens in ethanol under a lab microscope camera. There are no images of free-ranging animals, so this falls under specimens (E-CAPTIVE).

title: Selective social interactions and speed-induced leadership in schooling fish
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
reason: Video tracking of black neon tetra schools swimming in a laboratory experimental tank; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Drone-based infrared thermography to measure the intranasal temperature of baleen whales
reason: Primary study that develops an image-analysis method (flatfield correction, pixel intensity extraction, radiometric calibration) on drone thermal video of free-swimming North Atlantic right whales. Borderline: blowholes are marked manually, so the image analysis is calibration and pixel extraction rather than automated recognition.

title: Integrating bathymetry data and high-resolution satellite imagery for benthic habitat mapping in a marine-protected area in Brazil
reason: Benthic habitat mapping (land-cover style classification of coral reef habitat classes) from WorldView-2 satellite imagery and bathymetry; habitat is the subject, not animals.

title: Classification of dinosaur footprints using machine learning
reason: The study classifies fossil dinosaur footprints using machine learning on tabular landmark distances. The landmarks were placed earlier from published images, and the paper itself does no image analysis. The subjects are fossil traces, not living wild animals.

title: The importance of acoustic background modelling in CNN-based detection of the neotropical White-lored Spinetail (Aves, Passeriformes, Furnaridae)
reason: The study detects bird vocalizations in passive acoustic recordings; CNNs are applied to spectrograms of sound, and no images or video of animals are analysed.

title: Monitoring the effectiveness of fauna sensitive infrastructure along the Peak Downs Highway in Central Queensland reveals mixed results for koala conservation
reason: Primary study applying AI video analysis to camera-trap footage of free-ranging koalas and other wildlife at highway underpasses; domestic animals (cattle, dogs, horses, cats) also appear in the footage.

title: RETRACTED ARTICLE: A novel approach to coral species classification using deep learning and unsupervised feature extraction
reason: Proposes a deep learning method to classify coral species, which are wild marine animals, in underwater reef images.

title: A benchmark and a multi-stage pipeline for classifying underwater videos at scale
venue: International Journal of Image and Data Fusion
reason: The paper builds a benchmark and a video classification pipeline for coral reef footage. Corals are animals. Most of the footage shows natural reefs, but some comes from aquariums.

title: Deep Learning-based Detection of Bird’s Nests on Power Transmission Towers
reason: Applies YOLOv3 to detect nests of birds (direct signs of free-ranging wild birds) on power transmission towers in images.

title: You Only Look Once (YOLOv8) for Fish Species Detection
venue: IOP Conference Series Earth and Environmental Science
reason: Fish images come from a traditional fish market and the study is framed around the fisheries industry. The subjects are dead, market-sold fish, not wild free-ranging animals.

title: Evaluating machine learning-based elephant recognition in complex African landscapes using drone imagery
reason: Evaluates object detection models on drone imagery of free-ranging African bush elephants in Kasungu National Park, Malawi.

title: Transfer learning with generative models for object detection on limited datasets
reason: Proposes a generative-model transfer learning pipeline for object detection and validates it on OzFish, an underwater dataset of wild fishes in a marine environment (alongside a car dataset).

title: Biological characteristics of pregnancy in captive Yangtze finless porpoises revealed by urinary metabolomics
reason: Urinary metabolomics study (LC–MS) of captive Yangtze finless porpoises; no image or video analysis.

title: Increasing the impact of vertebrate scientific collections through 3D imaging: The openVertebrate (oVert) Thematic Collections Network
reason: Overview of a museum digitization network producing CT, surface-scan and photogrammetry 3D models of preserved museum specimens; no wild or free-ranging animals are imaged, and no CV method is developed or evaluated.

title: The establishment and potential spread of Osmia cornuta (Hymenoptera: Megachilidae) in North America
reason: The images analysed are mason bee cocoons from a mason bee farm and from beekeepers, photographed in a laboratory set-up. This is managed bee husbandry (beekeeping) rather than imagery of wild, free-ranging animals. The iNaturalist photos were only checked by eye, not analysed with computer vision.

title: Morphological Species Delimitation in The Western Pond Turtle (Actinemys): Can Machine Learning Methods Aid in Cryptic Species Identification?
reason: Analyses manually digitized landmarks from photographs of museum turtle specimens (plastron shape) with classical ML classifiers; subjects are museum specimens, not images of free-ranging animals.

title: Social behavior among nocturnally migrating birds revealed by automated moonwatching
reason: Primary study applying a computer-vision workflow to video of the Moon to detect wild nocturnally migrating birds and extract flight paths, used to quantify group flight behaviour.

title: Inferring Taxonomic Affinities and Genetic Distances Using Morphological Features Extracted from Specimen Images: A Case Study with a Bivalve Data Set
reason: Analyses images of bivalve shell specimens from museums, data aggregators and shell dealers; no free-ranging animals imaged, so museum-specimen exclusion applies.

title: Integrating Deep Learning Derived Morphological Traits and Molecular Data for Total-Evidence Phylogenetics: Lessons from Digitized Collections
reason: Deep learning traits are extracted from images of pinned museum specimens of rove beetles. No images of live, free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Ecological and phylogenetic influences on limb joint kinematics in wild primates
venue: Zoological Journal of the Linnean Society
reason: Wild primates filmed in the field, but joint angles were measured by hand in ImageJ, followed by statistical analysis. No computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Collective order and group structure of shoaling fish subject to differing risk-level treatments with a sympatric predator
reason: Wild-caught mosquitofish were filmed in a laboratory experimental arena (tank) and tracked with CTrax. No free-ranging animals were imaged.

title: New interactive machine learning tool for marine image analysis
reason: Applies a CNN-based interactive segmentation tool (RootPainter) to in-situ underwater images and ROV video frames of a wild deep-sea sponge to extract presence and surface area.

title: Brightness cues affect gap negotiation behaviours in zebra finches flying between perches
reason: Behavioural flight experiment on captive-bred zebra finches in an aviary; the video was reviewed and scored by hand, with no computer vision method. The animals are also captive only.

title: Solitary humpback whales manufacture bubble-nets as tools to increase prey intake
reason: Behavioural ecology study of wild humpback whales; drone and tag videos were measured and reviewed by hand (manual photogrammetry, video review). No computer vision method was developed or applied.

title: Rapid species discrimination of similar insects using hyperspectral imaging and lightweight edge artificial intelligence
reason: All analysed data are hyperspectral and RGB images of pinned, dried butterfly specimens imaged on a laboratory bench; no images of wild, free-ranging animals.

title: Behavioural responses of common dolphins to naval sonar
reason: Drone-based photogrammetry images of wild common dolphins are analysed to track focal individuals and infer subgroup movement during sonar exposure experiments.

title: Advances in remote sensing of emperor penguins: first multi-year time series documenting trends in the global population
venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences
reason: Applies supervised maximum-likelihood pixel classification to very-high-resolution satellite imagery to estimate the abundance of wild emperor penguin colonies across Antarctica.

title: Stress in the social environment: behavioural and social consequences of stress transmission in bird flocks
venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences
reason: Zebra finches kept in indoor laboratory aviaries and cages at a research institute and tracked with barcodes in an experimental set-up. No wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Context-dependent rhythmicity in chimpanzee displays
venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences
reason: Zoo-housed chimpanzees; videos and audio were annotated manually (Praat, BORIS) for rhythm analysis, with no computer vision method. The animals are captive only, so E-CAPTIVE also applies.

title: Towards a standardized framework for AI-assisted, image-based monitoring of nocturnal insects
venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences
reason: Framework/perspective paper: it describes a workflow for image-based monitoring of nocturnal insects and summarises results of earlier studies (Bjerge et al., Korsch et al., Jain et al.). It runs no experiments of its own and states it has no additional data.

title: DeepRod: A human-in-the-loop system for automatic rodent behavior analysis
reason: Behavior analysis of laboratory rodents in observation arenas for preclinical drug safety studies; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Multi-parametric assays capture sex- and environment-dependent modifiers of behavioral phenotypes in autism mouse models
reason: Behavioural phenotyping of genetically modified laboratory mice (autism models) in indoor laboratory arenas; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Sound-seeking before and after hearing loss in mice
reason: Neuroscience behavioural study of laboratory mice in an indoor arena; pose tracking (SLEAP) is applied to video of lab animals only, no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: LizardNet: A mobile hybrid deep learning tool for classification of 3D representations of Amazonian lizards
reason: Images are of alcohol-preserved museum specimens from the MPEG herpetological collection, not wild free-ranging animals.

title: MacAction: Realistic 3D macaque body animation based on multi-camera markerless motion capture
reason: Markerless 3D pose tracking and avatar animation of laboratory rhesus macaques housed in cages at a neuroscience facility, plus a human benchmark; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Utilising affordable smartphones and open-source time-lapse photography for monitoring pollinators
reason: Smartphone time-lapse images of wild flower-visiting insects were annotated and identified entirely by hand by annotators and taxonomists; no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Mountable miniature microphones to identify and assign mouse ultrasonic vocalizations
reason: Laboratory mice recorded in a custom acrylic recording box; the main contribution is a wearable ultrasonic microphone, with video pose tracking (SLEAP) as an add-on. No wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Anti-drift pose tracker (ADPT): A transformer-based network for robust animal pose estimation cross-species
reason: Pose estimation method developed and evaluated on laboratory animals (mice, caged monkeys, flies) plus public macaque, marmoset and dog datasets; no wild free-ranging animals are stated.

title: vmTracking: Virtual Markers Overcome Occlusion and Crowding in Multi-Animal Pose Tracking
reason: Pose-tracking method tested on laboratory mice in open-field arenas, fish in an aquarium and human dancers; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Iguanas from above: Citizen scientists provide reliable counts of endangered Galápagos marine iguanas from drone imagery
reason: Drone images of wild marine iguanas are detected and counted by online citizen-science volunteers and experts; no automated image analysis is applied. title: Social touch shapes communication and animal recognition in naked mole-rats
reason: Laboratory-housed naked mole-rat colonies recorded in an open field arena and tube test; pose tracking and behaviour segmentation applied to laboratory animals, no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Miniature linear and split-belt treadmills reveal mechanisms of adaptive motor control in walking Drosophila
reason: Laboratory-reared Drosophila melanogaster recorded on miniature treadmills, in an arena and tethered on a ball; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Laboratory application of the Aquascope approach of automated imaging and classification for long-term plankton monitoring
reason: Automated imaging and ML classification of wild lake plankton, including zooplankton such as rotifers, copepods and Daphnia, from Swiss lakes. The samples were imaged in the lab with an Aquascope and compared with an in-situ lake camera.

title: Effects of Input Image Size on the Accuracy of Fish Identification Using Deep Learning
reason: Applies Mask R-CNN to detect and classify wild-caught fish from set-net catches for stock assessment of wild fish stocks; capture fisheries, not aquaculture.

title: Key link between iron and the size structure of three main mesoplanktonic groups (Crustaceans, Rhizarians, and colonial N 2 -fixers) in the Upper Ocean
reason: Analyses images of wild marine mesoplankton (crustaceans, rhizarians, Trichodesmium) from in situ Underwater Vision Profilers and scanned net samples. The images are segmented, classified and measured to build size spectra, which are then modelled against environmental drivers.

title: FABEL: Forecasting Animal Behavioral Events with Deep Learning-Based Computer Vision
reason: Behavioural neuroscience study forecasting food interaction of laboratory mice filmed in an operant chamber; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: The FAIR-Device - a non-lethal and generalist semi-automatic Malaise trap for insect biodiversity monitoring: Proof of concept
reason: Field device records video of wild, free-ranging insects funnelled by a Malaise trap and classifies extracted frames with the iNaturalist computer vision system; primary proof-of-concept study.

title: Sexual dimorphism in the dorsal spot number and yellow surface in fire salamanders Salamandra salamandra ssp terrestris Linnaeus, 1758 (Caudata: Salamandridae)
reason: Field photographs of wild fire salamanders analysed with a Python algorithm that measures the percentage of yellow pixels, used to study sexual dimorphism.

title: Collective anti-predator escape manoeuvres through optimal attack and avoidance strategies
reason: Drone footage of wild sardines and marlin is analysed only through manual annotation and manual tracking, with an agent-based simulation model on top; no computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Zero-shot animal behavior classification with vision-language foundation models
reason: Primary study evaluating zero-shot vision-language models for behavior classification on camera trap images of wild European ungulates.

title: Regional Variations in Live Proportions of Southwest Pacific Cold-Water Coral Solenosmilia variabilis Reefs
reason: The study images wild deep-sea corals, but live coral and dead framework are labelled by hand in Adobe Photoshop. An existing R script then only turns the labelled areas into surface areas. No computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Novel mark recapture surveys reveal stable pigmentation patterns but age-related melanism in the common frog Rana temporaria
reason: Image analysis (ImageJ thresholding and segmentation, Wild-ID individual identification) of smartphone photos of a wild frog population in a garden.

title: Quantifying social roles in multi-animal videos using subject-aware deep-learning
reason: Computer vision method (LabGym2) for behaviour recognition. Most of the data come from lab animals, but one part analyses videos of wild, provisioned Japanese macaques filmed in monkey parks.

title: SegColR: Deep Learning for Automated Segmentation and Color Extraction
reason: Presents a deep-learning segmentation and colour-extraction pipeline, demonstrated on iNaturalist citizen-science images of wild organisms, including fish.

title: Video Foundation Models for Animal Behavior Analysis
reason: Evaluates frozen video foundation models for animal behavior analysis on several datasets. Most are lab mouse and fly data, but the evaluation also covers KABR, drone videos of wild Kenyan giraffes and zebras, and SSW60, wild bird videos.

title: Common marmosets use body posture as multi-functional signal to solicit, maintain, and modify social play
reason: Behavioural study of captive-born common marmosets in indoor enclosures. Videos were coded manually frame by frame and analysed with statistical models, so no computer vision method is used. The animals are also captive only (E-CAPTIVE).

title: PriMAT: A robust multi-animal tracking model for primates in the wild
reason: Proposes a multi-animal tracking and identification model evaluated on videos of wild Assamese macaques and redfronted lemurs; pretraining data are mostly zoo macaques.

title: Rough Grouping Enhances YOLO’s Pollinator Classification and Detection from Small Datasets
reason: YOLOv8 detection and classification of free-ranging flower-visiting insects filmed in the field at a botanic garden and solar field sites; primary research.

title: CV.eDNA: A hybrid approach to invertebrate biomonitoring using computer vision and DNA metabarcoding
reason: Computer vision classification of images of wild invertebrates collected in field pitfall traps (NEON bycatch) for biomonitoring; primary method study.

title: Pairwise interactions, feedback rule changes, and deliberative decisions underlie honeybee inflight group coordination
reason: The study tracks western honey bees from a managed hive at a university as they fly back to an actuated hive entrance. Managed honeybee colonies count as beekeeping, which falls under the agricultural exclusion.

title: Towards a mechanistic understanding of collective escape in starlings
reason: Video footage of wild starling flocks was analysed qualitatively by hand in video-editing software, alongside an agent-based simulation model. No computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Comprehensive Mosquito Wing Image Repository for Advancing Research on Geometric Morphometric- and AI-Based Identification
reason: Dataset paper of microscope images of dissected mosquito wings mounted on slides. The animals come from field traps and laboratory colonies. The imaging is a laboratory microscopy set-up of specimens, and the paper applies no computer vision method of its own.

title: Machine learning outcompetes human assessment in identifying eggs of a conspecific brood parasite
reason: Image analysis of UV-visible photographs of eggs (direct signs) of wild free-ranging barn swallows breeding in barns, with machine learning to identify parasitic eggs.

title: Social and spatial drivers of the multitiered structure of zebra finch social networks
reason: Camera-based barcode tracking of captive zebra finch colonies in aviaries only; no wild animals analysed.

title: Automated Analysis of Bird Head Motion from Videos in Unconstrained Settings
reason: Develops a detection and head key point estimation framework for videos and images of birds in natural habitats and unconstrained settings (eBird and bird image datasets), with an additional pigeon dataset (3D-POP) used for validation.

title: PrecisionTrack: A Platform for Automated Long-Term Social Behavior Analysis in Naturalized Environments
reason: The main data show 20 laboratory mice in an enriched open-field arena. The authors' own dataset contains no wild or free-ranging animals.

reason: Statistical analysis of behavioural state sequences derived from video of inbred laboratory fruit flies walking in a featureless arena; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Satellite Image Based Animal Identification System Using Deep Learning Assisted Remote Sensing Strategy
venue: International Conference on Advances in Computing, Communication and Applied Informatics (ACCAI)
reason: Primary study proposing a deep learning model (LASCM) for detecting and classifying animals in satellite images, with a stated wildlife monitoring and human-animal conflict application. title: Entomoscope: An Open-Source Photomicroscope for Biodiversity Discovery

reason: Proposes a CNN for fine-grained butterfly species classification. The dataset mixes butterflies photographed in the field with indoor specimen images, so part of the data shows wild animals.

title: An Efficient YOLO Network With CSPCBAM, Ghost, and Cluster-NMS for Underwater Target Detection
reason: Proposes a YOLO-based detector for underwater marine organisms (sea urchin, sea cucumber, scallop, starfish, fish, crab, shrimp) in underwater images.

title: HLASwin-T-ACoat-Net Based Underwater Object Detection
reason: Proposes a deep learning detector for underwater images and evaluates it on URPC2018, which shows marine organisms (holothurian, echinus, scallops, starfish) in various underwater environments.

title: Anemone Image Generation Based on Diffusion-Stylegan2
