title: IgnitusTracker: Tracking Bee Flights for Assessing the Activity of Bombus Ignitus Towards Keeping Optimal Pollination Environments
reason: Tracks commercially supplied Bombus ignitus bumblebees kept in managed hives for greenhouse crop pollination on a farm; managed pollinators in agricultural production, not wild free-ranging animals.

title: Analyzing Information Leakage on Video Object Detection Datasets by Splitting Images Into Clusters With High Spatiotemporal Correlation
reason: Generic dataset-splitting method for object detection evaluated on a handgun detection dataset; no animals involved.

title: Research on Underwater Small Target Detection Technology Based on Single-Stage USSTD-YOLOv8n
reason: Proposes a YOLOv8n-based detector for small underwater targets (marine organisms such as Echinus) on the URPC2018/URPC2020 underwater image datasets.

title: YOLO8-FASG: A High-Accuracy Fish Identification Method for Underwater Robotic System
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv8 detector for fish and evaluates it on Fish4Knowledge images recorded by fixed underwater cameras on Taiwan's coral reefs, i.e. wild free-ranging fish.

title: Improved YOLOv5 Based Deep Learning System for Jellyfish Detection
reason: Primary study proposing an improved YOLOv5n detector and a labelled dataset for underwater jellyfish, motivated by monitoring jellyfish blooms. title: Edge AI in Sustainable Farming: Deep Learning-Driven IoT Framework to Safeguard Crops From Wildlife Threats
reason: Deep learning classification of animal images for detecting wildlife (e.g., bears) intruding into farmland; the dataset mixes wild and domestic animals.

title: BSM-YOLO: A Dynamic Sparse Attention-Based Approach for Mousehole Detection
reason: Proposes a YOLOv5-based detector for Brandt's vole burrows (direct signs of wild rodents) in UAV images of natural grassland.

title: SMB-YOLOv5: A Lightweight Airport Flying Bird Detection Algorithm Based on Deep Neural Networks
reason: Proposes a deep-learning detector for free-flying wild birds in images from cameras at a real airport.

title: YOLOv7-PE: A Precise and Efficient Enhancement of YOLOv7 for Underwater Target Detection
reason: Proposes a YOLOv7-based detector for marine animals (scallops, sea cucumbers, sea stars, sea urchins) in images taken in real marine environments.

title: Fish as a Deformable Solid: An Innovative Method to Characterize Fish Swimming Behavior on Acoustic Videos
reason: Image-based computer vision (deformable mesh tracking) applied to multibeam acoustic camera videos of wild fish moving freely through a river and a hydropower intake canal.

title: The Art of Camouflage: Few-Shot Learning for Animal Detection and Segmentation
reason: Proposes a few-shot detection and instance segmentation method and a benchmark dataset (CAMO-FS) of camouflaged animals in the wild.

title: Underwater Target Detection Based on Improved YOLOv7 Algorithm With BiFusion Neck Structure and MPDIoU Loss Function
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv7 detector for underwater fish in marine environments (web-collected images and the OzFish dataset); the fish are wild, free-ranging animals.

title: ReDeformTR: Wildlife Re-Identification Based on Light-Weight Deformable Transformer With Multi-Image Feature Fusion
reason: The paper proposes a tiger re-identification model evaluated only on ATRW, whose images the paper states were all taken in zoos; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Novel Animal Detection System: Cascaded YOLOv8 With Adaptive Preprocessing and Feature Extraction
reason: Primary study proposing a cascaded YOLOv8 pipeline for wildlife detection, evaluated on camera-trap and other wildlife image datasets.

title: Fine-Grained Fish Classification From Small to Large Datasets With Vision Transformers
reason: Fine-grained fish species classification with a vision transformer on 14 fish image datasets; some show wild fish underwater in natural habitats, others show market, laboratory or on-board catch images.

title: Enhancing Manatee Aggregation Counting Through Augmentation and Cross-Domain Learning
reason: Proposes a CNN density-map counting pipeline for wild manatees in aerial images from Blue Spring State Park, Florida.

title: A Measurement Model for Aquatic Animals Based on Instance Segmentation and 3D Point Cloud
reason: Size measurement of seafood-market fish and shellfish for aquaculture using instance segmentation and a depth camera; no wild, free-ranging animals are stated as the subject.

title: EGA-Net: Edge Guided Attention Network With Label Refinement for Parsing of Animal Body Parts
reason: General part-segmentation method evaluated on the generic Pascal-Part and PartImageNet benchmarks; the analysed classes are domestic quadrupeds (dog, cat, horse, cow, sheep) and wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Bird and UAVs Recognition Detection and Tracking Based on Improved YOLOv9-DeepSORT
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv9-DeepSORT model for detecting and tracking birds (and drones) in visible-light and infrared images and in video of birds flying in natural environments.

title: YOLOv8-UC: An Improved YOLOv8-Based Underwater Object Detection Algorithm
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv8 detector for underwater organisms (echinus, holothurian, starfish, scallop) in underwater images from the URPC2021 dataset. The paper does not say whether the animals are wild or farmed.

title: PLGAT: Underwater Plectropomus Leopardus Recognition Using Global Attention Mechanism and Transfer Learning
reason: Proposes a CNN detector/recogniser for P. leopardus. The main data comes from breeding-lab fish, but the method is also trained and evaluated on the Brackish dataset, which shows wild fish filmed on the seabed of Limfjorden, Denmark. So part of the data shows wild animals.

title: Unmanned Aerial Surveillance and Tracking System in Forest Areas for Poachers and Wildlife
reason: A UAV anti-poaching system that trains YOLOv5 to detect poachers and wildlife species (lion, tiger, leopard, etc.) in images. title: UW-DETR:Feature fusion enhanced RT-DETR for improving underwater object detection
reason: Proposes a transformer-based detector for underwater organisms. It is evaluated on UTDAC2020 and on the Brackish dataset, whose images come from permanently installed cameras monitoring marine species in a strait.

title: Bird Species Classification Enhancement via Adaptive Inertia Weight Particle Swarm Optimization-Based Image Augmentation Selection
reason: Proposes an AIWPSO-based augmentation selection method for CNN classification of bird species images (CVIP 2018 Bird Species Challenge), aimed at identifying wild birds for conservation.

title: A Multispectral Automated Transfer Technique (MATT) for Machine-Driven Image Labeling Utilizing the Segment Anything Model (SAM)
reason: The paper detects vehicles (cars and trucks) in drone RGB/LWIR imagery. No animals are analysed.

title: An Automatic Highly Dynamical Digital Twin Design with YOLOv8 for hydrodynamic studies on living animals
venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence Computer Data Sciences and Applications Acdsa 2024
reason: Segmentation is trained and evaluated only on frames from a simulated, fish-like flexible body in CFD software. The intended application is fish in a laboratory water tank. No real or wild animals are analysed.

title: Improving the Accuracy of Animal Species Classification in Camera Trap Images Using Transfer Learning
venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Computer, Data Sciences and Applications (ACDSA)
reason: Primary study applying transfer-learning CNNs to classify animal species in camera trap images from a national park (Zakouma animal dataset).

title: An Adaptive Autonomous Aerial System for Dynamic Field Animal Ecology Studies
venue: Proceedings 2024 IEEE International Conference on Autonomic Computing and Self Organizing Systems Companion Acsos C 2024
reason: Doctoral research summary on autonomous UAV navigation using YOLO-based detection/tracking of wild zebra and giraffe herds filmed by drone in Kenya; reports results from the author's own work.

title: A Contemporary CNN Implanted Deep Learning Framework for Crop Protection from Animal Intrusion in Farming Environment
reason: Applies a CNN (Faster R-CNN) to detect and classify wild animals (elephants, leopards) entering farmland, so the subjects are wild animals in the context of human–wildlife conflict.

title: Birds Species Identification Using Deep Learning Model
reason: Applies CNN image classification to photographs of wild bird species (525 species).

title: Classifying Airborne Targets With Motion-Based Recognition Techniques
reason: Classifies synthetically generated azimuth/elevation trajectories of simulated birds and drones; no real images or video are analysed and no real animals are involved.

title: Deep Diving into VGG19 CNN Model driven Coral Health Monitoring for Sustainable Reef Conservation
venue: IEEE World Conference on Applied Intelligence and Computing (AIC)
reason: Applies a CNN (VGG19) to images of corals, which are wild marine animals, to classify them as bleached or healthy.

title: PetVision: Improved MobileViTv3-Based Image Classification for Cat Breed Identification
venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Sciences (AiDAS)
reason: The paper classifies breeds of pet cats using the cat images of the Oxford-IIIT Pet Dataset; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: A Novel Method for Studying Mosquito Oviposition Behaviour Using Computer Vision and Deep Learning Algorithm
venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Sciences (AiDAS)
reason: Laboratory-reared Aedes mosquitoes filmed in net cages in an insectary; no wild or free-ranging animals in the analysed data.

title: Efficient Classification of Bird Species Using Photographic Images: A MobileViT Based Approach
reason: Applies a MobileViT deep learning classifier to photographs of 525 bird species, with the stated aim of supporting biodiversity conservation and ecological monitoring.

title: Deep Learning and Computer Vision Based Warning System for Animal Disruption in Farming Environments
reason: Applies YOLOv6 animal detection for a human-wildlife conflict warning system; the analysed Kaggle images cover wild taxa (elephant, bear, zebra, giraffe, bird) together with domestic animals. The paper does not state whether the animals shown are free-ranging.

title: Exploring Fine-Grained Feature Analysis for Bird Species Classification using Layer-wise Relevance Propagation
reason: Applies a CNN classifier with Layer-wise Relevance Propagation to bird species classification on CUB-200-2011, and names wildlife monitoring and conservation as the application. Birds are the stated subject. The paper does not say whether the birds pictured are wild.

title: IoT-Based Smart Farmland Using Deep Learning
venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Applications Theme: Healthcare and Internet of Things (AIMLA)
reason: Applies CNN-based image classification/detection to camera images of animals intruding on farmland, including wild elephants alongside livestock (cows, goats, pigs); primary application study.

title: A Deep Assessment of Thermal Image-Base Object Detection for a Wide Range of Applications
venue: 2nd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Applications Healthcare and Internet of Things Aimla 2024
reason: This is a survey of thermal-image object detection methods across several application areas. It summarises cited studies, including one on drone imagery of deer, but runs no experiments and analyses no data of its own.

title: QH-Bird: A Fine-Grained Bird Visual Dataset and Hierarchical Consistency Denoising Method
venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Internet of Things and Cloud Computing Technology (AIoTC)
reason: Builds a fine-grained image dataset of wild birds of Qinghai Province and evaluates CNN classifiers and a deep learning denoising method on it.

title: Abnormal Clustering and Cross Slicing Transformer for Insect Fine-Grained Image Classification
reason: Proposes a vision transformer method for fine-grained classification of insect images from iNaturalist 2017 Insecta and IP102; insects are the stated subject.

title: Shark Fine-Grained Image Classification Based on Feature Fusion and Attention Mechanism
reason: Proposes a CNN-based fine-grained classification method for shark species images from a public shark dataset; the paper does not state whether the sharks are wild or captive, but sharks and their conservation are the stated subject.

title: Bleaching Detection in Coral Reef using Deep Convolutional Autoencoder based Model
venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Signal Processing (AISP)
reason: Proposes a deep convolutional autoencoder classifier to detect bleaching in underwater images of coral reefs. Corals are wild marine animals.

title: ReLU Activated Attention UNet Encipher Decipher Framework based Species Classification of Butterfly
reason: Proposes a deep learning model to classify butterfly species from images that are mostly ecological scenes of butterflies in natural surroundings.

title: WildPose: HRNet-based Lightweight and Efficient Wildlife Pose Estimation
venue: Asia-Pacific Signal and Information Processing Association Annual Summit and Conference (APSIPA ASC)
reason: Proposes a lightweight HRNet-based pose estimation model evaluated on the Animal Kingdom wildlife dataset, which the paper describes as showing natural animal behaviours in various environments.

title: Real Time Classification System of Black Soldier Fly Larva
venue: IEEE VTS Asia Pacific Wireless Communications Symposium (APWCS)
reason: Growth-stage detection of reared Black Soldier Fly larvae used for food-waste composting and animal feed production; farmed insects, no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Efficient Endangered Deer Species Monitoring with UAV Aerial Imagery and Deep Learning
reason: Primary study applying YOLOv8 to UAV aerial images of wild marsh deer and Pampas deer in their natural habitats; the dataset also contains images of cows.

title: On the Use of YOLOv8 for Detection and Classification of Mammals Species in Wildlife Environments in the Ecuadorian Amazon
reason: Applies YOLOv8 detection and classification to iNaturalist images of six Ecuadorian Amazon mammal species for conservation monitoring; primary research on wild animal images.

title: Comparative Analysis of Object Identification Techniques for Bird Species
venue: 2024 4th Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
reason: Primary study comparing YOLOv5 and YOLOv8 for detecting and identifying bird species in images gathered from internet databases and videos; birds are the stated subject, and the paper does not state whether the birds are wild or captive beyond videos collected in tropics and bird sanctuaries.

title: VGG19's Role in Safeguarding Coral Reefs using a CNN-Based Monitoring Model
venue: Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
reason: Applies CNN (VGG19 transfer learning) to images of coral reefs (wild marine invertebrates) to classify healthy vs bleached corals for conservation monitoring.

title: Artificial Intelligence of Things Real-Time Fish Counting System
venue: IEEE International Conference on Advanced Telecommunication and Networking Technologies (ATNT)
reason: Fish counting system motivated by aquaculture (fish farming) management; no wild or free-ranging animals are described in the data.

title: Flamingo Diet and Health Detection Based on Colour Classification
venue: IEEE/ACM International Conference on Big Data Computing, Applications and Technologies (BDCAT)
reason: Applies CNN classification to images of flamingos (wild birds) for species filtering and plumage-colour-based health assessment framed as wildlife conservation; the paper does not say whether the animals were wild or captive.

title: Research on Re-Identification of Amur Tigers and Bengal Tigers
venue: International Conference on Big Data and Privacy Computing (BDPC)
reason: Individual re-identification of tigers using images photographed only in a zoo (Pingnan Xiongsen Animal World); no wild or free-ranging animals in the analysed data.

title: Animal-JEPA: Advancing Animal Behavior Studies Through Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture in Video Analysis
venue: IEEE International Conference on Big Data (BigData)
reason: Self-supervised video model for behaviour classification of laboratory mice in home cages; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: From Data to Defense: A Deep Learning Approach to Automated Wildlife Monitoring and Anti-Poaching Efforts
venue: 2024 IEEE Flagship International BIT Conference Next Generation Applications in Green Energy Technology Bitcon 2024
reason: Primary study that builds a dataset of wildlife and poaching indicators and trains YOLOv10 plus a convolutional autoencoder for detection; wildlife images are stated to be taken in natural habitats.

reason: Mudsnails were extracted from sediment cores held in experimental mesocosm tanks, preserved in formalin and imaged in batches on petri plates under a stereomicroscope; no images of free-ranging animals in their habitat are analysed.

title: Scalable semantic 3D mapping of coral reefs with deep learning
reason: Primary study developing deep-learning SfM and semantic segmentation on diver-collected underwater video of wild coral reefs (corals, fish, sea urchins) in the Gulf of Aqaba.

title: 3D photogrammetry and deep‐learning deliver accurate estimates of epibenthic biomass
reason: Deep-learning semantic segmentation combined with SfM photogrammetry on in situ underwater imagery of wild epibenthic invertebrates on rocky reefs to estimate biomass.

title: Monitoring fast‐moving animals—Building a customized camera system and evaluation toolset
reason: Custom Raspberry Pi camera system and YOLOv5 toolset to detect free-flying mason bees at nesting aids in the field; bees were released from placed cocoons but recorded free-flying outdoors.

title: HawkEar : A bird‐borne visual and acoustic platform for eavesdropping the behaviour of mobile animals
reason: Presents a hawk-borne audio/video recording platform; video is only used to record and position, analysis is acoustic. No computer vision image analysis is performed.

title: 3DKMI: A MATLAB package to generate shape signatures from Krawtchouk moments and an application to species delimitation in planktonic foraminifera
reason: Analyses CT scans of collected planktonic foraminifera shell specimens from ocean drilling cores. These are specimens, not images of free-ranging animals.

title: Eyes on nature: Embedded vision cameras for terrestrial biodiversity monitoring
reason: Presents an embedded vision camera with on-device blob detection, ROI classification and object detection, field-tested on free-ranging bats, insects and waterfowl; one use case has bees in experimental enclosures and one has flowers only.

title: BATS : Bat‐aggregated time series—A python‐based toolkit for landscape‐level monitoring of free‐tailed bats via weather radar
reason: Pixel-wise ML classification of gridded weather radar images to detect wild free-tailed bats across landscapes in California and Texas.

title: Towards an automated protocol for wildlife density estimation using camera‐traps
reason: Primary study applying machine learning detection and classification (MegaDetector, Wildlife Insights) to camera-trap images of wild mammals in an Italian reserve, and evaluating the effect on density estimates.

title: A transferable approach for quantifying benthic fish sizes and densities in annotated underwater images
reason: Machine vision software for sizing and counting benthic fish in underwater images; validated on captive round gobies and netted lake trout, and applied to free-ranging round gobies imaged by an AUV in Lake Michigan.

title: Using unmanned aerial vehicles to estimate body volume at scale for ecological monitoring
reason: Primary study developing a UAV structure-from-motion photogrammetry method to estimate 3D body volume of wild grey seals at colony scale from aerial images.

title: RapidBenthos : Automated segmentation and multi‐view classification of coral reef communities from photogrammetric reconstruction
reason: Primary study developing an automated segmentation and classification workflow (SAM + ReefCloud) on underwater photogrammetry imagery of wild coral reef benthic communities (corals, soft corals, sponges, mobile biota) on the Great Barrier Reef.

title: Inferring dolphin population status: using unoccupied aerial systems to quantify age‐structure
reason: UAS photogrammetry of free-ranging bottlenose dolphins, but body lengths were measured manually on extracted video stills and individuals were matched by human analysts; analysis is statistical (log-linear and growth models), with no automated image analysis.

title: Advancing social insect research through the development of an automated yellowjacket nest activity monitoring station using deep learning
reason: Deep-learning detection, caste classification and tracking of free-flying wasps from a wild V. germanica nest moved to a nest box. The wasps still entered and left the colony freely, so they count as free-ranging.

title: Citizen science and color pattern analysis indicate unreported Batesian mimicry between Neotropical snakes
reason: Quantitative colour pattern analysis (pixel colour binning and chi-squared colour distances) of photographs of wild Neotropical snakes, plus citizen-science photos of wild individuals; primary research.

title: recolorize: An R package for flexible colour segmentation of biological images
reason: Presents an R package for colour segmentation of biological images. It is applied to field photographs of wild Neolamprologus cichlids in Lake Tanganyika, as well as to wasp face images and bird museum specimens.

title: Behavioural plasticity compensates for adaptive loss of cricket song
reason: Image-based tracking of laboratory-reared crickets in an indoor arena in a sealed room; no images of wild free-ranging animals were analysed (the Hawaii field surveys were manual counts).

title: BioEncoder : A metric learning toolkit for comparative organismal biology
reason: Metric-learning toolkit evaluated on images of wild damselflies caught from natural monitored populations in Sweden and imaged in the lab; animals are the subject of a CV classification task.

title: Modeling individual growth reveals decreasing gray whale body length and correlations with ocean climate indices at multiple scales
reason: Applies drone-based aerial photogrammetry (image measurement of whale length) to free-ranging gray whales, with a Bayesian model accounting for photogrammetric uncertainty.

title: Comparison of manual, machine learning, and hybrid methods for video annotation to extract parental care data
reason: Primary study evaluating an open-source computer vision tool (DeepMeerkat) against manual, crowd-sourced and hybrid annotation on field videos of wild house sparrows at nest boxes.

title: A novel fish individual recognition method for precision farming based on knowledge distillation strategy and the range of the receptive field
reason: Individual recognition of fish for precision aquaculture; the paper frames the work entirely as farming and does not present wild, free-ranging animals as its subject.

title: Novel use of deep neural networks on photographic identification of epaulette sharks (Hemiscyllium ocellatum) across life stages
reason: Photo-ID with deep learning of epaulette sharks kept only in captive research facility tanks; no wild animals in analysed data.

title: A methodological workflow for quantitative colouration and colour pattern comparison reveals taxonomic and habitat‐level differences in the polymorphic fire salamander (Salamandra salamandra)
reason: Wild fire salamanders were captured in the field and photographed, and colour segmentation and pattern analysis were run on the images before release.

title: Abundance estimate of Eastern Caribbean sperm whales using large scale regional surveys
reason: Population estimate of wild sperm whales from photo-identification with mark-recapture statistics; the paper describes no computer vision method or automated image analysis, only fluke photo quality rating and matching on the Flukebook platform.

title: Automated body length and body condition measurements of whales from drone videos for rapid assessment of population health
reason: Develops deep learning tools (DeteX, XtraX) to detect free-ranging gray whales in drone videos and extract body length and body condition measurements.

title: Auto machine learning tools to distinguish between two killer whale ecotypes
reason: Applies AutoML image classification to field photographs of wild killer whales to distinguish two ecotypes (R-type and T-type) in the northwestern Pacific.

title: Pediatric Drone: Estimating morphometric measurements in spinner dolphin (Stenella longirostris) calves based on aerial photogrammetry
reason: Drone video frames of free-ranging spinner dolphins analysed with image-based photogrammetry to estimate body measurements. The measurements were taken by hand in ImageJ; this still counts as image analysis, but it is a borderline case.

title: First documented movement of wild killer whales (Orcinus orca) between Iceland and Norway
reason: Wild killer whales were photo-identified by manual visual comparison by trained researchers. No computer vision or automated image analysis was used.

title: Behavioral responses of Bigg's and Southern Resident killer whales ( Orcinus orca ) to uncrewed aerial vehicle‐based breath sample collection
reason: Wild killer whales were filmed from a UAV and a boat, but biologists scored their behaviour by watching the video manually. No computer vision or automated image analysis is applied; the only modelling is a statistical GLMM on the manual scores.

title: Automated detection of migrating Gray whales and measurement of their bearing in satellite imagery
reason: Primary study developing an object-based image analysis workflow to detect free-ranging migrating gray whales and measure their orientation in satellite imagery.

title: Energetic cost of gestation and prenatal growth in humpback whales
reason: UAS aerial photogrammetry images of wild humpback whales are analysed to measure body length, volume and condition. Automated fluke recognition is used to identify individuals.

title: Maternal investment, body condition and calf growth in humpback whales
reason: Drone video of wild humpback whales analysed by image-based photogrammetry (pixel measurements of length and width) to estimate body size and condition; individuals identified partly with Happywhale image recognition.

title: Receptive field enhancement and attention feature fusion network for underwater object detection
reason: Proposes a CNN detector (RF-YOLO) for underwater images of marine invertebrates (echinus, starfish, holothurian, scallop) from the URPC datasets. The paper does not say whether the animals are wild or farmed, but nothing suggests captivity.

title: Computer vision–guided open-source active commutator for neural imaging in freely behaving animals
reason: Markerless pose tracking of laboratory mice in behavioural arenas to control a commutator for neural imaging; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: An in situ digital synthesis strategy for the discovery and description of ocean life
reason: Applies in situ quantitative imaging (laser-sheet scanning with segmentation and 3D reconstruction, plenoptic depth imaging) from an ROV to wild deep-sea midwater animals for morphological description.

title: High-resolution outdoor videography of insects using Fast Lock-On tracking
reason: Image-based closed-loop tracking (bright-point detection with a Kalman filter) and high-speed video of marked bees flying freely outdoors, including from a drone. The bees come from managed or commercial colonies but forage freely outdoors. The locusts are reared in the lab.

title: Automated Identification and Counting of Saigas (Saiga tatarica) by Using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks in High-Resolution Satellite Images
reason: Applies deep CNNs to detect and count wild saiga antelopes in high-resolution satellite images of steppe in Russia.

title: An assessment of survey techniques using unmanned aerial vehicles to monitor Nile crocodiles (Crocodylus niloticus)
reason: Drone imagery of wild Nile crocodiles was searched by hand and crocodiles were counted and measured manually in ArcGIS. The only processing was orthomosaic stitching; no computer vision method was applied to the animals.

title: Cross-Domain Coral Image Classification Using Dual-Stream Hierarchical Neural Networks
reason: Proposes a deep learning method for classifying coral species in underwater reef images taken in the field (Red Sea, Moorea, Philippines/Indonesia, Taiwan); corals are wild animals and the stated subject.

title: LemurLounge: Lemurs' Individual-Level, Group, and Cross-Species Use of an Interactive Audio Device in Zoos
venue: CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
reason: Interactive audio device for zoo-housed lemurs triggered by infrared proximity sensors; video was manually coded by researchers, with no computer vision analysis. All animals are captive (zoo).

title: Augmented Reality at Zoo Exhibits: A Design Framework for Enhancing the Zoo Experience
venue: CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
reason: HCI design-framework paper on augmented reality at zoo exhibits, based on scoping reviews, a stakeholder workshop and a qualitative field trip. It does no computer-vision analysis of animal images; the AR prototype only recognises animal pictures on zoo signage. All animals are captive zoo animals.

title: Investigating Lemurs Sensory Modality in Technologies: How do Lemurs Engage with Single and Multimodal Stimuli in Zoos?
venue: Extended Abstracts of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI EA)
reason: Animal-computer interaction study with an enrichment device for six zoo-housed red ruffed lemurs. Lemurs were detected with infrared distance sensors, and the recorded videos were only used manually to check triggers. No computer vision method is applied, and the animals are captive only.

title: Reviving the Context: Camera Trap Species Classification as Link Prediction on Multimodal Knowledge Graphs
venue: ACM International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM)
reason: Proposes a species classification method (COSMO) evaluated on camera trap images of wild animals from two wildlife datasets.

title: Transparency in the Wild: Navigating Transparency in a Deployed AI System to Broaden Need-Finding Approaches
reason: Case study on transparency of a deployed wildlife individual-identification CV system (Wildbook). The authors also trained and tested the MiewID re-identification model on a beluga whale image dataset and generated saliency maps for it.

title: An Underwater Organism Image Dataset and a Lightweight Module Designed for Object Detection Networks
venue: ACM Transactions on Multimedia Computing Communications and Applications
reason: All analysed images were recorded in an aquarium (Xiaomeisha Ocean World); no wild or free-ranging animals are in the data.

title: Underwater Image Captioning Based on Feature Fusion
venue: International Conference on Image and Graphics Processing (ICIGP)
reason: Generic underwater image captioning method tested on an image enhancement benchmark. Fish, corals and turtles appear only as salient objects alongside divers, shipwrecks and statues; wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Context or Clutter? Efficiently Matching Objects Across Scenes
reason: Annotation pipeline and user study for matching objects (curtains, lamps, desks) in hotel room images; no animals or wildlife involved.

title: FathomGPT: A natural language interface for interactively exploring ocean science data
venue: ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology (UIST)
reason: System paper that applies computer vision (ViT feature-based image similarity search, Segment Anything segmentation, colour-based pattern extraction) to FathomNet images of wild marine animals. The main contribution is a natural language interface.

title: Underwater Fish Tracking Algorithm Based on ViBE Detection and Covariance Matrix
venue: International Conference on Image, Video and Signal Processing (IVSP)
reason: Proposes a classical computer vision tracking method for fish in underwater videos, including Fish4Knowledge videos and videos from an underwater robot, aimed at natural waters.

title: Towards Labeling-free Fine-grained Animal Pose Estimation
venue: ACM International Conference on Multimedia (ACM MM)
reason: Proposes a pose estimation method (FreeNet) evaluated on animal pose datasets covering wild species (e.g., tigers, 54 species in AP-10k) alongside domestic animals (cat, dog, sheep, cow, horse).

title: From Persons to Animals: Transferring Person Re-Identification Methods to a Multi-Species Animal Domain
reason: Applies person re-identification models to images of wild common toads (rescued during migration, filmed and released) plus a second dataset of zoo animals; wild animals together with captive ones.

title: Poster: Towards Low-Power Comprehensive Biodiversity Monitoring
venue: ACM Conference on Embedded Networked Sensor Systems (SenSys)
reason: The paper presents a low-power multi-sensor device and a learned scheduler. All event detection and analysis runs on audio (BirdNET, Goertzel filtering and a spectrogram CNN). The camera is only triggered by the PIR sensor, and no images are analysed.

title: Ph.D Forum: Towards Low-Power Comprehensive Biodiversity Monitoring
venue: ACM Conference on Embedded Networked Sensor Systems (SenSys)
reason: The prototype device has a PIR-triggered camera, but the only data analysed are audio recordings of bird vocalizations (BirdNET, Goertzel filtering, a spectrogram CNN). No images or video are analysed.

title: Avian Activity Classification Using Recurrent Networks to Fuse Videos with Metadata on Imbalanced Datasets
venue: International Conference on Computing and Artificial Intelligence (ICCAI)
reason: Develops a deep learning model to classify activities of free-ranging birds in video recorded at operational solar energy facilities.

title: A Training Strategy of Flying Bird Object Detection Model Based on Improved Self-Paced Learning Algorithm
venue: International Conference on Cyber Security, Artificial Intelligence and Digital Economy (CSAIDE)
reason: Proposes a training strategy for a detection model of flying birds in surveillance video; birds are free-flying animals, so the paper meets the inclusion criteria.

title: Machine Learning Tool for Wildlife Image Classification
venue: International Conference on Machine Learning Technologies (ICMLT)
reason: Primary study that trains a DenseNet-121-based classifier on camera trap images (Snapshot Safari) and web/digital-camera images of wild animal species and deploys it as a web tool.

title: CR-Cross: Cross Domain Coral Recognitions with Reject Options For Coral Conservation
venue: ACM SIGCAS/SIGCHI Conference on Computing and Sustainable Societies (COMPASS)
reason: Proposes a cross-domain image classification method for corals (animals) using underwater coral reef image patches from natural marine regions.

title: A Novel Underwater Marine Dataset with Diverse Scenarios for Robust Object Detection
reason: All images were collected in public aquariums (Delhi, Udaipur, Singapore); no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Multi-level Approach for Detection and Identification of Camouflaged Lifeform: A comprehensive detailing of identifying camouflaged Lifeforms
reason: Proposes a multilevel computer vision approach (IR-based segmentation plus Google Lens API) to detect and identify camouflaged animals in natural-environment images from the C.H.A.M.E.L.E.ON dataset. The paper names ecological monitoring as an application. The paper does not say how the images were obtained, so subject_type is coded wild_free_ranging from its description of the images as natural-environment scenes.

title: Detection of Small Birds in Flight Pathways
reason: Primary study applying YOLOv8 to detect birds in images and webcam video for airport bird-strike mitigation; birds are the subject, though the paper does not state whether the birds in the Roboflow dataset or webcam frames are wild or captive.

title: Bird Action Recognition in Wetlands using Deep Learning
reason: Primary study applying deep learning image and video classification models to recognise actions of wild birds recorded in a protected wetland, with a new dataset.

title: MiTREE: Multi-input Transformer Ecoregion Encoder for Species Distribution Modelling
venue: ACM SIGSPATIAL International Workshop on AI for Geographic Knowledge Discovery (GeoAI)
reason: Species distribution modelling from satellite imagery and environmental rasters of habitat; the images show landscapes, not animals. Bird encounter rates come from citizen-science checklists and are used only as labels.

title: AI-Powered Animal Recognition and Tracking via Drone-Based Thermal Imaging: A User-Centric Mobile Application
reason: The system is aimed at wildlife monitoring with drone thermal imaging, but the only animal imagery the paper shows or describes is of cows in an open field; no wild or free-ranging non-domestic animals are stated in the analysed data, and the evaluation is a usability study of a prototype.

title: An Individual Identification Method for Cetaceans Based on EfficientNet
venue: International Conference on Machine Learning and Machine Intelligence (MLMI)
reason: Proposes a CNN-based individual identification method for whales and dolphins on a large cetacean image dataset; the paper does not state how or where the images were taken, so the wild status of the animals is not explicitly reported.

title: Marine Biodiversity for an Inclusive Society
venue: International Conference on Software Development and Technologies for Enhancing Accessibility and Fighting Info-exclusion (DSAI)
reason: Fine-grained visual classification of marine fish species on aggregated datasets, most of them underwater images of free-ranging fish, with some controlled and out-of-water images.

title: Automated Depth Sensing-Based Computer Vision for Dog Tail Wagging Interpretation
reason: The study analyses overhead depth-camera video of owned pet dogs in a controlled indoor experiment to measure tail wagging; no wild or free-ranging animals are involved.

title: Play That Trunky Music: Development of an Auditory Enrichment Device for Elephants in Zoos
reason: Auditory enrichment device for three zoo-housed African elephants at Zoo Atlanta. Engagement was measured with time-of-flight sensors and manually annotated video, so no computer vision was applied to the animals and all animals are captive.

title: Improving the wild boar detection algorithm of YOLOv8n
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv8n detector for wild boars on a self-built image dataset whose images were mostly captured in the wild.

title: Reliable Bird Species Recognition in Nordic Environments through Convolutional Neural Networks: A Comprehensive Performance Study
reason: CNN-based species classification of images of wild Finnish bird species sourced from the Macaulay Library.

title: YOLOv7-AD: An Efficient and Accurate Underwater Object Detection Algorithm Based on YOLOv7
venue: International Conference on Electronic Information Technology and Computer Engineering (EITCE)
reason: Proposes a detection algorithm for marine fauna (sea cucumbers, scallops, sea urchins, starfish) in underwater images from real marine environments.

title: Bird Detection Method for Airport Perimeters Based on an Improved YOLOv8
venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering (ICAICE)
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv8 detector for wild birds in airport surveillance imagery (AirBirds dataset) to reduce bird strikes.

title: Research and Application of YOLOv10 Algorithm Based on Image Recognition
venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Computer Engineering (ICAICE)
reason: Applies YOLO object detection to images of 54 Chinese Grade I protected wildlife species to support wildlife monitoring. The paper does not say where the images came from or whether they show free-ranging animals, but wildlife conservation is the stated application.

title: PKE-UIC: A Prior Knowledge-Enhanced Underwater Image Captioning Model
venue: International Conference on Sensors, Signal and Image Processing (SSIP)
reason: The paper captions general underwater scenes (coral, fish, divers) from a captioning dataset that mixes underwater and terrestrial scenes. Animals are not the stated subject; the work is generic scene captioning.

title: A New Efficient Classifier for Bird Classification Based on Transfer Learning
reason: Deep learning (transfer learning with EfficientNetB5) classification of 525 bird species from images; non-domestic bird species, motivated by nature conservation; primary method study.

title: Retracted: A Novel Attention-Based Lightweight Network for Multiscale Object Detection in Underwater Images
reason: The text is only a retraction notice. It has no methods, data or image analysis to code, and no animals are described as subjects.

title: Object detection of the bornean orangutan nests using drone and YOLOv5
venue: IAES International Journal of Artificial Intelligence
reason: Primary study applying YOLOv5 object detection to drone imagery of wild Bornean orangutan nests (direct signs of wild animals) in forests of Central Kalimantan.

title: Chelonia mydas detection and image extraction from noisy field recordings
venue: IAES International Journal of Artificial Intelligence
reason: YOLOv7 detection and cropping of wild nesting green sea turtles in field video recordings from a nesting beach.

title: You only look once v8 for fish species identification
venue: IAES International Journal of Artificial Intelligence
reason: The 21 classes are ornamental or pet fish: koi varieties, goldfish varieties (ranchu, oranda), black tetra, botia, angelfish ("manfish") and others. The images come from Kaggle and Roboflow. The paper does not show that any images are of wild, free-ranging fish.

title: New Miocene fossil taxa illuminate the evolution and paleobiogeography of the Ponto-Caspian gammaroid amphipod radiation
reason: Paleontological taxonomy and phylogenetics of fossil amphipods; photographs of fossil imprints are used only for manual drawing and measurement, with no computer vision method.

title: Efficient Highlighting of Visual Targets in Complex Natural Scenes
venue: Proceedings of the Human Factors and Ergonomics Society Annual Meeting
reason: Human factors experiment on how people visually search camera-trap images with highlighting (bounding-box outlines vs. blur). The study measures human accuracy and response times. It does not develop or evaluate a computer vision method; it only reuses precomputed MegaDetector boxes.

title: Fine-grained image classification on bats using VGG16-CBAM: a practical example with 7 horseshoe bats taxa (CHIROPTERA: Rhinolophidae: Rhinolophus) from Southern China
reason: CNN-based species classification of facial photographs of live wild horseshoe bats captured during field surveys, photographed and released.

title: Automated age grading of female Culex pipiens by an optical sensor system coupled to a mosquito trap
reason: Age classification of laboratory-reared mosquitoes from optical wingbeat sensor signals (frequency features with XGBoost); no image or video analysis.

title: Labeled images of emerged salmonids in a riverine environment
reason: Data note presenting annotated surveillance images of free-ranging salmonids at a river weir, intended for object detection models; GMM background subtraction and object detectors were used to build it.

title: Rapid assessment of human–elephant conflict: a crime science approach
reason: Qualitative social-science study (field observation, focus groups, interviews) of human-elephant conflict in Tamil Nadu; no image or video analysis or computer vision.

title: Hyperspectral lidar for monitoring high-resolution activity patterns of African stingless bee species
reason: Study monitors managed stingless bee colonies kept at a bee center (meliponiculture/beekeeping) with a hyperspectral lidar; beekeeping falls under E-AGRI.

title: Gaze tracking of large-billed crows ( Corvus macrorhynchos ) in a motion capture system
reason: Wild-caught large-billed crows were housed in an outdoor aviary and tested only in a motion-capture room built inside that aviary. All analysed data come from captive animals in an enclosure.

title: Research on Underwater Target Detection Model Based on ResNet50_SIMAM
reason: The paper applies a CNN (ResNet50 with SimAM attention) to underwater images of aquatic organisms, such as grey sharks, to classify them by species. The paper does not say where the images come from, but they show underwater animals, which are presumably wild.

title: Intelligent Detection Method for Chinese Sturgeon Based on YOLOv8
reason: Applies a YOLOv8-based detector to underwater video images of Chinese sturgeon, a non-domestic, endangered species, for conservation monitoring. The paper does not say where or under what conditions the footage was recorded.

title: Research on Monitoring Rodent Pests in Ruoergai Alpine Grassland Based on Low-Altitude Remote Sensing
reason: Applies object-based image analysis and supervised classification to UAV RGB images to extract burrows (direct signs) of wild plateau rodents in alpine grassland.

title: Integrated Instance Segmentation Network with Prototypes in Marine Environment
reason: Proposes a prototype-integrated instance segmentation network for marine organisms in underwater images (TrashCan and DUT-USEG datasets), which show wild marine animals.

title: DETECTION OF DEER IN IMAGES TO ACCOUNT POPULATIONS BY COMPUTER VISION METHODS
venue: Siberian Journal of Life Sciences and Agriculture
reason: Applies a CNN detector (Faster R-CNN ResNet50) to images of deer in different habitats for population counting; primary research with animals as subject. Wild vs. herded status of the depicted deer is not explicitly stated, but the images are described as from different natural habitats and the stated aim includes wild deer populations.

title: FishMOT: A Simple and Effective Method for Fish Tracking Based on IoU Matching
reason: Fish multi-object tracking evaluated only on idtracker.ai overhead videos of fish groups with a clear background (tracking-tool benchmark set-up). The paper does not describe any wild or free-ranging animals, and its stated application is aquaculture.

title: Short Communication: Photogrammetric analysis of the number and pattern of dorsal cranium scale of juvenile green iguana (Iguana iguana)
reason: Photo-identification (I3S) of juvenile green iguanas kept at a veterinary faculty and photographed on a studio set; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Recording animal-view videos of the natural world using a novel camera system and software package
reason: Develops a multispectral camera system and image-processing pipeline producing animal-view videos, applied to free-living animals (mockingbirds, bees, butterflies) in natural settings as well as museum specimens.

title: Hyperspectral imaging in animal coloration research: A user-friendly pipeline for image generation, analysis, and integration with 3D modeling
reason: Hyperspectral imaging and 3D modelling of avian museum specimens in a laboratory; no images of live free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: A toolkit for the dynamic study of air sacs in siamang and other elastic circular structures
reason: Computer vision tracking of air sacs in siamang recorded only in a zoo/wildlife park; no wild free-ranging animal data analysed (single YouTube frog clip used only as illustration).

title: Advanced vision transformers and open-set learning for robust mosquito classification: A novel approach to entomological studies
reason: Primary study applying vision transformers and open-set learning to classify images of ten mosquito species (non-domestic insects) from merged public image datasets. The paper does not state whether the mosquitoes were wild-caught, lab-reared or specimens, so the wild/free-ranging condition is unverified; included because no exclusion criterion is supported by the text.

title: Deep learning workflow to support in-flight processing of digital aerial imagery for wildlife population surveys
reason: Primary study developing deep learning filtering and detection of wild marine birds (sea ducks) in crewed aerial survey imagery.

title: Insect detect: An open-source DIY camera trap for automated insect monitoring
reason: Develops a camera trap with deep-learning detection, tracking and classification of free-ranging flower-visiting insects in orchard meadows; additional lab-reared hoverflies are used for a tracking test.

title: Performance of different automatic photographic identification software for larvae and adults of the European fire salamander
reason: Primary study comparing photo-identification software (computer vision pattern matching) on images of European fire salamanders; adults photographed in the wild in the field, larvae wild-caught and photographed in the laboratory.

title: Coral reefs in transition: Temporal photoquadrat analyses and validation of underwater hyperspectral imaging for resource-efficient monitoring in Guam
reason: Deep-learning classification of underwater hyperspectral scans of a wild coral reef; benthic categories include animals (scleractinian corals, sponges, octocorals/hydrozoans) alongside algae and substrate.

title: Digital image processing: A new tool for morphological measurements of freshwater turtles under rehabilitation
reason: Images analysed show only rescued turtles housed at a breeding and rehabilitation centre (captive); no free-ranging animals imaged.

title: Killer whale respiration rates
reason: Drone video of wild killer whales was only viewed by people to count breaths and label behaviour. The behaviour model (HHMM) was run on time-depth tag data, not on images, so no computer vision was applied.

title: Deep learning for identifying bee species from images of wings and pinned specimens
reason: All analysed images are of pinned bee specimens and detached or flattened wings from research collections, photographed under a microscope or scanner; no images of wild, free-ranging animals.

title: A method to estimate prey density from single-camera images: A case study with chinstrap penguins and Antarctic krill
reason: Primary study training a CNN frame classifier on animal-borne video from a free-ranging chinstrap penguin and estimating density of wild Antarctic krill from the images.

title: DNA barcodes from over-a-century-old type specimens shed light on the taxonomy of a group of rare butterflies (Lepidoptera: Nymphalidae: Calinaginae)
reason: Image-based wing colour pattern analysis is performed only on photographs of museum specimens (NHMUK), not on wild free-ranging animals.

title: Smartphone region-wise image indoor localization using deep learning for indoor tourist attraction
reason: The images are smartphone photos of fish tanks in a public aquarium, classified to localize visitors. The only animals are captive fish in aquarium tanks.

title: A semi-automated method using object-based image analysis (OBIA) to detect and enumerate beluga whales in summer from very high-resolution (VHR) satellite imagery
reason: Primary study developing a semi-automated object-based image analysis method to detect wild beluga whales in open Arctic water from VHR satellite imagery.

title: Penguin colony georegistration using camera pose estimation and phototourism
reason: Primary study presenting a semi-automated computer vision pipeline (SAM segmentation, camera pose estimation) on ground photographs of wild Antarctic penguin colonies.

title: FEB-YOLOv8: A multi-scale lightweight detection model for underwater object detection
reason: Proposes a lightweight YOLOv8-based detector for underwater marine organisms (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish) on the DUO and URPC2020 seabed image datasets. The paper does not say whether the animals are wild or farmed; it is included as marine organism detection.

title: Predicting pack-ice seal occupancy of ice floes along the Western Antarctic Peninsula
reason: Primary study applying a CNN seal detector and CNN sea-ice segmentation to very-high-resolution satellite imagery of wild Antarctic pack-ice seals, then modelling seal counts per ice floe.

title: AI-based coral species discrimination: A case study of the Siderastrea Atlantic Complex
reason: Images are scanning electron micrographs and stereomicroscope images of cleaned coral skeletons. The skeletons were collected from wild colonies and deposited in a zoological collection, so the analysed data show specimens only, not free-ranging animals.

title: Insect diversity estimation in polarimetric lidar
reason: Polarimetric Scheimpflug lidar (imaging linear CMOS detector) observations of wild free-flying insects over a pond, clustered to estimate insect diversity; primary research on wild animals with lidar-based sensing.

title: Deep learning-based image classification of sea turtles using object detection and instance segmentation models

reason: Applies a deep-learning object detector (MAIA/Faster R-CNN) to seafloor images of wild deep-sea benthic megafauna in the Clarion-Clipperton Zone; primary research.

title: Comparison of infrared thermography of the blowhole mucosa with rectal temperatures in killer whales (Orcinus orca)

title: Semi-supervised learning advances species recognition for aquatic biodiversity monitoring
reason: Primary study proposing a semi-supervised deep learning method for aquatic species (fish family) recognition from images of the FishNet dataset, with biodiversity monitoring as the stated application. The paper does not state whether the animals in the images are wild or captive.

title: Drone-based monitoring of intertidal blue mussel beds in the Wadden Sea – comparison of a threshold and two machine learning approaches
reason: Primary study applying threshold, Random Forest and SVM pixel classification to drone imagery of wild intertidal blue mussel beds in the Wadden Sea.

title: DeformableFishNet: a high-precision lightweight target detector for underwater fish identification
reason: Proposes a lightweight fish detector evaluated on underwater images of free-ranging fish (Fish4Knowledge, Brackish, RUOD) plus an author-collected park dataset of koi and tilapia.

title: Development and operation of a novel non-invasive opto-acoustic underwater fish observatory in Kiel Bight, Southwestern Baltic Sea
reason: Primary study that applies a YOLOv5-based stereo video pipeline (plus imaging sonar) to detect, classify, count and size wild fish and other marine organisms recorded in situ by an underwater observatory in Kiel Fjord.

title: Localization and tracking of beluga whales in aerial video using deep learning
reason: Primary study applying deep-learning detection and tracking to UAV video of wild beluga whales in the Canadian High Arctic.

title: What is hidden under our pontoons? Abundance and distribution of filter feeders (bivalves and tunicates) in the port area revealed. Artificial intelligence: an interesting analysis tool?
reason: Primary study applying YOLOv4 detection to underwater photographs of free-living bivalves and tunicates growing under marina pontoons.

title: RUSNet: Robust fish segmentation in underwater videos based on adaptive selection of optical flow
reason: Proposes a fish segmentation network evaluated on underwater videos of wild fish in natural coastal and estuarine habitats.

title: Ship-based RPA operations for cetacean research in Antarctica: progress, opportunities and challenges
reason: Paper characterises drone flight operations (flight metrics vs. environmental conditions) and reviews literature; no computer vision or image analysis method is developed or applied to the whale imagery.

title: A comparison of machine learning methods for quantifying self-grooming behavior in mice
reason: Compares automated behaviour analysis pipelines for self-grooming in laboratory C57BL/6 mice recorded in a home-cage apparatus; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: SARTAB, a scalable system for automated real-time behavior detection based on animal tracking and Region Of Interest analysis: validation on fish courtship behavior
reason: Real-time behavior detection system validated on cichlid fish kept in laboratory aquarium tanks for neurogenomic sampling; no wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: CLIB: Contrastive learning of ignoring background for underwater fish image classification
reason: Primary study proposing a contrastive learning method for classifying fish species in underwater images, motivated by ocean health monitoring. title: Brandt’s vole hole detection and counting method based on deep learning and unmanned aircraft system
reason: Deep learning object detection on UAS images of burrow holes (direct signs) of wild Brandt's voles in a natural steppe; primary research.

title: A Machine Vision System for Monitoring Wild Birds on Poultry Farms to Prevent Avian Influenza
reason: Primary study applying YOLOX and YOLOv5 object detection to video frames of free-ranging wild birds (gadwall, brown thrasher) recorded outside a poultry house.

title: Leveraging Hyperspectral Images for Accurate Insect Classification with a Novel Two-Branch Self-Correlation Approach
reason: Insect samples were imaged one batch at a time on a lab hyperspectral imaging stage under a fixed halogen lamp. No free-ranging animals were imaged in the field, and the work is framed around agricultural pests.

title: Overview and Comparison of Deep Neural Networks for Wildlife Recognition Using Infrared Images
reason: Despite the journal label 'Review', the paper is primary research: it introduces a new infrared dataset of Slovak wild animals in natural environments and experimentally compares CNN architectures for classifying them.

title: Automatic Detection of Feral Pigeons in Urban Environments Using Deep Learning

title: 3D Morphological Scanning and Environmental Correlates of Bufo gargarizans in the Yellow River Basin
reason: Wild-caught toads were killed, fixed in formalin and scanned indoors as specimens with a structured light scanner. No images of free-ranging animals are analysed, so the paper falls under the specimen part of E-CAPTIVE.

title: DiffusionFR: Species Recognition of Fish in Blurry Scenarios via Diffusion and Attention
reason: Proposes a deep-learning method (diffusion deblurring plus attention ResNet50) for fish species recognition on images from Fish4Knowledge, field photography and the Internet; the paper does not describe the fish as captive or farmed.

title: Dolphin-WET—Development of a Welfare Evaluation Tool for Bottlenose Dolphins (Tursiops truncatus) under Human Care
reason: Development of a welfare evaluation tool (indicators, scoring, questionnaires, app) for captive bottlenose dolphins; no image or video analysis is performed.

title: A Metric-Based Few-Shot Learning Method for Fish Species Identification with Limited Samples
reason: Proposes a few-shot CNN method for fish species classification, evaluated on three public datasets of underwater fish images, including images taken in the Adriatic and 'in the wild'.

title: Learning Rich Feature Representation and State Change Monitoring for Accurate Animal Target Tracking
reason: Proposes a correlation-filter tracker for animals, evaluated on animal videos that include wildlife habitats alongside domestic settings.

title: Minding the Minds: A Primer on Cognitive Challenge for Marine Mammals in Human Care
reason: Review/primer on cognitive enrichment for marine mammals in zoos and aquariums; no computer vision or image analysis and no wild animals.

title: Automatic Identification of Pangolin Behavior Using Deep Learning Based on Temporal Relative Attention Mechanism
reason: Behaviour recognition on video of captive pangolins housed in cages at a wildlife rescue centre; the paper states that no outdoor (wild) data were used.

title: A Serial Multi-Scale Feature Fusion and Enhancement Network for Amur Tiger Re-Identification
reason: The re-ID network is trained and evaluated only on the ATRW dataset, which the paper states was built from video clips of tigers in about 10 zoos in China; no wild or free-ranging animal images are analysed.

title: Automated Observations of Dogs’ Resting Behaviour Patterns Using Artificial Intelligence and Their Similarity to Behavioural Observations
reason: The study analyses CCTV video of domestic dogs housed in university kennels to classify sleep; no wild or free-ranging animals are in the data.

title: Application of Machine Learning for Automating Behavioral Tracking of Captive Bornean Orangutans (Pongo Pygmaeus)

title: Detection Probability and Bias in Machine-Learning-Based Unoccupied Aerial System Non-Breeding Waterfowl Surveys

title: An Intelligent Fishery Detection Method Based on Cross-Domain Image Feature Fusion
reason: Proposes a CNN-based fish detection model for multi-scene fish images, aimed at fishery ecological monitoring and fish diversity research. The paper does not state whether the fish are wild or farmed, and it also evaluates on public fish datasets.

title: A Study on the Automation of Fish Species Recognition and Body Length Measurement System
reason: Applies object detection (RT-DETR) to smartphone images of wild-caught fish and crustaceans of TAC-managed species at fish markets, for species recognition and body-length measurement in fishery resource management. title: Application of Aerial Photographs and Coastal Field Data to Understand Sea Turtle Landing and Spawning Behavior at Kili-Kili Beach, Indonesia

title: WormCNN-Assisted Establishment and Analysis of Glycation Stress Models in C. elegans: Insights into Disease and Healthy Aging
reason: Laboratory study of the model organism C. elegans imaged by microscope in 384-well plates; no wild or free-ranging animals.

reason: A CNN classifies images of fish species caught from a lake by an unmanned boat for capture fisheries, not aquaculture. Fish are the subject and the work is primary research.

reason: CNN classification of in situ images of free-living marine plankton (including zooplankton such as copepods and krill) recorded with a towed Video Plankton Recorder in the open ocean.

reason: 3D laser body-shape measurement of giraffes, okapi and black rhinoceros kept only in three Japanese zoos; no wild animals.

title: Automated Hyperspectral Feature Selection and Classification of Wildlife Using Uncrewed Aerial Vehicles
reason: UAV hyperspectral pixel classification of cows, horses and goats at a university animal research centre and a ranch, plus deer held at a university deer laboratory; no wild or free-ranging animals are in the analysed data.

title: Community-Based Monitoring for Rapid Assessment of Nearshore Coral Reefs Amid Disturbances in Teahupo’o, Tahiti
reason: Structure-from-Motion photogrammetry is applied to underwater images of wild coral reef communities to build 3D reconstructions and orthomosaics for assessing coral composition; corals are animals and the subject of the study. Colony annotation itself was manual.

title: Combining Multi-View UAV Photogrammetry, Thermal Imaging, and Computer Vision Can Derive Cost-Effective Ecological Indicators for Habitat Assessment
reason: Primary study applying object detection (thresholding, decision trees, CNNs) to UAV thermal imagery of wild migratory waterfowl in Nebraska wetlands for habitat assessment.

title: Wildlife Real-Time Detection in Complex Forest Scenes Based on YOLOv5s Deep Learning Network
reason: Proposes WL-YOLO, a lightweight YOLOv5s-based detector, trained and evaluated on camera-trap images of wild animals collected in Chinese national parks and nature reserves.

title: Detecting Moving Wildlife Using the Time Difference between Two Thermal Airborne Images
reason: Primary study proposing deep learning classification and detection methods to extract moving sika deer from pairs of airborne thermal images captured over Nara Park, Japan.

title: Identification of Rare Wildlife in the Field Environment Based on the Improved YOLOv5 Model
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv5 detector for rare wild mammals in camera-trap images from Giant Panda National Park.

title: Burrow Opening Measurements of Intertidal Macroinvertebrates from Optical Drone Images
reason: Image analysis (thresholding and segmentation) of drone images of burrow openings, which are direct signs of wild intertidal crabs, used to measure burrow size.

title: CLIP-Driven Few-Shot Species-Recognition Method for Integrating Geographic Information
reason: Proposes a CLIP-based few-shot species classification method evaluated on community-science (iNaturalist 2021) images of mammals, reptiles and amphibians, with wildlife species recognition as the stated application.

title: Detection of Coral Reef Bleaching by Multitemporal Sentinel-2 Data Using the PU-Bagging Algorithm: A Feasibility Study at Lizard Island
reason: Proposes a machine-learning method (PU-bagging) to map bleached wild corals from multitemporal Sentinel-2 satellite imagery at Lizard Island.

title: A Cross-Modal Semantic Alignment and Feature Fusion Method for Bionic Drone and Bird Recognition
reason: The paper is about recognising bionic drones (vehicles) for national defence. Birds appear only as the confounding class, so wildlife is not the stated subject. Where the bird images came from is not reported.

title: UAV-Based 3D-Calibration of Thermal Cameras for Bat Flight Monitoring in Large Outdoor Environments
reason: Primary study proposing a UAV-based 3D calibration for stereo thermal cameras and applying image processing to detect and 3D-reconstruct flight tracks of free-flying bats at wind farms.

title: Assessing Derawan Island’s Coral Reefs over Two Decades: A Machine Learning Classification Perspective
reason: Pixel-level benthic habitat / land-cover mapping (coral, sand/rubble, seagrass, mixed bottom) from satellite and UAV imagery; habitat mapping rather than vision on animals themselves.

title: Reptile Identification for Endemic and Invasive Alien Species Using Transfer Learning Approaches
reason: Primary study applying transfer-learning CNN classifiers to web-sourced photographs of four reptile species (two endemic, two invasive) of Gran Canaria. Images are mostly of free-ranging animals, but at least one example is captioned as a zoo photograph, so subject type is coded as mixed.

title: The Potential of Diffusion-Based Near-Infrared Image Colorization
reason: Primary study proposing a diffusion-based NIR colorization method for camera trap images of wild animals (Snapshot Serengeti), also evaluated through species classification.

title: YOLOv8-MU: An Improved YOLOv8 Underwater Detector Based on a Large Kernel Block and a Multi-Branch Reparameterization Module
reason: Proposes a YOLOv8-based detector for underwater marine organisms (echinus, starfish, holothurian, scallop) on URPC seabed datasets, and also evaluates it on an Aquarium dataset. Marine life detection is the stated application.

title: Fine-Grained Cross-Modal Semantic Consistency in Natural Conservation Image Data from a Multi-Task Perspective
reason: Vision-language method (classification, cross-modal retrieval, captioning) whose stated application is conservation-area species images; trained and evaluated on iNaturalist2018 (8142 species) and tested zero-shot on wildlife datasets.

title: Methodological Selection of Optimal Features for Object Classification Based on Stereovision System
reason: Primary study classifying wild birds (big raptors vs other birds vs aeroplanes) from features extracted from stereovision camera images and video at a wind farm.

title: Lizard Body Temperature Acquisition and Lizard Recognition Using Artificial Intelligence
reason: Lizards kept in captivity are filmed inside a cardboard box in a controlled laboratory environment; no wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: A Deep Learning Framework for Real-Time Bird Detection and Its Implications for Reducing Bird Strike Incidents
reason: Proposes a spatiotemporal CNN to detect flying birds in images for airport bird-strike prevention, evaluated on a public bird-vs-drone image dataset. The paper does not explicitly say the birds are wild; this is inferred from the in-flight, airport context.

title: Evaluating Thermal Infrared Drone Flight Parameters on Spider Monkey Detection in Tropical Forests
reason: Thermal drone videos of wild spider monkeys were reviewed and counted manually by human coders; no computer vision or automated image analysis method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Computer-Simulated Virtual Image Datasets to Train Machine Learning Models for Non-Invasive Fish Detection in Recirculating Aquaculture
reason: Fish detection for farmed rainbow trout in a recirculating aquaculture tank, trained on simulated and real in-tank images; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: RSE-YOLOv8: An Algorithm for Underwater Biological Target Detection
reason: Proposes a YOLOv8-based detector for underwater benthic invertebrates (sea urchins, starfish, conchs, scallops) in underwater images, with ecological assessment named as the application.

title: MPE-HRNetL: A Lightweight High-Resolution Network for Multispecies Animal Pose Estimation
reason: Proposes a lightweight CNN for multispecies animal pose estimation, evaluated on AP-10K (54 animal species, including wild ones such as giraffe, zebra, antelope) and on Animal Pose (domestic dog, cat, cow, horse, sheep).

title: Implementation of an Intelligent Trap for Effective Monitoring and Control of the Aedes aegypti Mosquito
reason: Primary study applying YOLOv7 detection/classification to images of mosquitoes, bees and butterflies, with a smart trap field-tested on free-ranging Aedes aegypti in urban Brazil.

title: Evaluation of Automated Object-Detection Algorithms for Koala Detection in Infrared Aerial Imagery
reason: Proposes and evaluates a bio-inspired detection algorithm on drone thermal imagery of free-ranging koalas in eucalyptus plantations.

title: Multi-Scale Feature Fusion Enhancement for Underwater Object Detection
reason: Proposes an object detector for underwater images and evaluates it on datasets of free-living marine organisms (DUO: echinus, starfish, holothurian, scallop; Brackish: fish, crabs, starfish). It also uses two underwater trash datasets.

title: Automated Pipeline for Robust Cat Activity Detection Based on Deep Learning and Wearable Sensor Data
reason: Activity recognition of household cats from wearable accelerometer, gyroscope and magnetometer signals with a 1D-CNN; video is used only for manual ground-truth labelling, no image analysis is performed.

title: Detection of Critical Parts of River Crab Based on Lightweight YOLOv7-SPSD
reason: Detection of crab tails on farmed (aquaculture) river crabs from breeding pools for automated food processing; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Sleeping and Eating Behavior Recognition of Horses Based on an Improved SlowFast Network
reason: Behaviour recognition of domestic horses kept in individual stalls at a horse base; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Improving Object Detection for Time-Lapse Imagery Using Temporal Features in Wildlife Monitoring
reason: Proposes a temporal-feature object detection method evaluated on time-lapse camera-trap images of wild breeding petrels on Round Island, Mauritius.

title: Towards Context-Rich Automated Biodiversity Assessments: Deriving AI-Powered Insights from Camera Trap Data
reason: Primary study combining a YOLOv10-X detector and a vision-language model on camera trap images of wild Sub-Saharan African mammals and birds.

title: ApeTI: A Thermal Image Dataset for Face and Nose Segmentation with Apes
reason: Thermal images of six chimpanzees filmed in a testing room at the Leipzig Zoo research center; there are no wild or free-ranging animals in the data.

title: Hybrid Intelligence for Marine Biodiversity: Integrating Citizen Science with AI for Enhanced Intertidal Conservation Efforts at Cape Santiago, Taiwan
reason: Applies YOLOv5s object detection to citizen-science photographs of wild intertidal marine organisms on a rocky bench at Cape Santiago, Taiwan.

title: A Deep CNN-Based Salinity and Freshwater Fish Identification and Classification Using Deep Learning and Machine Learning
reason: Images show dead fish photographed in fish markets (fisheries commodities), not wild free-ranging animals in their environment; application framed around fisheries and seafood market.

title: AI-RCAS: A Real-Time Artificial Intelligence Analysis System for Sustainable Fisheries Management
reason: Computer vision system (YOLOv10 + ByteTrack + counting) applied to on-vessel electronic monitoring video of wild-caught marine fish and crabs in capture fisheries (not aquaculture).

title: Assessment of Multiple Citizen Science Methods and Carbon Footprint of Tourists in Two Australian Marine Parks
reason: Citizen science expedition assessing survey tools, eDNA, social surveys and carbon footprint; photos uploaded to iNaturalist are identified by the community, and the paper itself develops, applies or evaluates no computer vision method.

title: YOLOv7-SN: Underwater Target Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv7
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv7 detector for underwater images of marine organisms (echinus, holothurian, scallop, starfish) in real underwater scenes.

title: Monitoring of Fish Migration in Fishways and Rivers—The Infrared Fish Counter “Riverwatcher” as a Suitable Tool for Long-Term Monitoring
reason: Describes and summarizes use of the VAKI Riverwatcher infrared light-barrier fish counter with manual video review; no computer vision method is developed or evaluated on image data.

title: The Effects of Data Quality on Deep Learning Performance for Aquatic Insect Identification: Advances for Biomonitoring Studies
reason: Wild-collected aquatic insect larvae were preserved in ethanol and photographed in the laboratory under a stereomicroscope. This is lab imaging of specimens, not imaging of free-ranging animals.

title: A Study on Wild and Domestic Animal Detection for Farm Protection by using Computer Vision
reason: Classical computer vision pipeline (SIFT, k-means, classical classifiers) classifying images of wild animals (elephant, leopard, monkey) and domestic animals (cattle, horse, pig) for protecting farms from wildlife intrusion. Image origin is not stated, so whether the animals are free-ranging cannot be confirmed from the text.

title: Animal Species Identification in Historical Parchments by Continuous Wavelet Transform–Convolutional Neural Network Classifier Applied to Ultraviolet–Visible–Near-Infrared Spectroscopic Data
reason: The paper classifies point reflectance spectra (UV–visible–NIR spectrophotometry) of parchments made from domestic calf, sheep and goat skins. It analyses no images or video, and the animals are neither wild nor free-ranging.

title: Bal Arı Hastalıklarının Sınıflandırılması için ConvMixer, VGG16 ve ResNet101 Tabanlı Topluluk Öğrenme Yaklaşımı
reason: The paper classifies hive health problems of managed honey bees (beekeeping) from the BeeImage dataset; no wild, free-ranging non-domestic animals are the subject.

title: REAL-TIME DETECTION AND CLASSIFICATION OF FISH IN UNDERWATER ENVIRONMENT USING YOLOV5: A COMPARATIVE STUDY OF DEEP LEARNING ARCHITECTURES
venue: Informatyka Automatyka Pomiary w Gospodarce i Ochronie Środowiska
reason: YOLOv5 detection/classification of goldfish and koi samples filmed by webcam in an aquarium; no wild or free-ranging animals in the analysed data.

title: Klasifikasi Ikan Cakalang dan Tongkol Menggunakan Convolutional Neural Network
reason: Classifies side-view images of dead skipjack and mackerel tuna gathered from the internet and a local market. These are fish specimens, not free-ranging animals photographed in the wild.

title: Application of artificial intelligence methods to automate post-spawn chum salmon individuals enumeration by means of unmanned aerial vehicles in Khabarovsk Territory
reason: Mask R-CNN is trained and tested on UAV orthophotos of spawning rivers to detect and count post-spawn (dead) wild chum salmon in Khabarovsk Territory rivers.

title: The lateral stripe – a reliable way for software assisted individual identification for Hyla arborea
reason: Applies software-assisted photographic individual identification (Hotspotter) to images of wild Common tree frogs captured and released at a pond in Bulgaria.

title: Digital Fish Image Segmentation Using U-Net for Shape Feature Extraction
reason: Applies U-Net segmentation to images of wild tuna caught by fishermen (fisheries catch, not aquaculture); the animals are the subject of the computer vision analysis.

title: Transfer Learning for Wildlife Classification: Evaluating YOLOv8 against DenseNet, ResNet, and VGGNet on a Custom Dataset
venue: Journal of Artificial Intelligence and Capsule Networks
reason: Primary study applying CNN classifiers to images of endangered wildlife species sourced from iNaturalist (wild observations) and ZooChat (zoo photographs), with wildlife monitoring as the stated application.

title: Underwater Image Restoration and Object Detection
reason: Generic underwater image restoration and object detection framework; animals are not the stated subject, no animal data or species analysed, and much of the paper is a short literature review.

title: Snake Species Classification Using ConvNeXtXLarge
reason: Primary study applying a deep learning image classifier to web-scraped snake images of 80 species; snakes are non-domestic wildlife and the stated application is species identification for conservation. The paper does not state whether the photographed snakes are wild or captive.

title: AI-driven Wildlife Behavior Monitoring using Computer Vision
reason: Conceptual description of a proposed wildlife monitoring system (YOLOv8, camera traps, drones). The paper reports no dataset, no experiments and no results, so no image analysis is actually performed on animal images.

title: Development and Efficacy of Laser Bird Repeller with PTZ Camera and Caffe Framework
reason: Primary study applying motion detection and a CNN bird/no-bird classifier to PTZ camera images of free-ranging magpies and crows in an outdoor area to drive a laser bird repeller.

title: Bornean Orangutan Nest Classification using Image Enhancement with Convolutional Neural Network and Kernel Multi Support Vector Machine Classifier
venue: Journal of Advanced Research in Applied Sciences and Engineering Technology
reason: Primary study applying image enhancement, CNN feature extraction and SVM classification to UAV images of wild Bornean orangutan nests (direct animal signs).
