title: Traits for Efficient Navigation and Search in Natural History Collections
reason: Conference abstract reporting expert interviews on potential traits for AI in natural history collections (museum specimens); no image analysis performed and no wild animals imaged.

title: AI Species Identification Using Image and Sound Recognition for Citizen Science, Collection Management and Biomonitoring: From Training Pipeline to Large-Scale Models
reason: The paper trains deep image-recognition models for species identification on citizen-science observation images of European organisms, including wild animals such as mollusks and arthropods. It reports results, so it counts as primary research, although it is a conference abstract.

title: Biodiversity monitoring with intelligent sensors: An integrated pipeline for mitigating animal-vehicle collisions
reason: Primary study applying a deep-learning detector (YoloV8) to camera-trap photos of wild ungulates (roe deer, wild boar) along a railway to map collision risk.

title: Implementing biodiversity monitoring of rocky shores using photo-quadrats and Artificial Intelligence in support of data-driven decision-making of marine living resources
reason: Workshop report on capacity building for rocky-shore photo-quadrat monitoring with CoralNet; not primary research evaluating or developing a computer vision method, and no results are reported.

title: Low-cost, high-volume imaging for entomological digitization
reason: Describes a low-cost imaging rig for pinned museum/collection arthropod specimens; no wild free-ranging animals imaged and minimal computer vision analysis.

title: Biological Butterfly Characterization with Mobile System Using Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) Classify Image
venue: International Journal of Interactive Mobile Technologies (iJIM)
reason: Builds a smartphone app that uses a CNN to classify butterfly species from images of butterflies, which are wild insects.

title: Maximising the value of visual data in South African National Parks
reason: Short communication about how camera trap and BRUV visual data are managed at SANParks. It analyses no images or video and applies no computer vision method.

title: SMART REPELLER: A Smart system to prevent Rhesus Macaque Trespassing in Human Settlements and Agricultural Areas
venue: EAI Endorsed Transactions on Internet of Things
reason: Applies YOLOv5-based computer vision to detect wild rhesus macaques entering human settlements and agricultural areas, as part of an automatic deterrent system.

title: An IoT Integrated Smart Prediction of Wild Animal Intrusion in Residential Areas Using Hybrid Deep Learning with Computer Vision
venue: Eai Endorsed Transactions on Internet of Things
reason: Primary study applying deep learning image classification/detection to web-scraped images of wild animal species (lion, tiger, elephant, etc.) for intrusion alerts; a domestic animal dataset from Kaggle is also used.

title: Effect of Turbidity on Semi-Automatic Analysis of Copepod Size and Abundance Distribution in the Water Column
reason: Primary study developing and testing image-processing algorithms (binarization, noise reduction, contour detection) to count and measure wild copepods in in situ underwater images taken off the Doce River, Brazil.

title: Application of Remote Sensing in Coral Reef Mapping and Assessment of Climatic and Environmental Conditions
venue: Journal of Geoscience and Environment Protection
reason: Satellite benthic habitat mapping (coral reef, seagrass, sand classes) and environmental parameter estimation; this is habitat/land-cover mapping, not computer vision on images of individual animals.

title: Research on Biometric Identification Method of Nuclear Cold Source Disaster Based on Deep Learning
reason: Proposes an improved Fast-R-CNN to recognise free-living shrimp and jellyfish, organisms that can cause disasters at the cooling-water intake of nuclear power plants.

title: Remote sensing of coral reef habitats in Madagascar using Sentinel-2 satellite images
venue: Western Indian Ocean Journal of Marine Science
reason: Benthic habitat mapping (coral, algae, seagrass, sand, rubble) from Sentinel-2 imagery. It is a habitat/land-cover classification, not an analysis of individual animals.

title: Hunting Resource Management by Population Size Control by Remote Sensing Using an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
reason: UAV thermal and RGB imagery of wild game animals in Siberian forests, processed by software that detects thermal anomalies to count animals.

title: Classification of Endangered Bird Species of Nepal Using Deep Learning
venue: International Research Journal of Innovations in Engineering and Technology
reason: Applies CNNs to classify images of 38 endangered wild bird species of Nepal, using photos from eBird.

title: Identifying ocelots by individual coat pattern marks using the Whiskerbook
reason: Applies the Whiskerbook platform (HotSpotter pattern matching) to camera trap images of wild ocelots in the Brazilian Amazon to identify individuals.

title: Safeguarding Humans from Attacks Using AI-Enabled (DQN) Wild Animal Identification System
venue: International Research Journal of Multidisciplinary Scope
reason: Deep learning classification of images containing wild animals, domestic animals and humans for wild animal identification; part of data shows wild animals in natural habitat.

title: Classification of Coral Reef Species using Computer Vision and Deep Learning Techniques
venue: Engineering Technology and Applied Science Research
reason: Applies deep learning image classification to images of coral reef species (wild marine animals) for monitoring and conservation.

title: Wildlife Tracker using Deep Learning
venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
reason: Applies YOLOv8 object detection to images and videos of wild animals for wildlife monitoring. The data and evaluation are described only vaguely.

title: Detection and Tracing of Wild Animals using Machine Learning
venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
reason: Project proposal for an RCNN-based wild animal detection and tracking system. The paper describes the planned system only: no images or video are analysed, no dataset is used and no experiments or results are reported, so no image analysis is actually performed.

title: Android and IoT Integrated Smart Wildlife Surveillance using Night Vision
venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
reason: System proposal for wild animal detection with a pre-trained YOLO V7 on a Raspberry Pi. The paper reports no dataset, experiment or result, so no image analysis of wild animals is actually performed.

title: Exploring Boundary of GPT-4V on Marine Analysis: A Preliminary Case Study
reason: Evaluates GPT-4V (a multimodal vision-language model) on marine images, including recognition, counting and re-identification of marine species, using frames from YouTube videos, internet images and a marine dataset.

title: PanAf20K: A Large Video Dataset for Wild Ape Detection and Behaviour Recognition
reason: Presents a camera-trap video dataset of wild chimpanzees and gorillas, with benchmarks for detection and behaviour recognition.

title: Align and Distill: Unifying and Improving Domain Adaptive Object Detection
reason: Domain adaptive object detection method paper that also introduces and evaluates on a new dataset (CFC-DAOD) for detecting migrating salmon in river sonar video, a stated environmental and fisheries monitoring application. Imaging sonar video counts as image data.

title: BG-YOLO: A Bidirectional-Guided Method for Underwater Object Detection
reason: Proposes a CNN detection method (BG-YOLO) for underwater images of marine organisms (echinus, starfish, holothurian, scallop) in URPC datasets. The paper never says whether the animals are wild or farmed; they are coded as free-ranging because the images are natural underwater scenes.

title: Pytorch-Wildlife: A Collaborative Deep Learning Framework for Conservation
reason: Open-source deep learning framework applied to animal detection and classification in camera trap images of wild animals (Amazon Rainforest, invasive opossums in Galápagos).

title: CLIBD: Bridging Vision and Genomics for Biodiversity Monitoring at Scale
reason: Multimodal contrastive model for insect taxonomic classification using images of insect specimens photographed in a laboratory setting (BIOSCAN-1M, INSECT); images do not show free-ranging animals in the wild.

title: Detecting Endangered Marine Species in Autonomous Underwater Vehicle Imagery Using Point Annotations and Few-Shot Learning
reason: Proposes a few-shot object detection framework for detecting wild endangered handfish in AUV seafloor imagery from Tasmania.

title: A machine learning pipeline for automated insect monitoring
reason: Computer vision pipeline (detection, classification, tracking) for wild moths attracted to camera traps in field deployments.

title: An open-source Autonomous Surface Vehicle for Acoustic Tracking, Bathymetric and Photogrammetric Surveys
reason: Hardware paper describing an autonomous surface vehicle. The only image analysis is photogrammetric 3D reconstruction of the seabed and its morphology (habitat mapping), with corals and a clam visible in the scene. Acoustic tracking was tested on a freediver, not on an animal.

title: Scarecrow monitoring system:employing mobilenet ssd for enhanced animal supervision
reason: Applies MobileNet SSD object detection to images of animals, including wild animals such as lions and cheetahs, to protect crops from wildlife. A domestic cat is also tested.

title: Evaluation of Segment Anything Model 2: The Role of SAM2 in the Underwater Environment
reason: Evaluates SAM2 on generic underwater instance segmentation benchmarks (UIIS, USIS10K). The paper never names animals as its subject and treats underwater instances in general, so wildlife is not the stated subject.

title: Whole-Herd Elephant Pose Estimation from Drone Data for Collective Behavior Analysis
reason: Pose estimation of wild elephant herds from drone video in Samburu National Reserve, Kenya.

title: BuckTales : A multi-UAV dataset for multi-object tracking and re-identification of wild antelopes
reason: Introduces a UAV video dataset of wild blackbuck at a lek for detection, multi-object tracking and re-identification, and benchmarks detectors and trackers on it.

title: Towards Scalable Insect Monitoring: Ultra-Lightweight CNNs as On-Device Triggers for Insect Camera Traps
reason: Develops lightweight CNN binary classifiers that detect insect presence in images, trained and tested on iNaturalist and field insect camera-trap datasets of free-living insects.

title: Multispecies Animal Re-ID Using a Large Community-Curated Dataset
reason: The paper trains a deep-learning model that re-identifies individual animals from images. Most of the 49 species are wild (whales, dolphins, big cats, giraffes, turtles), but the data also includes dogs and zoo chimpanzees, so the subjects are mixed.

title: Individual Tiger Identification using Transfer Learning
reason: Applies a CNN with transfer learning to identify individual wild tigers in camera-trap images from a tiger reserve.

title: An Intelligent Plant and Animal Identification Mobile Application for Increased Biodiversity Awareness and Safety using Machine Learning
reason: Mobile app using TensorFlow Lite image classification to identify animal (and plant) species for wildlife safety awareness; animal images from the web are analysed, though whether they show wild or captive animals is not stated.

title: First release of the Pelagic Size Structure database: global datasets of marine size spectra obtained from plankton imaging devices
reason: Dataset paper compiling bulk particle size spectra from morphometric measurements already extracted by plankton imaging instruments; the authors perform no image analysis themselves, and the subject is bulk particles (living and detrital) rather than animals.

title: Application of Photogrammetric Computer Vision and Deep Learning in High-Resolution Underwater Mapping: A Case Study of Shallow-Water Coral Reefs
venue: ISPRS annals of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences
reason: Evaluates photogrammetric and deep learning 3D reconstruction methods on underwater images of wild shallow-water coral reefs (corals are animals) at Moorea.

title: UAV and Deep Learning: Detection of selected riparian species along the Ganga River
venue: The international archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences/International archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences
reason: Applies YOLO-based object detection to UAV imagery of wild gharials and turtles basking along the Ganga River in a wildlife sanctuary.

title: Evaluating Linear Coral Growth Estimation Using Photogrammetry and Alternative Point Cloud Comparison Methods
venue: The international archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences/International archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences
reason: Underwater photogrammetric 3D reconstruction of wild Acropora coral colonies in the field to measure linear growth; image-based computer vision on wild animals.

title: Towards Estimation of 3D Poses and Shapes of Animals from Oblique Drone Imagery
venue: The international archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences/International archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences
reason: Primary study estimating 3D pose and shape of wild plains zebras from oblique drone video using parametric model fitting and photogrammetry.

title: Semantically-Based Animal Pose Estimation in the Wild
venue: The international archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences/International archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences
reason: Proposes a two-stage pose estimation method (YOLOv8 pose with semantic segmentation) tested on camera-trap images of wild animals from Ergaki National Park.

title: WebUOT-1M: Advancing Deep Underwater Object Tracking with A Million-Scale Benchmark
reason: Introduces a large underwater object tracking benchmark of web videos covering aquatic animals in sea, river and lake as well as in aquaria and fish tanks, and proposes a tracker. Marine animal conservation is a stated use. The data mixes wild and captive animals, plus people and inanimate objects.

title: LLM-AutoDA: Large Language Model-Driven Automatic Data Augmentation for Long-tailed Problems
reason: Generic long-tailed learning data augmentation method evaluated on generic benchmarks (CIFAR-100-LT, ImageNet-LT, iNaturalist 2018); wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: BuckTales: A multi-UAV dataset for multi-object tracking and re-identification of wild antelopes
reason: Introduces a UAV video dataset of wild blackbuck antelopes on a lek for detection, multi-object tracking and re-identification, with benchmark results.

title: BioTrove: A Large Curated Image Dataset Enabling AI for Biodiversity
reason: Primary dataset/benchmark paper building a large curated citizen-science (iNaturalist) image dataset of biodiversity, including wild animals (birds, insects, reptiles, molluscs, arachnids), and training/evaluating CLIP models for species classification.

title: INQUIRE: A Natural World Text-to-Image Retrieval Benchmark
reason: Introduces a text-to-image retrieval benchmark and dataset of iNaturalist natural world images, much of it wild animals, aimed at ecological and biodiversity research. It evaluates vision-language models on these images.

title: OPTIMIZING BUTTERFLY CLASSIFICATION THROUGH TRANSFER LEARNING: FINE-TUNING APPROACH WITH NASNETMOBILE AND MOBILENETV2
reason: Applies CNN transfer learning to classify images of 75 butterfly species, which are non-domestic animals. The paper does not say how or where the images were taken.

title: Underwater Object Detection Based on Spatial Pyramid and Channel Attention
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv7 detector for underwater organisms (scallops, holothurians, starfish, echinus) in images captured in real ocean environments.

title: YOLOv8 based fish detection and classification on fishnet dataset
reason: Applies YOLOv8 to detect and classify wild-caught tuna species in electronic monitoring images from commercial longline fishing vessels (capture fishery, not aquaculture).

title: SmartCS: Enabling the Creation of Machine Learning–Powered Computer Vision Mobile Apps for Citizen Science Applications without Coding
reason: Generic no-code platform for building ML citizen-science apps; the use cases described in detail are recyclables and rip currents. A seal vs. sea lion app is only named, and its details are in the supplement, so wildlife is not the subject of the analysed data.

title: Engaging Citizen Scientists in Biodiversity Monitoring: Insights from the WildLIVE! Project
reason: Citizen science engagement study: camera trap images of wild mammals are labeled manually by volunteers on Labelbox; no computer vision method is developed or applied, and machine learning is only planned for the future.

title: Image Recognition as a “Dialogic AI Partner” Within Biodiversity Citizen Science—an empirical investigation
reason: Fine-tunes and evaluates an image recognition model for classifying UK bumblebee species from citizen-science photographs taken in the wild, integrated into a human-AI collaboration interface.

title: GLOBE Observer: A Case Study in Advancing Earth System Knowledge with AI-Powered Citizen Science
reason: The only animal image analysis in this paper is localizing body parts of mosquito larvae with Faster R-CNN. The larvae were laboratory specimens photographed by smartphone in insectaries. The land cover and privacy screening work involves no animals.

title: Human Supervision is Key to Achieving Accurate AI-assisted Wildlife Identifications in Camera Trap Images
reason: Evaluates a CNN species classifier and a human-in-the-loop pipeline on camera trap images of wild African animals in Serengeti National Park against expert gold standard labels.

title: Artificial Intelligence and the Future of Citizen Science
reason: Editorial introducing a special collection on AI and citizen science; summarises other papers and reports no primary computer vision experiments of its own.

title: Innovative Animal Identification Model usingCNN–Based Multi–Classification
reason: CNN image classification of animal images including wild species (deer, tiger, zebra) together with domestic ones (cattle, horse), framed around wildlife conservation and animal-vehicle collisions.

title: Harmonizing Habitat: P-Yolov5 Enhanced Computer Vision For Mitigating Human-Wildlife Conflicts In Rural Areas
reason: Proposes a modified YOLOv5 detector for tigers and elephants entering villages, using CCTV images of wild animals.

title: Marine Life Identification System Based on Deep Learning
reason: Applies YOLOv5 object detection to images of marine organisms (fish, jellyfish, dolphins, sharks, etc.) for ecological monitoring; the source of the images is not stated, but the subject is non-domestic marine animals.

title: Animal detection and classification from camera trap images using residual neural networks
reason: Applies ResNet-50 to camera trap images of wildlife from Serengeti National Park, classifying them as blank (no animal) or non-blank (animal present).

title: Research on improving accuracy and efficiency of animal data collection and classification using machine learning
reason: Applies CNN, SVM and logistic regression to classify animal images that the paper says came from wildlife monitoring sites, so wild animals are the subject of an image classification study.

title: Bird image classification based on improved ResNet-152 image classification model
reason: Applies a CNN (ResNet-152) to classify bird species in photographs taken by bird photographers and bird watchers. This is primary research on images of wild birds.

title: Binning of biological image based on unsupervised semantic segmentation and no-reference image quality assessment
reason: Applies unsupervised semantic segmentation and no-reference image quality assessment to GBIF observation images of the wild bumblebee Bombus hypnorum to filter images for taxonomic identification.

title: Parrot Species Recognition by using CNN & SVM
venue: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
reason: Applies CNN and SVM image classification to recognise three parrot species, with automated wildlife monitoring as the stated application; the image source is not reported.

title: “Decoding Bird Species Diversity through Image Analysis
venue: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
reason: Primary study that trains a CNN to classify bird species from images (public bird datasets, online sources, field surveys) for biodiversity monitoring. Birds are the stated subject. The paper does not explicitly say the birds are wild; this is inferred from the image sources.

title: Ornithological Imaging: Transforming Bird Species Identification with Technology
venue: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
reason: Primary study applying a CNN to classify bird species from photographs gathered from online databases and citizen science contributions, aimed at bird monitoring and conservation. The paper does not state whether the birds are wild or captive.

title: AI-Powered Animal Repellent System for Smart Farming
venue: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
reason: The paper describes a MERN-stack e-commerce web platform connecting farmers and consumers; it involves no image or video analysis and no animals.

title: Search and classification of objects in the zone of reservoirs and coastal zones
reason: The study detects boats, ships, buoys, garbage, swimmers and drowning people on water surfaces. No animals are analysed.

title: Efficient Small and Overlapping Target Detection in Underwater Images
reason: Proposes a YOLOv8-based detector for underwater marine organisms (echinus, holothurian, scallop, starfish) in underwater images; whether the animals are wild or farmed is not stated.

title: Swimmer Safety Alert System for Encounters with Unidentified Marine Aquatic Animals
venue: International Journal of Innovative Research in Computer Science & Technology
reason: Conceptual proposal of an IoT-based swimmer alert system with literature review and research gaps; no image or video data is analysed and no computer vision experiments are reported.

title: Detecting Intended Target Birds and Using Frightened Techniques in Crops to Preserve Yield
venue: International Journal of Innovative Research in Computer Science & Technology
reason: Applies computer vision (YOLO detection and ResNet classification) to webcam images of wild birds in crop fields to trigger selective deterrence.

title: Deep Learning Techniques for Enhanced Underwater Remote Sensing: Applications in Marine Biodiversity and Infrastructure Inspection
venue: Journal of Image Processing and Intelligent Remote Sensing
reason: Primary study applying deep learning (modified YOLO) to underwater images to detect and classify marine species for biodiversity monitoring; the paper does not state whether the animals are wild or captive, but the data are described as underwater remote sensing imagery of marine life.

title: Quantifying minimum survey effort to reliably detect Amazonian manatees using an unoccupied aerial vehicle (UAV) at an ex situ soft-release site
venue: Latin American Journal of Aquatic Mammals
reason: The UAV surveys covered a closed population of five rehabilitating manatees in an enclosed man-made lake at a rescue centre, so the subjects are captive. Detection was also done by manual video review, with no automated computer vision.

title: Artificial intelligence improves the identification of fur seals recorded at Southern Brazilian coast
venue: Latin American Journal of Aquatic Mammals
reason: CNN-based species classification of facial images of living wild fur seals (Arctocephalus) found on the Brazilian coast; primary research.

title: Object Detection Model for Marine Organisms Based on Faster R-CNN
reason: Applies Faster R-CNN object detection to underwater images of wild marine organisms from the FathomNet 2023 dataset.

title: The Safe Catch: AI Protects Your Health from Formalin-Laced Fish
venue: Malaysian Journal of Science and Advanced Technology
reason: The paper classifies eye images of market food fish as formalin-treated or not, for food safety in the fish supply chain. It is not about wild, free-ranging animals.

title: WILD ANIMAL DETECTION AND ALERT SYSTEM USING YOLOv8
venue: International Research Journal of Modernization in Engineering Technology and Science
reason: Primary study applying YOLOv8 to video frames of lions and tigers for a wildlife detection and alert system. The paper frames the animals as wild but does not state whether the analysed footage shows wild or captive animals.

title: Segmenting Freshwater Fish Images with Convolutional Neural Networks
reason: Applies CNN instance segmentation to smartphone photos of wild-caught freshwater fish from the Madeira river basin, photographed at a fish market (fisheries data, not aquaculture).

title: Fish Catch Sorting and Detection Model Improved Based on YOLOv8 Model
reason: Develops an improved YOLOv8 detector for wild-caught marine fish and invertebrates from trawl catches. It is also evaluated on the public FishKnowledge fish dataset. This is not aquaculture or livestock.

title: Real-Time Detection of Sea Turtles Using UAV and Neural Networks on Edge Devices
venue: The Journal of Aviation/Aerospace Education and Research
reason: Applies a CNN object detector to UAV images of wild sea turtles in their natural marine habitat for conservation monitoring.

title: A deep learning approach for underwater fish detection
venue: Journal of Integrated Science and Technology
reason: Applies deep learning object detectors to detect fish in underwater videos (Fish4Knowledge) with dynamic backgrounds; fish in natural underwater settings.

title: Fine-scale tracking reveals visual field use for predator detection and escape in collective foraging of pigeon flocks
reason: Breeder-sourced pigeons housed in an aviary were tracked with marker-based motion capture inside an indoor laboratory tracking facility (SMART-BARN). No wild or free-ranging animals were imaged.

title: Fine-scale tracking reveals visual field use for predator detection and escape in collective foraging of pigeon flocks
reason: Pigeons from a breeder, housed in an aviary, were tracked with a marker-based motion-capture system in an indoor laboratory set-up (SMART-BARN). No wild or free-ranging animals appear in the data.

title: ASBAR: an Animal Skeleton-Based Action Recognition framework. Recognizing great ape behaviors in the wild using pose estimation
reason: Proposes a pose-estimation plus skeleton-based action recognition framework applied to camera trap videos of wild chimpanzees and gorillas; pose training data (OMC) also contain captive/research-center primates.

title: ASBAR: an Animal Skeleton-Based Action Recognition framework. Recognizing great ape behaviors in the wild using pose estimation with domain adaptation
reason: The authors propose a pose-estimation and skeleton-based action recognition framework. They apply it to camera-trap videos of wild chimpanzees and gorillas. The pose dataset (OMC) also contains images of captive primates from zoos and research centres.

title: Analysis of the performance of Faster R-CNN and YOLOv8 in detecting fishing vessels and fishes in real time
reason: Applies Faster R-CNN and YOLOv8 to detect fish and other marine animals, as well as fishing vessels, in maritime surveillance images from marine environments. This is primary computer-vision research in which animals are a subject.

title: Research on marine flexible biological target detection based on improved YOLOv8 algorithm
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv8 detector for marine flexible organisms (octopus, holothurian, starfish, jellyfish) in footage of authentic ocean environments.

title: High-resolution density assessment assisted by deep learning of Dendrophyllia cornigera (Lamarck, 1816) and Phakellia ventilabrum (Linnaeus, 1767) in rocky circalittoral shelf of Bay of Biscay
reason: Object detection models applied to in situ ROTV seafloor images of wild sessile benthic animals (a coral and a sponge) to produce density maps.

title: The best of two worlds: reprojecting 2D image annotations onto 3D models
reason: Primary study applying photogrammetric 3D reconstruction and ray-tracing reprojection to ROV images of deep-sea seabed with wild benthic fauna annotations (duplicate counting of fauna annotations).

title: Supplementing human observation with artificial intelligence impacts demographic estimates for a critically endangered lizard
reason: Primary study applying HotSpotter image-recognition software to photographs of wild-caught Kapitia skinks for individual identification in a capture-recapture programme.

title: DeepForestVision : Automated wildlife identification for camera traps of African tropical forests
reason: Develops and evaluates a deep learning detection + classification pipeline for camera trap photos and videos of wild mammals and birds in African tropical forests.

title: AInsectID Version 1.1: An Insect Species Identification Software Based on the Transfer Learning of Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
reason: Insect species classification trained on museum specimen images (National Museum of Scotland, Natural History Museum London) plus a Zenodo image dataset. The paper never says any images show wild, free-ranging animals in the field, so it is coded under the museum-specimen exclusion.

title: Fourier-Based Action Recognition for Wildlife Behavior Quantification with Event Cameras
reason: Proposes Fourier-based action recognition on event-camera recordings of wild breeding chinstrap penguins in Antarctica to classify ecstatic display behaviour.

title: Using 3D Photogrammetry to Quantify Usable Space in Zoo‐Housed Primate Habitats
reason: 3D photogrammetry reconstruction of zoo enclosures for zoo-housed primates only; no wild animals.

title: Quantifying Facial Gestures Using Deep Learning in a New World Monkey
reason: Pose estimation and behaviour classification of facial gestures, using footage only of captive cotton-top tamarins at a zoo.

title: Using Deep Learning to Automate Orangutan Nest Detections on Aerial Images Collected With Drones
reason: Primary study training and testing a YOLO v10 detector on drone images of nests (direct signs) of wild orangutans in Sabah and Sumatra forests.

title: Hominoid Hallucal Metatarsal Divergence and Tarsometatarsal Joint Morphology
reason: Comparative morphology study of 3D laser-scanned museum bone specimens of hominoids; no computer vision on images or video of wild, free-ranging animals.

title: On‐Land Pinniped Classification of Multiple Species and Demographic Classes on Multiple Substrates Using Deep Learning and Aerial Imagery
venue: Aquatic Conservation Marine and Freshwater Ecosystems
reason: Primary study training a RetinaNet object detector on aerial survey images of wild hauled-out elephant seals and harbour seals in California.

title: Anatomical distribution and flight control function of wing sensory hairs in Seba's short‐tailed bat
reason: Bats are from a laboratory colony flown in a wind tunnel, and the wings studied are preserved specimens imaged under a microscope. No wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Functional models from limited data: A parametric and multimodal approach to anatomy and 3D kinematics of feeding in basking sharks ( Cetorhinus maximus )
reason: The paper reconstructs 3D models of free-ranging, feeding basking sharks by running photogrammetry on video frames. It combines these with CT scans of specimens to build a poseable skeletal model, so image-based 3D reconstruction of wild animals is central to the work.

title: Patterns of spinal motion, kinematic spaces and the land‐to‐sea transition in carnivorans
reason: Functional morphology study using 3D surface scans of dry vertebrae from museum skeletons to estimate spinal range of motion; no images or video of live wild animals.

title: A Novel Underwater Blurred Target Detection Algorithm Based on RT ‐ DETR
venue: Concurrency and Computation Practice and Experience
reason: Proposes an RT-DETR based detector for underwater marine organisms (holothurians, echinoids, scallops, starfish) in URPC2020 underwater images.

title: A Two‐Stage Region Proposal Optimization for Efficient Bird Detection in Deep Learning Pipelines
venue: Concurrency and Computation Practice and Experience
reason: Proposes a Haar cascade + Gaussian blur preprocessing to optimise region proposals for R-CNN/YOLOv8 detection of wild bird species in images, also tested on a wild rabbit dataset.

title: Removing dead coral after marine heatwaves can mitigate coral–algae competition and increase viable coral recruitment
reason: Field experiment on a wild coral reef that uses AI-powered image segmentation (TagLab) on underwater photogrammetric orthophotos to quantify live and dead branching coral (animals) over time.

title: Developing custom computer vision models with Njobvu-AI: A collaborative, user-friendly platform for ecological research
reason: Presents a no-code tool and trains a YOLOv4 multiclass detector on camera trap images of free-ranging wildlife in a Malawian reserve; primary research.

title: Application of spatially robust stereo‐ BRUV sampling for quantifying fish assemblages in UK marine protected areas
reason: Ecological stereo-BRUV survey of wild marine fish and invertebrates. A single observer annotated the video by hand in EventMeasure (species ID, MaxN, stereo length measurement). No automated computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Novel Bat‐Monitoring Dataset Reveals Targeted Foraging With Agricultural and Pest Control Implications
reason: Applies a neural-network workflow (BATS) that classifies pixels of weather-radar scenes for the presence of wild bats, then maps foraging activity. The input is imaged radar data of free-ranging animals, so this is primary research.

title: Terrestrial Spatial Distribution and Summer Abundance of Antarctic Fur Seals ( Arctocephalus gazella ) Near Palmer Station, Antarctica, From Drone Surveys
reason: Wild Antarctic fur seals were surveyed by drone, but they were counted by hand on orthomosaics. No automated image analysis was applied to the animals; photogrammetry was used only to build maps, and habitat and abundance modelling used counts and terrain data.

title: Identification of Individual Texas Horned Lizards ( Phrynosoma cornutum ) Using Genotypes and Ventral Spot Patterns
reason: Applies HotSpotter image matching to photos of ventral spot patterns of wild Texas horned lizards captured in towns for individual identification.

title: Two‐Way Gateway Designs to Allow Free Movement Between Safe Havens for Bettongs: A Captive Trial
reason: Captive bettongs were filmed and their behaviour was coded by hand from the video (all-occurrence sampling, then GLM/ANOVA). No computer vision method is used, and the animals are captive.

title: Leveraging Community Science to Measure Bee Body Size From Museum Specimens
reason: Body size of museum bee specimens was measured by hand from images, by community scientists on Notes from Nature and by researchers in ImageJ. No computer vision method was developed or applied, and the animals are museum specimens rather than live wild animals.

title: Exploring the Effects of Giraffe Skin Disease Limb Lesions on Locomotion
reason: Gait kinematics of wild Masai giraffe were measured by manually digitizing video frames in GaitKeeper and ImageJ. No automated computer vision method was developed or applied.

title: The Motion Picture: Leveraging Movement to Enhance AI Object Detection in Ecology
reason: Primary study evaluating movement-based augmentation for YOLOv8 object detection on underwater monitoring video and camera trap images of free-ranging fish and terrestrial animals in Australia.

title: Natural Habitat and Wild Behaviors of the Dwarf Cuttlefish, Ascarosepion bandense
reason: A natural-history field study of wild dwarf cuttlefish. The underwater photos and videos were used for manual behavioural observation and documentation. The only image processing is colour-card measurement and a colour-attenuation simulation; the paper has no computer vision analysis of the animals.

title: Applying Deep Learning to Quantify Drivers of Long‐Term Ecological Change in a Swedish Marine Protected Area
reason: Trains a YOLOv8 object-detection model on archived ROV footage of wild benthic invertebrates on a rock wall in a Swedish marine protected area and applies it to quantify ecological trends.

title: DeepFaune New England: A Species Classification Model for Trail Camera Images in Northeastern North America
reason: Trains and evaluates a species classification model on trail camera images of wild North American wildlife (with some domestic classes such as cat, dog, cow).

title: Fossorial Form of Water Voles Select and Overexploit High‐Quality Habitats, Hindering Future Colonizations Evidence From Drone‐Based Monitoring of Dandelion‐Vole Interactions in Mountain Meadows
reason: Drone RGB imagery analysed with pixel classification to detect earth mounds (direct signs) of free-ranging fossorial water voles in meadows, and to relate them to dandelion density.

title: Identifying Small‐Displacement Stereotypical Behavior of Captive Slow Lorises Based on AnimalYOLO ‐Bytetrack Network
reason: Analyses videos of captive slow lorises at a rescue centre and web videos of other captive or domestic animals in enclosures showing stereotypies; no free-ranging animals.

title: Copy-Paste Augmentation Improves Automatic Species Identification in Camera Trap Images
reason: Primary study applying copy-paste augmentation and object detection to camera trap images of wild Serengeti animals.

title: Seeing Through the Mimicry of Papilio bootes by Combining Computer‐Aided and Human Eyesight Morphological Comparisons
reason: Images analysed are photographs of dead, dried butterfly specimens taken in a laboratory light box, not images of live free-ranging animals.

title: Incorporating Machine Learning Techniques to Enhance Rodent Surveillance in Marginalized Urban Communities
reason: Classifies photographs of tracking plates bearing marks (footprints, tail marks) of free-ranging urban rodents. These are direct animal signs, and the plates are analysed with image processing and machine learning.

title: Egg Characteristics of Female Common Terns Are Repeatable, and Vary With Maternal Age and Laying Order
reason: Image analysis (colour thresholding, RGB extraction, shape from photographs) of eggs from a wild breeding colony of common terns; eggs are direct signs of wild animals.

title: Estimating Total Body Lipid Store of Free‐Ranging Whales In Vivo Using Drone Photogrammetry and Biologging Tags
reason: Develops a method that uses UAV photogrammetry images of free-ranging sperm whales to measure body length and width, estimate volume and combine it with tag data to estimate lipid stores.

title: Rheotactic Responses in Bufo bufo Tadpoles—Insights Into Adaptation to Lotic Environment
reason: Applies Structure from Motion photogrammetry to photographs of wild Bufo bufo tadpoles in their natural cave stream habitat to measure their orientation.

title: Monitoring Fish Assemblages in Seasonal Off-Channel Habitats Using Underwater Video and Computer Vision
reason: Applies a YOLOv5 detector and SORT tracker to underwater video of free-ranging freshwater fish and tadpoles in a seasonal backwater slough in Norway.

title: An accurate and efficient semiautomated approach to counting birds: Estimating Northern Gannet colony size in Canada
reason: Counting of wild Northern Gannet nests in aerial photographs uses CountEm, a geometric sampling tool in which a human manually identifies and counts objects inside quadrats; no automated image analysis is performed.

title: Smart camera traps and computer vision improve detections of small fauna
reason: Field evaluation of two object detection models (a YOLOv5 model trained on SAWIT, and MegaDetector) on camera trap videos and images of wild fauna in Australian heathland.

title: Multiple hunting displays in wild broadclub cuttlefish
reason: Behavioural ecology study of wild cuttlefish hunting displays filmed with action cameras; displays were categorised by observers and analysed statistically, with no computer vision or automated image analysis.

title: A classification‐occupancy model based on automatically identified species data
reason: The study models occupancy from BirdNET detections of bird vocalizations in sound recordings (passive acoustic monitoring); no image or video analysis.

title: Engineering Hope via a Rapid Systems Engineering Approach to International Disaster Relief
reason: The paper describes a hackathon system that uses semantic segmentation to assess damaged urban buildings after disasters. No animals appear in the analysed images and wildlife is not the subject. None of the exclusion criteria fits well; E-GENERIC is the closest match for a non-wildlife vision application.

title: Three‐Dimensional Limb Kinematics in Brown‐Throated Three‐Toed Sloths (Bradypus variegatus) During Suspensory Quadrupedal Locomotion
venue: Journal of Experimental Zoology Part A Ecological and Integrative Physiology
reason: 3D kinematic video analysis of sloths held at a sanctuary, filmed walking on a custom-built runway beam (an enclosure/experimental set-up). No free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Testing the Impact of Prey Presentation Method on the Feeding Kinematics of Terrestrial and Aquatic Ambystomatidae
venue: Journal of Experimental Zoology Part A Ecological and Integrative Physiology
reason: Laboratory-bred salamanders filmed in a glass tank under controlled experimental conditions; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Oceanographic heterogeneity facilitates gelatinous zooplankton niche space and diversity
reason: In situ imaging (ISIIS) of wild gelatinous zooplankton in the northern Gulf of Mexico, with automated extraction of regions of interest from the images followed by taxonomic classification to map distributions and abundances.

title: Size matters: Perspective and angle‐correction improves accuracy in noninvasive image‐based body size measurements
reason: Fish length is measured manually by human observers in ImageJ on still images from a river video tunnel; the only automated step is a motion-detection trigger of the recorder, so no computer vision method is developed or evaluated.

title: Picturing plankton: Complementing net‐based plankton community assessments with optical imaging across diverse marine environments
reason: In situ optical imaging (Video Plankton Recorder) of wild marine zooplankton, with automated ROI segmentation and ZooScan image-based classification, compared against net sampling for density estimates.

title: Lions as Bone Accumulators? Exploring Multi‐Predator Contributions to the Olduvai Carnivore Site (OCS) (Tanzania) Through AI and Metric Analyses
reason: Deep-learning classification of microscope images of carnivore tooth marks (direct feeding signs) on a modern wildebeest bone assemblage formed by wild carnivores in the Serengeti. The training reference set combines marks made by captive and wild carnivores.

title: Discriminating footprints to improve identification of congeneric invasive Rattus species
reason: Image analysis (thresholding, blob detection, ellipse fitting) of scanned footprint cards of wild invasive rats, plus footprints from live-captured rats kept in a facility, to classify species.

title: Preventing exotic pet beetle invasion with an improved lightweight and efficient pest detection model deployed on mobile devices
reason: Images show exotic pet beetles intercepted at customs (live captive specimens and preserved samples) photographed on-site and in simulated laboratory scenarios; no wild free-ranging animals.

title: Remotely sensing coral bleaching in the Red Sea
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Develops a satellite multispectral image analysis model to detect and map bleaching severity of wild coral reefs (animals) in the Red Sea.

title: Automated extraction of right whale morphometric data from drone aerial photographs
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Primary study developing a Mask R-CNN pipeline to segment and measure free-living southern right whales in UAV aerial photographs collected at a calving ground in South Australia.

title: How to achieve accurate wildlife detection by using vehicle‐mounted mobile monitoring images and deep learning?
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv7 detector for wildlife images captured by a vehicle-mounted camera in national parks on the Tibetan Plateau; primary research on free-ranging animals.

title: Towards edge processing of images from insect camera traps
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Proposes a detection, classification and tracking pipeline for nocturnal insects imaged by light camera traps deployed in natural habitats in Denmark.

title: Object detection‐assisted workflow facilitates cryptic snake monitoring
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Primary study evaluating an object detection model (MegaDetector) on time-lapse camera trap images of wild, free-ranging snakes in the Everglades.

title: Increasing citizen scientist accuracy with artificial intelligence on UK camera‐trap data
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Primary study evaluating a CNN species classifier (alone and combined with citizen-scientist labels) on camera-trap images of wild UK mammals from MammalWeb.

title: Drone photogrammetry reveals contrasting body conditions of dugongs across the Indo‐Pacific
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Body length and width of wild dugongs were measured manually in ImageJ by an analyst on drone images; no automated computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Thermal drone observations capture fine‐scale population decline of short‐tailed shearwaters
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Applies UAS thermal imaging with automated counting to detect and count wild short-tailed shearwater chicks in burrows at natural colonies in Tasmania.

title: DuckNet : an open‐source deep learning tool for waterfowl species identification in UAV imagery
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Primary study training a deep learning object detector on UAV imagery of wild non-breeding waterfowl collected on wetland restoration easements.

title: Camera traps and deep learning enable efficient large‐scale density estimation of wildlife in temperate forest ecosystems
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Primary study evaluating a deep learning classifier (DeepFaune) on camera trap images of wild animals from 10 protected areas in Germany, and its effect on camera trap distance sampling density estimates.

title: A UAV ‐based deep learning pipeline for intertidal macrobenthos monitoring: Behavioral and age classification in Tachypleus tridentatus
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Develops a UAV-based deep learning detection and behaviour classification pipeline on field images of wild juvenile horseshoe crabs in an intertidal nature reserve.

title: Ground‐truthing of satellite imagery to assess seabird colony size: A test using Adélie penguins
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Primary study applying object-based SVM image classification to very high-resolution satellite imagery to extract guano stain area (a direct sign) of wild Adélie penguin colonies and relate it to colony size.

title: Seasonal variations and challenges in estimating populations and identifying species of Korean ungulates using drone‐derived thermal orthomosaic maps
reason: Drone thermal/RGB orthomosaic counting of three ungulate species kept in a fenced exhibition deer park (captive), not free-ranging animals; counts were also made manually.

title: The performance of drones and artificial intelligence for monitoring sage‐grouse at leks
reason: Primary study applying a YOLO-based detector to drone thermal video to count wild greater sage-grouse at leks.

title: Experimental assessment of large mammal population estimates from airborne thermal videography
reason: Deer in drone thermal video were counted by human observers who watched the footage. No computer vision or algorithmic image analysis is used. The deer are also an enclosed, captive population.

title: Sea‐turtle observations at Matura Beach, Trinidad, using thermal UAS imagery: A strategy to support monitoring and conservation efforts
reason: Thermal drone imagery of wild nesting sea turtles was analysed only by people looking at it (live feed, screen recordings, manual measurement). The paper uses no computer vision or automated image analysis method.

title: Can edge AI mitigate environmental effects on camera trap performance?
reason: Field comparison of camera trap hardware. The edge AI classifier works on PIR thermal sensor data before image capture, not on images; all images were annotated manually and analysed with statistical models.

title: Monitoring Pacific walrus coastal haulouts by satellite to estimate herd abundance and distribution
reason: Satellite images of wild Pacific walrus herds on shore are analysed. Herds are outlined by visual interpretation of images enhanced with bicubic kernel sharpening, and abundance is estimated from herd area.

title: Assessing the potential of unoccupied aerial vehicles and deep learning to survey wild turkey populations
reason: Primary study applying deep learning (U-Net detection plus tracking) to thermal UAV video of free-ranging roosting wild turkeys and vultures to estimate abundance.

title: Human-in-the-Loop Visual Re-ID for Population Size Estimation
venue: Lecture Notes in Computer Science Including Subseries Lecture Notes in Artificial Intelligence and Lecture Notes in Bioinformatics
reason: Proposes a human-in-the-loop population size estimation method built on visual Re-ID embeddings, evaluated on animal Re-ID image datasets that include wild animals (Taï chimpanzees, whale sharks, zebras and giraffes in Kenya) together with zoo chimpanzees and cattle.

title: No Plankton Left Behind: Preliminary Results on Massive Plankton Image Recognition
venue: Communications in computer and information science
reason: Deep learning classification of plankton images (including zooplankton sampled from the sea) from the large WHOI and ZooScanNet datasets; the plankton are free-ranging marine organisms.

title: MARINE: A Computer Vision Model for Detecting Rare Predator-Prey Interactions in Animal Videos
reason: Proposes a computer vision action recognition/detection model for predator attacks in videos of wild fish at a coral reef and in the Animal Kingdom dataset.

title: Animal Identification with Independent Foreground and Background Modeling
reason: Proposes a CV re-identification method evaluated on camera-trap images of wild Eurasian lynx and underwater photos of wild loggerhead sea turtles.

title: Open-Set Plankton Recognition
reason: Open-set classification of microscopic plankton imaged with plankton imaging instruments (ZooScan scans of water samples, IFCB imaging flow cytometer). This is microscopy-type imaging of sampled specimens, not images of free-ranging animals in their environment; half of the data is phytoplankton, which are not animals.

title: Closer to Ground Truth: Realistic Shape and Appearance Labeled Data Generation for Unsupervised Underwater Image Segmentation
reason: Computer vision method for fish segmentation in underwater video, evaluated on DeepFish (wild fish in coastal marine habitats of Australia) and on DeepSalmon (salmon held in tanks), so wild and captive/farmed animals appear together.

title: Generating Binary Species Range Maps
reason: Thresholding of deep species distribution models into binary range maps, also evaluated as geo priors for fine-grained image classification of iNaturalist images of wild species. The main work is on range maps, but the image classification experiment gives it a computer vision component, so the paper is included.

title: POLO – Point-Based, Multi-class Animal Detection
reason: Develops a point-based detection model (POLO) and evaluates it on drone images of wild waterfowl in the Izembek lagoon, Alaska, for animal counting.

title: Multimodal Fusion Strategies for Mapping Biophysical Landscape Features
reason: Deep learning classification of UAV thermal/RGB/LiDAR imagery to map direct signs of wild animals (rhino middens, termite mounds) in Kruger National Park.

title: WildFusion: Individual Animal Identification with Calibrated Similarity Fusion
reason: Proposes a computer vision method for individual animal re-identification evaluated on 17 animal re-ID datasets covering many wild species (tigers, hyenas, leopards, whales, sea turtles) together with cows.

title: Towards Zero-Shot Camera Trap Image Categorization
reason: Primary study benchmarking and proposing classification pipelines (supervised and zero-shot) for camera trap images of wild animals.

title: Deep Learning for Large-Scale Plankton Image Classification
venue: World Congress on Medical Physics and Biomedical Engineering, September 7 - 12, 2009, Munich, Germany
reason: Zooplankton were caught at sea with a net and then digitised as preserved samples on a flatbed scanner. The analysed images show collected specimens, not free-ranging animals imaged in their environment.

title: Advancing Underwater Image Quality Enhancement Through Hybrid Deep Learning Architectures
venue: Lecture notes in networks and systems
reason: Generic underwater image enhancement method; animals are not the subject and no wildlife application is analysed.

title: Detection of Animal Movement from Weather Radar Using Self-supervised Learning
venue: Communications in computer and information science
reason: Proposes a self-supervised U-Net segmentation method to detect wild waterbird movement in weather radar images from Darwin, Australia.

title: Enhancing Underwater Exploration Through ROV Design with 3D-Printed Components and Dual Cameras
reason: Engineering paper on ROV hardware design with 3D-printed parts and dual webcams; the cameras only provide video for navigation and recording. No image analysis, detection or counting method is implemented or evaluated, and no animals are analysed.

title: Detection of Underwater Multi-targets Based on Self-supervised Learning and Deformable Path Aggregation Feature Pyramid Network
venue: Communications in computer and information science
reason: Proposes a CNN detector (improved YOLOv5 with self-supervised pretraining) for detecting underwater marine organisms (scallop, echinus, starfish, fish, turtle, etc.) in underwater images.

title: Artificial intelligence as an ally to assess and manage the golden mussel (Limnoperna fortunei (Dunker, 1857)) bioinvasion
reason: CNN-based classification, segmentation and counting of free-living invasive golden mussels in field photographs from Brazilian reservoirs (natural substrates and recruitment plates).

title: Generalized category discovery in fine-grained recognition
reason: Method paper on generalized category discovery that is applied to individual identification of non-domestic red pandas and giant pandas, plus domestic cattle. The paper does not say whether the panda images show wild or captive animals. Wildlife individual identification is a stated application.

title: Octopus body language: body patterns of Abdopus capricornicus during social interactions
reason: Behavioural ethology study in which videos of wild-caught octopuses held in aquarium tanks were scored by hand in VLC Media Player. There is no computer vision or automated image analysis method, and the animals were recorded only in captivity.

title: Enhancing marine wildlife observations: the application of tethered balloon systems and advanced imaging sensors for sustainable marine energy development
reason: Field study applying thermal imaging from a tethered balloon and a surface camera, with a machine-learning whale blow detector compared against human review, to free-ranging migrating gray whales and seabirds.

title: Ocean Ruler– an image-based, AI-driven approach to small-scale fisheries monitoring and catch size estimation
reason: Applies computer vision (deep learning region detection plus OpenCV edge detection) to smartphone images of wild-caught marine fish and invertebrates from fisheries to estimate their size.

title: Comparing the performance of two scientific tools for obtaining fish length measurements
reason: Stereo-video photogrammetry (3D reconstruction from image landmarks) used to measure lengths of wild reef fish filmed in situ on a rocky reef; compares two software tools.

title: Reproductive status affects social network dynamics in pallid bats (Antrozous pallidus)
reason: The study builds social networks of wild pallid bats from RFID/PIT-tag detections inside a roost. It analyses no images or video.

title: First full census in 45 years of a large colony of breeding penguins at False Round Point, King George Island
reason: Drone orthomosaic census of wild penguins, but nests were counted manually by an expert observer and colonies traced by hand. Apart from photogrammetric stitching, no computer vision analysis of the animals is done.

title: Quantifying coral reef carbonate budgets: a comparison between ReefBudget and CoralNet
reason: Wild coral reef photoquadrats are analysed, but benthic cover comes from manual point annotation in CoralNet and manual measurement in JMicrovision. No automated computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated; the study compares carbonate budget calculation methods.

title: High-resolution aerial imagery reveals that the distribution and arrangement of Acropora palmata patches determine their resistance to hurricane impacts
reason: UAV imagery of wild Acropora palmata coral patches processed by photogrammetry into orthomosaics; patches delineated and a semi-automatic classification evaluated for accuracy.

title: Estimating coral reef carbonate budgets using Structure-from-Motion photogrammetry
reason: Develops an SfM photogrammetry (3D reconstruction) workflow from underwater images to quantify wild coral and bioeroding urchin metrics on natural reefs for carbonate budgets.

title: Fate-tracking early coral recruits following bleaching in a remote reef ecosystem
reason: Applies structure-from-motion photogrammetry to underwater images of wild coral reefs to reconstruct reefs and track individual coral recruits over time.

title: Modernising sea cucumber surveys using remotely operated vehicles and aerial drones
reason: Wild sea cucumbers on the Great Barrier Reef were surveyed with drone orthomosaics and ROV/GoPro video. However, experts counted and identified the animals by eye. No computer vision method was developed, applied or evaluated; the only automated image step is orthomosaic generation.

title: Coral-CAT: A semi-automatic coral color analysis tool
reason: Image analysis tool that segments corals and assigns colour codes to images of wild coral fragments and in situ underwater coral colonies from the Red Sea.

title: Respiration rates and inferred mass-specific field metabolic rates decline with body size among five sympatric cetaceans
reason: Bioenergetics study of wild cetaceans; UAV video was used only for manual breath counting (Solomon Coder) and manual photogrammetric body measurement. No computer vision method is developed or applied; the core analysis is respiration-based metabolic modelling.

title: Optimizing feature map matching for marine benthic organism detection
reason: Proposes a CNN-based detector for marine benthic organisms (sea urchins, sea cucumbers, scallops) in underwater seafloor images.

title: Low visibility underwater biological target detection based on the improved YOLOV5s
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv5s detector for marine organisms (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish) in images that underwater robots captured in real underwater environments. The paper does not mention aquaculture.

title: Measurement error and effect size in geometric morphometrics: assessing the impact of 2D landmark digitization error in interspecific comparisons of Procrustes shape data
reason: Methodological geometric morphometrics study of manual landmark digitization error on photographs of museum marmot crania; no computer vision method, and the subjects are museum specimens rather than free-ranging animals.

title: Deep learning on field photography reveals the morphometric diversity of Colombian freshwater fish
reason: Applies Grounding DINO + SAM segmentation to field photographs of live wild-caught Colombian freshwater fish (photographed in portable aquarium in the field) for morphometric analysis.

title: GUNNEL: guided mixup augmentation and multi-model fusion for aquatic animal segmentation
reason: Proposes an instance segmentation framework and a dataset (AAS) for aquatic animals, including camouflaged animals, built from existing image datasets. Primary CV research with animals as the subject. The paper does not state whether the animals are wild or captive.

title: Animal re-identification in video through track clustering
reason: Proposes a track-clustering method for individual animal re-identification in video; data include free-ranging pigeons filmed in public places (ground, kerb, square) as well as farm pigs and koi fish.

title: Statistical framework for butterfly species recognition using raw spatio-hyperspectral images
reason: The butterflies were collected as specimens and imaged while immobilised on a conveyor belt with a fixed hyperspectral camera. No free-ranging animals were imaged, and the rules place specimens under E-CAPTIVE. The authors also say the method is not yet suitable for butterflies moving freely in natural environments.

title: Japanese mayfly family classification with a vision transformer model
reason: Images are close-up photos of collected mayfly specimens taken with a digital camera or stereo microscope against black or ruler backgrounds, not of free-ranging animals in the field. The criterion lists specimen imaging under E-CAPTIVE.

title: A three-dimensional kinematic analysis of bipedal walking in a white-handed gibbon (Hylobates lar) on a horizontal pole and flat surface
reason: 3D marker-based kinematic analysis of a single captive white-handed gibbon walking on experimental substrates; no wild animals; landmarks digitized manually rather than by an automated vision method.

title: Unsupervised clustering optimization-based efficient attention in YOLO for underwater object detection
reason: The paper proposes a CV detection method for underwater marine organisms. Part of the data shows free-ranging animals: Brackish has fish, crabs and jellyfish filmed in strait waters, and RUOD has fish, turtles and corals. The rest comes from marine ranches, where animals are ranched or artificially released.

title: A data-centric framework for combating domain shift in underwater object detection with image enhancement
reason: Proposes and evaluates a framework using image enhancement for underwater object detection of fish, jellyfish and benthic organisms in real-world aquatic datasets.

title: A lightweight fine-grained pelagic fish recognition algorithm based on object detection
reason: Proposes a lightweight YOLOv8-based detector for fine-grained recognition of six wild pelagic fish species (sailfish, marlin, tunas). The images come from fisheries catch monitoring, not from aquaculture.

title: Utilizing the spotting patterns of bull trout to identify individuals in photo-identification software
reason: Primary study applying photo-identification software (I3S Classic) to photographs of wild bull trout captured at a weir in an Idaho creek to recognise individuals.

title: Modeling coordination and regularity in nocturnal behavior of ungulates in zoos
reason: Analyses nocturnal standing/lying behaviour of ungulates housed in German and Dutch zoos (behaviour classified from night-vision video with BOVIDS); only captive animals.

title: Smart IoT-based snake trapping device for automated snake capture and identification
reason: Primary study presenting a trap for wild snakes with an on-board CNN image classifier (venomous vs non-venomous). Mostly hardware design; the origin of the training images is not described, so whether they show wild animals is not stated.

title: Broadscale reconnaissance of coral reefs from citizen science and deep learning
reason: Primary study applying a semantic segmentation deep learning model to citizen-collected underwater images of wild corals (animals) on the Great Barrier Reef to estimate benthic cover.

title: Unsupervised deep clustering as a tool for the identification of dark taxa in biomonitoring
reason: Chironomid larvae collected in the field were slide-mounted and imaged under a stereomicroscope using a lab-based protocol. This is microscopy of specimens, not images of free-ranging animals.

title: Evidence for temporal morphological change in northern but not southern breeding crowned sparrows (Zonotrichia spp.)
reason: Morphological measurements of museum bird skins taken with digital calipers and analysed statistically; no image or video analysis.

title: Image-based South Asian bee species identification: a machine learning approach
reason: CNN classification of field-captured images of free-ranging South Asian social bees visiting crop flowers; a new dataset is introduced and benchmarked.

title: Detecting spatiotemporal changes in harvester ant disks in response to fire and rodent competition using small unoccupied aerial systems imagery
reason: Applies object-based image classification to sUAV imagery to detect disks (nest signs) of wild western harvester ants in a field experiment in the Great Basin Desert.

title: Long-term, landscape- and wind-driven snow conditions influence Adélie penguin colony extinctions
reason: Image analysis (supervised pixel classification, structure-from-motion) is applied only to snow cover and terrain (habitat/land cover). Penguin sub-colony perimeters were traced by hand from drone imagery, and the penguin data otherwise come from field censuses, so no computer vision method is applied to the animals.

title: Crown-of-thorns starfish promote additional fine-grained habitat fragmentation in a coral reef ecosystem
reason: Underwater photos of wild coral reefs were digitised and classified by hand in ArcGIS/QGIS, and the resulting maps were analysed with landscape metrics. No computer vision method is developed or applied to the images.

title: Enhancing structural connectivity through coral restoration by adopting a landscape ecology perspective
reason: Drone imagery of wild reefs is classified with OBIA (meanshift segmentation plus SVM) to map live Acropora palmata coral, and the map is used for connectivity modelling.

title: Towards interpretable and robust UAV-based foundation model for endangered species monitoring in complex ecosystems
reason: Primary study applying a fine-tuned SAM2 segmentation model and SVM classifier to UAV imagery of foraging trails (direct signs) of wild juvenile tri-spine horseshoe crabs on an intertidal mudflat.

title: Artificial intelligence—based detection and tracking of reef fish in coral habitats: an approach for Lakshadweep’s marine spatial planning
reason: Primary study applying YOLOv5 with DeepSORT to diver-captured underwater video of free-ranging reef fish in a coral lagoon.

title: An empirical study of automatic wildlife detection using drone-derived imagery and object detection
reason: Empirical benchmark of object detectors on drone imagery of wild animals (thermal wildlife signatures in native forest) plus a public drone dataset that also contains livestock classes.

title: A dual-path feature learning neural network for enhancing image classification in marine biology
reason: Proposes a dual-path CNN for classifying fish species in underwater images (LifeCLEF 2015, Fish4Knowledge), which show marine fish in underwater environments; primary research with a computer vision method.

title: FEFM-YOLO11: Underwater Object Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLO11
reason: Proposes an improved YOLO11 detector for marine benthic animals (echinus, holothurian, starfish, scallop) in images collected from real underwater environments.

title: A transfer learning approach to classify insect diversity based on explainable AI
reason: Classifies agricultural crop pest insects to help farmers protect crops and reduce pesticide use; the application is crop pest management in production, not wildlife.

title: A scalable two-stage model for real-time Wetland bird recognition
reason: Proposes a two-stage detection plus fine-grained classification model for recognising birds in images captured by cameras in a wetland park, i.e. free-ranging wild birds.

title: Multi-scale detection of underwater objects using attention mechanisms and normalized Wasserstein distance loss
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for marine organisms (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish) in real underwater images, with the stated aim of supporting biodiversity monitoring and conservation.

title: YOLOv11 optimization for efficient resource utilization
reason: Generic object-detection optimisation of YOLOv11 evaluated on weed/crop, blood cell, underwater pipe, airplane, brain tumor and face datasets; no animals are analysed and wildlife is not the subject.

title: MMFTrack: an occlusion-aware and species-specific real-time tracking model for marine multi-fish
reason: Proposes a multi-object tracking model for wild marine fish in underwater videos from the South China Sea and public reef fish datasets.

title: Multi-scale adaptive small and overlapping target detection in underwater images
reason: Proposes a YOLOv8n-based detector for underwater marine organisms (echinus, holothurian, starfish, scallop, fish, etc.) in underwater images. One generalization dataset (ADOD) comes from an aquarium, so the subjects are mixed.

title: Aquafuse-net: an accuracy-efficiency balanced framework for underwater target detection with multi-scale feature enhancement
reason: Proposes a deep learning detector for marine organisms (sea urchins, sea cucumbers, starfish, scallops, fish, jellyfish) in underwater images from natural coastal waters.

title: Learning with Enriched Inductive Biases for Vision-Language Models
reason: Generic few-shot vision-language adaptation method evaluated on general benchmarks (ImageNet, Pets, Caltech101, etc.); animals appear only as benchmark classes and wildlife is not the stated subject.

title: Learning Structure-Supporting Dependencies via Keypoint Interactive Transformer for General Mammal Pose Estimation
reason: Proposes a transformer-based pose estimation method for general mammals, evaluated on animal pose datasets (AP10K, AnimalKingdom, AnimalPose) that include wild mammals such as giraffes and bison alongside domestic species.

title: Animal-CLIP: A Dual-Prompt Enhanced Vision-Language Model for Animal Action Recognition
reason: Proposes a vision-language model for animal action recognition in videos of wild animals in natural environments (Animal Kingdom, MammalNet, LoTE-Animal).

title: Simplified Concrete Dropout - Improving the Generation of Attribution Masks for Fine-grained Classification
reason: Generic explainability/attribution method for fine-grained classification, evaluated only on standard fine-grained benchmarks (CUB-200-2011, NA-Birds, Stanford Dogs); wildlife conservation is not the stated subject.

title: From Forest to Zoo: Great Ape Behavior Recognition with ChimpBehave
reason: Introduces a zoo chimpanzee behaviour dataset and benchmarks action recognition models on it and on PanAf, camera-trap footage of wild chimpanzees and gorillas in African forests, so part of the analysed data shows wild animals.

title: BaboonLand Dataset: Tracking Primates in the Wild and Automating Behaviour Recognition from Drone Videos
reason: Presents a drone video dataset of wild olive baboons with benchmarks for detection, tracking and behaviour recognition.

title: Real-time underwater target detection based on improved YOLOv7
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv7 detector for marine invertebrates (holothurian, scallop, echinus, starfish) in real underwater images from the URPC 2019 dataset; primary computer vision research on free-ranging marine animals.

title: Enhanced underwater object detection with YOLO-LDFE: a model for improved accuracy with balanced efficiency
reason: Proposes a YOLOv8-based detector for underwater marine animals (fish, sharks, whales, urchins etc.) in underwater images and introduces a new multi-species dataset.

title: Rcf-yolo: an underwater object detection algorithm based on improved YOLOv10n
reason: Proposes a CNN detector (RCF-YOLO) for marine organisms in underwater images (URPC, DUO, RUOD). The animals are free-ranging marine fauna in a marine environment, and the paper does not describe captive or farmed settings.

title: Yolo-based power-efficient object detection on edge devices for USVs
reason: Object detection for unmanned surface vehicles, aimed at boats, buoys, jet-skis, swimmers and other obstacles. No animals are analysed.

title: LMC-YOLO: a lightweight underwater benthic organism detection network with multi-scale feature extraction
reason: Proposes a lightweight CNN detector for marine benthic organisms and other underwater animals in underwater images (URPC, RUOD). The paper does not say the animals are captive.

title: Lightweight real-time detection transformer with Single-Head Self-Attention and Feature Selection for underwater object detection
reason: Proposes a lightweight RT-DETR detector for marine organisms (sea cucumber, echinus, scallop, starfish) in underwater images. The paper does not explicitly say the animals are wild or farmed.

title: An optimized deep-learning framework for underwater object detection and classification using UGIF-Net and spatiotemporal attention
reason: Proposes a deep-learning method for detecting and classifying underwater objects. The evaluated categories are marine animals (echinus, holothurian, scallop, starfish) in underwater benchmark datasets. The paper does not say how the animals were imaged.

title: LUOD-YOLO: a lightweight underwater object detection model based on dynamic feature fusion, dual path rearrangement and cross-scale integration
reason: Proposes a lightweight YOLO-based detector for underwater marine organisms (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish) in underwater images; the paper does not say where the images come from or whether the animals are wild.

title: FA-YOLO: a YOLO model based on attention mechanism and feature fusion for object detection in multi-classification underwater datasets
reason: Proposes a YOLO-based detector for underwater organisms (fish, jellyfish, crabs, etc.) evaluated on the MKUO and DUO underwater datasets. The paper does not say whether the animals are wild or captive.

title: LUW-DETR: a lightweight underwater object detection based on DETR
reason: Proposes a lightweight DETR-based detector for underwater marine organisms (fish, sea turtles, jellyfish, echinoderms, etc.), evaluated on the RUOD and DUO underwater datasets, with marine ecosystem monitoring as a stated application.

title: Overcoming annotation bottlenecks in underwater fish segmentation: a robust self-supervised learning approach
reason: Proposes a self-supervised computer vision method for segmenting fish in underwater videos recorded in natural Australian habitats and estuaries.

title: Innovative deep learning solutions for Turkish butterfly species identification: a VGGNet enhancement study
reason: Primary study that classifies images of nine non-domestic butterfly species with CNNs for biodiversity monitoring. The images come from a public Kaggle dataset; the paper does not state whether they show free-ranging or captive individuals, so inclusion rests on the species being wild taxa.

title: YOLOv8-UW: innovative real-time algorithm for underwater object detection
reason: Proposes YOLOv8-UW for detecting marine benthic organisms (holothurian, echinus, starfish, scallop) in seabed images collected by an AUV in a real marine environment.

title: FishFusionNet: An ensemble-based approach for fish species identification using SqueezeNet and efficient attention-boosted semi-local network
reason: Fish species classification on images of harvested fish (live and dead) photographed out of water, mainly at fish markets; no images of free-ranging animals in their habitat. Borderline: the external dataset includes some images taken at river areas.

title: DarkActionNet: An efficient neural network for low-light animal behavior recognition
reason: Proposes a video behavior recognition network evaluated on the Animal Kingdom dataset (850+ animal species, wild animals) as well as lab mice and a human action benchmark; wildlife monitoring is a stated application.

title: TFEH-Net: Two-stage feature enhanced hybrid network for underwater object detection
reason: Proposes a deep detection network for underwater objects, evaluated on datasets of marine organisms (sea cucumber, sea urchin, scallop) and marine animals. The animals are the detection targets, although the paper does not say whether they are wild or farmed.

title: A novel multi-feature fusion network for semantic segmentation
reason: Generic semantic segmentation method evaluated on CamVid, Cityscapes and PASCAL VOC 2012; animals appear only as benchmark classes and wildlife is not the subject.

title: UES-YOLO: Underwater biological detection based on YOLO with an efficient sampling block
reason: Underwater detection on UDD (marine ranching, i.e. ranched/farmed seafood, framed for automated marine fishing) and the Aquarium dataset (zoo/aquarium animals). None of the analysed data is stated to show wild, free-ranging animals.

title: YOLO-Bird: Small Bird Object Detection in Natural Scenes
reason: Proposes a YOLO-based detector for small bird targets in natural scenes, evaluated on bird detection datasets showing free-ranging birds.

title: Semantic segmentation of marine animal image by U-Net based on multi-cognitive visual adapter and dual-attention fusion mechanism
reason: Proposes a segmentation network (DM-UNet) for underwater marine animal images, evaluated on a new transparent-organism dataset and on public marine animal segmentation datasets. The paper does not say whether the TGA animals were captive.
