title: Foreground-Centric learning improves robustness in fine-grained visual recognition
reason: Proposes foreground-centric (segmentation then classification) pipeline for fine-grained bird species recognition on raw field images, plus CUB-200-2011.

title: Self-paced learning strategy with easy sample prior based on confidence for the flying bird object detection model training
reason: Proposes a training strategy for detecting free-flying birds in outdoor surveillance videos (traction substations, farmland).

title: YOLO-DBS: Efficient Target Detection in Complex Underwater Scene Images Based on Improved YOLOv8
venue: Journal of Ocean University of China
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv8 detector for marine organisms (fish, starfish, coral, turtle, etc.) in underwater scene images from the RUOD dataset.

title: An Efficient and Dynamic Framework for Multi-Scale Target Detection of Underwater Organisms
venue: Journal of Ocean University of China
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv8 detector for underwater organisms (fish, turtles, jellyfish etc.) evaluated on the RUOD real underwater image dataset from diverse aquatic environments.

title: Enhanced underwater image classification using SAE-based adaptive golden eagle optimizer for high-accuracy marine species identification
reason: Primary study proposing a computer vision classifier for marine species in underwater images. Dataset 1 is named 'aquarium data' (suggesting captive animals); the origin of Dataset 2 ('sea animals') is not stated, so wild/captive status is not reported. Included because the stated subject is marine species identification and captive-only status is not established.

title: ARTEMIS: animal recognition through enhanced multimodal integration system
venue: International Journal of Machine Learning and Cybernetics
reason: Proposes a multimodal transformer framework for animal action recognition in video, evaluated on the Animal Kingdom dataset (850 species) and on UAV recordings of baboons (BaboonLand). The paper does not explicitly state that the animals are wild; this is inferred from the UAV baboon recordings and the framing as real-world animal monitoring.

title: Automatic avian parasitic egg identification from pertinent visual features using hybrid machine learning models
venue: International Journal of Machine Learning and Cybernetics
reason: Computer vision classification of egg images from nests of a wild Slender-Billed Gull colony (direct signs: nests/eggs) for conservation.

title: A Hybrid Method for Segmentation and Recognition of Butterfly Objects in Camouflage Images
venue: Arabian Journal for Science and Engineering
reason: Primary study proposing a hybrid segmentation and species-recognition method on web-collected images of camouflaged butterflies photographed in natural environments.

title: Faster R-CNN Marine Benthos Detection with Multi-scale Channel Attention Mechanism and RoIAlign
venue: Arabian Journal for Science and Engineering
reason: Proposes an improved Faster R-CNN for detecting marine benthic organisms in underwater images from two underwater detection datasets; whether the animals are wild or farmed is not stated.

title: Development of Technologies for Prevention of Wild-Animal Related Losses to Agricultural Fields
venue: Journal of the Institution of Engineers India Series B
reason: Proposes a WSN plus computer-vision system (WSN-CV) that detects and classifies wild animals raiding agricultural fields and reports detection accuracy. The image data are poorly described, but the subject is free-ranging wild animals.

title: A study of enhanced visual perception of marine biology images based on diffusion-GAN
reason: Proposes GAN/diffusion models to generate images of marine organisms (sea anemones, wild sea turtles) from underwater and web image datasets; primary computer vision research with wildlife as the stated subject.

title: Coral reef image classification using deep CNNs, transformer features, and YOLOv8
reason: Deep learning classification of real-world underwater images of healthy vs bleached corals (wild reef animals) for reef health monitoring.

title: MarineDetNet: Enhancing Underwater Image Quality for Improved Marine Object Detection
venue: Iranian Journal of Science and Technology Transactions of Electrical Engineering
reason: Proposes a CNN-based underwater image enhancement network combined with YOLOv8 to detect marine organisms (echinus, holothurian, scallop, starfish) in the DUO underwater dataset. The paper does not say whether these animals are wild or farmed; they are treated as free-ranging marine organisms in underwater habitats.

title: Automated cetacean detection in UAV imagery using AI models: a case study on Delphinid species
venue: International Journal of Data Science and Analytics
reason: CNN and CNN-LSTM models classify the presence of wild dolphins in UAV aerial images and video, validated on field UAV data collected offshore southern Portugal.

title: Ocean scope: a boosted novel ensemble deep learning-driven accurate underwater object detection and classification system using enhanced YOLOv8 and ACLS-RCNN
venue: International Journal of Data Science and Analytics
reason: Proposes a deep learning detection and classification pipeline for underwater organisms (echinus, holothurian, scallop, starfish, fish, crabs, jellyfish, shrimp) in underwater images and video from public datasets.

title: Contrastive Learning for Wildlife Re-identification: SimCLR, Supervised Tuning, and Methodological Insights
reason: Primary study applying SimCLR self-supervised pre-training and supervised fine-tuning to animal images from the WildlifeReID-10k dataset. The 37 classes include wild taxa (tiger, chimpanzee, polar bear, whale shark, sea turtles) alongside domestic ones (dog, cattle).

title: FINDER: Fish Identification using Deep Ensemble Recognition
reason: Deep ensemble CNN/ViT classification of fish species. One dataset (Croatian Fish) shows fish in their natural habitat. The other (Fish-Pak) shows carp photographed at various places in Pakistan, in an aquaculture context.

title: Dual-Attention DeepLabv3 + with MobileNetV2 for efficient underwater object detection
reason: Proposes a dual-attention DeepLabv3+ segmentation model for underwater object detection, evaluated on underwater images of marine animals (echinus, starfish, scallop, holothurian, and fish from tropical Australian marine environments).

title: Edge region segmenting scheme for underwater ecology object classification using lateral neural network
reason: Proposes an edge-segmentation and lateral neural network method to segment and classify underwater images of plants, fish and other living organisms as living or non-living, aimed at marine ecology monitoring.

title: An enhanced YOLOv8 algorithm for fish school recognition integrating SEAttention and LDConv
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv8 detector for fish evaluated on DeepFish, which records natural fish communities in marine habitats.

title: Bio-inspired underwater robotic vehicle for marine exploration and AI-powered fish detection
reason: Proposes Ghost-YOLOv12 fish detector trained and evaluated on DeepFish underwater images of fish from natural marine habitats in tropical Australia, alongside a simulated bio-inspired ROV design.

title: An Efficient EPReLU-CSGNN-MALSTCAM and SSOA-Based Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) to Generate Textual Explanations
reason: Proposes a computer vision pipeline for detection, classification, pose estimation and captioning of animal images (90 animal classes). The paper does not say whether the animals are wild or domestic, but animals are its stated subject.

title: Shape variation in the eye patch and dorsal fin of southern hemisphere killer whales (Orcinus orca)
reason: Image-based morphometric analysis (outline extraction, elliptical Fourier analysis, LDA classification) of photographs of wild killer whales in Australian and Antarctic waters.

title: Gait kinematics during forward and backward locomotion in the Ansell’s mole-rat (Fukomys anselli)
reason: Pose estimation with DeepLabCut is applied only to captive Ansell's mole-rats from a university breeding stock, filmed in lab tunnels and on a treadmill. No wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Automated approach for wildlife detection and tracking using YOLOv8 deep learning algorithm
reason: Applies YOLOv8 to detect wild animals (deer, elephants, tigers) in images for safari wildlife monitoring; primary research.

title: Early detection of marine bioinvasion by sun corals using YOLOv8
reason: Applies YOLOv8 object detection to underwater images of invasive sun corals (Tubastraea spp.), animals recorded in the wild via iNaturalist and researcher records; primary research.

title: Bi2F-YOLO: a novel framework for underwater object detection based on YOLOv7
reason: Proposes a YOLOv7-based detector for underwater objects, evaluated on the RUOD dataset of marine organisms (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish, fish, etc.) in natural underwater scenes. The stated application includes ecological conservation.

title: Underwater fish species recognition based on feature fusion visual attention graph convolutional networks
reason: Proposes a graph convolutional network for species classification of fish in underwater images recorded at observation platforms in natural waters (LCF-15 and Fish4Knowledge datasets).

title: UTNet: event-RGB multimodal fusion model for underwater transparent organism detection
reason: Proposes an event-RGB fusion CNN for detecting transparent underwater organisms (fish, prawn, jellyfish) on an image dataset. The paper does not say whether the animals were wild or kept in tanks, so it is included with subject type not reported.

title: Performance Metrics of Low-Code AI for Insect Species Classification
reason: Applies low-code CNN image classification to eight wild insect species from the Cholistan Desert. About 60% of the images were taken in natural field conditions.

title: Lightweight marine biodetection model based on improved YOLOv10
reason: Proposes a YOLOv10-based detector for marine organisms (fish, starfish, sea cucumbers, sea turtles, etc.) in underwater images from URPC and RUOD; the animals are not described as captive or farmed.

title: Deep learning approach to detect and visualize sexual dimorphism in monomorphic species
reason: Deep learning (EfficientNet) classifies sex from head photographs of wild, free-ranging sociable weavers captured in a nature reserve population.

title: Flight performance during courtship in male black-chinned hummingbirds, Archilochus alexandri
reason: Behavioural biomechanics study of wild hummingbird courtship flights. The flight trajectories came from manually digitising the birds in calibrated video, and no automated computer vision or image-analysis method is developed or evaluated.

title: 13. AnimalMotionViz: An interactive software tool for tracking and visualizing animal motion patterns using computer vision
reason: Tools for tracking motion and activity of livestock (dairy cattle in a barn, precision livestock monitoring); no wild animals.

title: Do pairs exhibit similar behaviours? Evaluating inter-individual synchrony in activities of Magellanic penguins
reason: The study analyses behaviour of captive aquarium penguins using immersion data loggers rather than images or video, so there is no computer vision. It would also fail the captive-only criterion.

title: DPAF-YOLO: YOLO-based dual-path attention fusion for glass eel detection and counting
reason: CNN detection and counting of wild glass eels (Anguilla japonica) filmed during on-site fishing operations in coastal waters. The animals are wild-caught, not farmed stock.

title: Advanced YOLOv4 for real-time underwater object detection: An application-oriented approach
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv4 detector applied to underwater images, including detection of wild fish, crabs, starfish, jellyfish and shrimp in the Brackish dataset.

title: Breaking biological camouflage: DFNet for unified detection across species leveraging depth and multimodal fusion
reason: Proposes a depth-guided segmentation network for camouflaged animals in natural scenes, evaluated on animal camouflage datasets; ecological and biodiversity monitoring is a stated application. Plant and human camouflage data are also used.

title: IoT and AI-driven solutions for human-wildlife conflict: Advancing sustainable agriculture and biodiversity conservation
reason: Applies YOLO-based detection to field camera images of wild crop-raiding animals (Nilgai, wild boar, elephants) together with domestic animals in Indian farmland.

title: A generalizable model for the facial recognition of sika deer with enhanced cross-domain performance
reason: All images show farmed sika deer at a deer farm, plus farm pigs and cattle; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: GS-YOLO: An improved plateau pika’s hole and bare patch detection algorithm based on YOLOv5s for UAV images
reason: Applies deep-learning object detection to UAV images of burrows (holes) and bare patches made by wild plateau pikas in alpine meadows. Burrows are direct signs of wild animals.

title: Deep learning and drone imagery for the automatic detection and quantification of common vole burrows in agricultural landscapes
reason: Applies deep learning (Mask R-CNN) and RF/SVM to UAV imagery to detect burrows (direct signs) of the free-ranging common vole, a wild rodent, in an alfalfa field.

title: bioWatch: a computer vision system for community-based identification and reporting of spotted lanternfly life stage
reason: Develops a YOLO-based detector for life stages of the invasive spotted lanternfly using iNaturalist photographs of free-living insects in natural habitats, framed as invasive species and biodiversity monitoring.

title: Step-by-step to success: Multi-stage learning driven robust audiovisual fusion network for fine-grained bird species classification
reason: Proposes an audiovisual fusion network that classifies bird species from video frames and audio. It is evaluated on bird video datasets (SSW60, AVB81). The paper does not say the birds are captive.

title: Effects of individual and group factors on the social relationships of Budgerigars
reason: Behavioural study of captive budgerigars bought from a pet market. One investigator scored the videos by hand and the analysis is statistical (GLMM, Elo rating), so no computer vision method is used. The animals are also captive only.

title: Swan Project promotes citizen science initiative through a public bird migration tracking
reason: Perspective article on a citizen-science swan tracking project; animal-borne camera images are only inspected visually, with no computer vision analysis.

title: Waterbird image recognition using lightweight deep learning in wetland environment
reason: Proposes a lightweight YOLO-based detector for recognising wild wetland waterbird species in images from Beijing wetlands.

title: SDNet: A self-supervised bird recognition method based on large language models and diffusion models for improving long-term bird monitoring
reason: Proposes a self-supervised bird species recognition method evaluated on images of wild birds from field monitoring stations in China and on a public bird dataset.

title: CDA-Net: Cross dimensional attention network for wetland bird detection
reason: Proposes a CNN-based detector for wild waterbirds in images collected in the Nanhai Wetland, China.

title: Short-term mating success in relation to fluctuating wing asymmetry in the male azure damselfly Coenagrion puella
reason: Wild-caught damselflies were killed and their dissected wings imaged under a stereomicroscope in the lab. The computer vision is applied to these microscopy images of specimens, not to images of free-ranging animals.

title: Selective observation causes differences in citizen science butterfly data
reason: The authors analyse occurrence records of wild butterflies from citizen-science photo-apps and GBIF to study observation bias. They do not develop, apply or evaluate any computer vision method on the images themselves.

title: Novel behavioral responses of sea turtles to gillnet fishing gear
reason: Wild-caught turtles were filmed only during controlled binary-choice trials in an experimental concrete tank, not free-ranging. Computer vision (SiamMargin tracking) is a minor measurement tool in a lab-style set-up.

title: Toward citizen science-based coral health detection using smartphone devices
reason: Deep-learning segmentation of coral health from smartphone images of tank corals, plus field monitoring images of wild corals from the Xisha Islands.

title: Food codes as an AI-based framework to investigate bird foraging ecology and interspecific interactions
reason: AI-based detection and species classification of wild birds visiting a garden feeder in a rural Mediterranean landscape, using time-lapse images.

title: Multi-stage image-based approach for fish detection and weight estimation
reason: Computer vision detection, species classification and weight estimation of wild-caught discarded fish from commercial fishing vessels, imaged on a conveyor belt.

title: Enhancing pollinator conservation: Monitoring of bees through object recognition
reason: Object detection of free-flying bees (Bombus, Apis mellifera) in images collected in situ at locations across the UK, framed as pollinator conservation monitoring.

title: Creating synthetic data sets for training of neural networks for automatic catch analysis in fisheries
reason: Computer vision (instance segmentation, species classification, keypoint detection) on images of wild-caught fish (cod, haddock, saithe) from commercial capture fisheries onboard fishing vessels; not aquaculture. Training data synthetic, evaluation on real vessel images.

title: DMSPN: A distortion-mitigated network for part-level pattern parsing of underwater squids
reason: Proposes a CNN-based part-level segmentation network for squid images collected in their natural underwater habitat.

title: FCNet: Accurate counting model of fish in complex underwater environments
reason: Fish counting in an aquaculture bucket and a near-shore aquaculture fish farm; farmed fish only, no wild free-ranging animals.

title: Zero shot multistage hierarchical fish classification using YOLOE and large language model
reason: Zero-shot detection and classification of coral reef fish in images of their natural habitat, using YOLOE and multimodal LLMs.

title: UB-Former: A fine-grained classification method for images of insects using biomorphic features
reason: Proposes a CV fine-grained classification method for insect images, evaluated on the iNaturalist 2017 Insecta subset (free-ranging insects) and IP102 pests; it is also tested on bird and domestic dog benchmarks.

title: Deep learning meets marine biology: Optimized fused features and LIME-driven insights for automated plankton classification
reason: Classifies phytoplankton (diatoms, dinoflagellates, ciliates, nanoflagellates, detritus) from Imaging FlowCytobot images; these are microalgae and protists, not animals, so no wild animals are the subject.

title: EcoWatch: Region of interest-based multi-quantization resource-efficient framework for migratory bird surveillance using wireless sensor networks and environmental context awareness
reason: Proposes an ROI-based compression framework with YOLOv8 detection and LTCE counting, evaluated on videos of wild migratory birds from the Macaulay Library.

title: Underwater target detection algorithm based on multi-scale feature fusion
reason: Proposes a YOLOv7-based detector for underwater organisms (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish) in seabed images from URPC2020. The stated application is marine-ranch monitoring, but the paper never says the animals are farmed; benthic invertebrates on the seabed are treated as free-ranging.

title: Animal tool use: Capturing tool-expertise development with a deep learning network
reason: Dispatch/commentary article discussing Moll et al.'s use of DeepLabCut on captive tool-naive carrion crows; no primary research or own image analysis.

title: Graph-based Moving Object Segmentation for underwater videos using semi-supervised learning
reason: Proposes a semi-supervised graph-based method to segment moving fish in underwater videos from fixed cameras off the coast of Taiwan (Fish4K). The authors' TFC pre-training dataset also includes aquarium images, so the subject type is mixed.

title: Real-time habitat mapping with YOLOv8: A multi-threaded approach to biodiversity preservation
reason: The detected classes are humans, dogs, cars, boats and trains. No wild animals are detected or analysed; the targets are mainly people and vehicles, and the only animal is the domestic dog.

title: IBERBIRDS: A dataset of flying bird species present in the Iberian Peninsula.
reason: Dataset paper presenting annotated images of wild flying bird species for detection and classification, with YOLOv11s used for automatic annotation.

title: A deep clustering framework for underwater image recognition
reason: Proposes a deep clustering method for recognising wild fish species in underwater images (WildFish dataset), aimed at assessing marine ecosystems.

title: MdeBEIA: Multi-task deep leaning for butterfly ecological image analysis
venue: Digital Signal Processing A Review Journal
reason: Proposes a multi-task deep learning model for segmentation and classification of butterfly ecological images, meaning butterflies photographed in natural habitats rather than specimens.

title: A video dataset for hadal snailfish along with the benchmark
venue: Deep Sea Research Part I Oceanographic Research Papers
reason: Primary study building an annotated video dataset of wild hadal snailfish recorded in the deep sea and benchmarking YOLOv8 instance segmentation models on it.

title: A cost-effective, open-source laboratory system for 3D photogrammetric analysis of corals
venue: Deep Sea Research Part II Topical Studies in Oceanography
reason: Laboratory aquarium system for photogrammetric 3D reconstruction of coral nubbins; all images were taken under controlled laboratory conditions, not of free-ranging animals.

title: Accelerating ecosystem monitoring through computer vision with deep metric learning
reason: Perspective paper introducing examples of deep metric learning applications in ecosystem monitoring; no primary image analysis performed.

title: Selective state models are what you need for animal action recognition
reason: Proposes a Mamba-based video model for animal action recognition, evaluated on Animal Kingdom (850 species) and BaboonLand (UAV footage of baboons).

title: In-field monitoring of ground-nesting insect aggregations using a scaleable multi-camera system
reason: Camera-based motion detection system applied to video of a wild, free-ranging ground-nesting bee aggregation outdoors, plus lab flight cages and bumblebee hives.

title: Efficient wildlife monitoring: Deep learning-based detection and counting of green turtles in coastal areas
reason: Develops YOLOv7 detection and BoT-SORT tracking/counting of wild green turtles in drone footage of Japanese coastal areas.

title: DeepFins: Capturing dynamics in underwater videos for fish detection
reason: Proposes a hybrid YOLOv11 + motion segmentation method for detecting fish in unconstrained underwater videos of natural marine habitats (OzFish, LifeCLEF 2015 coral reef videos).

title: An automatic identification method of common species based on ensemble learning
reason: Proposes an ensemble deep learning method to classify common wildlife species in camera trap images from Serengeti National Park and South Africa.

title: Advancing Sika deer detection and distance estimation through comprehensive camera calibration and distortion analysis
reason: The images the paper analyses show calibration targets: red-circle templates and chessboard patterns. No animal images or videos are analysed. Sika deer appear only through body measurements taken from the literature, which are used to estimate detection distances.

title: Deep sea spy: An online citizen science annotation platform for science and ocean literacy
reason: Wild deep-sea vent fauna are imaged, but the images are annotated manually by citizens and an expert. The only computation is aggregating annotation coordinates with Voronoi polygons; no automated image analysis or computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Metric learning unveiling disparities: A novel approach to recognize false trigger images in wildlife monitoring
reason: Proposes a metric-learning CNN method to recognise false-trigger (empty) camera trap images of wildlife from field deployments in Chinese forest parks/nature reserves.

title: Coral reef detection using ICESat-2 and machine learning
reason: Maps coral reef habitat presence ('coral' vs 'not coral' windows, merging coral/algae and rock classes) from ICESat-2 satellite LiDAR photon tracks turned into tabular features. This is habitat/geomorphic mapping, not image analysis of individual animals.

title: BEHAVE - facilitating behaviour coding from videos with AI-detected animals
reason: Software tool integrating AI animal detection (MegaDetector, YOLOv8) in videos to support behaviour coding, applied to field video of wild little auks.

title: Efficient tuna detection and counting with improved YOLOv8 and ByteTrack in pelagic fisheries
reason: Develops a YOLOv8-based detector plus ByteTrack counting method for images and video of wild-caught tuna on a pelagic longline fishing vessel. This is capture fisheries, not aquaculture.

title: A photogrammetric approach to the estimation of distance to animals in camera trap images
reason: Develops a photogrammetric (SfM depth map) method to estimate distance to wild animals in camera trap images for distance sampling.

title: Practical application of artificial intelligence for ecological image analysis: Trialling different levels of taxonomic classification to promote convolutional neural network performance
reason: Primary study training YOLOv5 object detectors on ROV seabed imagery of wild deep-sea benthic animals, comparing annotation at three levels of taxonomic resolution.

title: Wild ActionFormer: Enhancing wildlife action recognition for 11 endangered species in Wolong
reason: Develops a video action recognition network for wild animals recorded by infrared camera traps in Wolong Nature Reserve.

title: From underwater to drone: A novel multi-scale knowledge distillation approach for coral reef monitoring
reason: Primary study that trains vision transformer classifiers on underwater and drone images of wild coral reefs (coral morphotypes and associated fauna) in lagoons.

title: Exploiting facial side similarities to improve AI-driven sea turtle photo-identification systems
reason: Applies and evaluates computer vision re-identification methods (MegaDescriptor, SIFT) on photographs of wild sea turtles from Greece and Reunion Island.

title: Deep learning for automated coral reef monitoring a novel system based on YOLOv8 detection and DeepSORT tracking
reason: Applies YOLOv8 detection and DeepSORT tracking to underwater video transects of wild coral colonies on reefs in the Indian Ocean and New Caledonia, for reef monitoring.

title: Improving AI performance in wildlife monitoring through species and environment-specific training: A case study on desert Bighorn sheep
reason: Evaluates and retrains AI models to classify camera-trap images of wild desert bighorn sheep at desert water sources.

title: Underwater object detection algorithm integrating image enhancement and deformable convolution
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for underwater benthic organisms (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish) in underwater image datasets.

title: BirdRecon: A free open source tool for image based bird species recognition
reason: Deep ensemble CNN classification of 525 bird species from images, aimed at birdwatching, ornithology and biodiversity conservation; primary research.

title: Open real-time, non-invasive fish detection and size estimation utilizing binocular camera system in a Portuguese river affected by hydropeaking
reason: Develops and deploys a stereo-camera computer vision pipeline for detection and size estimation of wild fish in Portuguese rivers affected by hydropeaking.

title: Safe AI for coral reefs: Benchmarking out-of-distribution detection algorithms for coral reef image surveys
reason: Benchmarks out-of-distribution detection for deep learning classification of coral reef survey images (point annotations mapped to coral family labels) from wild reefs.

title: Reliable unmanned aerial vehicle-based thermal infrared target detection method for monitoring Procapra przewalskii in Qinghai
reason: Proposes a YOLOv8s-based multi-frame detection method for wild Procapra przewalskii in UAV thermal infrared video collected in the field in Qinghai.

title: Evaluating textural descriptors for automated image classification of stony reefs in turbid temperate waters
reason: Texture descriptors with a CatBoost classifier are applied to underwater seabed images from Baltic Sea reefs; the classes include wild blue mussels alongside algae and substrate types.

title: Supporting offshore wind growth: Automating data analysis in digital aerial surveys to enhance wildlife protection and survey efficiency
reason: Applies YOLOv5 object detection to digital aerial survey video to screen wild marine mammals and northern gannets at sea off Ireland.

title: Body-part-based individual feral cat identification from camera trap images using deep learning
reason: Deep learning individual identification of free-ranging feral cats from field camera trap images in Victoria, Australia.

title: SegmentR: Deep learning for automated segmentation with an R interface
reason: Software tool paper (R interface to GroundingDINO + SAM). The only animal images analysed are a horned bream image of unstated origin and a museum snake specimen; the iNaturalist images show flowers. No analysed data is shown to depict wild, free-ranging animals.

title: Conformal taxonomic validation: A semi-automated validation framework for citizen science records
reason: Primary study proposing a deep-learning plus conformal prediction framework for validating taxonomic identification of citizen-science photographs of medusozoans (jellyfish) recorded in the wild.

title: Best practices for AI-based image analysis applications in aquatic sciences: The iMagine case study
reason: Best-practice case-study paper that reports original CV results for wild marine animals: fish detection at the OBSEA observatory, deep-sea fauna detection in the Azores and on the Juan de Fuca Ridge, and Nephrops burrow detection. It also covers preserved zooplankton samples.

title: How many dollars are in the sea? Estimating sand dollar (Echinarachnius parma) abundance using an iteratively trained convolutional neural network and generalized additive models
reason: Applies a CNN detector (YOLO v7) and GAMs to underwater survey images to estimate abundance of wild sand dollars on the sea floor.

title: Automated recognition of deep-sea benthic megafauna in polymetallic nodule mining areas based on deep learning
reason: Proposes a deep learning detector (BM-YOLO) for wild deep-sea benthic megafauna in images taken in situ by baited Lander cameras in Pacific polymetallic nodule areas.

title: Mamba-based super-resolution and semi-supervised YOLOv10 for freshwater mussel detection using acoustic video camera: A case study at Lake Izunuma, Japan
reason: Develops super-resolution and YOLO-based detection of wild freshwater mussels in acoustic imaging sonar images from a field survey at Lake Izunuma.

title: A deep learning-based detection model and illumination-adaptive behavioral analysis for soldier crabs in the intertidal zone
reason: Deep learning detection of soldier crab behaviours on smartphone images taken in natural intertidal habitats in China. Tank-housed crabs were used only for the rhythm analysis and some generalisation tests.

title: Automated detection of sea cucumbers in turbid subtidal marine habitats: An explainable approach
reason: Applies YOLOv8 object detection to in-situ underwater video frames of wild sea cucumbers at coastal sites in Hong Kong for population surveys.

title: Contrasting the efficiency of imaging systems for mesozooplankton indicators across Pacific and Atlantic coastal ecosystems
reason: Wild zooplankton were collected with nets, preserved in formaldehyde and imaged in the laboratory with a flow imaging microscopy system (FlowCam Macro). This is laboratory microscopy of preserved specimens, not imaging of free-ranging animals.

title: Individual identification of wild raptors using a deep learning approach: A case study of the white-tailed eagle
reason: Deep learning framework for individual identification of wild white-tailed eagles from PTZ camera video in a wetland.

title: Integrating AI into ecology for fully automated monitoring of endangered seabird breeding colonies
reason: Deep learning detection, classification, tracking and counting of wild breeding Common and Little Terns in a seabird colony, using images from remotely controlled cameras.

title: Towards automated and real-time multi-object detection of anguilliform fishes from sonar data using YOLOv8 deep learning algorithm
reason: The study detects wild migrating eels and lampreys in rivers, but all of the analysed data are imaging-sonar (acoustic) frames. No optical images are used, so it falls under sonar only.

title: AntPi: A Raspberry Pi based edge–cloud system for real-time ant species detection using YOLO
reason: Develops and evaluates YOLO-based detection and species classification of wild arboricolous ants from field and citizen-science images, deployed on an in-field edge device.

title: Whale Vision: A tool for identifying sperm whales and other cetaceans by their flank or fluke
reason: Deep learning re-identification of individual wild sperm whales and dolphins from boat-based photographs in the Gulf of Naples.

title: How to minimize the annotation effort in aerial wildlife surveys
reason: Primary study benchmarking deep-learning detection and localization models for counting animals in aerial survey images; the data cover wild ungulates and waterbirds together with domestic camels, donkeys and sheep/goats.

title: An automated approach for counting ants in densely populated images and gaining insight into ant foraging behavior
reason: Ant detection and counting on images of laboratory ant colonies in foraging arenas and trays; only six iNaturalist images are used qualitatively in the limitations section.

title: An investigation of lightweight AI models to classify African ungulate species from tracks
reason: Deep learning detection/classification of species from photographs of tracks (direct signs) of free-ranging African ungulates in a Botswana sanctuary.

title: Advances in deep learning-driven photo identification and meta analysis of cetaceans in large data repositories
reason: Deep learning pipeline for detection and photo-identification of individual wild cetaceans from photographs of five free-ranging populations.

title: CoralSCOP-LAT: Labeling and analyzing tool for coral reef images with dense semantic mask
reason: Primary study presenting and evaluating a segmentation-based labelling tool on underwater images of wild coral reefs (corals are animals) from field surveys.

title: A digital-twin strategy using robots for marine ecosystem monitoring
reason: Perspective/roadmap paper proposing a digital-twin-of-the-ocean architecture; AI image classification at OBSEA is only illustrated as an example, with no primary computer vision experiments or evaluation.

title: Multi-camera synchronization and instance tracking for Avian behavior analysis in a floating aviary
reason: Tracking pipeline applied to hand-raised, imprinted geese kept in an enclosed floating aviary. All of the analysed animals are captive, so no wild or free-ranging animals appear in the data.

title: Integrating AI technologies and citizen science to fast-track small and ectothermic animal monitoring
reason: Applies and compares object detectors (YOLOv5, Faster R-CNN) on video camera-trap data of wild small fauna in Victoria, Australia. A few captive snake videos were added, so the subject type is mixed.

title: Temporal aggregation of vision-language features for high-accuracy fish classification in automated monitoring
reason: Computer vision (vision-language embeddings) applied to underwater fish counter video of wild salmonids in Icelandic rivers.

title: Bridging AI and wildlife conservation: Classifying wildcats from genetically validated images
reason: CNN classification of European wildcats, hybrids and domestic cats from real-world images (camera traps, roadkills); wild animals included alongside domestic cats.

title: Machine learning to detect, classify, and count blackbirds damaging agriculture using drone-based imagery: Supporting AI-driven automation for deployment of damage management tools
reason: Drone imagery of free-ranging wild blackbird flocks in sunflower fields, with CNN detection, classification and counting of the birds.

title: A robust metric distance and height estimation pipeline for wildlife camera trap imagery
reason: Develops a computer vision pipeline (monocular depth estimation, detection, segmentation) to estimate distance and height of wild animals in camera trap images from Bubye Valley Conservancy, Zimbabwe.

title: Deep tracks: Using deep learning and procedurally simulated data for automated vertebrate footprints classification
reason: CNN classification of photographs of footprints (direct signs) of wild extant mammals/birds and fossil dinosaurs, augmented with simulated images.

title: Deep learning approach to landmarking and measurement error analysis for gilthead seabream (Sparus aurata) origin classification in geometric morphometrics
reason: Deep learning landmark detection on images of gilthead seabream specimens that include wild-origin and farm-associated wild fish as well as farmed fish, with geometric morphometric origin classification.

title: Effects of input-image size on performance of fish detection and species classification using deep learning
reason: Applies Mask R-CNN to detect and classify wild-caught fish from set-net fishery catches (capture fisheries, not aquaculture) photographed on a conveyor belt for stock assessment.

title: Towards decentralized ecological monitoring: A local-first web-based AI platform for sea turtle detection
reason: Applies deep learning object detection to UAV video of free-ranging sea turtles at sea in Greece, within a browser-based platform.

title: Automized segmentation of animal paths in UAS Imagery using deep learning - a case study from the Kruger National Park
reason: Deep learning segmentation of animal paths (direct signs of wild animals) in UAS imagery from Kruger National Park.

title: From pictures to numbers: Multi-species seabird surveys using drone imagery and neural networks
reason: Applies a deep learning detector (Faster R-CNN) to UAV orthomosaics of wild seabird colonies on the Norwegian coast to detect, classify and count birds.

title: Automated crocodile detection using deep learning and synthetic data
reason: All real images show farmed crocodiles at a commercial crocodile farm; the other data is synthetic. No wild or free-ranging animals are in the analysed data.

title: A lightweight Mamba-frequency fusion algorithm for underwater image enhancement under physical model constraints
reason: Generic underwater image enhancement method evaluated on general underwater image benchmarks (UIEB, LSUI). Animals are not the subject of the analysis and only appear incidentally in example images.

title: Artificial reef based ecosystem design and monitoring
reason: Applies a YOLOv8 model to images from a fixed underwater observatory camera to detect, classify and count wild fish at an artificial reef in the Mediterranean.

title: Hydrodynamic thresholds during the spawning period of Schizothorax prenanti and habitat restoration study
reason: Computer vision (YOLOv8 tracking) is applied only to hatchery-supplied fish in an indoor laboratory flume at a breeding station; field work used hydraulic measurements, not images.

title: Deep learning for Amur tiger re-identification in camera traps: A tool assisting population monitoring and spatio-temporal analysis
reason: Deep learning segmentation and re-identification of wild Amur tigers from camera-trap videos in the Northeast Tiger and Leopard National Park.

title: Temporal comparison of coral reefs in the Galápagos using differential alignment of 3D models and Machine-Learning
reason: Applies photogrammetric 3D reconstruction and a deep-learning image classifier to underwater images of wild coral reefs in the Galápagos Marine Reserve.

title: MDFNet: Integrating multiscale features and dynamic attention for underwater fish counting
reason: Fish counting of farmed carp and grass carp in aquaculture breeding ponds; no wild free-ranging animals in the analysed data.

title: Coastal exposure and artificialization: Drivers of shell shape variation in intertidal limpets
reason: Geometric morphometric study of collected wild limpet shells; landmarks placed on photographs and analysed statistically (GPA, PCA, CVA). No computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: From pixels to peaks: integrating LiDAR and RGB drone imagery to map mussel spat on intertidal rocky shores
reason: UAV RGB imagery and LiDAR used with pixel-based machine learning to map wild mussel spat and goose barnacles on a natural intertidal rocky shore.

title: Monitoring coral reefs by remote sensing techniques and acoustic data as a ground truth reference in Hurghada, Red Sea, Egypt
venue: The Egyptian Journal of Aquatic Research
reason: Applies image analysis (depth-invariant index habitat classification, PIF radiometric normalization change detection) to Sentinel-2 imagery to map wild coral reefs and detect coral bleaching in the Red Sea, validated with ROV imagery.

title: Underwater moving target detection and tracking based on enhanced you only look once and deep simple online and realtime tracking strategy
reason: Proposes a computer vision method (improved YOLOv5 + Deep SORT) to detect and track fish in underwater images and video. The paper does not say where the fish were filmed, but it treats them as ocean targets.

title: WB-YOLO: An efficient wild bat detection method for ecological monitoring in complex environments
reason: Proposes a YOLOv7-based detector for wild bats photographed in natural habitats in Anhui Province, China.

title: A diffusion model and knowledge distillation framework for robust coral detection in complex underwater environments
reason: Proposes a computer-vision method for detecting corals (animals). The main dataset comes from a coral breeding centre (captive). A second dataset of aerial coral images, presumably of reefs, is used to test generalisation.

title: Classification of animal species using efficient neuron attention stage-by-stage network
reason: Proposes a deep learning method (ENAS-Net) for classifying animal species and evaluates it on public datasets, one of which is a wildlife image dataset. Wildlife monitoring is the stated application.

title: A lightweight algorithm for wildlife detection in outdoor environments based on you only look once version 8 network
reason: Proposes a lightweight YOLOv8-based detector (WL-YOLO) for wildlife detection in outdoor environments, evaluated on a wildlife image dataset and public animal datasets.

title: Performance evaluation of low-power and lightweight object detectors for real-time monitoring in resource-constrained drone systems
reason: The paper benchmarks YOLO detectors on drone images of vehicles, ships and aircraft. No animals are analysed.

title: Diffusion-based feature absorption approach for improving lightweight object detectors in adverse weather conditions
reason: Object detection of persons, cars and buses in rainy nighttime driving scenes; no animals analysed.

title: A lightweight deep learning network for the precise detection and classification of variable plankton
reason: Proposes a lightweight CNN detector/classifier for marine zooplankton and phytoplankton images from public plankton datasets; wild marine organisms are the subject.

title: Cross-species animal pose estimation via feature map orthogonal decomposition decoder
reason: Proposes a ViT-based animal pose estimation method evaluated on public animal datasets including wild field imagery (LoTE Wild, AP10K, Animal Kingdom) alongside laboratory mouse/fly datasets; wildlife monitoring is a stated application.

title: Augmenting community-driven vector surveillance with automated image classification: Lessons from the Artificial Intelligence Mosquito Alert (AIMA) system
reason: Deep-learning detection and classification of mosquito species from citizen-submitted photographs taken in the wild; external benchmark sets contain laboratory-reared mosquitoes, so subjects are mixed.

title: Sample imbalance remote sensing small target detection based on discriminative feature learning and imbalanced feature semantic enrichment
reason: Proposes a CNN/transformer detector for imbalanced small-target detection and applies it to UAV images of wild animals (kudu, rhinoceros) plus cows, framed as endangered-species monitoring.

title: Insect identification by combining different neural networks
reason: Classifies insect species from BOLD specimen images paired with DNA barcodes. The images show collected, barcoded specimens rather than free-ranging animals in the wild, so the paper falls under museum/specimen exclusion.

title: MobileNet- and attention-based MLP-Mixer architecture for geographical-region recognition of a marine fish (Perciformes: Carangidae) using otolith images
reason: The fish were caught in the wild, but the analysed images are stereomicroscope photographs of otoliths extracted from them in a laboratory. This is specimen microscopy, not imagery of free-ranging animals or their signs.

title: GDP-CT: Grouped data pruning for camera trap
reason: Proposes a data pruning strategy for training species classifiers on wild-animal camera trap images (CCT20, iWildCam-WILDS).

title: InvaderDefender: Multimodal recognition of invasive alien species via a large language model with vision-guided targeted RAG
reason: Proposes a CNN+LLM framework to classify images of 20 invasive alien species, mostly forest insect pests. Images come from GBIF/CABI and are supplemented with laboratory specimen photos, so the data mix free-living organisms with specimens.

title: Whale identification and size estimation in satellite imagery via intelligent subtle perception
reason: Proposes a deep learning detector (WST-YOLOv9) for detecting wild whales and estimating their size in very high resolution satellite imagery.

title: Animal identity recognition based on gait features
reason: Proposes a gait-based identity recognition network (AnimalGaitNet) using video of cows from farms and tigers from zoos and the Internet. The tiger data is described as mainly captured in the wild, so at least part of the analysed data shows wild animals.

title: Detecting underwater salient objects via self-supervised depth priors and task-driven optimization
reason: Generic underwater salient object detection method evaluated on general USOD benchmarks covering many object categories (facilities, litter, plants, fish, animals). Wildlife is not the stated subject, and the paper does not say whether the animals are wild.

title: Investigating potential fish distributions in artificial and natural reefs using an optical method: Insights from subtropical offshore wind farms
reason: Applies a YOLOX deep learning detector to underwater videos of wild fish at offshore wind farms and reefs in China to estimate fish densities.

title: Using morphometric relationships for total length prediction of Atlantic cod (Gadus morhua) in electronic monitoring videos
reason: Wild-caught Atlantic cod are filmed by an electronic monitoring camera, but the measurements are taken by hand in the EM software and analysed with OLS regression. No computer vision or automated image analysis method is developed or applied.

title: Deep learning for genera-level bark beetle taxonomic classification
reason: CNN classification of images of wild bark beetles (Scolytinae) at genus level, using lab specimen photos from French forests plus web images from InsectImage and iNaturalist; forest pests in natural forests, not production agriculture.

title: SPADE: Simulator-assisted Performability Design for UAV-based monitoring systems
reason: Applies YOLOv5 object detection to UAV video for ecological monitoring of wildlife (deer) in a forest. The images come from a simulated AirSim environment with virtual wild animals, and wildlife monitoring is the stated application.

title: Developing a new method using thermal drones for population surveys of the world's rarest great ape species, Pongo tapanuliensis
reason: Thermal and RGB drone imagery used to detect, count and segment wild Tapanuli orangutans and other canopy animals in Sumatra. A calibration experiment also used rehabilitant Bornean orangutans at a forest school.

title: Automated 24-h surveys of flower-visiting communities reveal temporal complementarities and overlaps among strawberry pollinators
reason: Camera traps record wild insect pollinators visiting strawberry flowers, but people watched the footage by hand. No computer vision or automated image analysis is developed or applied.

title: Moderate plateau pika activity had minor effect on ecosystem C and N in alpine grasslands
reason: Drone images of alpine grasslands are analysed with a CNN to detect burrow entrances of wild plateau pika, which are direct animal signs. Thresholding is used to map pika mounds. The detections feed pika density estimates.

title: “Monkey influencers”: conservation culturomics of human-macaque (Macaca fascicularis) interactions
reason: Conservation culturomics study in which online content about long-tailed macaques was categorized manually and analysed statistically; no computer vision or automated image analysis is applied.

title: MDG-YOLO: A Benthic Organism Detection Algorithm for Degraded Underwater Visual Features Environments
reason: Proposes a YOLOv8-based detector for marine benthic organisms (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish) in underwater images of the DUO dataset.

title: Enhancing Transformer Models with Specialized Optimization for Underwater Fish Classification
reason: Applies modified transformer models to classify fish species in images of fish in natural underwater conditions (WildFish dataset).

title: Investigating Bottlenose Dolphin Interactive Behavior and Movement: A Case Study
reason: Camera-based detection and tracking of trained bottlenose dolphins kept in a managed lagoon at Dolphin Quest Oahu. Only captive animals are analysed.

title: Quantum-omni: a quantum computing and GPT-4o solution for camel-vehicle collisions
venue: International Journal of Transportation Science and Technology
reason: Detects and tracks free-roaming camels on Gulf roads from vehicle-mounted LiDAR and thermal infrared cameras plus GPT-4o vision, framed as wildlife-vehicle collision prevention. Inclusion is borderline because dromedaries are a domesticated species, but the animals analysed are free-ranging rather than kept in production.

title: Multi-fish tracking with underwater image enhancement by deep network in marine ecosystems
reason: Proposes a deep multi-fish tracking framework with underwater image enhancement, evaluated on unconstrained marine fish videos (Fish4Knowledge) and GMOT-40 fish category.

title: DECF-FGVC: A discriminative enhancement and complementary fusion approach for fine-grained bird visual classification
reason: Proposes a ViT-based fine-grained bird species classification method motivated by species conservation, evaluated on bird image datasets (CUB-200-2011, NABirds) and iNaturalist2017.

title: Toward a spatialized index of the “benthic ecological state” using a new Coral Reef Rapid Assessment Method (CORRAM): case study at Reunion Island
reason: Divers estimated coral reef benthic indicators visually in the field (CORRAM) and the results were mapped with kriging. The paper analyses no images or video.

title: Language-guided reasoning segmentation for underwater images
reason: Proposes a language-guided segmentation method and a dataset for underwater images that show marine life such as fish and coral in natural underwater scenes.

title: STAMF: Synergistic transformer and mamba fusion network for RGB-Polarization based underwater salient object detection
reason: Generic underwater salient object detection with RGB-polarization; objects (fish models, shipwrecks, divers, reefs) in lab-simulated scenes and generic USOD benchmarks. Wildlife is not the stated subject.

title: Synchronizing 3D LiDAR-based reconstruction of animals and environment for in situ ecosystem characterization
reason: This short communication is mainly a perspective. It proposes a framework and a device (Liprotect) for synchronized 3D LiDAR reconstruction of animals and their habitat. It shows only illustrative or simulated examples and gives no experimental evaluation, so it is not a primary empirical study.

title: M2Emo: Fine-grained mamba transformer guided multi-task golden snub-nosed monkey emotion recognition
reason: Proposes a deep learning method for identity, emotion and gender recognition from facial images of wild golden snub-nosed monkeys (EmoKey dataset, wild and semi-wild environments).

title: A computer vision enhanced IoT system for koala monitoring and recognition
reason: Camera-trap computer vision system for detecting and identifying koalas; data from wild koalas at road/rail crossings plus koalas at koala centres/sanctuaries.

title: Bounding box versus point annotation: The impact on deep learning performance for animal detection in aerial images
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
reason: Evaluates deep learning detection of wild African elephants and antelopes in aerial survey imagery, comparing bounding box and point annotations.

title: Causal learning-driven semantic segmentation for robust coral health status identification
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
reason: Proposes a deep learning semantic segmentation network for coral health status (live, dead, bleached) in in-situ underwater images of wild coral reefs.

title: Multi-dataset-integrated Coral-Lab segmentation with enhanced towed camera array for rapid large-scale coral reef monitoring and mapping
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
reason: Semantic segmentation of wild reef corals in underwater imagery collected by a towed camera array off Kumejima Island; primary research.

title: Towards sustainable construction: A cost-effective framework for bird monitoring from on-site collected videos leveraging deep active learning and synthetic training data
reason: Deep learning detection and classification of wild egrets nesting in an urban park, recorded with a fixed video camera system; primary research.

title: Oyster reef recovery: Impacts of rotational management and restoration efforts on public fishing grounds
reason: The study models oyster reef metrics from patent tong survey samples and harvest records using GLMMs. No image or video data is analysed.

title: Detecting habitat preferences and monitoring population dynamics of sea cucumbers in coastal ecosystems through underwater photogrammetry
reason: Underwater SfM photogrammetry and image analysis of orthomosaics used to count, measure and map wild sea cucumbers in a Mediterranean coastal area.

title: An open-source method for spatially and temporally explicit herbivory monitoring in semi-arid savannas
reason: YOLOv10 detection and counting of wild large herbivores in camera trap images at waterpoints in Namibian nature reserves, used for herbivory monitoring.

title: A non-destructive method for three-dimensional characterizing plateau pika's burrow system
reason: Field study that combines drone imagery, in which image recognition locates burrow entrances of wild plateau pikas, with GPR to reconstruct burrow systems in 3D. Burrows count as direct signs of animals. The computer-vision part is small and borderline, but drone images are analysed.

title: Temporal insights into ecological community: Advancing waterbird monitoring with dome camera and deep learning
reason: Applies deep learning detection, tracking and fine-grained classification to dome-camera video of wild waterbirds in a restored wetland at Dianchi Lake.

title: Enhancing aquatic ecosystem monitoring through fish jumping behavior analysis and YOLOV5: Applications in freshwater fish identification
reason: Applies YOLOv5-based computer vision to surveillance video of free-ranging freshwater fish jumping in a reservoir to identify species.

title: Multifactor synergistic drivers of first arrival dates in Chinese birds: Nationwide evidence from audio-video fusion monitoring
reason: Applies deep-learning detection (YOLOv8), segmentation (SegGPT) and classification (ViT-B/16) to video of wild birds at Chinese wetland and forest monitoring stations to derive first arrival dates.

title: Deep-track: A real-time animal detection and monitoring system for mitigating human-wildlife conflict in fringe areas
reason: Applies deep learning (VGG16 + Deep SORT) to detect, classify and track wild animals in camera-trap images from Serengeti National Park, aiming to reduce human-wildlife conflict.

title: Nesting dynamics of hawksbill and leatherback turtles: a four-year photo-identification study in Martinique
reason: Applies semi-automated image-based photo-identification (I3S Pattern) to photographs of wild nesting hawksbill and leatherback turtles on Martinique beaches.

title: A novel deep transfer learning model with a bidirectional quasi-recurrent neural network for underwater object classification from aquarium images
reason: All analysed images come from two aquariums (Henry Doorly Zoo and National Aquarium); no wild animals.

title: WildlifeRailGuard: A novel conservation technology to mitigate train-animal collisions in forest regions
venue: Journal of Rail Transport Planning & Management
reason: Deep learning (YOLOv8) detection of wild elephants in images to prevent train-elephant collisions in forest regions.

title: Using drone-based infrared thermography for monitoring vital signs in dolphins
reason: Drone thermal imaging was applied only to bottlenose dolphins under human care in Sea World pools; no wild or free-ranging animals were imaged.

title: HySaM: An improved hybrid SAM and Mask R-CNN for underwater instance segmentation
venue: Journal of Visual Communication and Image Representation
reason: Proposes an instance segmentation method and dataset for marine life (fish, sea turtles, seahorses, etc.) in real underwater environments, using ROV footage and web videos.

title: FishDetectLLM: Multimodal instruction tuning with large language models for fish detection
reason: Proposes a multimodal LLM for fish detection and taxonomic classification on FishNet and DeepFish images of aquatic species, framed around biodiversity monitoring. The paper does not say whether the fish are wild or captive.

title: SFUDNet: Underwater object detection via spatial-frequency domain modulation with mixture of experts
reason: Proposes a CNN-based underwater object detector evaluated on underwater datasets in which every class is a marine animal (echinus, holothurian, starfish, scallop, fish, crab, jellyfish, shrimp). The paper does not say the animals are captive or farmed.

title: CIDNet: Cross-Scale Interference Mining Detection Network for underwater object detection
reason: Proposes a CNN detection network for underwater object detection, evaluated mainly on the DUO dataset of marine organisms (holothurians, echinus, starfish, scallops) in real underwater scenes. The paper does not explicitly say the animals are wild; this is inferred from the scenes.

title: An approach of transfer learning and feature concatenation for classification of camouflage images
reason: Proposes a CNN feature-fusion method that classifies camouflaged animals by species. It uses COD10K, made of web photographs of animals, and ERVA 1.0, made of butterfly images taken in natural environments.

title: Interannual health status stability of the reef-building coral Montastraea cavernosa in a Southwestern Atlantic marginal reef
reason: Ecological monitoring of wild coral colonies; photographs were quantified manually in ImageJ and CPCE point counts. No computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Rapid surveying of benthopelagic ecosystems with a towed mini-ROV
reason: Presents a towed mini-ROV survey method; sea cucumbers in video were identified by manual viewing, with no computer vision or automated image analysis applied.

title: Enhanced hermit crabs detection using super-resolution reconstruction and improved YOLOv8 on UAV-captured imagery
reason: Deep learning detection of wild hermit crabs in UAV imagery from a field survey at Lake Hamana, Japan.

title: Assessing and modeling the dynamics and persistence of mussels in rocky-shore microhabitats
reason: Drone RGB orthomosaics of natural rocky shores are analysed with a pixel-based index and threshold classification to map where wild mussels (Mytilus galloprovincialis) occur and how this changes over time.

title: A novel underwater Holothurians monitoring system using consumer-grade amphibious UAV with Mamba-based Super-Resolution Reconstruction and enhanced YOLOv10
reason: Instance segmentation and mapping of wild sea cucumbers on a natural reef in Koh Tao, Thailand, using underwater video taken from an amphibious drone.

title: Urchinbot: An open-source model for the rapid detection and classification of habitat-modifying sea urchin species
reason: Develops and applies a YOLOv5 object detection model to underwater imagery of wild sea urchins on temperate reefs in New Zealand and Australia.

title: Artificial intelligence as a tool for bionomic transects: the case of Isidella elongata (Esper, 1788) forests in the Western Mediterranean
reason: Applies YOLOv8 detection to towed-vehicle video of wild deep-sea bamboo coral colonies (Isidella elongata) in the Western Mediterranean to count them and estimate density.

title: High-resolution mapping of shark movements from drone footage at Queensland beaches improves risk assessment for beach safety
reason: Drone footage of wild sharks was reviewed by hand in a media player. Shark tracks come from drone telemetry files. No computer vision or automated image analysis is used.

title: Interconnected robotic platforms inform deep-sea ecological restoration trends
reason: Applies CNN detectors (YOLOv5, YOLOv8) to AUV, ROV and benthic-lander images of wild deep-sea fauna (Norway lobster, burrows, fish) in Mediterranean MPAs.

title: Multi-label classification for multi-temporal, multi-spatial coral reef condition monitoring using vision foundation model with adapter learning
reason: Primary study applying a vision foundation model to underwater field images of wild coral reefs (corals are animals) to classify reef condition and stressors.

title: Linking fish activity and turbidity through visual and sensor data fusion and deep learning
reason: Applies zero-shot deep learning fish detection and CNN turbidity estimation to underwater camera images of free-ranging fish at a port.

title: Multi-scale approach for coral condition assessment and Drupella sp. identification using a versatile low-cost camera system and point cloud semantic segmentation
reason: Field underwater imaging of natural coral reefs in Koh Tao; 3D reconstruction and point-cloud semantic segmentation of wild Drupella snails and compromised corals.

title: Using Mask R-CNN and distance transform to detect elephants on railway tracks for collision prevention
reason: Applies Mask R-CNN segmentation and distance transform to images of wild elephants on or near railway tracks to prevent train collisions.

title: Advancing marine mammal monitoring: Large-scale UAV delphinidae datasets and robust motion tracking for group size estimation
reason: Detection, tracking and group counting of free-ranging dolphins in aerial UAV video using YOLO11 and BoT-SORT.

title: Enhancing generalization in camera trap image recognition: Fine-tuning visual language models
reason: Proposes fine-tuning of vision-language models (Eco-CLIP, Eco-SigLIP) for species recognition in camera trap images of wild animals; additional generic benchmarks include domestic pets.

title: Improving consistency of marine mammals tracking in challenging drone recordings through visual particle filter integration
reason: Proposes a tracking method (SORT-PF) and a new dataset for wild harbour porpoises recorded by drones in Danish coastal waters.

title: Exploiting module evolution correlation relationship for fine-grained bird image classification with structural functional representation
reason: Proposes a CNN-Mamba method for fine-grained classification of bird species, evaluated on wild bird image datasets (CUB-200-2011, NABirds). The paper frames its motivation around ornithology and conservation. It also runs extension experiments on Stanford Dogs (domestic) and Stanford Cars.

title: A new dataset, model, and benchmark for lightweight and real-time underwater object detection
reason: Proposes a new underwater object detector and dataset for detecting marine organisms (starfish, sea urchins, sea cucumbers, scallops) in real underwater environments, framed around marine ecological monitoring.

title: End-to-end transformer-based detection with density-guided query selection for small objects
reason: Generic small-object detection transformer evaluated on VisDrone (vehicles, pedestrians) and MS-COCO; wildlife is not the subject or application.

title: Underwater complex environment domain adaptation for few-shot object detection based on transfer learning
reason: Proposes a cross-domain few-shot object detection method for marine organisms (echinus, holothurian, scallops, starfish, crown-of-thorns starfish) in underwater images. Most data come from field scenes (harbor, brackish water, reef); the Aquarium dataset shows captive animals.

title: AnimalRTPose: Faster cross-species real-time animal pose estimation
reason: Proposes a real-time cross-species animal pose estimation model evaluated on wild-animal datasets (AP10K, APT36K, Animal Kingdom, ATRW, LoTE Wild) plus laboratory datasets, with wildlife monitoring as a stated application.

title: Deep learning approaches for robust mosquito classification from body and wing images
reason: Mosquito specimens (field-collected and laboratory colonies) photographed under stereomicroscopes in a controlled laboratory setting; microscopy-based specimen classification rather than free-ranging animals in the field.

title: A rapid bycatch assessment framework for small-scale fisheries: A case study on horseshoe crab (Tachypleus tridentatus) bycatch
reason: Computer vision is only used to detect fishing vessels in satellite images, plus spectral-index mapping of tidal flats. The horseshoe crab bycatch data come from questionnaires and field counts, not image analysis.

title: Cross-species pose estimation via ultra-low compression ratio array-light-based single-pixel imaging
reason: Pose estimation from single-pixel imaging tested on laboratory mice and flies in experimental set-ups plus humans; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Fast and robust multi-object plankton imaging using multi-autofocusing off-axis digital holography
reason: Digital holography reconstruction of cultured plankton imaged in a laboratory glass aquarium set-up; no open-water or wild free-ranging data.

title: Visible-NIR hyperspectral imaging based on characteristic spectral distillation used for species identification of similar crickets
reason: Crickets were collected in the field but imaged as dried, pinned specimens under a laboratory hyperspectral setup. The criterion lists museum specimens under E-CAPTIVE, and no live free-ranging animals were imaged.

title: Jellyfish detection algorithm of underwater image based on TBFRNet and reinforcement learning
reason: Proposes a deep learning detector for 12 jellyfish species in underwater ocean images, including field-collected images of free-ranging jellyfish.

title: Advanced light attenuation compensation-driven stable training generative model for marine organism image style transfer
reason: Proposes a generative (image synthesis / style transfer) model trained on web-collected underwater images of wild marine organisms (sea anemones, sea turtles).

title: EAMSF-DETR: Edge-aware multi-scale feature fusion network based on DETR for underwater object detection
reason: Proposes a DETR-based detector for underwater images of marine organisms (echinus, holothurian, scallop, starfish, fish, etc.) from real underwater scenes, with ocean ecosystem surveillance as the stated application.

title: Geometric self-supervision for monocular 3D animal pose estimation
reason: Method paper on unsupervised monocular 3D animal pose estimation (2D-to-3D lifting), evaluated on synthetic SMAL feline poses and the real multi-camera AcinoSet video dataset. The paper does not say whether the AcinoSet animals are wild or captive; its stated motivation is observing animals in the wild.

title: FN-NET: Adaptive data augmentation network for fine-grained visual categorization
reason: Generic fine-grained visual categorization data augmentation method evaluated on CUB, Aircraft and Stanford Cars benchmarks; wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: AquaSlot-SAM: Coupling slot-based state space models with SAM for robust underwater video multi-object segmentation
reason: Proposes a video segmentation method (AquaSlot-SAM) evaluated on underwater videos of wild fish from field-deployed cameras (DeepFish, Seagrass, Fish4Knowledge).

title: Bi-focus cosine complement network for few-shot fine-grained image classification
reason: Generic few-shot fine-grained classification method evaluated on CUB, Stanford Dogs and Stanford Cars benchmarks; wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Evaluation of unsupervised learning algorithms for the classification of behavior from pose estimation data
reason: Compares unsupervised behaviour-classification tools on pose-estimation data from laboratory mice in an open-field arena; no wild animals.

title: Short- and long-term captivity impacts on bird memory, corticosterone level, and oxidative stress genes: Perspectives on deep learning analysis
reason: Wild-caught birds were housed in a university research laboratory, and all analysed videos were recorded in an experimental cage. No free-ranging animals appear in the image data.

title: Training-free fish species population monitoring in unconstrained underwater videos
reason: Training-free CV pipeline for detecting, classifying and counting (MaxN) wild fish in BRUV underwater videos from the Tyrrhenian Sea.

title: CoralClassify: Advancing Coral Health Monitoring using Deep Learning
reason: Deep learning image classification of healthy vs bleached corals (wild reef animals) from underwater images.

title: Venomify: Automated Classification of Venomous and Non-Venomous Snake Species Using Deep Learning
reason: Deep learning classification of web-collected images of snakes (non-domestic wildlife) into venomous vs non-venomous for public safety and wildlife management; primary research. Capture context of the animals is not reported.

title: Comparison of Deep Learning and Object-Based Image Classification Methods: Identification of Horses from RGB Imagery
reason: Applies object-based and deep learning classification to UAV RGB imagery to identify free-ranging horses in a nature reserve.

title: Deep learning-based detection and tracking of fin whales using high-resolution space-borne remote sensing data
venue: Remote Sensing Applications Society and Environment
reason: Deep learning segmentation, detection, classification and tracking of wild fin whales in satellite, aerial and thermal imagery.

title: Discrimination of the intertidal goose barnacle Pollicipes pollicipes from rocky shore invertebrates and macroalgae using in situ hyperspectral signatures
venue: Remote Sensing Applications Society and Environment
reason: Wild intertidal invertebrates are classified from point reflectance spectra recorded with a handheld spectroradiometer. These are not images or video, so there is no image analysis.

title: Advancing underwater binary image segmentation with PDBU-Net: A progressive approach to feature extraction and accuracy improvement
reason: Generic underwater foreground/background binary segmentation of objects (divers, wrecks, ruins, marine animals); marine animals are only one of several object types in the data, and wildlife is not the stated subject.

title: A multi-scale gated attention and wavelet transform-based lightweight network for efficient plankton classification
reason: Proposes a lightweight CNN for classifying images of marine plankton captured by in situ / field imaging systems (ISIIS in the Florida Straits, ZooScan in the Ligurian Sea).

title: Unlocking flow–habitat relationships in mountain rivers of Epirus, Greece using object detection and hydrodynamic simulation
venue: The Science of The Total Environment
reason: Applies Faster R-CNN and YOLOv8 to detect wild trout in underwater video from a natural river, combined with habitat modelling.

title: Photo-id as an alternative to monitor marine turtles in the Gulf of Venezuela
reason: Applies computer-aided photo-matching (I3S Pattern, NPM/SIFT) to photos of wild marine turtles captured and released, to re-identify individuals.

title: MAGNET: Multi-level feature guidance network for few-shot fine-grained image classification
reason: Generic few-shot fine-grained classification method evaluated on general benchmarks (CUB birds, Stanford Dogs, Stanford Cars); wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: ANTi-JAM solutions for smart roads: Ant-inspired traffic flow rules under CAVs environment
reason: Applies YOLOv4-Tiny detection and Kalman tracking to videos of free-ranging ants on a natural outdoor trail in Italy to estimate traffic flow variables.

title: A high-throughput phenome-based analysis of morphological variation and environmental adaptation in extremely high-altitude schizothoracine fishes
reason: Applies YOLOv8 keypoint detection to images of wild schizothoracine fishes sampled from rivers and lakes on the Tibetan Plateau, to obtain phenotypes and study environmental adaptation.

title: Weakly supervised bird-flock counting in wetlands based on multimodal optical image perception
reason: Proposes a weakly supervised CLIP-based method for counting wild wetland bird flocks in images from the Yellow River Delta Nature Reserve.

title: Can artificial intelligence support Bactrian camel conservation? Testing machine learning on aerial imagery in Mongolia’s Gobi Desert
reason: Applies YOLOv8 object detection to drone imagery of free-ranging Bactrian camels (wild and domestic populations, not distinguished) in the Gobi Desert for conservation monitoring.

title: Impacts of the 2023 Marine Heatwave in the Florida Keys: Detection and Analysis of a Mass Coral Bleaching Event Using Spaceborne Remote Sensing Imagery
reason: Applies image analysis (satellite multispectral reflectance change detection, unsupervised classification) to detect bleaching of wild corals on reefs in the Florida Keys.

title: Digital flocks, predators allow ecologists to simulate real-world animal behaviour
reason: Nature news feature about digital twins in ecology, not primary research. It contains no computer vision analysis of animal images; the digital twins described use tracking and sighting data.

title: In situ light-field imaging of octopus locomotion reveals simplified control
reason: Light-field imaging from an ROV with markerless point tracking and 3D depth reconstruction of free-living deep-sea octopuses in situ.

title: Deep Imputation for Skeleton data (DISK) for behavioral science
reason: Imputation of skeleton keypoint data from laboratory recordings of mice, rats, tethered flies and tank-kept zebrafish, plus human motion capture; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Skeletal trait measurements for thousands of bird species
reason: Computer vision is applied to photographs of museum skeletal specimens, not to living wild animals. Museum specimens fall under E-CAPTIVE.

title: Pomerania Fish: A dataset for fishes across Pomerania freshwater waterbodies in-situ environments.
reason: Dataset paper presenting in-situ underwater video frames of wild freshwater fish in Pomeranian rivers, with bounding box and segmentation annotations and baseline detection/segmentation models.

title: Snake-DETR: a lightweight and efficient model for fine-grained snake detection in complex natural environments
reason: Proposes a detection model (Snake-DETR) and evaluates it on images of 27 wild snake species taken from the SnakeCLEF 2021 image library; wildlife monitoring is the stated application.

title: A novel target-oriented enhanced infrared camera trap data screening method
reason: Proposes a preprocessing plus YOLO detection method for infrared camera trap images of wild animals in natural reserves.

title: Improving Hokkai shrimp tracking accuracy using YOLOv8 with reflection and parallax correction
reason: YOLOv8 tracking of a single Hokkai shrimp in a controlled aquarium tank; no free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Stratification of insect diversity and daily activity patterns in the West African virgin forest Taï assessed by entomological Lidar
reason: Wild insects are monitored with an entomological Lidar, but the analysis clusters 1-D backscatter time series and their modulation power spectra. No computer vision is applied to image or video data of the animals; the drone images were used only to render the forest site.

title: Enhancing occluded and standard bird object recognition using fuzzy-based ensembled computer vision approach with convolutional neural network
reason: Primary study proposing a fuzzy-based CNN ensemble for bird species classification on bird image datasets, with biodiversity monitoring as the stated application. The paper does not explicitly state that the photographed birds are wild; this is inferred from its framing of birds in their native habitat.

title: Benthic communities on restored coral reefs confer equivalent aesthetic value to healthy reefs
reason: Applies a CNN (ResNet) to field photographs of wild coral reef benthic communities to predict aesthetic value on restored, healthy and degraded reefs.

title: Application of wings interferential patterns (WIPs) and deep learning (DL) to classify some Culex. spp (Culicidae) of medical or veterinary importance
reason: Images are of dissected wings from reference collection specimens (ARIM collection) mounted on glass slides and imaged in the lab; no free-ranging animals are imaged.
