title: Automated tick classification using deep learning and its associated challenges in citizen science
reason: Deep learning classification of images of wild tick species (non-domestic arthropods) submitted by citizens in Sweden and from GBIF, plus lab photos of frozen specimens; primary research.

title: DMM-YOLO: A high efficiency soil fauna detection model based on an adaptive dynamic shuffle mechanism
reason: Soil fauna detection on images acquired through laboratory microscopy of samples; no field imagery of free-ranging animals.

title: Automated underwater image analysis reveals sediment patterns and megafauna distribution in the tropical Atlantic
reason: Primary study applying CNN-based detection and clustering to seafloor images of wild deep-sea benthic megafauna and their traces (Lebensspuren) in the tropical North Atlantic.

title: Fine-scale spatial organisation of deep-sea sea pens in a NE atlantic submarine canyon conservation area
reason: Applies image-based 3D photogrammetry (Structure-from-Motion) and image annotation to ROV seabed imagery of wild deep-sea sea pens and co-occurring fauna in order to analyse their spatial patterns.

title: Lightweight underwater object detection method based on multi-scale edge information selection
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for underwater marine organisms (holothurian, echinus, starfish, scallop) in seabed images. The Aquarium dataset adds aquarium animals, so the subjects are mixed.

title: Increasing canopy cover elevates vehicle collision risk for barbastelle bats (Barbastella barbastellus) at roads
reason: Applies video-based automated 3-D tracking to near-infrared footage of wild barbastelle bats flying over roads.

title: SCSFish2025: a large dataset from South China sea for coral reef fish identification
reason: Introduces a bounding-box dataset of wild coral reef fish from in-situ underwater video at Subi Reef and benchmarks four object detection models on it.

title: A deep learning framework for bone fragment classification in owl pellets using YOLOv12
reason: Applies YOLOv12 object detection to images of rodent bones from barn owl pellets, which are direct signs of free-ranging predators and prey, to estimate wild rodent abundance non-invasively.

title: Successes and limitations of pretrained YOLO detectors applied to unseen time-lapse images for automated pollinator monitoring
reason: Evaluates pretrained YOLO detectors on field time-lapse images of free-ranging flower-visiting arthropods (pollinators) captured in urban green spaces.

title: Environmental and biological drivers of movement activity in Callimico goeldii under zoo conditions
reason: Automatic video analysis of motor activity of a single family group of Callimico goeldii in an indoor zoo enclosure; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Rapid consistent reef surveys with DeepReefMap
reason: Semantic segmentation and 3D mapping of underwater video transects of wild coral reefs (corals and other benthic invertebrates) in the Red Sea; primary research.

title: A multi-objective hybrid algorithm for optimizing neural network architectures in wildlife conservation: a theoretical framework with practical validation
reason: Proposes a neural architecture search algorithm for species identification and evaluates it on public camera-trap datasets of wild animals.

title: Gorilla knuckle-walking mechanics suggest independent evolution in African great apes
reason: Biomechanics study of zoo-housed gorillas using force plates; video used only for manual gait digitizing. All animals are captive.

title: Adaptive identity-regularized generative adversarial networks with species-specific loss functions for enhanced fish classification and segmentation through data augmentation
reason: Main data is a public Kaggle dataset of supermarket fish. The paper also runs a pilot on wild mammals from camera-trap datasets, so part of the analysed data shows free-ranging animals.

title: A bird target detection model designed for substation scenarios
reason: Proposes a YOLOv9-based detector for free-ranging wild birds at power substations, using images from drone cameras and web crawling.

title: Automated rhinoceros detection in satellite imagery using deep learning
reason: Applies deep learning object detection to satellite imagery of free-ranging white rhinoceroses (and elephants) in South African reserves.

title: Cyber physical solutions for aquatic monitoring using YOLO with BCP loss for intelligent underwater camouflaged object detection
reason: Proposes a modified YOLOv8 detector and loss for camouflaged fish/animal detection, evaluated on COD10K (camouflaged animals) and an underwater halibut dataset; the paper does not state whether the animals are wild or farmed.

title: Segmentation of plateau zokor mounds in alpine meadows from UAV images using an improved UNet network
reason: Deep learning segmentation of mounds (direct signs) of wild plateau zokor in UAV images of alpine meadows.

title: Lidar reveals distinct insect daily activity and diversity between habitats
reason: The study records free-flying wild insects with an entomological lidar. Its analysis works on 1-D backscatter time series and modulation power spectra, using hierarchical clustering of wingbeat signals. No images or video are analysed with computer vision.

title: Optimized YOLOv8s framework with deformable convolution for underwater object detection
reason: Proposes a YOLOv8s-based detector for fish in underwater images. The LFIW data come from ROV cameras in natural marine environments, so wild fish are analysed. The OI subset also includes aquarium and fish-market images, so the subject type is mixed.

title: Identification of Indigenous fish species in lake Tana using deep learning
reason: Deep learning (YOLO) detection/identification of indigenous wild fish species sampled from Lake Tana, Ethiopia, photographed with a fixed camera; supports biodiversity conservation.

title: A spatiotemporal transformer with cross-frame encoding and trajectory-aware decoding for multi-target fish tracking
reason: Proposes a transformer-based multi-object fish tracker. It is evaluated on fish filmed in a lab tank and on the public UOT32 underwater dataset, which the paper describes as showing real-world conditions with multiple fish species.

title: Enhancing crayfish sex identification with Kolmogorov-Arnold networks and stacked autoencoders
reason: Images of wild-caught narrow-clawed crayfish from three lakes are analysed with convolutional autoencoders plus classifiers to identify sex for population-demography purposes. This is primary computer vision research on wild animals.

title: Spectroscopic aspects of underwater digital holography of plankton
reason: A submersible digital holographic camera images free-living zooplankton in situ in Lake Baikal and the Barents Sea. The holograms are reconstructed and processed to give plankton concentration time series.

title: A small underwater object detection model with enhanced feature extraction and fusion
reason: Proposes a CNN detection model for small underwater organisms (sea urchins, sea cucumbers, scallops, starfish) evaluated on underwater image datasets described as covering scenes such as coral reefs and seagrass beds; the paper does not state whether the animals are wild or farmed.

title: A geometric morphometric approach for detecting different reproductive stages of a free-ranging killer whale Orcinus orca population
reason: Analyses drone images of free-ranging Northern Resident killer whales, using landmark-based geometric morphometrics to classify reproductive status.

title: A generative adversarial network with multiscale and attention mechanisms for underwater image enhancement
reason: Generic underwater image enhancement GAN evaluated on generic enhancement benchmarks (UIEB, EUVP, UFO-120); animals are not the stated subject of analysis.

title: Hierarchical image classification using transfer learning to improve deep learning model performance for amazon parrots
reason: Primary study applying a hierarchical YOLOv5 detection/classification model to citizen-science and web images of Amazon parrots for monitoring wild populations and trade; the paper does not state whether the photographed birds are wild or captive.

title: Polar bears and expanding sea ice in the Mid Holocene Aleutian Islands, Alaska
reason: Zooarchaeological study of bear bone specimens using morphology, caliper measurements and PCA; no computer vision or image analysis is performed.

title: A computer vision solution for behavioral recognition in red pandas
reason: The images show red pandas living in an artificial habitat at Bifengxia Wildlife World, which is a captive facility. The web-crawled images are not described as showing wild animals.

title: Spatial-frequency feature fusion network for small dataset fine-grained image classification

reason: Proposes a CNN + self-attention method that classifies images of wild corals on the Great Barrier Reef as bleached or healthy.

venue: IEEE Asia Pacific Conference on Geoscience Electronics and Remote Sensing Technology Agers
reason: Primary study proposing a CNN-RF method to classify wild-caught marine megafauna (sharks, turtles) in onboard fisheries electronic monitoring imagery.

venue: 2025 International Conference for Artificial Intelligence, Applications, Innovation and Ethics (AI2E)
reason: Object detection for roadside animal-vehicle collision avoidance, but the analysed animals are only domestic livestock (camels, cows, donkeys, horses); no wild, non-domestic animals are in the data.

reason: The images the paper describes collecting and analysing come from zoo animals (20 zoos in China). The authors mention nature reserves elsewhere, but the data-collection section names only zoos, so no free-ranging data is clearly analysed.

venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Data Sciences (AiDAS)
reason: Proposes a fuzzy inference thermal image classification pipeline for wild animal detection. title: DSAM-YOLO: Advancing UAV and Bird Detection in Airport Clearance Zones with a Dual-Stream Attention Network
venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Human-Computer Interaction and Robotics (AIHCIR)
reason: Proposes a deep-learning detector for UAVs and free-flying birds in images collected around airports; birds are one of the two detected classes and the data show wild birds.

title: Improving Object Counting Accuracy with Adaptive CNN Models and Meta-Level Routing
venue: 2025 IEEE 6th Annual World AI Iot Congress Aiiot 2025
reason: Primary study proposing a video-based CNN framework to count bats for population monitoring; the paper does not state where the bat videos were recorded or whether the bats were wild, but it analyses bat video ROIs aimed at real-world population monitoring.

title: Farm Eye Raspberry PI and YOLO Based Animal Detector
venue: Proceedings 3rd International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Applications Healthcare and Internet of Things Aimla 2025
reason: Farm intrusion detection system; the tested animals were cats, dogs and cows (domestic). No wild animals appear in the analysed data.

venue: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning Applications Theme: Healthcare and Internet of Things (AIMLA)
reason: Applies CV (FunieGAN enhancement + YOLOv8 detection/classification) to underwater images of marine species (fish, corals) from public datasets and deep-sea imaging.

reason: Applies CNN-based image detection/classification to identify wild animals (elephants, wild pigs, buffaloes) intruding into farmland for crop protection; the analysed web images mix wild species (lynx, puma, cheetah, wolf, etc.) with domestic ones (cats, hamsters, guinea pigs).

title: Real-Time Lion Detection in Forest Near Village Area Using YOLO

reason: The paper applies YOLO object detection to images of lions in forest and grassland settings. The goal is to send real-time warnings that reduce human-lion conflict near the Gir region.

reason: Proposes a CNN-based fine-grained classification method for bird species images collected from natural habitats, motivated by biodiversity monitoring.

reason: Applies a fine-tuned CNN to classify images of two wild Indian snake species, Indian Rock Python and Russell's Viper, for human safety and conservation.

title: A Lightweight CNN-Based Approach for Automated Jellyfish Species Classification Using Image Data
reason: Applies a CNN to classify images of six non-domestic jellyfish species for marine species monitoring; it is primary research. The paper does not say whether the animals were wild or captive.

title: Performance Analysis of Deep Learning and Machine Learning for Bird Species Recognition
reason: Primary study comparing deep learning and classical machine learning for image-based bird species classification, framed as biodiversity conservation; the paper does not state whether the birds in the two image datasets are wild or captive.

title: Enhancing CNN Model Re-Classification through Image Segmentation and Enhancement Technique for Bornean Orangutan Nest
reason: Primary study applying CNN classification with preprocessing to aerial images of wild Bornean orangutan nests (direct signs of wild animals).

reason: Proposes a deep learning model (ResDANet / 3D ResDANet) to identify wildlife species from images and video frames (plus audio spectrograms). The paper does not say whether the animals in its web-sourced images and videos were wild or captive, but wildlife is the stated subject.

title: Coral Reef Detection Using Deep Learning With Attenuation And Backscatter
reason: YOLO-based detection of corals (wild marine animals) in underwater images from ROVs and divers in the field, plus public coral datasets.

title: Elemantra: An End-to-End Framework Empowered with Edge AI to Tackle Human-Elephant Conflict
reason: Primary study applying a deep learning detector (YOLOv7-tiny) to infrared images of elephants to prevent human-elephant conflict involving free-ranging elephants.

title: AI-Enabled Monitoring of Migratory Birds
venue: Asian Conference on Innovation in Technology (ASIANCON)
reason: Proposes a framework that includes CNN-based species classification of migratory birds from drone and trail camera images, though most of the data is synthetic and the image data are described only vaguely.

venue: International Conference on Advancements in Smart, Secure and Intelligent Computing (ASSIC)
reason: Applies YOLO object detection to underwater reef images and video to detect crown-of-thorns starfish, which are wild marine animals.

title: InfraNet: An Ensemble Approach for Real-time Wildlife Detection using Infrared Thermal Imaging
reason: Thermal-image detection of elephants, with data from a forest range (wild) plus an elephant training center and domestic animals; proposes an ensemble detection method.

title: FD-VFSL: A Feature Fusion-Based Variational FewShot Learning Model for Cross-Domain Underwater Fish Detection
reason: Proposes a few-shot detection model for marine fish evaluated on Fish4Knowledge images of fish captured in open sea environments.

title: Automated Species Classification: A Vision Transformer Model for Biodiversity Monitoring
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Biomedical Engineering Computer and Information Technology for Health Becithcon 2025
reason: Applies a Vision Transformer to classify images of butterfly species for biodiversity monitoring, plus agricultural pests. Butterflies are wild, free-ranging animals.

title: Coral Reef Health Assessment through Deep Residual Learning: A High-Precision ResNet101 Framework for Automated Monitoring and Conservation in the Indo-Pacific Region
venue: Beyond Technology Summit on Informatics International Conference Bts I2c 2025
reason: Deep learning classification of underwater images of wild coral reefs (healthy vs. bleached corals) from Indo-Pacific monitoring sources.

reason: Primary study applying YOLO object detectors to citizen-science (iNaturalist) photographs of free-living ladybird beetles in natural settings.

reason: Thermal image classification of cats (domestic animals; stray cats/pets) under cars; no wild non-domestic animals analysed.

reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv8 detector for animal detection with wildlife monitoring as the stated application; the animal images are analysed with computer vision. The paper does not say where the images came from.

reason: Animal detection with YOLOv8 on photos the authors took in zoos and nature reserves (nature reserves imply at least some free-ranging animals), combined with COCO animal images that include domestic species.

reason: The paper trains detection and pose estimation models for laboratory mice on synthetic Blender images and tests them on laboratory mouse datasets (MARS, DeepLabCut tri-mouse). No wild animals are analysed.

venue: IEEE Annual Computing and Communication Workshop and Conference (CCWC)
reason: Deep learning CNN classification of tiger beetle (wild insect) images to genus level, including curated specimens and living beetles photographed in natural environments.

reason: Proposes a CNN-LSTM model that classifies forest wildlife video sequences into behaviour categories (avian, instinctual, danger).

title: Self-supervised Learning for Animal Species Classification in Long-Tailed Camera Trap Datasets

reason: Evaluates self-supervised and supervised vision representations for species classification of wild animals in camera trap images (iWildCam 2022).

title: Enhanced Wildlife Species Classification using YOLOv10-X for Sustainable Management Decisions

reason: Applies a YOLOv10-x object detector to classify and localise African wildlife species in images from the African Wildlife dataset for conservation monitoring.

title: Convolutional Neural Networks for Stingless Bee Species Classification in Conservation Efforts Suhita Valley
venue: International Conference on Computer System, Information Technology, and Electrical Engineering (COSITE)
reason: Classifies stingless bee species photographed at a stingless bee edutourism/bee farm site to support beekeepers managing colonies (meliponiculture), which falls under beekeeping.

reason: Applies YOLOv8/CNN to thermal and RGB camera images to detect and classify wild animals (e.g. wild boars, elephants, deer, monkeys) entering farmland near forests.

reason: Applies YOLO v11 + CNN to detect and classify animal species, aimed at wildlife monitoring. Training data include iNaturalist 2021 wildlife images, mixed with generic ImageNet and COCO animal classes.

venue: 2025 9th International Conference on Computational System and Information Technology for Sustainable Solutions Csitss 2025
reason: Applies YOLOv8 object detection to underwater images of a wild soft coral species (an animal), Pseudopterogorgia elisabethae, for conservation monitoring.

reason: Text-to-motion generation of 3D skeletal animal motion sequences extracted from a simulation game (Planet Zoo); no images or video of real animals are analysed.

reason: Generic interpretability method for fine-grained classification, evaluated on benchmarks from many domains (birds, fish, insects, dogs, pets, plants, fungi, cars, food). Wildlife is not the stated subject; animals appear only as benchmark classes.

reason: Introduces a camera trap video dataset of wild chimpanzees and evaluates behaviour recognition models on it.

title: Fish-Vista: A Multi-Purpose Dataset for Understanding & Identification of Traits from Images
venue: IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings - IEEE Computer Society Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition/Proceedings
reason: All images are of preserved fish specimens from museum collections; no wild free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Fine-Grained Few-Shot Classification with Part Matching

reason: Generic few-shot fine-grained classification method; birds (CUB) and reptiles (Reptilia) appear only as benchmark datasets alongside cars, flowers and hotel rooms. Wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: WildlifeReID-10k: Wildlife Re-Identification Dataset with 10k Individual Animals

reason: Introduces a re-identification dataset and benchmark built from 37 existing datasets; most individuals are wild animals, alongside domestic and zoo animals, and CNN/transformer baselines are evaluated on it.

title: EV-Flying: An Event-Based Dataset for In-the-Wild Recognition of Flying Objects

reason: Proposes a CNN pose estimation method for birds evaluated on the Animal Kingdom wildlife video dataset, aimed at wild bird and wetland monitoring.

reason: YOLOv8 underwater object detection is trained and evaluated on an aquarium dataset. The paper never says that any of its data shows wild, free-ranging animals.

title: Real-Time Wildlife Intrusion Detection Using YOLOv8 and OpenCV

reason: Applies YOLOv8 and OpenCV to camera video to detect and classify wild animals (wild boar, tiger, elephant, deer) intruding on farmland; primary research on human-wildlife conflict.

venue: Proceedings 2025 International Conference on Digital Image Computing Techniques and Applications Dicta 2025
reason: Generic 3D non-rigid shape registration method evaluated on rendered views of synthetic SMAL 3D animal models (lions, cows, dogs, hippos, horses); no images of wild free-ranging animals are analysed and wildlife conservation is not the stated application.

title: Optimized Detection of Crown-of-Thorns Starfish on the Great Barrier Reef Using Deep Learning Techniques
venue: IEEE International Conference on Distributed Computing, VLSI, Electrical Circuits and Robotics (DISCOVER)
reason: Applies deep learning object detection to underwater images of wild crown-of-thorns starfish on the Great Barrier Reef.

reason: Applies a CNN to classify animal footprint images (direct signs) for wildlife monitoring. The classes include wild taxa (bear, raccoon, rat) and domestic ones (dog, horse).

title: Empowering Wildlife Conservation Through Real-Time Anti-Poaching System
venue: IEEE International Conference on Distributed Computing, VLSI, Electrical Circuits and Robotics (DISCOVER)
reason: The system detects poachers, tools and human intruders for anti-poaching alerts. Animals are only one class used to avoid false alarms, so people are the subject.

title: Enhanced YOLOv8 for Real-Time Stray Animal Detection in Challenging Visibility Conditions
venue: 2025 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Deep Learning and Computer Vision (DLCV)
reason: Proposes an enhanced YOLOv8 detector evaluated on stray cat/dog images and on the African Wildlife dataset (buffalo, elephant, rhino, zebra), so part of the data shows wild animals.

reason: Proposes a YOLO-based detector for wild animals (cheetah, fox, hyena, lion, tiger, wolf) using a dataset of images taken in remote wild areas, for search-and-rescue situational awareness.

reason: Proposes an improved YOLO11 detector for marine organisms (scallops, sea cucumbers, sea urchins, starfish) in underwater natural-scene images from the DUO dataset.

venue: 2025 International Conference on Electrical, Computer and Communication Engineering (ECCE)
reason: Primary study applying a Vision Transformer to classify photographs of Bangladeshi snake species taken at various locations with natural backgrounds; the paper does not explicitly state whether the snakes were free-ranging or held (a venom research centre assisted collection).

title: Unlocking Thermal Aerial Imaging: Synthetic Enhancement of UAV Datasets
venue: 2025 European Conference on Mobile Robots Ecmr 2025 Proceedings
reason: Synthetic thermal deer are composited into real UAV thermal backgrounds and used to train a detector, with wildlife monitoring stated as the application.

reason: Proposes an optimized YOLOv7 detector for underwater images of marine organisms (sea cucumbers, starfish, scallops) from the URPC and Brackish datasets, including real-world coastal imagery.

title: Environment-Aware Dynamic Pruning for Pipelined Edge Inference

title: Research On Fish Classification And Recognition Based On Improved VGG-16 Model

reason: Images show dead seafood products (fish and shrimp) photographed at a supermarket, not wild or free-ranging animals; commercial fishery/aquaculture products.

title: Moe-Tsqformer: Dynamic Context-Aware Query Generation for Multi-Label Animal Behavior Recognition Via Mixture of Experts
venue: International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Communication (EIECC)
reason: Proposes a video transformer method for multi-label behavior recognition of in-the-wild animals, evaluated on the Animal Kingdom dataset.

title: AD-YOLO: An Animal Object Detection Algorithm in Complex Scenes Based on Improved YOLO11

reason: Proposes an improved YOLO11 detector for animals, evaluated on AP-10K mammal images with natural backgrounds such as forests, grasslands and deserts.

venue: International Conference on Electrical, Telecommunication and Computer Engineering (ELTICOM)

reason: Detection of goldfish (domestic ornamental fish) kept in a basin, with aquaculture as the stated application; no wild or free-ranging animals.

reason: The study detects domestic livestock (Katahdin sheep and Angus Cross cattle) kept in paddocks in UAV images. No wild animals are analysed.

title: A Data-Driven RetinaNet Model for Small Object Detection in Aerial Images
venue: Proceedings 2025 IEEE International Conference on Future Machine Learning and Data Science Fmlds 2025
reason: Proposes a RetinaNet-based detector (DDR-Net) and evaluates it on public aerial image datasets of wild birds.

title: Development of an Automated Monitoring System for Japanese Wild Birds Using Deep Learning
venue: IEEE Global Conference on Consumer Electronics (GCCE)
reason: Applies YOLOv5 to detect and identify wild bird species in trail camera images at bird baths in Japan.

title: A Diffusion Model-Based Computer Vision Recognition Scheme for Coral Reef Classification

reason: Proposes a Faster R-CNN ResNet50-FPN detector for wild animals intruding into human settlements, using day and night image datasets.

title: DeepMarineSegNet: A Multi-Scale Attention-Enhanced Network for Underwater Semantic Segmentation
venue: International Conference on Intelligent Systems and Embedded Design (ISED)
reason: Proposes a CNN for semantic segmentation of coral and fish in underwater marine images, with marine life monitoring as the stated application. The paper does not say explicitly where or how the Kaggle images were taken; wild subjects are inferred from its description of underwater marine scenes.

title: Plankton Types Classification in Image Using Transformer-Based Model Approaches
venue: International Seminar on Application for Technology of Information and Communication (iSemantic)
reason: Applies deep learning image classification to images of marine crustacean zooplankton (wild organisms) from the ZooScan/EcoTaxa dataset.

title: Fine-Tuned EfficientNetB0 Model for Accurate Bird Species Identification and Multi-Classification
venue: International Conference on Signal Processing, Computing and Control (ISPCC)
reason: Applies CNN transfer learning to classify images of six wild bird species gathered from web sources; wildlife monitoring is the stated application.

title: Deep Learning for Turbid Waters: A Noise-Robust Faster R-CNN with Res2Net101 and Data Augmentation
venue: IEEE International Symposium on Sustainable Energy, Signal Processing and Cyber Security (iSSSC)
reason: Proposes a deep-learning detector for underwater images of marine life (fish, stingrays, rare species) for marine biodiversity monitoring.

title: AI For Wildlife Monitoring
venue: Proceedings 2025 IEEE 3rd International Symposium on Sustainable Energy Signal Processing and Cybersecurity Isssc 2025
reason: Applies and compares deep learning detection and classification models on camera-trap and UAV images of wild animals in natural habitats.

title: InsectAgent: Improving Insect Recognition through Dynamic Information Augmentation with Multimodal Large Language Models
venue: Proceedings of IEEE Computer Society Annual Symposium on VLSI Isvlsi
reason: Insect classification method evaluated only on the IP102 agricultural insect pest dataset. The paper names agricultural pest management as an application and does not describe where the images come from or whether the insects are free-ranging.

title: Fish Image Instance Segmentation Using the Separation of the Mask Produced for Fish Size Measurement
reason: Instance segmentation of handled tilapia (Oreochromis) placed on boards, baskets, ice and grass for fishery size measurement. The paper never says the fish are wild or free-ranging. The subject is fish handled for fishery or production use, not free-ranging animals.

title: High Accuracy Individual Identification Method for Sea Turtles with Deep Learning
venue: International Technical Conference on Circuits/Systems, Computers and Communications (ITC-CSCC)
reason: Deep learning and HotSpotter are applied to images of individual sea turtles for re-identification in support of conservation. Sea turtles are a non-domestic species. The paper does not say where or how the images were collected.

title: Fish and Species Detection in Underwater Environments Using Deep Learning
venue: International Conference on Intelligent Technologies for Sustainable Electric and Communications Systems (iTech SECOM)
reason: Deep learning detection of fish in underwater imagery from public underwater fish datasets (Label Fishes in the Wild, Fish4Knowledge) for marine biodiversity monitoring.

title: Effective Marine Animal Detection and Rare Species Classification Using Autonomous Drones
venue: 2025 Second International Conference on Intelligent Technologies for Sustainable Electric and Communications Systems (iTech SECOM)
reason: Applies CNN-based image classification to web-scraped aerial images of marine animals (dolphins, seals, whales, turtles etc.) for monitoring; goldfish class is a domestic taxon, so subjects are mixed.

title: Tool-Assisted Annotation of Seafloor Sediment-Linked Features Using Weakly Supervised Semantic Segmentation
venue: International Conference on Image and Vision Computing New Zealand (IVCNZ)
reason: Weakly supervised semantic segmentation of in-situ seafloor video frames with wild benthic animals and their biogenic signs (bryozoa, worm patches, dog cockle shells).

title: Automated Activity Monitoring of Cryptic Species in a Zoo Environment
venue: International Conference Image and Vision Computing New Zealand
reason: Activity monitoring of captive Whitaker's skinks held in glass habitats at Wellington Zoo; no wild or free-ranging animals in the data.

title: Enhanced Small Object Detection Using Multi-Scale Attention for Automated Seabird Detection
venue: International Conference on Image and Vision Computing New Zealand (IVCNZ)
reason: Proposes a YOLOv8-based detector for wild seabirds in footage from cameras on commercial fishing vessels in New Zealand waters.

title: Deep Learning Based Crab Classification for Marine Pest Monitoring
venue: International Conference on Image and Vision Computing New Zealand (IVCNZ)
reason: Deep learning classification of images of wild invasive and native crabs in natural coastal and marine habitats (iNaturalist plus field-collected images).

title: IoT-Enabled Modular Bird Repellent System: A Pattern-Based Approach for Enhanced Detection and Control
reason: IoT bird repellent system with a perception module that uses CNN-based image processing and object detection to detect free-flying wild birds at airports, agricultural fields and industrial sites.

title: TransSIL: A Silhouette Cue-Aware Image Classification Framework for Bird Ecological Monitoring Systems
reason: Proposes a transformer-based fine-grained bird species classification framework for bird ecological monitoring, evaluated on bird image datasets (CUB-200-2011, NABirds); a dog-breed extension experiment adds domestic animals.

title: CoSimR: Similarity Cues-Aware Consanguinity Relationship Mining Framework for IoT-Based Bird Monitoring Systems
reason: Proposes a transformer-based fine-grained bird species classification method for IoT bird monitoring, evaluated on bird image datasets (CUB-200-2011, NABirds, iNaturalist), with an extra test on Stanford Dogs.

title: UWDET: IoT-Enabled Training Enhancement for Resource-Limited Underwater Object Detection
reason: Proposes training enhancements for underwater object detection, evaluated on underwater datasets whose classes include free-living marine animals (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish).

title: Cross-Scale Attention Feature Pyramid Network for Challenged Underwater Object Detection
reason: Proposes a CNN detection method for underwater object detection evaluated on real underwater images of marine animals (crabs, fish, starfish, etc.), including a marine species monitoring dataset.

title: HKCoral: Benchmark for Dense Coral Growth Form Segmentation in the Wild
reason: Introduces a field-captured underwater dataset of wild hard corals (animals) with dense annotations and benchmarks semantic segmentation models on it.

title: Utility-Centered Underwater Image Quality Evaluation
reason: Proposes a utility-centered image quality assessment model for underwater fish detection. Its images come from the Fish4Knowledge underwater video repository, which the paper describes as marine and seabed scenes; it does not explicitly say the fish are wild.

title: An Improved YOLOv8-Based Shallow Sea Creatures Object Detection Method
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv8 detector for shallow sea creatures (holothurians, echinus, fish, turtles, etc.) in real underwater images, with marine ecological monitoring as the stated application.

title: Joint Image Enhancement for Underwater Object Detection in Various Domains
reason: Proposes a CNN detection framework that it evaluates on underwater datasets annotated with marine organisms (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish, fish, etc.) in real underwater scenes. These are domain-specific underwater benchmarks rather than a generic vision benchmark.

title: Power- and Memory-Efficient Low-Cost IoT Sensing System for Biodiversity Surveillance Developed on Resource-Constrained Platform
reason: IoT camera system whose only image analysis evaluation is on mason bees at a beehive, i.e. managed bees (beekeeping context); main focus is power and transmission engineering.

title: MOA-YOLO: An Accurate, Real-Time, and Lightweight YOLOv10-Based Algorithm for Deep-Sea Fish Detection
reason: Proposes a YOLOv10-based detector for wild deep-sea fish in underwater survey imagery (rockfish surveys).

title: BG-UISNet: A Novel Boundary-Guided Network for Robust and Precise Underwater Image Segmentation
reason: Proposes a segmentation network for underwater images evaluated on marine animal segmentation datasets (MAS3K, RMAS) showing free-ranging marine organisms; primary method research.

title: USBTrack: Efficient Underwater Single-Branch Tracker via Template Prompt Learning
reason: Proposes a vision tracker for underwater object tracking. The stated application is following individual fish and other marine organisms in schools, using underwater video benchmarks.

title: Computer Vision Corrections Enhance UAV-Based Retrievals in Shallow Waters
venue: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing
reason: The paper corrects optical distortions in UAV video of a shallow lagoon and checks geometry with artificial reference objects. It maps habitat and substrate (coral reef, rubble, sand), and no animal taxa are the subject of the analysis.

title: Distinguishing Emperor Penguin Colonies From Space: A New Method Using the CIE Chromaticity Diagram
venue: IEEE Journal of Selected Topics in Applied Earth Observations and Remote Sensing
reason: Proposes a pixel classification method on Sentinel-2 satellite imagery to detect guano (a direct sign) of wild emperor penguin colonies in Antarctica.

title: Endangered Alert: A Field-Validated Self-Training Scheme for Detecting and Protecting Threatened Wildlife on Roads and Roadsides
reason: Self-training object detection pipeline for wild cassowaries crossing roads, field-deployed with roadside RGB and thermal cameras in Queensland.

title: Point Cloud-Based 3-D Tracking for Asynchronous and Uncalibrated Multicamera Systems
reason: The experiments track a UAV and a vehicle with multiple cameras. Wildlife appears only as a possible application in the introduction, and no animal images are analysed.

title: Token Aggregation and Selection Hashing for Efficient Underwater Image Retrieval
reason: Proposes a deep hashing method for retrieving underwater images of fish and marine species, evaluated on underwater animal datasets (WildFish, Sea Animals).

title: A NeRF 3D Based Fish Weighing Model Under Fluctuating Measuring Condition
reason: Fish weighing from 3D NeRF reconstruction of individual dead/caught fish placed on an electronic scale in a controlled set-up; no free-ranging wild animals are imaged.

title: Generative One-shot Camouflage Instance Segmentation
venue: International Conference on Multimedia Analysis and Pattern Recognition (MAPR)
reason: Generic one-shot camouflage instance segmentation method evaluated on the CAMO-FS benchmark. Animals such as octopus and shrimp appear only as benchmark classes. Wildlife is mentioned only as one possible application, and the authors plan to generalise to the general domain.

title: Few-Shot Instance Segmentation: An Exploration in the Frequency Domain for Camouflage Instances
venue: International Conference on Multimedia Analysis and Pattern Recognition (MAPR)
reason: Generic few-shot camouflage instance segmentation method tested on the CAMO-FS benchmark. The stated applications are search and rescue and military surveillance, not wildlife, and the paper never says whether the animals in the images are wild.

title: Deep Learning-Based Coral Reef Segmentation: A Satellite Imagery Study of the Trincomalee District
reason: Satellite-based benthic habitat mapping: reef extent is segmented from sea, seagrass and rocky areas using rugosity. No individual animals or animal signs are analysed, so this is habitat/land-cover mapping only.

title: AI-based technology to monitor behavioural responses in marine invertebrates
venue: IEEE International Workshop on Metrology for the Sea; Learning to Measure Sea Health Parameters (MetroSea)
reason: Computer vision (YOLOv11 detector + CNN classifier) applied to video of barnacles to monitor valve-opening behaviour. Part of the data comes from field trials in Genoa harbour; the rest comes from laboratory trials.

title: Vision-Language Models for Underwater Ecological Monitoring
venue: 2025 IEEE International Workshop on Metrology for the Sea Learning to Measure Sea Health Parameters Metrosea 2025 Proceedings
reason: Vision-language and segmentation system applied to underwater coral reef images (corals and Crown-of-Thorns Starfish) for ecological monitoring; primary research on wild reef organisms.

title: Underwater Inspection Platform for Vision-Based Biodiversity Identification
venue: IEEE International Workshop on Metrology for the Sea; Learning to Measure Sea Health Parameters (MetroSea)
reason: CNN detection of marine animals; dataset mixes aquarium photographs, public datasets and field images of wild coastal dolphins in the UAE.

title: Restoration and Identification of Objects in Aqua Environment using Deep Learning
reason: Deep learning pipeline for underwater image restoration and fish species detection/classification, using footage of fish recorded in coastal waters (Fish4Knowledge).

title: UWOT-Net: Underwater Object Tracking by Attention Driven Network in Unconstrained Marine Environments
reason: Proposes a transformer-based tracking method for fish and other marine animals in real-world underwater videos (BrackishMOT, UTB180, GMOT40 fish).

title: A Hybrid Deep Learning Approach with Explainable AI for Bangladeshi Birds Classification
venue: International Conference on Next-Generation Computing, IoT and Machine Learning (NCIM)
reason: Deep learning detection and classification of wild Bangladeshi bird species from eBird community images, with Grad-CAM explainability.

title: Ocean Fish Classification using pre-train CNN models and Performance Evaluation
venue: International Conference on Next-Generation Computing, IoT and Machine Learning (NCIM)
reason: Applies pre-trained CNNs to classify ocean fish species in images from the Croatian Fish Dataset of fish photographed in the ocean.

title: Underwater Object Detection Using Transfer Learning and Deep Neural Network
venue: 2025 International Conference on Networks and Cryptology Netcrypt 2025
reason: Applies transfer-learning CNNs to underwater images that contain marine species, some from field studies. The stated applications include marine biology and conservation.

title: Chimp Classification: An Deep Learning Approach to Monkey Identification
venue: 2025 IEEE North Karnataka Subsection Flagship International Conference (NKCon)
reason: Applies CNN transfer learning to classify images of ten non-domestic monkey species for wildlife monitoring and conservation; the image source is not described, so it is unclear whether the animals are wild or captive.

title: Deep Learning-Driven Butterfly Species Classification: Integrating Multisource Data, Real-Time Detection, and Interpretability for Biodiversity Conservation
venue: IEEE North Karnataka Subsection Flagship International Conference (NKCon)
reason: Applies CNN-based image classification to butterfly species (non-domestic insects) for biodiversity conservation, using images from public sources and real-time capture. The paper does not say whether the animals are wild or captive.

title: Unseen Eyes, Unheard Cries: Exposing Poaching Through Visual Intelligence
venue: IEEE North Karnataka Subsection Flagship International Conference (NKCon)
reason: Deep learning image classification of poached and non-poached wildlife (plus armed humans) in forest surveillance images from camera traps and drones.

title: Advancing Entomological Research Using Artificial Intelligence
reason: Applies a CNN (InceptionV3) to classify insect images from public datasets including iNaturalist citizen-science photos, aiming at biodiversity and ecological research as well as pest management.

title: UAV-Based Surveillance of Endangered Wildlife Using Machine Learning and Artificial Intelligence
reason: Proposes a CNN-based framework (EcoDroneNet) that classifies endangered wildlife species in UAV and open-source imagery.

title: Real-Time Detection and Tracking of Foreign Object Intrusions in Power Systems via Feature-Based Edge Intelligence
venue: IEEE Open Access Journal of Power and Energy
reason: The paper detects and tracks foreign objects near power transmission lines, such as construction vehicles, nets, films and banners. No animals are analysed.

title: Deep Learning-Driven Super-Resolution and DenseCLIP-Based Semantic Segmentation for Coral Reef Mapping
reason: Semantic segmentation of wild corals in seafloor images from a field survey in Pujada Bay, Philippines, with super-resolution preprocessing.

title: Ensemble-Based Fish Species Recognition in Challenging Underwater Environments
reason: Computer vision detection of saithe and pollock in underwater imagery. Data mix fish-farm footage, an aquarium set and a Trondheim-fjord set used to test generalisation to an unseen underwater environment, so wild fish are taken to appear alongside captive ones. The fjord set's wild status is not stated explicitly (it is described as recorded in Trondheim biological centre), so inclusion rests on that reading.

title: Real-Time Benthic Target Detection and Monitoring Using a Lightweight AUV
reason: Real-time YOLOv8 detection of red king crabs on the seafloor, using a lightweight AUV in open water off Hokkaido. The model was trained on images of wild specimens.

title: PlanktonTNet: Rethinking Plankton Classification from a Global View with Swin-Transformer
reason: Proposes a CNN + Swin-Transformer model to classify images of natural plankton (mostly zooplankton taxa) from the ZooScanNet and Kaggle plankton datasets.

title: AVESGUARD: ML POWERERD NON-INVASIVE PIGEON DETERRENT
venue: Picc 2025 5th International Conference on Power Instrumentation Control and Computing Instrumentation Control Communication and Computing Techniques for A Smarter and Energy Efficient Tomorrow
reason: Applies YOLOv8 object detection to images/video of free-ranging urban pigeons for a deterrent system; primary research on non-domestic animals.

title: AW-HRNet: A Spatially-Aware and Context-Enhanced Network for Few-Shot Animal Keypoint Detection
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Pattern Recognition, Machine Vision and Artificial Intelligence (PRMVAI)
reason: Few-shot keypoint detection evaluated only on the Animal Pose dataset of cats, dogs, cows, horses and sheep. These are all domestic animals, and there is no wild data.

title: AI & Iot Enabled Animal Collision Detection and Prevention
venue: 2025 IEEE Pune Section International Conference Punecon 2025
reason: Applies a modified YOLOv8 detector to roadside camera images to detect wild animals (elephant, tiger, deer, wild pig) and cattle crossing roads near forests to prevent collisions.

title: WildGuard: Realtime Wildlife Detection System Using Deep Learning
reason: Applies YOLOv8 to detect and classify wild animals (lion, tiger, leopard, bear) in images extracted from online videos, for preventing human-wildlife conflict.

title: An Adaptive Deep Neuro-Fuzzy Framework for Wildlife Detection Using YOLOv3 and LGXP Features
reason: Proposes a deep neuro-fuzzy CV pipeline for detecting and classifying wild animal species in video frames using the NTLNP wildlife dataset.

title: CSMRA-YOLO for Marine Species Recognition
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for marine species (fish, corals, cuttlefish, etc.) in underwater images from the RUOD dataset; the stated application is marine species detection.

title: Hybrid Vision Transformer Naive Bayes Model for Mosquito Species Recognition with Virus Colony Search Optimization
reason: Computer vision classification of images of three non-domestic mosquito vector species; the paper does not say whether specimens were wild-caught or lab-reared, and no exclusion criterion clearly applies.

title: Development of an IoT-Enabled Smart Scarecrow with Resource-Efficient Computer Vision
venue: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Quantum Photonics Artificial Intelligence and Networking Qpain 2025
reason: Applies YOLOv8s object detection to video from an ESP32-CAM scarecrow to detect free-ranging birds intruding on crop fields and trigger deterrents. Birds raiding crops are wild animals, not livestock, so E-AGRI does not apply.

title: Jellyfish Species Identification: A CNN Based Artificial Neural Network Approach
reason: Primary study applying CNN feature extractors and classifiers to underwater jellyfish images for species identification. The paper does not state whether the animals were wild or captive; included because the images are described as underwater imagery for marine monitoring.

title: ARTEMIS2 & ARTEMIS2-Mini: From Full-Scale to Distilled Real-Time Animal Behavior Recognition in a Robotic Dog
venue: 2025 5th International Conference on Robotics Automation and Artificial Intelligence Raai 2025
reason: Develops a video action recognition model evaluated on the Animal Kingdom animal behaviour benchmark, which the paper contrasts with human-activity data as wildlife, and also tests a distilled model on cats from a robotic dog. Wild and domestic animals are both analysed.

title: MambaReID: A Resource-Efficient Computer Vision Approach for Generalized Animal Re-Identification
venue: 2025 IEEE 4th International Conference on Robotics Automation Artificial Intelligence and Internet of Things Raaicon 2025
reason: Proposes Mamba-based models for animal individual re-identification on WildlifeReID-10k. The data includes wild species such as zebra, giraffe, turtle, shark and polar bear, alongside domestic cats, dogs and cattle.

title: Animal Intrusion Detection System using YOLOv11
venue: International Conference on Recent Advances in Electrical, Electronics, Ubiquitous Communication, and Computational Intelligence (RAEEUCCI)
reason: Applies YOLOv11 detection to images/video of wild crop-raiding animals (monkeys, wild pigs, squirrels) in farmland in Tamil Nadu; primary research.

title: Real-Time Wildlife Behavior Alerts with Hybrid DL Approaches
venue: International Conference on Recent Advances in Information Technology
reason: Proposes a hybrid VGG-19+Bi-GRU deep learning model for detecting and classifying wild animals and their behaviour in camera-trap and web image datasets. Some data shows domestic hoofed animals (horses, goats, sheep, cows).

title: You Sense Only Once Beneath: Ultra-Light Real-Time Underwater Object Detection
venue: IEEE International Conference on Real-time Computing and Robotics (RCAR)
reason: Proposes a lightweight CNN detector for underwater marine organisms (holothurian, echinus, starfish, scallop) on underwater image datasets URPC2020 and DUO. The paper does not say whether the animals are wild or farmed.

title: Improving the Performance of the Lightweight Detector Through Effective Collaboration with Visibility Enhancement Technique
venue: RIVF International Conference on Computing and Communication Technologies (RIVF)
reason: Proposes a CV detection network for underwater fish evaluated on published underwater fish datasets (DeepFish, OzFish) showing free-ranging fish.

title: Harm-Aware IoT-Powered Smart Digital Fencing Framework for Real-Time Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Using Solar Energy
venue: International Conference on Research Methodologies in Knowledge Management, Artificial Intelligence and Telecommunication Engineering (RMKMATE)
reason: Applies camera-based CNN detection/classification of wildlife (elephants, wild boars, etc.) intruding into farmland for a digital fencing system.

title: Automatic Classification of Camera Trap Images Using a Convolutional Neural Network
venue: IEEE International Symposium on Applied Computational Intelligence and Informatics (SACI)
reason: Primary study applying a CNN to classify camera trap images of wild birds and mammals from a habitat survey in Hungary.

title: Energy-Efficient Embedded Camera Trap with Sensor Fusion Triggering for Predator Monitoring in Grazing Areas
reason: Prototype camera trap for predator monitoring; the only images analysed show a human volunteer, detected with a YOLOv8 model pre-trained on people. No animal images are analysed.

title: Integrated Farm Security System
venue: 2025 IEEE International Students Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computer Science Sceecs 2025
reason: Applies a pre-trained CNN to detect and identify animals (elephant, deer, chimpanzee, plus cow) and humans for crop protection against wildlife intrusion; wildlife detection is the stated application. The source of the test images is not stated.

title: Collision Prevention System - Specializing in Animals Equipped with Distance Estimation
venue: 2025 IEEE International Students Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computer Science Sceecs 2025
reason: The animals analysed are only domestic classes (cat, cow, dog, goat, horse) for vehicle collision avoidance. No wild animals appear in the analysed data.

title: Deep Learning Approach for Animal Classification and Detection: Leveraging ResNeXt, MaXViT and K-D Trees for Accurate and Scalable Wildlife Monitoring
venue: 2025 12th International Conference on Software Defined Systems (SDS)
reason: Proposes a hybrid CV framework for animal classification and detection aimed at wildlife monitoring. The web image dataset mixes wild taxa (elephant, squirrel, butterfly, spider) with domestic ones.

title: End-to-End Web-GIS and Computer Vision System using UAV imagery for Avian Monitoring and Risk Assessment
venue: 2025 10th South East Europe Design Automation Computer Engineering Computer Networks and Social Media Conference Seeda Cecnsm 2025
reason: End-to-end system applying CV (detection, tracking, segmentation, VQA behaviour classification) to UAV RGB and thermal imagery of wild birds for monitoring and disease risk assessment.

title: Fish Species Classification Using Deep Learning: A Comparative Study
venue: South-East Europe Design Automation, Computer Engineering, Computer Networks and Social Media Conference (SEEDA-CECNSM)
reason: Applies and compares CNNs for fish species classification on images from aquatic settings, aimed at conservation and biodiversity monitoring; primary study.

title: Hybrid YOLOv8-ViT Framework for Real-Time Intelligent Wildlife Monitoring System with XAI Insights
venue: 2025 International Conference on Sensors and Related Networks Sennet 2025 Special Focus on Digital Healthcare 64220
reason: Proposes a YOLOv8n-ViT detector for real-time detection of wild animal species (cheetah, fox, hyena, lion, tiger, wolf) for wildlife monitoring and human-wildlife conflict mitigation. The paper does not say where the images came from or whether the animals are wild or captive.

title: AquaFeat: A Features-Based Image Enhancement Model for Underwater Object Detection
venue: SIBGRAPI Conference on Graphics, Patterns and Images (SIBGRAPI)
reason: Proposes a feature-enhancement module for detecting fish in underwater images and video, evaluated on wild fish datasets (OzFish, DeepFish, FishTrack23).

title: UOT-FRCNN: Underwater Object Tracking Using Faster R-CNN with ResNet-50 FPN on the UOT32 Dataset
reason: Applies Faster R-CNN detection and IoU-based tracking to underwater fish images and video (UOT32 fish-following subset), for marine ecology applications.

title: Underwater Turbid Image Restoration Using Diffusion Models
venue: Signal Processing and Communications Applications Conference (SIU)
reason: This is a generic underwater image restoration (dehazing) paper. Training data are tank images made turbid with river sand, plus synthetic noise. Fish appear only in a few test frames, and the paper does not say whether they are wild. Animals are not the subject of the analysis.

title: Enhancing Snake Species Identification in Sri Lanka Through Explainable Artificial Intelligence Techniques
venue: SLAAI International Conference on Artificial Intelligence (SLAAI-ICAI)
reason: CNN/VGG16 classification of six Sri Lankan wild snake species from images (mostly iNaturalist/HerpMapper), with XAI analysis.

title: FCD-YOLO: An Accurate and Efficient Method for Underwater Object Detection
venue: Conference proceedings/Conference proceedings - IEEE International Conference on Systems, Man, and Cybernetics
reason: Proposes a YOLOv8-based detector for underwater marine organisms (echinus, starfish, holothurian, scallop) in real-world marine scenes from the URPC dataset. The paper does not say whether the animals are wild or farmed.

title: An Zooplankton Image Classification Based on Transfer Learning Network
reason: Deep CNN classification of marine zooplankton images from field-collected plankton datasets (ZooScan, in situ ISIIS imaging).

title: Autonomous Intrusion Monitoring for Mountainous Terrain Using Hybrid MobileNet-SSD Algorithm
venue: International Conference on Software Systems and Information Technology Ssitcon 2025
reason: Primary study applying MobileNet-SSD to detect humans and animals in images from mountainous terrain, with wildlife monitoring as a stated application. The paper does not say whether the animals are wild, so subject_type is not_reported. Inclusion is borderline because the main focus is intrusion and border surveillance.

title: Comparative Study of Detection and Tracking Models for Automated Monitoring of Endangered Species
reason: Applies and compares YOLO object detectors on images of endangered big cats (tiger, lion, cheetah, leopard, jaguar) for wildlife conservation monitoring; source of images not specified but framed as wild animal monitoring.

title: A Comprehensive Evaluation of State-of-The-Art Deep Learning Object Detection Frameworks for Crown-of-Thorns Starfish in Coral Reef Monitoring
venue: International Symposium on Ocean Electronics Sympol
reason: Comparative evaluation of YOLO object detectors on underwater video frames of wild Crown-of-Thorns Starfish recorded on the Great Barrier Reef.

title: BioVIEW: Automatic Remote Nondestructive Platform for Biodiversity Evaluation
reason: Primary study presenting a field-deployed camera station for insect biodiversity monitoring; classifiers are trained and evaluated on field images of free-ranging olive fruit flies (a wild pest insect) captured on a plate in an olive grove.

title: An Attention-Locating Algorithm for Eliminating Background Effects in Fine-Grained Visual Classification
venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology
reason: Generic fine-grained visual classification method tested on standard FGVC benchmarks (birds, dogs, food, pests). Wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Prior-Guided Dual-Reference Contrastive Learning for Underwater Object Detection
venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology
reason: Proposes a deep learning detection method for marine creatures (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish, fish, turtle, etc.) in underwater images from RUOD and URPC2020; the stated application is exploration of marine ecological resources.

title: Adaptive Multi-Resolution Feature Fusion for Fine-Grained Visual Classification
venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology
reason: Generic fine-grained visual classification method evaluated on CUB-200-2011, FGVC-Aircraft and Stanford Cars; birds are only benchmark classes and wildlife is not the stated application.

title: Cross-Domain Animal Pose Estimation With Skeleton Anomaly-Aware Learning
venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology
reason: Cross-domain animal pose estimation method. It is evaluated on a new laboratory rat dataset and on the public TigDog and AP-10K datasets, which contain wild animal species such as tiger, zebra, moose and gorilla, so part of the data shows non-captive animals.

title: ShareCMP: Polarization-Aware RGB-P Semantic Segmentation
venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology
reason: Generic RGB-polarization semantic segmentation method for AUV perception. Animal classes (fish, starfish, shell, conch) are only object classes in a tank benchmark. The starfish are dried specimens and wildlife is not the stated subject.

title: BTG-Net++: Enhanced Bi-Directional Task-Guided Network for Few-Shot Fine-Grained Image Classification
venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology
reason: Generic few-shot fine-grained image classification method evaluated on standard benchmarks (CUB, Stanford Dogs, Stanford Cars, meta-iNat); wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Depth-Assisted Network for Indiscernible Marine Object Counting With Adaptive Motion-Differentiated Feature Encoding
venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology
reason: Proposes a CNN-based video counting method for fish schools in real underwater marine videos and introduces a new fish video dataset.

title: HPCTrans: Heterogeneous Plumage Cues-Aware Texton Correlation Representation for FBIC via Transformers
venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology
reason: Proposes a transformer method for fine-grained bird species classification, evaluated on datasets the authors describe as images of wild birds; birds and their conservation are the stated subject.

title: Computer Vision-Guided Humans and Animals Detection in Aquatic Disaster Zones
venue: IEEE Region 10 Annual International Conference Proceedings TENCON
reason: Disaster-rescue system detecting humans and unspecified animals in flood imagery; wildlife or free-ranging animals are never stated as the subject, and the focus is humanitarian life detection.

title: Autonomous and Teleoperated Technologies for Comprehensive Rainforest Biodiversity Monitoring
reason: Field report on drone-deployed canopy sensor units. Wild-animal camera-trap images from the rainforest were run through MegaDetector to detect animals, and drone thermal imagery fed a nocturnal animal count map.

title: Integrating Robotics, Remote Sensing, and Machine Learning for Scalable Biodiversity Monitoring in Tropical Rainforests
reason: Systems paper on robotic platforms and sensors for rainforest biodiversity monitoring. Camera traps captured images of animals, but no computer vision analysis of those images is described. Species identification relies on bioacoustics and eDNA.

title: Online Decoupled Distillation Based on Prototype Contrastive Learning for Lightweight Underwater Object Detection Models
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
reason: Proposes a knowledge-distillation method for detecting marine animals (sea urchins, sea cucumbers, starfish, scallops) in real underwater images.

title: Pseudo-Label Guided Object Detection in Sparsely Annotated Underwater Optical Images
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
reason: Proposes a detection method for marine benthic animals (holothurian, echinus, starfish, scallop) in underwater optical images acquired in real marine environments.

title: UMIS-YOLO: Underwater Multimodal Images Instance Segmentation With YOLO
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
reason: Proposes a CV instance segmentation method applied to underwater images of wild corals on reefs at Moorea Island and the UIIS underwater dataset (fish, corals).

title: Frequency Introduced Cascade Feature Fusion Network via Knowledge Distillation for Infrared Small Target Detection
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
reason: Proposes a deep network for detecting/segmenting wild tiny birds in thermal infrared images from substation monitoring cameras.

title: Towards Effective Rotation Generalization in UAV Object Re-Identification
venue: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security
reason: Proposes a transformer ReID method mainly for UAV person/vehicle ReID, but also tests it on animal ReID datasets (pandas, elephants, pigeons). The paper describes these as coming from wild environments, online platforms and wildlife parks, so part of the data shows wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Efficient Underwater Object Detection With Enhanced Feature Extraction and Fusion
reason: Proposes a deep learning detector for underwater objects, evaluated on datasets of free-ranging marine animals (COTS, holothurians, echinus, fish, crabs, etc.) with a stated ecological monitoring application.

title: Cascaded State Space and Contrastive Learning for Cross-Domain Few-Shot Segmentation
reason: Generic cross-domain few-shot semantic segmentation method evaluated on general benchmarks (PASCAL VOC, FSS-1000, ISIC, Chest X-ray, DeepGlobe); wildlife is not the subject or application.

title: TOPIC: A Parallel Association Paradigm for Multi-Object Tracking Under Complex Motions and Diverse Scenes
reason: Generic multi-object tracking paper whose only animal data is bee colony activity filmed at a beehive (beekeeping setting); other datasets are pedestrians/dancers/general MOT benchmarks. Wild free-ranging animals are not the stated subject.

title: Webly Supervised Fine-Grained Classification by Integrally Tackling Noises and Subtle Differences
reason: General webly supervised fine-grained classification method evaluated on generic fine-grained benchmarks (aircraft, birds, cars, iNat); birds are only benchmark classes and wildlife is not the stated application.

title: High-Resolution Underwater Creature Segmentation
reason: Introduces a high-resolution dataset and a segmentation network for marine creatures in underwater photographs, i.e. computer vision applied to free-ranging marine animals.

title: Multi-Granularity Query Network With Adaptive Category Feature Embedding for Behavior Recognition
reason: Proposes a video behavior recognition network evaluated mainly on the Animal Kingdom dataset, which covers many animal species including wild ones. Charades (human) is only used to test generalization.

title: Improved Plankton Species Classification Accuracy Using the Ensemble Learning Method
venue: International Conference on Telecommunication Systems, Services, and Applications
reason: Classification of microscope images of plankton genera (diatoms, dinoflagellates, chrysophytes) supplied by research institutions; microscopy-based set-up, not images of free-ranging animals in the field.

title: Human-Guided Image Generation for Expanding Small-Scale Training Image Datasets
venue: IEEE Transactions on Visualization and Computer Graphics
reason: Generic human-guided dataset expansion method evaluated on Oxford Pets dog/cat breeds and COCO animal classes; wildlife is only named as a motivating example, not the subject or the data.

title: Multi-Modal Smart Animal Detection System for Farm Surveillance
venue: Proceedings of 1st IEEE Uttar Pradesh Section Women in Engineering International Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computer Engineering Upwiecon 2025
reason: Farm surveillance system detecting livestock and domestic animals (cows, goats, dogs) on farms; no wild free-ranging animals analysed.

title: Automated Wildlife Detection in Protected Areas with Camera Traps and Deep Learning
venue: IEEE Ural-Siberian Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Radioelectronics and Information Technology (USBEREIT)
reason: Proposes an SSD-based detector with dual-stream attention to detect wild animals in camera trap images, trained on Wildlife Insights and tested on images from a Russian reserve.

title: Underwater Sea Cucumber Detection Using Consumer-Grade Amphibious UAV and Deep-Learning Based Computer Vision
reason: Deep-learning instance segmentation of wild sea cucumbers in underwater images from a field survey at a coral reef in Thailand.

title: Distributed AI-Based Communication Systems for Sustainable Internet of Underwater Things
reason: Underwater communication framework; the CNN classification is only run on the MNIST handwritten digit dataset as a stand-in for fish images, so no animal images are analysed.

title: Context-Aware Outlier Rejection for Robust Multi-View 3D Tracking of Similar Small Birds in An Outdoor Aviary
venue: 2025 IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
reason: All analysed footage shows house sparrows housed in an enclosed outdoor aviary. The birds were captured locally, but there are no images of free-ranging animals.

title: CATALOG: A Camera Trap Language-Guided Contrastive Learning Model
venue: Proceedings 2025 IEEE Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision Wacv 2025
reason: Proposes a foundation-model-based method for recognising animal species in camera-trap images of wildlife, evaluated on two camera-trap datasets.

title: TaxaBind: A Unified Embedding Space for Ecological Applications
venue: 2025 IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
reason: Primary method paper that trains and evaluates a multimodal embedding (including an image encoder) for species classification on iNaturalist ground-level species images and bird image datasets; wildlife/ecology is the stated application.

title: DreaMo: Articulated 3D Reconstruction from a Single Casual Video
venue: 2025 IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
reason: Computer vision method for articulated 3D reconstruction of animals from casual Internet videos (28 animal species); motivated by the difficulty of 3D scanning wildlife. The paper does not say whether the filmed animals are wild or captive.

title: Sifting Through the Haystack - Efficiently Finding Rare Animal Behaviors in Large-Scale Datasets
venue: 2025 IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
reason: The image-derived (pose) data come only from laboratory zebrafish larvae. The only wild-animal data (meerkats) are accelerometer signals, not images or video.

title: A Two-Head Loss Function for Deep Average-K Classification
venue: IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
reason: Generic loss-function paper for average-K classification evaluated on CIFAR-100 and a plant dataset (Pl@ntNet-300K); wildlife is not the subject.

title: SegBuilder: A Semi-Automatic Annotation Tool for Segmentation
venue: 2025 IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
reason: Generic semi-automatic segmentation annotation tool (SAM-based). Animal images are web-queried underwater categories plus generic benchmarks. The paper never names wildlife or conservation as its subject and never says the animals are wild.

title: UnDIVE: Generalized Underwater Video Enhancement Using Generative Priors
venue: IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
reason: Generic underwater video enhancement method evaluated on underwater video datasets (divers, scenes); animals are not the stated subject or application.

title: Evaluation of Spatio-Temporal Small Object Detection in Real-World Adverse Weather Conditions
venue: IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision Workshops (WACVW)
reason: Surveillance small-object detection of persons, vehicles, cyclists and some animals all merged into one class; wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Marine Event Vision: Harnessing Event Cameras for Robust Object Detection in Marine Scenarios
venue: IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision Workshops (WACVW)
reason: Event-camera object detection tested only on toys (toy fish, rubber duck, toy mouse), a hydrophone and a robotic arm in a laboratory water tank; no real or wild animals are imaged.

title: AutoFish: Dataset and Benchmark for Fine-Grained Analysis of Fish
venue: IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision Workshops (WACVW)
reason: Dead, commercially caught fish were imaged on a conveyor belt in a laboratory setup for catch documentation. No free-ranging animals appear in the analysed images.

title: Challenges in Underwater Video Data Processing
reason: Analyses underwater fish image/video datasets with image processing, clustering, a CNN and Grad-CAM, aimed at biodiversity monitoring. The paper never directly says the animals are wild; that is inferred from the underwater, coral reef and marine fish imagery.

title: Real-Time Wild Animal Detection using YOLOv10 Algorithm
venue: International Conference on Wireless Communications, Signal Processing and Networking (WiSPNET)
reason: Applies YOLOv10 object detection to images of wild animal species (deer, elephant, bear, fox, cheetah) for wildlife monitoring, deployed on an edge device; primary research.

title: Climate explains global functional trait variation in bees
reason: Computer vision segmentation applied only to photographs of dried, pinned museum bee specimens; no live wild animals imaged.

title: Body size, nutritional state and endocrine state are associated with calving probability in a long‐lived marine species
reason: Ecological Bayesian state-space model of health and calving in wild gray whales; drone photogrammetry estimates are taken from a previous model and photo-ID is manual, so the paper itself performs no computer vision analysis.

title: Disentangling the influence of environmental conditions on sex determination in haplodiploid organisms
reason: Field study of free-flying European orchard bees at trap nests in agricultural landscape; videos filtered with a YOLOv5 CNN to detect bees, supporting ecological analysis.

title: Towards a better understanding of avian collision in wind energy facilities using automatic detection systems
reason: Applies camera-based automatic detection systems and video analysis (BirdTracker) to detect and track wild birds flying near wind turbines.

title: Estimating abundance of aggregated populations with drones while accounting for multiple sources of errors: A case study on the mass nesting of Giant South American River Turtles
reason: Wild river turtles were surveyed with drones, but human observers counted the animals by hand in the orthomosaics. The paper's method is a statistical abundance model, not automated image analysis.

title: Wasp‐Hive Candidate Site Search System Using a Small Drone
reason: Primary study that applies deep-learning object detection to drone imagery to locate wasp hives (nests, a direct sign of wild insects). Most targets are hive models, but one actual hive is included in the forest experiment.

title: A Novel Multidisciplinary Approach for Reptile Movement and Behavior Analysis
reason: Two wild-caught reptiles were filmed, motion-captured and 3D-scanned only inside lab and semi-natural enclosures. The analysis is mainly accelerometer-based, with the image data used for manual ground-truthing, MoCap and 3D reconstruction. No free-ranging animals were imaged.

title: Predicting Social Rankings in Captive Chimpanzees ( Pan troglodytes ) Through Communicative Interactions‐Based Data‐Driven Model
reason: Video of captive zoo chimpanzees was coded manually by observers; the genetic algorithm ranks individuals from behavioural and demographic variables, so no image analysis is performed. The animals are also zoo-housed only.

title: An Automated AI Framework for Quantitative Measurement of Mammalian Behavior
reason: Deep-learning framework for behaviour recognition, pose estimation, tracking and individual identification from video of 10 mammal species; Sichuan snub-nosed monkey video was partly collected in the wild, the other species in enclosures or zoos.

title: Epidemiological Dynamics of a Visually Apparent Disease: Camera Trapping and Machine‐Learning Applied to Rumpwear in the Common Brushtail Possum
reason: Primary study that trains a CNN on camera trap images of wild common brushtail possums to classify a visually apparent disease (rumpwear) and maps its predicted distribution across Tasmania.

title: Avoiding confusion: Modelling image identification surveys with classification errors
reason: Proposes a Bayesian model for counts from an image classifier (ResNet-50) applied to images of wild zooplankton taken by the Plankton Imager on a pelagic survey.

title: AMMonitor 2: Remote monitoring of biodiversity in an adaptive framework in R
reason: Software/data-management paper describing an R package (database, Shiny GUI, labelling tools, tutorials). It does not develop, apply or evaluate any computer vision method in experiments. It only mentions that labels from external ML models such as MegaDetector can be imported.

title: YOLO-Behaviour: A simple, flexible framework to automatically quantify animal behaviours from videos
reason: Proposes a YOLOv8-based framework for detecting animal behaviour in video. Some of the data shows wild animals (house sparrows on Lundy, Siberian jays in Lapland, zebras and giraffes in Kenya). The rest shows homing pigeons and humans.

title: Counting animals in orthomosaics from aerial imagery: Challenges and future directions
reason: The article is published as a Perspective that describes error sources in orthomosaic-based wildlife counts and discusses future directions. It does contain an illustrative example on wild turtles with a prototype pixel-prioritising orthomosaic method, so inclusion is a borderline call; coded as excluded because the article type is perspective.

title: Dude, everyone wants pattern analysis tools (DEWPAT): Tools for measuring visual pattern complexity from digital images
reason: Introduces an image-analysis toolkit (DEWPAT) for measuring colour pattern complexity, demonstrated on images of non-domestic animals (longhorn beetles, Anolis lizard dewlaps). The paper does not say whether the animals were photographed in the wild.

title: Zero‐shot animal behaviour classification with vision‐language foundation models
reason: Evaluates zero-shot vision-language models for behaviour classification on camera trap images of wild alpine and African fauna.

title: A new underwater camera trap for freshwater wildlife monitoring
reason: Presents an underwater camera trap that uses frame-difference motion detection to record free-ranging newts and other freshwater animals in a pond. It also uses picture-matching software to identify individual Great Crested Newts.

title: Towards scalable insect monitoring: Ultra‐lightweight CNNs as on‐device triggers for insect camera traps
reason: Develops lightweight CNN binary classifiers to detect insects in images from citizen-science photos and field insect camera traps; primary research on wild insects.

title: Zero‐shot shark tracking and biometrics from aerial imagery
reason: Proposes a zero-shot segmentation and tracking method (FLAIR) applied to drone videos of free-ranging sharks.

title: A framework for fast, large‐scale, semi‐automatic inference of animal behaviour from monocular videos
reason: Develops a CNN-based detection, tracking and behaviour classification framework on drone videos of wild plains and Grévy's zebras in Kenya.

title: A centralised multi-unit recording system for automated, off-grid animal observation and environmental monitoring
reason: Presents a multi-unit field recording system and applies a YOLOv8 computer vision pipeline to nest-box images of wild jackdaws.

title: Essential tools but overlooked bias: Artificial intelligence and citizen science classification affect camera trap data
reason: Primary study evaluating AI (EfficientNet, DeepFaune) and citizen science classification of camera trap images of wild mammals in Doñana National Park and the effect on occupancy estimates.

title: An active ensemble classifier for detecting animal sequences from global camera trap data
reason: Primary study proposing a computer vision classifier that separates animal, human and empty sequences in camera trap images from field sites worldwide; data show wild animals together with some pets.

title: Comparative assessment of automated and manual monitoring in comprehensive plant–pollinator communities
reason: Develops and field-validates a Raspberry Pi camera system with a YOLOv5 detector for wild pollinators visiting flowers in natural plant communities on the Balearic Islands.

title: Vision transformers for age prediction from facial images in a wild primate
reason: Deep learning models are trained on facial photographs of wild, habituated mandrills taken in the forest in Gabon to predict chronological age.

title: evsBat : An automated toolkit for tracking and quantifying rapid movement of nocturnal animals using event cameras
reason: Develops an event-camera analysis pipeline for tracking bats and estimating wingbeat frequency; data include captive laboratory flights and free-flying wild bats over a natural pond.

title: Monitoring African Megafauna in an Anthropogenic Landscape: A 15‐Year Case Study of the Vulnerable West African Giraffe
reason: Primary study applying pattern-recognition software (HotSpotter) to photographs of free-ranging West African giraffe to correct individual identification before capture-mark-recapture analysis.
