title: Batmobile—Using Nocturnal Drone Imagery to Assess the Habitat Use and Population Size of a Tropical Island‐Endemic Flying‐Fox
reason: Thermal drone video of wild flying-foxes was reviewed manually by human observers; no computer vision or automated image analysis was applied.

title: S‐ACORD: Spectral Analysis of COral Reef Deformation
reason: Analyses 3D models of wild coral reefs reconstructed from underwater photogrammetry images to detect growth and decay over time.

title: Optimizing automated photo identification for population assessments
reason: Applies a CNN individual-identification algorithm (AnyDorsal) to 39 photo-ID image datasets of cetaceans to estimate misidentification rates and their effect on abundance estimates; primary research on free-ranging animals.

title: Evaluating Dogs’ Real-World Visual Environment and Attention
reason: The study analyses egocentric scene video from head-mounted eye-trackers worn by pet dogs during walks. The subjects are domestic pets, not wild animals.

title: Promoting human–elephant coexistence through integration of AI , real‐time alerts, and rapid response
reason: Field deployment of AI-embedded camera alert system detecting wild Asian elephants in West Bengal, India.

title: From Presence‐Only to Abundance Species Distribution Models Using Transfer Learning
reason: The CNN works on environmental rasters and Sentinel-2 satellite images of habitat to predict where fish occur and how abundant they are. No animals appear in the analysed images. Fish data come from GBIF occurrence records and diver counts, not from images, so image analysis covers habitat only.

title: From Data Deficient to Big Data in Shark Conservation
reason: Presents the sharkPulse platform, which uses a CNN ensemble (Shark Detector) to identify and classify images of free-ranging sharks mined from social networks and citizen-science sources, turning them into occurrence records.

title: Challenging Paradigms Around the Role of Colony Size, Taxa, and Environment on Bleaching Susceptibility
reason: Underwater photogrammetry (3D reconstruction and orthomosaics) of wild coral colonies on the Great Barrier Reef, used to measure colony size and score bleaching. This is primary research applying image-based methods to wild animals.

title: Longer Wing Bones in Warmer Climates Suggest a Role of Thermoregulation in Bird Wing Evolution
reason: Computer vision is applied to photographs of museum skeletal specimens, not to images of live wild animals. Museum specimens fall under E-CAPTIVE.

title: Enhancing fish community monitoring at a cabled observatory by combining environmental DNA and imaging analysis
reason: Fish in underwater observatory images were identified manually and compared with eDNA metabarcoding. The paper applies no automated computer vision or image analysis method.

title: A blacktip's black tip: The reliability of using dorsal‐fin patterns for photo identification of blacktip reef sharks (Carcharhinus melanopterus)
reason: Analyses photographs of wild-caught neonatal and juvenile blacktip reef sharks with image-based shape analysis (EFA, Gower distance) to test whether dorsal-fin patterns can be used for photo identification.

title: FFM ‐ ViT : an efficient fish species classification method based on deep features and transformers
reason: Proposes a hybrid CNN-ViT classifier for fish species images; the aggregated dataset includes underwater and open-water fish images alongside caught fish and fishery scenes, with biodiversity conservation as a stated application.

title: Turning trade‐offs: hummingbird power reserves are used to decrease turning radius or increase turning velocity
reason: Wild-caught hummingbirds were temporarily housed and filmed in a laboratory flight arena with an automated tracking system; there is no free-ranging imagery.

title: Rapid postfire color shift in a Mediterranean lizard
reason: Wild-caught lizards from burned and unburned field sites were photographed, and their dorsal colour was quantified by image analysis (luminance, colour bins, k-means colour segmentation). The animals are free-ranging and were released after photography.

title: Spotted correctly? Human expertise remains essential in AI ‐assisted identification of Eurasian lynx
reason: Evaluates the Whiskerbook detection and individual identification algorithms (MiewID, HotSpotter) on camera trap photos of wild Eurasian lynx from field monitoring in Croatia and Slovenia.

title: Using deep learning to distinguish cryptic traits in animal colour patterns
reason: CNN classification of field photographs of wild salamanders and painted turtles to distinguish species, populations and sexes by colour pattern.

title: Edge Device Integration to Visualize Blue Whale Tracking Using Space‐Borne Remote Sensing Data
reason: Primary study that develops deep learning detection, segmentation and classification of free-ranging whales in very-high-resolution satellite imagery.

title: ZMFISC: Zhu-Ming data set with a convolutional neural network for identifying Indo-Pacific humpback dolphins (Sousa chinensis)
reason: Primary study that builds a photo-ID dataset of wild Indo-Pacific humpback dolphins from boat surveys and proposes a CNN-based segmentation plus classification method for individual identification.

title: Evaluating the Efficacy of Drone‐Based Thermal Images for Measuring Wildlife Abundance and Physiology
reason: Primary study applying Mask R-CNN to drone RGB and thermal imagery of wild northern elephant seals hauled out at a reserve to detect, segment and count them.

title: A Practical Guide for Improving Confidence in Data Collected With Consumer‐Level Drones
reason: Methodological note on calibrating consumer drones (lens distortion, field of view, barometric altimeter) using photos of calibration objects. No images of real animals are analysed; the only whale is a rendered 3D model used to show wide-angle lens effects.

title: Semi‐Automated Detection of Right Whales ( Eubalaena spp. ) in Very High‐Resolution Satellite Imagery
reason: Primary study that builds and tests CNN classification and detection models to find free-swimming right whales and other large whales in very high-resolution satellite imagery.

title: Investigating Harvest and Vessel Traffic Exposure as Drivers of Social Group Characteristics in Canadian Beluga ( Delphinapterus leucas ) Populations
reason: Belugas in VHR satellite imagery were identified, measured and aged manually by one human observer in ArcGIS; no computer vision or automated image analysis method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Drone‐Based Photogrammetry Provides Estimates of the Energetic Cost of Migration for Humpback Whales Between Antarctica and Colombia
reason: Drone-based photogrammetric image analysis of free-ranging humpback whales to measure body condition.

title: Harbor Seals ( Phoca vitulina ) Sighted 34 Years After Their Inclusion in a Capture‐Mark‐Recapture Study
reason: Wild harbor seals were resighted by people looking through drone, DSLR and aerial survey images for freeze brands. The paper has no computer vision or automated image analysis.

title: Elevating Photo‐Identification: Aerial‐Identification Improves Re‐Sight Rates and Supports Long‐Term Monitoring of Humpback Whales
reason: Primary study that identifies individual free-ranging humpback whales from drone imagery using partially automated pattern-recognition software (I3S), compared with fluke photo-identification.

title: How Robust is Eschrichtius robustus ? A Novel Photographic Index of Body Condition From Boat‐Based Photographs of Gray Whales
reason: The study is about wild gray whales, but analysts measured the body condition angle by hand in ImageJ. No computer vision or automated image analysis is developed or applied.

title: Automated identification of spotted‐fever tick vectors using convolutional neural networks
reason: CNN classification of preserved tick specimens from scientific collections photographed under stereomicroscopes in the laboratory; not images of free-ranging animals.

title: Descriptron : Artificial intelligence for automating taxonomic species descriptions with a user‐friendly software package
reason: Software/method paper analysing images of preserved psyllid specimens (forewings) for automated taxonomic descriptions; no wild free-ranging animals imaged in the field, i.e. specimen-only data.

title: Robust Perception in Degraded Visual Environments: а Multimodal Enhancement Framework
reason: Proposes image/video enhancement methods and evaluates downstream object detection on thermal UAV imagery of wildlife (BIRDSAI), with wildlife monitoring a stated application; other datasets are non-animal.

title: Abundance and distribution of ringed and bearded seals in the Chukchi Sea: a reference for future trends
reason: Aerial thermal and colour imaging survey of wild ringed and bearded seals on Arctic sea ice, with automated thermal hot-spot detection used to detect and count seals for abundance estimation.

title: A framework for detecting and tracking elephants in drone videos
reason: Detection and tracking of wild African elephants in drone videos recorded in a South African game reserve.

title: Deep Learning-Based Automatic Identification System for Marine Plankton
venue: Admit 2024 Conference Proceedings 2024 3rd International Conference on Algorithms Data Mining and Information Technology
reason: Deep learning classification of marine plankton (including zooplankton such as copepods and rotifers) from images collected on sea sampling expeditions and from public sources.

title: Artificial Intelligence as Catalyst for Biodiversity Understanding
reason: Opinion article in Communications of the ACM discussing AI for biodiversity and taxonomy; no primary image analysis or data.

title: Reshaping Human-Animal Relationships: Exploring Lemur and Human Enrichment through Smell, Sound, and Sight
venue: CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
reason: HCI enrichment study with six zoo-housed red-ruffed lemurs. Lemurs are detected by infrared proximity sensors, and the recorded video is only checked by hand to verify triggers. No computer vision analysis is performed, and all subjects are captive.

title: GreenCrossingAI: A Camera Trap/Computer Vision Pipeline for Environmental Science Research Groups
venue: Pearc 2025 Practice and Experience in Advanced Research Computing 2025 the Power of Collaboration
reason: Primary study that implements an on-premise pipeline running MegaDetector on the authors' camera trap images of wild animals along Interstate 5 in southern Oregon.

title: ML Field Planner: Analyzing and Optimizing ML Pipelines For Field Research
reason: The authors build ML Field Planner and use it to evaluate MegaDetector detection models on camera-trap images of wild small animals from the Ohio Small Animal Survey.

title: EPIC: Efficient Pruning for Inference on Constrained Devices
reason: Image segmentation of spotted lanternflies (wild, invasive insect) in live field images, framed as an animal ecology task; primary method paper on pruning for edge deployment.

title: Rainforest-YOLO: Combining swin transformer for tropical rainforest wildlife detection
venue: Iccip 2024 2024 the 10th International Conference on Communication and Information Processing
reason: Proposes a YOLOv8-based detector evaluated on camera-trap images of wild squirrels from a tropical rainforest nature reserve.

title: Automated Pest Control: Computer Vision for Wildlife Surveillance
venue: Ciis 2024 2024 the 7th International Conference on Computational Intelligence and Intelligent Systems
reason: Primary study training CNN classifiers to identify invasive wildlife (foxes, rats, pigeons, raccoons, squirrels) with evaluation on trail-camera and surveillance images; wildlife is the stated subject.

title: Demo: InvisibleFence: Non-Lethal Edge-Optimized AI for Human Wildlife Coexistence and Crop Protection
venue: Mobisys 2025 Proceedings of the 23rd ACM International Conference on Mobile Systems Applications and Services
reason: Poster presenting an edge-AI system that detects and classifies free-ranging garden/farm wildlife (deer, raccoon, rabbit, fox, etc.) in field-collected images, together with humans and pets.

title: Bringing Edge Intelligence to Wildlife Camera Traps with Hyperdimensional Computing
venue: Mobisys 2025 Proceedings of the 23rd ACM International Conference on Mobile Systems Applications and Services
reason: Primary study applying a hyperdimensional-computing image classifier to camera trap images (Caltech Camera Traps and an own outdoor deployment) to separate animal images from empty or low-value ones.

title: Continuous Marine Monitoring via Autonomous UAV Handoff
venue: Mobisys 2025 Proceedings of the 23rd ACM International Conference on Mobile Systems Applications and Services
reason: Primary study evaluating visual trackers and a UAV handoff method on aerial footage of a wild shark in shallow coastal waters.

title: ZooplanktonBench: A Geo-Aware Zooplankton Recognition and Classification Dataset from Marine Observations
venue: Proceedings of the ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining
reason: Benchmark dataset paper applying detection and classification models to in situ images of free-living marine zooplankton from the northern Gulf of Mexico, plus benchtop videos of net-captured animals in a container.

title: What Does AI See through Animals' Eyes? Zero-Shot Activity Recognition from Bio-loggers
venue: Ubicomp Companion 2025 Companion of the 2025 ACM International Joint Conference on Pervasive and Ubiquitous Computing
reason: Proposes a zero-shot VLM-based activity recognition pipeline on egocentric video from bio-loggers mounted on wild streaked shearwaters; primary research on wild animals.

title: Descriptive Analysis of Online Wildlife Products Using Vision Language Models
venue: ACM SIGCAS/SIGCHI Conference on Computing and Sustainable Societies (COMPASS)
reason: Images are online advertisement photos of wildlife products (skins, fibres, bones, teeth, taxidermy, a few live animals for sale). None show wild, free-ranging animals or their direct field signs. The data are specimens and products, which falls under the specimen part of E-CAPTIVE.

title: Animal Species Classification using Convolutional Neural Network
venue: International Conference on Software Engineering and Information Management (ICSIM)
reason: Applies a CNN (MobileNet) to classify images of 15 animal classes from a Kaggle dataset. The classes include wild animals (tigers, elephants) alongside domestic ones (cats, cows), and the stated application is wildlife monitoring and conservation.

title: Identification of first-level national protected animals based on YOLOv5 and YOLOv8 algorithms
venue: Icea 2024 International Conference on Intelligent Computing and Its Emerging Applications
reason: Applies YOLOv5/YOLOv8 detection to images of 17 endangered wild animal species; images are web-crawled with a small number of zoo photos, so wild and captive animals are mixed.

title: iMagine: AI-Powered Image Data Analysis in Aquatic Science
venue: Platform for Advanced Scientific Computing Conference (PASC)
reason: Overview of an AI infrastructure platform and its best practices for aquatic image analysis. It reports no experiments or results on wild animal images. The one detailed case study is phytoplankton classification on FlowCam instrument images.

title: TT-DSC: Enhancing YOLO for Marine Ecosystem through Efficient Tensor Train-based Depthwise Separable Deep Neural Network
venue: ACM Transactions on Autonomous and Adaptive Systems
reason: Model compression method (TT-based depthwise separable convolution) for YOLO, with marine ecosystem conservation as the stated application, evaluated on the FISHINV fish and invertebrate detection dataset as well as generic benchmarks.

title: Wildlife Detection using Motion History Information Captured by Camera Trap in the Dark
reason: Primary study proposing an optical-flow-based CNN classification method for nocturnal infrared camera trap images of wildlife captured in mountainous areas.

title: Thermal-to-RGB Video Translation for Wildlife Monitoring: Enhancing Low-Resolution Thermal Imagery with Large Diffusion Models
venue: Hotsense 2025 Proceedings of the 2025 ACM International Workshop on Thermal Sensing and Computing
reason: Primary study proposing a thermal-to-RGB video generation pipeline for wildlife monitoring. It is evaluated on thermal video of free-ranging animals (UAV footage over national parks, New Zealand wildlife) together with sanctuary cheetahs and a rodent dataset.

title: APGNet: Adaptive Prior-Guided for Underwater Camouflaged Object Detection
venue: Proceedings of the 7th ACM International Conference on Multimedia in Asia Mmasia 2025
reason: Proposes a segmentation network for camouflaged marine animals in underwater images, evaluated on two marine animal segmentation datasets. The paper does not explicitly state the animals are wild; this is taken from its framing of marine organisms in underwater environments.

title: FSCDiff: Frequency-Spatial Entangled Conditional Diffusion model for Underwater Salient Object Detection
venue: ACM International Conference on Multimedia (ACM MM)
reason: Generic underwater salient object detection method evaluated on USOD benchmarks. The salient objects include divers and trucks as well as animals, and wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Fine-grained Zero-Shot Object Detection
venue: ACM International Conference on Multimedia (ACM MM)
reason: Proposes a fine-grained zero-shot object detection method and builds a wild-bird detection dataset (web and camera images), with conservation of endangered birds as the stated application.

title: MSC: A Marine Wildlife Dataset for Video Understanding with Grounded Segmentation and Clip-Level Captions
venue: Mm 2025 Proceedings of the 33rd ACM International Conference on Multimedia Co Located with mm 2025
reason: Introduces a marine wildlife video dataset recorded during diving expeditions with segmentation masks and captions, and benchmarks captioning, visual grounding and video generation models on it.

title: MetaWild: A Multimodal Dataset for Animal Re-Identification with Environmental Metadata
venue: Mm 2025 Proceedings of the 33rd ACM International Conference on Multimedia Co Located with mm 2025
reason: Primary study presenting a camera-trap re-identification dataset of wild animals in New Zealand and an adapter module evaluated on it.

title: MCOD: The First Challenging Benchmark for Multispectral Camouflaged Object Detection
venue: ACM International Conference on Multimedia (ACM MM)
reason: Generic multispectral camouflaged object detection benchmark; the paper never says the camouflaged objects are animals, and wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: AI-Enabled Smart Camera Traps for Wildlife Monitoring in African Ecosystems
reason: Applies YOLO detectors to images of African wildlife species and free-ranging invasive green iguanas for a smart camera trap; the prototype was also field-tested at a safari park.

title: PAD3R: Pose-Aware Dynamic 3D Reconstruction from Casual Videos
venue: Proceedings SIGGRAPH Asia 2025 Conference Papers SA 2025
reason: Category-agnostic dynamic 3D reconstruction method for articulated objects (people or animals) aimed at gaming, film and AR/VR. It is evaluated on synthetic animal renderings and generic video datasets, and wildlife is not the stated subject.

title: Quantification of Crown-of-Thorns Starfish in Visual Data Using YOLOv11 for Coral Reef Outbreak Monitoring
venue: International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Metaheuristics & Swarm Intelligence (ISMSI)
reason: Applies YOLOv11 to detect and count wild crown-of-thorns starfish in underwater coral reef images.

title: Real-Time Aerial Object Detection via YOLOv11 with Coordinate Attention Enhancement
reason: Generic aerial object detection (drones, birds, airplanes) aimed mainly at surveillance and airspace management. Birds are just one of three classes, wildlife is not the stated subject, and the paper does not describe where the images come from.

title: Ape Jam: Exploring Cognitive Enrichment
reason: Workshop proposal on digital/touchscreen cognitive enrichment for zoo-housed apes; no image or video analysis is performed and no primary CV research is reported.

title: Swing it On: Design of Responsive Acoustic Environments for Zoo-housed Colobus Monkeys
reason: Design and proposed evaluation protocol of an IMU-sensor-based interactive acoustic swing for zoo-housed colobus monkeys; no computer vision or image analysis is performed (and animals are zoo-housed only).

title: Exploring the Cockatoo's Engagement with Audiovisual Stimuli: An Inclusive Avian-IoT Interaction Design
reason: Pilot study of an IoT interaction system with a single captive salmon-crested cockatoo in Kyoto City Zoo; camera-based motion detection used only on a zoo animal.

title: A Computer Vision Pipeline to Augment Touchscreen Tasks for Chimpanzees
venue: ACI 2025 Proceedings of the ACM 12th International Conference on Animal Computer Interaction
reason: Facial detection and individual identification of chimpanzees housed at the Indianapolis Zoo; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Keeping it Trunky: Engineering Improvements for Enabling Long Term Interactive Enrichment for Elephants
venue: ACI 2025 Proceedings of the ACM 12th International Conference on Animal Computer Interaction
reason: Computer vision trunk detection on African elephants housed at Zoo Atlanta only; no wild or free-ranging animals in the data.

title: Edge-Native, Behavior-Adaptive Drone System for Wildlife Monitoring
reason: Computer vision (detection and behaviour classification) on drone video of zebras, giraffes and horses; includes free-ranging animals in Kenya together with animals at a managed conservation centre (The Wilds, USA).

title: Poster: An Edge-Native Approach to Behavior-Adaptive Navigation in Drone Systems
reason: Edge-native drone system using YOLO detection and behavior recognition on video of zebras at conservation parks; poster with real-world deployments.

title: Poster: An Edge-to-Cloud Framework for Vigilance-Adaptive Drones
reason: Poster that correlates drone telemetry with existing behaviour annotations from the KABR dataset and proposes a conceptual edge-to-cloud framework; no computer vision method is developed or applied to images.

title: Incorporating Wavelet Convolution into DETR for Accurate Bird Detection
venue: International Conference on Computer Information Science and Artificial Intelligence (CISAI)
reason: Proposes an improved DETR detector for birds in wild environments, evaluated on CUB-200-2011 fused with a COCO bird subset; wildlife (bird detection) is the stated application. The paper does not state whether the birds in the images are wild or captive.

title: DSH-DETR: Dual Spatial Hybrid Detection Transformer for Underwater Small Object Detection
reason: Proposes a transformer detector for small underwater objects, evaluated on underwater datasets RUOD and URPC2020. The stated application is marine ecological monitoring and surveys of small aquatic organisms.

title: Automatic Identification and Counting of South African Animal Species in Camera Traps Using Deep Learning
reason: Primary study applying CNN classifiers and object detectors to camera trap images of wild South African mammals for species identification and counting.

title: A hybrid approach of pattern recognition to detect marine animals
venue: International Journal of Informatics and Communication Technology
reason: Proposes a HoG+CNN+SVM classifier for images of sharks and saltwater crocodiles, aimed at warning swimmers near the coast. The paper does not state whether the images show wild or captive animals; images come from unspecified external sources.

title: Automated Detection and Classification of Underwater Species Using YOLOv8 for Real-time Marine Ecosystem Monitoring
venue: International Journal of Environmental Monitoring and Analysis
reason: YOLOv8 detection and segmentation of marine animals in underwater images. Scenes include open water and coral reefs, but some images come from aquarium environments, so the subjects are coded as mixed. The paper does not state the image source explicitly.

title: Using large-scale community science data and computer vision to evaluate thermoregulation as an adaptive driver of physiological color change in Anolis carolinensis
reason: Applies a computer vision pipeline (groundedSAM segmentation, K-means color classification) to iNaturalist field photos of wild green anoles to study color change.

title: An advanced approach for detecting burrows of multiple macroinvertebrate species in intertidal sediments using artificial intelligence and drone imagery
reason: Primary study applying YOLOv7 object detection to drone orthophotos to detect burrow openings (direct signs) of wild intertidal macroinvertebrates in tidal flats.

title: A simple method for rapid reconstruction of 3D animal trajectory from monocular video
reason: Method paper on 3D trajectory reconstruction from monocular video; the analysed data are bats filmed in a controlled predation experiment with a fixed camera and take-off point, and marker-bearing walking pigeons from 3D-POP. No wild, free-ranging footage is stated.

title: Development of AI-based smart box trap system for capturing a harmful wild boar
reason: Primary study that trains a YOLOv7-tiny detector on images of free-ranging wild boars and raccoons and deploys it in a field box trap system.

title: Underwater paddling kinematics and hydrodynamics in a surface swimming duck versus a diving duck
reason: Biomechanics study of trained captive ducks (lent by a zoo and housed in an aviary) swimming in a custom-built pool. Body and foot landmarks were digitized by hand from high-speed video. No data show wild animals.

title: The key to bubble-net feeding: how humpback whale morphology functionally differs from other baleen whales
reason: Kinematics study of wild humpback whales based mainly on inertial biologging tag data. The images are used only for manual aerial photogrammetry (whale length, ring size) and for a 3D model of an excised flipper. The paper develops or evaluates no computer vision method.

title: Landing on a swinging perch: peach-faced lovebirds prefer extremes
reason: Captive lovebirds filmed in an indoor laboratory flight corridor for biomechanics study; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: WildPose: a long-range 3D wildlife motion capture system
reason: Presents a camera + LiDAR motion capture system with a segmentation and tracking pipeline applied to free-ranging wildlife recorded in Kgalagadi Transfrontier Park.

title: Fine-Grained Recognition and Monitoring of Wild Birds Based on Deep Learning and UAV Image Acquisition
reason: Proposes an improved CNN for fine-grained species recognition of wild birds, evaluated on bird image datasets (Birdsnap, CUB-200-2011); wild birds are the stated subject.

title: YOLO-Vortex: Underwater Target Detection Model Based on Vortex Aggregation Network
reason: The paper proposes a general underwater object detector and tests it on the TrashCan marine-debris dataset. Animals (fish, starfish, crab and others) appear only as some of its 22 classes, and wildlife is not the stated subject.

title: Proposed Solar-Powered Motion Sensor for Farm Monitoring and Surveillance: A Solar-Powered Assisted Process
reason: Prototype for farm pest (rodent/small-animal) surveillance and deterrence; the detector is trained on web-collected and public images with no statement that the animals are wild or free-ranging, and no field data are analysed.

title: Solar-powered motion sensor for farm monitoring and surveillance: a solar-powered assisted process
reason: Primary study applying a YOLOv8n detector to images of non-domestic small mammals (rat, mouse, squirrel, chipmunk, mole) for farm intrusion monitoring. Images are web-sourced and from a public rat dataset; the paper does not state whether the animals shown are wild or captive, so this is a borderline case against E-AGRI (pest animals in farm settings).

title: Solar-powered motion sensor for farm monitoring and surveillance: a solar-powered assisted process
reason: Farm pest-surveillance prototype: YOLOv8n detects rodents and other small pest animals for crop protection and deterrence. Images come from web sources and an unnamed public rat dataset; the paper does not state whether the animals shown are wild.

title: A Deep Learning Based Model for Detection and Tracking of Stray Animals in the Fields
reason: Deep learning detection and tracking of animals, including wild species such as elephants, tigers, bears and deer, entering crop fields. The goal is to reduce human-wildlife conflict. Domestic animals such as bulls and goats are also included.

title: Combining Camera Trapping and Deep Learning for Labor-Saving Monitoring of Perching Sympetrum Dragonflies （Odonata: Libellulidae）
venue: Japanese Journal of Applied Entomology and Zoology
reason: Applies a deep-learning image classifier (ResNet-50) to camera-trap photographs of wild Sympetrum dragonflies perching in rice paddy fields in Fukushima, Japan; primary research.

title: Mapping coral reefs growth using drone imagery in Gili Labak Island, Sumenep District, East Java, Indonesia
reason: Drone imagery of wild coral reefs (animals) classified pixel-wise into coral genera with supervised maximum likelihood to map coral cover change.

title: Progress in developing a bark beetle identification tool
reason: Images are of preserved bark beetle specimens (stored in ethanol) photographed in a petri dish in a controlled lab set-up; no images of free-ranging animals.

title: A framework for assessing reliability of observer annotations of aerial wildlife imagery, with insights for deep learning applications
reason: Primary study of expert and volunteer annotations (boxes, classes, counts) of drone imagery of wild migratory waterfowl, intended as deep learning training data. Image analysis is limited to texture features, annotation clustering and a deep learning filter for empty tiles, so inclusion is borderline against E-NOCV.

title: A multi-target tracking method for UAV monitoring wildlife in Qinghai
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv7 + Deep SORT multi-object tracking method on UAV video of wild Przewalski's gazelle collected in the field in Qinghai.

title: Comprehensive assessment of snow leopard distribution and population in the Indian Trans-Himalaya, Ladakh: Standardizing methods for evidence-based conservation
reason: Camera-trap images of wild snow leopards; species identified with AI software and individuals re-identified using pattern-recognition software (Extract-Compare) for SECR population estimation.

title: TransembleNet: Enhancing vector mosquito species classification through transfer learning-based ensemble model
reason: Proposes a transfer-learning ensemble CNN that classifies images of non-domestic adult vector mosquito species. The paper does not say whether the mosquitoes were wild-caught or lab-reared.

title: MADNet: Marine Animal Detection Network using the YOLO platform
reason: Proposes a YOLO-based detector (MADNet) for marine animals and evaluates it on underwater image datasets captured in real marine environments.

title: A novel approach combining YOLO and DeepSORT for detecting and counting live fish in natural environments through video
reason: Applies YOLOv10 and DeepSORT to detect, track and count live fish in underwater videos from natural environments (coral reefs, seagrass meadows, and others).

title: Utilizing CNNs for classification and uncertainty quantification for 15 families of European fly pollinators
reason: CNN image classification of 15 European pollinating fly families using GBIF field images; museum, laboratory and fossil images were removed where possible, so the data shows wild insects.

title: SCR-Net: A novel lightweight aquatic biological detection network
reason: Proposes a lightweight CNN detector for marine organisms (sea urchins, sea cucumbers, starfish, scallops) in underwater images from two open datasets; the paper does not state whether the animals are wild or farmed.

title: Drone-based observations of scarring patterns in humpback whales (Megaptera novaeangliae) in the New York Bight provide insight into foraging behavior and anthropogenic threats
reason: Drone images of wild humpback whales were scored for scars by eye, by human observers, and body length was measured manually with photogrammetry software. No computer vision method was developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Factors shaping giraffe behavior in U.S. zoos: A multi-institutional study to inform management
reason: Behavioural study of zoo-housed giraffes using manual observer scoring with the ZooMonitor app and statistical models (GLMMs). No computer vision or automated image analysis is performed, and all the animals are captive.

title: Method for assessing rodent infestation in plateau based on SegFormer
reason: Primary study proposing a semantic segmentation model (EM-SegFormer) on UAV imagery of burrows of wild plateau rodents, i.e. direct signs of free-ranging animals.

title: Impact of deep learning and post-processing algorithms performances on biodiversity metrics assessed on videos
reason: Pure simulation study: video surveys and detection/classification outputs are simulated numerically; no real images or video are analysed.

title: Neural network-based identification for scallops (Pecten maximus) in natural marine habitats
reason: Applies a deep learning detector (NetHarn Cascade Faster R-CNN in VIAME) to towed underwater video transects to detect and count naturally occurring king and queen scallops on the seabed.

title: Advancing fishery dependent and independent habitat assessments using automated image analysis: A fisheries management agency case study
reason: The paper classifies benthic habitat types (sand, macroalgae, seagrass, reef structure) from seabed images. Sponges and corals are only folded into a broad 'ReefStructure' habitat class, so the subject is habitat, not animals.

title: Leveraging synthetic data produced from museum specimens to train adaptable species classification models
reason: All images (synthetic renders and photographs) come from museum skull specimens of the Canadian Museum of Nature; no images of free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Refining animal care through technology: Addressing alopecia in Jaculus jaculus with validated computer vision analysis
reason: Computer vision behaviour classification of jerboas from a laboratory research colony housed in terraria; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Zero-shot image classification based on class representation learning and attribute embedding learning
reason: Generic zero-shot image classification method evaluated on standard benchmarks (CUB, SUN, AWA2); wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Testing a bat fatality detection system at wind turbines
reason: Applies thermal video analysis (background subtraction, tracking, ML classification) to detect free-ranging bat fatalities at wind turbines in Texas.

title: Comparison of flight behaviour and flight morphology between perching Lycaena phlaeas and patrolling Zizeeria maha (Lepidoptera: Lycaenidae)
reason: Video of free-flying wild butterflies in the field is analysed with stereo 3D reconstruction (DLT) to track flight trajectories, so this counts as image-based analysis of wild animals.

title: Dual Encoder Ensemble with EfficientNet and VGG for Bird Species Identification
venue: Ssrg International Journal of Electronics and Communication Engineering
reason: Primary study proposing a CNN dual-encoder for bird species identification from images, framed for wildlife conservation; the paper does not state whether the Kaggle bird images show wild or captive birds.

title: Improved CNN Recognition Algorithm for Identifying Bird Hazards in Transmission Lines
venue: International Journal of Advanced Computer Science and Applications
reason: Proposes a CNN feature-fusion + SVM classifier to identify wild bird species on power transmission lines. Images come from tower surveillance cameras and from the web.

title: A Comparative Analysis of Convolutional Neural Network (CNN): MobileNetV2 and Xception for Butterfly Species Classification
reason: Primary study applying CNN image classification to 100 butterfly species (non-domestic animals) with conservation monitoring as the stated application. The paper does not state whether the Kaggle images show wild, captive or specimen butterflies.

title: CLASSIFICAÇÃO DE IMAGENS DE CRUSTÁCEOS USANDO APRENDIZADO DE MÁQUINA E APRENDIZADO PROFUNDO, COM ÊNFASE NA SUPERORDEM PERACARIDA (MALACOSTRACA: CRUSTACEA)
reason: Primary study applying CNN/DNN image classification to images of wild marine crustaceans (zooplankton ZooScan samples, web/iNaturalist photos, specimen photos); includes a literature review section but the core is experimental.

title: Wild Boar Detection on Sea Turtle Nesting Beaches Using Camera Trap Images: Automated Image Recognition with YOLO Models and Their Evaluation
reason: Applies YOLO-family object detectors to camera trap footage of feral wild boars and free-ranging goats on sea turtle nesting beaches; primary research on free-ranging animals.

title: Multi-scale Activation, Selection, and Aggregation: Exploring Diverse Cues for Fine-Grained Bird Recognition
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
reason: Proposes a ViT-based computer vision method for fine-grained bird species recognition, framed around bird conservation, and evaluates it on bird image datasets (CUB-200-2011, NABirds) and iNat2017. The paper does not say whether the birds pictured are wild or captive.

title: SatCLIP: Global, General-Purpose Location Embeddings with Satellite Imagery
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
reason: General-purpose geographic location encoder pretrained on Sentinel-2 satellite imagery. Animals show up only as one of nine downstream benchmarks (iNaturalist species classification); wildlife is not the stated subject.

title: AI-based Animal Intrusion Detection System for Human-Wildlife Conflicts in Bhutan
reason: YOLOv8-based detection and classification of wild crop-raiding animals (bear, boar, deer, elephant, monkey) together with cattle and horse, trained on web-sourced images, for human-wildlife conflict mitigation in Bhutan.

title: Detection of Bird Species Found in Bhutan Using Vision Transformer-based Transfer Learning
reason: Primary study fine-tuning a Vision Transformer to classify images of 23 bird species found in Bhutan, using photographs from local birdwatchers and a Kaggle dataset. The paper does not explicitly state that the birds are wild; this is inferred from the birdwatcher source.

title: AI-based channel infused coral identification and tracking algorithm for autonomous underwater vehicles
reason: Primary study training YOLOv8 and ByteTrack to detect, classify, segment and track wild corals (and feather stars) in ROV video recorded on natural reefs in the South Andaman Islands.

title: Tackling the problem of multi-class imbalanced classification on species distribution models using machine learning techniques
reason: Species distribution modelling on a tabular fish occurrence dataset (441 observations, 3 variables) using ensemble ML; no image or video analysis.

title: C2-Net: Improving Feature Extraction and Alignment for Few-Shot Fine-Grained Image Classification
reason: Generic few-shot fine-grained classification method evaluated on general benchmarks (Stanford Dogs, Stanford Cars, CUB, meta-iNat); wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Deep Learning on field photography reveals the morphometric diversity of Colombian Freshwater Fish
reason: Applies Grounding DINO and SAM to segment field photographs of live wild Colombian freshwater fish, then analyses the fish's morphometric diversity.

title: Population density of medium- and large-sized mammals in the Alfina Plateau, central Italy
reason: Camera-trap images were used only to count independent encounters for Random Encounter Model density estimation. Species were identified by hand and no computer vision or automated image analysis was applied.

title: Habitat and morphometric data based identification of tiger beetle (Coleoptera, Cicindelinae) species in Sri Lanka using Classification algorithms
reason: Tiger beetle species are classified from tabular habitat and morphometric records using classical ML. No images or video are analysed.

title: TIDE-YOLO: Lightweight Algorithm for Underwater Object Detection
reason: Proposes a lightweight YOLOv8s-based detector for underwater marine organisms (echinus, holothurian, scallop, starfish, fish, turtles, etc.). It is evaluated on public underwater datasets. The paper calls the DUO species aquaculture species, but RUOD covers a wider range of marine organisms.

title: DGP-DETR : A real-time detection algorithm for underwater target detection
reason: Proposes a DETR-based detector for underwater targets, evaluated on underwater images of marine organisms (sea cucumbers, sea urchins, scallops, starfish, biological specimens) in marine environments.

title: Biodiversity and Ecosystem Monitoring using deep learning
reason: Applies CNNs to camera trap images (Snapshot Serengeti, Wildlife Insights) for species identification, alongside satellite imagery and bioacoustics; primary study with reported results.

title: A Computer Vision-Based Detection Model for Wild Chinese Giant Salamanders in Complex Environments
reason: Proposes a YOLO v11n-based detection model for wild Chinese giant salamanders in their natural habitat, using images taken in a nature reserve.

title: Humans versus Machines: Artificial intelligence performs similarly to manual analysis in benthic reef monitoring
reason: Evaluates CoralNet automated (CNN-based) annotation of field reef photoquadrats containing wild corals and zoanthids, compared with manual annotation.

title: Assessing the diversity of benthic foraminifera in coral reefs: a global perspective
reason: Literature-based compilation of benthic foraminifera species occurrence records with beta-diversity statistics; no image or video analysis or computer vision method.

title: Paving the way for improved insect metabarcoding
reason: The paper compares DNA metabarcoding with expert morphological identification of insects from Malaise traps. No images or video are analysed and no computer vision is used.

title: Wildlife responses to recreational trail density are mediated by landscape configuration rather than short-term increases in recreation intensity
reason: Camera trap ecology study of wildlife responses to recreation; images were manually processed and annotated, with analyses being statistical (activity kernels, Poisson regression). No computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Harnessing YOLO and TensorFlow for Smarter Wildlife Monitoring: A Step Toward Scalable, RealTime Conservation
venue: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)
reason: Applies a YOLO-based detector to images of wild animals (tigers, lions, elephants, leopards), with some domestic animals (bulls) also shown; the data sources are only loosely described.

title: New method of image processing via statistical analysis for application in intelligent systems
reason: Generic image processing method tested on scanning electron microscopy images of nickel nanowires in alumina membranes; no animals involved.

title: Beneath the Surface: The Role of Underwater Image Enhancement in Object Detection
reason: Evaluates underwater image enhancement and object detection on underwater images of free-ranging marine animals (RUOD: holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish, fish, turtle, jellyfish, etc.). One dataset (CUPDD) covers aquatic plants, but the RUOD part covers wild animals.

title: Feature Fusion Units for Fine-Grained Image Categorization
reason: Generic fine-grained classification method evaluated on CUB-200-2011 and Stanford Dogs benchmarks; wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: SGCap: Decoding Semantic Group for Zero-shot Video Captioning
reason: Generic zero-shot video captioning method evaluated on general video benchmarks (MSVD, MSR-VTT, VATEX); wildlife is not the subject.

title: Carnivorous Animal Detection Using AI & ML
venue: International Journal for Research in Applied Science and Engineering Technology
reason: Primary study applying CNN and Random Forest classifiers to animal images to separate carnivorous from non-carnivorous species for wildlife monitoring. The paper does not say whether the Kaggle images show wild or captive animals, so inclusion rests on the stated wildlife application.

title: Constructing Mammal Occurrence Status and Deep Learning Training Data from Camera Trap Surveys in Wind Farm
reason: Camera-trap survey of wild mammals at two wind farms with a manual, user-assisted labeling GUI that produces COCO-style annotations. Species were identified and boxes drawn by people; no computer vision model was trained, applied or evaluated.

title: RHAM-CA-Det: An Attention Mechanism for Butterfly Detection
reason: Proposes a deep learning detector for butterflies in natural-environment images from the EIAB dataset.

title: Small Object Detection for Ornithological Monitoring Tasks
reason: Proposes a CNN-based detector for small birds in video frames from ornithological monitoring in natural scenes.

title: Tracking Small Objects in Global Motion Conditions for an Ornithological Monitoring System
reason: Proposes a computer vision tracking method (SAM2 plus a Kalman filter) for free-flying birds in video from an ornithological monitoring system.

title: Wildlife Target Re-Identification Using Self-Supervised Learning in Non-Urban Settings
reason: Proposes self-supervised wildlife re-identification trained on camera trap data of wild animals from South African safaris; evaluation also includes domestic animals (cat, cow, dog).

title: An Autonomous Patrol Robot for Wild Animal and Electric Fence Anomaly Detection
venue: International Conference on Control, Automation and Systems (ICCAS)
reason: Develops a CNN (YOLO11n) detector for wild Japanese black bears, wild boars and deer as part of an autonomous patrol robot for electric fences.

title: Rope Deployment Method for Enhancing Multi-Angle Imaging Quality of Wildlife Pests in RCMS
reason: The paper optimises where to put the camera ropes with NSGA-II and tests this on simulated 2D fields of target points. Its own experiments analyse no images or video; image quality is scored with an evaluation function taken from earlier work.

title: AI Infused Underwater Analysis for Enhanced Coral Species
venue: Proceedings of the 2025 12th International Conference on Computing for Sustainable Global Development Indiacom 2025
reason: Applies deep learning detection, segmentation and tracking to underwater images of coral reef species (wild marine animals).

title: Camera Trap Data Analysis for Grevy's Zebra Monitoring
reason: Applies MegaDetector and EfficientNet to camera trap images of wild Grevy's and Plains zebras in a Kenyan conservancy.

title: Deployment and Evaluation of the Autonomous Monitoring of Insects (AMI) System for Ecosystem Health Assessment in Kenya
reason: Primary study applying an image-processing insect counting algorithm to images of wild nocturnal insects attracted to a UV light trap deployed in a forested conservancy in Kenya.

title: MVA 2025 Small Multi-Object Tracking for Spotting Birds Challenge: Dataset, Methods, and Results
reason: Introduces a UAV video dataset and challenge for detecting and tracking small wild birds in real-world environments.

title: A Novel Framework for Decoding Inter-Species Communication with Octopodes (DISC-O)
reason: All described image data come from a custom 200 L aquarium tank holding juvenile Octopus vulgaris; the paper names in-situ deployment in natural habitats only as future work.

title: An Underwater Object Detection and Classification System by Integration of YOLOv8 and EfficientNet Using an Advanced Enhancement Method
reason: Proposes an enhancement, detection and classification pipeline for underwater images of marine benthic animals from the DUO dataset.

title: GTRF: Global Tracking Transformers for Underwater Fish Species Monitoring
reason: Transformer-based multi-object tracking of wild fish in underwater survey videos from the Gulf of America.

title: Synthetic Data Augmentation for Coral Health Detection: A Joint Training Approach with CycleGAN and UNIT
reason: Generates synthetic coral images with CycleGAN/UNIT joint model and detects compromised coral with YOLOv9 on underwater field images of wild coral reefs.

title: Large-Scale Underwater Multi-Fish Tracking Using the ByteTrack Algorithm
reason: Applies YOLOX detection and ByteTrack multi-object tracking to underwater video of fish in their natural habitats from a fishery-independent survey dataset.

title: Robust Multi-Fish Detection and Tracking in Underwater Videos Using a GUI-Supported Annotation Review Framework
reason: Applies deep-learning detection and tracking to underwater survey videos of wild reef fish in their natural habitats in the Gulf of America.

title: Improved Ground-Truthing and Benthic Habitat Characterization with Machine Learning Models and 3D Photogrammetry
reason: Applies ML segmentation models to SfM orthomosaics from AUV images to map live mussels on the Lake Michigan lakebed (wild invertebrates in the field).

title: PEMANTAUAN MUSANG PANDAN MENGGUNAKAN METODE COMPUTER VISION DENGAN MODEL YOLOV11
venue: Jurnal Informatika dan Teknik Elektro Terapan
reason: YOLOv8 detection of Asian palm civets kept in captive breeding enclosures only; no free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: MEWC: A user-friendly AI workflow for customised wildlife-image classification
reason: Presents an open-source deep-learning workflow for detecting and classifying wildlife in camera-trap images, demonstrated on free-ranging Tasmanian wildlife.

title: Tracking butterfly flight in the field from an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV): a methodological proof of principle
reason: Primary study that develops an image-filtering and video-tracking method to reconstruct flight tracks of wild, untagged, free-flying Pieris butterflies from UAV video.

title: Assessment of the occurrence of the pond turtle Emys orbicularis in Poleski National Park based on drone monitoring
venue: Journal of Animal Science Biology and Bioeconomy
reason: Drone photos of wild pond turtles were taken, but the turtles were photographed and counted by hand to study habitat preferences. No computer vision method was developed or applied to detect or classify the animals. WebODM was used only to make habitat orthophotos.

title: Federated Learning and Blockchain-Based Collaborative Framework for Real-Time Wild Life Monitoring
reason: Federated learning / blockchain framework tested only on a subset of a generic Open Images-derived Kaggle dataset; the paper does not state that the images show wild or free-ranging animals and no field data are used.

title: Hoofed animal detection in UAV thermal images using Balanced Random Forest and CNN features
reason: Proposes a UAV thermal-image detection method for hoofed animals. The main data come from a fenced enclosure, and an auxiliary flight over a semi-open area recorded free-ranging wild ungulates.

title: Kinematic Adaptation in Space Robotics Inspired by Animal Righting Reflexes
reason: Applies computer vision (segmentation, pose estimation, keypoint tracking) to videos of lizards to extract motion patterns. Training uses the public Animal Kingdom dataset. The paper does not state whether the animals are wild or captive, and none of the exclusion criteria clearly applies.

title: Automation of unmanned counting for spawners of chum and coho salmon with methods of artificial intelligence
reason: Deep learning model for species-specific detection of wild chum and coho salmon spawners and post-spawn chum salmon in rivers on UAV aerial photographs; primary research.

title: Joint Multi-Scale Channel Attention and Multi-Perception Head for Underwater Object Detection
reason: Proposes a CNN detector (JMM-Net) for marine organisms (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish) in underwater images from public datasets, framed around marine ecological monitoring. The paper does not say whether the animals are farmed, so they are treated as free-ranging.

title: Animal detection in fields using image processing
reason: Prototype vision system that detects wild animals entering crop fields to reduce human-wildlife conflict. The example images show both wild animals (bear) and domestic ones (horse, cow, sheep).

title: Utilising affordable smartphones and open-source time-lapse photography for pollinator image collection and annotation
reason: Wild pollinators were photographed with smartphone time-lapse, but every annotation and identification was done by human experts. No computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated; automated detection and classification are left as future work.

title: Integrating Deep Learning with Remote Sensing for Early Detection of Coral Reef Degradation
reason: Applies a CNN-Transformer to satellite images to classify the condition of wild coral reefs (live, bleached and dead coral). Corals are wild animals, so the paper is included.

title: Utilizing Deep Learning for Automated Detection of Endangered Species in Camera Trap Data
reason: Applies deep learning (CNN with transfer learning) to camera trap images to detect and classify endangered wild species.

title: Fish Species Classification with Deep Learning and Bayesian Optimization: Effectiveness and Comparative Results
venue: International Journal of Pure and Applied Sciences
reason: Primary study applying CNN classifiers to images of 31 fish species from a fishing port in the Philippines, framed as marine ecosystem monitoring. The paper does not say whether the fish are live, caught or free-ranging, so the wild status is not stated; included because non-domestic fish are the stated subject and no exclusion criterion clearly applies.

title: Simulating the Behavior of Forest Animal Groups to Generate Synthetic Data in Unreal Engine 5
venue: Optical Memory and Neural Networks Information Optics
reason: Develops a synthetic data generation system for detecting wild forest animals in aerial imagery and evaluates YOLOv8 trained on real wild-animal images mixed with synthetic ones.

title: Modeling the Behavior of a Flock of Birds to Generate Synthetic Data in Unreal Engine 5
reason: Develops synthetic bird-flock data generation in UE5 and evaluates YOLOv11 bird detection on real images of bird flocks from open sources.

title: Detection Of Pufferfish Using Computer Vision And Deep Learning Methods
reason: Applies YOLO object detection to underwater diver videos of wild invasive pufferfish (Lagocephalus sceleratus) in the Mediterranean.

title: U-YOLOv3: A Model Focused on Underwater Object Detection
reason: Proposes a modified YOLOv3 for underwater object detection, evaluated on the Brackish dataset, which has annotated fish, crabs, jellyfish, shrimp and starfish in underwater images.

title: Pinworm infections in red squirrels at the urban-forest interface
reason: Primary veterinary parasitology study that applies YOLOv5 detection and DeepLabCut-based individual identification to camera-trap images and video of free-ranging red squirrels at feeding stations.

title: [Paper] Appearance-and-Spectral-Based Identification System for Penguin Individuals
venue: ITE Transactions on Media Technology and Applications
reason: Individual identification of penguins using hyperspectral images captured only at Ueno Zoo; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: WOLO: Wilson Only Looks Once – Estimating Ant Body Mass From Reference-Free Images Using Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
reason: All images show leaf-cutter ants from a laboratory colony, recorded in acrylic arenas, Petri dishes and a laboratory foraging trail. No wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: A Self-Supervised Hybrid Similarity Framework for Underwater Coral Species Classification
reason: Few-shot computer vision method for classifying coral families (animals, Cnidaria) from underwater photographs gathered from online repositories; coral reef monitoring is the stated application. The paper does not explicitly say the corals are wild, but describes the images as underwater reef imagery.

title: Wild Animal Movement Detection and Alert System
venue: International Journal of Scientific Research in Computer Science Engineering and Information Technology
reason: Describes an ESP32-CAM + YOLO system for detecting wild animals in natural habitats with alerts. The paper reports no concrete data or results, but it is a primary CV application aimed at wild animals.

title: YOLO-Based Automatic Deer Antler Identification for Population Assessment
reason: YOLOv8 detection of deer antlers on images that include camera-trap photographs, aimed at wildlife population monitoring; the paper does not state whether the photographed deer are wild or captive.

title: Automated insect monitoring with camera traps is transforming ecological understanding
reason: Applies automated camera traps with deep-learning detection, classification, tracking and counting to wild nocturnal moths in Danish nature reserves, then uses the outputs for ecological analyses.

title: Feasibility of using very high-resolution satellite imagery to monitor Tristan albatrosses Diomedea dabbenena on Gough Island
reason: Wild Tristan albatrosses were counted in satellite imagery, but the counts were done entirely by hand by experts and volunteers. The paper applies no automated computer vision method; the only image processing is orthorectification and pansharpening.

title: Tracking trends in foraging sea turtle aggregations at Reunion Island using aerial and photo-ID surveys (2008-2023)
reason: Wild sea turtles are monitored through aerial surveys by human observers and through manual photo-ID of head scales. No computer vision or automated image analysis is developed or applied.

title: High sea turtle density in a Mediterranean foraging ground revealed by UAV surveys and machine learning
reason: Applies YOLOv8 detection to drone videos of wild loggerhead turtles at sea to estimate density.

title: Estimation of short-tailed albatross Phoebastria albatrus population on the Senkaku Islands using satellite images
reason: Wild albatrosses were counted by hand on colour prints of satellite images. No computer vision or automated image-analysis method was used.

title: Age-specific body length, mass, and energetic cost of growth in humpback whales
reason: Applies UAS (drone) image photogrammetry and automated photo-identification matching to free-ranging humpback whales in Hawai'i and Southeast Alaska to estimate body size, mass and growth costs.

title: Male bluegill vary in color and behavior relative to their position in a lek
reason: Applies computer vision colour segmentation (k-means via recolorize/patternize) to photographs of wild-caught bluegill from a lake to relate body colour to lek position.

title: Adaptation of shell morphology to different tidal zones—insights into phenotypic plasticity of Littorina brevicula
reason: Shell morphometrics study: landmarks were placed by hand in ImageJ on lab photographs of collected shells, then analysed with GPA/PCA/CVA, plus 3D scanning for flow simulation. There is no computer vision method; the image work is manual measurement on specimens.

title: Identification, abundance, and behavior of North American bobcat (Lynx rufus) along road mitigation structures designed for endangered species in South Texas
reason: Primary study that evaluates the pattern-recognition software HotSpotter (against manual visual identification and a spatio-temporal strategy) for individual identification of wild bobcats in camera trap photos at wildlife crossing structures.

title: Leveraging artificial intelligence for photo identification to aid CITES enforcement in combating illegal trade of the endangered humphead wrasse (Cheilinus undulatus)
reason: Photo re-identification of wild-caught humphead wrasse, but every analysed image shows fish held in retail shop tanks. No image shows free-ranging animals.

title: GIWT-YOLO: an efficient multi-scale framework for real-time Scolytinae pests detection
reason: Pest detection for forestry/agricultural pest management (Scolytinae bark beetle pests and rice crop pests), with images mainly taken in controlled settings; not wildlife monitoring or conservation.

title: Detecting and quantifying deep sea benthic life using advanced object detection
reason: The paper trains and evaluates a YOLOv8 object detector on ROV images of wild deep-sea benthic fauna from the North Atlantic.

title: LFN-YOLO: precision underwater small object detection via a lightweight reparameterized approach
reason: Proposes a lightweight YOLO-based detector for underwater marine organisms, evaluated on public underwater datasets of free-living marine animals (URPC, Brackish, TrashCan) and on fish fry in a tank.

title: Assisting human annotation of marine images with foundation models
reason: Applies the Segment Anything foundation model to segment and localise wild marine organisms in field-collected underwater images from four datasets.

title: Automatic detection, identification and counting of deep-water snappers on underwater baited video using deep learning
reason: Primary study applying Faster R-CNN to baited underwater video of wild deep-water snappers in New Caledonia to detect, identify and count fish.

title: 3D reconstructions of stranded marine mammals via easily accessible remote sensing tools for use in morphometrics and visualizations
reason: Applies image-based 3D reconstruction (smartphone LiDAR/photogrammetry, UAV SfM-MVS) to stranded wild marine mammals in British Columbia for morphometrics and visualization.

title: Development of a multi-modal deep-learning-based web application for image classification of marine decapods in conservation practice
reason: Deep-learning image classification of marine decapod species from web database images (WoRMS) for conservation and non-indigenous species monitoring; non-domestic marine animals are the subject.

title: Automatic deep learning-based pipeline for Mediterranean fish segmentation
reason: Instance segmentation model (YOLOv8) for wild Mediterranean fish from underwater observatory, citizen-science and field-deployed stereo camera images; primary research.

title: A novel edge-feature attention fusion framework for underwater image enhancement
reason: Generic underwater image enhancement method evaluated on general underwater benchmarks (UIEB, LSUI, U45, SQUID); animals appear only incidentally in scenes and wildlife is not the stated subject.

title: Whose bite? Evaluating the use of structure-from-motion for monitoring fish corallivory
reason: Applies structure-from-motion photogrammetry to underwater imagery of wild coral reefs to quantify fish bite marks (direct signs of wild corallivorous fishes) on wild corals, compared against in situ surveys.

title: Hybrid Mamba for amphibious Limulidae low-light image enhancement
reason: Proposes a deep learning (hybrid Mamba) low-light image enhancement method for images of horseshoe crabs (Limulidae) in amphibious outdoor environments, aimed at biological monitoring. The paper does not say whether the animals were wild or captive. The images are outdoor scenes collected with a marine biodiversity conservation laboratory, so the paper is included.

title: Training marine species object detectors with synthetic images and unsupervised domain adaptation
reason: Proposes a sea urchin object detector trained on synthetic images with domain adaptation. It is evaluated on real underwater images: AUV surveys of wild benthos off Tasmania, plus UDD images taken in an open-sea farm.

title: Benthos-DETR: a high-precision efficient network for benthic organisms detection
reason: Detection of sea cucumbers, sea urchins and scallops in images from an open-sea farm (mariculture) for an underwater picking system; the animals are farmed seafood, not wild free-ranging wildlife.

title: Humpback whale (Megaptera novaeangliae) maturity and body condition in Ireland, Norway and Cabo Verde based on UAS photogrammetry data
reason: Applies UAS aerial photogrammetry (image-based measurement) to free-ranging humpback whales to estimate body length and condition.

title: Detection of the largest herd of dugongs (Dugong dugon) in the Central Arabian Gulf using unmanned aerial vehicles
reason: Wild dugongs were filmed by drone, but the images were only counted by hand by human observers after manual colour adjustments. No computer vision method was developed or applied.

title: Efficient underwater ecological monitoring with embedded AI: detecting Crown-of-Thorns Starfish via DCGAN and YOLOv6
reason: Deep learning detection of wild Crown-of-Thorns Starfish in underwater imagery from the Great Barrier Reef.

title: A lightweight YOLO network for robotic underwater biological detection
reason: Proposes a lightweight YOLO detector for marine organisms (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish) in underwater images of real marine scenes.

title: Deep-sea organism detection method based on the SDA-HTransYOLOv8n model
reason: Proposes an object detection model for wild deep-sea organisms in video frames captured by the Jiaolong manned submersible in the western Pacific.

title: UOD-YOLO: a lightweight real-time model for detecting marine organisms
reason: Proposes a lightweight YOLO-based detector for marine organisms (fish, echinus, holothurian, turtles, etc.) in underwater images from public underwater benchmarks; application to marine ecological monitoring.

title: Multimodal fusion image enhancement technique and CFEC-YOLOv7 for underwater target detection algorithm research
reason: Proposes underwater image enhancement and a YOLOv7-based detector for marine organisms (sea cucumbers, sea urchins, starfish) in real underwater images.

title: OpenLabCluster: active learning based clustering and classification of animal behaviors based on kinematic body keypoints
reason: Behaviour classification from keypoints of laboratory animals (home-cage mice, zebrafish, C. elegans) and macaques in an enclosure; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: YOLO-Pika: a lightweight improved model of YOLOv8n incorporating Fusion_Block and multi-scale fusion FPN and its application in the precise detection of plateau pikas
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for burrows (direct signs) of wild plateau pikas and Brandt's voles in UAV images of grassland.

title: A mobile hybrid deep learning approach for classifying 3D-like representations of Amazonian lizards
reason: Images are of alcohol-preserved museum specimens from a herpetological collection; no living wild animals are imaged.

title: A novel approach to Indian bird species identification: employing visual-acoustic fusion techniques for improved classification accuracy
reason: Primary study classifying Indian bird species with a CNN on bird images (from Wikipedia and field surveys) fused with LSTM audio features; wild birds are the stated subject.

title: Is AI currently capable of identifying wild oysters? A comparison of human annotators against the AI model, ODYSSEE
reason: Primary study evaluating a deep learning oyster detection model against human annotators on underwater images of a wild oyster reef.

title: 3D colored point cloud classification of a deep-sea cold-water coral and sponge habitat using geometric features and machine learning algorithms
reason: Primary study classifying SfM point clouds derived from ROV video of wild deep-sea cold-water corals and sponges (sessile animals) using machine learning on RGB and geometric features.

title: Advancing Taxonomy with Machine Learning: A Hybrid Ensemble for Species and Genus Classification
reason: The images are insect, beetle and fish samples from the BOLD barcode repository, each paired with a DNA barcode. These are collected specimens, not wild free-ranging animals photographed in the field. The paper builds a multimodal image + DNA classifier.

title: AI-Driven Insect Detection, Real-Time Monitoring, and Population Forecasting in Greenhouses
reason: Detects and forecasts black aphid crop pests on sticky traps in a cucumber greenhouse used for production; this is agricultural pest monitoring, not wildlife.

title: Deep Learning-Based Snake Species Identification for Enhanced Snakebite Management
reason: CNN-based species classification of Moroccan snakes from images collected by herpetologists in natural habitats plus the citizen-science SnakeCLEF 2021 dataset.

title: Integration of YOLOv8 Small and MobileNet V3 Large for Efficient Bird Detection and Classification on Mobile Devices
reason: Applies YOLOv8 detection and MobileNet V3 classification to images of five wild bird species from the Zacatecas region, including field tests with a smartphone app.

title: From Camera Image to Active Target Tracking: Modelling, Encoding and Metrical Analysis for Unmanned Underwater Vehicles †
reason: Vision-based (camera image only) active target tracking of a wild marine mammal (bottlenose dolphin) by an underwater vehicle, developed for cetacean conservation monitoring. Training and evaluation use simulated renders of a dolphin model; no captive or domestic animals are involved.

title: MDA-DETR: Enhancing Offending Animal Detection with Multi-Channel Attention and Multi-Scale Feature Aggregation
reason: Proposes a transformer-based detector (MDA-DETR) evaluated on camera-trap images of six wild mammal species from the Northeast China Tiger and Leopard National Park.

title: Underwater Weight Estimation of Three Sea Cucumber Species in Culture Tanks Using Image Analysis and ArUco Markers
reason: Wild-collected sea cucumbers were photographed only while held in cement culture tanks at a research station, so no image shows free-ranging animals.

title: Data Augmentation for Enhanced Fish Detection in Lake Environments: Affine Transformations, Neural Filters, SinGAN
reason: Anomaly-based computer vision detection of wild fish in video of the surface of a natural lake in Japan, recorded during electrofishing boat surveys.

title: YOLO-WildASM: An Object Detection Algorithm for Protected Wildlife
reason: Proposes a YOLOv8-based object detector for protected wildlife species, trained on images from field-deployed infrared cameras and other photographic sources, and tested on a public wildlife dataset. Some sources (iStock, panda breeding and research centres) may include captive animals, but the paper does not say so.

title: IECA-YOLOv7: A Lightweight Model with Enhanced Attention and Loss for Aerial Wildlife Detection
reason: Proposes a lightweight YOLOv7-tiny-based detector for drone imagery of grassland wildlife (antelope, elephant, giraffe, zebra) with sheep also included; data are aerial images of free-ranging animals from reserves and web sources.

title: Comparing Manual and Automated Spatial Tracking of Captive Spider Monkeys Using Heatmaps
reason: Pose estimation applied only to two captive spider monkeys in an indoor zoo enclosure at Aalborg Zoo; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Hierarchical Dual-Model Detection Framework for Spotted Seals Using Deep Learning on UAVs
reason: Primary study proposing deep-learning object detection models for wild spotted seals in UAV imagery from a river estuary.

title: EyeInvaS: Lowering Barriers to Public Participation in Invasive Alien Species Monitoring Through Deep Learning
reason: Primary study benchmarking deep learning image classifiers for 54 invasive alien species, 21 of which are animals (insects, mollusks, fishes, an amphibian, reptiles), with invasive species monitoring as the stated application. Images are web-scraped and the paper does not state whether the animals shown are wild or captive; the field deployment covered a plant only.

title: MSFN-YOLOv11: A Novel Multi-Scale Feature Fusion Recognition Model Based on Improved YOLOv11 for Real-Time Monitoring of Birds in Wetland Ecosystems
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv11 detector for wild wetland bird species, using web-sourced and drone field images plus field-captured videos.

title: Weighted Feature Fusion Network Based on Multi-Level Supervision for Migratory Bird Counting in East Dongting Lake
reason: Proposes a density-map regression network to count wild migratory birds in surveillance video frames from East Dongting Lake wetland; also evaluated on non-animal counting datasets.

title: Fish Detection in Fishways for Hydropower Stations Using Bidirectional Cross-Scale Feature Fusion
reason: Proposes a lightweight fish detection model evaluated on a mix of wild underwater video (Fish4knowledge) and laboratory fish images, then deployed on free-ranging migratory fish in a hydropower station fishway.

title: WDS-YOLO: A Marine Benthos Detection Model Fusing Wavelet Convolution and Deformable Attention
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for marine benthos (holothurian, echinus, starfish, scallop) in underwater images from natural marine environments.

title: RHS-YOLOv8: A Lightweight Underwater Small Object Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv8
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv8 for detecting marine organisms in underwater images (DUO, RUOD), aimed at marine species monitoring. DUO organisms are described as aquaculture species, while RUOD includes wild marine animals such as fish, turtles and jellyfish.

title: Transferring Face Recognition Techniques to Entomology: An ArcFace and ResNet Approach for Improving Dragonfly Classification
reason: The paper applies computer vision (YOLOv10 detection, and ResNet50 with ArcFace classification) to images of wild dragonflies, including citizen-science photos from iNaturalist. It is primary research.

title: Improving Moving Insect Detection with Difference of Features Maps in YOLO Architecture
reason: Proposes a motion module for YOLOv8 to detect small moving insects. Evaluation uses outdoor time-lapse images of free-flying honeybees visiting flowering plants, plus a synthetic dataset of crop pests on raspberry plants. Because part of the data shows free-ranging insects outdoors, the paper is included. The pest part is agricultural.

title: DeepFishNET+: A Dual-Stream Deep Learning Framework for Robust Underwater Fish Detection and Classification
reason: Proposes a CV method to detect and classify fish species in images. The main dataset comes from a marine fishing port and the paper is framed around aquaculture. The validation datasets include Fish4Knowledge reef fish families, so at least part of the data shows wild fish.

title: Transmission Line Bird Species Detection and Identification Based on Double Data Enhancement and Improvement of YOLOv8s
reason: Develops an improved YOLOv8s model to detect and identify wild bird species on power transmission lines, using field and web images.

title: FPH-DEIM: A Lightweight Underwater Biological Object Detection Algorithm Based on Improved DEIM
reason: Proposes a lightweight detector for underwater marine organisms (echinus, holothurian, scallop, starfish) in images taken by underwater robots in natural underwater scenes.

title: Daily Variation in the Feeding Activity of Pacific Crown-of-Thorns Starfish (Acanthaster cf. solaris)
reason: Applies structure-from-motion photogrammetry and image colour analysis to field imagery of feeding scars (direct signs) left by wild crown-of-thorns starfish on corals of the Great Barrier Reef.

title: Assessing Birds of Prey as Biological Pest Control: A Comparative Study with Hunting Perches and Rodenticides on Rodent Activity and Crop Health
reason: Field study applying YOLOv5 detection and tracking to continuous video of wild raptors (barn owls, black-shouldered kites) in alfalfa fields to quantify perch use; primary research.

title: Birds-YOLO: A Bird Detection Model for Dongting Lake Based on Modified YOLOv11
reason: Proposes a modified YOLOv11 detector for wild birds at Dongting Lake, evaluated on field-collected images and CUB-200-2011.

title: A Novel Fish Pose Estimation Method Based on Semi-Supervised Temporal Context Network
reason: Pose estimation of a single carp filmed in a laboratory water tank; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Smart Wildlife Monitoring: Real-Time Hybrid Tracking Using Kalman Filter and Local Binary Similarity Matching on Edge Network
reason: Primary study proposing a detection and hybrid tracking pipeline on video of free-ranging fallow deer, wild boar and wolves recorded in a park.

title: Swin-Panda: Behavior Recognition for Giant Pandas Based on Local Fine-Grained and Spatiotemporal Displacement Features
reason: Video-based behavior recognition of giant pandas. The data combine captive pandas from the Chengdu breeding base, online videos, and a wild giant panda video dataset, so part of the data shows wild animals.

title: FGBNet: A Bio-Subspecies Classification Network with Multi-Level Feature Interaction
reason: Proposes a fine-grained CNN for bio-subspecies image classification aimed at biodiversity monitoring; evaluated on datasets that include wild animals (CUB birds, iNaturalist) together with domestic dogs and flowers.

title: Enhancing Endangered Feline Conservation in Asia via a Pose-Guided Deep Learning Framework for Individual Identification
reason: Proposes a deep learning re-identification network evaluated on images of wild Amur tigers (ATRW) and wild snow leopards from infrared camera videos.

title: Macao-ebird: A Curated Dataset for Artificial-Intelligence-Powered Bird Surveillance and Conservation in Macao
reason: Introduces a web-collected image dataset of 24 protected bird species of Macao (captive birds excluded) with classification and detection subsets and YOLO baseline experiments.

title: Enhancing Wildlife Detection Using Thermal Imaging Drones: Designing the Flight Path
reason: Thermal drone survey of free-ranging (feral) sika deer; animals were detected and counted by manual visual inspection of the photographs, with no computer vision method. The contribution is flight path design.

title: Drone-Based Detection and Classification of Greater Caribbean Manatees in the Panama Canal Basin
reason: Primary study applying YOLOv8 with SAHI and AltCLIP zero-shot classification to UAV images of free-ranging manatees in Gatun Lake, Panama Canal Basin.

title: The Use of Open Vegetation by Red Deer (Cervus elaphus) and Fallow Deer (Dama dama) Determined by Object Detection Models
reason: Primary study applying a YOLOv8 object detection model to drone thermal video of free-ranging red and fallow deer in a nature reserve to classify behaviour.

title: Tracking Fin Whale Morphology with Drone Photogrammetry: Growth Tendencies, Developmental Changes, and Sexual Dimorphism
reason: Drone photogrammetry study of free-ranging fin whales in which all body measurements were marked manually in MorphoMetriX and analysed statistically; no automated computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.
