title: Autonomous UAV Detection of Ochotona curzoniae Burrows with Enhanced YOLOv11
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv11 detector for burrows of wild plateau pika, which are direct animal signs, in UAV imagery from the Tibetan Plateau.

title: New Methods for Waterfowl and Habitat Survey Using AI and Drone Imagery
reason: Primary study applying deep learning detection and counting to drone images of wild waterfowl in Missouri conservation areas, together with habitat segmentation and image-overlap detection.

title: Drone Monitoring and Behavioral Analysis of White-Beaked Dolphins (Lagenorhynchus albirostris)
reason: Primary study applying CNN-based detection and behaviour classification (LabGym) to drone video of free-ranging white-beaked dolphins in Skjálfandi Bay, Iceland.

title: A Novel Entropy-Based Approach for Thermal Image Segmentation Using Multilevel Thresholding
reason: Proposes an entropy-based thresholding method for segmenting thermal aerial images of wildlife (BIRDSAI, kangaroo surveys) for conservation and anti-poaching monitoring.

title: HRDS: A High-Dimensional Lightweight Keypoint Detection Network Enhancing HRNet with Dim-Channel and Space Gate Attention Using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks
reason: Proposes a lightweight animal keypoint detection (pose estimation) network evaluated on AP-10K, a mammal pose dataset the paper describes as built for animal pose estimation in wild environments; animals are the stated subject.

title: Mitigating Class Imbalance Challenges in Fish Taxonomy: Quantifying Performance Gains Using Robust Asymmetric Loss Within an Optimized Mobile–Former Framework
reason: Primary study proposing a lightweight image classification model (Mobile-Former with robust asymmetric loss) for fish taxonomy on the FishNet dataset, which the paper describes as images from global aquatic environments and underwater imagery; whether the fish are wild or captive is not explicitly stated.

title: Multi-Scale Attention-Driven Hierarchical Learning for Fine-Grained Visual Categorization
reason: Generic fine-grained visual categorization method evaluated only on food, aircraft and car benchmarks; no animal images are analysed.

title: A Uniform Multi-Modal Feature Extraction and Adaptive Local–Global Feature Fusion Structure for RGB-X Marine Animal Segmentation
reason: Proposes a SAM-based RGB-X segmentation method for marine animals in underwater ocean images and video; primary research on animal imagery.

title: Semantic-Guided Mamba Fusion for Robust Object Detection of Tibetan Plateau Wildlife
reason: Proposes an object detection framework and evaluates it on an author-curated image dataset of 13 Tibetan Plateau wildlife species; the paper presents all classes, including yak, as wildlife.

title: A Citizen Science Approach for Documenting Mass Coral Bleaching in the Western Indian Ocean
reason: Applies an automated image classifier (CoralNet) to underwater photographs of wild reef-building corals in Kenya to estimate coral cover and bleaching prevalence.

title: Optimizing IoT Video Data: Dimensionality Reduction for Efficient Deep Learning on Edge Computing
reason: Primary study proposing dimensionality reduction methods for deep-learning-based bird behavior classification on videos of birds in natural environments.

title: Real-Time Farm Surveillance Using IoT and YOLOv8 for Animal Intrusion Detection
reason: Primary study applying CNN classifiers and YOLO detectors to images of animals intruding on farmland; the stated application is wildlife intrusion, and the paper treats intruders as wild or domesticated animals (the demo shows a cow). The animal species in the Kaggle data are not named, so the wild share is not explicitly verified.

title: Utilizing an Enhanced YOLOv8 Model for Fishery Detection
reason: Detection of sea urchins, sea cucumbers, starfish and scallops in images from a marine ranch (stocked seabed aquaculture), with the stated aim of precision fishing and biological harvesting. This is a fishery/aquaculture production application.

title: An Inexpensive 3D Camera System Based on a Completely Synchronized Stereo Camera, Open-Source Software, and a Raspberry Pi for Accurate Fish Size, Position, and Swimming Speed
reason: Stereo camera system tested only on Atlantic cod held in a tank at the Øresund Aquarium; no wild or free-ranging animals were imaged.

title: Study on the Flow Velocity Preference of the Four Major Chinese Carps Using Convolutional Neural Networks
reason: Sub-adult carps obtained from an aquaculture company were filmed in a laboratory flume to measure flow velocity preference. No wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: UM-YOLOv10: Underwater Object Detection Algorithm for Marine Environment Based on YOLOv10 Model
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv10 detector for marine benthic organisms (echinus, holothurian, scallop, starfish) in underwater seabed images from the China Underwater Robot Competition dataset.

title: Mobile-YOLO: A Lightweight Object Detection Algorithm for Four Categories of Aquatic Organisms
reason: Proposes a lightweight object detector for four benthic aquatic organisms in underwater images collected from open sea waters near Zhangzi Island; computer vision on images of animals in a natural marine environment.

title: YOLO-DFAM-Based Onboard Intelligent Sorting System for Portunus trituberculatus
reason: Deep-learning detection, tracking and weight estimation of wild-caught swimming crabs on the sorting conveyor of capture-fishery vessels (fishery catch monitoring, not aquaculture).

title: RetinalCoNet: Underwater Fish Segmentation Network Based on Bionic Retina Dual-Channel and Multi-Module Cooperation
reason: Proposes a CNN segmentation network for fish in underwater video collected in open environments (ponds, reservoirs, rivers), with ecological monitoring as the stated application.

title: Uncertainty Label-Driven Automated Tuna Catch Counting with Robust Object Tracking for Occlusion Fishing Vessels
reason: Computer vision detection, tracking and counting of wild-caught tuna in video from longline fishing vessel decks. These are wild marine fish caught at sea, not aquaculture.

title: IMM-DeepSort: An Adaptive Multi-Model Kalman Framework for Robust Multi-Fish Tracking in Underwater Environments
reason: Proposes a detection-and-tracking method for wild marine fish filmed by underwater video monitoring systems in natural coastal waters.

title: Intelligent Fish Recognition Method Based on Variable-Step Size Learning Rate Optimization Strategy
reason: Classifies caught commercial fish (perch, cod, snapper, golden pompano) for automated sorting in fishery production and food processing. These are not images of free-ranging animals in the wild.

title: Roe Deer as a Model Species for Aerial Survey-Based Ungulate Population Estimation in Agricultural Habitats
reason: Primary study applying object-based image analysis to aerial thermal imagery to detect and count free-ranging roe deer in an agricultural landscape.

title: Thermal Video Enhancement Mamba: A Novel Approach to Thermal Video Enhancement for Real-World Applications
reason: Proposes a thermal video enhancement method and evaluates it, including elephant detection on the BIRDSAI wildlife-monitoring thermal dataset; wildlife monitoring is a stated application.

title: CNN-Based Optimization for Fish Species Classification: Tackling Environmental Variability, Class Imbalance, and Real-Time Constraints
reason: Primary study comparing CNN, classical and hybrid classifiers for fish species classification on images; part of the dataset shows fish in natural underwater (in situ) conditions, alongside controlled and out-of-water photographs.

title: Combining Object Detection, Super-Resolution GANs and Transformers to Facilitate Tick Identification Workflow from Crowdsourced Images on the eTick Platform
reason: Applies object detection, super-resolution and classification to citizen-science photographs of wild ticks submitted to the eTick platform in Canada.

title: Large-Scale Coastal Marine Wildlife Monitoring with Aerial Imagery
reason: Deep learning detection and classification of wild elephant seals, sea lions and seabirds in aerial survey images of coastal colonies in Patagonia.

title: Underwater Target Detection with High Accuracy and Speed Based on YOLOv10
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Applies YOLOv10 object detection to underwater images of marine benthic organisms (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish) from the URPC2020 dataset.

title: Plankton Concentration Model Consistent with Natural Events and Monitoring Series of Holographic Measurements
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: A submersible digital holographic camera records wild autochthonous zooplankton in the Barents Sea. Particles are reconstructed and automatically recognised to count zooplankton, and these counts feed the concentration time-series analysis.

title: Counting of Underwater Static Objects Through an Efficient Temporal Technique
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Primary study that detects, tracks and counts burrows (direct signs) of wild Nephrops norvegicus in underwater survey video using YOLOv3 and a spatial-temporal tracking algorithm.

title: An Improved YOLOv9s Algorithm for Underwater Object Detection
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv9s detector for underwater marine organisms (holothurian, scallop, echinus, starfish, fish, crabs, etc.) evaluated on the URPC and Brackish underwater image datasets; motivated by marine life monitoring.

title: Neural Network for Underwater Fish Image Segmentation Using an Enhanced Feature Pyramid Convolutional Architecture
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Proposes a CNN segmentation model for underwater fish images, evaluated on Fish4Knowledge and on an author-collected deep-sea dataset of free-ranging fish, crabs and shrimp.

title: Research on Method for Intelligent Recognition of Deep-Sea Biological Images Based on PSVG-YOLOv8n
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv8n detector for deep-sea organisms in video captured in situ by a manned submersible in the western Pacific; wild free-ranging marine animals.

title: Incremental Learning with Dynamic Adaptive Elastic Weight Consolidation for Adaptive, Scalable, and Generalizable User-Defined Behavior Recognition and Analysis of Cetacean and Pinniped Species
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: All analysed video comes from cameras mounted above dolphin pools at an ocean park, so only captive animals are studied.

title: An Improved YOLOv8 and OC-SORT Framework for Fish Counting
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Detection, tracking and counting of wild reef fish in underwater footage from a coral ecosystem cabled observatory.

title: LatentResNet: An Optimized Underwater Fish Classification Model with a Low Computational Cost
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Proposes a lightweight CNN for fish species classification and evaluates it on underwater images of wild reef fish from Fish4Knowledge (Taiwan).

title: EMR-YOLO: A Multi-Scale Benthic Organism Detection Algorithm for Degraded Underwater Visual Features and Computationally Constrained Environments
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Proposes a YOLO-based detector for marine benthic organisms (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish) in underwater images from the DUO dataset.

title: YOLOv11-MSE: A Multi-Scale Dilated Attention-Enhanced Lightweight Network for Efficient Real-Time Underwater Target Detection
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Proposes a YOLOv11-based detector evaluated on underwater images of benthic animals (sea cucumbers, sea urchins, scallops) captured under real open-sea conditions.

title: Influence of Bottom Substrate, Bottom Depth and Day/Night on In Situ Coloration Variability of Pomatoschistus minutus (Pallas, 1770) (Actinopterygii: Oxudercidae)
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Quantitative image analysis (colour standardization, RGB colour histograms, Earth Mover's Distance) of in situ underwater photographs of wild sand gobies.

title: UW-YOLO-Bio: A Real-Time Lightweight Detector for Underwater Biological Perception with Global and Regional Context Awareness
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Proposes a YOLOv8-based detector for underwater marine organisms (echinus, holothurian, starfish, scallop, jellyfish, corals, fish), evaluated on real underwater imagery. Part of the data comes from a marine ranch, so free-ranging and ranched animals are mixed.

title: F3M: A Frequency-Domain Feature Fusion Module for Robust Underwater Object Detection
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Proposes a CV detection module evaluated on aquarium soft corals (captive) and deep-sea ROV imagery that includes wild biological organisms (fish, crabs, starfish) as a detection class.

title: A Federated Learning Architecture for Bird Species Classification in Wetlands
venue: Journal of Sensor and Actuator Networks
reason: Federated learning with CNNs for classifying wild wetland bird species from video frames recorded in natural, uncontrolled environments in Spain.

title: Improving Zoo Exhibit Design: Why We Need Temporary Exhibit Design
venue: Journal of Zoological and Botanical Gardens
reason: Opinion paper on temporary zoo exhibit design; no image data or computer vision analysis, and no primary research.

title: Zero-Shot Elasmobranch Classification Informed by Domain Prior Knowledge
reason: Zero-shot CLIP-based species classification of real images of wild elasmobranchs (sharks and rays) photographed out of the water, in a fisheries/bycatch conservation context. The paper does not describe the animals as captive or farmed.

title: IchthyNet: An Ensemble Method for the Classification of In Situ Marine Zooplankton Shadowgraph Images
reason: CNN ensemble classifying in situ shadowgraph images of free-living marine zooplankton collected off Delaware Bay.

title: Using Tourist Diver Images to Estimate Coral Cover and Bleaching Prevalence in a Remote Indian Ocean Coral Reef System
reason: Applies an automated image classifier (CoralNet) to diver photographs of wild coral reefs to estimate coral cover and bleaching; corals are wild animals and the study is primary research.

title: Understanding the Influence of Image Enhancement on Underwater Object Detection: A Quantitative and Qualitative Study
reason: Study of how generic underwater image enhancement affects object detection on the general RUOD underwater benchmark (classes include divers); marine animals appear only as benchmark classes and wildlife monitoring is not the stated subject.

title: Mapping Coastal Marine Habitats Using UAV and Multispectral Satellite Imagery in the NEOM Region, Northern Red Sea
reason: The paper maps benthic habitat and geomorphic classes (coral/algae, seagrass, sand, rubble, rock) from Sentinel-2 pixels, using UAV imagery as ground truth. It is habitat mapping, not computer vision on animals.

title: Using Night-Time Drone-Acquired Thermal Imagery to Monitor Flying-Fox Productivity—A Proof of Concept
reason: Drone thermal imagery of wild flying-foxes is analysed only by manual counting in Fiji; no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: AI-Driven Real-Time Monitoring of Ground-Nesting Birds: A Case Study on Curlew Detection Using YOLOv10
reason: Primary study that trains a YOLOv10x detector and deploys it on real-time camera-trap images of wild nesting curlews in Wales; the training classes also include domestic animals (sheep, cattle, dog, cat, goat).

title: Real-Time UAV Surveys with the Modular Detection and Targeting System: Balancing Wide-Area Coverage and High-Resolution Precision in Wildlife Monitoring
reason: UAV thermal/RGB detection system validated in field trials on free-ranging gulls and on domestic cows; wild animals are part of the analysed data.

title: Advanced Insect Detection Network for UAV-Based Biodiversity Monitoring
reason: Proposes a CNN detector (AIDN) and evaluates it on images of free-ranging insects visiting flowers outdoors; primary research with a computer vision method on animal images.

title: An Improved Machine Learning-Based Method for Unsupervised Characterisation for Coral Reef Monitoring in Earth Observation Time-Series Data
reason: Satellite-based unsupervised mapping of coral reef areas into habitat zones (reef belt, shoals, channels) plus cloud masking and depth correction; habitat/benthic cover mapping rather than analysis of animals themselves.

title: Remote Sensing Reveals Multidecadal Trends in Coral Cover at Heron Reef, Australia
reason: Primary study that classifies satellite imagery and in situ photoquadrats to map cover of wild reef-building corals (animals) at Heron Reef. Borderline with habitat mapping (E-PLANT), but coral cover is the stated subject and the photoquadrat labels include coral genera.

title: Mapping Trails and Tracks in the Boreal Forest Using LiDAR and Convolutional Neural Networks
reason: CNN segmentation of LiDAR-derived terrain models to map wildlife trails (direct signs of wild ungulates) together with OHV tracks in the boreal forest; primary research.

title: Spatial Variation in Coral Diversity and Reef Complexity in the Galápagos: Insights from Underwater Photogrammetry and New Data Extraction Methods
reason: Underwater photogrammetry (Structure-from-Motion 3D reconstruction) of wild coral reefs in the Galápagos, with 3D annotation of coral genera and new structural complexity metrics computed from the reconstructions.

title: Mapping Waterbird Habitats with UAV-Derived 2D Orthomosaic Along Belgium’s Lieve Canal
reason: UAV orthomosaics of wild waterbirds are analysed, but birds were detected and counted by manual visual interpretation; the only automated image analysis (ISO clustering, SfM) is applied to land cover and orthomosaic generation, not to animals.

title: Integration of Convolutional Neural Networks and UAV-Derived DEM for the Automatic Classification of Benthic Habitats in Shallow Water Environments
reason: Benthic habitat/land-cover mapping from UAV orthomosaics (corals, sand, macroalgae, seagrass, rubble). The classes are habitat cover types, not animals as subjects, so the paper falls under habitat mapping only.

title: A Novel UAV- and AI-Based Remote Sensing Approach for Quantitative Monitoring of Jellyfish Populations: A Case Study of Acromitus flagellatus in Qinglan Port
reason: Primary study applying Mask R-CNN to UAV aerial images of wild jellyfish (Acromitus flagellatus) in coastal waters to detect, count and size individuals.

title: Semantic Segmentation of Coral Reefs Using Convolutional Neural Networks: A Case Study in Kiritimati, Kiribati
reason: Primary study training a CNN for semantic segmentation of benthic classes (living coral morphologies, dead coral, substrate) on diver-collected orthomosaics of wild coral reefs in Kiritimati.

title: Contextual-Semantic Interactive Perception Network for Small Object Detection in UAV Aerial Images
reason: Generic small-object detection method for UAV images, mainly persons and vehicles. The WAID wildlife dataset is only one of four benchmarks used to test the general detector; wildlife is not the stated subject.

title: Mapping Coral Reef Habitats with ICESat-2 and Satellite Imagery: A Novel Spectral Unmixing Approach Compared to Machine Learning
reason: Benthic habitat / land-cover mapping of a coral reef from PlanetScope multispectral pixels (live coral, dead coral, sand, land, deep water). This is pixel-level habitat classification, not computer vision on images of individual animals.

title: Bird Species Detection Net: Bird Species Detection Based on the Extraction of Local Details and Global Information Using a Dual-Feature Mixer
reason: Proposes a bird species detection network and evaluates it on surveillance images of wild birds at Poyang Lake plus two public bird datasets.

title: Identifying Novel Emotions and Wellbeing of Horses from Videos Through Unsupervised Learning
reason: Applies contrastive learning (MoCo) and YOLOv8 to video-derived images of free-living, wild/semi-feral horses to recognise emotional/behavioural states; primary research.

title: A Real-Time Fish Detection System for Partially Dewatered Fish to Support Selective Fish Passage
reason: Deep-learning fish detection on video of wild fish volitionally passing through a fish lift at a river weir, supplemented with a dataset of manually introduced and culled fish passed through an optical scanner.

title: Novelty Recognition: Fish Species Classification via Open-Set Recognition
reason: Image-based open-set species classification of wild-caught North Sea fish (fishery discards) on a vessel conveyor belt; wild, non-farmed animals, primary research.

title: BGLE-YOLO: A Lightweight Model for Underwater Bio-Detection
reason: Proposes a lightweight CNN detector for underwater marine organisms (holothurians, echinus, scallops, starfish, fish, etc.) in real-world underwater images from DUO and RUOD.

title: YOLOv8-TF: Transformer-Enhanced YOLOv8 for Underwater Fish Species Recognition with Class Imbalance Handling
reason: Proposes a transformer-enhanced YOLOv8 detector for recognising reef fish species in underwater survey imagery from the Gulf of Mexico (SEAMAPD21).

title: Wild Boars’ Selective Capture with IoT and Electronic Devices Solutions for Innovative, Sustainable and Ethical Management
reason: Field study using camera traps and an AI-based (YOLOv8) infrared camera to count wild boars and classify their age classes for selective capture of free-ranging wild boars.

title: SEANet: Semantic Enhancement and Amplification for Underwater Object Detection in Complex Visual Scenarios
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for marine organisms (fish, sea urchins, starfish, sea turtles, etc.) in real-world underwater images from public datasets.

title: MAS-YOLOv11: An Improved Underwater Object Detection Algorithm Based on YOLOv11
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv11 detector for underwater marine organisms (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish, fish, turtles, etc.) in real underwater images from the DUO and RUOD datasets.

title: BSE-YOLO: An Enhanced Lightweight Multi-Scale Underwater Object Detection Model
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for underwater marine animals (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish) in real underwater images from the URPC2020 and DUO datasets. The paper does not say whether the animals are wild or farmed. It describes the images as real underwater scenes, so they are coded as free-ranging marine animals.

title: Image Processing Algorithms Analysis for Roadside Wild Animal Detection
reason: Compares image processing and deep learning methods for detecting wild animals (deer, moose, wild boar) in thermal images from a roadside surveillance system.

title: An AI-Based Integrated Multi-Sensor System with Edge Computing for the Adaptive Management of Human–Wildlife Conflict
reason: Primary study that trains and field-tests a YOLOv8 detector on images of wild wolves, roe deer, red deer and bears as part of an edge-AI deterrence system.

title: Coral-YOLO: An Intelligent Optical Vision Sensing Framework for High-Fidelity Marine Habitat Monitoring and Forecasting
reason: Proposes an object detection and forecasting framework for in situ underwater images of wild coral colonies (corals are animals) to monitor bleaching and health state.

title: An Improved Lightweight Model for Protected Wildlife Detection in Camera Trap Images
reason: Proposes a lightweight YOLO11-based detector for protected wild animals in camera trap images collected in a national park.

title: Deep Learning for Wildlife Monitoring: Near-Infrared Bat Detection Using YOLO Frameworks
reason: Primary study training YOLO detectors on near-infrared images of wild bats recorded inside natural caves in Mexico.

title: LiDAR-Based Detection of Field Hamster (Cricetus cricetus) Burrows in Agricultural Fields
reason: Primary study that develops an automatic method to detect burrow entrances (direct signs) of the wild European hamster in UAV LiDAR point clouds from an agricultural field.

title: A Novel Application of Deep Learning–Based Estimation of Fish Abundance and Temporal Patterns in Agricultural Drainage Canals for Sustainable Ecosystem Monitoring
reason: Applies YOLOv8n to underwater time-lapse images of free-ranging fish in an agricultural drainage canal to detect and count them.

title: Improvement and Optimization of Underwater Image Target Detection Accuracy Based on YOLOv8
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv8s detector for marine organisms (sea urchin, sea cucumber, scallop, starfish) in underwater images, including a natural sea experiment from an ROV.

title: YOLO-AWK: A Model for Injurious Bird Detection in Complex Farmland Environments
reason: Proposes a YOLO-based detector for wild injurious bird species (mynas, sparrows, crows, etc.) in farmland images; the birds are free-ranging wild animals, not livestock.

title: Nu—A Marine Life Monitoring and Exploration Submarine System
reason: Paper develops an ROUV with a CV pipeline (YOLOv8 detection + ResNet50 classification) for fish species in marine monitoring, tested in part on videos shot in Kuwaiti waters.

title: Trends in Coral Reef Habitats over Two Decades: Lessons Learned from Nha Trang Bay Marine Protected Area, Vietnam
reason: Satellite-based benthic habitat mapping of coral reef cover (live coral vs rock/dead coral vs deep water) by pixel classification; it maps habitat/land cover, not individual animals.

title: Machine Learning in Paleontology: Automating Fossil Identification and Analysis
venue: Journal of Software Engineering and Simulation
reason: Classifies images of mammal skulls sourced from natural history museum collections (museum specimens), not wild free-ranging animals.

title: Integrated use of uav and information technologies to improve pacific salmon stock management
reason: Strategic roadmap for UAV salmon surveys. In the authors' 2025 surveys the fish were counted by eye on photomosaics, not with a neural network, so no computer vision was applied to the animal images in this paper.

title: Assessment pup production in the harp seal population of the White Sea in 2023 and 2024
reason: UAV aerial survey of wild harp seals on drifting ice in the White Sea; visible and infrared images processed with a YOLO v4 neural network to find and classify pups and adults for abundance estimation.

title: Application of unmanned aerial systems and artificial intelligence technology to assess the population of Baikal seals
reason: UAV aerial photographs of wild Baikal seals on Lake Baikal ice processed with a YOLOv4 neural network to detect and count animals for population assessment.

title: Intelligent Motion based Animal Repulsion System for Agriculture
venue: Journal of Artificial Intelligence and Capsule Networks
reason: The authors apply YOLOv5 to live camera images in farm field tests. The images show wild birds that raid crops, together with cows, which are livestock. Because part of the data shows free-ranging wild birds, the paper meets the inclusion rule.

title: Agro Guard Edge AI - Development of Sustainable IoT Framework for Wildlife Intrusion Detection
venue: Journal of Electrical Engineering and Automation
reason: Primary study applying a YOLOv8 detector on an ESP32-CAM to detect and classify wild animals intruding on farmland; the paper describes its training data as wildlife images from the Marudhamalai foothills.

title: A YOLOv8-based AI System for Real-Time Endemic Species Threat Detection and Response
reason: Applies a YOLOv8-based object detector to images of wild African animals (elephant, rhino, buffalo, zebra) plus poachers, for conservation threat detection.

title: AI-Driven Ultrasound Fencing
reason: Applies a fine-tuned YOLOv11 detector to camera images of wild animals (elephants, deer, wild boars, monkeys) entering farmland, as part of an ultrasonic deterrent system for human-wildlife conflict.

title: Image-free cross-species pose estimation via an ultra-low sampling rate single-pixel camera
reason: Generic single-pixel-camera pose estimation method evaluated on laboratory mice (Tri-Mouse), horses (Horse10) and humans; no wild free-ranging animals and wildlife is not the stated subject.

title: Reefshape: A System for the Efficient Collection and Automated Processing of Time-Series Underwater Photogrammetry Data for Benthic Habitat Monitoring
reason: Protocol for underwater SfM photogrammetry (3D reconstruction, orthomosaics) of wild coral reef benthos, applied to a time series in The Bahamas, with AI-assisted coral colony segmentation.

title: Measuring the Structure, Composition, and Change of Underwater Environments with Large-area Imaging
reason: Protocol for diver-based large-area imaging with Structure-from-Motion 3D reconstruction and image-based segmentation, community composition and density analysis of wild coral reef organisms (corals, sea urchins) in Hawaii.

title: Snapshot Japan 2023: the first camera trap dataset under a globally standardised protocol in Japan
reason: Data paper presenting a camera-trap image dataset of wild mammals and birds in Japan. A pre-trained AI model from Wildlife Insights was used to place bounding boxes on animals. Some domestic animals (goat, cat, dog) also appear.

title: Estimating relative density of an invasive ungulate in a biodiversity hotspot using drone-based thermal video surveys
reason: Thermal drone videos of wild invasive Javan deer were reviewed manually by human observers to count deer. No computer vision or automated image-analysis method was developed or applied.

title: A digitization workflow of dry-pinned collections of Lepidoptera
reason: Digitization workflow for dry-pinned museum specimens of Lepidoptera; no wild free-ranging animals, image analysis limited to barcode reading.

title: An expert system for honeybee species identification and information retrieval
reason: Applies computer vision (VGG16, SIFT+SVM) to classify honeybee species from iNaturalist photographs of bees on flowers and leaves in natural surroundings; primary research.

title: Birds Species Identification Using Deep Learning
venue: REST Journal on Data Analytics and Artificial Intelligence
reason: CNN-based classification of bird species from photographs; birds are the stated subject and are described as being in natural habitats, though the image source is not described.

title: Computer Vision for Biodiversity Monitoring: Improving Accuracy in Tracking Endangered Species of Wildlife in Impacted Ecosystems
venue: International Research Journal of Innovations in Engineering and Technology
reason: Presents itself as primary research proposing a multi-modal computer vision framework (YOLOv8 + DeepSORT, ViT, CNN-GNN) for detecting and tracking endangered wildlife and reports performance figures. However, it describes no dataset, study site or analysed animals, so the wild-animal data criterion rests on the stated application only.

title: Harnessing Computer Vision and Deep Learning to Monitor Coral Reef Health
reason: Applies YOLO object detection to underwater images of wild Red Sea coral reefs to assess health (healthy, bleached, dead).

title: Slow motion analysis of flight curves in Odonata
reason: Wild Odonata were filmed in the field with slow-motion cameras, but the flight kinematics were measured by hand and judged qualitatively frame by frame. No automated image analysis or computer vision method is used.

title: Wild Animal Deterrent System for Crop Protection: Leveraging TensorFlow IoT-based Acoustic Classification System
venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
reason: CNN image classification of 13 wild animal classes that intrude on farmland, for a crop-protection deterrent system. The paper only says the images were collected 'in controlled environments', so whether the animals shown are free-ranging is unclear; included because wild animals are the stated subject.

title: Creating Alert Messages Based on Wild Animal Activity Detection using Hybrid Deep Neural Network
venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
reason: The paper presents a hybrid VGG-19 + Bi-LSTM model for wild animal detection and activity-based alerts, and says it was tested on 40,000 images from three benchmark datasets with 25 classes. Inclusion is borderline: the text is incoherent, the background covers cloud-storage caching, and the only results section reports human face recognition. The animal datasets are never named or described, so the subject type cannot be confirmed.

title: AI-Powered Identification of Bird Species
venue: International Journal of Advanced Research in Science Communication and Technology
reason: Applies CNN image classification (fused with audio spectrogram CNN) to photographs of wild bird species from CUB-200-2011 for biodiversity monitoring.

title: AquaticCLIP: A Vision-Language Foundation Model for Underwater Scene Analysis
reason: Vision-language foundation model for underwater scenes, evaluated on classification, detection, segmentation and counting of marine animals, mostly free-ranging (field datasets like DeepFish, Brackish), with some aquarium and supermarket images.

title: Towards Application-Specific Evaluation of Vision Models: Case Studies in Ecology and Biology
reason: Evaluates vision models with application-specific metrics. One case study uses camera trap videos of wild chimpanzees; the other uses pigeons in an experimental arena.

title: Automated Detection of Salvin's Albatrosses: Improving Deep Learning Tools for Aerial Wildlife Surveys
reason: The paper applies deep learning object detection to drone images of wild Salvin's albatrosses breeding on the Bounty Islands.

title: Detection of trade in products derived from threatened species using machine learning and a smartphone
reason: Applies object detection to images of traded products from wild threatened species (elephant ivory/skin, pangolin scales/claws, tiger skins/bones) to monitor illegal wildlife trade. These are products, not live animals. It is included as a conservation application on wild species.

title: Domain-Adaptive Pretraining Improves Primate Behavior Recognition
reason: Video-based behavior recognition of great apes; PanAf has camera trap videos of wild chimpanzees and gorillas, and ChimpACT shows zoo chimpanzees.

title: MobileNetV2: Transfer Learning for Elephant Detection
reason: Applies CNN transfer learning to classify elephant vs other images from cameras in a tiger reserve (wild animals).

title: Quantitative imaging datasets of surface micro- to mesoplankton communities and microplastic across the Pacific and North Atlantic oceans from the Tara Pacific expedition
reason: Dataset paper of images of wild marine micro- and mesoplankton (including zooplankton such as copepods and cnidarians) sampled at sea. The images were segmented with ZooProcess and classified automatically in EcoTaxa, then checked by experts.

title: Long-term plankton and environmental monitoring dataset from the marine protected area of the Iroise Marine Natural Park (2010–2023) in the Iroise Sea, North Atlantic
reason: Data paper releasing ZooScan images of wild zooplankton sampled at sea in a marine protected area. The images were segmented automatically, then classified by supervised learning algorithms and validated by experts.

title: Automatic Extraction and Counting of Fish from Underwater Videos Using YOLO-Based Deep Learning Algorithms
venue: The international archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences/International archives of the photogrammetry, remote sensing and spatial information sciences
reason: Deep learning detection, classification, tracking and counting of wild fish in underwater videos from Sardinian Marine Protected Areas.

title: Web-Scale Collection of Video Data for 4D Animal Reconstruction
reason: Computer vision pipeline and benchmark for 4D reconstruction of quadruped animals from YouTube videos. The 23 categories include wild species (elephant, wolf, rhino, tiger, etc.) alongside domestic ones (cow, dog, cat, etc.).

title: BioCLIP 2: Emergent Properties from Scaling Hierarchical Contrastive Learning
reason: Biology foundation vision model (BioCLIP 2) trained on organism images including citizen-science and camera-trap images of wild animals, evaluated on wildlife species classification including LILA-BC camera traps; data also includes museum specimens and plants.

title: Integration of a Dual Hybrid Deep Convolutional Neural Network Framework for Insect Taxonomic Classification
reason: The paper proposes a CNN ensemble for classifying insect images at order, family and species level. The images come from online biodiversity sources (GBIF, BugGuide, Kaggle). The paper does not say whether the insects were wild, but these sources mainly hold observations of non-domestic insects, so the paper is included.

title: Enhanced CNN and SVM with Adaptive Modality Switching and Audio-Based Video Summarization for Real-Time Agricultural Intrusion Detection
venue: Journal of Information Systems Engineering & Management
reason: All reported evaluation is audio classification of animal and human sounds (MFCC features with CNN and SVM). The YOLOv4-Tiny video detector is only described, with no image data or results reported. Classes mix wild and domestic animals, and the application is farm intrusion.

title: Butterfly Species Classification Using CNN and VGG16
venue: Journal of Information Systems Engineering & Management
reason: Applies CNN and VGG16 to classify butterfly species from images. Butterflies are non-domestic animals, and the stated aim is biodiversity monitoring and conservation. The paper does not say where or how the images were taken.

title: CREATING ALERT MESSAGES BASED ON WILD ANIMAL ACTIVITY DETECTION USING HYBRID DEEP NEURAL NETWORKS
venue: American Journal of AI Cyber Computing Management
reason: Proposes a hybrid VGG-19 + Bi-LSTM model to detect wild animals, classify species and recognise activity in images and video frames from forest regions, in order to generate alert messages.

title: Automated Wildlife Conservation
venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
reason: Primary study building a deep-learning system to detect and classify wildlife species in images and video for wildlife monitoring; the image data are wildlife images from open sources, though the paper does not state whether the animals are free-ranging.

title: HydroLens: Pioneering Underwater Surveillance with IoT-powered Object Detection and Tracking using the Hybrid ResNeXt DenseNet Model
reason: Generic underwater surveillance object detection/tracking system (vessels, mines, plastic, infrastructure). Animals are mentioned only as examples, and wildlife is not the stated subject; no animal classes in the analysed data are reported.

title: Enhancing Underwater Object Recognition: Integrating Transfer Learning with Hybrid Optimization Techniques for Improved Detection Accuracy
reason: Generic underwater object recognition (rocks, marine life, debris, man-made structures); wildlife is not the stated subject, and no animal dataset or species is specified.

title: Improving Agricultural Safety Through Deep Neural Networks for Intrusion Monitoring
reason: Although the paper frames the work as wild boar segmentation, the only dataset it describes is the Farm Animals (Pigs) Detection Kaggle dataset of domestic pigs. The source of the tracking videos is not stated.

title: ZebraPoseNet: A Deep UNet-Based Framework with Attention Mechanisms for Animal Pose Estimation
venue: Highlights in Science Engineering and Technology
reason: Pose-estimation method evaluated on a custom zebra image dataset; the paper never states where or how the images were taken, so it does not establish that any of the data shows wild or free-ranging animals.

title: A Lightweight Sea Urchin Detection Algorithm Based on Improved Yolov8
venue: Highlights in Science Engineering and Technology
reason: Develops an improved YOLOv8 detector for sea urchins and starfish in underwater images of natural Yellow Sea seabed habitats.

title: SUD-YOLO:A Stable Underwater Target Detection Algorithm Based on Sampling Improved YOLOv11
reason: Proposes a YOLOv11-based detector evaluated on underwater image datasets of fish and benthic marine animals recorded in natural habitats.

title: Wildlife Detection System Using Deep Neural Networks
venue: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
reason: Primary study applying CNN models to camera-trap images of wild animals for animal/empty classification, detection and counting.

title: Intelligent Wildlife Detection and Alert System for Rural & Agricultural Regions
venue: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
reason: The paper proposes a wildlife detection and alert system for farms, but the only data it reports analysing is the Animal-10N dataset. The text does not state that any of the analysed images show wild or free-ranging animals, and no field data collection is described.

title: Advanced Surveillance Robot for Farm
venue: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
reason: Hardware design of a farm surveillance robot that only streams live video for manual monitoring and fires a sound deterrent; no image analysis is implemented or evaluated, and no animal image data are analysed.

title: AI-Based Animal Repellent System for Agricultural Fields Using YOLOv5 and OpenCV for Farmer Safeguard
venue: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
reason: Applies YOLOv5 object detection to camera images of wild animals (deer, wild boar, monkeys, elephants) intruding into agricultural fields, alongside cows; primary research on human-wildlife conflict.

title: Agroguard – Crop Protection Using AI to Detect and Deter Animals
venue: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
reason: Primary study applying YOLO object detection to a camera feed to detect wild animals (bear, deer, elephant, lion, tiger) for human-wildlife conflict mitigation and crop protection. The paper does not describe the image data it analysed, so the subject type is not reported.

title: Wild Guard: Solar Powered Animal Intrusion Detection and Alert System
venue: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
reason: Primary study applying a camera-based deep-learning detector to animals intruding on farmland in a field trial; the data include wild animals (wild boars) together with domestic ones (dogs, cows).

title: Intelligent Habitat Surveillance and Protection System
venue: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
reason: The paper presents a YOLOv8-based system for wildlife species detection, behaviour classification and anomaly detection and reports accuracy figures. It does not describe the images analysed, so the subject type is not reported; inclusion rests on the stated wildlife application.

title: Elephant Detection System Using AI
venue: INTERANTIONAL JOURNAL OF SCIENTIFIC RESEARCH IN ENGINEERING AND MANAGEMENT
reason: Primary study describing a YOLOv8/CNN-based system to detect wild elephants in CCTV video near forest borders and farms; the paper states both domestic and wild elephants are considered.

title: Creating Alert Message Based On Wild Animals Activity Detection Using Hybrid Deep Neural Network
venue: International Journal of Research Publication and Reviews
reason: Primary study that claims a hybrid CNN-LSTM model for detecting and classifying wild animal activity in images and video. The paper is internally inconsistent: its 'Proposed System' section describes house-price prediction, and the animal data are three unnamed benchmark datasets whose origin is not described, so the wild status rests only on the paper's own wording.

title: PFM-TurtleNet: Sea Turtle Species Identification Using a Parallel Fusion Module
venue: Electronic Letters on Computer Vision and Image Analysis
reason: Proposes a modified YOLOv10-nano detector for sea turtle species in underwater images taken in a marine park; the animals are wild and free-ranging.

title: Comparative Analysis of CNN Architectures (ResNet152V2, InceptionV3, and Xception) in Animal Species Classification
venue: Indonesian Journal of Interdisciplinary Research in Science and Technology
reason: Compares CNN architectures for animal species classification, motivated by biodiversity conservation. The Animals-10 dataset contains wild taxa (elephant, squirrel, butterfly, spider) together with domestic animals.

title: The Western Channel Observatory Automated Plankton Imaging and Classification System
reason: Short perspective/system description of a planned automated plankton imaging system (APICS) that is still being operationalized; it reports no image analysis, data or results.

title: Kraken: Open-Source Computer Vision for Underwater Fish Detection and Measurement
reason: The system is built for aquaculture (fish farming). The paper says it 'specifically targets real-world fish farming operations'. Its images come from websites and YouTube videos recorded in a controlled environment, and the paper never says the fish shown are wild or free-ranging.

title: Development and Evaluation of Advanced Morphological Algorithms for Automated Fish Measurement in Sustainable Fisheries
reason: Image-based morphological measurement of wild-caught fish from Madeira River basin fisheries (lab and fish markets); primary research using image analysis.

title: Innovative Bird Strike Mitigation Strategies: Integrating Drones and Cutting-Edge Technologies to Enhance Airport Safety
venue: International Journal of Aviation Aeronautics and Aerospace
reason: The paper reviews and qualitatively compares bird strike mitigation technologies (radar, cameras, drones, acoustics) and proposes a conceptual integrated framework. It does not analyse any image or video data and runs no computer vision experiments.

title: Source control of the blooming jellyfish: Mitigating threats for nuclear power plants
reason: Commentary/perspective on controlling jellyfish blooms at aquaculture pond sources; no computer vision or image analysis is performed.

title: Implementation of MobileNet V3 In Classifying Butterfly Species with Android and Cloud Based Application Development
venue: Journal of Artificial Intelligence and Engineering Applications (JAIEA)
reason: Applies a CNN (MobileNetV3-Large) to classify images of six butterfly species, part of which were obtained through direct field observations; primary research.

title: Optimizing Animal Classification through Convolutional Neural Networks
reason: Applies a CNN (ResNet50 transfer learning) to classify animal images for wildlife monitoring. The Animals-10 data mixes wild taxa (elephant, squirrel, butterfly) with domestic ones.

title: Freshwater Fish Detection Based on the Yolov8 Model
venue: International Journal of Computer Science and Information Technology
reason: Applies YOLOv8-based detection to underwater images of freshwater fish species for water-environment and biodiversity monitoring. The images come from the web and do not show farmed or captive fish specifically. The paper does not say whether the fish are wild.

title: Hybrid transformer-CNN model for precise Fish segmentation, localization, and species classification in aquaculture
venue: Journal of Integrated Science and Technology
reason: Proposes a hybrid transformer-CNN model for segmentation, localization and species classification of fish in underwater photos of 120 marine species from the FishNet dataset. The title mentions aquaculture, but the data is marine biodiversity imagery.

title: A HYBRID DEEP LEARNING FRAMEWORK FOR WILD ANIMAL DETECTION AND AUTOMATED ALERT MESSAGING
venue: International Journal of Engineering Research and Science & Technology
reason: Primary study proposing a deep learning pipeline (YOLOR detection plus hybrid VGG-19+Bi-LSTM classification) for wild animals, using camera trap and wild animal image datasets.

title: AUTOMATED DETECTION OF LARGE ANIMALS IN ROAD SCENE ENVIRONMENTS USING DEEP LEARNING
venue: International Journal of Interpreting Enigma Engineers.
reason: Applies deep object detectors to images of large animals (wild species such as bear, fox, zebra, elephant, giraffe together with domestic ones) for wildlife-vehicle collision avoidance in road scenes.

title: Improved detection and classification of cryptic ‘Phylloscopus’ warblers with integrated computer vision and deep learning method
reason: YOLOv5-based detection and species classification of cryptic Phylloscopus warblers from photographs taken in natural settings (own images plus citizen-science/web images); primary research.

title: Cataloguing of Animal Species Utilizing Convolutional Neural Networks
reason: Applies a CNN (ResNet152V2) to classify animal images from the Animal-10 dataset, with wildlife monitoring as the stated application. The paper names only two classes, a non-domestic one (elephant) and a domestic one (dog), and does not say whether the images show free-ranging animals, so inclusion is borderline.

title: Real-Time Wildlife Intrusion Detection System Using IoT and YOLOv8
venue: Journal of Smart Sensors and Computing
reason: Applies YOLOv8n detection to camera images of wild animals (monkeys, pigs) intruding into farms, with field testing.

title: Yolov8:A Cutting-Edge Approach To Prevent Wildlife Encroachment
reason: Applies YOLOv8 to CCTV video to detect wild animals (elephants, wild boars, deer) intruding farmland and trigger deterrents.

title: Advancing Environmental Monitoring: YOLO Algorithm For Real- Time Detection Of Greater One-Horned Rhinos
reason: Primary study evaluating YOLO object detectors on images of the Greater One-horned Rhino for wildlife monitoring; the paper does not state whether the photographed animals are wild or captive.

title: CREATING ALERT MESSAGES BASED ON WILD ANIMAL ACTIVITY DETECTION USING HYBRID DEEP NEURAL NETWORKS
venue: International Journal of Data Science and IoT Management System
reason: Proposes a hybrid VGG-19 + Bi-LSTM pipeline with YOLOR detection for detecting and classifying wild animals and their activity in forest camera images, evaluated on camera-trap and wild animal datasets.

title: Bridging the Data Gap: A Standardized Framework for Monitoring Coral Reefs in Remote Locations via the Recreational Cruising Fleet
reason: Describes a citizen-science protocol and web platform for coral reef video transects. The paper does no computer vision or automated image analysis; machine learning appears only as a possible future use.

title: Development and evaluation of a low-cost, automated camera trap for surveying bumble bee communities
reason: Primary study that builds a time-lapse camera trap and trains deep-learning object detection models to detect wild bumble bees visiting platform lures in a field.

title: Dynamic adjustment of feeding behavior depending on dominant-subordinate relationship in large-billed crows
reason: Captive large-billed crows housed in lab cages and tested in an indoor experimental apparatus; DeepLabCut tracking is applied only to laboratory set-up video, no free-ranging animals in data.

title: Gray bats spatially segregate when navigating flight with conspecifics in complex environments
reason: Stereoscopic infrared video of a wild gray bat colony is used for 3D tracking of flight trajectories, which then feed behavioural analysis and modelling.

title: Testing Photogrammetry in Assessing Health of Houston Toads (Bufo [=Anaxyrus] houstonensis)
reason: Image-based (photogrammetric) body measurement of wild-caught adult Houston toads and captive-bred juveniles, evaluated against caliper measurements for body condition assessment.

title: vassi – verifiable, automated scoring of social interactions in animal groups
reason: Behavioural classification software evaluated on laboratory mice (CALMS21) and captive cichlid groups filmed in experimental aquaria; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: ASBAR: an Animal Skeleton-Based Action Recognition framework. Recognizing great ape behaviors in the wild using pose estimation
reason: Pose estimation and skeleton-based behaviour recognition of wild chimpanzees and gorillas from camera-trap videos; the pose training data (OMC) also includes zoo and research-centre primates.

title: New approaches for capturing and estimating variation in complex animal color patterns from digital photographs: application to the Eastern Box Turtle (Terrapene carolina)
reason: Develops a threshold-based image segmentation pipeline for extracting colour patterns from photographs of Eastern box turtles, partly photographed wild in the field (12) plus museum specimens (43).

title: Multimodal system for recording individual-level behaviors in songbird groups
reason: Zebra finches bred in the authors' colony and recorded in a laboratory sound-isolation chamber; the study builds a multimodal recording system, with little image analysis.

title: Size and body condition drive the energetic cost of a baleen whale foraging in shallow habitat
reason: Drone video of wild PCFG gray whales is analysed only by manual review: behaviour annotation in BORIS, breath timing, and manual photogrammetry in MorphoMetriX. Energetics are then modelled statistically. No automated computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Bornean orangutan nest identification using computer vision and deep learning models to improve conservation strategies
reason: Deep learning image classification of UAV imagery for nests (direct signs) of wild Bornean orangutans in forest reserves in Sabah.

title: “Stripecode Guardians”: Individual Tiger Identification Using Machine Learning
reason: Individual identification of nine tigers photographed at a zoological park; the abstract mentions camera traps, but the dataset section states the images were manually captured at the zoo, so no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: High-throughput recognition of small invertebrates via computer vision
reason: Computer vision pipeline for individual identification of burying beetles collected from nature reserves for photographic capture-mark-recapture. Beetles were handled and photographed against neutral backgrounds; the paper does not state explicitly whether they were released or kept, so the wild status rests on the collection statement.

title: A study on edge devices for image classification of the Tasmanian devil ( Sarcophilus harrisii ) for vaccine delivery
reason: CNN image classification of Tasmanian devils vs. other species on trail camera images from wildlife monitoring in Tasmania, evaluated for deployment on edge devices. The non-devil class includes some cattle images, so subject_type is mixed.

title: Machine‐assisted image analysis facilitates conservation of iconic elasmobranchs
reason: Deep-learning photo-ID pipeline (segmentation plus metric learning) applied to angler-contributed photographs of wild-caught flapper skate for individual recognition.

title: Counting elephants from space: An analytic framework for wildlife abundance surveys in heterogeneous terrain using satellites and AI
reason: Primary study training a YOLO11 detector on very high-resolution satellite imagery to detect and count free-roaming African savanna elephants in northern Botswana, validated against a synchronous aerial count.

title: Advancing wildlife image analysis: A Graph Attention Contrastive Learning approach for region‐specific mammal classification
reason: Develops a deep learning classification model (GACL) for camera-trap images of wild mammals in South Korea; primary research on free-ranging wildlife.

title: Testing the transferability of image‐based automated insect detection under different light conditions
venue: Approaches in Entomology Methods Philosophies and Ethics
reason: Primary study training and evaluating an object detection model on time-lapse images of wild insects caught on sticky sheets at field sites under different light conditions.

title: CapuchinAI 1.0: Development of a Machine Learning‐Based Touchscreen Paradigm to Test Cognition in Wild Capuchins
reason: Develops and deploys a YOLO-based facial recognition/detection model on video of habituated wild white-faced capuchins at a field site, integrated into a touchscreen cognitive testing station.

title: Positional Behavior in Zoo‐Housed Bonobos ( Pan paniscus )
reason: Behavioural study of zoo-housed bonobos. The video was coded by hand, frame by frame, in ELAN by one observer, and no computer vision method is used. The animals are also captive only.

title: A New Experimental Protocol for Assessing Hominoid Assisted Arboreal Bipedalism
reason: Experimental protocol recording video of six captive zoo chimpanzees in an indoor enclosure; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed. Joint positions were digitized by hand rather than by an automated computer vision method.

title: ACFD ‐Net: An Attention‐Guided Cosine‐Similarity Feature Distillation Framework for Real‐Time Underwater Object Detection
venue: Concurrency and Computation Practice and Experience
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for underwater benthic organisms (starfish, echinus, scallop, holothurian) in real underwater images, motivated by marine ecological monitoring.

title: A Machine Learning Application to Camera-Traps: Robust Species Interactions Datasets for Analysis of Mutualistic Networks
reason: Applies MegaDetector to camera-trap videos of wild frugivores visiting fruiting plants in Doñana National Park and evaluates the information loss of the CV step.

title: Automated Detection and Monitoring of Ground-Nesting Bee Nests Using Drone Imagery and Deep Learning
reason: Deep learning object detection on drone imagery of nest tumuli (direct signs) of a wild ground-nesting bee aggregation in the field.

title: Drone Infrared Thermography for Detecting Skin Thermal Anomalies in Bottlenose Dolphins: Preliminary Insights
reason: Drone thermal imaging of bottlenose dolphins kept at Sea World (under human care); no wild animals in the analysed data.

title: Environmental Factors and Co‐Occurrence Patterns Influence Dorsal Brightness in Two Jumping Mice Species in the Western United States
reason: Image-based colour quantification and LDA species assignment done only on photographs of museum skins, not on live free-ranging animals; museum specimens are excluded under E-CAPTIVE.

title: Uncovering Hidden Predators: Thermal Drone Detection of Antarctic Fur Seals in Tussac Grass at South Georgia
reason: Thermal and RGB drone survey of wild Antarctic fur seals, but seals were geotagged and counted manually in GIS; no computer vision method is applied to the animal imagery (only photogrammetric orthomosaic generation).

title: Individual Escape Flight Performance Is Repeatable and Differs Between Long‐Tailed Finch ( Poephila acuticauda ) Subspecies but Not as Predicted by Asymmetrical Introgression
reason: Video-based 3D flight tracking (Argus) of wild-derived long-tailed finches that are kept in university aviaries and cages; all filmed animals are captive, and flights were recorded in an enclosed aviary.

title: Nocturnal at Noon? Addressing False Positives in Activity Pattern Data
reason: The method corrects false positives in diel activity estimates. The only empirical data are BirdNET-labelled acoustic recordings, so no images or video are analysed.

title: Leveraging Co‐Occurrence to Improve Deep Learning Photo‐Identification in Social Animals
reason: Primary study that post-processes deep learning photo-identification outputs on photographs of a wild killer whale population, using encounter co-occurrence to improve individual identification.

title: Combining Artificial Intelligence and Local Ecological Knowledge to Document the Largest Ever‐Counted Cape Buffalo Mega‐Herd
reason: Primary study applying deep-learning detection and tracking to drone video of a wild Cape buffalo herd in Botswana to count individuals.

title: Facial Recognition Analyses Reveal Social Networks of Co‐Occurrence at Harbor Seal Haul‐Out Sites
reason: Applies facial recognition software (SealNet 2.0) to photographs of wild harbor seals at haul-out sites to identify individuals and build co-occurrence networks.

title: Toward Precision Biodiversity Detection: An Edge‐Deployable Framework for Mitigating Data Redundancy
reason: Proposes a lightweight YOLO-based detector evaluated on camera-trap images of wild animals (NTLNP also contains two domesticated species), plus a generic benchmark.

title: Eyespots in Automeris Moths Mimic Sympatric Owl Species (Lepidoptera: Saturniidae)
reason: Applies CNN segmentation, classification and saliency mapping to iNaturalist photographs of wild Automeris moths and owls in natural poses to test eyespot mimicry.

title: Confidence Thresholds: Towards an Automated Workflow for Unmarked Wildlife Population Modelling With Camera Trap Data
reason: Primary study that fine-tunes a deep learning ensemble to detect and classify fauna in camera trap images of free-ranging macropods in Tasmania and links output to abundance modelling; classes also include domestic animals (cattle, sheep, cat) and persons.

title: Deep Learning‐Based Monitoring of European Hamster Activity
reason: A YOLOv8n detector is applied to camera-trap videos of reintroduced, free-living European hamsters in fenced agricultural reintroduction areas to derive activity patterns.

title: Measuring Bird Morphology From Field Photographs
reason: Image-based photogrammetric estimation (pinhole camera model) of morphometric traits of wild birds photographed in the field, plus validation on mounted museum specimens.

title: Estimating Three‐Dimensional Posture to Correct Drone‐Based Measurements of Free‐Swimming Marine Mammals: An Application to Dugongs in Shallow Waters
reason: Develops a drone-based photogrammetric method to reconstruct the 3D posture of free-swimming wild dugongs and correct their body measurements.

title: EverWatch airborne bird imagery dataset for detection and classification of Everglades wading birds.
reason: Data paper providing UAS airborne imagery with detection and species labels of wild wading birds in the Florida Everglades for computer vision models.

title: Joint Angular Excursions and Angular Range Utilization During Stance‐Phase Locomotion in Terrestrial Mammals: A Comparative Morphofunctional Data Set
venue: Journal of Experimental Zoology Part A Ecological and Integrative Physiology
reason: Joint angles were digitized manually, frame by frame, with Tracker software from online videos and published sources. No computer vision method is developed or applied, and the paper does not say whether the animals filmed were wild or captive.

title: Spatial Resolution Impact Assessment for Long‐Term Population Monitoring of Adélie Penguin Guano
venue: New Zealand Journal of Geology and Geophysics
reason: Analyses UAV and satellite imagery of guano stains and nests of a wild Adélie penguin colony to detect colony area and estimate abundance.

title: A design‐based framework for estimating wildlife density from uncrewed aerial systems imagery
reason: Primary study applying deep learning detection (YOLOv5) to UAS imagery of free-ranging overwintering waterfowl and cranes at a wildlife refuge to estimate density and abundance.

title: Seafloor‐image analysis techniques to highlight the role of substrate as a driver of benthic community structure in Arctic cold seep areas
reason: ROV video of wild Arctic benthic fauna turned into SfM orthomosaics and DEMs. Epibenthic fauna individuals were annotated and counted on the orthomosaics, and OBIA was used to classify substrate. The study analyses how substrate relates to benthic community structure.

title: Diel dynamics of zooplankton fecal pellet flux revealed by integrated in situ imaging observations and modeling
reason: In situ imaging (UVP5, GelCam) of free-living marine zooplankton and their fecal pellets in the open ocean, with segmentation and Random Forest classification of image ROIs.

title: Deep learning–assisted coral morphology cover across 742 sites on the Great Barrier Reef (2022–2025): A Great Reef Census citizen science dataset
reason: Data article applying a deep learning segmentation model to underwater images of wild reef corals (animals) on the Great Barrier Reef to derive coral morphology cover.

title: PNNL ‐ TUNAMELT : Toward automating the detection of interactions with marine energy devices using acoustic camera sensors
reason: Image-based detection pipeline on imaging-sonar video of wild marine life (fish) near a tidal turbine in Cobscook Bay; releases a labeled dataset and method.

title: An in situ stereo‐imaging system for characterizing behavior, distributions, and aggregations of meso‐ and macro‐zooplankton in diverse aquatic environments
reason: Primary methods paper presenting an in situ stereo-imaging system and image-processing pipeline (disparity, depth, segmentation, 3D tracking) applied to free-ranging ctenophores and a fish school in an estuary.

title: A machine learning assisted method for rapidly annotating benthic megafauna in large volumes of marine imagery
reason: Develops a machine-learning-assisted object detection annotation method on images of wild deep-sea benthic megafauna from a cabled observatory camera.

title: Optimizing stereo‐baited remote underwater video sampling efficiency in turbid waters through horizontal field of view adjustments
reason: Stereo-video calibration and measurement accuracy trials done in a swimming pool on reference scale-bar targets. No animal images were analysed; field validation with real fish is left for future work.

title: Deep learning to monitor the deep sea: a category‐oriented automated framework for quantifying animal behavior at hydrothermal vents
reason: Develops a detection and tracking pipeline (YOLOv8 with category-specific trackers) on in situ observatory video of wild deep-sea hydrothermal vent fauna (mussels, shrimps, crabs).

title: Method‐dependent differences in zooplankton abundance and size metrics: Microscopy vs. ZooScan
reason: Image-based analysis (ZooScan scanning, ZooProcess segmentation, EcoTaxa random forest classification) of wild zooplankton collected by net in the East China Sea, compared with microscopy for abundance and size metrics.

title: MusselFinder : Automated dreissenid mussel density estimation via robotic benthic imaging
reason: Deep learning segmentation of wild invasive dreissenid mussels in AUV-collected benthic images from Lake Michigan for density estimation.

title: Deep Learning Pipeline for the Identification of Ground Beetles (Carabidae) in New Zealand
reason: All images are of pinned museum specimens from the New Zealand Arthropod Collection photographed in a controlled set-up; no images of free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: LMBC: Low‐Power Marine Benthos Counting Framework for Underwater Robotic Real‐Time Applications
reason: Proposes a CV detection-tracking-counting framework for marine benthos (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish) in underwater video, including field ROV footage from a shallow-sea environment, for aquaculture and ecological monitoring. The paper does not say the animals are farmed, so they are coded as free-ranging.

title: Applying computer vision to accelerate monitoring and analysis of bird incubation behaviors: a case study using common eider nest camera footage
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Primary study applying a YOLOv7 + StrongSORT detection and tracking pipeline to time-lapse nest camera footage of wild nesting common eiders on Alaskan barrier islands.

title: Using time-series remote sensing to identify and track individual bird nests at large scales
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Primary study applying a CNN bird detector and rule-based time-series matching to UAS imagery of wild wading bird colonies in the Everglades to detect nests.

title: Automated object detection based on YOLOv11 for monitoring benthic population dynamics: A new approach combining photogrammetry and open‐source GIS tools applied to sea cucumbers
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Applies YOLOv11 object detection to underwater photogrammetric orthomosaics to detect and count wild sea cucumbers in Mediterranean seabeds.

title: Deep learning‐based ecological analysis of camera trap images is impacted by training data quality and quantity
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Primary study training CNN species classifiers on camera trap images of wild mammals from Kenya and Nepal and evaluating effects on ecological metrics; data also contain domestic species, which were removed for the final ecological analyses.

title: From snapshots to continuous estimates: Augmenting citizen science with computer vision for fish monitoring
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Primary study applying deep-learning detection, tracking and counting to underwater video of wild migrating river herring in three Massachusetts rivers.

title: Lacking data? No worries! How synthetic images can alleviate image scarcity in wildlife surveys: A case study with muskox ( Ovibos moschatus )
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Trains and evaluates a CNN object detector on aerial images of muskoxen, including wild free-ranging populations surveyed by helicopter and plane, together with drone images of captive zoo animals and synthetic images.

title: Big Bird: A global dataset of birds in drone imagery annotated to species level
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Primary study presenting a drone image dataset of free-ranging wild birds labelled to species level, with a trained detection and classification model.

title: Semi‐automated seal detection on the Western Antarctic Peninsula: an unsupervised machine learning approach for detecting ice seals in aerial survey data
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Primary study that develops a semi-automated image analysis pipeline (thresholding plus hierarchical clustering) to detect wild ice seals in aerial survey imagery from the Western Antarctic Peninsula.

title: Historical remote sensing highlights long‐term persistence of Emperor Penguin ( Aptenodytes forsteri ) colonies
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Guano stains of wild emperor penguin colonies are found and measured in satellite imagery by manual visual interpretation and manual tracing; no computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated. The statistics (GAM, Spearman correlation) operate on the manually measured areas, not on images.

title: Deep learning‐based super‐resolution reconstruction and improved YOLOv9 for efficient benthos detection: a case study at Lake Hamana, Japan
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Primary study applying super-resolution and an improved YOLOv9 detector to drone imagery of wild hermit crabs on a mudflat at Lake Hamana.

title: Accounting for animal movement during aerial imaging surveys
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Primary study using CNN detections on drone imagery of wild overwintering waterbirds to assess count error and platform bias.

title: Ground-based robotic remote sensing for standardized biodiversity monitoring in coastal habitats
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Primary study that trains YOLOv11 detection/instance-segmentation models on field images of wild Brithys crini moth larvae on coastal dunes, taken by citizens and a quadruped robot.

title: Inferring Brown Bear Hair Snare Interactions by Automatically Detecting Bipedalism on Camera Trap Images Using Pose Estimation and a Multilayer Perceptron
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Primary study developing a pose estimation and posture classification method on camera trap images of wild brown bears in the Pyrenees.

title: Tracking Wintertime Behaviour of Emperor Penguins Using High‐Resolution Synthetic Aperture Radar Imagery
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Wild emperor penguin huddles are studied in SAR satellite imagery, but all detection and measurement was done by manual visual interpretation and delineation in ArcGIS Pro. No computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Development and Evaluation of a Low‐Cost, Semi‐Automated Camera Trap for Surveying Bumble Bee Communities
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Primary study that builds a camera trap and trains deep-learning detection models on images of wild, free-flying bumble bees visiting lure platforms in a field.

title: Efficient and Accurate Spatio-Temporal Population Monitoring of Mobile Animals Using Drones and Computer Vision
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Develops computer vision counting methods on drone imagery of wild spawning sockeye salmon in Alaska ponds.

title: A Tracking‐By‐Detection Framework to Automatically Count Rare and Elusive Megafauna in Aerial Video Surveys
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Primary study developing a YOLO-based tracking-by-detection framework to count wild dugongs in aerial video surveys.

title: Discovery and Fine‐Scale Mapping of Hadal Xenophyophore Habitat in the Nova Canton Trough, Central Pacific Ocean
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Applies SfM photogrammetry and semi-automated DEM-based delineation to submersible video of wild deep-sea benthic organisms (xenophyophores) to detect and count them, and links the results to co-occurring metazoan fauna annotated from the same video.

title: Improving Demographics and Conservation of Fishes Through Multi‐Frame Individual Distinctions by Size ( MIDS )
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Fish in stereo-video are measured manually in EventMeasure; the proposed MIDS method is a statistical filter on length measurements and precision errors, not automated image analysis.

title: High‐Resolution Satellite Imagery Reveals Landscape‐Scale Benthic Habitat Changes in a Turbid Coral Reef
venue: Remote Sensing in Ecology and Conservation
reason: Primary study classifying satellite imagery (and CoralNet-annotated underwater photo-quadrats) of a wild reef into benthic classes that include coral- and zoanthid-dominated cover, i.e. sessile wild animals. Borderline with E-PLANT because the framing is benthic habitat mapping, but coral and zoanthid classes are animal targets.

title: Evaluating machine learning models for multi‐species wildlife detection and identification on remote sensed nadir imagery in South African savanna
reason: Primary study evaluating deep-learning detectors on UAV nadir imagery of non-domestic African ungulates in savanna for aerial census. The animals were kept in large fenced camps (18-81 ha) on game-breeding farms, so the wild/free-ranging status is borderline; coded as included because they are non-domestic wildlife in natural savanna habitat.

title: Improving manual tagging of camera trap videos for wildlife studies: a visual assistance tool applied to the endangered huillin Lontra provocax
reason: Software with frame-differencing movement masks applied to camera trap videos of wild endangered otters and other wildlife in a national park (some domestic dogs/cats also recorded).

title: Indirect effects of hunting on wildlife
reason: This is an editorial introducing a special issue on the indirect effects of hunting on wildlife. It contains no primary computer vision research and analyses no images.

title: Field evaluation of artificial intelligence early warning for bird depredation at carp ponds
reason: Field pilot applying a multimodal generative model and a YOLO11 baseline to surveillance-camera screenshots to classify presence of free-ranging piscivorous birds at a carp farm; the birds, not the farmed fish, are the subject.

title: Behavioral Patterns of Zoo‐housed Lowland ( Tapirus terrestris ) and Malayan tapirs ( Tapirus indicus ), With a Focus on Sleeping Behavior
reason: Behaviour of zoo-housed tapirs was coded manually from video in BORIS and analysed statistically. No automated computer vision was used, and all animals were captive.

title: Effects of Density and Food Availability on the Growth of Captive‐Reared Eastern Hellbenders
reason: Husbandry experiment on growth of captive-reared hellbenders; photographs used only for manual spot-pattern identification, no computer vision analysis. Animals are also captive only.

title: Benchmark on Monocular Metric Depth Estimation in Wildlife Setting
reason: Benchmark of monocular depth estimation on camera trap images of people holding ChARUCO calibration patterns; no animals appear in the analysed data.

title: Nearest-Class Mean and Logits Agreement for Wildlife Open-Set Recognition
venue: Communications in Computer and Information Science
reason: Proposes a post-processing open-set recognition method evaluated on camera-trap crops of African and Swedish wildlife; the Swedish class list also contains domestic classes (cattle, dog, horse, livestock).

title: A Dual-Pipeline Approach for Underwater Fish Detection and Segmentation: Integrating YOLOv8 and RF-DETR with SAM 2.1
venue: Lecture notes in networks and systems
reason: Applies CV detection and segmentation to underwater fish images. The paper names marine biology as an application. It does not say where the images come from or whether the fish are wild or farmed.

title: Real-Time Tiger Intrusion Detection System Using Machine Learning and IoT
venue: Communications in Computer and Information Science
reason: Applies a MobileNet CNN to detect tigers in images for a human-wildlife conflict alert system; training data includes Serengeti wildlife images. The paper does not state whether the COCO and Image-Net images show wild or captive animals.

title: GeloVec: Higher Dimensional Geometric Smoothing for Coherent Visual Feature Extraction in Image Segmentation
reason: Generic semantic segmentation method. Birds appear only through the CUB-200-2011 benchmark, used next to non-animal datasets (LSDSC, flood scenes). Wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Coral Reef Health Monitoring Using AI and Remote Sensing
venue: Lecture notes in networks and systems
reason: Applies deep learning image classification (MobileNetV2) to images of wild coral reefs to classify coral health (healthy, bleached, dead).

title: Smart Animal Intrusion Detection System for Safeguarding Farm Lands
venue: Lecture notes in networks and systems
reason: Farm intrusion detection prototype tested on a miniature farm testbed using placards with pictures of domestic animals (dog, cow); YOLOv3 trained on COCO-format animal data. No wild or free-ranging animals appear in the analysed images.

title: A Novel Deep Learning Framework for Automated Identification and Classification of Indian Bird Species Using Convolutional Neural Networks
venue: Lecture notes in networks and systems
