reason: Proposes a CNN framework that classifies Indian bird species from images. The birds are wild, non-domestic animals.

title: Cross-Modal Learning for Plankton Recognition
reason: The organisms classified are phytoplankton (algae, dinoflagellates, cyanobacteria), not animals. They were imaged with a CytoSense imaging flow cytometer, partly from lab cultures and partly in situ in the Baltic Sea. No wild animals are the subject.

title: Deep in the Jungle: Towards Automating Chimpanzee Population Estimation
reason: Applies monocular depth estimation, detection and segmentation to camera trap videos of a wild chimpanzee population to estimate distances, density and abundance.

title: Simple Deep Feature Fusion Learning with Efficient Hard Mining Triplet Loss for Improved Mosquito Classification
venue: Lecture notes in networks and systems
reason: Mosquito specimens (larvae and adults) from a laboratory and field surveys imaged with a digital microscope in a laboratory set-up for vector surveillance; no images of free-ranging animals in their environment.

title: A Comprehensive Benchmarking of Explainable AI Techniques on Camel Type Dataset
venue: Lecture notes in networks and systems
reason: Benchmarks XAI methods on YOLO classifiers of racing vs non-racing camels photographed on two farms, so the animals are livestock, not wild.

title: WildProp: Visual Estimation of Wildlife Body Proportions at Scale
reason: Training-free computer vision framework (retrieval, keypoint matching) that estimates body-proportion distributions of wild animals from iNaturalist photographs captured in the wild.

title: HieDG: A Hierarchical Discrete Geometry-Guided Framework for Multi-Animal Tracking
reason: Proposes a computer vision multi-animal tracking method evaluated on video benchmarks that include wild animals (AnimalTrack, BuckTales wild antelopes) together with some domestic animals.

title: Forecasting Motion in the Wild
reason: Proposes a diffusion transformer that forecasts animal motion as point trajectories from unconstrained in-the-wild animal video (filtered MammalNet), and releases the MammalMotion dataset. The data spans the whole MammalNet taxonomy, including wild mammals (lions, tigers, leopards, polar bear, caribou) together with domestic ones (alpaca, dog, hamster).

title: Lessons and Open Questions from a Unified Study of Camera-Trap Species Recognition Over Time
reason: Primary study that builds a camera-trap benchmark (StreamTrap) from wildlife camera-trap datasets and evaluates foundation-model species classification and adaptation over time.

title: Bootstrapping Articulated 3D Reconstruction from 2D Image Collections
reason: Proposes a computer vision method for single-image articulated 3D reconstruction of animals, trained and evaluated partly on in-the-wild images of chimpanzees and elephants, plus domestic horses, cows and sheep.

title: WildDepth: A Multimodal Dataset for 3D Wildlife Perception and Depth Estimation
reason: Multimodal RGB-LiDAR dataset and benchmarks of wild animals in Kgalagadi and Bubye Valley, plus safari park and some domestic animals; depth estimation, behaviour recognition and 3D reconstruction.

title: Prompting-MammAlps: Fine-Grained Text-to-Video Retrieval for Camera-Trap Data
reason: Introduces a text-to-video retrieval benchmark and a video transformer method on camera-trap videos of wild mammals recorded in the Swiss National Park.

title: Towards Benchmarking Western Bluebird Detection in the Wild
reason: Introduces a benchmark dataset and evaluates detection and segmentation models on fixed-camera video frames of wild Western bluebirds breeding in nest boxes under natural conditions.

title: A Novel Token-Based Classification Module for Fine-Grained Image Recognition Tasks
reason: Generic fine-grained recognition module evaluated on CUB-200-2011 as a benchmark; wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Detection of Submerged Objects Through Enhanced Imaging and Vision Transformer
reason: Generic underwater object detection on the EUVP image dataset. The text never says the detected objects are animals, and wildlife is not the stated subject; marine research is listed only as one possible application.

title: Sustainable Dual-Function Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV) System for Crop Detection and Animal Intrusion Monitoring Using YOLO v8
reason: UAV-based agricultural monitoring detecting cattle intrusion and crop pests with YOLOv8; no wild animals are the subject.

title: Airship Formations for Animal Motion Capture and Behavior Analysis
reason: Primary study presenting an airship system with on-board CNN detection and visual tracking of wild Przewalski's horses in a national park.

title: Transformer-based end-to-end multiple object fast-tracking model for golden monkeys
reason: Proposes a Transformer-based end-to-end multi-object tracker for golden monkeys and evaluates it on video recorded in wild habitats.

title: T-PhISH-Net: temporally consistent underwater image enhancement via a transformer-based extension of PhISH-Net
reason: Generic underwater video enhancement method evaluated with no-reference image quality metrics; animals are not the subject of the analysis and no animal-specific task is performed.

title: Detecting abyssal megabenthos in the Great Atlantic Sargassum Belt – Comparing quantitative assessments via manually processed OFOS-videos with AUV-images utilising deep learning models
reason: Primary study applying a YOLOv5 detection model to AUV seafloor images of wild abyssal megafauna and comparing with manually processed OFOS video.

title: HideAndSeg: an AI-driven approach to monitoring benthic octopuses in the wild
reason: Develops a computer vision pipeline (SAM2 + YOLOv11) to segment wild octopuses in underwater videos filmed in their natural habitat.

title: Distance defines us: determining dolphin group membership through analysis of inter-individual distances
reason: Drone video of wild Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins is analysed with ML-based object detection to locate individuals and measure the distances between them.

title: Inferring the rules of social interaction in moving Tibetan antelopes
reason: Drone video of wild Tibetan antelope groups is processed with automated detection/tracking (TrackMate) and optical-flow camera motion compensation to derive trajectories for collective movement analysis.

title: Detecting Antarctic flying seabird breeding occupancy with satellite remote sensing: opportunities and limitations
reason: Satellite imagery of wild Antarctic seabird colonies (guano stains) is classified by a human analyst through visual inspection; no computer vision or automated image analysis method is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: Drone survey reveals a severe chinstrap penguin decline and a novel gentoo colony in an Antarctic specially protected area
reason: Drone imagery of wild penguin and shag colonies, but nests were counted manually on orthomosaics; the only automated image processing is photogrammetric orthomosaic generation, with no computer vision analysis of animals.

title: Beyond the uniform: uncovering structural complexity within Adélie penguin colonies
reason: Ecological study of wild Adélie penguin colonies using drone DEMs/orthomosaics, but nests were identified manually and analysis is Voronoi tessellation and GAMMs; no computer vision analysis of animals in images.

title: Energetic requirements and prey consumption of five different-sized cetaceans in Icelandic waters
reason: Applies UAV photogrammetry (image-based morphometric measurement) to aerial video of wild free-ranging cetaceans in Iceland to estimate body size, condition and volume, which then feed into bioenergetic modelling.

title: Streamlining ringed seal (Pusa hispida) abundance estimation through Computer Vision models
reason: Primary study training a YOLOv8 object detector on UAS aerial imagery of wild ringed seals on sea ice in Svalbard.

title: Tracking morphological development in stony corals
reason: Applies image-based 3D photogrammetry to reconstruct and quantify the morphology of wild stony coral colonies in situ.

title: Tipping the balance: reef community shifts after a regional urchin population collapse
reason: Applies SfM photogrammetry and CoralNet CNN classification to underwater images of wild reef benthic communities (corals, sponges), with sea urchins assessed from the orthomosaics.

title: A novel biometric approach for non-invasive monitoring of octocoral forests using image analysis
reason: Primary study developing an image-analysis morphometric method (ImageJ measurement, threshold segmentation) on underwater video frames and photographs of wild octocoral colonies (animals) in a marine protected area.

title: Tropical Eastern Pacific coral morphometrics: a toolkit for coral studies
reason: Applies image-based 3D reconstruction (structure-from-motion photogrammetry) and structured-light scanning to stony corals. The corals are in situ colonies at a reef restoration site plus skeletons from collections, so part of the data shows free-ranging animals.

title: Enhanced feature fusion for precise small object detection in complex environments
reason: Proposes a YOLOv9-based small-object detector evaluated on images of free-ranging insects visiting flowers (green roof webcams, field camera traps).

title: Reptile species classification using Swin Transformers for biodiversity conservation in the Canary Islands
reason: Primary study applying Swin Transformer image classification to photographs of endemic and invasive reptiles, sourced from iNaturalist and from specimens documented in the Canary Islands.

title: Sexual dimorphism and allometry of the skull in the sand-swimming skink, Scincus scincus (LINNAEUS, 1758): a three-dimensional geometric morphometric analysis
reason: Photogrammetric 3D reconstruction of macerated skull specimens imaged on a turntable in a lab; no images of living free-ranging animals, comparable to museum specimen studies.

title: WL-YOLOv11: enhanced YOLOv11 for wildlife detection and counting in complex environments
reason: Proposes a modified YOLOv11 detector and counting procedure for wild animals in drone-captured imagery of their natural habitat.

title: Enhancing fish classification based on transfer learning and DCNN with Fish Species Identification Algorithm (FSIA)
reason: Fish species classification on a Kaggle image dataset framed around aquaculture and smart fishing. The paper does not state how or where the images were taken and itself says the data are controlled rather than from natural aquatic habitats, so wild or free-ranging animals cannot be established from the text.

title: Enhancing underwater object detection through hybrid sparse-annotation optimization
reason: Proposes a CV detection framework for underwater images of benthic organisms (DUO) and hydroids recorded in marine field settings for ecological monitoring.

title: Enhanced underwater object detection via multi-scale attention and adaptive feature fusion
reason: Proposes a DEIM-based detector for underwater organisms (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish and others) in natural underwater scenes, using public underwater datasets.

title: Multi-domain collaborative feature fusion network for underwater object detection
reason: Proposes a CNN-Mamba object detector evaluated on underwater datasets (DUO, RUOD) whose classes are mostly marine animals (sea cucumbers, urchins, starfish, scallops, fish, turtles, jellyfish) in real underwater scenes. The paper does not say whether the animals are wild.

title: Butterflies and benchmarks: a systematic evaluation of deep learning backbones to identify the best model for image-based butterflies species recognition
reason: Benchmarks CNN and ViT feature extractors for butterfly species classification on two public datasets. Most images show wild butterflies in their natural habitats.

title: A drone-based framework for coral habitat mapping via weakly supervised segmentation
reason: Primary study that trains segmentation models on drone and underwater imagery of wild coral colonies (and sea cucumbers) in reef lagoons.

title: ARFNet: a dual-backbone network for object detection in degraded underwater environments
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for underwater marine organisms (holothurian, echinus, starfish, scallop, fish, corals, jellyfish) in real-world underwater images from the URPC2020 and RUOD datasets.

title: DVS-StereoInsect: experimental evaluation of an event-based stereo dataset for foreground-background insect segmentation
reason: Presents and evaluates an event-camera dataset for segmenting wild insects (insect hotel, wasp nest, flowerbed area) from vegetation backgrounds.

title: Comparative spatial cognition in wild Tanganyikan cichlids: navigation performance varies with home range and shelter availability
reason: Primary behavioural study of wild shell-dwelling cichlids in Lake Tanganyika that applies structure-from-motion (COLMAP) to diver-filmed underwater video to reconstruct 3D scenes, home ranges and return trajectories. The onshore arena tests use wild-caught fish and appear to be scored manually.

title: Continuous foraging behavior shapes patch-leaving decisions in pigeons: a 3D tracking study
reason: Homing pigeons from breeders tested in a controlled laboratory arena; no wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Fish-GCvT: a hybrid deep learning architecture based on Convolutional Vision Transformers and graph convolutional networks for fish species classification
reason: Proposes a hybrid CNN/CvT/GCN classifier for fish species images; two of four datasets show free-ranging fish filmed underwater in the sea (Fish4Knowledge, Croatian Fish Dataset), while Fish-gres shows fish at markets.

title: Approximating the age of Eurasian otter (Lutra lutra) cubs from camera trap footage using proportional body measurements
reason: Lengths are measured by hand: observers trace polylines on paused camera-trap frames in BORIS. No automated image analysis or computer vision algorithm is used. Subjects are wild otters plus domestic ferrets for validation.

title: Deep learning-based monitoring and spatiotemporal analysis of wildlife and human activities using camera trap imagery
reason: Primary study training YOLO detectors on camera trap images of wild mammals (plus humans and domestic goats) in and around Chitwan National Park, followed by spatiotemporal analysis.

title: SAG-DETR: spatio-spectral adaptive gating with prompt-aware state-space refinement for underwater fish detection
reason: Fish detection for intensive aquaculture monitoring; self-collected data come from an industrial aquaculture tank. The FishNet images are not described as wild-fish data, and the stated application is aquaculture production.

title: Computer vision-based population monitoring of immobile synchronous firefly swarms
reason: Primary study developing a custom computer vision method to detect, track and count wild fireflies in field video recordings.

title: Underwater dynamic target tracking algorithm based on CWSCNet-RCAM
reason: Generic underwater single-object tracking method. Animals (fish, crabs, scallops) appear only as categories of the UOT32 tracking benchmark. The authors' own experiments track a chair, a basin, robots, a door and divers. Wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Understanding the efficacy and efficiency of thermal infrared UAV for wildlife monitoring
reason: UAV thermal/RGB survey of wild mammals in Chitwan NP, but animals were detected and identified manually by the pilot and observers. Orthomosaic processing (SfM, direct georeferencing) was only a demonstration and was not used for animal detection, so no computer vision method is applied to the animals.

title: Testing the feasibility of deep learning approaches to enhance monitoring of marine macroinvertebrates: Insights from a case study using the gastropod Peringia ulvae
reason: Field-collected Peringia ulvae were preserved in IMS, sorted and photographed on petri dishes in the laboratory. No images show live or free-ranging animals in situ, so this is a laboratory set-up with preserved specimens.

title: Exploring the Relationship Between Personality, Interest, and Success in Cognitive Enrichment in Western Gorillas (Gorilla gorilla)
reason: Behavioural/personality study of zoo-housed gorillas; videos were coded manually by an observer and analysed with GLMMs, so no computer vision is involved. The animals are also zoo-only.

title: Can camera trap distance sampling outperform line transects for estimating arboreal and semi-terrestrial primate density?
reason: Camera trap videos of wild primates were annotated by hand in Timelapse, and distances were judged by eye against reference markers. Density was then estimated with distance sampling. No computer vision or automated image analysis method is developed or applied.

title: Interpreting deep learning models for explainable animal detection using Grad-Cam with RetinaNet, SSD and YOLOv8
reason: Deep learning object detection (YOLOv8n, SSD, RetinaNet) on images of wild animals (tiger, bear, elephant, lion, cheetah, leopard) for a human-wildlife conflict early-warning system.

title: Underwater target detection based on target feature enhancement and semantic-position path aggregation
reason: Proposes an RT-DETR-based detector for underwater marine animals (sea cucumbers, urchins, scallops, starfish, fish, crabs) in underwater images and video of natural underwater scenes.

title: Detection and multi-class classification of freshwater fish species using space-to-depth convolution and YOLOv11
reason: Proposes a YOLOv11 + space-to-depth convolution detector/classifier for fish species, trained and tested on underwater images of fish recorded in a marine environment (Mediterranean fish dataset, OBSEA observatory).

title: Beyond labels: Semi-supervised underwater habitat detection with image enhancement as augmentation
reason: Semi-supervised object detection of fish and marine invertebrates in underwater images from real marine habitats (DeepFish, UTDAC2020).

title: TFL-IoUT: Transfer federated learning for privacy preserving coral classification on the internet of underwater things
reason: Primary study proposing a federated transfer-learning CNN framework for classifying underwater coral images (corals are animals) from public in-situ reef datasets.

title: Dscyolo: dynamic snake convolutional YOLO network for underwater image recognition
reason: Proposes a YOLO-based detector for underwater marine organisms (jellyfish, cuttlefish, coral) evaluated on underwater organism detection datasets.

title: A lightweight deep architecture with adaptive multi-scale features for efficient avian detection
reason: Proposes a lightweight YOLOv8-based detector for birds, trained and evaluated on bird images from web and citizen-science sources in natural environments and on a public bird dataset collected in Shanghai.

title: On Combining Animal Re-Identification Models to Address Small Datasets
reason: Primary study evaluating and combining computer-vision re-identification methods on image datasets of six wildlife species (seals, whale sharks, zebras, leopards, belugas).

title: Recurrence over Video Frames (RoVF) for Animal Re-identification
reason: All analysed video shows captive animals: meerkats at Wellington Zoo and polar bears from European zoos (PolarBearVidID). No wild data.

title: Wild Animal Tracking with High-Quality Segment Anything Model and Domain Adaptation
reason: Proposes a domain-adaptation single-object tracking framework and a new video dataset for wild animals; videos of wild animals collected from the Internet are analysed.

title: Watching Swarm Dynamics from Above: A Framework for Advanced Object Tracking in Drone Videos
reason: Proposes a computer vision tracking and segmentation framework for wild fish schools in the open ocean recorded by drone.

title: WildIng: A Wildlife Image Invariant Representation Model for Geographical Domain Shift
reason: Proposes a vision-language model for species classification in camera trap images of wild animals under geographical domain shift.

title: CamoVid60K: A Large-Scale Video Dataset for Moving Camouflaged Animals Understanding
reason: Primary study presenting a video dataset and benchmark for segmentation, detection and classification of camouflaged animals, built from web videos and existing datasets showing animals in their native habitats.

title: A Motion-Based Compression and Tracking System for Video Camera Trap-Based Insect Behaviour Studies
reason: Primary method paper: motion-based video compression plus automated detection and tracking of free-foraging insect pollinators in outdoor video (gardens, a strawberry farm, a bee nest); two of the six datasets are from controlled or semi-controlled environments.

title: AlphaChimp: Tracking and Behavior Recognition of Chimpanzees
reason: All analysed video shows a captive chimpanzee group in the indoor and outdoor enclosures of Leipzig Zoo. No wild or free-ranging animals are included.

title: RareSpot+: A Benchmark, Model, and Active Learning Framework for Small and Rare Wildlife in Aerial Imagery
reason: Primary study proposing a detection framework and benchmark for wild prairie dogs and their burrows in drone imagery of prairie colonies.

title: PosePAL: Efficient Animal Pose Labeling Using Point Trackers
reason: Proposes a computer vision pipeline (point-tracker test-time optimization) for animal pose labeling in videos. Animals are the subject. Data mixes natural-video animals (DAVIS goat and other quadrupeds, APTv2) with tethered lab flies and pigeons filmed in a controlled environment. The paper does not explicitly say any animals are wild, so inclusion is borderline.

title: EffBirdNet: an efficient and lightweight network based on synergistic feature fusion for fine-grained bird image classification
reason: Proposes a lightweight CNN for fine-grained classification of wild bird species from field images taken in Xixi National Wetland Park and from public bird datasets.

title: MCAB-YOLO: multimodal cross-attention for RGB-D underwater object detection
reason: Proposes an RGB-D detection model and evaluates it on underwater images of aquatic animals (fish, sea turtles, jellyfish) from the public MKUO dataset. The paper does not say whether the animals were wild or captive.

title: UW-D-FINE: degradation-aware real-time underwater object detection
reason: Proposes a real-time detector for underwater marine organisms (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish, fish, etc.) evaluated on underwater detection datasets RUOD and DUO; the animals are the main detection targets. The paper does not say whether the animals are wild or farmed.

title: YOLO-NIR-DGLL: a lightweight animal detection model for nighttime active near-infrared imagery
reason: Proposes a YOLO-based detector for nighttime active-NIR camera-trap images of wild animals (bear, leopard, wolf, etc.). Domestic cat and dog also appear in the data, so the subject type is mixed.

title: AF-DETR: a dual-stream frequency enhancement and blur-adaptive transformer for underwater object detection
reason: Proposes a transformer detector for underwater marine organisms (starfish, scallops, sea urchins, sea cucumbers) evaluated on underwater image datasets, motivated by marine biodiversity monitoring.

title: AACF-Net: an adaptive collaborative and high-resolution feature enhancement network for underwater biological detection
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for underwater marine organisms (sea urchin, sea cucumber, starfish, scallop, fish, sea turtles) in natural seabed scenes; primary research on animal images.

title: Extraction of small, blurred targets using penguins as an example
reason: Proposes a YOLOv5-based detector for wild penguins in UAV imagery from Vestfold Hills, Antarctica.

title: A lightweight transformer-enhanced YOLOv8 framework for robust underwater object detection and classification
reason: Proposes a CV detection and classification framework for underwater animals (fish, jellyfish, shark, etc.). The main dataset appears to be from an aquarium (based on the Kaggle URL), but the paper also validates on other underwater datasets and frames the work around marine ecosystems, so it is included.

title: YEILAN-ConvViT: hybrid transformer-enhanced real-time marine object detection using improved YOLO with efficient inter-layer aggregation
reason: Proposes a detection model for underwater marine objects, mostly marine animals (crabs, fish, starfish, scallops, holothurians, echinus), and evaluates it on underwater image datasets.

title: Enhanced segmentation of underwater crab images using an improved Otsu-based coati optimizer
reason: Proposes a thresholding-based segmentation method for underwater crab images, including video recorded in a mangrove forest in India; the crabs in this video are free-ranging.

title: Withdrawal behaviour of the sea pen Pennatula aculeata (Pennatuloidea): a 10-month fine-scale study with implications for conservation monitoring
reason: Applies supervised machine-learning pixel segmentation (RootPainter) to time-lapse seafloor images of wild sea pens in a marine protected area to quantify withdrawal behaviour.

title: TigerNet: individual identification of Stripe patterns in Amur Tigers like human fingerprint
reason: Proposes a computer vision re-identification method trained on captive Amur tigers (Siberian Tiger Park) and also evaluated on a public dataset of wild plains zebras from Nairobi National Park, so part of the data shows wild animals.

title: AQUA20: A Benchmark Dataset for Underwater Species Classification under Challenging Conditions
venue: Arabian Journal for Science and Engineering
reason: Introduces a benchmark dataset of real-world underwater images of marine species and evaluates 13 deep learning classifiers on it; marine conservation is a stated application.

title: Lightweight bird behavior recognition using dual-branch attention and cross-rate feature fusion for ecological monitoring
venue: Arabian Journal for Science and Engineering
reason: Proposes a video-based deep learning model for recognising behaviours of birds in ecological scenes (wetland and public videos).

title: Machine Learning Framework for Genus - Level Coral Classification in the Lakshadweep Reef Ecosystem
venue: Thalassas An International Journal of Marine Sciences
reason: Primary study proposing a CNN-based classifier for underwater video frames of wild reef corals (animals) filmed in situ in a lagoon in Lakshadweep.

title: Advancing coral reef monitoring: a deep learning perspective on automated segmentation and classification
reason: Primary experiments train deep segmentation models on underwater images of wild coral (Dipsastraea, Porites) from reefs in Kuantan, Malaysia; the paper also contains a literature review but includes its own dataset and experiments.

title: Optimization algorithm for 3D bird target tracking in transmission corridor based on YOLOv8–GhostNet
reason: Proposes a YOLOv8–GhostNet detection and tracking framework for wild birds in power transmission corridor images.

title: Configuring, Training, and Deploying AI Applications Through Integrated Gateways and Frameworks for Scientific Field Research
reason: Cyberinfrastructure/MLOps framework paper whose case study benchmarks animal detection models (MegaDetector, YOLO variants) on camera-trap images and video for wildlife monitoring. The paper never says whether the animals in the data are wild.

title: Energy-conserving behavioural strategies in southern right whale mother-calf pairs during early lactation
reason: UAV video of wild southern right whales was coded by hand for behaviour, and body measurements were taken by manual aerial photogrammetry. The analysis is statistical (GLMMs). No computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Underwater object detection using global flower pollination-based sunflower optimization (GFP-SFO) on YOLOv6
reason: Proposes a YOLOv6-based detector, tuned with the GFP-SFO optimiser, for underwater images. It detects marine animals (fish, sea urchins, corals) in seawater images from the EUVP dataset, and the paper frames the work as marine ecosystem and biodiversity monitoring.

title: Sea animal image classification using machine learning algorithms for accurate and scalable prediction
reason: Applies image classification (Inception-v3 embeddings + ML classifiers) to images of marine animals (squid, starfish, whale) in underwater settings; primary research.

title: Automated under-ice monitoring system for fish detection in Central Arctic Ocean
reason: Develops and deploys a YOLOv5-based fish detection system on under-ice video in the Central Arctic Ocean (wild marine fauna); also tested in pool and lake with test fish.

title: Coral Intel: a YOLOv8 deep learning framework for monitoring Caribbean corals
reason: Primary study applying YOLOv8 object detection to underwater images of wild Caribbean scleractinian corals (animals), with web-sourced training images and field transect photoquadrats from a reef in Puerto Rico.

title: Underwater tiny object detection network based on multi-scale attention and adaptive feature fusion
reason: Proposes a YOLO-based detector for benthic marine organisms (sea urchins, sea cucumbers, starfish, scallops) in underwater images collected offshore of Dalian, China.

title: Social tolerance and large group feeding behaviours in response to anthropogenic resource provision in reportedly solitary Neotropical foxes
reason: Primary case study applying a YOLOv8 detector to video of wild free-ranging Lycalopex foxes at a carcass disposal site to detect and count individuals.

title: Nocturnal activity patterns and mother-offspring interactions during early rearing in yellow-backed duikers (Cephalophus silvicultor)
reason: Behavioural case study of zoo-housed yellow-backed duikers in which researchers scored the video footage by hand with BORIS. There is no computer vision or automated image analysis, and all animals are captive.

title: Lml-yolo: Composite enhanced YOLO object detection model for underwater complex environments
venue: Journal of King Saud University - Computer and Information Sciences
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for marine organisms (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish) in real underwater images. Part of the data comes from sea farms (UDD); the other data are real underwater scenes, and the paper frames the work around biodiversity monitoring.

title: ST-YOLOv11: An improved small-target detection algorithm for pika holes and bare patches based on YOLOv11
venue: Journal of King Saud University - Computer and Information Sciences
reason: Proposes a YOLOv11-based detector for pika holes (burrows, a direct sign of wild animals) and bare patches in UAV imagery of alpine meadows.

title: BioVis-Det: scale–adaptive and noise–resilient underwater detection via dynamic aggregation and orthogonal calibration
venue: Journal of King Saud University - Computer and Information Sciences
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for underwater images of benthic marine organisms (URPC, RUOD) from real marine environments; wild marine animals are the detection targets.

title: VTS-PANDA: fine-grained wild giant panda behavior recognition via ecological semantic knowledge from infrared videos
venue: Journal of King Saud University - Computer and Information Sciences
reason: Proposes a multimodal video behavior recognition framework evaluated on infrared camera-trap videos of wild giant pandas (and wild rhesus macaques).

title: RGN-UOD: An information redistribution-guided network for underwater object detection
venue: Journal of King Saud University - Computer and Information Sciences
reason: Proposes a detection network for underwater benthic animals (sea cucumber, sea urchin, scallop, starfish) in images from real underwater environments.

title: AfriTickID: An AI-assisted image-based approach for tick species identification in Kenya
reason: Tick species classification from stereomicroscope images of preserved laboratory specimens (plus GBIF images); veterinary/public-health vector identification using lab microscopy rather than imagery of wild free-ranging animals.

title: AquaSelect: Learning when to abstain via score fusion for reliable underwater species classification
reason: Proposes a selective prediction framework for classifying underwater marine species images of free-ranging marine animals from two public datasets.

title: Agentic Ontology-guided Image Generation and Evaluation for Rare-event Data Augmentation in Safety-critical Perception
reason: Proposes a computer vision framework that generates and evaluates synthetic images of wild large animals (deer, kangaroo, camel, elephant) in wildlife–traffic scenes, and tests zero-shot animal detection on them. The application is wildlife–vehicle collisions. Inclusion is borderline because the analysed images are mostly synthetic depictions of wild animals.

title: APG-DynaFFNet: Anatomical priors guided dynamic multi-granularity feature fusion for Animal Pose Estimation
reason: Proposes a pose estimation network evaluated on images of wild golden monkeys, lynxes and snow leopards.

title: H-Net: A transformer based multistage fusion convolutional neural network for underwater object detection in complex environments
reason: Proposes a CNN-transformer detector for underwater object detection, evaluated on real underwater image datasets whose classes are mainly marine animals (fish, echinus, holothurian, starfish, scallop, turtle, etc.). The paper never says the animals are wild; free-ranging marine fauna is the closest fit.

title: MTDL-BMG: Multi-task deep learning with branch-mutual guidance for unified butterfly natural image analysis
reason: Proposes a multi-task deep learning method for segmenting and classifying natural-scene images of butterflies; specimen images were excluded.

title: DSP-YOLO11n: An efficient enhancement for real-time benthos detection
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for benthic marine organisms (sea cucumber, sea urchin, scallop, starfish) in underwater images from the URPC and DUO datasets.

title: Seafood target detection network with hierarchical perception capability
reason: Proposes a CNN-based detector (HPW-YOLO) for underwater seafood/benthic organisms (sea cucumber, scallop, sea urchin, starfish) in real seabed images from URPC and RUOD. The paper never says these animals are farmed, so they are coded as free-ranging marine animals.

title: UWCOSNet: Underwater camouflaged object segmentation network with frequency edge enhancement
reason: Proposes a CNN/transformer segmentation network for camouflaged marine animals in underwater images (MAS3K-CAM, Aqua-Test); primary method research on free-ranging animals.

title: Exploring linear attention in underwater image enhancement with Retinex theory
reason: Generic underwater image enhancement method evaluated on general underwater image benchmarks; animals are not the stated subject and wildlife is not analysed.

title: Enhancing underwater perception via sonar-optical collaboration: An adaptive feature alignment fusion framework and multi-target dataset
reason: Sonar-optical object detection of mostly man-made underwater objects. The only animals (fish) were recorded at a single indoor underwater test site, so none of the data shows wild, free-ranging animals.

title: Automatic identification of Kuril Habor seals (Phoca vitulina stejnegeri) in underwater video footage recorded at a salmon set-nets
reason: Detects wild Kuril harbor seals entering salmon set-nets, using a deep learning model on underwater video recorded in the field.

title: YOLO-FSD: A lightweight deep learning framework for crested ibis (Nipponia nippon) detection and segmentation in complex natural environments
reason: Proposes a deep learning detection and segmentation model for wild crested ibis photographed under natural field conditions.

title: Image-based individual identification of wild Black-necked Cranes (Grus nigricollis) using deep learning
reason: The paper applies a deep learning pipeline to identify individual wild Black-necked Cranes from field images taken by drones and a camera.

title: Prolonged reduction in grassland arthropod activity after mowing revealed by AI camera trap monitoring
reason: AI camera traps with detection and classification of free-ranging arthropods in German grasslands to study mowing effects.

title: Revisiting “Penguins in the anthropause: Covid-19 closures drive gentoo penguin movement among breeding colonies”
reason: Analyses drone (RPAS) imagery of wild gentoo penguin colonies. It improves orthomosaic image processing and annotates the images to count nests and adults. This is image analysis of wild animals.

title: Mauritius' macaques under the thermal camera lens: a 40-year overdue update on a controversial non-native species
reason: Wild macaques were surveyed with thermal and RGB drone video, but people counted the animals by hand. The paper uses no automated image analysis or computer vision method; its analysis is statistical (MaxEnt, N-mixture models, a Horvitz-Thompson estimator).

title: Spatial ecology and recovery patterns of a translocated mammal community in southern Africa
reason: Camera-trap images of translocated free-ranging herbivores in a Malawian reserve, processed with a YOLOv4 detector to support occupancy modelling.

title: Underwater ecological assessment via intelligent monitoring robot based on semi-supervised semantic segmentation
reason: Proposes a semi-supervised semantic segmentation method for underwater ecological monitoring. It segments marine organisms such as fish and other underwater animals in underwater imagery, and is tested on a robot platform.

title: Foreground refinement network for paleontological fossil image segmentation incorporating boundary-aware features and frequency domain information
reason: The paper segments images of Cambrian fossil specimens, not wild free-ranging animals. Fossils are coded like museum specimens. The COD benchmarks are only used to test a general method.

title: Topological and network dynamics reveal state transitions in honeybee bee-ball formation
reason: Apiary guard bees and collected hornets filmed in a Petri dish indoors under controlled conditions; no free-ranging animals in the analysed data.

title: An interpretable framework using foundation models for fish sex identification
reason: All images show hatchery-reared delta smelt at the Fish Conservation and Culture Laboratory, so they are captive animals only. None of the data shows wild or free-ranging fish.

title: Crab semantic segmentation method based on dual image encoders
reason: Proposes a segmentation model for crabs using iNaturalist images of crabs in natural environments plus public marine animal segmentation datasets; wild animals are the image subject.

title: Occlusion-Robust fish individual identification: a multi-model video recognition framework for complex underwater environments
reason: Individual identification of fish (koi, goldfish, pufferfish, clownfish) filmed in aquaculture facilities/aquaria and online videos; no wild free-ranging animals; aquaculture application.

title: Underwater object detection based on channel expansion and feature fusion
reason: Proposes a YOLOv11-based detector for marine organisms (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish, fish, etc.) in underwater images from public underwater datasets, framed as marine environment monitoring.

title: Home cage monitoring of group-housed animals in highly enriched enclosures
reason: Research-colony rhesus macaques, bred at the MRC Centre for Macaques and kept in indoor enclosures, monitored by CCTV. No wild or free-ranging animals appear in the data.

title: Individual identification of brown bears using pose-aware metric learning
reason: Develops a pose-aware deep metric learning model for individual re-identification of wild Alaskan brown bears from photographs.

title: Precise, individualized foraging flights in honeybees revealed by multicopter drone-based tracking
reason: Image-based (IR stereo camera) drone tracking of honeybees from managed beekeeping hives; beekeeping falls under E-AGRI.

title: Automated flower monitoring with deep learning reveals fine-scale microclimate selection by pollinators
reason: Applies deep-learning camera traps (YOLOv8 detection + EfficientNetV2 classification) to images of wild insect pollinators visiting flowers in field experiments.

title: Space-based monitoring of penguin diet links sea ice, food webs, and population change
reason: Primary study analysing Landsat multispectral satellite imagery of guano-covered pixels (direct sign) at wild Adélie penguin colonies to infer diet.

title: Quantifying the control laws governing terminal attack in lions
reason: Drone video of captive lions attacking a mechanized lure inside a 1.3-hectare enclosure at a safari park; no wild free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: A YOLO-OC real-time small object detection in ocean scenes
reason: Proposes a YOLO-based detector for small marine animals (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish) in images from real underwater environments.

title: An annotated dataset of images of Chinese giant salamanders
reason: Dataset paper releasing annotated images of wild Chinese giant salamanders filmed in a nature reserve for object detection.

title: AvianAction101: A Dataset for the dancing behavior of rose-ringed parakeets(Psittacula krameri)
reason: Video dataset of rose-ringed parakeet courtship actions taken from YouTube videos. The videos show birds in domestic or semi-natural settings interacting with humans, pets, mirrors and toys, so the subjects are pet birds rather than wild free-ranging animals.

title: FishNet: A dataset of freshwater fish from Bangladesh for deep learning-based fish species classification
reason: Dataset paper of freshwater fish and crustaceans photographed on a white board at fish markets, ponds and rivers. It is aimed at fisheries, smart aquaculture and food authentication, and the authors train or evaluate no computer vision model.

title: A stereo dataset of annotated budgerigar flight trajectories for multi-agent collision avoidance studies
reason: Dataset of flight-trained budgerigars recorded in a controlled indoor laboratory flight arena; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Enhancing wildlife monitoring with computer vision: A dataset for automated detection of barbary macaques
reason: Dataset of Barbary macaques recorded only in a zoo enclosure (ZooParc de Beauval); no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: DCF-Net:Dynamic cross-fusion network for underwater object detection
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for marine organisms (sea urchin, holothurian, starfish, scallop) in underwater images; the paper does not say whether the animals are wild or farmed.

title: Bi-branch attention and receptive field enhanced network for marine small organism detection
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for marine organisms (echinus, holothurian, scallop, starfish, fish, crabs) in underwater images from URPC2020 and Brackish datasets.

title: Training neural network for benthic image analysis using legacy point annotations: A case study in HAUSGARTEN LTER
reason: Applies YOLOv8 object detection to towed-camera seabed images of wild deep-sea benthic megafauna at HAUSGARTEN LTER, using legacy point annotations converted to bounding boxes.

title: Computer vision for infectious disease surveillance; Saprolegnia spp. in salmonids
reason: CNN image classification of saprolegniasis-like infection in images of wild-caught salmonids from citizen science platforms and fishery stakeholders.

title: Benthic habitat influences sea scallop distributions and swimming behavior based on underwater imagery and machine learning
reason: Applies CNN-based detectors and classifiers to towed underwater camera imagery of wild Atlantic sea scallops on fishing grounds to study habitat and swimming behaviour.

title: PantherAI: An autonomous behavioural monitoring tool for assessing activity budget and space use in a zoo-housed tiger
reason: Computer vision behavioural monitoring of a single zoo-housed Amur tiger from CCTV footage at the Toronto Zoo; no wild or free-ranging animals in the data.

title: YOLO-HARVEST: A hybrid ViT architecture with locality-enhanced attention for automated wildlife species classification
reason: Proposes a YOLOv8 + transformer hybrid for species classification of wildlife in camera trap images (OSU Small Animals, African wildlife, CCT).

title: AI-driven analysis of fish reproductive behaviour
reason: Applies YOLOv9 to underwater videos of wild grey wrasse to detect reproductive behaviours in their natural habitat.

title: Optical imaging and machine learning to identify and enumerate early developmental stages of fish species
reason: Eggs and larvae of hatchery-reared fish, including koi, were euthanized and imaged in a laboratory flow-through system. No wild or free-ranging animals appear in the data, and aquaculture and hatchery counting are stated applications.

title: AEWD: A weakly observable object detection benchmark for UAV-based endangered wildlife monitoring
reason: Presents a UAV image dataset of wild endangered animals in Chinese forest protected areas and benchmarks object detectors on it.

title: Insect size matters: Using image and dimensions together improves image classification
reason: The only analysed data is BIOSCAN-1M, which the paper describes as a lab imaging setup with a standardized imaging system and fixed camera-to-specimen distance; no images of wild, free-ranging insects are analysed.

title: Towards automated bycatch monitoring: Optimizing and evaluating multi-object tracking of salmon in pollock trawls
reason: Applies object detection and multi-object tracking to in-situ video of wild Pacific salmon and walleye pollock inside a commercial trawl net in the Bering Sea.

title: LEPY: A Python pipeline for automated trait extraction from standardised Lepidoptera images
reason: The images are of mounted Lepidoptera specimens photographed under standardised studio conditions, not of free-ranging animals. Museum specimens fall under E-CAPTIVE.

title: Distance-based population density estimates from camera traps: Strong impact of technical choices in automated pipelines
reason: Applies computer vision (MegaDetector detection, monocular depth estimation, SAM/Segformer segmentation) to camera trap images of wild red deer in a German forest to estimate population density via CTDS.

title: FDM-YOLO: Real-time small-target UAV wildlife detection via attention-guided cross-modality fusion
reason: Proposes a UAV thermal-RGB fusion detector for wild cervids and birds recorded in a Chinese nature reserve; primary research using computer vision.

title: InsectRoleVision: A computer vision system to study arthropod diversity and functional roles
reason: Deep learning detection and classification of wild arthropods caught on sticky traps in wildflower beds for biodiversity and functional-role monitoring.

title: SharkTrack: An accurate, generalisable software for streamlining shark and ray underwater video analysis
reason: Develops and evaluates a CNN detector and multi-object tracking pipeline on BRUVS underwater video of wild sharks and rays.

title: Quantifying jellyfish bloom dynamics using aerial surveys and image-based cohort analysis in a Mediterranean lagoon
reason: Primary study applying a threshold-based image analysis algorithm to aerial images of a wild jellyfish (Rhizostoma pulmo) bloom in a Mediterranean lagoon to detect, count, size and map the animals.

title: Testing the transferability of AI models for cold-water coral detection and classification
reason: Primary study training and testing YOLOv5 object detectors on ROV seabed imagery of wild cold-water corals (animals in their natural deep-sea habitat).

title: Deep learning based detection of wild bee parasites under natural conditions
reason: Deep learning object detection of parasites (Stylopidae, Meloidae larvae) on wild bees in citizen-science photographs taken under natural conditions.

title: From observation to replication: Machine-learning-driven quantification and replication of fine-scale fish kinematics and behavior
reason: Pose estimation of a single tagged juvenile white sturgeon housed in an indoor laboratory tank; no wild or free-ranging animals in the data.

title: SOCI-YOLO11n: A deep learning model for identifying invasive freshwater turtles in complex ecological contexts
reason: The paper proposes a YOLO11n-based detector for invasive freshwater turtles. Its images come from a turtle breeding and conservation centre (captive) plus open-source platform images, and Fig. 1B shows images from complex environments. The stated application is monitoring wild invasive turtles, so the paper is included.

title: Enhancing satellite-based detection of marine fauna using synthetic data
reason: Develops diffusion-based synthetic satellite imagery and YOLO detection of wild southern right whales and beluga whales in real satellite images.

title: Deep learning-based keypoint detection for morphological measurement of termite legs with potential occlusion
reason: Termites were trapped in the field but the analysed images are microscope images of collected specimens taken in the laboratory for leg morphometry, so the paper falls under microscopy/laboratory set-up.

title: Enhancing red-billed gull detection in reflective aquatic habitats: A deep-learning approach with triple-stage UAV image enhancement
reason: Proposes an image enhancement plus U-Net segmentation framework for detecting wild overwintering red-billed gulls in UAV images of wetlands in Kunming.

title: Low-disturbance UAV-AI monitoring of the endangered Przewalski's gazelle on the Qinghai-Tibetan plateau
reason: Applies deep-learning object detectors to UAV imagery to detect and count wild Przewalski's gazelles on the Qinghai-Tibetan Plateau.

title: Beyond classification accuracy: Uncertainty-aware deep learning for coral reef monitoring
reason: Deep learning classification of benthic survey images of wild coral reef communities (corals are animals) for coral cover estimation.

title: PhotoDB: a customizable platform for image data management, processing, and annotation
reason: Software platform paper for image data management; the only computer vision case study detects and segments oak leaves for phenology monitoring. MegaDetector is used only to flag humans. The arthropod (flatbug) dataset is used only to demonstrate data management, not analysed with CV.

title: From relative to metric: Calibrating AI-based monocular depth learning models for distance sampling in wildlife monitoring applications
reason: Proposes a calibration pipeline for monocular depth estimation to estimate camera-to-animal distances for wild ungulates in forest camera-trap videos and images.

title: InsectMorphoAI: A deep learning framework for automated insect morphometrics and biomass estimation with taxon-specific volumetric validation
reason: Images are of ethanol-preserved insect specimens imaged individually in a controlled laboratory Entomoscope set-up; no free-ranging animals are imaged. The closest exclusion criterion is museum or preserved specimens.

title: INQUIRE-Search: Interactive discovery in large-scale biodiversity databases
reason: Vision-language retrieval system applied to iNaturalist images of wild animals (bird diet, bird mortality, humpback whale re-identification) as well as plants; primary research.

title: Annotation strategy trade-offs for deep learning-based underwater fish detection
reason: Deep learning (YOLO) detection of wild fish and other fauna in baited/unbaited remote underwater video from Norwegian and Swedish coasts; some cod annotations come from a semi-natural mesocosm.

title: Fine-grained tuna detection in complex dynamic monitoring scenarios: A lightweight framework based on feature decoupling and partial convolution
reason: Proposes a CV detector for fine-grained detection of wild-caught tuna species in shipborne electronic monitoring video from longline fishing vessels (wild fisheries catch, not aquaculture).

title: A deep-learning based approach to detect and classify animals flying near wind turbines using thermal surveillance cameras and open-source software
reason: Coded from the title only: the manuscript was withdrawn and the text holds just the title and a withdrawal notice. The title describes a deep-learning approach to detect and classify animals flying near wind turbines in thermal camera footage, which meets the inclusion criteria, but no methods, data or results are available to confirm it.

title: Odontocete strandings from space: Accurately counting individuals with very high-resolution optical and synthetic aperture radar satellite imagery
reason: Stranded wild odontocetes were detected and counted by human observers who manually annotated satellite and aerial images. The only automated step is hierarchical clustering of the observers' point annotations, which is not image analysis, so the paper has no computer vision method.

title: Speeding up image annotation and AI-model training for wildlife images
reason: Pipeline for annotating camera-trap images of wild small mammals in Eastern Canada and training YOLO detection and segmentation models on them.

title: Near-perfect photo-ID of the Hula painted frog with zero-shot deep local-feature matching
reason: Primary study evaluating computer-vision photo re-identification on ventral photographs of wild Hula painted frogs captured during field capture-recapture surveys.

title: Automated bird flight pattern extraction and classification using machine learning
reason: Primary study that develops a computer vision pipeline (detection, wing-stroke classification, species classification) on citizen-contributed videos and images of birds in flight for bird monitoring.

title: Automated waterbird detection, classification, and mapping from UAV imagery using a two-stage deep learning pipeline
reason: Primary study applying a YOLOv8 + EfficientNet deep learning pipeline to UAV RGB imagery of free-ranging waterbirds on a canal in Belgium.

title: Beyond approach distance: A drone–hydrophone integrated framework for quantifying vessel noise masking risk to free ranging wild dolphins
reason: Drone video of wild Indo-Pacific bottlenose dolphins and vessels is processed. Vessels are found with YOLO, and dolphin surfacing positions are annotated in the video and georeferenced from pixel coordinates to estimate noise exposure. The animals are the subject of the study.

title: Advancing AI-based species identification for marine bycatch monitoring: Insights from faster R-CNN experiments
reason: Applies object detection (Faster R-CNN, YOLO) to images of wild marine megafauna (sharks, turtles) caught as bycatch on fishing-vessel decks.

title: Swimming behavior of fish across habitats: A trajectory based analysis using YOLO–DeepSORT and Markov chain models
reason: Computer vision (detection, tracking, behaviour modelling) applied to videos of damselfish in natural marine habitats.

title: AI-based automated monitoring of the invasive pearl oyster (Pinctada radiata) in the Aegean Sea using underwater surveys
reason: Applies YOLOv11 + ByteTrack to in situ underwater video of wild invasive pearl oysters for detection, counting and morphometrics.

title: Similarity learning network using quadruplet loss for animal re-identification
reason: CNN-based individual re-identification of wild sea turtles from photographs taken in the wild, using public datasets.

title: Anatomical landmark detection of giant pandas in the wild with infrared camera traps
reason: Proposes a pose/landmark detection CNN for wild giant pandas in infrared camera-trap images from a nature reserve.

title: Automated detection, tracking and laser-based sizing of scallops from towed video using deep learning
reason: Applies deep learning detection, tracking and sizing to towed underwater video of wild scallop populations in a fishery survey area.

title: A deep learning-based pipeline combining UAV imagery and YOLO models for intertidal population dynamics monitoring
reason: Develops a UAV + YOLO detection and segmentation pipeline for faecal casts (direct signs) of wild lugworms Arenicola marina on an intertidal beach.

title: Automated landmark and semilandmark annotation for wing geometric morphometrics in Diptera using deep learning
reason: Automated landmark annotation on microscope/macro images of mounted Diptera wing specimens (mosquitoes, tsetse, Drosophila mutants); laboratory specimen imaging, not images of free-ranging animals.

title: Deep learning-based optical monitoring system on floating platforms: enabling long-term activity monitoring of the finless porpoise in the Nanjing section
reason: Deep learning detection and tracking of wild Yangtze finless porpoises in video from a camera on a floating platform in the Yangtze River.

title: Reducing annotation burden in benthic ecology: Weak supervision for automated detection of seafloor sediment-linked features
reason: Weakly supervised object detection of benthic animals and their burrows (Nephrops burrows, sponges, bryozoans, anemones, etc.) in field seafloor imagery.

title: An uncertainty-aware compute continuum architecture for underwater species detection
reason: Uncertainty-aware object detection of wild fish species in imagery from the OBSEA cabled underwater observatory (Mediterranean); primary research with computer vision.

title: Automated detection of moose and deer in thermal imagery using unmanned aerial vehicles and deep learning
reason: Applies deep learning object detectors to thermal UAV imagery of wild moose and deer collected in field surveys in Manitoba, Canada.

title: Automated morphometric modelling of an endangered freshwater cetacean from unscaled UAV imagery using an internal scaling framework
reason: Develops an image-based morphometric (body length) estimation framework from UAV images of wild Yangtze finless porpoises rescued from drought-isolated habitats.

title: Computer vision-based estimation of small arthropod biomass
reason: Computer vision (CNNs and image-derived linear models) estimates the dry mass of wild arthropods. The specimens were collected in field monitoring (emergence traps in Danish farmland and benthic surveys in Finnish lakes) and imaged with the BIODISCOVER device.

title: An intelligent multi-stage fishway integrating computer vision and adaptive hydraulic control
reason: Applies a YOLOv12 detector to images of freshwater fish to trigger gates in a fishway for migratory fish. The training images come from online repositories and their capture conditions are not stated. A validation test used live specimens in the lab. The stated subject is wild migratory fish passage.

title: Automating coastal bioindicator acquisition with deep learning: crab community monitoring for enhanced wetland management
reason: Deep learning detection, classification and segmentation of wild crabs and their burrows in field images from coastal mangrove wetlands in China.

title: AI-powered underwater imaging reveals multiscale occurrence and volume-based abundance patterns in coastal fishes
reason: Applies deep-learning detection and classification to images of free-ranging coastal fish. The images come from a fixed underwater camera at a Mediterranean harbour entrance, and the detections are used to derive occurrence and density indicators.

title: Teinopalpus aureus, an indicator species of Asian montane evergreen broad-leaved forests: a deep learning-based case study on butterfly hilltopping
reason: Applies deep learning detection and classification to surveillance video of wild butterflies hilltopping at mountaintop sites in a nature reserve.

title: A mechanistic approach to understanding birth timing, calf growth, and residency of southern right whale mother–calf pairs on their calving ground
reason: Analyses UAV aerial photographs of wild southern right whale mother–calf pairs: body measurements are taken in pixels from the images and converted to metres (photogrammetry), and individuals are identified from photos. The image-derived morphometrics feed a mechanistic residency model.

title: Scalable juvenile small-tuna identification and new insights into spawning and population structure in the Adriatic Sea
reason: Species identification of dead juvenile tunas from fisheries bycatch uses landmarks placed by hand in tpsDIG on photos, followed by statistical shape analysis (Procrustes, PCA, GMM, CVA) and DNA barcoding. No computer vision method is applied to the images.

title: Automated Detection and Counting of 12 Macrobenthic Taxa on the Basque Coast using Computer Vision on ROV Videos
reason: Deep learning detection, tracking and counting of wild macrobenthic taxa in ROV video from the Basque continental shelf.

title: Morphological edge enhancement and bottleneck layers for robust underwater object detection
reason: Detection method evaluated only on the Kaggle Aquarium Dataset (aquarium animals: fish, jellyfish, penguin, puffin, shark, starfish, stingray); no wild free-ranging data.

title: Comparison of line intercept transect method, underwater photo transect, underwater 3D photo, drone, and satellite imagery in coral reef survey
venue: The Egyptian Journal of Aquatic Research
reason: Despite being labelled a review article, this is a primary field study. It applies image analysis (SfM 3D reconstruction, supervised classification of UAV and Sentinel-2 imagery) to wild coral reefs in Indonesia.

title: Estimating the biomass of soil macrofauna communities using composite images
reason: Soil invertebrates were collected in the field, then killed and scanned as specimens on a desktop scanner in the laboratory. The image analysis therefore runs on a laboratory set-up, not on images of free-ranging animals.

title: A Policy-Driven Design of Energy-Autonomous Intelligent Observatories for Marine Biodiversity Monitoring
reason: Views & Comments perspective paper proposing a conceptual design for energy-autonomous marine observatories; no image data are analysed and no computer vision experiments are reported.

title: Dynamic generative adversarial network augmented Cross-Shaped Window transformer for underwater object detection with adaptive feature extraction and adaptive resolution enhancement mechanism
reason: Proposes a transformer-based detection method for underwater images of marine organisms (fish, jellyfish, starfish, sponges) from the DeepFish and DUO datasets. The stated application is marine biodiversity monitoring and conservation.

title: Diffusion model-enhanced coral identification: A lightweight multi-scale network for benthic imagery analysis
reason: Proposes a lightweight CNN detector for fine-grained coral recognition (coral monitoring). Data mix captive corals from cultivation tanks with internet coral images and the UODAC underwater dataset of free-ranging marine invertebrates.

title: Automated annotation with gradient-reversal-based domain adaptive feature learning for animal trespass detection under day-night surveillance
reason: Proposes weakly supervised annotation and domain-adaptive detection of animals in infrared camera footage from a national park; the data include 15 wild and 2 domestic classes.

title: Joint underwater image enhancement and multi-scale fish detection
reason: Proposes a deep learning detector with joint underwater image enhancement for detecting free-swimming fish in underwater images from natural habitats.

title: In-field evaluation and behavioral analysis of a drawing-based penguin observation system
reason: Field deployment of a drawing-based identification system for African penguins kept in an aquarium. Only captive animals are involved, and the analysis covers visitor interaction logs, not image analysis of wild animals.

title: UPinst: Real time instance segmentation of underwater optical images
reason: Proposes a real-time instance segmentation network evaluated on URPC, real underwater images of marine organisms (sea cucumbers, starfish, shells, sea urchins) captured in real marine environments.

title: Part-aware cross-integration transformer with proximity guided regularization for domain generalizable animal re-identification
reason: Proposes a transformer method for domain-generalizable individual re-identification of animals, evaluated on unseen wildlife species (zebra, seal, giraffe, tiger). Training categories include a domestic horse breed (Appaloosa).

title: SAM2-WaveUNet: A frequency-enhanced segmentation network for fine-grained marine organism delineation
reason: Proposes a segmentation network for marine animals in underwater images, evaluated on four public marine animal segmentation datasets. Primary method research. The paper does not say where the animals were filmed.

title: WM-DETR: Dual-branch wavelet-Mamba and sparse attention for robust underwater object detection
reason: Proposes a detector for underwater objects, evaluated on benchmarks of marine animals (fish, turtles, jellyfish, echinus, holothurian, scallop, starfish). DUO also includes data from an open-sea farm, so wild and farmed animals appear together.

title: ViS2T: A vision and scene graph to text model for captive giant panda video captioning
reason: Video captioning applied only to captive giant pandas at a research base; the other datasets are generic video benchmarks.

title: Parameter-efficient vision–language adaptation with continuous metadata conditioning for animal re-identification
reason: Proposes a CLIP-based re-identification method evaluated on images of wild corkwing wrasse plus several wildlife ReID benchmarks; some benchmarks include cattle.

title: Hybrid quantum–classical multimodal fusion under weak cross-modal alignment for bird species recognition
reason: Proposes a hybrid quantum-classical multimodal (image + audio) fusion method for classifying wild bird species, using images of free-ranging birds from Malaysia and citizen-science images from Singapore and Thailand.

title: Plankton-LDM: A data augmentation method for class-imbalanced plankton image classification
reason: Proposes a diffusion-based image generation method to augment in situ marine plankton images from Daya Bay (wild zooplankton taxa) and evaluates downstream classification.

title: Estimating escapees using automated video analysis: Assessing the sorting efficiency of the Excluder in the North Sea sandeel fishery
reason: Applies an object detection and tracking model to underwater video of wild fish escaping a commercial trawl in the North Sea, to estimate how many escape.

title: Assessing the nest building activity of ground-nesting bees by surveilling tumuli changes using camouflaged instance segmentation
reason: Computer vision (camouflaged instance segmentation) applied to field images of nest tumuli (direct signs) of the wild ground-nesting bee Andrena vaga in a meadow.

title: Detection of South American porcupines (Rodentia: Erethizontidae) by thermal drones: A new opportunity for surveying and monitoring of elusive species
reason: Wild porcupines were filmed with thermal drones, but the detections were made by human operators in real time and during manual video review. The paper applies no computer vision or automated image analysis.

title: Automatic re-identification of terrestrial mammals using deep learning and camera trap images
reason: Proposes a deep learning re-identification network for individual Amur tigers and leopards from camera trap images of wild terrestrial mammals.

title: Modernizing alpine grassland biodiversity conservation: Efficient AI-powered detection of large herbivores in the Qinghai-Tibet plateau
reason: Applies an improved YOLOv10 to detect and count four wild herbivore species in field photographs from line-transect surveys in Sanjiangyuan National Park.

title: A multimodal learning approach for automated detection of wildlife trade on social media
reason: Develops a multimodal approach with CNN species-presence classification of YouTube video keyframes to detect trade in CITES-listed wild species. The videos show traded animals and wildlife documentaries, and fine-tuning used iNaturalist images of wild animals.

title: Can you identify a numbat by its stripes? Optimising identification of individuals of a threatened mammal from camera trap images
reason: Wild numbats in camera trap images are identified individually by human observers using manually scored pelage features; no computer vision or automated image analysis is developed or applied.

title: A machine learning framework for combatting poaching challenges in wildlife
reason: Conceptual framework paper proposing a DRCNN/3D ResNet/CNN+SVM anti-poaching detector; no images or video are analysed and no experiments are run, as the authors state no dataset was used.

title: DEF-Net: A detection-oriented enhancement and discriminative feature learning framework for underwater object detection
reason: Proposes a deep-learning detector for underwater benthic marine organisms (echinus, holothurian, starfish, scallop) evaluated on underwater organism datasets of natural seabed scenes.

title: An enhanced YOLOv11-based architecture for underwater object detection using Deformable Large-Kernel Attention and Adaptive Focal Loss
reason: Proposes a YOLOv11-based detector for underwater images of marine organisms (holothurians, echinus, scallops, starfish, fish, crabs, jellyfish, shrimp) from underwater benchmarks, with marine ecological monitoring as the stated application.

title: SEAD-Net:Complex underwater image segmentation via semantic-enhanced and detail-aware collaboration
reason: Proposes a deep learning segmentation method for marine animals in underwater images, evaluated on public marine animal segmentation datasets.

title: EmoSkeMPR: ViT-based masked position reconstruction and skeleton feature fusion for multi-task emotion and behavior recognition
reason: Proposes a computer vision framework for emotion and behaviour recognition of wild Qinling golden monkeys photographed in natural habitats.

title: Embodied postural dynamics underlie behavioral diversity in a benthic sessile chordate
reason: Wild-caught adult Ciona intestinalis were moved to an indoor facility and filmed in laboratory glass tanks under controlled stimuli. None of the analysed images show free-ranging animals.

title: Beyond accuracy: Cross-session stability in representation-based animal identification
reason: Evaluates identity stability of representation-based identification on laboratory animals (Drosophila, mice, zebrafish, rats in operant chambers); no wild animals.

title: DEEPFIN: A deep learning tool for fish image classification from unlabeled data
reason: Unsupervised CV pipeline for classifying fish images by species and developmental stage. The data include wild reef fish filmed by underwater video surveillance (Fish4Knowledge) and in situ underwater images, together with lab-reared anemonefish and commercial fish.

title: Sparse multimodal feature fusion transformer with frequency-convolution collaboration for wildlife multi-object tracking in UAV monitoring
venue: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing
reason: Proposes a transformer-based multi-object tracker for UAV videos of free-ranging Milu deer, also evaluated on drone baboon and wild-animal AnimalTrack videos.

title: VT-FLAC: A visible-thermal fusion network for robust wildlife monitoring in open-field environments using near-remote sensing imagery
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
reason: Proposes a visible-thermal CNN for counting and localization of wild Tibetan wild asses (plus domestic sheep), evaluated also on wildlife drone datasets (elephants, Przewalski's gazelle).

title: Integrating aerial optical and bathymetric LiDAR data for coral reef mapping
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
reason: Proposes a deep learning semantic segmentation method for mapping wild corals (colonial animals) on an atoll from aerial RGB imagery and bathymetric LiDAR.

title: Reproducible mapping of marine biodiversity using autonomous surface vehicles and deep learning
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
reason: Deep learning multi-label classification of underwater images of wild coral reef benthos (coral morphotypes, sea urchins, sponges) collected in the field by autonomous surface vehicles.

title: Real-time control of wetlands alters waterbird activity and water quality outcomes
reason: Camera traps in a constructed stormwater wetland record free-ranging waterbirds. A pre-trained YOLOv9e model detects and counts them to study how real-time control of water level affects them.

title: Fine-scale drivers of plateau pika burrow distribution: Integrating UAV deep learning and GAMM to reveal topography–vegetation interactions
reason: Applies U-net semantic segmentation to UAV imagery to detect and count burrows of wild plateau pika (direct animal signs) in alpine meadows.

title: A new method for geometric analysis of mandibular features: A case study of Middle Pleistocene hominin upper condylar region
reason: Geometric analysis of 3D scans of fossil hominin mandible casts and archaeological human bones; specimens, not wild free-ranging animals.

title: RED-YOLO: A lightweight synergistic fusion framework with channel-efficient neck and multi-dimensional attention for underwater small object detection
venue: Journal of Ocean Engineering and Science
reason: Proposes a lightweight YOLOv8-based detector for underwater objects, including marine organisms such as sea cucumbers, sea urchins, starfish and scallops, in underwater benchmark images.

title: Using infrared thermography to understand the thermal ecology of wild bumblebees
reason: Thermal images of wild foraging bumblebees are used only to read temperatures by hand with spot and line tools in FLIR software. No computer vision method is developed or applied; the analysis is statistical modelling of the temperatures.

title: Appendages in zoo-housed animals: application of thermal imaging to study the thermal state of wildlife under human care
reason: Narrative review of infrared thermography of appendages in zoo-housed animals; only illustrative thermal images of zoo animals, no computer vision method.

title: Behavioral patterns of the critically endangered Malayan tiger Panthera tigris jacksoni under captive conditions
reason: Behaviour of four captive Malayan tigers was scored by a human observer from live CCTV feeds. No computer vision or automated image analysis was applied, and all animals were captive.

title: Bio-inspired temporal difference and spatial-frequency gaming network for video camouflaged object detection
reason: Generic video camouflaged object detection method evaluated on VCOD benchmarks (MoCA-Mask, CAD) and also on VSOD/VOS and medical polyp datasets; wildlife is only mentioned as one possible application, not the stated subject.

title: Frequency-context dynamic convolution and a large-scale benchmark dataset for underwater dense image prediction
reason: Proposes a CNN module and a web-sourced underwater instance segmentation dataset of real-world marine scenes, mostly fish. The paper says the category distribution reflects real-world underwater ecology. Detection and segmentation of these underwater organisms is the subject.

title: Meta-contrastive learning with lightweight support-based query interaction for few-shot fine-grained visual classification
reason: Generic few-shot fine-grained visual classification method evaluated on standard benchmarks (CUB, NABirds, Stanford Dogs, mini-ImageNet); animals appear only as benchmark classes and wildlife is not the stated application.

title: Harnessing the power of Squidle+ to develop flexible machine learning models
reason: Develops CNN classifiers on point-annotated seafloor imagery from Australian field campaigns. One of the four classifiers targets hard coral, which are wild animals (Cnidaria). The other targets (kelp, macroalgae, seagrass) are not animals.

title: Cost-effective ecological monitoring in shallow waters using amphibious unmanned aerial vehicles (AUAV) and deep learning-based computer vision
reason: Applies YOLOv8 detection and instance segmentation to AUAV imagery of wild sea cucumbers in a bay in Thailand. A river litter case study is also included.

title: Preliminary evidence of intra-offshore wind farm variation in epibiotic assemblages from automated ROV image analysis
reason: Applies CNN/transformer segmentation and SfM photogrammetry to ROV video of wild epibiotic marine invertebrates on offshore wind turbine foundations.

title: Life in colour: The influence of habitat colouration on the recruitment of coral reef fish
reason: The study is about wild damselfish, but the image analysis only measures the colour of the reef substrate (habitat) inside quadrats. The fish themselves are not analysed in the images, and the paper notes they often hid.

title: Zooplankton as indicators of coastal water quality: a comparative study of PlanktonScope imaging and DNA metabarcoding of seawater and mesh-screened samples
reason: In situ shadowgraph imaging of wild marine zooplankton, with Mask R-CNN segmentation and ResNet classification, compared against eDNA metabarcoding.

title: Complementary acoustic–visual monitoring array for Indo-Pacific humpback dolphin habitat use in the Pearl River Estuary
reason: Deploys YOLOv5-based visual detection of wild Indo-Pacific humpback dolphins from fixed bridge-mounted cameras in the Pearl River Estuary.

title: Combining new technologies with traditional knowledge to improve fishing efficiency and preserve the last Spanish Mediterranean Almadraba
reason: An underwater camera buoy recorded video of wild migratory fish in a tuna trap net at sea. YOLOv9 was evaluated for detecting fish species in this footage. Most of the paper is about policy and participation, but it still contains a primary computer vision application on wild animals.

title: Coral-CRCA: A Color-Reference Chart Automation algorithm for coral bleaching visualization and severity assessment
reason: Computer vision pipeline for assessing bleaching of wild reef corals in field-collected underwater images from the Arabian/Persian Gulf.

title: Patch-level colorimetric quantification of coral bleaching for marine pollution monitoring using standardized CoralWatch references
reason: Computer vision pipeline (dehazing, detection, segmentation, colour matching) to quantify bleaching of corals in ROV imagery from Arabian Gulf reefs; corals are wild animals. The pool tests used artificial coral structures.

title: A non-invasive framework for automated fish monitoring and morphological trait extraction: Implications for ecological monitoring and sustainable fisheries
reason: Deep-learning fish detection, instance segmentation and morphological trait extraction on underwater images. The data mixes natural marine and freshwater habitats (DeepFish, OzFish) with aquaculture settings, so part of the data shows wild fish.

title: An integrated deep learning framework for automated coral health assessment using a custom-annotated database
