reason: Deep learning detection and classification of healthy vs. bleached coral (wild reef animals) in underwater images from documentary footage; primary research.

title: UAV-based super-resolution instance segmentation enables ecological monitoring of sea cucumbers in shallow coral reef habitats
reason: Proposes a UAV-based super-resolution and instance-segmentation framework for wild sea cucumbers on a shallow coral reef flat in Thailand.

title: An algorithm for animal detection and counting in unmanned aerial imagery under complex environments
reason: Proposes a UAV-image animal detection and counting method. It is trained on livestock data and also evaluated on the AOD dataset of African wildlife (zebra, giraffe, impala, wildebeest), so part of the analysed data shows wild animals.

title: Bird hazard detection technology for transmission line towers based on VIF-YOLO model and temporal average DIOU
reason: Computer vision bird detection and behaviour grading on transmission towers; data combine domestic pigeons in a simulated tower scene with web-collected images of wild birds (storks, cormorants, egrets, etc.) on transmission towers.

title: Open-source satellite image pre-processing and annotation workflows: Stranded whale and dolphin case study
reason: Protocol paper for satellite image pre-processing (projection, pansharpening) and manual annotation of stranded cetaceans in QGIS and Python; no automated computer vision analysis of the images is developed, applied or evaluated.

title: On class imbalance in machine learning-based taxa identification: A comparative analysis of mitigation strategies
reason: Classification of insect and macroinvertebrate specimens photographed with laboratory imaging systems (FIN-Benthic2 dual-camera system, BIOSCAN specimen images). The paper describes these as microscopic taxonomic imagery. The images show specimens in an imaging set-up, not free-ranging animals.

title: ChronoPoints: Trajectory-based classification of small flying objects
reason: Proposes a LiDAR point-cloud sequence classifier that separates UAVs from three free-flying bird species recorded outdoors in real-world conditions; birds are classified at species level.

title: Underwater visual tracking with a large scale dataset and image enhancement
reason: Introduces an underwater visual tracking dataset of wild marine creatures (fish, turtles, sharks, dolphins, etc.) captured in the wild, benchmarks trackers and proposes an image enhancement method; primary CV research on wild animals.

title: Boosting tiger re-ID with 360∘ video generation: A generative synthesis approach
reason: Proposes a synthetic 360° video generation framework to train tiger Re-ID models, evaluated on real camera-trap images of wild Amur tigers.

title: Cross-long short distance attention network for noise-robust and multi-scale underwater object detection
reason: The paper proposes a general underwater object detector. Its main case study uses sonar images of man-made objects (UATD). The DUO marine-animal classes serve only as a second benchmark to test generalisation, and wildlife is never stated as the subject or application.

title: SFAPose: Animal pose estimation via flow-field alignment and text-prior assisted localization
reason: Proposes a CNN-based animal pose estimation method evaluated on AP-10K (54 species from 23 families) and AnimalPose (domestic species). Because AP-10K has many non-domestic species, the data mixes wild and domestic animals.

title: Last-layer committee machines for uncertainty estimations of benthic imagery
reason: The benthic images are classified into seafloor substrate and habitat classes such as silt/mud, reef and boulders, not animal taxa. The second dataset is MNIST handwritten digits. No animals are the analysed subject.

title: MIP-Net: Multi-scale inverted pyramid network with local adaptive contrast for underwater object detection
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for underwater marine organisms (sea cucumber, sea urchin, scallop, starfish) in real underwater images from the DUO dataset. COCO is used only to test generalization.

title: Statistical image processing for application in intelligent systems
reason: Image-processing workflow applied to scanning electron microscopy images of nickel nanowire arrays; no animals, laboratory microscopy only.

title: UM-RTDETR: An adaptive detection model for underwater heterogeneous targets
reason: Proposes a transformer-based detector for underwater images. The targets include marine life, and the model is also evaluated on UODD, which has real-world images of marine organisms taken in natural marine environments.

title: Underwater object detection via degradation-aware backbone, spatial-frequency background suppression, and adaptive-gated scale fusion: The DBS-Net Framework
reason: Proposes a deep-learning detector for underwater marine invertebrates (holothurian, echinus, starfish, scallop) in seabed images with sediment and reef backgrounds.

title: U-AsymSeg: Asymmetric dual-stream RGB-Polarization network for underwater semantic segmentation
reason: Generic underwater RGB-polarization semantic segmentation method; animal categories (fish, starfish, conch, shell) appear only as classes alongside mines, UUVs, cups, persons; wildlife is not the stated subject.

title: Artificial intelligence and automated monitoring for Marine Protected Area Management: A case of Chaojing marine protected area in Taiwan
reason: Applies computer vision (instance segmentation of benthos/corals, indicator fish detection and counting) to underwater video of wild reef organisms in a Taiwanese marine protected area.

title: Automated monitoring of insects system: building a non-lethal and scalable solution for monitoring of nocturnal insects
reason: Open-hardware paper describing an insect camera trap; field images of wild nocturnal insects from Costa Rica are analysed with computer vision tools to count insects and filter moths, so it meets the inclusion conditions although CV is a minor part.

title: SF-YOLO: A shallow feature enhancement model based on spatial-frequency dual-stream collaboration for underwater object detection
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for underwater marine organisms (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish) in public underwater image datasets.

title: Polarization-multiplexed metalens and ASFSDI-BiYOLO for underwater polarimetric target detection
reason: Proposes a YOLOv11-based detector for marine organisms (sea cucumber, crab, scallop, starfish) in underwater polarimetric images taken by an underwater robot in seabed scenes. The paper also designs a metalens, but that part has no animal images.

title: YOLO-FCE: A feature and clustering enhanced object detection model for species classification
reason: Proposes a YOLOv9-based detector for classifying 50 Australian wild animal species in images captured in natural environments (GBIF images).

title: FG-MoE: Heterogeneous mixture of experts model for fine-grained visual classification
reason: Generic fine-grained visual classification method evaluated on standard FGVC benchmarks (birds, dog breeds); wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: Hyperanimal: Identity hypersphere guided synthetic datasets generation for individual animal identification
reason: Synthetic image generation for individual animal identification evaluated on red pandas in indoor breeding environments, giant panda streaming videos and Amur tigers in zoos; the analysed data show no free-ranging animals.

title: WildAnimal650+: A large-scale annotated dataset for generalized animal segmentation in unconstrained environments
reason: Introduces a pixel-level segmentation dataset of 658 animal species, mostly wild, taken from documentary footage. It benchmarks segmentation models on it, with wildlife and biodiversity monitoring as the stated application. A cross-dataset comparison uses a pet dataset, and a few livestock classes (e.g. Cow) also appear.

title: PGMM: Prior Guided Multi-expert Model for Long-tailed Classification
reason: A generic method for long-tailed image classification, tested on CIFAR-LT, ImageNet-LT and iNaturalist 2018. Wildlife is not the stated subject or application.

title: ReMatch: Re-identification of patterned species in open-set scenarios by matching keypoints and lines
reason: Proposes a keypoint/line matching pipeline for individual re-identification of wild patterned animals (lizards, zebras, seals, whale sharks), with human fingerprints as an extra test set.

title: VLKD-YOLO: A semantic-aware visual-language distillation framework for lightweight underwater object detection
reason: Proposes a CV detection method for underwater marine organisms (fish, echinus, holothurians, jellyfish, corals) evaluated on underwater benchmarks; the training corpus also includes an Aquarium dataset, so subjects are mixed.

title: High-resolution underwater camouflaged object detection: GBU-UCOD dataset and topology-aware and frequency-decoupled networks
reason: Introduces a benchmark and a segmentation network for camouflaged marine organisms in underwater videos of free-ranging animals.

title: A lightweight high-resolution feature aggregation design for animal pose estimation
reason: Proposes a lightweight CNN for animal pose estimation. It is evaluated on the multi-species AP-10K benchmark and on a dataset the authors collected of caged macaques. The data mixes captive animals with a general animal benchmark, and the stated application is animal monitoring.

title: A Hybrid Probabilistic Framework for Robust Object Detection under Limited Training Data
reason: Proposes a hybrid probabilistic detection framework applied to drone images of Arabian oryx in nature reserves for wildlife monitoring.

title: Real-Time Animal Monitoring and Identification Using Deep Computer Vision
reason: Computer vision framework for detecting and classifying animals in video; the dataset contains 32 wild and 14 domestic animal classes recorded in natural habitats and taken from YouTube, so wild animals are part of the data.

title: Enhanced Butterfly Image Segmentation Using Deep Encoder–Decoder Based Architecture
reason: Proposes a deep encoder-decoder segmentation model for butterflies in ecological images (Leeds dataset and field-collected images from a natural environment).

title: DeepEcoTrack: Aquatic Object Detection and Eco-Health Monitoring
reason: Deep learning detection of underwater pollutants and marine organisms in underwater imagery; marine life in natural aquatic environments is among the detected subjects.

title: Image classification and object detection complexity optimization: Exploring deep learning models on camera trap and surveillance clips
reason: Proposes a CNN resolution-selection framework for classifying animal species in camera-trap images of wild animals (Missouri camera trap dataset).

title: Smart surveillance with conversational alerts for wild elephant early warning
venue: Remote Sensing Applications Society and Environment
reason: Applies YOLOv8 detection to CCTV and camera-trap images of wild elephants for human-elephant conflict early warning.

title: Deep learning for UAV thermal bird detection: Benchmarking YOLOv8–YOLOv26
venue: Remote Sensing Applications Society and Environment
reason: Benchmarks YOLO detectors on UAV thermal images of wild little bustards in Spain.

title: CubeSat constellation shines light on fisheries studies: A case study of fish mortality events
venue: Remote Sensing Applications Society and Environment
reason: Primary study applying image analysis (thresholding, spectral similarity, morphological thinning) to satellite imagery to detect and quantify floating dead wild fish in a river and a coastal bay.

title: What's in a coral pixel? Spatial variability in co-occurrence patterns for coral reef benthic communities
venue: Remote Sensing Applications Society and Environment
reason: Applies machine-learning image classification (CoralNet, ReefCloud) to field photoquadrats of wild coral reef benthos (hard and soft corals) to derive benthic cover for spatial co-occurrence analysis.

title: Mapping rodent-induced disturbance of biological soil crusts using PlanetScope imagery and deep-learning-informed graph cut
reason: Deep-learning segmentation of satellite imagery to map burrow systems (direct signs) of wild burrowing rodents in a desert; primary research.

title: Use of AI-mediated image analysis to investigate the influence of environmental factors and recreational scuba diving on fish activity patterns in a marine protected area
reason: Applies YOLOv5 to footage from an unmanned underwater camera to detect, classify and count wild reef fish in a marine protected area.

title: An innovative photogrammetric approach for the monitoring of the endangered fan mussel Pinna nobilis: A case study from the Venice Lagoon
reason: Applies Structure-from-Motion photogrammetry to underwater images of a wild Pinna nobilis population in the Venice Lagoon to reconstruct 3D models and measure individuals.

title: Mapping rocky intertidal zonation using drone-derived multispectral and elevation data with Random Forest classification
reason: Applies Random Forest classification to drone multispectral images to map wild sessile benthic animal assemblages (mussels, barnacles, tunicates) on rocky intertidal platforms.

title: AI and computer vision for wildlife identification in camera trap images: Fine-tuning SpeciesNet outperforms local models for species classification
reason: Compares global, local and fine-tuned CNN species classifiers on camera-trap images of free-ranging wildlife in the Australian Wet Tropics rainforests. A few classes are domestic animals (cattle, dogs).

title: ThermalBird-Mamba: Thermal adaptive state space learning for real time UAV bird detection under low contrast and cluttered backgrounds
venue: The Science of The Total Environment
reason: Proposes a deep learning detector for wild birds (little bustard and other steppe birds) in UAV thermal imagery from field surveys in Spain.

title: Seagrass habitat mapping using UAV imagery in a port environment in Sabah, Malaysia
reason: The paper maps seagrass and benthic substrate habitat classes from UAV imagery. Animals are not the subject of the image analysis.

title: Advanced marine data analytics and underwater object detection using mask R-CNN for ecosystem monitoring
reason: Mask R-CNN detection and segmentation of marine animals in underwater images for marine ecosystem monitoring. The paper does not say whether the animals were wild or captive.

title: ASMAG-TRC: A Safety-Arbitrated Runtime Architecture for Adaptive Inference Control on Resource-Constrained Edge AI Cameras
reason: Runtime inference-control architecture for edge surveillance cameras, evaluated on change-detection benchmarks showing people and vehicles. The paper is not about animals and analyses no wildlife.

title: Vision-based Camel Detection and VMS Alert System for Enhanced Road Safety in KSA
reason: Detects free-roaming but owned (domestic) camels near roads in Saudi Arabia, using web images that include highways, deserts and captivity. Camels are domestic livestock kept by camel owners, not wild animals.

title: Continuous diurnal monitoring of pollinator activity in urban rain gardens using camera traps, unsupervised machine learning algorithms, and deep learning detection: A proof-of-concept
reason: Camera-trap video of free-ranging pollinating insects in urban rain gardens and a restored prairie, used to train a YOLOv8n detector for pollinator classes.

title: Assessing Zooplankton Communities' Influence on Particulate Organic Carbon Concentration
reason: Analyses in situ UVP5 images of wild marine zooplankton. It extracts image features (gray level, shape, size), builds a morphospace with PCA and k-means, and derives community metrics that are related to POC gradients.

title: Quantification of molar sub-regions suggests increasing herbivory during primate origins
reason: Computer vision segmentation is applied to 3D µCT surface meshes of museum and fossil tooth specimens, not to images of living wild animals. Museum specimens fall under E-CAPTIVE.

title: CzechLynx: A Dataset for Individual Identification and Pose Estimation of the Eurasian Lynx
reason: Dataset paper presenting camera trap images of wild Eurasian lynx annotated for individual identification, pose estimation and instance segmentation, with a complementary synthetic set.

title: A wild fish image dataset for individual re-identification and phenotyping.
reason: Dataset paper presenting images of wild-caught, PIT-tagged corkwing wrasse from a capture-mark-recapture survey, with YOLOv8 detection and keypoint models trained and evaluated on the images.

title: A long-term photographic dataset for individual identification of the Balearic wall lizard.
reason: Data descriptor of a photographic dataset of wild, field-captured Balearic wall lizards for individual re-identification, with a computer vision segmentation pipeline (Grounded-SAM, YOLOv8) applied to the images.

title: Genes, shells, and AI: using computer vision to detect cryptic morphological divergence between genetically distinct populations of limpets
reason: Images are of dry limpet shell specimens (field-collected and museum) photographed under standardised studio conditions, not of free-ranging animals in the wild.

title: The use of multi-sensor drone data for the development and validation of methods to track and characterize marine animals
reason: Develops and validates drone video-based methods (semi-automated tracking with mean shift, photogrammetric length/position estimation) for free-swimming wild white sharks.

title: Estimated predator composition using environmental DNA analyses and color patterns of male guppies in introduced rivers
reason: Wild introduced guppies were photographed, but color spots were traced by hand in Inkscape and pixel areas measured. The authors explicitly rejected an automated tool. The main analysis is eDNA metabarcoding plus GLMM statistics, with no computer vision method.

title: An efficient and consistent framework for multi-rank taxonomic identification in wildlife images
reason: Proposes a multi-rank detection and classification model (TaxonomyNet with WAL correction) trained and evaluated on camera-trap and public-submission images of 50 Australian animal species in natural environments.

title: A novel deep learning approach for mosquito species classification via a dual-head structure and calibration-aware fusion architecture
reason: Deep learning classification of mosquito species (wild vector insects) from smartphone/citizen-science whole-body images for vector surveillance.

title: Deep learning based individual identification and population estimation of the yellow spotted mountain newt (Neurergus derjugini)
reason: Primary study applying classical image processing and CNNs to smartphone photographs of wild-caught and released newts for individual identification and population estimation.

title: High-resolution in situ imaging reveals size-specific moonlight responses in zooplankton diel vertical migration
reason: Primary field study applying an in situ plankton imager and a CNN image classifier to free-living freshwater zooplankton in a lake to quantify diel vertical migration.

title: Hyperparameter optimization to enhance the performance of deep learning models for the early detection of invasive turtles in Korea
reason: YOLO11s object detection applied to citizen-science (iNaturalist) images of six invasive freshwater turtle species for early detection; primary research on non-domestic animals.

title: Ultraviolet light illuminates species-specific biofluorescent casque patterns in cassowaries (Casuarius)
reason: Images analysed show museum-preserved cassowary specimens and live captive birds at a conservation facility, zoos and farms; no free-ranging wild animals were imaged.

title: Coral morphology detection in underwater imagery using YOLOv12 with CNN and transformer encoder fusion
reason: Proposes a YOLOv12 CNN-transformer fusion detector for coral morphology (corals are animals) in underwater reef images from a public dataset.

title: YOLO-Starfish: fish object detection learning complex underwater features
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for fish in natural underwater freshwater environments, using a new dataset built from web videos that shows both farmed and natural freshwater species.

title: Improving rare-class detection in deep-sea imagery via generative augmentation with stable diffusion
reason: Primary study proposing generative augmentation to improve object detection of wild deep-sea megabenthos in seafloor survey imagery collected by OTV and AUV.

title: Inferring sperm whale (Physeter macrocephalus) sex and developmental stage using aerial photogrammetry
reason: Drone video photogrammetry of wild sperm whales off Galápagos: image-based morphometric measurement used to infer sex and developmental stage.

title: An efficient method for monitoring small bird targets in wetland environments based on object detection
reason: Proposes a YOLOv8n-based detector (RLCB-YOLO) for small wild birds in images collected by the authors in a wetland park.

title: HST-former: hierarchical spatio-temporal aggregation for video-based animal re-identification
reason: Proposes a computer vision method for individual re-identification of animals on image/video datasets; the Saimaa ringed seal data are wild animals, while the meerkat data come from a zoo, so the subjects are mixed.

title: Design and implementation of a fine-grained detection method for Qinghai Lake birds via fusion of knowledge guidance and feature enhancement
reason: Proposes a YOLOv8-based detector (YOLO_BD) for wild birds imaged at Qinghai Lake Bird Island Nature Reserve; primary research on images of free-ranging birds.

title: Improving wildlife track classification through human-in-the-loop method and explainable AI
reason: Primary study training a CNN detector/classifier on field-collected images of tracks (direct signs) of free-ranging wildlife in Botswana reserves.

title: In situ swimming behavior of the Mariana snailfish Pseudoliparis swirei
reason: Applies a computer vision pipeline (segmentation, tracking, monocular depth estimation) to in situ baited lander video of wild Mariana snailfish in the hadal zone.

title: A two-stage OOD-aware approach for mosquito species detection based on RT-DETRv2
reason: Proposes a vision-based detector for mosquito species (non-domestic, free-living insects) using real-world images, largely from iNaturalist; primary method research.

title: Class-incremental few-shot underwater object detection framework
reason: Proposes a few-shot, class-incremental object detection framework for underwater images and tests it on underwater datasets that contain free-ranging marine animals (fish, crabs, jellyfish, starfish, and others) for ecological monitoring.

title: An accurate, efficient, and accessible AI-powered solution for wildlife re-identification in conservation
reason: Primary study presenting a computer vision system for individual re-identification of wild Masai giraffes from field survey photographs.

title: An intelligent SCADA-integrated deep learning framework for bird-safe offshore wind farm operation
reason: Primary study that trains a CNN to classify images of 525 bird species, with bird protection at offshore wind farms as the stated application. The paper does not say how or where the images were taken, so wild versus captive origin is not reported.

title: Underwater biological target detection algorithm based on DVS-YOLO11
reason: Proposes a YOLO11-based detector for underwater marine organisms (sea cucumber, sea urchin, scallop, starfish) in underwater images from the public DUO and RUOD datasets.

title: Deep learning-based body length estimation in soil-dwelling arthropods
reason: Deep learning regression of body length from images of soil arthropods; part of the data are field-collected wild soil fauna from Hungary (Test 3), the rest are laboratory cultures.

title: Reappraisal of the extinct barbelthroat shark †Bavariscyllium and the nebulous origin of carcharhiniform galeomorphs
reason: Palaeontological study of fossil shark specimens; body measurements taken manually in ImageJ and analysed with PCA/LDA and parsimony. No computer vision method is applied to images of living wild animals.

title: Unraveling hidden species diversity of talpid moles using phylogenomics and skull-based deep learning
reason: The CNN classifies photos of museum skull specimens of talpid moles. No live wild animals are imaged, and museum specimens fall under E-CAPTIVE.

title: Stay Local or Go Global: Geo-Referenced Bounding Boxes for Tracking Wildlife in Thermal Drone Videos
reason: Proposes geo-referenced multi-object tracking for wildlife in thermal drone videos; data recorded in wild animal enclosures as well as natural habitats.

title: CCFF‐Net: Cross‐Channel Feature Fusion Network for Underwater Object Detection
reason: Generic underwater object detection method evaluated on benchmark datasets of echinus, holothurian, starfish and scallops. The only data source the paper describes is open-sea aquaculture (UDD). No wild or conservation setting is stated.

title: Design and Development of a YOLOv8-Based Automatic Repellent System for Preventing Crop Raiding by Peacocks
reason: Applies YOLOv8 detection to webcam video of wild peacocks raiding agricultural fields to trigger a non-lethal deterrent (human-wildlife conflict).

title: Intelligent Multi-Modal Monitoring Framework for Birds in Forest Ecosystems and Zoo Animals through AI, CCTV, IR, and Drone Surveillance
reason: Proposes and reports results for an AI/CNN-based CCTV, IR and drone monitoring system that detects and classifies free-ranging forest birds together with zoo animals.

title: Vision-Based Elephant Behavior and Posture Recognition for Early Human–Elephant Conflict Mitigation
reason: Vision-based (YOLOv8 + DeepSORT + LSTM) posture and behaviour recognition of free-ranging elephants in surveillance and wildlife video for human-elephant conflict mitigation.

title: Remote underwater video and analysis with AI show differences between fish communities at chain moorings and at Environmentally Friendly Moorings
reason: Primary study applying a YOLO object-detection model to baited and unbaited remote underwater video of wild demersal fish at mooring and reference sites in Tasmania.

title: Elucidating the potential of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) and satellite imagery for the improvement of coral reef community mapping
reason: Pixel-based benthic habitat mapping of a coral reef (sand, rock, rubble, dead coral, live coral cover classes) from UAV and satellite imagery. It is habitat or land-cover mapping, not analysis of individual animals.

title: Drone surveys of birds foraging in intertidal habitats: a proof-of-concept in Moreton Bay, Australia
reason: Proof-of-concept drone survey of wild birds foraging on an intertidal mudflat; a computer vision tool is applied to detect and classify birds in drone image mosaics and evaluated against manual annotation.

title: Using unmanned aerial vehicles to estimate the abundance, density, body size structure, and seasonal site use of Caiman yacare in the northeastern Pantanal, Brazil
venue: Studies on Neotropical Fauna and Environment
reason: Wild Caiman yacare were surveyed with drone images, but people counted them in real time and measured body length by hand in ImageJ. No computer vision method was developed or applied.

title: Detection of One-Horned Rhino in Thermal Images Using Deep Model Architectures
reason: Computer vision detection of one-horned rhinos, but all analysed thermal images were captured in a zoo (Assam State Zoo cum Botanical Garden); no wild or free-ranging animals in the data.

title: Context-Aware YOLO Transformer Fusion with IoT -Driven Adaptation for Robust Underwater Object Detection
reason: Proposes a YOLO-Transformer detection model applied to underwater images of aquatic animals (fish, jellyfish, penguin, puffin, shark, starfish, stingray), with marine ecology assessment as a stated application. The paper does not say whether the animals were wild or captive.

title: Supporting post-bushfire biodiversity through citizen science tourism: recovery, regeneration, and reflections
reason: Citizen science tourism program paper; tourists submit photos and observations of wildlife, but no computer vision or automated image analysis is developed or applied. Analyses are survey statistics (chi-square, Cramer's V).

title: Deep learning-based monitoring and localization in autonomous underwater vehicle networks for aquatic ecosystem analysis
venue: Journal of Environmental Science and Health Part A
reason: Proposes a deep learning framework (DSRCN) that classifies aquatic species in underwater images from AUV networks; the images are of a natural marine environment. The paper never names the animals in its image data, so subject_type is not_reported and inclusion is borderline.

title: MREM-YOLO: a lightweight underwater object detection algorithm based on improved YOLOv8
venue: International Journal of Computers and Applications
reason: Proposes a YOLOv8-based detector for marine organisms (holothurian, echinus, scallop, starfish) in underwater images from the DUO and URPC2020 datasets. The URPC2020 images were taken by underwater robots in real underwater environments.

title: CRUHI-Mamba: a Mamba-based underwater hyperspectral image classification framework for coral reef benthic mapping
reason: Proposes a Mamba-based method that classifies underwater hyperspectral images of natural coral reef benthos, including wild coral and sponge species, captured in the field off Curaçao.

title: Developing a simple automatic elephant detection system aimed at achieving individual recognition in a specific forest site using image processing and supervised machine learning
reason: Primary study developing a Haar cascade detector and eigenfaces + KNN individual recognition on camera-trap video of wild elephants in Kibale National Park, Uganda.

title: Fish recognition and interpretability mechanisms based on the VGG model – a case study of Thunnus albacares
reason: CNN image classification with interpretability analysis on images of wild-caught yellowfin tuna from a research longline survey and web underwater images.

title: Enhancing marine species detection and classification with a hybrid GCS-Yolov5-Hcnn model for underwater monitoring
venue: International Journal of Image and Data Fusion
reason: Primary study proposing a detection and classification model for marine species on a web-sourced sea animal image dataset; the paper frames the images as underwater marine images but does not state whether the animals are wild or captive.

title: Untapped potential of European natural history collections of megadiverse Diptera
reason: Survey of European natural history collections holding Diptera specimens. The paper analyses no images or video; it compiles questionnaire data from the collections.

title: A multidisciplinary assessment of endocrine and morphometric correlates of lactation physiology in southern right whales
reason: Analyses UAV video stills of free-swimming southern right whales with photogrammetry to measure body condition, linked to blubber hormone data. Image analysis is manual photogrammetric measurement, a borderline case for the computer-vision criterion.

title: Energetic benefits of resting behaviour in humpback whale mother–calf pairs revealed by biologging and UAS-photogrammetry
reason: Field study of wild humpback whales in Hawaiʻi that measures morphometrics from drone (UAS) video by photogrammetry. The image analysis is part of a biologging energetics study.

title: The MESOSCAN dataset: a collection of mesofauna images from UK forest and peatland soils
venue: Forestry An International Journal of Forest Research
reason: The mesofauna were collected from UK forest and peatland soils, but they were extracted, preserved in ethanol and photographed as specimens in a laboratory macro-photography enclosure. No live free-ranging animals were imaged, so this is specimen-based imaging.

title: 3D Imaging of Honeybee Swarm Assembly and Disassembly
reason: Study images artificial swarms of managed European honeybees taken from hives in an apiary (beekeeping), so it falls under the agriculture/beekeeping exclusion.

title: Deep learning for accurate vision-based catch composition in tropical tuna purse seiners
reason: Computer vision pipeline (segmentation, tracking, classification) applied to video of wild-caught tropical tunas on purse seiner conveyor belts for catch composition estimation in fisheries monitoring.

title: Stability shifts in gliding flight: hawks morph from an unstable to stable state when navigating a gap
venue: Journal of The Royal Society Interface
reason: Motion capture of one captive-bred, trained Harris's hawk flying in an indoor flight hall. No wild or free-ranging animals appear in the data.

title: Fine-scale spatiotemporal predator–prey interactions in an Antarctic fur seal colony
reason: Applies a YOLO-based detector to time-lapse images of a wild Antarctic fur seal breeding colony and its avian predator-scavengers, then uses the detections to study predator-prey interactions.

title: Using machine learning effectively in marine benthic ecology: a question-driven toolkit
reason: Workshop participants trained interactive U-Net segmentation models (RootPainter) on time-lapse and ROV imagery of wild benthic fish, crustaceans, corals and sponges in the NW and NE Atlantic. The paper analyses these models and user perceptions.

title: Unlocking a hidden fossil archive: synchrotron micro-computed tomography illuminates ‘ghost’ radiolarians linked to Late Ordovician oceanic anoxic events
reason: Synchrotron microCT imaging of fossil radiolarian specimens in rock mini-cores; no living wild or free-ranging animals are imaged, so the subjects are specimens.

title: Variation in body size growth trajectories between ecologically distinct mountain gorilla populations
venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences
reason: Applies image-based parallel-laser photogrammetry to photos of wild habituated mountain gorillas to measure body size growth.

title: The presence of mahi-mahi at multi-predator feeding aggregations modifies striped marlin attack behaviour
venue: Philosophical Transactions of the Royal Society B Biological Sciences
reason: UAV video of wild pelagic predators (striped marlin, mahi-mahi) is analysed for behaviour, and a computer vision tracking pipeline is used to detect, classify and track the animals.

title: NeuralFur: Animal Fur Reconstruction from Multi-View Images
reason: Computer-graphics method for strand-based fur reconstruction aimed at animated film assets; evaluated on the Artemis multi-view dataset and a synthetic tiger asset. The paper does not say that any of the data shows wild or free-ranging animals and states no wildlife application. It notes that such multi-view data may not be available for in-the-wild animals.

title: AI Vision System of Ocean Deep-Sea Fish Schools and Sea Collisions Mitigation Sustainability: Energy-Efficient
reason: Proposes a YOLOv13-based detector for fish in underwater images from natural marine habitats of tropical Australia (DeepFish), so computer vision is applied to wild, free-ranging animals.

title: A Step Toward Instrument-Agnostic Plankton Classification in the Shared Label Space of IFCB and FlowCam Data
reason: Marine plankton (mostly phytoplankton) were sampled from the sea by research vessel and then imaged with imaging flow cytometers (IFCB, FlowCam). This is microscopy-type laboratory imaging of water samples, not imaging of free-ranging animals in their habitat.

title: DINO-Explorer: Active Underwater Discovery via Ego-Motion Compensated Semantic Predictive Coding
reason: Computer vision method (DINOv3-based semantic surprise) applied to ROV video of wild marine habitats and fauna, including animal behaviour events such as fish trajectory changes, for ecosystem monitoring.

title: Low-Light Animal Detection on Highways Using Enhanced YOLOv5 and Image Preprocessing Techniques
venue: OPJU International Technology Conference on Smart Computing for Innovation and Advancement in Industry (OTCON)
reason: Applies YOLOv5 with CLAHE/Retinex preprocessing to detect wild animals (deer, fox, bear) in nighttime forest and highway images.

title: BirdNet-XAI: A Hybrid EfficientNetB0-ViT Model with Explainable AI for Fine-Grained Classification of Native Bangladeshi Birds
venue: 2026 International Conference on Power Electronics Communications Computing and Intelligent Infrastructure Peccii 2026
reason: Proposes a hybrid CNN-ViT model with XAI to classify images of 15 native (wild) Bangladeshi bird species for biodiversity monitoring.

title: Smart City Myths in the Wild: A Post-Mortem of an Edge AI Energy Failure in Wildlife Deterrence
venue: IEEE International Conference on Pervasive Computing and Communications Workshops and other Affiliated Events (PerCom Workshops)
reason: Field-deployed edge AI system that uses camera-based detection (YOLOv8, VIS/NIR and thermal) of wild predators (wolves, bears) and deer on pastures. Livestock and other non-target animals also appear in the images. The paper is a primary post-mortem of a field deployment.

title: A Deep Learning Approach for Identifying Endangered Animals in Bangladesh
venue: 2026 IEEE 2nd International Conference on Quantum Photonics Artificial Intelligence and Networking Qpain 2026
reason: Applies CNN image classification to photos of 10 endangered wild animal species (web-sourced) for conservation monitoring.

title: Multimodal Integration of Sensors with Computer Vision to Detect and Alert Wild Animal Intrusion
venue: 2026 International Conference on Recent Advances in Electrical Electronics Ubiquitous Communication and Computational Intelligence Raeeucci 2026
reason: Applies YOLOv8 detection and DeepSORT tracking to images of wild animals (tigers, elephants, leopards, wild boars) to mitigate human-wildlife conflict.

title: AI-Based Wildlife Crossing Detection and Alert System
venue: 2026 International Conference on Recent Advances in Electrical Electronics Ubiquitous Communication and Computational Intelligence Raeeucci 2026
reason: Primary study applying CNN object detectors to images of wildlife species (tiger, elephant, rhinoceros, buffalo, giraffe) together with domestic animals (cow, horse) for a wildlife-vehicle collision alert system. The paper does not state whether the source images show free-ranging animals; the test frames were captured in a controlled environment.

title: InceptionResNetV2-Based Deep Learning Framework for Multi-Class Classification of Reptile and Amphibian Species
venue: IEEE International Students' Conference on Electrical, Electronics and Computer Science (SCEECS)
reason: Applies a CNN (InceptionResNetV2 transfer learning) to classify images of non-domestic reptiles and amphibians for biodiversity monitoring.

title: A Hybrid Framework for Human-Wildlife Conflict Mitigation Using Infrared-Triggered YOLO and IoT Alerting
venue: 2026 IEEE International Students Conference on Electrical Electronics and Computer Science Sceecs 2026
reason: Applies YOLOv11s detection to images of wild animals (elephants, tigers) together with domestic animals (cows, goats) for human-wildlife conflict alerting. It also evaluates on the African Wildlife and iWildCam datasets.

title: A Multi-Modal Sensor Fusion System for Detecting sUAS, Wildlife, and Aircraft near Airports
venue: Systems and Information Engineering Design Symposium
reason: Conceptual systems-design paper for an airport multi-sensor surveillance architecture; no image data is analysed and no computer vision method is developed or evaluated.

title: Coral Reef Damage Classification Using ResNet50 and MobileNetV2
venue: International Conference on Smart Computing, IoT and Machine Learning (SIML)
reason: Primary study applying CNN image classification to underwater images of reef corals (animals) to distinguish healthy from bleached colonies for reef monitoring and conservation.

title: Animal Re-Identification on Microcontrollers
venue: Proceedings 2026 IEEE International Conference on Smart Internet of Things Smartiot 2026
reason: Primary study on image-based animal re-identification. The data cover non-domestic species (tigers, lions, pandas) together with domestic cattle and dogs, and wildlife monitoring is a stated application. The paper does not say whether the tiger, lion and panda images show wild or captive animals, so inclusion rests on the species being non-domestic.

title: Edge-Optimized DINOv3-YOLOv8-DeepSORT: A Self-Supervised Approach for Real-Time Cross-Dataset Wildlife Surveillance
venue: International Conference on System of Systems Engineering Sose
reason: Proposes a DINOv3-YOLOv8-DeepSORT detection and tracking framework for wildlife monitoring. It is evaluated on SAWIT, which shows small wild animals in natural environments, and on a custom dataset that also contains domestic animals (cat, cattle).

title: Leveraging Pretrained ResNet Architectures for Enhanced Real-Time Bat Counting
reason: Applies pretrained CNNs to count free-flying wild bats in video of colony emergences at cave exits.

title: A human-in-the-loop solution for individual leopard identification in unlabeled camera trap images
venue: IEEE Transactions on Automation Science and Engineering
reason: Primary study proposing a human-in-the-loop individual identification algorithm applied to camera trap images of wild African leopards.

title: M4FT: Mamba, Migratory, Mobile, and Multiple Fish Tracking
venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology
reason: Proposes a vision tracking framework for fish evaluated on underwater video of fish in real-world/wild waters (BrackishMOT, FishTrack23) as well as aquaculture (MFT22).

title: PhyTrans: Learning Phylogenetic Relationships for FBIC via Hierarchical Taxonomy Representation
venue: IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology
reason: Proposes a fine-grained bird species classification method (PhyTrans), motivated by bird conservation, evaluated on bird image datasets (CUB-200-2011, NABirds) of birds in natural habitats; also tests on dog and cat images for generalization.

title: Domain-Adaptive Benthonic Organism Detection via Uniformizing Light Field and Color Distribution
reason: Proposes a domain-adaptive CNN detector for benthic marine organisms (echinus, scallop, starfish, holothurian) in underwater images from the URPC2020 and DUO datasets and ROV footage. The intro mentions marine ranching, but the paper never says the data show farmed animals.

title: Unsupervised Domain Adaptation for Fish Counting: From Optical to Forward-Looking Sonar Images
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
reason: Computer vision fish counting on optical and sonar images; part of the data comes from an aquaculture cage (farmed Atlantic salmon), but the SonarFC2 and ARIS datasets show fish in ocean, river and lagoon environments, so subject type is mixed.

title: YOLO-UOD: Location-Edge Co-Perception Network With Multiscale Features Fusion for Underwater Object Detection
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for marine organisms (holothurians, echini, scallops, starfish, fish, turtles etc.) in underwater images, motivated by ecological monitoring. The paper does not say whether the animals were farmed or wild; it treats them as marine organisms in natural underwater environments.

title: CoralSMIA: Physically Grounded Scattering Modeling and Illumination Adaptation for Generalized Underwater Coral Segmentation
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
reason: Proposes a computer vision method for segmenting wild corals in underwater images collected in natural reefs across several sea areas.

title: A Lightweight Reliability-Aware Visible–Infrared Decision-Level Fusion Framework for Spotted Seal Monitoring in Complex Marine Environments
venue: IEEE Transactions on Geoscience and Remote Sensing
reason: Proposes a detection and visible–infrared fusion method for wild spotted seals in UAV imagery of nearshore marine environments.

title: HFP-SAM: Hierarchical Frequency Prompted SAM for Efficient Marine Animal Segmentation
reason: Proposes a SAM-based segmentation method for marine animals in underwater images and evaluates it on public marine animal datasets.

title: Expose Camouflage in the Water: Underwater Camouflaged Instance Segmentation and Dataset
reason: Proposes a SAM-based instance segmentation method and a new dataset (UCIS4K) of camouflaged marine organisms photographed in underwater scenes; applications include ecological preservation.

title: SkeFormer: Skeletal Cues-Aware Bone Point Relationship Learning for Efficient FBIC via Transformers
reason: Proposes a Transformer method for fine-grained bird species classification motivated by identifying endangered birds in outdoor environments; evaluated on bird datasets (CUB-200-2011, NABirds) of birds in natural environments.

title: HitBack: Transformer With Hierarchical-Semantic Cross Attention and Background Contrast for Weakly Supervised Wildlife Semantic Segmentation
reason: Proposes a weakly supervised semantic segmentation method and a new pixel-annotated dataset for wildlife camera-trap images from the Serengeti.

title: IO-MOT: Dual-Modal Feature Fusion With Instance Embeddings and Optical Flow for Multi-Object Tracking
reason: Generic multi-object tracking method evaluated on human dance and sports benchmarks plus one bird tracking benchmark; wildlife is not the stated subject of the paper.

title: Band-Mixed Edge-Aware Interaction Learning for RGB-T Camouflaged Object Detection
reason: Generic RGB-thermal camouflaged object detection method and dataset. The objects are mostly camouflaged personnel and vehicles; animals appear only in a wildlife-park scene, and wildlife is not the stated subject.

title: HomLLM: Exploiting Semantic Homology Relationship for Fine-Grained Bird Image Classification via Large Language Models
venue: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
reason: Proposes a vision-language method for fine-grained classification of wild bird species (CUB-200-2011, NABirds), motivated by biodiversity conservation; an extension experiment also uses domestic dog images (Stanford Dogs).

title: AquaticCLIP: A Vision-Language Foundation Model and Dataset for Underwater Scene Analysis
venue: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
reason: Proposes a vision-language foundation model for underwater scene analysis, applied to classification, detection, segmentation and counting of marine animals (fish, corals) in natural aquatic imagery.

title: PteFBIC: Exploiting Pterylotic Relationship for Fine-Grained Bird Image Classification via Rachidian Orientation Learning
venue: IEEE Transactions on Neural Networks and Learning Systems
reason: Proposes a bird-specific fine-grained classification method motivated by ecological monitoring, evaluated on bird image datasets (CUB-200-2011, NABirds) showing birds in natural scenes. Birds are the stated subject, so this is not E-GENERIC.

title: AniMer+: Unified Pose and Shape Estimation Across Mammalia and Aves via Family-Aware Transformer
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
reason: Proposes a transformer for 3D pose and shape estimation of mammals and birds from images; evaluated on in-the-wild animal images (Animal Kingdom, CUB) alongside domestic animals and synthetic data.

title: Concept Drift and Long-Tailed Distribution in Fine-Grained Visual Categorization: Benchmark and Method
venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
reason: The main dataset (CDLT) contains images of succulent plants. Animals appear only as classes in generic fine-grained benchmarks (CUB, Stanford Dogs, Oxford Pets, NABirds), which are used to test general methods and CLIP.

title: WILDWATCH: Intelligent Animal Monitoring and Protection for Farmlands
venue: International Conference on Trends in Quantum Computing and Emerging Business Technologies (TQCEBT)
reason: Applies YOLO-based detection to images of wild animals (elephants, wild boars, deer, Indian bison, bears) plus cows to detect intrusion into farmland; the data includes wild animals.

title: Deep Learning-Based Benthonic Organism Detection: Fuzzy Channel--Spatial Attention
venue: IEEE Transactions on Systems Man and Cybernetics Systems
reason: Proposes a deep learning detector for benthic organisms (echinus, scallop, starfish, holothurian) in real-world underwater seabed images from public datasets.

title: Split Deep Inference for Underwater Image Classification over Low-Bitrate Acoustic Links
reason: The paper is about split DNN inference and compressing feature maps for acoustic links, tested on CIFAR-100 and the Aqua20 underwater image dataset. Animals and wildlife are never stated as the subject, and no animal taxa are named.

title: Comparison of Deep Learning Methods For Jellyfish Aurelia Aurita Over Surface Detection Utilizing Augmentation
venue: IEEE Ural-Siberian Conference on Biomedical Engineering, Radioelectronics and Information Technology (USBEREIT)
reason: CNN classification of above-surface sea images for presence of wild moon jellyfish (Aurelia aurita) recorded on Istanbul coasts and from social media.

title: Edge AI Wildlife Classification with FPGA-Based Deterministic Deterrence on PYNQ-Z2
venue: International Symposium on VLSI Design and Test (VDAT)
reason: Applies CNN image classification to wildlife species (bear, deer, elephant, monkey, wild boar etc.) for human-wildlife conflict deterrence; dataset also includes domestic animals (cow, goat, horse).

title: Overcoming Fine-Grained Visual Challenges in Animal Re-Identification via Semantic Feature Alignment
venue: Proceedings 2026 IEEE Cvf Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision Wacv 2026
reason: Proposes a CLIP-based animal re-identification framework evaluated on animal ReID benchmarks (including cattle and dogs) and a newly collected real-world stoat dataset for wildlife monitoring.

title: One-Shot Fine-Grained Re-Identification of Paint Marked Honey Bees using Vision Foundation Models
venue: 2026 IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
reason: Computer vision re-identification of free-flying paint-marked honey bee foragers recorded at an outdoor bee feeder, framed as pollinator behaviour and ecological monitoring. The paper does not describe a hive-monitoring or beekeeping study.

title: MarineEval: Assessing the Marine Intelligence of Vision-Language Models
venue: IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
reason: Benchmark of vision-language models on marine image QA, including species identification, behaviour and counting of marine organisms in mostly underwater photographs.

title: ORCA: Object Recognition and Comprehension for Archiving Marine Species
venue: 2026 IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
reason: Dataset and benchmark of web-sourced images of diverse marine species for detection, instance captioning and visual grounding aimed at marine biological surveys.

title: TaxonRL: Reinforcement Learning with Intermediate Rewards for Interpretable Fine-Grained Visual Reasoning
venue: IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
reason: Proposes a VLM reinforcement-learning method for fine-grained species verification and individual re-identification of animals, including wild gorillas, chimpanzees and sea stars.

title: Are All Marine Species Created Equal? Performance Disparities in Underwater Object Detection
venue: 2026 IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
reason: Systematic analysis of object detection and classification performance on underwater images of marine invertebrates (scallop, echinus, holothurian, starfish) from seafloor and web-collected datasets.

title: An improved architecture for part-based animal re-identification through semantic segmentation distillation
venue: 2026 IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
reason: Proposes a ViT-based part-aware re-identification method evaluated on Amur tigers (ATRW, 'in the Wild') and yaks; at least part of the data shows wild animals.

title: Improving Animal Pose Estimation through Species Similarity Measures and Rigorous Label Definition
venue: Proceedings 2026 IEEE Cvf Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision Wacv 2026
reason: Develops animal pose estimation methods (training data selection by species similarity, refined keypoint labels) targeting antelopes and other wild mammals using AP-10K images, which also contain domestic species.

title: ZebraPose: Zebra Detection and Pose Estimation using only Synthetic Data
venue: 2026 IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
reason: Primary study training zebra detection and 2D pose estimation models on synthetic data and evaluating them on real zebra images, including UAV footage of Grevy's zebras in an arena and public animal pose datasets. The paper frames the work as wild zebra monitoring; the real data appear to mix in-the-wild dataset images with zebras held in an arena.

title: GorillaWatch: An Automated System for In-the-Wild Gorilla Re-Identification and Population Monitoring
venue: 2026 IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
reason: Develops a detection, tracking and re-identification pipeline for camera-trap videos of wild western lowland gorillas in Odzala-Kokoua National Park. A zoo dataset is also used for cross-domain evaluation.

title: FG-DINO: Inducing Foreground Approximation Into DINO for Low-Resolution Surveillance Videos
venue: IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision Workshops (WACVW)
reason: The paper detects pedestrians in low-resolution surveillance videos. No animals are analysed.

title: Enhancement as Augmentation: Improving Detection in Highly Degraded Underwater Images Through Mixed-Domain Training
venue: IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision Workshops (WACVW)
reason: Applies a YOLO-based object detection method to AUV underwater images of wild round goby fish in the Great Lakes, with underwater image enhancement used as data augmentation.

title: SSeg: Active Sparse Point-Label Augmentation for Semantic Segmentation
venue: Proceedings 2026 IEEE Cvf Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision Workshops Wacvw 2026
reason: Proposes a point-label augmentation method for semantic segmentation, evaluated on coral reef imagery (UCSD Mosaics) with multi-species coral classes, and aimed at marine ecology monitoring. The paper also uses an aerial urban benchmark (SkyScapes) that contains no animals.

title: UNO-FRCNN: Underwater Object Detection Using Deep Learning Based Fast Region Convolutional Neural Network
reason: Proposes a deep learning detector for underwater images whose classes include fish, coral, tortoises and starfish, alongside humans. The paper does not say where the animals were imaged, but underwater scenes of these taxa are taken as showing free-ranging animals.

title: Life history induces markedly divergent insect responses to habitat loss
reason: Primary study applying a YOLOv8 object detection model to photographs of sticky traps to identify and measure wild insects captured in the field in the Balbina archipelago.

title: Evaluation of BugBox, a software platform for AI-assisted bioinventories of arthropods
reason: Arthropods were collected in the field but the analysed images are lab photographs of individual dead specimens, taken with a digital microscope while suspended in gel. This is specimen imaging, not imaging of free-ranging animals.

title: Contextually conspicuous species are more likely to be venomous: Habitat‐dependent aposematic colouration found throughout snakes
reason: Quantitative colour image analysis of iNaturalist photographs of wild snakes in their natural habitat, used to measure contextual conspicuousness.

title: UAV-based remote sensing of bee nesting aggregations with computer vision for object detection
reason: Applies a YOLOv5 object detection workflow to UAV imagery to detect and census nests (direct signs) of a wild ground-nesting bee aggregation.

title: Identification of camera trap images by artificial intelligence and human experts produces similar multi-species occupancy models
reason: Primary study applying an AI detector and species classifier (MegaDetector, SpeciesNet) to camera trap images of wild mid-large mammals and comparing the resulting occupancy models with those from expert labels.

title: Automatic traps foster the monitoring and prediction of bark beetle swarming
reason: Wild bark beetles are counted with infrared light-barrier sensors inside pheromone traps, and swarming is then modelled with GLMs on climate data. No image or video data are analysed.

title: A Wildlife Multi‐Modal Recognition Method Based on Infrared Camera Images Using MWAC
reason: Proposes a multimodal (image + text) deep learning model for species classification of camera-trap images of wild birds and mammals from a nature reserve.

title: A Lightweight Deep Neural Network for Individual Leopard Identification: Supporting Movement Ecology in the Taihang Mountains of Henan
reason: Proposes a deep learning model for individual identification of leopards using camera-trap images of wild North China leopards together with zoo images of captive leopards and jaguars.

title: WildWing: An open-source, autonomous and affordable UAS for animal behaviour video monitoring
reason: Autonomous drone system with YOLO-based detection, tested only on animals kept in fenced pastures of a conservation centre (The Wilds, Ohio), which the paper itself calls semi-wild; no data on wild, free-ranging animals is analysed.

title: Peering into the world of wild passerines with 3D-SOCS: Synchronized video capture and posture estimation
reason: Develops a multi-camera markerless 3D posture tracking system and applies it to video of wild great tits and blue tits visiting a field-deployed feeder.

title: Introducing TropiCam‐AI: A taxonomically flexible automated classifier of Neotropical arboreal mammals and birds from camera‐trap data
reason: Develops a deep learning classifier for wild Neotropical arboreal mammals and birds from arboreal camera-trap images, augmented with iNaturalist images.

title: High-throughput information extraction of printed specimen labels from large-scale digitization of entomological collections using a semi-automated pipeline
reason: The pipeline pulls text from printed labels on pinned insect specimens in museum collections. These are museum specimens, not wild or free-ranging animals, and the labels rather than the animals are the subject.

title: As above, so below: A perspective into the application of land‐forest monitoring methods for the assessment of marine animal forests
reason: Primary study that applies SfM photogrammetry to underwater images of wild Mediterranean gorgonian forests (sessile animals), then processes the 3D point clouds to segment them and detect individual organisms. The title calls it a perspective, but the paper reports original data and a method.

title: A general method for detection and segmentation of terrestrial arthropods in images
reason: Develops a detection and instance segmentation method for terrestrial arthropods; data combine field camera-trap and citizen-science images of live wild insects with laboratory, ethanol and museum specimens.

title: Paying attention to other animal detections improves camera trap classification models
reason: Proposes a self-attention module to improve species classification of camera trap crops of wild African mammals (Snapshot Serengeti, Snapshot Safari).

title: Automated counting of fish in moving diver-operated videos (DOV) for biodiversity assessments
reason: Primary study that develops automated counting methods on diver-operated underwater videos of wild Mediterranean fish, using a YOLOv7 detector and counting methods.

title: COPIS : A robust and versatile robotic imaging system for the 3D digitization of natural history specimens with photogrammetry
reason: Robotic photogrammetry system for 3D digitization of natural history museum specimens; no wild free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: AutoPollS: A tool for automated monitoring of pollinators using deep learning
reason: Introduces a camera system and deep learning pipeline (detection and classification) for monitoring free-ranging flower-visiting insects in field deployments.

title: charisma: An R package to perform reproducible colour characterization of digital images for biological studies
reason: Software for colour classification demonstrated on photographs of bird museum specimens (plus colour swatches and beetle/fish images); no wild free-ranging animals imaged in the field.

title: From video to behaviour: An LSTM ‐based approach for automated nest behaviour recognition in the wild
reason: Primary study developing an LSTM-based video behaviour recognition framework for wild birds (sociable weavers, blue tits, great tits) filmed at their nests in the field.

title: Mothbox and Mothbot: Automated light trap and data processing system for scalable insect monitoring
reason: Presents an automated light trap and a computer vision pipeline (YOLO11 detection, BioCLIP identification) applied to images of wild nocturnal insects in field deployments in Panama.

title: RAPID: Real-time animal pattern re-identification on edge devices, an open-source tool for field deployment
reason: Primary study proposing a computer-vision re-identification tool, evaluated on images and video of wild zebras, giraffes, tigers and jaguars, plus one domestic cattle dataset.

title: Descriptron‐ GBIF Annotator: A browser‐based platform for crowdsourced morphological annotation of biodiversity images
reason: Browser-based annotation tool with SAM2 segmentation for morphological annotation of museum specimen images from GBIF and taxonomic literature; it does not work on live wild animals.

title: Theia: An end-to-end edge-AI mobile framework for high-throughput field phenotyping and on-device geometric morphometrics
reason: The paper presents automated landmark detection and geometric morphometrics on Erysimum flower images (plants). No animals are analysed.

title: Multi‐angle, cross‐domain fusion strategy enhances automated insect identification and hierarchical categorization: a case study on assassin bugs (Hemiptera: Reduviidae)
reason: Deep learning classification of assassin bugs using pinned museum specimen photos and iNaturalist field images of wild insects in natural environments; primary research.

title: Are we there yet? Reliable occupancy modeling from AI-labeled trail camera data
reason: Primary study evaluating the SpeciesNet computer-vision classifier on trail camera images of free-ranging Florida mammals and its effect on occupancy estimates.

title: Geographic Classification of Social Bees Using Automated Wing Pattern Analysis
reason: Wing images of honeybees sampled from managed beekeeping colonies and imaged under a stereomicroscope; beekeeping falls under E-AGRI, and the data includes no wild free-ranging animals.

title: An AI ‐Driven Biomass Estimation Tool Enabling Population‐ and Specimen‐Level Variation Analyses: A Case Study on Parasitoid Flies
reason: Wild tachinid flies were caught in Malaise traps, but the images analysed are of preserved dead specimens photographed under a photomicroscope. The paper does not analyse images of free-ranging live animals, so it falls under the specimen exclusion.

title: Cryptic and Ecologically Relevant Locomotor Activity Patterns in Lake Malawi Cichlids Revealed Through Computer Vision Pipeline
reason: Cichlids obtained from the aquarium trade were reared and filmed in laboratory glass aquaria. No wild or free-ranging animals were imaged.

title: An Angler‐Friendly AI Pipeline for Self‐Reporting and Automatic Catch Analysis in Recreational Fisheries
reason: Computer vision pipeline (detection, segmentation, species classification, length estimation) applied to smartphone photos of wild marine fish caught by recreational anglers in the Mediterranean.

title: Advancing Automated Fish Size Estimation From Images: Applications, Challenges and a Case Study for Images Without a Specified Reference Object
reason: Review plus original case study applying a vision transformer and regression to estimate the length of wild fish caught by recreational anglers in photos from an angling app.

title: Rapid Decreases and Performance Declines in Northeast Pacific Seamount Foundation Species Detected in an Oxygen Minimum Zone
reason: Applies Structure-from-Motion photogrammetric reconstruction to ROV and drop-camera video of wild deep-sea corals and sponges to monitor abundance and condition.

title: UAV ‐based terrain metrics reveal species‐specific nest‐site preferences in Pygoscelis penguins
reason: UAV imagery of wild penguin colonies is used only to build terrain models and orthophotos through photogrammetry. Breeding groups and nests were delineated by hand in ArcMap and then analysed with GIS and statistics. No computer vision method is applied to the animals in the images.

title: Comparing deep learning models for butterfly and moth (Lepidoptera) species identification
reason: Primary study comparing 40 deep learning image classifiers on citizen-science photographs of free-ranging butterflies and moths recorded in Austria.

title: Automated whale shark recognition and tracking using drones and deep learning
reason: Primary study applying deep learning (DeepLabCut pose estimation and a DenseNet121 patch classifier) to drone video of free-ranging whale sharks in Bahía de los Ángeles, Mexico.

title: Automated Detection and Risk-Related Behavior Recognition of Long-Tailed Macaques in a University Campus Area Using CNN-Based Object Detection
reason: YOLOv8-based detection of free-ranging long-tailed macaques and their risk-related behaviours from photos and videos taken on a university campus.

title: A Smart-Alarm Detection and Deterrent System for Long-Tailed Macaque Intrusion in Human Residential Zones
reason: Primary study applying YOLOv8 object detection to CCTV video of free-ranging long-tailed macaques entering a university campus, for conflict mitigation.

title: Melanism in salamanders: effects of insularity, sex and size on dorsal colouration in Salamandra salamandra
reason: Wild-caught fire salamanders were photographed, and image colour segmentation was used to measure how much of each dorsal surface is black. The animals are free-ranging and were released at the place of capture.

title: Using Drones for Large Mammal Monitoring
reason: Practice Insights article combining a short review with a new drone georeferencing pipeline; the only data analysed in the experiments show human subjects used as proxies for wildlife, and the detector was fine-tuned on a human dataset. No wild animal imagery is evaluated in the text.

title: Validation of a Body Condition Scoring System for Indo‐Pacific Humpback Dolphins ( Sousa chinensis )
reason: Wild dolphins are photographed, but body condition is scored by eye by human raters and UAV body measurements are taken by hand in MorphoMetriX. No computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Predicting Individual Body Length, Volume, and Mass From Dominant Stroke Cycle Frequency in Sperm Whales: Empirical Cross‐Validation and Prediction Functions
reason: UAV photogrammetry images of free-ranging sperm whales are measured to estimate body length and volume, which are then used to validate stroke frequency from tags. The image analysis is manual morphometric measurement.

title: Characterizing the Distribution and Behavior of Sperm Whales, Physeter macrocephalus , Over the Otago Submarine Canyons, New Zealand
reason: This is a field ecology study of wild sperm whales. Fluke photographs were matched to catalogues by eye by researchers, and the other data came from acoustics and statistical models. No computer vision or automated image analysis is used.

title: Beyond the Ridge: Rethinking Thermal Windows in Beluga Whales
reason: Infrared thermography of four beluga whales held in indoor aquarium pools; only captive animals, and no computer vision method is described beyond surface temperature measurement.

title: Evaluating the Effectiveness of a Multispecies Matching Algorithm Applied to a Novel Species, Risso's Dolphins ( Grampus griseus )
reason: Evaluates an automated photo-identification matching algorithm on dorsal fin photographs of free-ranging Risso's dolphins taken from research vessels in the Southern California Bight.

title: Exploring Progesterone Levels and Scaled Mass Index as Predictors of Pregnancy in Free‐Ranging Belugas
reason: Applies UAV-based aerial photogrammetry (morphometric image analysis) to free-ranging St. Lawrence Estuary belugas to estimate Scaled Mass Index and relate it to pregnancy; primary research on wild animals.

title: Machine Learning Detection of Scarring Events in Killer Whales
reason: Develops a CV pipeline (nnU-Net segmentation plus clustering) to detect and count conspecific scarring events on photo-identification images of wild Bigg's killer whales.

title: Citizen Science Data Reveal Humpback Whales Feeding Along the Eastern Coast of Australia
reason: Social media photos and videos of wild humpback whales were inspected by people to record feeding events. No computer vision or automated image analysis is used.

title: Comparing Drone and Vessel‐Based Imaging to Quantify Epibiont Coverage on Humpback Whales
reason: Primary study applying semiautomated image segmentation (graph-cut, colour thresholding) to drone and vessel images of free-ranging humpback whales to quantify epibiont coverage.

title: A Deep Learning Framework for Cetacean Detection: Integrating YOLOv11 With ADRIF Post‐Processing
reason: Develops and evaluates a YOLOv11-based detection framework with post-processing on vessel-based photographs of free-ranging cetaceans collected during research cruises in Indian waters.

title: UAV ‐Based Dolphin Tracking Enables Automated Quantification of Spatial Group Cohesion in Natural and Exposure Settings
reason: Develops a UAV video pipeline with a YOLOv5 object detector to localize free-ranging common dolphins off the Azores and quantify inter-individual distances.

title: A Computer Vision Framework for Estimating Body Size and Condition in Multiple Cetacean Species
reason: Applies a Mask R-CNN based pipeline (WHALESHAPE) to UAV images of free-ranging whales to estimate body length, volume and condition.

title: Using Aerial Photogrammetry to Estimate Body Condition and Assess Sexual Dimorphism in Narwhals
reason: Aerial photogrammetry from drone video of free-ranging narwhals, used to measure body dimensions in images and estimate body condition indices.

title: Det-LIME: Detector-Aware, Multi-Instance Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations for Automated Marine Mammal Detection
reason: Proposes an explainability method (Det-LIME) for object detectors and evaluates it on drone imagery of wild harbor seals and a seabird colony dataset.

title: Development and Validation of Girth‐, Volume‐, and Mass‐Based Body Condition Indices for Free‐Swimming Dugongs, via Drone Photogrammetry
reason: Drone photogrammetric image analysis of free-swimming wild dugongs to derive morphometrics and body condition indices.

title: Detecting Polar Bears on Land Using Satellite Imagery and Deep Learning
reason: Primary study applying deep learning object detectors to very high-resolution satellite imagery of wild polar bears on land along the Beaufort Sea coast of Alaska.

title: Contemporary Growth Curves for Individual Humpback Whales in Eastern Australia Using Aerial Photogrammetry
reason: Wild humpback whales are filmed by drone, but body length is measured by hand by one observer in measurement software, and photo-ID is manual catalogue matching. No automated computer vision method is developed or applied; the analysis is Bayesian growth modelling.

title: Tracking Tool for Fiddler Crabs in Natural Settings to Promote a Model Organism for Synchrony
venue: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
reason: Develops a motion-tracking algorithm (optical flow plus clustering) for field videos of wild fiddler crabs in natural settings.

title: Evolutionary Stability of the Shark Snout: Geometric Morphometrics of Ventral Facial Openings
venue: Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences
reason: Comparative morphology study: landmarks were placed by hand in ImageJ on book illustrations of sharks, then analysed with geometric morphometrics and phylogenetic statistics. There is no computer vision method and no photographs or video of animals.

title: Automated specimen triage for dark taxa: Deep learning enables orientation, sex identification and anatomical segmentation from robotic imaging
reason: Images are of dead, ethanol-preserved Malaise-trap specimens taken with a robotic lab imaging system and a photomicroscope. This is a laboratory microscopy set-up, not imaging of free-ranging animals.

title: Validation of aerial photogrammetry methods to measure body size, condition and mass in small cetaceans
reason: UAV photogrammetry is validated only on bottlenose dolphins under human care at Sea World, Gold Coast. No wild animals are in the analysed data.

title: Improving the Accuracy of Automatic Wildlife Detection in Nature Reserves Using Infrared Imaging
reason: Proposes a deep-learning detector (SSD-ADSAR with infrared preclassification) for wild animals in camera trap images from protected areas.

title: Application of a Non-Specialized Convolutional Neural Network Model for the Automatic Detection of Macroscopic Organisms in Underwater Video Recordings from the Chukchi Sea
reason: Applies a COCO-pretrained Faster R-CNN detector to ROV video of wild benthic macrofauna on the Chukchi Sea floor and evaluates it against human annotation.

title: OpenAqua: A Large-Scale Fine-Grained Dataset and Benchmark for Open Underwater Visual Perception
venue: Proceedings of the ACM SIGKDD International Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining
reason: Primary study that builds a fine-grained fish detection/segmentation dataset from FishNet and iNaturalist images and benchmarks computer vision models on it for aquatic biodiversity monitoring. The paper does not explicitly state whether animals are wild or captive; wild status is inferred from the iNaturalist source and the exclusion of non-natural subjects.

title: DeepTaxon: An Interpretable Retrieval-Augmented Multimodal Framework for Unified Species Identification and Discovery
venue: ACM SIGKDD Conference on Knowledge Discovery and Data Mining (KDD)
reason: Proposes a retrieval-augmented multimodal method for species identification and discovery, trained and evaluated on iNaturalist citizen-science images of free-ranging organisms (including animals) for biodiversity research. It also uses domestic dog images and non-animal benchmarks.

title: CreatureConnect: Exploring Shared Control of Multimodal Displays Between People and Lemurs
venue: CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
reason: HCI study of an interactive enrichment device for five zoo-housed red-ruffed lemurs. Only captive animals appear, and there is no computer vision method: interaction is sensed with infrared proximity sensors, and the CCTV footage was only used to cross-check the logs.

title: Drawing Attention: A Field Study of Sketch-Based Penguin Identification for Aquarium Visitor Engagement
venue: CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
reason: Sketch-based identification of individual Cape penguins kept at an aquarium; all animals are captive and the system matches visitor drawings rather than analysing images of wild animals.

title: Outfoxed: Design and Evaluation of a Modular Interactive Puzzle for Cognitive Enrichment of Zoo Animals
venue: CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
reason: HCI study of a puzzle feeder for a zoo-housed Arctic fox and coatis; video was coded manually in BORIS, with no computer vision method. The animals are also captive only.

title: UnCageNet: Tracking and Pose Estimation of Caged Animals
venue: Proceedings of Icvgip 2025 16th Indian Conference on Computer Vision Graphics and Image Processing
reason: The paper is about pose estimation and tracking of caged animals. The real data is zoo footage (Kankariya Zoo), and the benchmark data (APT-36K, plus OMPD built on AP36k/APT10k) has synthetic cages added to simulate enclosures. The method is meant for research facilities, zoos and agricultural settings, not wild, free-ranging animals.

title: WildFiT: Autonomous In-Situ Model Adaptation for Resource-Constrained IoT Systems
reason: Primary method paper on on-device species classification of wild animals in camera trap images (Serengeti and Enonkishu datasets), with synthetic-data fine-tuning to handle domain shift.

title: The Summit Lake Watershed Environmental Observation Network: A Design Framework for a High-Throughput, Remote Field Sensor Network
reason: Field sensor network paper whose wildlife-camera component applies MegaDetector detection and BoT-SORT tracking to video of free-ranging wildlife on the Summit Lake Paiute Reservation.

title: Bio-DetectNet: A Deep Learning Framework for Wildlife Conservation and Biodiversity Monitoring
venue: Icimmi 2025 7th International Conference on Information Management and Machine Intelligence
reason: Proposes a YOLOv5-based detector trained on camera-trap, drone and roadside images of wild animals; primary research.

title: From Virtual Forests to Real Wildlife: Synthetic Non-Radiometric Thermal UAV Data for Animal Detection
reason: Develops a synthetic thermal UAV data pipeline and evaluates YOLO detectors on real-world thermal UAV recordings of forest wildlife (deer, wild boar).

title: Lightweight Underwater Object Detection Algorithm Based on YOLOv11
venue: International Conference on Computer, Artificial Intelligence and Control Engineering (CAICE)
reason: Proposes a lightweight YOLOv11 detector for marine organisms (sea cucumbers, scallops, starfish) in real-world underwater images from the public UODD dataset.

title: LightSea-DETR: A Lightweight Underwater Object Detection Transformer with Edge-Enhanced and Frequency-Aware Features
venue: International Conference on Computer, Artificial Intelligence and Control Engineering (CAICE)
reason: Proposes a transformer-based detector for marine benthic organisms (sea urchin, sea cucumber, starfish, scallop) in underwater images collected by AUVs in the field, framed as supporting marine ecological monitoring.

title: Centripetal-Scale Coupling and Sparsity-Guided Label Assignment for Tiny Object Detection in Steppe Rathole Monitoring
reason: Proposes a label assignment method for detecting steppe rodent burrows (direct animal signs) in UAV imagery; primary research on wild animal signs.

title: AI-Assisted Workflows for Historical Map Metadata Extraction
venue: ACM/IEEE Joint Conference on Digital Libraries
