reason: The paper extracts text and metadata from scanned historical maps. There are no animals in the data, and wildlife is not the subject or application.

title: Demo: Field Calibration of Smart Camera Trap Based on Augmented Reality and Few-shot CNN Retraining
reason: Demo paper presenting a smart camera trap that runs an on-device CNN for animal vs. no-animal classification with in-situ few-shot calibration, intended for wildlife monitoring in the field. The paper does not describe the animals in the analysed images.

title: Leveraging ResNet-50 for Automated Image-Based Fish Species Classification
venue: International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Metaheuristics & Swarm Intelligence (ISMSI)
reason: Applies a CNN (ResNet50) to classify 75 fish species from FishBase images, including underwater images, for biodiversity and fisheries monitoring. Whether the fish are wild or captive is not stated.

title: An AI-based Approach for Automated Region-of-Interest Detection and Cropping in Underwater Coral Reef Quadrat Imagery
venue: International Conference on Intelligent Systems, Metaheuristics & Swarm Intelligence (ISMSI)
reason: Applies YOLOv11 detection and segmentation to field underwater photoquadrat images of wild coral reefs in Sogod Bay, as a preprocessing step for estimating coral cover.

title: RobustLT: A Noise-Aware Collaborative Optimization Framework for Large-Scale Fine-Grained Visual Recognition in Noisy and Long-Tailed Scenarios
reason: Generic webly-supervised fine-grained recognition method for label noise and long-tail; biodiversity monitoring is only an example and the evaluated web benchmarks are not described as wildlife data.

title: Behavioral Strategies and Kinematic Mechanisms of Canine Animals Jumping Over Obstacles While Running
reason: The only animal in the data is one domestic, trained police dog (Belgian Malinois) filmed with markers on a training field. No wild or free-ranging animals appear.

title: Based on Improved YOLOv11 Transmission Line Bird Hazard Detection
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv11 detector for wild birds on power transmission lines, using bird images.

title: Object Detection, Recognition, Deep Learning, and the Universal Law of Generalization
reason: Trains a CNN (AlexNet) to classify images of clear and camouflaged wild animals (web/public camouflage images) and analyses its internal representations; images show free-ranging animals and the animals are the subject.

title: Application of infrared thermography coupled with Eulerian Video Magnification to monitor vital signs in wild seals, from sandy beaches to icy shores
reason: Primary study that applies video processing (Eulerian video magnification on infrared thermography video) to wild, free-living seals to extract respiration and heart rate.

title: Transformer-enhanced YOLOv5 With cross-convolution for underwater object detection
venue: Journal on Advances in Signal Processing
reason: Proposes a CV detection method for underwater marine invertebrates (sea urchin, sea cucumber, starfish, scallop) in images captured in the sea (DUO dataset).

title: Variable evidence of radio-tag backpacks affecting hummingbird time budgets in captivity
reason: Videos of temporarily captive hummingbirds in a flight tent were scored manually frame-by-frame in BORIS for time budgets. No computer vision or automated image analysis is applied.

title: Improved YOLOv11-based algorithm for identifying birds intruding on power lines
venue: Journal of Engineering and Applied Science
reason: Proposes a lightweight YOLOv11-based detector for free-flying birds intruding on power transmission lines, trained on images and video frames from two open bird datasets.

title: A dataset of beluga distribution in the Canadian sub-Arctic derived from WorldView imagery (2021–2022)
reason: Data paper building a beluga and harp seal distribution dataset from WorldView satellite imagery of wild animals, using SAM-assisted annotation and a YOLOv8 detector.

title: Measurement error models for morphometric data
reason: Statistical measurement-error model for morphometric data; measurements were taken by hand from drone images in Tracker software. No computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: Adaptive mask resolution with collaborative edge optimization for wildlife instance segmentation
venue: Beijing Linye Daxue Xuebao Journal of Beijing Forestry University
reason: Proposes an instance segmentation method for camera-trap images of wild animals (giant panda, Amur tiger, etc.) collected in Chinese protected areas.

title: Classifying behaviors from animal-borne cameras using machine learning: automated identification of breathing events in sea turtles
reason: Applies ResNet-50 and ViT to classify breathing behavior from animal-borne camera footage of wild juvenile green turtles in Bahamian mangrove creeks.

title: In the tracks of a whale: inferring size class, orientation and swimming speed from thermal flukeprints
reason: Analyses UAV thermal and RGB video of free-ranging humpback whales to infer age class, swimming speed and heading from thermal flukeprints (photogrammetric image measurement).

title: Tail flaring during agonism in hummingbirds
reason: Computer vision (DeepLabCut pose estimation) is applied only to captive calliope hummingbirds held in an indoor competition arena. The field videos of free-ranging birds were scored manually for whether tail flaring was present.

title: Research on Yak Object Detection and Counting System Based on YOLO Series Algorithms
reason: Detection and counting of farmed yaks (adult and young) in pasture pens and channels for livestock management; livestock, not wild animals.

title: Intelligent Video Detection Method of Underwater Chinese Sturgeon Based on YOLOv11
reason: All analysed video comes from Chinese sturgeon held in breeding/rearing ponds (above-water and underwater); no free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: YOLO11-Swin: A Target Detection Model for Complex Underwater Environments
reason: Proposes a deep learning detector for marine organisms (sea cucumber, sea urchin, scallop, starfish) in real underwater images; the stated application is marine resource and ecological monitoring. The paper does not say whether the animals are wild or farmed.

title: Research and Application on an Intelligent System for Fish Recognition and Monitoring Based on Improved YOLOv8n
reason: Improved YOLOv8n for detecting and recognising 13 fish species in underwater images, built for marine biodiversity monitoring. Images come from Kaggle and web image platforms. The paper does not say whether the fish are wild or captive, but it frames the data as underwater scenes for marine ecological monitoring.

title: DMS-YOLO: An Underwater Blurred Object Detection Algorithm
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for underwater targets, evaluated on RUOD. The images come from real underwater environments and most classes are marine animals (fish, starfish, turtles, etc.).

title: Solar-Powered Motion-Triggered Edge AI Monitoring System for Small-Animal Surveillance in Farm Environments
reason: Prototype for detecting small pest animals (rodents, mole) in farm surveillance; the detector is trained on web-curated images and a public rat dataset, with no stated wild or free-ranging field data, so it falls under crop pests in production.

title: Large testing of AI-based camera traps on a forest defoliating pest in Europe
reason: Field evaluation of AI-based camera traps (Faster R-CNN detection on trap images) for wild pine processionary moths in forest and urban habitats in four European countries.

title: FRM-hm: Heatmap Refinement for Small Object Detection in Center-based Detectors with Application to Rice-field Bird Monitoring
venue: Journal of Advances in Information Technology
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for free-flying and perched wild granivorous birds in images from videos recorded in an agricultural field.

title: The Effect of Data Balancing Techniques in RMSProp and Adam Optimizers in Deep Learning Models for Wildlife Recognition: A Pathway to Image-Based Visual Servoing (IBVS)
venue: Journal of Advances in Information Technology
reason: Primary study training CNN classifiers (AlexNet, ResNet, DenseNet) on images of wild animals from Serengeti National Park, comparing data balancing techniques and optimizers.

title: BehaveAI enables rapid detection and classification of objects and behavior from motion
reason: Proposes a motion-encoding CNN video framework; case studies include wild grass moths, wild sea slaters and wild semaphore flies, alongside a pigeon dataset, human sperm and lab beetles.

title: Speeding up taxonomy in the digital age: A deep learning approach for identifying cryptic freshwater snails
reason: Images are laboratory digital-microscope photographs of collected snail shell specimens (deposited in a university collection), not images of free-ranging animals in the field; specimens are covered under E-CAPTIVE.

title: Dynamics of jaw kinematics and fundamental frequency suggest vocal tract tuning in the indris’ song
reason: Primary study applying a DeepLabCut markerless pose estimation model to field video recordings of wild indris to measure mouth opening during song.

title: Development of a deep learning based framework for classification of Indian venomous snakes integrated with explainable artificial intelligence for primary and emergency care providers
reason: Deep learning classification of photographs of wild Indian snakes (snakebite incident photos, roadkill, field expeditions) into venomous vs non-venomous.

title: Observations of marine animal interactions with a small tidal turbine
reason: Underwater optical camera imagery of wild seals, seabirds and fish near a tidal turbine, with a YOLO detection model used in real time to trigger recording.

title: A deep learning-based model for automatic identification of mesopelagic organisms from in-trawl cameras
reason: Trains and evaluates an object detector on in-trawl camera images of wild mesopelagic organisms recorded during research surveys at sea.

title: Placing anurans in water can improve photo-based individual identification
reason: Photo-based individual identification of free-ranging agile frogs captured at a breeding pond, using HotSpotter software on images.

title: Photo-based individual identification is more reliable than visible implant elastomer tags or toe-tipping in young agile frogs
reason: Compares toe clipping, VIE tags and photo-based identification in captive-reared agile froglets; photo-ID is done by eye by researchers, and no computer vision or image analysis algorithm is developed or applied. The animals were also kept in mesocosms and housing boxes.

title: A deep learning-based fusion framework for robust fine-grained classification of sea turtles in support of marine biodiversity
reason: Proposes CNN fusion modules for species classification of sea turtles from images collected from public repositories, including real-world underwater scenes; wildlife monitoring is the stated application. The paper does not explicitly state that the animals are wild.

title: MosQNet-SA: Explainable convolutional-attention network for mosquito classification with application as a RESTful API for dengue and malaria risk mapping
reason: Proposes a CNN-attention model to classify mosquito genera from images. The data include citizen-science photos of free-ranging mosquitoes alongside laboratory and plain-background images.

title: GAN-based underwater image enhancement and scene classification using transfer learning
reason: Primary study applying image enhancement and CNN classification to underwater video and images of free-ranging marine animals (fish, corals, sea turtles) recorded in Indonesian waters and from LifeCLEF-2015.

title: Ontogenetic shifts in morphology and ecology of eastern Pacific white sharks revealed by computer vision
reason: Primary study that develops and validates a deep learning segmentation pipeline on drone imagery of free-swimming wild white sharks to extract morphometrics.

title: Integrating deep learning, biological hierarchies, and high-resolution imagery to create a new identification tool for cryptic coral reef fishes
reason: Deep learning classification of wild cryptobenthic reef fishes, using lab photos of field-collected specimens plus in situ underwater web images (iNaturalist, FishBase, STRI).

title: Integrating 3-D thermal videography, ultrasonic acoustics, and weather radar to characterize bird and bat activity at wind turbines
reason: Applies YOLOv3-based detection and stereo 3-D tracking to thermal video of wild migrating birds and bats at wind turbines.

title: iNaturalist mammal observations classified by evidence type
reason: Trains an image classifier on iNaturalist photos of wild North American mammals and their signs (tracks, scat, other sign) and publishes the resulting evidence-type dataset.

title: Optimized bilateral segmentation deep learning network for wild animal detection
reason: Proposes a CNN-based segmentation and classification method for wild animal identification, tested on web images of 90 animal species. The paper presents it as a wildlife application but does not say which species are wild or domestic.

title: Detecting Fish Movement Behavior based on Constant Temperature and pH using the IoT and Realtime Object Detection Model
venue: Journal of Applied Informatics and Technology
reason: Aquarium/aquaculture fish (Malawi cichlids) kept in an experimental tank and monitored for aquaculture water quality; no wild free-ranging animals.

title: Automated photogrammetric close-range imaging of small invertebrates using acoustic levitation
reason: Imaging system for preserved insect specimens (stored in ethanol) levitated in a laboratory set-up; no living wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Integrating modeling and in situ imagery at the individual level to reveal the phenotypic plasticity of Arctic copepod communities
reason: In situ LOKI images of wild Arctic copepods are segmented (lipid sac and prosome masks), and the mask areas are used to estimate lipid traits that calibrate an individual-based model. The image analysis is manual but still applied to free-ranging animals.

title: Not So Fatal Attraction: Captive Female Burmese Python Lures Do Not Improve Wild Python Detection
reason: Camera-trap study of wild Burmese Pythons in the Everglades; MegaDetector (CV) used to filter images containing animals.

title: Breeding Population Size and Spatial Extent of Socotra Cormorants on Hawar Islands, Bahrain: The Utility of Drone Footage and a Counting Algorithm
reason: Primary study applying an image thresholding method to drone photos to count nests of wild, free-ranging Socotra Cormorants at a breeding colony.

title: Watching Swarm Dynamics from Above: A Framework for Advanced Object Tracking in Drone Videos
venue: edoc Publication server (Humboldt University of Berlin)
reason: Proposes a particle-filter plus segmentation framework to track wild fish schools in the open ocean from drone videos, with a new dataset.

title: Wild Animal Tracking for Effective Wildlife Conservation using YOLOv8 and Machine Learning Technologies
reason: Applies YOLOv8 object detection to images of Amur tigers from the ATRW (Annotated Tigers in the Wild) dataset, which the paper describes as free-roaming tigers, for wildlife conservation.

title: BASES VISUAIS E MATEMÁTICAS PARA O USO DE INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL NA IDENTIFICAÇÃO DE QUATRO ESPÉCIES DO GÊNERO MUGIL
venue: Revista Brasileira de Engenharia de Pesca
reason: Applies classical image processing (segmentation, morphometric and texture descriptors) to digital images of four wild coastal Mugil species to support species identification; primary study.

title: Quality-driven unsupervised data curation and robust learning method for bird image data
reason: Proposes a data curation and robust learning method for classifying wild river-lake birds imaged by field surveillance cameras at monitoring stations in Beijing.

title: Development of a Smart Animal Intrusion Detection and Monitoring System Using PIR Motion Sensor, Camera Module, and Real-Time Mobile Alerting via IoT Connectivity
reason: IoT alarm system where detection is triggered by a PIR motion sensor; the camera only captures images for the user to check visually. Frame differencing is mentioned but no image analysis is evaluated or reported.

title: Classification of butterfly species with improved models based on transfer learning method of convolutional neural networks
reason: Proposes a CNN transfer learning method to classify butterfly species from nature photographs of free-living butterflies.

title: A Three-Stage Detection, Segmentation, and Feature Analysis Framework for Unique Individual Identification in Flamingo Populations
reason: UAV video of wild flamingos in a wetland, analysed for detection, tracking, segmentation and individual re-identification.

title: Developing a Low Resource Intensive Algorithm for Early Detection of Flying Swarm of Pest Birds
reason: Proposes a computer vision pipeline that detects flying swarms of wild Red-billed Quelea in video footage for early warning.

title: A Lightweight Appearance-Guided Association Module for Underwater Multi-Fish Tracking
reason: Fish multi-object tracking method explicitly framed for densely stocked industrial aquaculture monitoring; the paper does not describe the MFT25 recording environment as wild.

title: A Hybrid Computer Vision and AI Framework for Wildlife Hospital Patient Identification Systems: Kangaroo Facial Recognition as a Case Study
reason: Facial re-identification of injured kangaroos held in a wildlife rehabilitation centre. All the images show animals in enclosures in care, not free-ranging animals.

title: ODConv-GFPN-LSPCD: A Multi-Module Enhanced YOLOv11n for Marine Organism Detection
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv11n detector for marine organisms in underwater images from URPC 2021 and footage the authors filmed in the field off Qingdao and Sanya.

title: Synergistic Convergence of Multiple Environmental Drivers Triggered a Multi‑taxa Regime Shift in the Yangtze Estuary
reason: Ecological regime-shift analysis of field survey species abundance records and environmental variables; there is no image or video analysis.

title: Spatial Configuration and Multi-trophic Colonization in Modular Artificial Reefs: A Design-Research Field Study for Reef Restoration in the Gulf of Thailand
reason: Artificial reef field study in which wild reef fauna were assessed by observer-based visual review of underwater imagery and visual census; no computer vision or automated image analysis is developed or applied.

title: Coral-Algal Interactions on Coral Patches of Santa Cruz Island, Galápagos-Ecuador
reason: Ecological field study of wild corals in Galápagos; underwater photographs and photoquadrats were classified manually by visual criteria and analysed with statistical tests (Fisher's exact test, MCA). There is no computer vision or automated image analysis.

title: Sustained warming alters Bombus impatiens foraging, colony performance, and pollination of zucchini (Cucurbita pepo)
reason: Growth-chamber experiment on commercially sourced bumble bee micro-colonies; videos were scored by hand by a human observer, with no computer vision method applied. The bees are also managed/captive, not wild.

title: Urban mammals in Italy: the hidden role of common species in structuring communities
reason: Camera-trap ecology study in which images were labelled manually in Timelapse software. No computer vision method is developed or applied; Random Forest is used only on species frequency data.

title: Chronoecology of sympatric wildlife: Niche segregation of the Ratel (Mellivora capensis) in Mitiyala Wildlife Sanctuary, Gujarat, India
reason: Camera-trap study of wild mammals and birds in a wildlife sanctuary. MegaDetector and YOLOv8 were used to detect and classify animals in the images before the activity-pattern analysis.

title: Long-life remote underwater video reveals dawn cleaning station use in the rare stingray, Megatrygon microps
reason: Wild stingrays and other elasmobranchs filmed with remote underwater video, but all footage was reviewed manually and analysed statistically. No computer vision method is developed or applied.

title: A behaviour-centric digital twin framework for animal monitoring: from managed enclosures to landscapes
reason: Digital twin of rescue-centre enclosures (captive bears and hippos); validation uses only synthetic detections from virtual cameras. No wild free-ranging animal data are analysed.

title: Automated estimation of gadoid and flatfish abundance in stereo-BRUV footage using YOLO object detection
reason: YOLO-based object detection applied to baited remote underwater video of wild fish at offshore wind farms to estimate abundance (MaxN).

title: Urban mammals in Italy: how common species shape communities’ differentiation
reason: Camera-trap ecology study; images were identified manually in Timelapse software and the analyses (PERMANOVA, Random Forest) use species detection frequencies, not image data. No computer vision method is used.

title: Automated Identification of Vespid Wasps Using Transformer-Based Deep Learning Models: A Biodiversity Informatics Approach from Sri Lanka
reason: Images are of preserved, field-collected wasp specimens photographed under a stereo microscope in a lab, not of free-ranging animals in the wild.

title: Seasonal variation of mesozooplankton communities in relation to environmental variables from a subtropical estuary of Bangladesh
reason: Ecological field study of estuarine mesozooplankton using net sampling, manual microscope identification and multivariate statistics; no computer vision or image analysis is performed.

title: Monsoon-Driven Environmental Gradients Structure Seasonal Mesozooplankton Community Turnover in the Moheshkhali Channel, a Subtropical Estuary in Bangladesh
reason: Field ecology study of estuarine mesozooplankton. Specimens were identified and counted by hand under a stereomicroscope and analysed with multivariate statistics. No computer vision or automated image analysis is used.

title: Seeing the unseen: thermal drone surveys enhance detection and provide first density indices for threatened tree kangaroos in Papua New Guinea’s Torricelli Mountain Range
reason: Wild tree kangaroos were surveyed by thermal drone, but pilots spotted animals by eye on the live video feed. The paper applies no automated image analysis or computer vision method.

title: Graph-based Extraction and Tracking of Insect Motion in Event-Camera Data Streams
reason: Graph-based semantic and instance segmentation of free-flying wild insects recorded with an event camera in front of a meadow in the field, with a real-world annotated dataset.

title: High-Throughput Rice Field Eel Counting: An Edge-Deployable Method via Lightweight Tracking
reason: Counting of farmed rice field eel juveniles on an aquaculture chute platform; animals are aquaculture stock, not wild free-ranging.

title: Migratory phenology of the Central American humpback whale (Megaptera novaeangliae) population unit in breeding areas
reason: Applies automated image recognition (Happywhale) to photo-identify wild humpback whales from fluke photographs to study migratory phenology.

title: An 11-year spatiotemporal roadkill dataset derived from citizen reports in Tsukuba, Japan
reason: Data descriptor of citizen-reported roadkill records; photographs were used only for manual expert species identification, and no computer vision method is developed or applied. Records include wild species together with domestic cats and dogs.

title: Lightweight Visual Detection Framework for Endangered Species Monitoring in Complex Natural Environments
reason: Develops a YOLO-based detection model for wild Chinese giant salamanders using images from field monitoring equipment in a nature reserve.

title: In-situ Volume Estimation Method for Sea Cucumbers Based on Lightweight Binocular Vision and Spatiotemporal Constraints
reason: Volume estimation of sea cucumbers in a marine ranch, explicitly for precision aquaculture management and yield estimation, so it is an aquaculture production application.

title: Monsoon-Driven Hydrographic Gradients Shape Seasonal Mesozooplankton Assemblages in the Moheshkhali Channel, a Subtropical Estuary in Bangladesh
reason: Field ecology study of wild estuarine mesozooplankton. Specimens collected by net were identified and counted by hand under a stereomicroscope and analysed with multivariate statistics; no computer vision method is applied.

title: DiffPose-Animal: A Language-Conditioned Diffusion Framework for Animal Pose Estimation
reason: Proposes an animal pose estimation method evaluated on animal pose datasets. Animals are the subject, and the data include wild animals in natural environments alongside domestic animals.

title: Biokinetic modelling of dugongs (Dugong dugon) deep and shallow foraging dive
reason: Biokinetic model of wild dugong foraging dives whose locomotion parameters (fluke motion, body centerline, flipper angles) were taken from video of dugongs in natural environments using image processing (manual binary masks, Sobel contour extraction). The image analysis is mostly manual and only supports the biomechanical model, so this is a borderline inclusion.

title: Intelligent bear deterrence system based on computer vision: Reducing human–bear conflicts in remote areas
reason: Primary study that trains a YOLOv5-MobileNet detector for wild Tibetan brown bears and deploys it in the field; training images also include domestic animals, humans and vehicles.

title: BeeMonitor: Automated IoT video surveillance and an AI-powered video processing system for monitoring the foraging and nesting behavior of cavity-nesting solitary bees
reason: Computer vision pipeline (detection, tracking, event classification) applied to field video of free-flying, non-domestic solitary bees (Osmia cornifrons) nesting in a bee hotel under natural conditions.

title: LizardLens: A Two-Stage Deep Learning Pipeline for Detecting and Classifying Similar Species in Visually Complex Environments
reason: Primary study that develops a two-stage detection and classification pipeline on iNaturalist field photographs of free-ranging Anolis lizards in Florida.

title: ResNet50 Based Transfer Learning Approach for Coral Reef Health Monitoring
venue: International Conference on Computing for Sustainable Global Development
reason: Applies CNN transfer learning to classify underwater images of coral reefs (wild animals) by health status.

title: Sustainable Computing for Ocean Health: An Approach to Enhance Crown of Thorn Starfish Detection
venue: International Conference on Computing for Sustainable Global Development
reason: Classical CV/ML pipeline classifying underwater reef images for crown-of-thorns starfish, a wild marine animal.

title: Multi-Class Species Classification for Biodiversity Monitoring using InceptionResNetV2
venue: International Conference on Computing for Sustainable Global Development
reason: Applies a CNN (InceptionResNetV2) to classify images of reptiles and amphibians for biodiversity monitoring. The images show the animals in natural scenes.

title: Computer Vision-Enabled IoT Framework for Wildlife Deterrence System in Sustainable Farming and Livestock Protection
venue: 16th ITU Kaleidoscope Academic Conference AI and Frontier Technologies for Good ITU K 2026 Proceedings
reason: Applies YOLOv5 detection to images of wild animals (elephants, tigers, leopards, gaur, etc.) together with domestic animals and humans for farmland wildlife deterrence.

title: Transfer Learning–Based Coral Classification Using Convolutional Neural Networks
venue: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
reason: Applies CNN-based image classification to underwater images of reef corals (wild marine animals).

title: Testing the efficacy of artificial flowers as a novel attractant for automated pollinator monitoring
reason: Wild insects were filmed responding to attractants, but the videos were reviewed and classified by hand. No computer vision or automated image analysis was done; the analysis is statistical (GLMMs, hurdle models).

title: Auto Fish: Leveraging AI for fish species identification in natural habitats
reason: The analysed images are single centred fish specimens photographed at fish markets and research facilities against a uniform background under controlled lighting; no images of wild, free-ranging animals are analysed despite the title.

title: Mapping Shallow Water Benthic Habitats Using High Resolution Multispectral UAV Data: A Case Study of Panggang Island
venue: Jurnal Ilmu dan Teknologi Kelautan Tropis
reason: Pixel-based mapping of benthic habitat cover classes (sand, seagrass, coral, algae, rubble) from UAV imagery; habitat/land-cover mapping rather than analysis of animals.

title: Knowledge Transfer from Human to Animal Pose Estimation Using Task Editing in Small-Scale Datasets
venue: Journal of Japan Society for Fuzzy Theory and Intelligent Informatics
reason: Pose-estimation transfer from humans to animals using the Animal Pose dataset. The paper does not say which species the dataset contains or that any are wild. The stated motivation is livestock farming and animal welfare, not wildlife.

title: Improving Real-Time Animal Detection Using Group Sparsity in YOLOv8: A Solution for Animal-Toy Differentiation
reason: Proposes a YOLOv8-based detector that tells real animals from toy replicas. Images come from the web, including NatGeoWild documentaries showing wild animals, together with Animals-10 and generic benchmarks. The stated application includes wildlife corridors and wildlife reserves.

title: Underwater Objects Detection Based on a Multi-Stage Deep Learning Framework
reason: Proposes a deep learning detection framework for underwater imagery (SUIM) whose classes include fish/vertebrates and reefs/invertebrates in ocean scenes; underwater-specific dataset, not a general benchmark.

title: REAL-TIME DOLPHIN DETECTION IN AQUATIC ENVIRONMENTS USING YOLO11-NANO
reason: Applies YOLO11-Nano to detect dolphins in field video frames, above and below water, in aquatic environments.

title: Body condition differs among social clusters and across years in endangered false killer whales in Hawai‘i
reason: Applies UAS-based aerial photogrammetry (image-based morphometric measurement) to free-ranging endangered false killer whales in Hawai'i, validated with aquarium animals.

title: Drone photogrammetry reveals age-structure shifts with potential consequences for the viability of spinner dolphins in Hawai'i
reason: Applies UAS (drone) photogrammetry to video frames of free-ranging spinner dolphins to measure body length and infer population age structure; image-based measurement of wild animals.

title: Seasonal differences in group composition of common dolphins off southern California, USA
reason: Drone aerial images of free-ranging common dolphins analysed photogrammetrically to measure total length and infer group composition.

title: Epi- and mesopelagic zooplankton and micronekton vertical zonation patterns in the Slope Sea
reason: Applies YOLOv8 detection and classification to in situ shadowgraph images of wild zooplankton and micronekton in the open ocean (Slope Sea) to study how they are distributed by depth.

title: Lettuce get along: effects of feeding enrichment on green sea turtle behavior and interactions
reason: Behavioural case study of two captive male green sea turtles in an aquarium. Behaviour was recorded by human observers with scan and all-occurrence sampling in ZooMonitor. No images or video were analysed and no computer vision was used. The animals are also captive only.

title: A non-invasive footprint technique for accurate identification of cryptic small mammal species: a sengi case study
reason: Classifies two wild sengi species from images of footprints (direct signs) of live-captured, released animals using image-based morphometric feature extraction and LDA.

title: Weakly supervised framework for wildlife detection and counting in challenging Arctic environments: a case study on caribou (Rangifer tarandus)
reason: Primary study proposing weakly supervised pretraining for a point-based detector (HerdNet) to detect and count wild caribou in aerial survey imagery from Alaska.

title: BugNet: a rapid and scalable pipeline for automated insect monitoring using hierarchical data
reason: Develops and evaluates a computer vision pipeline (localization and hierarchical classification) for wild insects, tested on GBIF images and on field camera trap images.

title: From noise to nature: diffusion models to advance wildlife detection in aerial imagery
reason: Primary study training YOLOv8 detectors on drone imagery of wild humpback whales, augmented with diffusion-generated synthetic images.

title: Wildlife detection for biodiversity monitoring and forest management in forest ecosystems under limited data using lightweight tri modal fusion
venue: Frontiers in Forests and Global Change
reason: Proposes a few-shot object detection framework for wildlife images (raccoon, kangaroo, tiger, plus field camera-trap subsets of ocelot and black-tailed deer); one dataset shows horses, so the subjects are mixed wild and domestic.

title: Squidle+: a collaborative platform to manage, discover and annotate marine imagery
reason: Platform paper for managing and annotating marine benthic imagery of wild organisms. It integrates and deploys ML detectors, classifiers and segmentation models (urchins, handfish, benthic indicators), with reported classifier performance.

title: Automated quantification of ecological interactions from video
reason: Primary study developing a detection, tracking and behaviour classification pipeline on in situ underwater video of wild reef fish.

title: Self-supervised transfer learning for few-shot classification on marine plankton images
reason: Proposes a few-shot self-supervised transfer learning method for classifying images of marine plankton (including zooplankton taxa) collected in the sea at Daya Bay and from the WHOI-plankton dataset.

title: PICOGRAM - informing coral reef resilience-based management through prediction of individual coral organismal growth, recruitment, and mortality
reason: Develops and evaluates a promptable segmentation model for coral colonies (wild marine animals) in in-situ underwater reef survey imagery; primary research.

title: Improving marine protected area zoning through species-oriented analysis using wildlife remote sensing
reason: Primary study applying a brightness-based image analysis method to very high-resolution satellite imagery to detect and count wild overwintering whooper swans in a nature reserve.

title: Underwater sea turtle behavior recognition: a lightweight pose-to-action pipeline
reason: The behaviour videos of the sea turtles were recorded in a test tank at a research facility. The paper never says that any of the analysed images show wild animals.

title: High-accuracy fish species identification using transfer learning on vision foundation models
reason: Primary study that compiles a dataset of citizen-science underwater images of wild Mediterranean fish and trains deep learning classifiers for species identification.

title: A holistic perspective on planktonic communities across the Northwestern Mediterranean Sea
reason: Field-collected wild marine zooplankton from net tows were imaged with ZooScan, and the images were classified semi-automatically with EcoTaxa (Random Forest and deep learning). Imaging is a smaller part of a study that is mostly metabarcoding, but it still applies computer vision to images of wild animals.

title: Cm-scale marine habitat mapping of entire Tumon Bay, Guam Coral Reef using NASA airborne fluid lensing and NeMO-Net pre (2022) and post (2024) Typhoon Mawar
reason: Deep-learning segmentation of drone imagery of a wild coral reef; the classes include branching and massive coral colonies (animals) alongside substrate classes. Borderline with habitat mapping (E-PLANT), but coral colonies are mapped as explicit targets.

title: FMRAG: retrieval-augmented multimodal large language models for fisheries intelligence
reason: Proposes a multimodal retrieval-augmented MLLM framework for fish species identification and biomass estimation. It is evaluated on underwater fish image datasets, including Fish4Knowledge underwater cameras in Taiwan.

title: Point-to-Polygon transformation to enhance legacy data
reason: Proposes a SAM-based method that converts point annotations to polygon masks. It is evaluated on underwater images of wild deep-sea benthic fauna and reef fish, plus a dataset of bridge infrastructure.

title: Edge-guided dual-branch network for underwater object detection via grayscale representation and spatially guided pyramid fusion
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for underwater images of marine organisms (holothurians, echinus, scallops, starfish, fish, turtles, etc.) from real-world underwater benchmarks; ecological surveys are a stated application.

title: Benthic communities of DeepInsight Hill, Mohn’s Ridge (Arctic Ocean)
reason: Applies a YOLO-based object detection model (DeepSee) to ROV video of wild deep-sea benthic megafauna on Mohn's Ridge to map and quantify taxa.

title: Image filtering to increase the efficiency in the construction of underwater photomosaics
reason: The paper filters redundant images to build photomosaics of Posidonia oceanica seagrass habitats on the seabed. Its subject is habitat and plants, not animals.

title: Spatial attention–driven hybrid Vision Transformers for automated classification of crown-of-thorns starfish in coral reef ecosystems
reason: Primary study proposing a hybrid Vision Transformer classifier for underwater photographs of crown-of-thorns starfish and four similar-looking marine taxa. The paper describes the images as underwater photographs but does not state how or where they were taken.

title: Autonomous underwater stereo vision system for non-invasive fish length estimation in marine environments
reason: Computer vision pipeline (segmentation, tracking, stereo reconstruction) for fish length estimation. It is validated on post-mortem and captive fish in tanks and deployed in open-sea conditions on wild fish off Cabrera, Spain.

title: An underwater dual-modal denoising detection network for illumination fluctuation and dense occlusion scenes
reason: Proposes an RGB-depth detection network for underwater marine organisms. The data combine aquaculture-zone images (sea urchins, sea cucumbers, starfish, scallops) with public imagery of wild marine taxa such as corals, turtles and jellyfish from coral reef ecosystems.

title: Seasonal and developmental patterns of body condition in Arctic seals
reason: Physiological study of captive seals using manual morphometrics and ultrasound blubber depth measurements analysed with statistical models; no computer vision method is developed or applied, and all animals are in captive care.

title: RSF-YOLOv8: a re-parameterized multi-branch feature augmentation network for polarization-guided underwater object detection
reason: Proposes a YOLOv8-based detector for marine organisms (sea cucumber, sea urchin, scallop, starfish, etc.) in underwater images. Part of the evaluation data was collected in real marine environments.

title: Using semi-supervised learning to detect beluga whales from aerial image sequences
reason: Primary study evaluating semi-supervised and supervised object detectors on UAV imagery of free-ranging beluga whales in Arctic coastal waters.

title: An updated census of southern elephant seals Mirounga leonina at South Georgia using satellite imagery
reason: Census of wild southern elephant seals from satellite and UAV imagery, but all counts were made manually by a human observer; no automated computer vision method is developed, applied or evaluated (only orthorectification and pansharpening as preprocessing).

title: FSD-Net: underwater object detection based on frequency and spatial domain feature enhancement
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for underwater marine organisms (echinus, holothurian, starfish, scallop, fish, crabs) evaluated on underwater marine monitoring datasets.

title: Hjort-YOLO: a lightweight and explainable computer vision framework for wildlife detection
reason: Proposes a YOLO-based detector for wild red deer in camera-trap images from Svanøy Island, Norway, and evaluates it on an African wildlife dataset.

title: WildDrone: autonomous drone technology for monitoring wildlife populations
reason: Project overview paper reporting preliminary computer vision results (detection, tracking, pose and 3D reconstruction) on drone imagery of free-ranging wildlife, mainly in Kenya; one sub-study uses harbour porpoises under human care.

title: Evaluating AI-based mosquito monitoring technologies: a field study in Zhejiang Province, 2025
reason: Field evaluation of AI camera-based traps that automatically identify (genus, sex) and count wild mosquitoes captured outdoors, validated against manual identification.

title: Development of an AI-Based Automatic Wild Boar Capture System and Its Field Validation in Island Regions
reason: Primary study that trains and deploys a YOLO detector on field images of free-ranging wild boars entering box traps on an island, and validates it in the field.

title: First-Stage Algorithm for Photo-Identification and Location of Marine Species
reason: Proposes a colour-index thresholding segmentation and SURF-based location method evaluated on sighting images of free-ranging whales and dolphins from the happywhale dataset.

title: Olfactory Enrichment of Captive Pygmy Hippopotamuses with Applied Machine Learning
reason: Pose estimation and behaviour classification applied only to three captive pygmy hippopotamuses in an indoor zoo enclosure; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Enhancing Wildlife Monitoring: An Advanced AI Approach for Accurate Giant Panda Behavior Detection and Conservation Insights
reason: Develops a deep learning behavior detection model on infrared camera-trap videos of wild giant pandas in Wolong.

title: Applicability of Machine Learning in Behavioural Monitoring of the Red Panda (Ailurus fulgens) in Zoos
reason: Study applies ML behaviour recognition to video of a single captive red panda in a zoo enclosure; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: CGS-BR: Construction and Benchmarking of a Respiratory Behavior Dataset for the Chinese Giant Salamander
reason: All images come from Chinese giant salamanders kept in an artificial breeding pond at a commercial breeding facility. No free-ranging animals were recorded.

title: Underwater Multi-Target Tracking and Behavioral Rhythm Analysis of Chinese Giant Salamander Based on TransTrack-OC-SORT
reason: Proposes a multi-object tracking algorithm applied to video of wild Chinese giant salamanders recorded in a national nature reserve river.

title: RCAF-Net: Wildlife Target Detection in Complex Forest Scenarios
reason: Proposes a YOLO11n-based detector (RCAF-Net) for wild mammals in forest monitoring imagery from Northeast China; primary research on images of wild animals.

title: Automated Activity Tracking and Space Use Monitoring of Captive Jaguars with Machine Learning
reason: Applies LabGym detectors and a behaviour categorizer to video of three captive zoo jaguars and to camera-trap videos of wild jaguars in Ecuador; part of the data shows wild animals.

title: Keypoint-Based Forest Musk Deer Behavioral Recognition Method
reason: All images come from captive forest musk deer in enclosures at a breeding base; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: DMN-YOLO: A Lightweight Small-Object Detector for Multi-Species Animal Detection in UAV Grassland Imagery
reason: Proposes a CV detector for UAV images of wild animals together with cattle and sheep in grassland; wild animals form part of the analysed data.

title: Underwater Photogrammetry for the Study of Vulnerable Benthic Species: The Case of Pinna rudis Linnaeus, 1758
reason: Applies SfM photogrammetry (computer vision 3D reconstruction) to video of wild Pinna rudis in a marine cave in a national park.

title: Mamba-YOLO-SRC: An Automatic Deep Learning Framework for Respiratory Behavior Detection in the Chinese Giant Salamander
reason: Detection of respiratory behaviours of Chinese giant salamanders housed in artificial streams and caves at a captive breeding base; no free-ranging animals in the data.

title: AVB81: A Fine-Grained Audiovisual Dataset and Benchmark for Bird Classification in the Wild
reason: Constructs an audiovisual dataset of 81 wild bird species (field videos, images, audio) and benchmarks image/video-frame classification models and audiovisual fusion on it.

title: Assessing Rodent-Induced Ecological Disturbance in Natural Grasslands Using Multi-Source Spatial Data
reason: Applies UAV imagery with YOLOv5 detection of burrows (direct signs) of wild plateau pika and Brandt's vole in natural grasslands to assess rodent damage.

title: Structure-Driven Feature Modeling for Robust Fish Detection in Complex Underwater Environments
reason: Main dataset shows Medaka (a laboratory model fish) in a larval-breeding tank at a university. The paper does not say the external Blue Bot Dataset shows wild fish, so no data is confirmed to show wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Reannotation-Free Automatic Recognition Methods for Empty Camera Trap Images Based on MegaDetector Optimization
reason: Primary study proposing MegaDetector-based methods to recognise empty camera trap images from wildlife surveys in Africa and China.

title: An Ultra-Lightweight Fish Detection Model for Real-Time Aquatic Animal Monitoring on Embedded Platforms
reason: Proposes a CV fish detector evaluated on captive aquarium fish (Fish-BJ) and on a WildFish subset of fish images from natural aquatic environments, so part of the data shows wild fish.

title: Automated Auricular Surface Temperature Monitoring in Asian Elephants Using Deep Learning and Infrared Thermography
reason: Deep-learning detection of the outer ear in infrared thermograms of Asian elephants. The training data include historical images of semi-captive, captive and wild elephants, so part of the data shows wild animals.

title: Exploratory Comparison of Behavior and Welfare-Related Indicators in Captive Lions (Panthera leo) Across Three Zoo Enclosures Using Machine-Learning Quantification
reason: Machine-learning video analysis of lion behaviour, but all animals are housed in three Danish zoo enclosures; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Deep Learning for Snake Species Identification to Support Snakebite Treatment: A Comparative Study of Efficient CNN and Vision Transformer Architectures
reason: Deep learning image classification of wild snake species from citizen-science photographs (SnakeCLEF 2024); primary research comparing architectures.

title: Bird Detection in the Field with the IA-Mask-RCNN
reason: Primary study that adapts Mask-RCNN to detect wild, free-ranging corvids and pigeons in images taken by fixed cameras in crop fields. The birds are wild animals damaging crops, not livestock or farmed animals.

title: Biological Feasibility of a Novel Island-Type Fishway Inspired by the Tesla Valve
reason: Juvenile silver carp were tested in an indoor laboratory flume (experimental fishway). YOLOv5 tracking was applied only to these laboratory fish, so no wild or free-ranging animals were imaged.

title: Dual-Task Learning for Fine-Grained Bird Species and Behavior Recognition via Token Re-Segmentation, Multi-Scale Mixed Attention, and Feature Interleaving
reason: Primary study proposing a dual-task CNN-Transformer network for bird species and behaviour recognition on bird photographs (CUB-200-2011 extended with eBird images), with bird monitoring as the stated application. The paper does not explicitly say the birds are wild; this is inferred from the image sources.

title: DeepPanda: A Video-Based Framework for Automatic Behavior Recognition of Giant Pandas
reason: Behavior recognition of captive giant pandas in a breeding center enclosure; no wild or free-ranging animals in the analysed data.

title: Research on a Lightweight Detection Method for Underwater Diseased Corals
reason: Proposes a lightweight object detector (CD-YOLO) for diseased and healthy corals in underwater images; corals are wild, non-domestic animals and the work is primary research.

title: An Adaptive Audiovisual Fusion Method Based on Prediction Confidence for Fine Granularity Bird Species Recognition
reason: Proposes an audiovisual fusion method for fine-grained bird species classification, with an image CNN branch evaluated on field photographs of wild birds (SSW60: iNaturalist 2021 and NABirds images).

title: Underwater Image Feature Extraction and Classification Using a Multi-Scale Vision Transformer with Cross-Scale Biased Attention Fusion
reason: Proposes a vision transformer that classifies underwater images, with fish and coral among the classes. The data combine the Roboflow Aquarium dataset (aquarium images) with RUIE, which the paper describes as real-world underwater images. The stated application is marine biodiversity monitoring.

title: NEB-YOLO: An Improved Lightweight YOLOv8 Network for Fine-Grained Bird Recognition in Complex Environments
reason: Proposes a lightweight YOLOv8-based detector for fine-grained recognition of bird species in natural environments, evaluated on the CUB-200-2011 bird dataset; wildlife monitoring is the stated application.

title: AntID_APP: Empowering Citizen Scientists with YOLO Models for Ant Identification in Taiwan
reason: YOLO-based detection and genus-level identification of ants in citizen-science (iNaturalist) photographs, deployed as a web application for biodiversity monitoring.

title: CABIF-Net: Robust Confidence-Based Audio-Visual Fusion for Fine-Grained Bird Recognition
reason: Proposes an audio-visual fusion network that classifies wild bird species from video frames and web images, combined with audio.

title: Computer Vision-Assisted Semiautomatic Analysis of Zooplankton in a Longitudinal Study of the Ecological State of Lake Baikal
reason: Wild zooplankton are net-sampled from Lake Baikal, fixed in formalin and imaged under a light microscope in the laboratory. The analysis is microscopy of preserved specimens, not imaging of free-ranging animals, so it falls under the microscopy exclusion.

title: DSCF-DET: An RT-DETR-Based Framework for Fine-Grained Detection of Musk Deer and Visually Similar Artiodactyls
reason: Proposes an RT-DETR-based detector for musk deer and similar artiodactyls on ecological images (iNaturalist, photo library, documentary frames) and evaluates on a camera-trap wildlife dataset.

title: Spatial Variation in Stream-Water Bacterial Communities Across Sites Differing in Wild Chinese Giant Salamander Detection Frequency
reason: Applies a YOLO-based object-detection model to field video of wild Chinese giant salamanders in streams to derive site-level detection frequency.

title: Stroke Asymmetry in Bird Wing Dynamics During Flight from Video Data
reason: Applies DeepLabCut pose estimation and mask-based segmentation to video of free-flying wild birds (Canada geese, lesser frigatebird) to quantify wing kinematics.

title: From Above: Drone-Driven Computer Vision for Reliable Elephant Body Condition Assessment
reason: Drone-image analysis (background removal, Canny edge detection, landmark distances) to measure elephant morphometry; validated on captive trained Sumatran elephants and applied to free-ranging wild elephants.

title: Tracking Spatial and Activity Patterns in Captive Reptiles Using Deep Learning
reason: Pose estimation and tracking of captive-bred geckos housed in terrariums only; no wild or free-ranging animals.

title: Recapturing Vipera ursinii: Photo-Identification and HDF Telemetry in a Meadow Viper Population from Maiella National Park, Italy
reason: Primary study applying software-assisted photo-identification (Wild-ID, Hotspotter) to head photographs of wild-caught, released meadow vipers in a national park.

title: Non-Invasive Individual Re-Identification of Water Monitors (Varanus salvator) Using Deep Learning
reason: Primary study benchmarking deep learning and classical feature matching for photographic individual re-identification of free-ranging urban water monitors.

title: Towards Robust Underwater Object Detection: UWOD Dataset and Transfer Learning Insights
reason: Dataset and benchmark paper for underwater object detection; most classes are marine animals, drawn from field sources (brackish strait, open sea, online video of marine species) together with aquarium tank images and divers.

title: BEHAVE-UAV: A Behaviour-Aware Synthetic Data Pipeline for Wildlife Detection from UAV Imagery
reason: Develops a synthetic data pipeline and evaluates object detectors on real UAV imagery of wild swamp deer in natural habitats.

title: Thermal Drones Aid to Uncover Nocturnal Subgrouping Patterns of a Diurnal Primate
reason: Thermal drone videos of wild spider monkeys were reviewed and counted manually by human observers; no computer vision or automated image analysis method is applied.

title: Preliminary Findings of a Novel Thermal Drone-Based and AI Approach to Sampling Mesopredator Behaviour and Habitat Use
reason: Primary study applying an AI video-analysis tool (LabGym) to thermal drone video of wild, free-ranging foxes, badgers and otters in Denmark for species detection and behaviour classification.

title: UAV Georeferencing for High-Precision Spatial Localization of Surfacing Yangtze Finless Porpoises
reason: UAV imagery of wild Yangtze finless porpoises in the Yangtze–Poyang Lake system; proposes LapConv-enhanced YOLO-OBB detection and georeferencing.

title: EFE_UODNet: Enhanced Underwater Organism Detection in Complex Environments
reason: Proposes a detection network for underwater organisms (sea cucumber, sea urchin, scallop, starfish) evaluated on underwater image datasets; the paper presents the data as real underwater environments but does not state whether animals are wild or farmed.

title: A Comprehensive Evaluation of YOLO-Based Deer Detection Performance on Edge Devices
reason: Benchmarks YOLO detectors for deer detection on camera-trap images of free-ranging deer (Idaho Cameratraps), with an annotated dataset released.

title: Efficient 3D Bird Pose Estimation via Gated Large-Kernel Attention and Unsupervised Geometric Constraints
reason: Proposes a CNN-based 2D pose estimation backbone and unsupervised 3D lifting for birds, evaluated on bird images collected from wild environments (Animal Kingdom).

title: eBirdNet-Nano: An Operator-Aware Lightweight Detector and Edge AI Terminal for Endangered Bird Real-Time Monitoring
reason: Proposes a lightweight object detector and edge terminal for detecting 24 protected and endangered wild bird species in Macao, with field deployment in a reserve.

title: Improved Lightweight YOLOv8n with Dynamic Sampling Convolution and CBAM Attention for UAV Wildlife Detection
reason: Proposes an improved YOLOv8n detector for wildlife detection. It is trained on Caltech Camera Traps field images of wild animals and validated on UAV aerial wildlife images.

title: Multi-Dimensional Collaborative Enhancement Method for Small-Object Detection in Complex Underwater Scenarios
reason: Proposes a CNN detector for underwater organisms (echinus, holothurian, scallop, starfish, fish, crab, etc.) in underwater images from natural scenes; primary research.

title: Adaptive Visual Enhancement and Semi-Supervised Learning for Robust Underwater Object Detection
reason: Proposes CV methods (adaptive enhancement + semi-supervised detection) for underwater object detection on URPC2022, which includes marine organisms such as echinus; the paper does not say whether the organisms are wild or farmed.

title: Zero-LUT Open-Set Plankton Classification on Edge MPSoC and GPU Platforms
reason: Primary study that classifies in situ images of plankton (including zooplankton such as annelids, copepods and pteropods) with a CNN pipeline and open-set rejection on edge hardware.

title: Neocaridina (Cherry Shrimp) Sex Identification Using You Only Look Once Version 9
reason: Sex identification of ornamental cherry shrimp kept in breeding/holding tanks for breeders and aquarium hobbyists; no wild animals.

title: Image Classification of Asiatic Parakeets Using YOLOv5 and Residual Network 50
reason: The parakeet images all come from birds photographed in a custom container at a private aviary. Random eBird images were used only to train the bird detector, and the paper does not say they show wild birds.

title: Mussel Classification Using Convolutional Neural Network with MobileNet
reason: Mussel species classification for the aquaculture industry. Individual mussel specimens are placed in an enclosure under a fixed Raspberry Pi camera. No free-ranging animals are imaged in the field, and the stated application is aquaculture.

title: Time Series Analysis of the Behavior of Wild Animals Using Camera Traps
reason: The study runs time-series and statistical analysis (ARIMA, seasonal decomposition, statistical tests) on the timestamps and species labels of camera-trap records. No images are analysed with computer vision.

title: Bridging Local Ecological Knowledge and Remote Sensing for Wildlife Assessment and Conservation: Insights from Sebitoli, Kibale National Park, Uganda
reason: Primary study applying an automated deep-learning classifier (DeepForestVision) to camera-trap videos of wild vertebrates in Kibale National Park, alongside acoustic monitoring and local ecological knowledge surveys.

title: Tackling Scale Variation and Annotation Scarcity in Semi-Supervised Small Pest Detection with Image Slicing and Pseudo-Label Refinement
reason: Detection of pest insects in light-trap images from nursery, economic fruit forest and planted forest production sites; pest monitoring for forestry/agricultural production rather than wildlife conservation.

title: DAAL-YOLOv12n: A Method for Detecting Common Forest Pests Incorporating Dynamic Attention and Adaptive Lightweight Modules
reason: Proposes a YOLO-based detector for free-living forest pest insects on field-acquired and online images; framed as forest pest monitoring rather than crop production, although field images come from an orchard base.

title: Morphological Classification of the Sagittal Otoliths of Two Species of Sciaenidae Based on the Landmark Point Method
reason: Geometric morphometrics on digital-microscope images of extracted otoliths from dead fish in a laboratory. Landmarks were placed by hand and analysed statistically. There is no imaging of free-ranging animals.

title: Fish Resource Assessment in the Huoyanshan Waters of Poyang Lake Using DIDSON and Deep Learning Models
reason: Applies YOLO and DeepSORT object detection/tracking to DIDSON imaging-sonar images of wild fish in Poyang Lake for resource assessment.

title: Multi-Class Marine Organism Detection Using Multi-Scale Attention-Enhanced YOLO11n
reason: Proposes a CBAM/CIoU-enhanced YOLO11n detector and evaluates it on real underwater video of marine organisms (fish, crab, shrimp, starfish, jellyfish) recorded in brackish water; primary research with a computer vision method on animal imagery.

title: Research on Fish Recognition in Complex Backgrounds Using ViT-Enhanced YOLOv11
reason: Images show dead fish specimens bought at an aquatic products market and photographed indoors. No wild or free-ranging animals are imaged.

title: Ultra-Fine-Grained Fish Recognition with a Pruned Lightweight Transformer Based on Few-Shot Learning
reason: Individual recognition of farmed koi for aquaculture monitoring; the core data are three farmed koi imaged under controlled conditions. Public fish datasets serve only as supplementary benchmarks.

title: Morphometric Information for Yangtze Finless Porpoises Using Detection-Guided SAM2 Segmentation with UAV Imagery
reason: Develops a detection-guided SAM2 segmentation and morphometric workflow on UAV imagery of free-ranging Yangtze finless porpoises in natural waters.

title: Workflow of Visualisation of Mole-Rat Burrows Using 3D Datasets Derived from GPR, UAV Surveys, and Interpretative Processing
reason: Primary study reconstructing 3D models of the burrows and mounds of wild mole-rats (direct animal signs) from UAV RGB photogrammetry combined with GPR volumes. This is borderline: the image-analysis part is photogrammetric 3D reconstruction, and the burrows themselves come from radar traced by hand.

title: Making Animal Re-Identification Accessible: A Web-Based Giraffe ID System for Zoos
reason: Re-identification of the four zoo giraffes at Wellington Zoo. The supplementary GZGCID detection data is not described as showing wild animals, so the study is coded as zoo animals only.

title: Multi-View Pareto Optimization for Minimal-Diagnostic-Set Identification of Disease Vectors
reason: Images are microscope photographs of euthanized, pinned fly and mosquito specimens taken in surveillance labs. The insects were wild-caught, but the imaging is laboratory microscopy of specimens.

title: Estimation of the Length at First Maturity of the Swimming Crab (Portunus trituberculatus) in the Yellow Sea of Korea Using Machine Learning
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Applies image analysis (HSV colour segmentation plus ML classification) to smartphone images of gonads from wild-caught swimming crabs, to estimate maturity for managing the wild stock.

title: SEAF-Net: A Sustainable and Lightweight Attention-Enhanced Detection Network for Underwater Fish Species Recognition
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Proposes a YOLO-based detector for underwater fish species; dataset aggregated from open-source and web images covering aquaculture as well as natural water environments (e.g., coral reef), so part of the data shows wild fish.

title: PIRATE—Precision Imaging Real-Time Autonomous Tracker & Explorer
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Autonomous surface vehicle that runs onboard computer vision (YOLOv7 detection, STARK tracking) on live underwater video of free-ranging fish at Mediterranean coastal sites, plus public underwater fish datasets.

title: Coral Species Strategies in the Gulf of Eilat (Aqaba)
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Applies ResNet-50 CNN to classify wild stony coral genera in field underwater imagery from reefs in the Gulf of Eilat.

title: A Lightweight Fish Detection Method for Complex Underwater Scenes
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Proposes a lightweight YOLOv8n-based detector for fish in real-world underwater images (WildFish dataset), intended for ecological monitoring.

title: Underway Shadowgraphic Imaging for Plankton Detection and Classification
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: In situ shadowgraphic imaging of wild marine plankton (zooplankton) in the open ocean, with automated detection and random forest classification of the imaged particles.

title: Beyond Nuclear Norm: Adversarial Spectral Distribution Alignment for Cross-Domain Underwater Object Recognition
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Proposes a domain adaptation method for classifying marine animals in underwater images; uses real-world underwater images (AQUA20) together with aquarium images (MKUO).

title: Combining Deep Learning and Ecological Monitoring for BRUV Coral Reef Megafauna Assessment
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering
reason: Primary study applying a deep learning object detector and temporal tracker to baited remote underwater video of free-ranging coral reef megafauna and predatory fishes in a marine protected area.

title: Physics-Aware Diffusion Synthesis for Robust Underwater Object Detection
venue: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering

reason: Develops a spatio-temporal action detector for behaviours of wild wintering cranes in field videos from fixed infrared cameras in nature reserves.

reason: Computer vision detection, tracking and counting of wild-caught tuna on the deck of a distant-water longline vessel, using electronic monitoring video. The fish are wild ocean fish from capture fisheries, not aquaculture.

reason: Proposes a detection, health-classification and forecasting framework for corals on underwater images collected at natural reef sites; corals are wild, non-domestic animals.

reason: Proposes a CNN attention module for YOLO-based detection and counting of fish (herring, mackerel, blue whiting, mesopelagic) in underwater images from oceanographic campaigns in the Northeast Atlantic.

reason: Primary study presenting a multi-sensor vision system with YOLO-based detection and stereo/3D reconstruction, applied to near-infrared video of wild bats recorded in natural caves in Mexico.

reason: Primary study that builds an annotation framework and trains a YOLOv8 detector on unbaited remote underwater video of free-ranging fish and gelatinous zooplankton at kelp farms and reference sites.

title: Sustainable Hierarchical Networking for Extreme-Edge AI-Based Wildlife Monitoring in Resource-Constrained Environments
reason: Deploys YOLOv8m detection and tracking on PIR-triggered camera nodes recording wild fallow deer, wild boar and wolves in the field.

title: Spatiotemporal Decision-AI for Species-Specific and Non-Lethal Management of Avian Predators in Aquaculture
reason: YOLOv8 detection, classification and counting of wild birds (herons, egrets, geese) that visit outdoor aquaculture ponds, using images from field cameras. The birds are wild visitors, not farmed animals.

reason: Proposes a video-text multimodal model (ABCLIP) for behavior recognition of wild endangered animals filmed by camera traps in nature reserves in China.

reason: Proposes a spiking-network object detector for underwater images of marine organisms (sea urchin, sea cucumber, starfish, scallop, fish, turtle, etc.). The stated application is aquatic ecosystem monitoring.

title: Assessment of the Baikal seal population and its pup production
reason: Applies trained neural-network models to visible and thermal UAV images to detect and count wild Baikal seals and their birth lairs on the ice of Lake Baikal.

reason: Applies YOLOv8 object detection to UAS orthomosaic images of a wild black-tailed gull breeding colony to count individuals for population estimation.

title: The perceptual and spatial architecture of Müllerian mimicry in Heliconius Butterflies

reason: Computer vision pipeline (MegaDetector, SAM, DPT depth) applied to camera trap images of wild mammals and birds in US montane forests to estimate density parameters.

reason: Deep learning identification of mosquito species from images of wild field-trapped specimens (plus insectary-reared specimens) for vector surveillance in Italy.

reason: Individual identification of captive budgerigars housed in a research aviary under laboratory conditions; no wild or free-ranging animals are analysed.

title: Brinkmanship and the sensory–motor limits of pursuit predation

reason: Develops and validates a deep-learning pipeline for detection, morphometry and size classification of wild harbor seals at haulouts from UAV orthomosaics.

reason: Trains and evaluates a general-purpose object detector for animals in aerial drone imagery spanning wild African, Asian and European mammals together with livestock.

title: A Framework for Clustering and Zero-Shot Labeling of Ecological Images Using Foundation Models
reason: Proposes a foundation-model framework for clustering and zero-shot species labeling of images of wild moths (light-trap camera) and birds (camera trap, Flickr).

title: Fish Instance Segmentation and Closed-Polygon Boundary Visualization Using YOLO Mode
venue: Journal of Environmental Research and Engineering
